/-- To bisect a given rectilineal angle. -/
theorem Prop9 {A B C : Point} (hBAC : Triangle B A C) :
    ∃ F : Point, SameSideOf F C A B ∧ SameSideOf F B A C ∧
      ∠ B A F = ∠ F A C ∧ ∠ B A F + ∠ F A C = ∠ B A C := by
  -- Let the angle BAC be the given rectilineal angle.
  have hAB : A ≠ B := hBAC.ne₁₂.symm
  have hAC : A ≠ C := hBAC.ne₂₃
  obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B hAB
  obtain ⟨AC, hA_AC, hC_AC⟩ := Postulate1 A C hAC
  have hC_AB : ¬ OnLine C AB := hBAC.off_line hB_AB hA_AB
  -- It is then required to bisect it.
  -- Let a point D be taken at random on AB;
  /- At random, but not too far out, since AD is about to be cut off from AC: D is
     taken nearer to A than C is (`exists_between_nearer` in Book Zero, with a
     circle about A through C). -/
  have hAA_AC : ‖A A‖ < ‖A C‖ := by
    rw [len_self]
    exact len_pos hAC
  obtain ⟨D, hADB, hAD_AC⟩ := exists_between_nearer hAB (Or.inl rfl) hAA_AC
  have hAD : A ≠ D := ne_of_between hADB
  have hD_AB : OnLine D AB := on_line_of_between_ends hADB hA_AB hB_AB
  -- let AE be cut off from AC equal to AD; [I. 3]
  obtain ⟨E, hAEC, hAE_AD⟩ := Prop3 hAD hAD_AC
  have hAE : A ≠ E := ne_of_between hAEC
  have hE_AC : OnLine E AC := on_line_of_between_ends hAEC hA_AC hC_AC
  -- let DE be joined, and on DE let the equilateral triangle DEF be constructed;
  /- E is off AB, or C would be on it; so ADE is a triangle. The equilateral triangle
     goes on the side of DE away from A, which Euclid leaves to his figure: we take a
     point Q on that side (System E, Points 6) and ask I.1 for Q's side. -/
  have hE_AB : ¬ OnLine E AB := fun h => hC_AB (on_line_of_between hAEC hA_AB h)
  have hADE : Triangle A D E := Triangle.of_line hA_AB hD_AB hAD hE_AB
  have hDE : D ≠ E := hADE.ne₂₃
  obtain ⟨Q, hQA, -⟩ := exists_oppositeSidesOf hADE.bca []
  obtain ⟨F, ⟨-, -, hEF_FD⟩, hside⟩ := Prop1 D E hDE Q
  have hFA : OppositeSidesOf F A D E := (hside hQA.triangle).trans_opposite hQA
  -- let AF be joined.
  /- Joined, AF falls within the angle BAC. That is Proclus' objector answered: AF
     crosses DE between D and E (`Prop9.crossing`, by I.5 and I.7), and from there F is
     on C's side of AB and on B's side of AC (`Prop9.side`). -/
  have hFD_FE : ‖F D‖ = ‖F E‖ := hEF_FD.symm.trans (len_symm E F)
  obtain ⟨M, hAMF, hDME⟩ := Prop9.crossing hBAC hADB hAEC hAE_AD.symm hFD_FE hFA
  have hFC : SameSideOf F C A B := Prop9.side hBAC hADB hAEC hDME hAMF
  have hFB : SameSideOf F B A C := Prop9.side hBAC.cba hAEC hADB (between_symm hDME) hAMF
  have hF_AB : ¬ OnLine F AB := hFC.triangle.off_line hA_AB hB_AB
  have hF_AC : ¬ OnLine F AC := hFB.triangle.off_line hA_AC hC_AC
  have hAF : A ≠ F := fun h => hF_AB (h ▸ hA_AB)
  -- I say that the angle BAC has been bisected by the straight line AF.
  -- For, since AD is equal to AE,
  have hAD_AE : ‖A D‖ = ‖A E‖ := hAE_AD.symm
  -- and AF is common,
  have hAF_AF : ‖A F‖ = ‖A F‖ := rfl
  -- the two sides DA, AF are equal to the two sides EA, AF respectively.
  -- And the base DF is equal to the base EF;
  have hDF_EF : ‖D F‖ = ‖E F‖ := (len_symm D F).trans hEF_FD.symm
  -- therefore the angle DAF is equal to the angle EAF. [I. 8]
  /- ADF and AEF are triangles, since F is off AB and off AC. -/
  have hADF : Triangle A D F := Triangle.of_line hA_AB hD_AB hAD hF_AB
  have hAEF : Triangle A E F := Triangle.of_line hA_AC hE_AC hAE hF_AC
  have hDAF_EAF : ∠ D A F = ∠ E A F := Prop8 hADF hAEF hAD_AE hAF_AF hDF_EF
  -- Therefore the given rectilineal angle BAC has been bisected by the straight line AF.
  /- The angle DAF is the angle BAF, since D lies on AB, and the angle EAF is the angle
     CAF, that is, FAC, since E lies on AC (an angle depends only on its rays). And
     since F lies within the angle BAC, that angle is made up of BAF and FAC
     (System E, Diagram-angle 2). -/
  have hbisect : ∠ B A F = ∠ F A C := by
    rw [← angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between hADB) hAF.symm, hDAF_EAF,
      angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between hAEC) hAF.symm, angle_symm hAC.symm hAF.symm]
  have hAB_AC : AB ≠ AC := fun h => hC_AB (h ▸ hC_AC)
  have hwhole : ∠ B A C = ∠ B A F + ∠ F A C :=
    angle_add_of_inside hA_AB hA_AC hB_AB hC_AC hAB hAC hF_AB hF_AC hAB_AC
      (same_side_symm (hFB.2 AC hA_AC hC_AC)) (same_side_symm (hFC.2 AB hA_AB hB_AB))
  exact ⟨F, hFC, hFB, hbisect, hwhole.symm⟩
  -- Q. E. F.

helper_signatures.Elements.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop1:
/-- On a given finite straight line to construct an equilateral triangle. -/
theorem Prop1 (A B : Point) (hAB : A ≠ B) (P : Point) :
    ∃ C : Point, Equilateral A B C ∧ (¬ Collinear A B P → SameSideOf C P A B)
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop3:
/-- Given two unequal straight lines, to cut off from the greater a straight line equal to the
less. -/
theorem Prop3 {A B C₁ C₂ : Point} (hC : C₁ ≠ C₂) (h : ‖C₁ C₂‖ < ‖A B‖) :
    ∃ E : Point, Between A E B ∧ ‖A E‖ = ‖C₁ C₂‖
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop5:
/-- In isosceles triangles the angles at the base are equal to one another, and, if the equal
straight lines be produced further, the angles under the base will be equal to one another. -/
theorem Prop5 {A B C D E : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖A C‖)
    (hD : Between A B D) (hE : Between A C E) :
    ∠ A B C = ∠ A C B ∧ ∠ C B D = ∠ B C E
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop5.base:
/-- The angles at the base, and only those. Our I.5 is stated as Euclid states it,
with the equal sides produced and the angles under the base as well, so a proof that
cites it must first produce AB and AC (Post. 2). When only the angles at the base are
wanted, as in I.7, I.9, I.18, I.19, I.20 and I.24, any points beyond B and C
will do, and this produces them once. [I. 5] -/
theorem Prop5.base {A B C : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (h : ‖A B‖ = ‖A C‖) :
    ∠ A B C = ∠ A C B
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop7:
/-- Given two straight lines constructed on a straight line (from its extremities) and meeting in a
point, there cannot be constructed on the same straight line (from its extremities), and on the
same side of it, two other straight lines meeting in another point and equal to the former two
respectively, namely each to that which has the same extremity with it. -/
theorem Prop7 {A B C D : Point} (hCD : SameSideOf C D A B) (hCA : ‖C A‖ = ‖D A‖)
    (hCB : ‖C B‖ = ‖D B‖) :
    C = D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop8:
/-- If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have also the base
equal to the base, they will also have the angles equal which are contained by the equal
straight lines. -/
theorem Prop8 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖D F‖) (hBC : ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖) :
    ∠ B A C = ∠ E D F
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop9.crossing:
/-- Where does the straight line AF cross DE? Since F is on the other side of DE
from A, the straight line AF crosses DE at a point M (Intersection 1, Pasch
4). And M falls between D and E. It is not D or E: that is Proclus' first
case, `Prop9.not_on_arm`. Nor is it beyond D or beyond E: then D and E would
be on the same side of AF, and I.7 would make them one point, since AD is equal
to AE and FD to FE. -/
theorem Prop9.crossing {A B C D E F : Point} (hBAC : Triangle B A C) (hADB : Between A D B)
    (hAEC : Between A E C) (hAD_AE : ‖A D‖ = ‖A E‖) (hFD_FE : ‖F D‖ = ‖F E‖)
    (hF : OppositeSidesOf F A D E) : ∃ M : Point, Between A M F ∧ Between D M E
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop9.not_on_arm:
/-- Proclus' objector has a first case: F might fall on AB itself, beyond D. Proclus
answers him with the second part of I.5 (Heath, vol. 1, p. 265). Since FD is equal
to FE, the angle FDE is equal to the angle FED [I. 5]. Since AD is equal to
AE, the angles EDF, DEC under the base of the triangle ADE are equal [I. 5].
So the angle DEF is equal to the angle DEC, with F and C on the same side of
DE; then F lies on the straight line EC (`onRay_of_angle_eq`), that is, on AC.
But AB and AC meet only at A. -/
theorem Prop9.not_on_arm {A B C D E F : Point} (hBAC : Triangle B A C) (hADB : Between A D B)
    (hAEC : Between A E C) (hAD_AE : ‖A D‖ = ‖A E‖) (hFD_FE : ‖F D‖ = ‖F E‖)
    (hF : OppositeSidesOf F A D E) : ¬ Between A D F
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop9.side:
/-- Where AF crosses DE tells the side of AB: M, between D and E, is on
E's side of AB, and F, beyond M from A, is on M's side; and E, between
A and C, is on C's side (Pasch 2). So F is on C's side of AB. -/
theorem Prop9.side {A B C D E F M : Point} (hBAC : Triangle B A C) (hADB : Between A D B)
    (hAEC : Between A E C) (hDME : Between D M E) (hAMF : Between A M F) :
    SameSideOf F C A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.of_between:
/-- A point between A and B is on the ray from A through B. -/
theorem OnRay.of_between (h : Between A P B) : OnRay P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.onLine:
/-- Every straight line through A and B passes through each point of the ray
from A through B. -/
theorem OnRay.onLine (h : OnRay P A B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) : OnLine P L
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.symm:
/-- P is on the ray from A through B exactly when B is on the ray from A
through P: they are one and the same ray. -/
theorem OnRay.symm (h : OnRay P A B) : OnRay B A P
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSides:
/-- `A` and `B` lie on opposite sides of the straight line `L`. -/
def OppositeSides (A B : Point) (L : Line) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf:
/-- `P` and `Q` lie on opposite sides of the straight line `AB`. -/
def OppositeSidesOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.oppositeSides:
/-- Two points on opposite sides of the straight line AB are on opposite sides of
any straight line drawn through A and B. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.oppositeSides (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) (hA : OnLine A L)
    (hB : OnLine B L) : OppositeSides P Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.swap:
/-- "On opposite sides of AB" is the same as "on opposite sides of BA". -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.swap (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : OppositeSidesOf P Q B A
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the other side of AB from Q, then Q is on the other side
from P. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.symm (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : OppositeSidesOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.triangle:
/-- A point on either side of the straight line AB is not on it, so ABP is a
triangle. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.triangle (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : Triangle A B P
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate1:
/-- **Postulate 1.** To draw a straight line from any point to any point. -/
axiom Postulate1 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf:
/-- `P` and `Q` lie on the same side of the straight line `AB`. -/
def SameSideOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.of_line:
/-- Two points on the same side of a straight line L through A and B are on
the same side of the straight line AB, however that line is named: two points
fix one straight line. -/
theorem SameSideOf.of_line (hAB : A ≠ B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (h : SameSide P Q L) : SameSideOf P Q A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.swap:
/-- "On the same side of AB" is the same as "on the same side of BA". -/
theorem SameSideOf.swap (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf P Q B A
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the same side of AB as Q, then Q is on the same side as P. -/
theorem SameSideOf.symm (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.trans:
/-- Points on the same side as a third are on the same side as each other. -/
theorem SameSideOf.trans (h₁ : SameSideOf P Q A B) (h₂ : SameSideOf Q R A B) :
    SameSideOf P R A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.trans_opposite:
/-- A point on Q's side of the straight line AB, where Q is on the other side
from R, is itself on the other side from R. -/
theorem SameSideOf.trans_opposite (h₁ : SameSideOf P Q A B) (h₂ : OppositeSidesOf Q R A B) :
    OppositeSidesOf P R A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.triangle:
/-- A point on one side of the straight line AB is not on it, so ABP is a
triangle. -/
theorem SameSideOf.triangle (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : Triangle A B P
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.angle_add_of_inside:
/-- If D lies within the angle BAC, then BAC is made up of BAD and DAC.
(Diagram-angle 2) -/
axiom angle_add_of_inside (hAL : OnLine A L) (hAM : OnLine A M) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (hC : OnLine C M) (hAB : A ≠ B) (hAC : A ≠ C) (hDL : ¬ OnLine D L) (hDM : ¬ OnLine D M)
    (hLM : L ≠ M) (hBD : SameSide B D M) (hCD : SameSide C D L) :
    ∠ B A C = ∠ B A D + ∠ D A C
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.angle_symm:
/-- The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4) -/
axiom angle_symm (hAB : A ≠ B) (hCB : C ≠ B) : ∠ A B C = ∠ C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_cases:
/-- Of three different points on a straight line, one is between the other two.
(Between 6) -/
axiom between_cases (hAB : A ≠ B) (hBC : B ≠ C) (hAC : A ≠ C) (hA : OnLine A L)
    (hB : OnLine B L) (hC : OnLine C L) : Between A B C ∨ Between B A C ∨ Between A C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_symm:
/-- If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1) -/
axiom between_symm (h : Between A B C) : Between C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.len_self:
/-- The "straight line" from a point to itself has no length. (Metric 1) -/
axiom len_self (A : Point) : ‖A A‖ = 0
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.len_symm:
/-- The straight line AB is the straight line BA. (Metric 3) -/
axiom len_symm (A B : Point) : ‖A B‖ = ‖B A‖
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.line_unique:
/-- Two points determine a straight line. (Generalities 1) -/
axiom line_unique (hAB : A ≠ B) (hAL : OnLine A L) (hBL : OnLine B L) (hAM : OnLine A M)
    (hBM : OnLine B M) : L = M
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.lines_meet_of_opposite_si:
/-- A straight line joining points on opposite sides of L crosses L.
(Intersection 1) -/
axiom lines_meet_of_opposite_sides (h : OppositeSides A B L) (hAM : OnLine A M)
    (hBM : OnLine B M) : LinesMeet L M
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between:
/-- A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between_ends:
/-- The ends of a finite straight line differ. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between:
/-- A straight line through A and B, with B between A and C, passes
through C. (Between 2) -/
axiom on_line_of_between (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    OnLine C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between_ends:
/-- A straight line through A and C passes through every point between them.
(Between 3) -/
axiom on_line_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hC : OnLine C L) :
    OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.pasch2:
/-- If B is between A and C, A is on L and B is off it, then B and C are
on the same side of L: a straight line that leaves L at A does not cross it
again. (Pasch 2) -/
axiom pasch2 (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : ¬ OnLine B L) : SameSide B C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.pasch3:
/-- A straight line through a point between A and C separates them. (Pasch 3) -/
axiom pasch3 (h : Between A B C) (hB : OnLine B L) : ¬ SameSide A C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.pasch4:
/-- If two different straight lines L and M meet at B, and A and C are points
of M, different from each other and from B, that are not on the same side of
L, then B is between A and C. (Pasch 4) -/
axiom pasch4 (hLM : L ≠ M) (hBL : OnLine B L) (hBM : OnLine B M) (hAM : OnLine A M)
    (hCM : OnLine C M) (hAC : A ≠ C) (hAB : A ≠ B) (hCB : C ≠ B) (h : ¬ SameSide A C L) :
    Between A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.same_side_refl:
/-- A point off a straight line is on the same side of it as itself. (Same side 1) -/
axiom same_side_refl (h : ¬ OnLine A L) : SameSide A A L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.same_side_symm:
/-- If A is on the same side of a straight line as B, then B is on the same side
as A. (Same side 2) -/
axiom same_side_symm (h : SameSide A B L) : SameSide B A L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.same_side_trans:
/-- Two points on the same side of a straight line as a third point are on the same
side as each other. (Same side 4) -/
axiom same_side_trans (h₁ : SameSide A B L) (h₂ : SameSide A C L) : SameSide B C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.bca:
/-- The triangle ABC, named from B, as BCA. -/
theorem Triangle.bca (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle B C A
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.cab:
/-- The triangle ABC, named from C, as CAB. -/
theorem Triangle.cab (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle C A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.cba:
/-- The triangle ABC, named the other way round, as CBA. -/
theorem Triangle.cba (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₁₂:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₁₂ (h : Triangle A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₁₃:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₁₃ (h : Triangle A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₂₃:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₂₃ (h : Triangle A B C) : B ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.of_line:
/-- Two different points of a straight line, and a third point off it, make a
triangle. -/
theorem Triangle.of_line {P Q R : Point} (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L) (hPQ : P ≠ Q)
    (hR : ¬ OnLine R L) : Triangle P Q R
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.off_line:
/-- In the triangle ABC, the corner C is off every straight line through A
and B. -/
theorem Triangle.off_line (h : Triangle A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    ¬ OnLine C L
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_onRay_left:
/-- One arm traced through another point of its ray: if B' is on the ray from A
through B, the angle B'AC is the angle BAC. (System E, Diagram-angle 4) -/
theorem angle_onRay_left {B' : Point} (hB : OnRay B' A B) (hCA : C ≠ A) :
    ∠ B' A C = ∠ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.exists_between_nearer:
/-- A chance point, but not too far out. If P is nearer to O than C is, and Q
lies beyond P as seen from O (or O is P itself), there is a point F between
P and Q that is nearer to O than C is, too. Euclid takes a point "at random" on
a straight line and in the next breath needs it near enough (I.5, I.9). A circle about
O through C keeps it in: P is inside that circle; if Q is not outside it, any
point between P and Q will do; if Q is outside, take a point between P and the
place X where PQ leaves the circle (Intersections 4). Either way F lies between
O and a point no farther from O than C is, Q or X, so OF is the less, as
the part is less than the whole. The order of the points does it, not System E's
Circle 2, which contains III.2; so I.5 and I.9 do not rest on that rule. -/
theorem exists_between_nearer {O P Q C : Point} (hPQ : P ≠ Q)
    (hO : O = P ∨ Between O P Q) (h : ‖O P‖ < ‖O C‖) :
    ∃ F : Point, Between P F Q ∧ ‖O F‖ < ‖O C‖
helper_signatures.Elements.exists_oppositeSidesOf:
/-- "Let a point be taken at random on the other side of the straight line AB"
(I.12): if P is off the straight line AB, there is a point on the other side
of it from P, which may be chosen different from any points already in the
figure. (System E, Points 6) -/
theorem exists_oppositeSidesOf (hP : Triangle A B P) (avoid : List Point) :
    ∃ Q : Point, OppositeSidesOf Q P A B ∧ Q ∉ avoid
helper_signatures.Elements.len_pos:
/-- A finite straight line with different ends has some length. -/
theorem len_pos (h : A ≠ B) : 0 < ‖A B‖
helper_signatures.Elements.onRay_of_angle_eq:
/-- On one side of a straight line, only one ray from a point of it makes a given
angle with it. If P and F are on the same side of the straight line DE, and
the angle EDP is equal to the angle EDF, then P lies on the ray from D
through F.

Otherwise either P would lie within the angle EDF, or F within the angle
EDP (System E, Triple incidence 2 says which), and either way an angle would be
a part of an angle equal to it (Diagram-angle 1 and 2, with C.N. 5). Pasch 3
puts P on F's side of D rather than behind it. -/
theorem onRay_of_angle_eq {D E F P : Point} (hPF : SameSideOf P F D E)
    (h : ∠ E D P = ∠ E D F) : OnRay P D F
helper_signatures.Elements.same_side_of_opposite_sides:
/-- A straight line has only two sides: two points, each on the other side of the
straight line L from C, are on the same side of L as each other. (System E,
Same side 5) -/
theorem same_side_of_opposite_sides {C D E : Point} (h₁ : OppositeSides C D L)
    (h₂ : OppositeSides C E L) : SameSide D E L

I.1.enunciation: On a given finite straight line to construct an equilateral triangle.

I.3.enunciation: Given two unequal straight lines, to cut off from the greater a straight line equal to the less.

I.5.enunciation: In isosceles triangles the angles at the base are equal to one another, and, if the equal straight lines be produced further, the angles under the base will be equal to one another.

I.7.enunciation: Given two straight lines constructed on a straight line (from its extremities) and meeting in a point, there cannot be constructed on the same straight line (from its extremities), and on the same side of it, two other straight lines meeting in another point and equal to the former two respectively, namely each to that which has the same extremity with it.

I.8.enunciation: If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have also the base equal to the base, they will also have the angles equal which are contained by the equal straight lines.

state.commentary:
Euclid builds the equilateral triangle on DE by I.1, though Heath gives no reference for it here. On which side? "Euclid does not say, in his description of the construction, that the equilateral triangle should be constructed on the side of DE opposite to A; he leaves this to be inferred from his figure" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 264). Proclus even provides for a reader who "could not recognise the existence of any space below DE": he builds on A's side, and the vertex may then fall on A, above A or below it (Heath, vol. 1, p. 264). We grant that space by a rule of System E (Points 6), which gives a point beyond DE from A, and our I.1 builds on that point's side.

Proclus also imagined an objector for whom F might fall on an arm of the angle BAC, or outside it (Heath, vol. 1, p. 265). Our proof has to be that objector, because I.10 will want AF within the angle. Were F on AB, the angles under the base of I.5 would put it on AC as well: "Here then is the second case in which, in Proclus' view, the second part of I. 5 is useful for refuting objections" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 265). Were AF to cross DE beyond D or E, I.7 would make D and E one point. So AF crosses DE between them, and falls within the angle.

Proclus stresses the word "rectilineal", for "it is difficult to say whether it is possible to bisect the so-called *horn-like* angle" between a circle and a straight line touching it (Heath, vol. 1, p. 265), the angle that III.16 meets. Here too he gives "his valuable historical note about the *trisection* of any acute angle, which (as well as the division of an angle in any given ratio) requires resort to other curves than circles" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 265): the conchoid of Nicomedes, the quadratrix of Hippias, the spiral of Archimedes. In 1837 Pierre Wantzel proved that straight lines and circles alone cannot trisect every angle.

**The modern way.** Put A at the origin, with unit vectors $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ along AB and AC. Their sum $\mathbf{u} + \mathbf{v}$, the diagonal of the rhombus on them, points along the bisector, as the diagonal AF of Euclid's kite ADFE does. Read as complex numbers $u$ and $v$, the argument of $u + v$ is the average of theirs, taken less than $\pi$ apart.
state.heath_proof:
Let the angle BAC be the given rectilineal angle.

It is then required to bisect it.

Let a point D be taken at random on AB;

let AE be cut off from AC equal to AD; [I. 3]

let DE be joined, and on DE let the equilateral triangle DEF be constructed;

let AF be joined.

I say that the angle BAC has been bisected by the straight line AF.

For, since AD is equal to AE,

and AF is common,

the two sides DA, AF are equal to the two sides EA, AF respectively.

And the base DF is equal to the base EF;

therefore the angle DAF is equal to the angle EAF. [I. 8]

Therefore the given rectilineal angle BAC has been bisected by the straight line AF.

Q. E. F.
state.lean_proof:
/-- To bisect a given rectilineal angle. -/
theorem Prop9 {A B C : Point} (hBAC : Triangle B A C) :
    ∃ F : Point, SameSideOf F C A B ∧ SameSideOf F B A C ∧
      ∠ B A F = ∠ F A C ∧ ∠ B A F + ∠ F A C = ∠ B A C := by
  -- Let the angle BAC be the given rectilineal angle.
  have hAB : A ≠ B := hBAC.ne₁₂.symm
  have hAC : A ≠ C := hBAC.ne₂₃
  obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B hAB
  obtain ⟨AC, hA_AC, hC_AC⟩ := Postulate1 A C hAC
  have hC_AB : ¬ OnLine C AB := hBAC.off_line hB_AB hA_AB
  -- It is then required to bisect it.
  -- Let a point D be taken at random on AB;
  /- At random, but not too far out, since AD is about to be cut off from AC: D is
     taken nearer to A than C is (`exists_between_nearer` in Book Zero, with a
     circle about A through C). -/
  have hAA_AC : ‖A A‖ < ‖A C‖ := by
    rw [len_self]
    exact len_pos hAC
  obtain ⟨D, hADB, hAD_AC⟩ := exists_between_nearer hAB (Or.inl rfl) hAA_AC
  have hAD : A ≠ D := ne_of_between hADB
  have hD_AB : OnLine D AB := on_line_of_between_ends hADB hA_AB hB_AB
  -- let AE be cut off from AC equal to AD; [I. 3]
  obtain ⟨E, hAEC, hAE_AD⟩ := Prop3 hAD hAD_AC
  have hAE : A ≠ E := ne_of_between hAEC
  have hE_AC : OnLine E AC := on_line_of_between_ends hAEC hA_AC hC_AC
  -- let DE be joined, and on DE let the equilateral triangle DEF be constructed;
  /- E is off AB, or C would be on it; so ADE is a triangle. The equilateral triangle
     goes on the side of DE away from A, which Euclid leaves to his figure: we take a
     point Q on that side (System E, Points 6) and ask I.1 for Q's side. -/
  have hE_AB : ¬ OnLine E AB := fun h => hC_AB (on_line_of_between hAEC hA_AB h)
  have hADE : Triangle A D E := Triangle.of_line hA_AB hD_AB hAD hE_AB
  have hDE : D ≠ E := hADE.ne₂₃
  obtain ⟨Q, hQA, -⟩ := exists_oppositeSidesOf hADE.bca []
  obtain ⟨F, ⟨-, -, hEF_FD⟩, hside⟩ := Prop1 D E hDE Q
  have hFA : OppositeSidesOf F A D E := (hside hQA.triangle).trans_opposite hQA
  -- let AF be joined.
  /- Joined, AF falls within the angle BAC. That is Proclus' objector answered: AF
     crosses DE between D and E (`Prop9.crossing`, by I.5 and I.7), and from there F is
     on C's side of AB and on B's side of AC (`Prop9.side`). -/
  have hFD_FE : ‖F D‖ = ‖F E‖ := hEF_FD.symm.trans (len_symm E F)
  obtain ⟨M, hAMF, hDME⟩ := Prop9.crossing hBAC hADB hAEC hAE_AD.symm hFD_FE hFA
  have hFC : SameSideOf F C A B := Prop9.side hBAC hADB hAEC hDME hAMF
  have hFB : SameSideOf F B A C := Prop9.side hBAC.cba hAEC hADB (between_symm hDME) hAMF
  have hF_AB : ¬ OnLine F AB := hFC.triangle.off_line hA_AB hB_AB
  have hF_AC : ¬ OnLine F AC := hFB.triangle.off_line hA_AC hC_AC
  have hAF : A ≠ F := fun h => hF_AB (h ▸ hA_AB)
  -- I say that the angle BAC has been bisected by the straight line AF.
  -- For, since AD is equal to AE,
  have hAD_AE : ‖A D‖ = ‖A E‖ := hAE_AD.symm
  -- and AF is common,
  have hAF_AF : ‖A F‖ = ‖A F‖ := rfl
  -- the two sides DA, AF are equal to the two sides EA, AF respectively.
  -- And the base DF is equal to the base EF;
  have hDF_EF : ‖D F‖ = ‖E F‖ := (len_symm D F).trans hEF_FD.symm
  -- therefore the angle DAF is equal to the angle EAF. [I. 8]
  /- ADF and AEF are triangles, since F is off AB and off AC. -/
  have hADF : Triangle A D F := Triangle.of_line hA_AB hD_AB hAD hF_AB
  have hAEF : Triangle A E F := Triangle.of_line hA_AC hE_AC hAE hF_AC
  have hDAF_EAF : ∠ D A F = ∠ E A F := Prop8 hADF hAEF hAD_AE hAF_AF hDF_EF
  -- Therefore the given rectilineal angle BAC has been bisected by the straight line AF.
  /- The angle DAF is the angle BAF, since D lies on AB, and the angle EAF is the angle
     CAF, that is, FAC, since E lies on AC (an angle depends only on its rays). And
     since F lies within the angle BAC, that angle is made up of BAF and FAC
     (System E, Diagram-angle 2). -/
  have hbisect : ∠ B A F = ∠ F A C := by
    rw [← angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between hADB) hAF.symm, hDAF_EAF,
      angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between hAEC) hAF.symm, angle_symm hAC.symm hAF.symm]
  have hAB_AC : AB ≠ AC := fun h => hC_AB (h ▸ hC_AC)
  have hwhole : ∠ B A C = ∠ B A F + ∠ F A C :=
    angle_add_of_inside hA_AB hA_AC hB_AB hC_AC hAB hAC hF_AB hF_AC hAB_AC
      (same_side_symm (hFB.2 AC hA_AC hC_AC)) (same_side_symm (hFC.2 AB hA_AB hB_AB))
  exact ⟨F, hFC, hFB, hbisect, hwhole.symm⟩
  -- Q. E. F.

statement.note: The angle is given as the triangle BAC, its arms not in one straight line, as Definition 8 asks; the bisector AF is proved to fall within it.

state.lean_proof:
/-- To bisect a given finite straight line. -/
theorem Prop10 {A B : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) :
    ∃ D : Point, Between A D B ∧ ‖A D‖ = ‖D B‖ := by
  -- Let AB be the given finite straight line.
  /- Our proof names the straight line itself, to say later that D is on it
     and C is off it. -/
  obtain ⟨L, hA_L, hB_L⟩ := Postulate1 A B hAB
  -- Thus it is required to bisect the finite straight line AB.
  -- Let the equilateral triangle ABC be constructed on it, [I. 1]
  /- No side of AB matters here, so I.1 is given a point of AB itself, A,
     as the point whose side the triangle is to be on. -/
  obtain ⟨C, ⟨hABC, hAB_BC, hBC_CA⟩, -⟩ := Prop1 A B hAB A
  have hC_L : ¬ OnLine C L := hABC.off_line hA_L hB_L
  -- and let the angle ACB be bisected by the straight line CD; [I. 9]
  /- I.9 bisects the angle ACB by a straight line CF, with F within the
     angle: on B's side of CA and on A's side of CB. Euclid's D is the
     point where that straight line meets AB. He draws it there without a
     word; it is the crossbar (Book Zero, `crossbar`) that makes the bisector,
     falling within the angle, cross the base between A and B. -/
  obtain ⟨F, hF_CA, hF_CB, hACF_FCB, -⟩ := Prop9 hABC.acb
  obtain ⟨D, hADB, hD_CF⟩ := crossbar hF_CA hF_CB
  have hD_L : OnLine D L := on_line_of_between_ends hADB hA_L hB_L
  have hDC : D ≠ C := hD_CF.2.1
  -- I say that the straight line AB has been bisected at the point D.
  -- For, since AC is equal to CB,
  have hAC_CB : ‖A C‖ = ‖C B‖ :=
    (len_symm A C).trans (hBC_CA.symm.trans (len_symm B C))
  -- and CD is common,
  have hCD : ‖C D‖ = ‖C D‖ := rfl
  -- the two sides AC, CD are equal to the two sides BC, CD respectively;
  have hCA_CB : ‖C A‖ = ‖C B‖ := (len_symm C A).trans hAC_CB
  -- and the angle ACD is equal to the angle BCD;
  /- The angles ACD and BCD are the halves ACF and FCB that I.9 made equal,
     since D is on the ray from C through F (`angle_onRay_right`,
     `angle_onRay_left`); the second is then read the other way round. -/
  have hACD_BCD : ∠ A C D = ∠ B C D := by
    rw [angle_onRay_right hD_CF hABC.ne₁₃, hACF_FCB,
      ← angle_onRay_left hD_CF hABC.ne₂₃, angle_symm hDC hABC.ne₂₃]
  -- therefore the base AD is equal to the base BD. [I. 4]
  /- The two triangles are CAD and CBD: D is on AB, and C is off it. -/
  have hCAD : Triangle C A D := (Triangle.of_line hA_L hD_L (ne_of_between hADB) hC_L).cab
  have hCBD : Triangle C B D :=
    (Triangle.of_line hB_L hD_L (ne_of_between (between_symm hADB)) hC_L).cab
  have hAD_BD : ‖A D‖ = ‖B D‖ := (Prop4 hCAD hCBD hCA_CB hCD hACD_BCD).1
  -- Therefore the given finite straight line AB has been bisected at D.
  exact ⟨D, hADB, hAD_BD.trans (len_symm B D)⟩
  -- Q. E. F.

Does every proposition called by the proof unit in `lean_proof` do work towards its conclusion or a substantive intermediate step of Euclid's argument? Also check for artificial hypothesis uses. Judge this unit's uses of the supplied helper signatures; helper bodies are outside this question. Heath's sentences stand as `--` lines and `cited` gives exact enunciations. In Lean, `have h : T := p` proves T by p and calls the result h; `obtain ⟨…⟩ := p` takes p apart into named pieces; `rw [h34, h37, …]` rewrites the goal by the equalities named. state.commentary:
Euclid bisects the angle ACB by the straight line CD and at once treats D as a point of AB, between A and B. Our I.9 hands back a bisector that falls within the angle, for just this use, and [Book Zero](../../Elements/Figure)'s [`crossbar`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean), the crossbar theorem of the geometry books that follow David Hilbert, finds D: the bisector's straight line separates A from B, so it crosses AB, and Pasch's rules put the crossing between them, on the ray from C along the bisector. The rest of the proof is Euclid's.

Apollonius, Proclus reports, "bisected a straight line AB by a construction like that of I. 1" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 268): two circles about A and B with radius AB meet at C and D, and CD, joined, bisects the angle ACB by I.8 and then AB by I.4. It is the construction taught with ruler and compass today. Heath's complaint is one of method. Instead of assuming the bisection of the angle, done already in I.9, Apollonius "unnecessarily does over again what has been done before, which is open to objection from a theoretical point of view" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 268). We take Euclid's way, and cite I.9; under I.11 Heath finds a kinder word for Apollonius.

Can every line be halved? Proclus "warns us against being moved by this proposition to conclude that geometers assumed, as a preliminary hypothesis, that a line is not made up of indivisible parts" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 268), for a line of an odd number of indivisibles could not be halved at all. Following Geminus, Proclus answers that geometers assumed only that a continuous magnitude is divisible. "But *infinite* divisibility was not assumed by them" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 268): they proved it, in showing that some magnitudes are incommensurable. He adds that I.10 may serve to refute the indivisible lines of Xenocrates. Our I.10 assumes nothing of the kind: its D is simply where two straight lines cross.
state.heath_proof:
Let AB be the given finite straight line.

Thus it is required to bisect the finite straight line AB.

Let the equilateral triangle ABC be constructed on it, [I. 1]

and let the angle ACB be bisected by the straight line CD; [I. 9]

I say that the straight line AB has been bisected at the point D.

For, since AC is equal to CB,

and CD is common,

the two sides AC, CD are equal to the two sides BC, CD respectively;

and the angle ACD is equal to the angle BCD;

therefore the base AD is equal to the base BD. [I. 4]

Therefore the given finite straight line AB has been bisected at D.

Q. E. F.

/-- To bisect a given finite straight line. -/
theorem Prop10 {A B : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) :
    ∃ D : Point, Between A D B ∧ ‖A D‖ = ‖D B‖ := by
  -- Let AB be the given finite straight line.
  /- Our proof names the straight line itself, to say later that D is on it
     and C is off it. -/
  obtain ⟨L, hA_L, hB_L⟩ := Postulate1 A B hAB
  -- Thus it is required to bisect the finite straight line AB.
  -- Let the equilateral triangle ABC be constructed on it, [I. 1]
  /- No side of AB matters here, so I.1 is given a point of AB itself, A,
     as the point whose side the triangle is to be on. -/
  obtain ⟨C, ⟨hABC, hAB_BC, hBC_CA⟩, -⟩ := Prop1 A B hAB A
  have hC_L : ¬ OnLine C L := hABC.off_line hA_L hB_L
  -- and let the angle ACB be bisected by the straight line CD; [I. 9]
  /- I.9 bisects the angle ACB by a straight line CF, with F within the
     angle: on B's side of CA and on A's side of CB. Euclid's D is the
     point where that straight line meets AB. He draws it there without a
     word; it is the crossbar (Book Zero, `crossbar`) that makes the bisector,
     falling within the angle, cross the base between A and B. -/
  obtain ⟨F, hF_CA, hF_CB, hACF_FCB, -⟩ := Prop9 hABC.acb
  obtain ⟨D, hADB, hD_CF⟩ := crossbar hF_CA hF_CB
  have hD_L : OnLine D L := on_line_of_between_ends hADB hA_L hB_L
  have hDC : D ≠ C := hD_CF.2.1
  -- I say that the straight line AB has been bisected at the point D.
  -- For, since AC is equal to CB,
  have hAC_CB : ‖A C‖ = ‖C B‖ :=
    (len_symm A C).trans (hBC_CA.symm.trans (len_symm B C))
  -- and CD is common,
  have hCD : ‖C D‖ = ‖C D‖ := rfl
  -- the two sides AC, CD are equal to the two sides BC, CD respectively;
  have hCA_CB : ‖C A‖ = ‖C B‖ := (len_symm C A).trans hAC_CB
  -- and the angle ACD is equal to the angle BCD;
  /- The angles ACD and BCD are the halves ACF and FCB that I.9 made equal,
     since D is on the ray from C through F (`angle_onRay_right`,
     `angle_onRay_left`); the second is then read the other way round. -/
  have hACD_BCD : ∠ A C D = ∠ B C D := by
    rw [angle_onRay_right hD_CF hABC.ne₁₃, hACF_FCB,
      ← angle_onRay_left hD_CF hABC.ne₂₃, angle_symm hDC hABC.ne₂₃]
  -- therefore the base AD is equal to the base BD. [I. 4]
  /- The two triangles are CAD and CBD: D is on AB, and C is off it. -/
  have hCAD : Triangle C A D := (Triangle.of_line hA_L hD_L (ne_of_between hADB) hC_L).cab
  have hCBD : Triangle C B D :=
    (Triangle.of_line hB_L hD_L (ne_of_between (between_symm hADB)) hC_L).cab
  have hAD_BD : ‖A D‖ = ‖B D‖ := (Prop4 hCAD hCBD hCA_CB hCD hACD_BCD).1
  -- Therefore the given finite straight line AB has been bisected at D.
  exact ⟨D, hADB, hAD_BD.trans (len_symm B D)⟩
  -- Q. E. F.

Thus it is required to bisect the finite straight line AB.

Let the equilateral triangle ABC be constructed on it, [I. 1]

and let the angle ACB be bisected by the straight line CD; [I. 9]

I say that the straight line AB has been bisected at the point D.

For, since AC is equal to CB,

and CD is common,

the two sides AC, CD are equal to the two sides BC, CD respectively;

and the angle ACD is equal to the angle BCD;

therefore the base AD is equal to the base BD. [I. 4]

Therefore the given finite straight line AB has been bisected at D.

Q. E. F.

state.heath_proof:
Let AB be the given straight line, and C the given point on it.

Thus it is required to draw from the point C a straight line at right angles to the straight line AB.

Let a point D be taken at random on AC;

let CE be made equal to CD; [I. 3]

on DE let the equilateral triangle FDE be constructed, [I. 1]

and let FC be joined;

I say that the straight line FC has been drawn at right angles to the given straight line AB from C the given point on it.

For, since DC is equal to CE,

and CF is common,

the two sides DC, CF are equal to the two sides EC, CF respectively;

and the base DF is equal to the base FE;

therefore the angle DCF is equal to the angle ECF; [I. 8]

and they are adjacent angles.

But, when a straight line set up on a straight line makes the adjacent angles equal to one another, each of the equal angles is right; [Def. 10]

therefore each of the angles DCF, FCE is right.

Therefore the straight line CF has been drawn at right angles to the given straight line AB from the given point C on it.

Q. E. F.

definitions.Kind:

inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:

opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Point:

opaque Point : Type
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:

noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.rightAngle:

it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/

Thus it is required to draw from the point C a straight line at right angles to the straight line AB.

Let a point D be taken at random on AC;

let CE be made equal to CD; [I. 3]

on DE let the equilateral triangle FDE be constructed, [I. 1]

and let FC be joined;

For, since DC is equal to CE,

and CF is common,

and the base DF is equal to the base FE;

state.lean_proof:
/-- To draw a straight line at right angles to a given straight line from a given point on it. -/
theorem Prop11 {A B C Q : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hC : Collinear A B C) (hQ : ¬ Collinear A B Q) :
    ∃ F : Point, SameSideOf F Q A B ∧ ∀ P : Point, Collinear A B P → P ≠ C → ∠ P C F = ∟ := by
  -- Let AB be the given straight line, and C the given point on it.
  /- Our proof names the straight line AB (Post. 1), with C on it and Q off it. -/
  obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B hAB
  have on_AB : ∀ {P : Point}, Collinear A B P → OnLine P AB := by
    rintro P ⟨M, hA_M, hB_M, hP_M⟩
    rw [line_unique hAB hA_AB hB_AB hA_M hB_M]
    exact hP_M
  have hC_AB : OnLine C AB := on_AB hC
  have hQ_AB : ¬ OnLine Q AB := fun h => hQ ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB, h⟩
  -- Thus it is required to draw from the point C a straight line at right angles to the
  -- straight line AB.
  -- Let a point D be taken at random on AC;
  /- Euclid's figure has C between A and B. In Lean C may be any point of the
     straight line AB, even A itself, and then there is no AC to take D on: B
     will do. All the proof needs is a point D of AB other than C (System E,
     Points 3). -/
  obtain ⟨D, hD_AB, hDC⟩ : ∃ D : Point, OnLine D AB ∧ D ≠ C := by
    by_cases hCA : C = A
    · exact ⟨B, hB_AB, by rw [hCA]; exact hAB.symm⟩
    · obtain ⟨D, hD_AB, hADC, -⟩ := exists_point_between hA_AB hC_AB (Ne.symm hCA) []
      exact ⟨D, hD_AB, (ne_of_between (between_symm hADC)).symm⟩
  -- let CE be made equal to CD; [I. 3]
  /- CE is cut off from DC produced beyond C, far enough for I.3 to have a
     greater straight line to cut it from (`produce_longer` in Book Zero). So C
     lies between D and E (`between_cut`): the figure's D, C, E in a row. -/
  obtain ⟨G, hDCG, hCD_CG⟩ := produce_longer hDC hDC.symm
  obtain ⟨E, hCEG, hCE_CD⟩ := Prop3 hDC.symm hCD_CG
  have hDCE : Between D C E := between_cut hDCG hCEG
  have hE_AB : OnLine E AB := on_line_of_between hDCE hD_AB hC_AB
  have hDE : D ≠ E := ne_of_between_ends hDCE
  have hEC : E ≠ C := ne_of_between (between_symm hDCE)
  -- on DE let the equilateral triangle FDE be constructed, [I. 1]
  /- On Q's side of DE, which is Q's side of AB: one straight line passes
     through D and E. -/
  obtain ⟨F, ⟨-, hDE_EF, hEF_FD⟩, hFQ⟩ := Prop1 D E hDE Q
  have hF_Q : SameSide F Q AB :=
    (hFQ (Triangle.of_line hD_AB hE_AB hDE hQ_AB)).sameSide hD_AB hE_AB
  have hF_AB : ¬ OnLine F AB := not_on_line_of_same_side hF_Q
  -- and let FC be joined;
  have hFC : F ≠ C := fun h => hF_AB (h ▸ hC_AB)
  obtain ⟨FC, -, -⟩ := Postulate1 F C hFC
  -- I say that the straight line FC has been drawn at right angles to the given straight line
  -- AB from C the given point on it.
  -- For, since DC is equal to CE,
  have hDC_CE : ‖D C‖ = ‖C E‖ := (len_symm D C).trans hCE_CD.symm
  -- and CF is common,
  have hCF : ‖C F‖ = ‖C F‖ := rfl
  -- the two sides DC, CF are equal to the two sides EC, CF respectively;
  have hCD_CE : ‖C D‖ = ‖C E‖ := (len_symm C D).trans hDC_CE
  -- and the base DF is equal to the base FE;
  have hDF_EF : ‖D F‖ = ‖E F‖ := (len_symm D F).trans (hEF_FD.symm)
  -- therefore the angle DCF is equal to the angle ECF; [I. 8]
  have hCDF : Triangle C D F := Triangle.of_line hC_AB hD_AB hDC.symm hF_AB
  have hCEF : Triangle C E F := Triangle.of_line hC_AB hE_AB hEC.symm hF_AB
  have hDCF_ECF : ∠ D C F = ∠ E C F := Prop8 hCDF hCEF hCD_CE hCF hDF_EF
  -- and they are adjacent angles.
  /- Adjacent: C lies between D and E, and F is off the straight line DE. -/
  have hDCF_FCE : ∠ D C F = ∠ F C E := hDCF_ECF.trans (angle_symm hEC hFC)
  -- But, when a straight line set up on a straight line makes the adjacent angles equal to one
  -- another, each of the equal angles is right; [Def. 10]
  /- Definition 10 says what a right angle is, and Postulate 4 that every right
     angle is the right angle `∟`. -/
  have hDCF_right : IsRightAngle D C F := ⟨E, hDCE, hCDF.bac, hDCF_FCE⟩
  have hECF_right : IsRightAngle E C F :=
    ⟨D, between_symm hDCE, hCEF.bac, hDCF_ECF.symm.trans (angle_symm hDC hFC)⟩
  -- therefore each of the angles DCF, FCE is right.
  have hDCF : ∠ D C F = ∟ := Postulate4 hDCF_right
  have hFCE : ∠ F C E = ∟ := (angle_symm hFC hEC).trans (Postulate4 hECF_right)
  -- Therefore the straight line CF has been drawn at right angles to the given straight line
  -- AB from the given point C on it.
  /- Every other point P of AB lies on the ray from C through D, or on the ray
     from C through E (`OnRay.cases_of_between`), and the angle PCF is the angle
     DCF or the angle ECF (`angle_onRay_left`; both are in Book Zero). -/
  refine ⟨F, SameSideOf.of_line hAB hA_AB hB_AB hF_Q, fun P hP hPC => ?_⟩
  rcases OnRay.cases_of_between hDCE hD_AB hE_AB (on_AB hP) hPC with hPD | hPE
  · rw [angle_onRay_left hPD hFC]
    exact hDCF
  · rw [angle_onRay_left hPE hFC, angle_symm hEC hFC]
    exact hFCE
  -- Q. E. F.

helper_signatures.Elements.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop1:
/-- On a given finite straight line to construct an equilateral triangle. -/
theorem Prop1 (A B : Point) (hAB : A ≠ B) (P : Point) :
    ∃ C : Point, Equilateral A B C ∧ (¬ Collinear A B P → SameSideOf C P A B)
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop3:
/-- Given two unequal straight lines, to cut off from the greater a straight line equal to the
less. -/
theorem Prop3 {A B C₁ C₂ : Point} (hC : C₁ ≠ C₂) (h : ‖C₁ C₂‖ < ‖A B‖) :
    ∃ E : Point, Between A E B ∧ ‖A E‖ = ‖C₁ C₂‖
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop8:
/-- If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have also the base
equal to the base, they will also have the angles equal which are contained by the equal
straight lines. -/
theorem Prop8 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖D F‖) (hBC : ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖) :
    ∠ B A C = ∠ E D F
helper_signatures.Elements.Collinear:
/-- `A`, `B`, `C` lie on one straight line. -/
def Collinear (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.IsRightAngle:
/-- **Definition 10.** "When a straight line set up on a straight line makes the
adjacent angles equal to one another, each of the equal angles is right."

The angle `ABC` is right when, continuing `AB` beyond `B` to some `D`, the
straight line `BC` makes the adjacent angles `ABC` and `CBD` equal. The clause
`¬ Collinear A B C` rules out a degenerate `C`, such as `C` at `B`, where both
angles would be nothing and Postulate 4 would be false. -/
def IsRightAngle (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.cases_of_between:
/-- A point cuts a straight line into two rays. If A lies between B and C, every
other point P of the straight line BC lies on the ray from A through B or on
the ray from A through C: either A is not between P and B, or it is, and
then it cannot also be between P and C (System E, Between 7). -/
theorem OnRay.cases_of_between {A B C P : Point} {L : Line} (h : Between B A C)
    (hB : OnLine B L) (hC : OnLine C L) (hP : OnLine P L) (hPA : P ≠ A) :
    OnRay P A B ∨ OnRay P A C
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.symm:
/-- P is on the ray from A through B exactly when B is on the ray from A
through P: they are one and the same ray. -/
theorem OnRay.symm (h : OnRay P A B) : OnRay B A P
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate1:
/-- **Postulate 1.** To draw a straight line from any point to any point. -/
axiom Postulate1 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate4:
/-- **Postulate 4.** That all right angles are equal to one another: every right
angle (in the sense of Definition 10) is equal to `∟`. -/
axiom Postulate4 {A B C : Point} (h : IsRightAngle A B C) : ∠ A B C = ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf:
/-- `P` and `Q` lie on the same side of the straight line `AB`. -/
def SameSideOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.of_line:
/-- Two points on the same side of a straight line L through A and B are on
the same side of the straight line AB, however that line is named: two points
fix one straight line. -/
theorem SameSideOf.of_line (hAB : A ≠ B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (h : SameSide P Q L) : SameSideOf P Q A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.sameSide:
/-- Two points on the same side of the straight line AB are on the same side of
any straight line drawn through A and B. -/
theorem SameSideOf.sameSide (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    SameSide P Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the same side of AB as Q, then Q is on the same side as P. -/
theorem SameSideOf.symm (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.trans:
/-- Points on the same side as a third are on the same side as each other. -/
theorem SameSideOf.trans (h₁ : SameSideOf P Q A B) (h₂ : SameSideOf Q R A B) :
    SameSideOf P R A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.angle_symm:
/-- The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4) -/
axiom angle_symm (hAB : A ≠ B) (hCB : C ≠ B) : ∠ A B C = ∠ C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_symm:
/-- If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1) -/
axiom between_symm (h : Between A B C) : Between C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.exists_point_between:
/-- Let a point be taken between B and C. (Points 3) -/
axiom exists_point_between {B C : Point} {L : Line} (hB : OnLine B L) (hC : OnLine C L)
    (hBC : B ≠ C) (avoid : List Point) : ∃ A : Point, OnLine A L ∧ Between B A C ∧ A ∉ avoid
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.len_symm:
/-- The straight line AB is the straight line BA. (Metric 3) -/
axiom len_symm (A B : Point) : ‖A B‖ = ‖B A‖
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.line_unique:
/-- Two points determine a straight line. (Generalities 1) -/
axiom line_unique (hAB : A ≠ B) (hAL : OnLine A L) (hBL : OnLine B L) (hAM : OnLine A M)
    (hBM : OnLine B M) : L = M
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between:
/-- A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between_ends:
/-- The ends of a finite straight line differ. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.not_on_line_of_same_side:
/-- Points on one side of a straight line are not on it. (Same side 3) -/
axiom not_on_line_of_same_side (h : SameSide A B L) : ¬ OnLine A L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between:
/-- A straight line through A and B, with B between A and C, passes
through C. (Between 2) -/
axiom on_line_of_between (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    OnLine C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.bac:
/-- The triangle ABC, named the other way round, as BAC. -/
theorem Triangle.bac (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.of_line:
/-- Two different points of a straight line, and a third point off it, make a
triangle. -/
theorem Triangle.of_line {P Q R : Point} (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L) (hPQ : P ≠ Q)
    (hR : ¬ OnLine R L) : Triangle P Q R
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_onRay_left:
/-- One arm traced through another point of its ray: if B' is on the ray from A
through B, the angle B'AC is the angle BAC. (System E, Diagram-angle 4) -/
theorem angle_onRay_left {B' : Point} (hB : OnRay B' A B) (hCA : C ≠ A) :
    ∠ B' A C = ∠ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.between_cut:
/-- Cutting off beyond a point: if B is between A and C, and D between B and
C, then B is between A and D. This is the step after "let CE be made equal to
CD [I. 3]" on a straight line produced: what is cut off from BC still lies beyond
B. -/
theorem between_cut (h₁ : Between A B C) (h₂ : Between B D C) : Between A B D
helper_signatures.Elements.produce_longer:
/-- Room to cut off. A finite straight line AB can be produced beyond B further
than a given straight line BC from B. Postulate 2 produces a straight line but
never says how far, and I.3 cuts off only from a *greater* straight line; so Euclid's
"let CE be made equal to CD [I. 3]", on a straight line produced, needs this first
(I.11, I.16, I.20, I.22). Describe the circle with centre B and distance BC
[Post. 3]; the straight line AB, produced beyond the centre, cuts it at some Y
(System E, Intersections 5); and BY, produced a little further still to X
[Post. 2], is greater than BY, that is, than BC [Def. 15, C.N. 5]. -/
theorem produce_longer (hAB : A ≠ B) (hBC : B ≠ C) :
    ∃ X : Point, Between A B X ∧ ‖B C‖ < ‖B X‖

I.1.enunciation: On a given finite straight line to construct an equilateral triangle.

I.3.enunciation: Given two unequal straight lines, to cut off from the greater a straight line equal to the less.

I.8.enunciation: If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have also the base equal to the base, they will also have the angles equal which are contained by the equal straight lines.

definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Equilateral:
/-- **Definition 20.** "Of trilateral figures, an equilateral triangle is that
which has its three sides equal." -/
def Equilateral (A B C : Point) : Prop :=

definitions.IsRightAngle:
/-- **Definition 10.** "When a straight line set up on a straight line makes the
adjacent angles equal to one another, each of the equal angles is right."

straight line `BC` makes the adjacent angles `ABC` and `CBD` equal. The clause

angles would be nothing and Postulate 4 would be false. -/

  ∃ D : Point, Between A B D ∧ ¬ Collinear A B C ∧ ∠ A B C = ∠ C B D

state.commentary:
Heath's reference for "let CE be made equal to CD" is I.3. But I.3 cuts a less straight line off a greater, and nothing says CB is longer than CD; C might even be B. Postulate 2 produces a straight line "continuously", but never says how far. So [Book Zero](../../Elements/Figure)'s [`produce_longer`](../../Elements/Figure/Lines.lean) makes room: DC, produced beyond C, cuts the circle about C through D again, and a little further on it is greater than CD. I.3 cuts CE off it, and C then lies between D and E, which is what makes the angles at C adjacent. Euclid then stops at "each of the angles DCF, FCE is right", with Definition I.10: an angle equal to its neighbour is right. Our statement goes one step further, to `∟`, the one size that all right angles share, and here Postulate 4, that all right angles are equal, does its first work. From now on two right angles are `∟ + ∟` in the Lean, whoever drew them, which answers Isaac Todhunter's worry under I.14.

Augustus De Morgan remarks that this proposition, which is "to bisect the angle made by a straight line and its continuation", should be a particular case of I.9. Heath agrees, with a doubt: "This is certainly worth noting, though I doubt the advantage of rearranging the propositions in consequence" (vol. 1, pp. 269–270). For us the rearrangement is not on offer, since our I.9 asks for a triangle BAC, and a straight line with its continuation makes none. Apollonius drew circles "in the manner of I. 1 meeting at F" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 270), and so had to prove DF equal to FE all over again. Heath, sterner under I.10, is generous here: "While however the substitution of Apollonius' constructions for I. 10 and 11 would show faulty arrangement in a theoretical treatise like Euclid's, they are entirely suitable for what we call *practical* geometry" (vol. 1, p. 270).

**The modern way.** Put C at the origin and let $\mathbf{u}$ point along AB, so that D and E are $-\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{u}$. F, at $\mathbf{f}$, is as far from one as from the other, $|\mathbf{f} + \mathbf{u}|^2 = |\mathbf{f} - \mathbf{u}|^2$, and that simplifies to $\mathbf{f} \cdot \mathbf{u} = 0$: CF is at right angles to AB. In the complex plane it is shorter still, since multiplying by $i$ turns a direction through $\pi/2$.
state.heath_proof:
Let AB be the given straight line, and C the given point on it.

Thus it is required to draw from the point C a straight line at right angles to the straight line AB.

Let a point D be taken at random on AC;

let CE be made equal to CD; [I. 3]

on DE let the equilateral triangle FDE be constructed, [I. 1]

and let FC be joined;

I say that the straight line FC has been drawn at right angles to the given straight line AB from C the given point on it.

For, since DC is equal to CE,

and CF is common,

the two sides DC, CF are equal to the two sides EC, CF respectively;

and the base DF is equal to the base FE;

therefore the angle DCF is equal to the angle ECF; [I. 8]

and they are adjacent angles.

But, when a straight line set up on a straight line makes the adjacent angles equal to one another, each of the equal angles is right; [Def. 10]

therefore each of the angles DCF, FCE is right.

Therefore the straight line CF has been drawn at right angles to the given straight line AB from the given point C on it.

Q. E. F.
state.lean_proof:
/-- To draw a straight line at right angles to a given straight line from a given point on it. -/
theorem Prop11 {A B C Q : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hC : Collinear A B C) (hQ : ¬ Collinear A B Q) :
    ∃ F : Point, SameSideOf F Q A B ∧ ∀ P : Point, Collinear A B P → P ≠ C → ∠ P C F = ∟ := by
  -- Let AB be the given straight line, and C the given point on it.
  /- Our proof names the straight line AB (Post. 1), with C on it and Q off it. -/
  obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B hAB
  have on_AB : ∀ {P : Point}, Collinear A B P → OnLine P AB := by
    rintro P ⟨M, hA_M, hB_M, hP_M⟩
    rw [line_unique hAB hA_AB hB_AB hA_M hB_M]
    exact hP_M
  have hC_AB : OnLine C AB := on_AB hC
  have hQ_AB : ¬ OnLine Q AB := fun h => hQ ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB, h⟩
  -- Thus it is required to draw from the point C a straight line at right angles to the
  -- straight line AB.
  -- Let a point D be taken at random on AC;
  /- Euclid's figure has C between A and B. In Lean C may be any point of the
     straight line AB, even A itself, and then there is no AC to take D on: B
     will do. All the proof needs is a point D of AB other than C (System E,
     Points 3). -/
  obtain ⟨D, hD_AB, hDC⟩ : ∃ D : Point, OnLine D AB ∧ D ≠ C := by
    by_cases hCA : C = A
    · exact ⟨B, hB_AB, by rw [hCA]; exact hAB.symm⟩
    · obtain ⟨D, hD_AB, hADC, -⟩ := exists_point_between hA_AB hC_AB (Ne.symm hCA) []
      exact ⟨D, hD_AB, (ne_of_between (between_symm hADC)).symm⟩
  -- let CE be made equal to CD; [I. 3]
  /- CE is cut off from DC produced beyond C, far enough for I.3 to have a
     greater straight line to cut it from (`produce_longer` in Book Zero). So C
     lies between D and E (`between_cut`): the figure's D, C, E in a row. -/
  obtain ⟨G, hDCG, hCD_CG⟩ := produce_longer hDC hDC.symm
  obtain ⟨E, hCEG, hCE_CD⟩ := Prop3 hDC.symm hCD_CG
  have hDCE : Between D C E := between_cut hDCG hCEG
  have hE_AB : OnLine E AB := on_line_of_between hDCE hD_AB hC_AB
  have hDE : D ≠ E := ne_of_between_ends hDCE
  have hEC : E ≠ C := ne_of_between (between_symm hDCE)
  -- on DE let the equilateral triangle FDE be constructed, [I. 1]
  /- On Q's side of DE, which is Q's side of AB: one straight line passes
     through D and E. -/
  obtain ⟨F, ⟨-, hDE_EF, hEF_FD⟩, hFQ⟩ := Prop1 D E hDE Q
  have hF_Q : SameSide F Q AB :=
    (hFQ (Triangle.of_line hD_AB hE_AB hDE hQ_AB)).sameSide hD_AB hE_AB
  have hF_AB : ¬ OnLine F AB := not_on_line_of_same_side hF_Q
  -- and let FC be joined;
  have hFC : F ≠ C := fun h => hF_AB (h ▸ hC_AB)
  obtain ⟨FC, -, -⟩ := Postulate1 F C hFC
  -- I say that the straight line FC has been drawn at right angles to the given straight line
  -- AB from C the given point on it.
  -- For, since DC is equal to CE,
  have hDC_CE : ‖D C‖ = ‖C E‖ := (len_symm D C).trans hCE_CD.symm
  -- and CF is common,
  have hCF : ‖C F‖ = ‖C F‖ := rfl
  -- the two sides DC, CF are equal to the two sides EC, CF respectively;
  have hCD_CE : ‖C D‖ = ‖C E‖ := (len_symm C D).trans hDC_CE
  -- and the base DF is equal to the base FE;
  have hDF_EF : ‖D F‖ = ‖E F‖ := (len_symm D F).trans (hEF_FD.symm)
  -- therefore the angle DCF is equal to the angle ECF; [I. 8]
  have hCDF : Triangle C D F := Triangle.of_line hC_AB hD_AB hDC.symm hF_AB
  have hCEF : Triangle C E F := Triangle.of_line hC_AB hE_AB hEC.symm hF_AB
  have hDCF_ECF : ∠ D C F = ∠ E C F := Prop8 hCDF hCEF hCD_CE hCF hDF_EF
  -- and they are adjacent angles.
  /- Adjacent: C lies between D and E, and F is off the straight line DE. -/
  have hDCF_FCE : ∠ D C F = ∠ F C E := hDCF_ECF.trans (angle_symm hEC hFC)
  -- But, when a straight line set up on a straight line makes the adjacent angles equal to one
  -- another, each of the equal angles is right; [Def. 10]
  /- Definition 10 says what a right angle is, and Postulate 4 that every right
     angle is the right angle `∟`. -/
  have hDCF_right : IsRightAngle D C F := ⟨E, hDCE, hCDF.bac, hDCF_FCE⟩
  have hECF_right : IsRightAngle E C F :=
    ⟨D, between_symm hDCE, hCEF.bac, hDCF_ECF.symm.trans (angle_symm hDC hFC)⟩
  -- therefore each of the angles DCF, FCE is right.
  have hDCF : ∠ D C F = ∟ := Postulate4 hDCF_right
  have hFCE : ∠ F C E = ∟ := (angle_symm hFC hEC).trans (Postulate4 hECF_right)
  -- Therefore the straight line CF has been drawn at right angles to the given straight line
  -- AB from the given point C on it.
  /- Every other point P of AB lies on the ray from C through D, or on the ray
     from C through E (`OnRay.cases_of_between`), and the angle PCF is the angle
     DCF or the angle ECF (`angle_onRay_left`; both are in Book Zero). -/
  refine ⟨F, SameSideOf.of_line hAB hA_AB hB_AB hF_Q, fun P hP hPC => ?_⟩
  rcases OnRay.cases_of_between hDCE hD_AB hE_AB (on_AB hP) hPC with hPD | hPE
  · rw [angle_onRay_left hPD hFC]
    exact hDCF
  · rw [angle_onRay_left hPE hFC, angle_symm hEC hFC]
    exact hFCE
  -- Q. E. F.

statement.note: Proved for any point C of AB, with F on the side of a given point Q; the angle PCF is the right angle ∟ for every point P of AB other than C.

/-- Room to cut off. A finite straight line AB can be produced beyond B further
than a given straight line BC from B. Postulate 2 produces a straight line but
never says how far, and I.3 cuts off only from a *greater* straight line; so Euclid's
"let CE be made equal to CD [I. 3]", on a straight line produced, needs this first
(I.11, I.16, I.20, I.22). Describe the circle with centre B and distance BC
[Post. 3]; the straight line AB, produced beyond the centre, cuts it at some Y
(System E, Intersections 5); and BY, produced a little further still to X
[Post. 2], is greater than BY, that is, than BC [Def. 15, C.N. 5]. -/
theorem produce_longer (hAB : A ≠ B) (hBC : B ≠ C) :
    ∃ X : Point, Between A B X ∧ ‖B C‖ < ‖B X‖

Let AB be the given infinite straight line, and C the given point which is not on it;

Let AB be the given infinite straight line, and C the given point which is not on it;

For let a point D be taken at random on the other side of the straight line AB, and with centre C and distance CD let the circle EFG be described; [Post. 3]

let the straight line EG be bisected at H, [I. 10]

and let the straight lines CG, CH, CE be joined. [Post. 1]

I say that CH has been drawn perpendicular to the given infinite straight line AB from the given point C which is not on it.

For, since GH is equal to HE,

and HC is common,

the two sides GH, HC are equal to the two sides EH, HC respectively;

and the base CG is equal to the base CE;

therefore the angle CHG is equal to the angle EHC. [I. 8]

And they are adjacent angles.

But, when a straight line set up on a straight line makes the adjacent angles equal to one another, each of the equal angles is right, and the straight line standing on the other is called a perpendicular to that on which it stands. [Def. 10]

Therefore CH has been drawn perpendicular to the given infinite straight line AB from the given point C which is not on it.

Q. E. F.
state.lean_proof:
/-- To a given infinite straight line, from a given point which is not on it, to draw a
perpendicular straight line. -/
theorem Prop12 {A B C : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hC : ¬ Collinear A B C) :
    ∃ H : Point, Collinear A B H ∧ ∀ P : Point, Collinear A B P → P ≠ H → ∠ C H P = ∟ := by
  -- Let AB be the given infinite straight line, and C the given point which is not on it;
  /- The infinite straight line AB is the straight line through A and B
     (Postulate 1), and C is off it, so ABC is a triangle. -/
  obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B hAB
  have hABC : Triangle A B C := hC
  have hC_AB : ¬ OnLine C AB := hABC.off_line hA_AB hB_AB
  -- thus it is required to draw to the given infinite straight line AB, from the given point C
  -- which is not on it, a perpendicular straight line.
  -- For let a point D be taken at random on the other side of the straight line AB, and with
  -- centre C and distance CD let the circle EFG be described; [Post. 3]
  /- "At random on the other side" is System E, Points 6, which Book Zero gives
     as `exists_oppositeSidesOf`. D is not C, since C is not on the other
     side of AB from itself. -/
  obtain ⟨D, hDC, -⟩ := exists_oppositeSidesOf hABC []
  have hCD_AB : OppositeSides C D AB := hDC.symm.oppositeSides hA_AB hB_AB
  have hCD : C ≠ D := by
    rintro rfl
    exact hCD_AB.2.2 (same_side_refl hC_AB)
  obtain ⟨EFG, hC_EFG, hD_EFG⟩ := Postulate3 C D hCD
  /- The circle's centre C is inside it and D is on it, on the other side of AB,
     so AB cuts the circle in two points (System E, Intersection 2). Heath's figure
     calls them G and E. F, the third letter of the circle's name, is only a name:
     the proof never uses it. -/
  obtain ⟨E, G, hEG, hE_AB, hE_EFG, hG_AB, hG_EFG⟩ :=
    line_meets_circle_of_opposite_sides (Or.inl (centre_inside hC_EFG)) (Or.inr hD_EFG) hCD_AB
  -- let the straight line EG be bisected at H, [I. 10]
  obtain ⟨H, hEHG, hEH_HG⟩ := Prop10 hEG
  have hH_AB : OnLine H AB := on_line_of_between_ends hEHG hE_AB hG_AB
  have hHG : H ≠ G := (ne_of_between (between_symm hEHG)).symm
  have hHE : H ≠ E := (ne_of_between hEHG).symm
  have hCH : C ≠ H := fun e => hC_AB (e ▸ hH_AB)
  -- and let the straight lines CG, CH, CE be joined. [Post. 1]
  /- Our proof uses only the points; the straight lines are drawn for the eye.
     It does use the two triangles they make with HG and HE: C is off AB, and H,
     G, E are on it. -/
  have hHGC : Triangle H G C := Triangle.of_line hH_AB hG_AB hHG hC_AB
  have hHEC : Triangle H E C := Triangle.of_line hH_AB hE_AB hHE hC_AB
  -- I say that CH has been drawn perpendicular to the given infinite straight line AB from the
  -- given point C which is not on it.
  -- For, since GH is equal to HE,
  have hGH_HE : ‖G H‖ = ‖H E‖ := (len_symm G H).trans (hEH_HG.symm.trans (len_symm E H))
  -- and HC is common,
  have hHC : ‖H C‖ = ‖H C‖ := rfl
  -- the two sides GH, HC are equal to the two sides EH, HC respectively;
  have hHG_HE : ‖H G‖ = ‖H E‖ := (len_symm H G).trans hGH_HE
  -- and the base CG is equal to the base CE;
  /- Both are radii of the circle EFG. [Def. 15] -/
  have hCG_CE : ‖C G‖ = ‖C E‖ := Definition15 hC_EFG hG_EFG hE_EFG
  -- therefore the angle CHG is equal to the angle EHC. [I. 8]
  have hGHC_EHC : ∠ G H C = ∠ E H C :=
    Prop8 hHGC hHEC hHG_HE hHC ((len_symm G C).trans (hCG_CE.trans (len_symm C E)))
  have hCHG_EHC : ∠ C H G = ∠ E H C := (angle_symm hCH hHG.symm).trans hGHC_EHC
  -- And they are adjacent angles.
  /- Adjacent: H lies between G and E, so HG and HE make one straight line. -/
  have hGHE : Between G H E := between_symm hEHG
  -- But, when a straight line set up on a straight line makes the adjacent angles equal to one
  -- another, each of the equal angles is right, and the straight line standing on the other is
  -- called a perpendicular to that on which it stands. [Def. 10]
  /- Definition 10 is `IsRightAngle`: the angle GHC is right, its neighbour being
     CHE, and so is EHC, its neighbour being CHG. Each is then the right angle `∟`
     (Post. 4, as in I.11). -/
  have hGHC_right : IsRightAngle G H C :=
    ⟨E, hGHE, hHGC.bac, hGHC_EHC.trans (angle_symm hHE.symm hCH)⟩
  have hEHC_right : IsRightAngle E H C :=
    ⟨G, hEHG, hHEC.bac, hGHC_EHC.symm.trans (angle_symm hHG.symm hCH)⟩
  have hCHG : ∠ C H G = ∟ := (angle_symm hCH hHG.symm).trans (Postulate4 hGHC_right)
  have hCHE : ∠ C H E = ∟ := (angle_symm hCH hHE.symm).trans (Postulate4 hEHC_right)
  -- Therefore CH has been drawn perpendicular to the given infinite straight line AB from the
  -- given point C which is not on it.
  /- Perpendicular to the whole infinite straight line: any other point P of AB
     lies on the ray from H through G or on the ray from H through E
     (`OnRay.cases_of_between`), and then the angle CHP is the angle CHG or the
     angle CHE (`angle_onRay_right`). -/
  refine ⟨H, ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB, hH_AB⟩, fun P hP hPH => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨L, hA_L, hB_L, hP_L⟩ := hP
  rw [line_unique hAB hA_L hB_L hA_AB hB_AB] at hP_L
  rcases OnRay.cases_of_between hGHE hG_AB hE_AB hP_L hPH with hPG | hPE
  · exact (angle_onRay_right hPG hCH).trans hCHG
  · exact (angle_onRay_right hPE hCH).trans hCHE
  -- Q. E. F.

helper_signatures.Elements.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop10:
/-- To bisect a given finite straight line. -/
theorem Prop10 {A B : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) :
    ∃ D : Point, Between A D B ∧ ‖A D‖ = ‖D B‖
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop8:
/-- If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have also the base
equal to the base, they will also have the angles equal which are contained by the equal
straight lines. -/
theorem Prop8 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖D F‖) (hBC : ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖) :
    ∠ B A C = ∠ E D F
helper_signatures.Elements.Collinear:
/-- `A`, `B`, `C` lie on one straight line. -/
def Collinear (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Definition15:
/-- **Definition 15.** "A circle is a plane figure contained by one line such
that all the straight lines falling upon it from one point among those lying
within the figure are equal to one another."

So any two radii of a circle are equal. -/
axiom Definition15 {A B C : Point} {α : Circle} (hA : Centre A α) (hB : OnCircle B α)
    (hC : OnCircle C α) : ‖A B‖ = ‖A C‖
helper_signatures.Elements.IsRightAngle:
/-- **Definition 10.** "When a straight line set up on a straight line makes the
adjacent angles equal to one another, each of the equal angles is right."

The angle `ABC` is right when, continuing `AB` beyond `B` to some `D`, the
straight line `BC` makes the adjacent angles `ABC` and `CBD` equal. The clause
`¬ Collinear A B C` rules out a degenerate `C`, such as `C` at `B`, where both
angles would be nothing and Postulate 4 would be false. -/
def IsRightAngle (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.cases_of_between:
/-- A point cuts a straight line into two rays. If A lies between B and C, every
other point P of the straight line BC lies on the ray from A through B or on
the ray from A through C: either A is not between P and B, or it is, and
then it cannot also be between P and C (System E, Between 7). -/
theorem OnRay.cases_of_between {A B C P : Point} {L : Line} (h : Between B A C)
    (hB : OnLine B L) (hC : OnLine C L) (hP : OnLine P L) (hPA : P ≠ A) :
    OnRay P A B ∨ OnRay P A C
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.symm:
/-- P is on the ray from A through B exactly when B is on the ray from A
through P: they are one and the same ray. -/
theorem OnRay.symm (h : OnRay P A B) : OnRay B A P
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSides:
/-- `A` and `B` lie on opposite sides of the straight line `L`. -/
def OppositeSides (A B : Point) (L : Line) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.oppositeSides:
/-- Two points on opposite sides of the straight line AB are on opposite sides of
any straight line drawn through A and B. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.oppositeSides (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) (hA : OnLine A L)
    (hB : OnLine B L) : OppositeSides P Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the other side of AB from Q, then Q is on the other side
from P. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.symm (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : OppositeSidesOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate1:
/-- **Postulate 1.** To draw a straight line from any point to any point. -/
axiom Postulate1 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate3:
/-- **Postulate 3.** To describe a circle with any centre and distance.

Like Euclid's own compass, this one "collapses": the circle has centre `A` and
passes through `B`. Carrying a distance from one place to another is
Proposition 2's job. -/
axiom Postulate3 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ α : Circle, Centre A α ∧ OnCircle B α
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate4:
/-- **Postulate 4.** That all right angles are equal to one another: every right
angle (in the sense of Definition 10) is equal to `∟`. -/
axiom Postulate4 {A B C : Point} (h : IsRightAngle A B C) : ∠ A B C = ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.angle_symm:
/-- The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4) -/
axiom angle_symm (hAB : A ≠ B) (hCB : C ≠ B) : ∠ A B C = ∠ C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_symm:
/-- If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1) -/
axiom between_symm (h : Between A B C) : Between C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.centre_inside:
/-- The centre of a circle is inside it. (Generalities 3) -/
axiom centre_inside (hA : Centre A α) : InsideCircle A α
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.len_symm:
/-- The straight line AB is the straight line BA. (Metric 3) -/
axiom len_symm (A B : Point) : ‖A B‖ = ‖B A‖
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.line_meets_circle_of_oppo:
/-- A straight line separating two points of a circle cuts the circle.
(Intersection 2) -/
axiom line_meets_circle_of_opposite_sides (hA : InsideCircle A α ∨ OnCircle A α)
    (hB : InsideCircle B α ∨ OnCircle B α) (h : OppositeSides A B L) : LineMeetsCircle L α
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.line_unique:
/-- Two points determine a straight line. (Generalities 1) -/
axiom line_unique (hAB : A ≠ B) (hAL : OnLine A L) (hBL : OnLine B L) (hAM : OnLine A M)
    (hBM : OnLine B M) : L = M
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between:
/-- A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between_ends:
/-- A straight line through A and C passes through every point between them.
(Between 3) -/
axiom on_line_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hC : OnLine C L) :
    OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.same_side_refl:
/-- A point off a straight line is on the same side of it as itself. (Same side 1) -/
axiom same_side_refl (h : ¬ OnLine A L) : SameSide A A L
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.bac:
/-- The triangle ABC, named the other way round, as BAC. -/
theorem Triangle.bac (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.of_line:
/-- Two different points of a straight line, and a third point off it, make a
triangle. -/
theorem Triangle.of_line {P Q R : Point} (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L) (hPQ : P ≠ Q)
    (hR : ¬ OnLine R L) : Triangle P Q R
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.off_line:
/-- In the triangle ABC, the corner C is off every straight line through A
and B. -/
theorem Triangle.off_line (h : Triangle A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    ¬ OnLine C L
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_onRay_right:
/-- The other arm traced through another point of its ray: if C' is on the ray
from A through C, the angle BAC' is the angle BAC. (System E,
Diagram-angle 4) -/
theorem angle_onRay_right {C' : Point} (hC : OnRay C' A C) (hBA : B ≠ A) :
    ∠ B A C' = ∠ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.exists_oppositeSidesOf:
/-- "Let a point be taken at random on the other side of the straight line AB"
(I.12): if P is off the straight line AB, there is a point on the other side
of it from P, which may be chosen different from any points already in the
figure. (System E, Points 6) -/
theorem exists_oppositeSidesOf (hP : Triangle A B P) (avoid : List Point) :
    ∃ Q : Point, OppositeSidesOf Q P A B ∧ Q ∉ avoid
