question.instructions:
Does every proposition called by the proof unit in `lean_proof` do work towards its conclusion or a substantive intermediate step of Euclid's argument? Also check for artificial hypothesis uses. Judge this unit's uses of the supplied helper signatures; helper bodies are outside this question. Heath's sentences stand as `--` lines and `cited` gives exact enunciations. In Lean, `have h : T := p` proves T by p and calls the result h; `obtain ⟨…⟩ := p` takes p apart into named pieces; `rw [h34, h37, …]` rewrites the goal by the equalities named. Follow uses through helper calls and tactics as well as explicit names. An anonymous binding or an unused hypothesis alone does not establish a defect. If both defects occur, choose `a dummy citation`.

docs/FORMALIZATION.md, section 5:
A checked intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid is legitimate, even if the
  final proof term could do without it.

criteria.cannot tell: What is given here is not enough to decide.
criteria.all do work: Every proposition call supports a later step or the conclusion, or establishes a substantive intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid. No hypothesis is mentioned merely to look used. With no proposition calls the citation part alone is vacuous; hypothesis use must still be inspected.
criteria.a dummy citation: Some proposition call does no substantive work: its result neither supports the argument nor establishes a substantive intermediate fact, and merely supplies a citation while the step is done another way.
criteria.an artificial hypothesis use: No dummy citation is established, but a hypothesis is mentioned only so that it looks used, and does no substantive work.

state.commentary:
Two straight lines from B and C to a point D within the triangle are together less than BA, AC, yet contain a greater angle than BAC. Euclid gets both halves from one stroke, BD drawn through to E: then I.20 twice for the lengths, and I.16 twice for the angles. Of the enunciation's "meeting", Heath notes: "The word 'meeting' is not in the Greek … but it is necessary in English to indicate that they *meet*" (vol. 1, p. 289).

"The editors generally call attention to the fact that the lines drawn within the triangle in this proposition must be drawn, as the enunciation says, from the *ends* of the side; otherwise it is not necessary that their sum should be less than that of the remaining sides of the triangle" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 290). Proclus shows it simply: in a right-angled triangle ABC, take a point D on BC, cut off DE from DA equal to AB, and bisect AE at F; then CF, FD together are greater than CA, AB (Heath, vol. 1, p. 290). Pappus goes further, with propositions "selected apparently from 'the so-called paradoxes' of one Erycinus" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 290): in any triangle but an equilateral one, or an isosceles one with base less than one of the other sides, two straight lines on the base and within the triangle, not drawn from its ends, can together equal the other two sides, and "the lines may be so constructed that their sum will bear to the sum of the two sides of the triangle any ratio less than 2 : 1" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 290).

Our statement reads "within the triangle" as three facts, D on the inner side of each side, and our proof needs all three: two bring BD, drawn on, to meet AC, as in I.10, and the third keeps D short of E. Euclid's figure shows the three together.

**The modern way.** The points $P$ with $|P - \mathrm{B}| + |P - \mathrm{C}| = \mathrm{AB} + \mathrm{AC}$ make an ellipse with foci B and C through A, and the triangle lies within it, where the sum is less. The points on A's side of BC that see BC under the angle BAC lie on one part of the circumference of the circle through A, B and C (III.21), and from within that circle, as D is, BC is seen under a greater angle.
state.heath_proof:
On BC, one of the sides of the triangle ABC, from its extremities B, C, let the two straight lines BD, DC be constructed meeting within the triangle;

I say that BD, DC are less than the remaining two sides of the triangle BA, AC, but contain an angle BDC greater than the angle BAC.

For let BD be drawn through to E.

Then, since in any triangle two sides are greater than the remaining one, [I. 20]

therefore, in the triangle ABE, the two sides AB, AE are greater than BE.

Let EC be added to each;

therefore BA, AC are greater than BE, EC.

Again, since, in the triangle CED,

the two sides CE, ED are greater than CD,

let DB be added to each;

therefore CE, EB are greater than CD, DB.

But BA, AC were proved greater than BE, EC;

therefore BA, AC are much greater than BD, DC.

Again, since in any triangle the exterior angle is greater than the interior and opposite angle, [I. 16]

therefore, in the triangle CDE,

the exterior angle BDC is greater than the angle CED.

For the same reason, moreover, in the triangle ABE also,

the exterior angle CEB is greater than the angle BAC.

But the angle BDC was proved greater than the angle CEB;

therefore the angle BDC is much greater than the angle BAC.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- If on one of the sides of a triangle, from its extremities, there be constructed two straight
lines meeting within the triangle, the straight lines so constructed will be less than the
remaining two sides of the triangle, but will contain a greater angle. -/
theorem Prop21 {A B C D : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hD : InsideTriangle D A B C) :
    ‖B D‖ + ‖D C‖ < ‖B A‖ + ‖A C‖ ∧ ∠ B A C < ∠ B D C := by
  -- On BC, one of the sides of the triangle ABC, from its extremities B, C, let the two
  -- straight lines BD, DC be constructed meeting within the triangle;
  /- The statement hands us D within the triangle. -/
  -- I say that BD, DC are less than the remaining two sides of the triangle BA, AC, but
  -- contain an angle BDC greater than the angle BAC.
  -- For let BD be drawn through to E.
  /- BD produced crosses AC at E, beyond D: see `Prop21.through`. -/
  obtain ⟨E, hBDE, hAEC⟩ := Prop21.through hD
  /- B is off AC, since ABC is a triangle. And C is off BE: else BE would be BC,
     and D, which is on A's side of BC, would lie on it. -/
  obtain ⟨AC, hA_AC, hC_AC⟩ := Postulate1 A C hABC.ne₁₃
  have hE_AC : OnLine E AC := on_line_of_between_ends hAEC hA_AC hC_AC
  have hB_AC : ¬ OnLine B AC := hABC.acb.off_line hA_AC hC_AC
  have hA_E : A ≠ E := ne_of_between hAEC
  have hB_E : B ≠ E := ne_of_between_ends hBDE
  have hD_E : D ≠ E := (ne_of_between (between_symm hBDE)).symm
  obtain ⟨BE, hB_BE, hE_BE⟩ := Postulate1 B E hB_E
  have hD_BE : OnLine D BE := on_line_of_between_ends hBDE hB_BE hE_BE
  have hC_BE : ¬ OnLine C BE := by
    intro hC
    obtain ⟨BC, hB_BC, hC_BC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hABC.ne₂₃
    have hD_BC : ¬ OnLine D BC := not_on_line_of_same_side (hD.1.sameSide hB_BC hC_BC)
    exact hD_BC (line_unique hABC.ne₂₃ hB_BE hC hB_BC hC_BC ▸ hD_BE)
  /- So ABE and CED are triangles. -/
  have hAEB : Triangle A E B := Triangle.of_line hA_AC hE_AC hA_E hB_AC
  have hEDC : Triangle E D C := Triangle.of_line hE_BE hD_BE hD_E.symm hC_BE
  -- Then, since in any triangle two sides are greater than the remaining one, [I. 20]
  -- therefore, in the triangle ABE, the two sides AB, AE are greater than BE.
  have hBE_lt : ‖B E‖ < ‖B A‖ + ‖A E‖ := (Prop20 hAEB.acb).1
  -- Let EC be added to each;
  have hBEC : ‖B E‖ + ‖E C‖ < ‖B A‖ + ‖A E‖ + ‖E C‖ := add_lt_add_right ‖E C‖ hBE_lt
  -- therefore BA, AC are greater than BE, EC.
  /- AE and EC together make up AC, since E lies between A and C. -/
  have hBA_AC : ‖B E‖ + ‖E C‖ < ‖B A‖ + ‖A C‖ := by
    rw [← len_add_of_between hAEC, ← add_assoc]
    exact hBEC
  -- Again, since, in the triangle CED,
  have hCED : Triangle C E D := hEDC.cab
  -- the two sides CE, ED are greater than CD,
  have hCD_lt : ‖C D‖ < ‖C E‖ + ‖E D‖ := (Prop20 hCED).2.1
  -- let DB be added to each;
  have hCDB : ‖C D‖ + ‖D B‖ < ‖C E‖ + ‖E D‖ + ‖D B‖ := add_lt_add_right ‖D B‖ hCD_lt
  -- therefore CE, EB are greater than CD, DB.
  /- ED and DB together make up EB, since D lies between E and B. -/
  have hCE_EB : ‖C D‖ + ‖D B‖ < ‖C E‖ + ‖E B‖ := by
    rw [← len_add_of_between (between_symm hBDE), ← add_assoc]
    exact hCDB
  -- But BA, AC were proved greater than BE, EC;
  have : ‖B E‖ + ‖E C‖ < ‖B A‖ + ‖A C‖ := hBA_AC
  -- therefore BA, AC are much greater than BD, DC.
  /- BD, DC are CD, DB taken the other way round, and BE, EC are CE, EB. -/
  have hsides : ‖B D‖ + ‖D C‖ < ‖B A‖ + ‖A C‖ := by
    have h₁ : ‖B D‖ + ‖D C‖ = ‖C D‖ + ‖D B‖ := by
      rw [add_comm, len_symm D C, len_symm B D]
    have h₂ : ‖C E‖ + ‖E B‖ = ‖B E‖ + ‖E C‖ := by
      rw [add_comm, len_symm C E, len_symm E B]
    rw [h₁]
    exact lt_trans (h₂ ▸ hCE_EB) hBA_AC
  -- Again, since in any triangle the exterior angle is greater than the interior and opposite
  -- angle, [I. 16]
  -- therefore, in the triangle CDE,
  /- In the triangle CDE the side ED is produced to B. -/
  have hEDB : Between E D B := between_symm hBDE
  -- the exterior angle BDC is greater than the angle CED.
  /- I.16 reads both angles the other way round, as DEC and CDB. -/
  have hCED_BDC : ∠ C E D < ∠ B D C := by
    rw [angle_symm (ne_of_between (between_symm hAEC)) hD_E,
      angle_symm (ne_of_between hBDE) hEDC.ne₂₃.symm]
    exact (Prop16 hCED hEDB).1
  -- For the same reason, moreover, in the triangle ABE also,
  /- In the triangle ABE the side AE is produced to C. -/
  have hBAE : Triangle B A E := hAEB.cab
  -- the exterior angle CEB is greater than the angle BAC.
  /- I.16 gives the angle EAB less than BEC. The angle EAB, read the other way
     round, is BAE, and that is the angle BAC, since E lies on the ray from A
     through C. -/
  have hBAC_CEB : ∠ B A C < ∠ C E B := by
    rw [← angle_onRay_right (OnRay.of_between hAEC) hABC.ne₁₂.symm,
      angle_symm hABC.ne₁₂.symm hA_E.symm,
      angle_symm (ne_of_between (between_symm hAEC)) hB_E]
    exact (Prop16 hBAE hAEC).1
  -- But the angle BDC was proved greater than the angle CEB;
  /- The angle CED is the angle CEB, since D lies on the ray from E through
     B. -/
  have hCEB_BDC : ∠ C E B < ∠ B D C := by
    rw [← angle_onRay_right (OnRay.of_between hEDB) (ne_of_between (between_symm hAEC))]
    exact hCED_BDC
  -- therefore the angle BDC is much greater than the angle BAC.
  have hangle : ∠ B A C < ∠ B D C := lt_trans hBAC_CEB hCEB_BDC
  -- Therefore etc.
  exact ⟨hsides, hangle⟩
  -- Q. E. D.

On BC, one of the sides of the triangle ABC, from its extremities B, C, let the two straight lines BD, DC be constructed meeting within the triangle;

I say that BD, DC are less than the remaining two sides of the triangle BA, AC, but contain an angle BDC greater than the angle BAC.

For let BD be drawn through to E.

Then, since in any triangle two sides are greater than the remaining one, [I. 20]

therefore, in the triangle ABE, the two sides AB, AE are greater than BE.

Let EC be added to each;

therefore BA, AC are greater than BE, EC.

Again, since, in the triangle CED,

the two sides CE, ED are greater than CD,

let DB be added to each;

therefore CE, EB are greater than CD, DB.

But BA, AC were proved greater than BE, EC;

therefore BA, AC are much greater than BD, DC.

Again, since in any triangle the exterior angle is greater than the interior and opposite angle, [I. 16]

therefore, in the triangle CDE,

the exterior angle BDC is greater than the angle CED.

For the same reason, moreover, in the triangle ABE also,

the exterior angle CEB is greater than the angle BAC.

But the angle BDC was proved greater than the angle CEB;

therefore the angle BDC is much greater than the angle BAC.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.

state.enunciation: Out of three straight lines, which are equal to three given straight lines, to construct a triangle: thus it is necessary that two of the straight lines taken together in any manner should be greater than the remaining one.
state.lean_proof:
/-- Out of three straight lines, which are equal to three given straight lines, to construct a
triangle: thus it is necessary that two of the straight lines taken together in any manner
should be greater than the remaining one. [I. 20] -/
theorem Prop22 {A₁ A₂ B₁ B₂ C₁ C₂ E F P : Point}
    (hAB : ‖C₁ C₂‖ < ‖A₁ A₂‖ + ‖B₁ B₂‖) (hAC : ‖B₁ B₂‖ < ‖A₁ A₂‖ + ‖C₁ C₂‖)
    (hBC : ‖A₁ A₂‖ < ‖B₁ B₂‖ + ‖C₁ C₂‖) (hFE : F ≠ E) (hP : ¬ Collinear F E P) :
    ∃ G K : Point, OnRay G F E ∧ SameSideOf K P F E ∧
      ‖K F‖ = ‖A₁ A₂‖ ∧ ‖F G‖ = ‖B₁ B₂‖ ∧ ‖G K‖ = ‖C₁ C₂‖ := by
  -- Let the three given straight lines be A, B, C, and of these let two taken together in any
  -- manner be greater than the remaining one,
  /- Straight lines, and so none of them is nothing (`Prop22.ne_zero`): each has
     two different ends, as I.3 will want. -/
  have hA : A₁ ≠ A₂ := fun e => Prop22.ne_zero hAB hAC (by rw [e]; exact len_self A₂)
  have hB : B₁ ≠ B₂ := fun e =>
    Prop22.ne_zero (by rw [add_comm]; exact hAB) hBC (by rw [e]; exact len_self B₂)
  have hC : C₁ ≠ C₂ := fun e =>
    Prop22.ne_zero (by rw [add_comm]; exact hAC) (by rw [add_comm]; exact hBC)
      (by rw [e]; exact len_self C₂)
  -- namely A, B greater than C,
  have hAB_C : ‖C₁ C₂‖ < ‖A₁ A₂‖ + ‖B₁ B₂‖ := hAB
  -- A, C greater than B,
  have hAC_B : ‖B₁ B₂‖ < ‖A₁ A₂‖ + ‖C₁ C₂‖ := hAC
  -- and B, C greater than A;
  have hBC_A : ‖A₁ A₂‖ < ‖B₁ B₂‖ + ‖C₁ C₂‖ := hBC
  -- thus it is required to construct a triangle out of straight lines equal to A, B, C.
  -- Let there be set out a straight line DE, terminated at D but of infinite length in the
  -- direction of E,
  /- The straight line DE is the straight line through the given points F and E
     [Post. 1]. Its end D is not given: it is set out behind F, at the distance A,
     in the next breath. -/
  obtain ⟨DE, hF_DE, hE_DE⟩ := Postulate1 F E hFE
  have hP_DE : ¬ OnLine P DE := fun h => hP ⟨DE, hF_DE, hE_DE, h⟩
  -- and let DF be made equal to A, FG equal to B, and GH equal to C. [I. 3]
  /- Three times I.3, each time cutting off from a straight line produced far
     enough to cut from (`Prop22.room`): FD from EF produced beyond F, FG from DF
     produced beyond F, and GH from FG produced beyond G. So D, F, G, H lie in that
     order along DE, as in Euclid's figure (`between_cut`), and G lies on the ray
     from F through E. -/
  obtain ⟨X, hEFX, hA_FX⟩ := Prop22.room hFE.symm hA
  obtain ⟨D, hFDX, hFD⟩ := Prop3 hA hA_FX
  have hDFE : Between D F E := between_symm (between_cut hEFX hFDX)
  obtain ⟨Y, hDFY, hB_FY⟩ := Prop22.room (ne_of_between hDFE) hB
  obtain ⟨G, hFGY, hFG⟩ := Prop3 hB hB_FY
  have hDFG : Between D F G := between_cut hDFY hFGY
  obtain ⟨Z, hFGZ, hC_GZ⟩ := Prop22.room (ne_of_between hFGY) hC
  obtain ⟨H, hGHZ, hGH⟩ := Prop3 hC hC_GZ
  have hFGH : Between F G H := between_cut hFGZ hGHZ
  have hD_DE : OnLine D DE := on_line_of_between (between_symm hDFE) hE_DE hF_DE
  have hG_DE : OnLine G DE := on_line_of_between hDFG hD_DE hF_DE
  have hG_ray : OnRay G F E :=
    ⟨hFE, (ne_of_between hFGY).symm, ⟨DE, hF_DE, hE_DE, hG_DE⟩,
      not_between_of_between_between hDFG hDFE⟩
  -- With centre F and distance FD let the circle DKL be described;
  obtain ⟨DKL, hF_DKL, hD_DKL⟩ := Postulate3 F D (ne_of_between hDFE).symm
  -- again, with centre G and distance GH let the circle KLH be described;
  obtain ⟨KLH, hG_KLH, hH_KLH⟩ := Postulate3 G H (ne_of_between hGHZ)
  /- Euclid takes K where the circles cut one another, without a word on why they
     should. They do, because two of A, B, C taken together in any manner are
     greater than the remaining one (`Prop22.meet`: Heath's argument, closed by
     System E, Intersection 4). They cut one another on each side of DE, the
     straight line through their centres, and K is taken on P's side (System E,
     Intersections 8). -/
  have hmeet : CirclesMeet KLH DKL :=
    Prop22.meet hFGH hF_DKL hD_DKL hG_KLH hH_KLH
      (by rw [hGH, hFD, hFG]; exact hAB_C) (by rw [hGH, hFD, hFG]; exact hAC_B)
      (by rw [hGH, hFD, hFG]; exact hBC_A)
  obtain ⟨K, hK_KLH, hK_DKL, hKP⟩ :=
    circles_meet_same_side hmeet hG_KLH hF_DKL hG_DE hF_DE hP_DE
  -- and let KF, KG be joined;
  obtain ⟨KF, -, -⟩ := Postulate1 K F (ne_of_centre_of_on hF_DKL hK_DKL)
  obtain ⟨KG, -, -⟩ := Postulate1 K G (ne_of_centre_of_on hG_KLH hK_KLH)
  -- I say that the triangle KFG has been constructed out of three straight lines equal to A,
  -- B, C.
  /- A triangle indeed: K is off DE, on P's side of it, and F and G are on it. -/
  have : Triangle K F G :=
    (Triangle.of_line hF_DE hG_DE (ne_of_between hFGY) (not_on_line_of_same_side hKP)).cab
  -- For, since the point F is the centre of the circle DKL,
  -- FD is equal to FK.
  have hFD_FK : ‖F D‖ = ‖F K‖ := Definition15 hF_DKL hD_DKL hK_DKL
  -- But FD is equal to A;
  have hFD_A : ‖F D‖ = ‖A₁ A₂‖ := hFD
  -- therefore KF is also equal to A.
  have hKF : ‖K F‖ = ‖A₁ A₂‖ := (len_symm K F).trans (hFD_FK.symm.trans hFD_A)
  -- Again, since the point G is the centre of the circle LKH,
  -- GH is equal to GK.
  have hGH_GK : ‖G H‖ = ‖G K‖ := Definition15 hG_KLH hH_KLH hK_KLH
  -- But GH is equal to C;
  have hGH_C : ‖G H‖ = ‖C₁ C₂‖ := hGH
  -- therefore KG is also equal to C.
  have hKG : ‖K G‖ = ‖C₁ C₂‖ := (len_symm K G).trans (hGH_GK.symm.trans hGH_C)
  -- And FG is also equal to B;
  have hFG_B : ‖F G‖ = ‖B₁ B₂‖ := hFG
  -- therefore the three straight lines KF, FG, GK are equal to the three straight lines A, B,
  -- C.
  have hGK : ‖G K‖ = ‖C₁ C₂‖ := (len_symm G K).trans hKG
  -- Therefore out of the three straight lines KF, FG, GK, which are equal to the three given
  -- straight lines A, B, C, the triangle KFG has been constructed.
  /- With FG along the given ray from F through E, and K on P's side of FE. -/
  exact ⟨G, K, hG_ray, SameSideOf.of_line hFE hF_DE hE_DE hKP, hKF, hFG_B, hGK⟩
  -- Q. E. F.

/-- The circles meet. Euclid takes K where the circle about F and the circle
about G cut one another, and never says why they should. Heath's own argument
(vol. 1, p. 294) is that the circle about G has a point outside the circle about
F, and a point inside it.

* H is outside: FH is FG and GH together, which is greater than FD.
* The point M where GF (produced if need be) cuts the circle about G is
  inside. GM is equal to GH. If M falls between G and F, then FM and
  GH together make FG, which is less than FD and GH together, so FM is
  less than FD. If M falls beyond F, then FM and FG together make GM,
  that is GH, which is less than FD and FG together, so again FM is less
  than FD. And if M is F, it is the centre.

Then the two circles cut one another (System E, Intersection 4, in LeanEuclid's
corrected form): this is the "Principle of Continuity" that Heath invokes here, as he
does for I.1. -/
theorem Prop22.meet {D F G H : Point} {α β : Circle} (hFGH : Between F G H)
    (hF_α : Centre F α) (hD_α : OnCircle D α) (hG_β : Centre G β) (hH_β : OnCircle H β)
    (h₁ : ‖G H‖ < ‖F D‖ + ‖F G‖) (h₂ : ‖F G‖ < ‖F D‖ + ‖G H‖)
    (h₃ : ‖F D‖ < ‖F G‖ + ‖G H‖) : CirclesMeet β α
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop22.ne_zero:
/-- None of the three given straight lines is nothing. If `a` were nothing, the
other two would each be greater than the other: `c` less than `b` (from `a`, `b`
greater than `c`) and `b` less than `c` (from `a`, `c` greater than `b`). Euclid
calls A, B, C straight lines, so for him the question never arises; in our
foundations a finite straight line is a pair of points, which may coincide, and
I.3 wants them apart. -/
theorem Prop22.ne_zero {k : Kind} {a b c : Magnitude k} (h₁ : c < a + b) (h₂ : b < a + c) :
    a ≠ 0
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop22.room:
/-- Room to cut off a given straight line. Euclid's DE is "of infinite length in
the direction of E", so that whatever is to be cut off from it, there is room.
Our `Line` is a whole straight line, with no length to cut from, and I.3 cuts off
only from a greater finite straight line; so we find a point Z on DF produced
beyond F with FZ greater than the given straight line X₁X₂. At F place a straight
line FY equal to X₁X₂ [I. 2], and produce DF beyond F further than FY
(`produce_longer`, as in I.11). -/
theorem Prop22.room {D F X₁ X₂ : Point} (hDF : D ≠ F) (hX : X₁ ≠ X₂) :
    ∃ Z : Point, Between D F Z ∧ ‖X₁ X₂‖ < ‖F Z‖
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop3:
/-- Given two unequal straight lines, to cut off from the greater a straight line equal to the
less. -/
theorem Prop3 {A B C₁ C₂ : Point} (hC : C₁ ≠ C₂) (h : ‖C₁ C₂‖ < ‖A B‖) :
    ∃ E : Point, Between A E B ∧ ‖A E‖ = ‖C₁ C₂‖
helper_signatures.Elements.Centre:
/-- `Centre A α`: the point `A` is the centre of the circle `α`. (Def. 16) -/
opaque Centre : Point → Circle → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.CirclesMeet:
/-- Two circles that cut one another (in two points). -/
def CirclesMeet (α β : Circle) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Collinear:
/-- `A`, `B`, `C` lie on one straight line. -/
def Collinear (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Definition15:
/-- **Definition 15.** "A circle is a plane figure contained by one line such
that all the straight lines falling upon it from one point among those lying
within the figure are equal to one another."

So any two radii of a circle are equal. -/
axiom Definition15 {A B C : Point} {α : Circle} (hA : Centre A α) (hB : OnCircle B α)
    (hC : OnCircle C α) : ‖A B‖ = ‖A C‖
helper_signatures.Elements.InsideCircle:
/-- `InsideCircle A α`: the point `A` lies inside the circle `α`. -/
opaque InsideCircle : Point → Circle → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
helper_signatures.Elements.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_righ:
/-- Take the same thing away from two unequal magnitudes, and the less remains the
less: if `x` and `a` together are less than `y` and `a` together, then `x` is less
than `y`. Otherwise `y` would be equal to `x` or less, and adding `a` to each would
keep it so (the laws of magnitudes, System E §3.5). -/
theorem Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_right {k : Kind} {a x y : Magnitude k} (h : x + a < y + a) :
    x < y
helper_signatures.Elements.OnCircle:
/-- `OnCircle A α`: the point `A` lies on the circumference of the circle `α`. -/
opaque OnCircle : Point → Circle → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.between_of_len_lt:
/-- Of two points on a ray, the one nearer the start lies between the start and
the other. -/
theorem OnRay.between_of_len_lt (hP : OnRay P A B) (hQ : OnRay Q A B) (h : ‖A P‖ < ‖A Q‖) :
    Between A P Q
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.eq_of_len_eq:
/-- On a ray, only one point lies at a given distance from its start: a point P
on the ray from A through B, as far from A as B is, is B itself.

This is Sir Henry Savile's argument, which Heath reports on I.4 (vol. 1,
p. 250): otherwise P falls short of B or beyond it, and either way the less
would be equal to the greater. -/
theorem OnRay.eq_of_len_eq (hP : OnRay P A B) (h : ‖A P‖ = ‖A B‖) : P = B
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.self:
/-- B itself is on the ray from A through B. -/
theorem OnRay.self (h : A ≠ B) : OnRay B A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.symm:
/-- P is on the ray from A through B exactly when B is on the ray from A
through P: they are one and the same ray. -/
theorem OnRay.symm (h : OnRay P A B) : OnRay B A P
helper_signatures.Elements.OutsideCircle:
/-- `A` lies outside the circle `α`: neither inside it nor on it. -/
def OutsideCircle (A : Point) (α : Circle) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate1:
/-- **Postulate 1.** To draw a straight line from any point to any point. -/
axiom Postulate1 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate3:
/-- **Postulate 3.** To describe a circle with any centre and distance.

Like Euclid's own compass, this one "collapses": the circle has centre `A` and
passes through `B`. Carrying a distance from one place to another is
Proposition 2's job. -/
axiom Postulate3 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ α : Circle, Centre A α ∧ OnCircle B α
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf:
/-- `P` and `Q` lie on the same side of the straight line `AB`. -/
def SameSideOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.of_line:
/-- Two points on the same side of a straight line L through A and B are on
the same side of the straight line AB, however that line is named: two points
fix one straight line. -/
theorem SameSideOf.of_line (hAB : A ≠ B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (h : SameSide P Q L) : SameSideOf P Q A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the same side of AB as Q, then Q is on the same side as P. -/
theorem SameSideOf.symm (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.trans:
/-- Points on the same side as a third are on the same side as each other. -/
theorem SameSideOf.trans (h₁ : SameSideOf P Q A B) (h₂ : SameSideOf Q R A B) :
    SameSideOf P R A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.add_comm:
/-- The order of adding does not matter. (System E §3.5) -/
axiom add_comm (a b : Magnitude k) : a + b = b + a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.add_zero:
/-- Adding nothing changes nothing. (System E §3.5) -/
axiom add_zero (a : Magnitude k) : a + 0 = a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_symm:
/-- If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1) -/
axiom between_symm (h : Between A B C) : Between C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.centre_inside:
/-- The centre of a circle is inside it. (Generalities 3) -/
axiom centre_inside (hA : Centre A α) : InsideCircle A α
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.circles_meet_of_on_inside:
/-- Two circles cut one another if the first passes through a point A inside the
second, and a point B outside the second is inside or on the first. (Intersection
4, in LeanEuclid's corrected form) -/
axiom circles_meet_of_on_inside_outside (hAα : OnCircle A α)
    (hBα : InsideCircle B α ∨ OnCircle B α) (hAβ : InsideCircle A β) (hBβ : OutsideCircle B β) :
    CirclesMeet α β
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.circles_meet_same_side:
/-- Two circles that cut one another do so on each side of the straight line
through their centres. (Intersections 8) -/
axiom circles_meet_same_side {α β : Circle} {B C D : Point} {L : Line}
    (h : CirclesMeet α β) (hC : Centre C α) (hD : Centre D β) (hCL : OnLine C L)
    (hDL : OnLine D L) (hB : ¬ OnLine B L) :
    ∃ A : Point, OnCircle A α ∧ OnCircle A β ∧ SameSide A B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.inside_of_len_lt:
/-- A point nearer the centre than the circumference is inside. (Diagram-segment 4) -/
axiom inside_of_len_lt (hA : Centre A α) (hB : OnCircle B α) (h : ‖A C‖ < ‖A B‖) :
    InsideCircle C α
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.len_add_of_between:
/-- If B is between A and C, then AB and BC together make up AC.
(Diagram-segment 1) -/
axiom len_add_of_between (h : Between A B C) : ‖A B‖ + ‖B C‖ = ‖A C‖
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.len_self:
/-- The "straight line" from a point to itself has no length. (Metric 1) -/
axiom len_self (A : Point) : ‖A A‖ = 0
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.len_symm:
/-- The straight line AB is the straight line BA. (Metric 3) -/
axiom len_symm (A B : Point) : ‖A B‖ = ‖B A‖
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.line_circle_beyond:
/-- A straight line through a point B inside a circle, produced beyond B
away from C, cuts the circle there. (Intersections 5) -/
axiom line_circle_beyond {B C : Point} {L : Line} {α : Circle}
    (hB : InsideCircle B α) (hBL : OnLine B L) (hCL : OnLine C L) (hCB : C ≠ B) :
    ∃ A : Point, OnCircle A α ∧ OnLine A L ∧ Between A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.lt_irrefl:
/-- No magnitude is less than itself. (System E §3.5) -/
axiom lt_irrefl (a : Magnitude k) : ¬ a < a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.lt_trans:
/-- What is less than the less is less still. (System E §3.5) -/
axiom lt_trans {a b c : Magnitude k} : a < b → b < c → a < c
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.lt_trichotomy:
/-- Of two magnitudes, one is less, or they are equal, or the other is less.
(System E §3.5) -/
axiom lt_trichotomy (a b : Magnitude k) : a < b ∨ a = b ∨ b < a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between:
/-- A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.not_between_of_between_be:
/-- If B is between A and C, and also between A and D, then B is not
between C and D: C and D lie on the same side of B. (Between 7) -/
axiom not_between_of_between_between (h₁ : Between A B C) (h₂ : Between A B D) :
    ¬ Between C B D
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.not_on_line_of_same_side:
/-- Points on one side of a straight line are not on it. (Same side 3) -/
axiom not_on_line_of_same_side (h : SameSide A B L) : ¬ OnLine A L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between:
/-- A straight line through A and B, with B between A and C, passes
through C. (Between 2) -/
axiom on_line_of_between (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    OnLine C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.cab:
/-- The triangle ABC, named from C, as CAB. -/
theorem Triangle.cab (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle C A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.of_line:
/-- Two different points of a straight line, and a third point off it, make a
triangle. -/
theorem Triangle.of_line {P Q R : Point} (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L) (hPQ : P ≠ Q)
    (hR : ¬ OnLine R L) : Triangle P Q R
helper_signatures.Elements.between_cut:
/-- Cutting off beyond a point: if B is between A and C, and D between B and
C, then B is between A and D. This is the step after "let CE be made equal to
CD [I. 3]" on a straight line produced: what is cut off from BC still lies beyond
B. -/
theorem between_cut (h₁ : Between A B C) (h₂ : Between B D C) : Between A B D
helper_signatures.Elements.ne_of_centre_of_on:
/-- A point on a circle is not its centre. -/
theorem ne_of_centre_of_on (hA : Centre A α) (hC : OnCircle C α) : C ≠ A
helper_signatures.Elements.ne_of_len_eq:
/-- If a finite straight line AB has the length of one with different ends,
its own ends are different. -/
theorem ne_of_len_eq (h : ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖) (hCD : C ≠ D) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.outside_of_len_gt:
/-- A point farther from the centre than the circumference is outside the
circle. -/
theorem outside_of_len_gt (hA : Centre A α) (hD : OnCircle D α) (h : ‖A D‖ < ‖A B‖) :
    OutsideCircle B α
helper_signatures.Elements.produce_longer:
/-- Room to cut off. A finite straight line AB can be produced beyond B further
than a given straight line BC from B. Postulate 2 produces a straight line but
never says how far, and I.3 cuts off only from a *greater* straight line; so Euclid's
"let CE be made equal to CD [I. 3]", on a straight line produced, needs this first
(I.11, I.16, I.20, I.22). Describe the circle with centre B and distance BC
[Post. 3]; the straight line AB, produced beyond the centre, cuts it at some Y
(System E, Intersections 5); and BY, produced a little further still to X
[Post. 2], is greater than BY, that is, than BC [Def. 15, C.N. 5]. -/
theorem produce_longer (hAB : A ≠ B) (hBC : B ≠ C) :
    ∃ X : Point, Between A B X ∧ ‖B C‖ < ‖B X‖

I.2.enunciation: To place at a given point (as an extremity) a straight line equal to a given straight line.

I.3.enunciation: Given two unequal straight lines, to cut off from the greater a straight line equal to the less.

definitions.Line:

without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,

definitions.Magnitude:

  A ≠ B ∧ P ≠ A ∧ Collinear A B P ∧ ¬ Between P A B
definitions.Point:

definitions.SameSide:

question.instructions:
Does every proposition called by the proof unit in `lean_proof` do work towards its conclusion or a substantive intermediate step of Euclid's argument? Also check for artificial hypothesis uses. Judge this unit's uses of the supplied helper signatures; helper bodies are outside this question. Heath's sentences stand as `--` lines and `cited` gives exact enunciations. In Lean, `have h : T := p` proves T by p and calls the result h; `obtain ⟨…⟩ := p` takes p apart into named pieces; `rw [h34, h37, …]` rewrites the goal by the equalities named. Follow uses through helper calls and tactics as well as explicit names. An anonymous binding or an unused hypothesis alone does not establish a defect. If both defects occur, choose `a dummy citation`.

docs/FORMALIZATION.md, section 5:
A checked intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid is legitimate, even if the
  final proof term could do without it.

criteria.cannot tell: What is given here is not enough to decide.
criteria.all do work: Every proposition call supports a later step or the conclusion, or establishes a substantive intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid. No hypothesis is mentioned merely to look used. With no proposition calls the citation part alone is vacuous; hypothesis use must still be inspected.
criteria.a dummy citation: Some proposition call does no substantive work: its result neither supports the argument nor establishes a substantive intermediate fact, and merely supplies a citation while the step is done another way.
criteria.an artificial hypothesis use: No dummy citation is established, but a hypothesis is mentioned only so that it looks used, and does no substantive work.

state.commentary:
Not every three straight lines make a triangle, as the enunciation says. "This is the first case in the *Elements* of a διορισμός to a problem in the sense of a statement of the conditions or limits of the possibility of a solution. The criterion is of course supplied by the preceding proposition" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 293). We state the three conditions as hypotheses; the proof needs no I.20, which shows only that they cannot be dropped. Euclid sets out DE "terminated at D but of infinite length in the direction of E", so that I.3 has room to cut DF, FG and GH off it. But I.3 cuts only from a greater finite straight line, so we say how far to go: I.2 sets out a straight line equal to the one to be cut off, and the straight line to be cut from is produced further, as in I.11.

**"Who is so dull?"** Heath notes: "It was early observed that Euclid assumes, without giving any reason, that the circles drawn as described will meet" when the condition holds (vol. 1, p. 293). Robert Simson was impatient: "For who is so dull, though only beginning to learn the Elements, as not to perceive that the circle described from the centre F, at the distance FD, must meet FH betwixt F and H, because FD is less than FH" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 293). Lean is exactly that dull.

Heath's answer is that the circle about G has a point outside the circle about F and a point inside it. H is outside, FH being B and C together, greater than A. The point M where GF, produced if need be, meets the circle about G is inside, since taking the same thing from two unequals leaves FM less than A; our proof also takes the case he passes over, where M is F itself. Then "we have only to invoke the Principle of Continuity, as we have to do in I. 1" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 294). Our rule here is System E, Intersection 4, in the corrected form LeanEuclid gives it.

**The modern way.** Let $a$, $b$, $c$ be the lengths of A, B, C. In the complex plane put $\mathrm{F} = 0$ and $\mathrm{G} = b$, and let $\mathrm{K} = x + iy$, with $x = (a^2 + b^2 - c^2)/(2b)$ and $y = \sqrt{a^2 - x^2}$. Then $|\mathrm{K}| = a$ and $|\mathrm{K} - b| = c$, and $y$ is real and positive exactly when $|a - b| \lt c \lt a + b$: the three conditions of I.22, in one line.
state.lean_proof:
/-- Out of three straight lines, which are equal to three given straight lines, to construct a
triangle: thus it is necessary that two of the straight lines taken together in any manner
should be greater than the remaining one. [I. 20] -/
theorem Prop22 {A₁ A₂ B₁ B₂ C₁ C₂ E F P : Point}
    (hAB : ‖C₁ C₂‖ < ‖A₁ A₂‖ + ‖B₁ B₂‖) (hAC : ‖B₁ B₂‖ < ‖A₁ A₂‖ + ‖C₁ C₂‖)
    (hBC : ‖A₁ A₂‖ < ‖B₁ B₂‖ + ‖C₁ C₂‖) (hFE : F ≠ E) (hP : ¬ Collinear F E P) :
    ∃ G K : Point, OnRay G F E ∧ SameSideOf K P F E ∧
      ‖K F‖ = ‖A₁ A₂‖ ∧ ‖F G‖ = ‖B₁ B₂‖ ∧ ‖G K‖ = ‖C₁ C₂‖ := by
  -- Let the three given straight lines be A, B, C, and of these let two taken together in any
  -- manner be greater than the remaining one,
  /- Straight lines, and so none of them is nothing (`Prop22.ne_zero`): each has
     two different ends, as I.3 will want. -/
  have hA : A₁ ≠ A₂ := fun e => Prop22.ne_zero hAB hAC (by rw [e]; exact len_self A₂)
  have hB : B₁ ≠ B₂ := fun e =>
    Prop22.ne_zero (by rw [add_comm]; exact hAB) hBC (by rw [e]; exact len_self B₂)
  have hC : C₁ ≠ C₂ := fun e =>
    Prop22.ne_zero (by rw [add_comm]; exact hAC) (by rw [add_comm]; exact hBC)
      (by rw [e]; exact len_self C₂)
  -- namely A, B greater than C,
  have hAB_C : ‖C₁ C₂‖ < ‖A₁ A₂‖ + ‖B₁ B₂‖ := hAB
  -- A, C greater than B,
  have hAC_B : ‖B₁ B₂‖ < ‖A₁ A₂‖ + ‖C₁ C₂‖ := hAC
  -- and B, C greater than A;
  have hBC_A : ‖A₁ A₂‖ < ‖B₁ B₂‖ + ‖C₁ C₂‖ := hBC
  -- thus it is required to construct a triangle out of straight lines equal to A, B, C.
  -- Let there be set out a straight line DE, terminated at D but of infinite length in the
  -- direction of E,
  /- The straight line DE is the straight line through the given points F and E
     [Post. 1]. Its end D is not given: it is set out behind F, at the distance A,
     in the next breath. -/
  obtain ⟨DE, hF_DE, hE_DE⟩ := Postulate1 F E hFE
  have hP_DE : ¬ OnLine P DE := fun h => hP ⟨DE, hF_DE, hE_DE, h⟩
  -- and let DF be made equal to A, FG equal to B, and GH equal to C. [I. 3]
  /- Three times I.3, each time cutting off from a straight line produced far
     enough to cut from (`Prop22.room`): FD from EF produced beyond F, FG from DF
     produced beyond F, and GH from FG produced beyond G. So D, F, G, H lie in that
     order along DE, as in Euclid's figure (`between_cut`), and G lies on the ray
     from F through E. -/
  obtain ⟨X, hEFX, hA_FX⟩ := Prop22.room hFE.symm hA
  obtain ⟨D, hFDX, hFD⟩ := Prop3 hA hA_FX
  have hDFE : Between D F E := between_symm (between_cut hEFX hFDX)
  obtain ⟨Y, hDFY, hB_FY⟩ := Prop22.room (ne_of_between hDFE) hB
  obtain ⟨G, hFGY, hFG⟩ := Prop3 hB hB_FY
  have hDFG : Between D F G := between_cut hDFY hFGY
  obtain ⟨Z, hFGZ, hC_GZ⟩ := Prop22.room (ne_of_between hFGY) hC
  obtain ⟨H, hGHZ, hGH⟩ := Prop3 hC hC_GZ
  have hFGH : Between F G H := between_cut hFGZ hGHZ
  have hD_DE : OnLine D DE := on_line_of_between (between_symm hDFE) hE_DE hF_DE
  have hG_DE : OnLine G DE := on_line_of_between hDFG hD_DE hF_DE
  have hG_ray : OnRay G F E :=
    ⟨hFE, (ne_of_between hFGY).symm, ⟨DE, hF_DE, hE_DE, hG_DE⟩,
      not_between_of_between_between hDFG hDFE⟩
  -- With centre F and distance FD let the circle DKL be described;
  obtain ⟨DKL, hF_DKL, hD_DKL⟩ := Postulate3 F D (ne_of_between hDFE).symm
  -- again, with centre G and distance GH let the circle KLH be described;
  obtain ⟨KLH, hG_KLH, hH_KLH⟩ := Postulate3 G H (ne_of_between hGHZ)
  /- Euclid takes K where the circles cut one another, without a word on why they
     should. They do, because two of A, B, C taken together in any manner are
     greater than the remaining one (`Prop22.meet`: Heath's argument, closed by
     System E, Intersection 4). They cut one another on each side of DE, the
     straight line through their centres, and K is taken on P's side (System E,
     Intersections 8). -/
  have hmeet : CirclesMeet KLH DKL :=
    Prop22.meet hFGH hF_DKL hD_DKL hG_KLH hH_KLH
      (by rw [hGH, hFD, hFG]; exact hAB_C) (by rw [hGH, hFD, hFG]; exact hAC_B)
      (by rw [hGH, hFD, hFG]; exact hBC_A)
  obtain ⟨K, hK_KLH, hK_DKL, hKP⟩ :=
    circles_meet_same_side hmeet hG_KLH hF_DKL hG_DE hF_DE hP_DE
  -- and let KF, KG be joined;
  obtain ⟨KF, -, -⟩ := Postulate1 K F (ne_of_centre_of_on hF_DKL hK_DKL)
  obtain ⟨KG, -, -⟩ := Postulate1 K G (ne_of_centre_of_on hG_KLH hK_KLH)
  -- I say that the triangle KFG has been constructed out of three straight lines equal to A,
  -- B, C.
  /- A triangle indeed: K is off DE, on P's side of it, and F and G are on it. -/
  have : Triangle K F G :=
    (Triangle.of_line hF_DE hG_DE (ne_of_between hFGY) (not_on_line_of_same_side hKP)).cab
  -- For, since the point F is the centre of the circle DKL,
  -- FD is equal to FK.
  have hFD_FK : ‖F D‖ = ‖F K‖ := Definition15 hF_DKL hD_DKL hK_DKL
  -- But FD is equal to A;
  have hFD_A : ‖F D‖ = ‖A₁ A₂‖ := hFD
  -- therefore KF is also equal to A.
  have hKF : ‖K F‖ = ‖A₁ A₂‖ := (len_symm K F).trans (hFD_FK.symm.trans hFD_A)
  -- Again, since the point G is the centre of the circle LKH,
  -- GH is equal to GK.
  have hGH_GK : ‖G H‖ = ‖G K‖ := Definition15 hG_KLH hH_KLH hK_KLH
  -- But GH is equal to C;
  have hGH_C : ‖G H‖ = ‖C₁ C₂‖ := hGH
  -- therefore KG is also equal to C.
  have hKG : ‖K G‖ = ‖C₁ C₂‖ := (len_symm K G).trans (hGH_GK.symm.trans hGH_C)
  -- And FG is also equal to B;
  have hFG_B : ‖F G‖ = ‖B₁ B₂‖ := hFG
  -- therefore the three straight lines KF, FG, GK are equal to the three straight lines A, B,
  -- C.
  have hGK : ‖G K‖ = ‖C₁ C₂‖ := (len_symm G K).trans hKG
  -- Therefore out of the three straight lines KF, FG, GK, which are equal to the three given
  -- straight lines A, B, C, the triangle KFG has been constructed.
  /- With FG along the given ray from F through E, and K on P's side of FE. -/
  exact ⟨G, K, hG_ray, SameSideOf.of_line hFE hF_DE hE_DE hKP, hKF, hFG_B, hGK⟩
  -- Q. E. F.

statement.note: Euclid's condition is taken as three hypotheses; the triangle is built with its corner at F, a side along the ray FE and its third corner on P's side.

state.lean_proof:
/-- On a given straight line and at a point on it to construct a rectilineal angle equal to a given
rectilineal angle. -/
theorem Prop23 {A B C D E P : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hDCE : Triangle D C E) (hP : ¬ Collinear A B P) :
    ∃ F G : Point, OnRay G A B ∧ SameSideOf F P A B ∧ ∠ F A G = ∠ D C E := by
  -- Let AB be the given straight line, A the point on it, and the angle DCE the given
  -- rectilineal angle;
  /- The given angle comes as the triangle DCE: its arms CD, CE are two straight
     lines through C, not one, so it is a true rectilineal angle. We shall need the
     straight line AB itself, to see that the angle we build is not flat either. -/
  obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B hAB
  -- thus it is required to construct on the given straight line AB, and at the point A on it,
  -- a rectilineal angle equal to the given rectilineal angle DCE.
  /- We build the angle on the ray from A through B, and on the side of AB where P
     is, so that later propositions can place it where they need it (I.24, I.31). -/
  -- On the straight lines CD, CE respectively let the points D, E be taken at random;
  /- The statement already names a point on each arm, D on CD and E on CE, so we
     take those. Any others would do as well: an angle depends only on its two rays
     (`angle_eq_of_onRay` in Book Zero). -/
  -- let DE be joined,
  /- Our proof uses only the points D and E; the straight line DE is drawn for the eye.
     Joined, it closes the triangle DCE, whose three sides are the three straight
     lines that I.22 is about to take. -/
  -- and out of three straight lines which are equal to the three straight lines CD, DE, CE let
  -- the triangle AFG be constructed in such a way that CD is equal to AF, CE to AG, and
  -- further DE to FG. [I. 22]
  /- I.22 asks that two of the three taken together in any manner be greater than the
     remaining one, and points to I.20 for it. The three are the sides of the
     triangle DCE, so I.20, applied to it named from C, says just that, once each sum
     is read in I.22's order. -/
  obtain ⟨hDE_lt, hCE_lt, hCD_lt⟩ := Prop20 hDCE.bac
  have h₁ : ‖D E‖ < ‖C D‖ + ‖C E‖ := by
    rw [← len_symm D C]
    exact hDE_lt
  have h₂ : ‖C E‖ < ‖C D‖ + ‖D E‖ := hCE_lt
  have h₃ : ‖C D‖ < ‖C E‖ + ‖D E‖ := by
    rw [add_comm, len_symm C E]
    exact hCD_lt
  /- I.22 puts the corner of its triangle at A, the side AG along the ray from A
     through B, and the third corner F on P's side of AB. Its lengths, in its own
     order and Euclid's, are CD, CE and DE. Heath notes that Euclid asks more of
     I.22 here than I.22, as Euclid gives it, provides: a triangle placed on a given
     straight line at a given point (vol. 1, p. 295). Our I.22 is stated so as to
     provide it. -/
  obtain ⟨G, F, hG, hF, hFA_CD, hAG_CE, hGF_DE⟩ :=
    Prop22 (A₁ := C) (A₂ := D) (B₁ := C) (B₂ := E) (C₁ := D) (C₂ := E) h₁ h₂ h₃ hAB hP
  /- Euclid calls AFG a triangle, and I.8 will need it to be one. G is on the
     straight line AB (a point of the ray from A through B, so not A itself), and F,
     being on one side of AB, is off it (`OnRay.onLine`, `SameSideOf.triangle`,
     `Triangle.off_line`, `Triangle.of_line` in Book Zero). -/
  have hG_AB : OnLine G AB := hG.onLine hA_AB hB_AB
  have hA_G : A ≠ G := hG.2.1.symm
  have hF_AB : ¬ OnLine F AB := hF.triangle.off_line hA_AB hB_AB
  have hAFG : Triangle A F G := (Triangle.of_line hA_AB hG_AB hA_G hF_AB).acb
  -- Then, since the two sides DC, CE are equal to the two sides FA, AG respectively,
  have hCD_AF : ‖C D‖ = ‖A F‖ := hFA_CD.symm.trans (len_symm F A)
  have hCE_AG : ‖C E‖ = ‖A G‖ := hAG_CE.symm
  -- and the base DE is equal to the base FG,
  have hDE_FG : ‖D E‖ = ‖F G‖ := hGF_DE.symm.trans (len_symm G F)
  -- the angle DCE is equal to the angle FAG. [I. 8]
  have hDCE_FAG : ∠ D C E = ∠ F A G := Prop8 hDCE.bac hAFG hCD_AF hCE_AG hDE_FG
  -- Therefore on the given straight line AB, and at the point A on it, the rectilineal angle
  -- FAG has been constructed equal to the given rectilineal angle DCE.
  exact ⟨F, G, hG, hF, hDCE_FAG.symm⟩
  -- Q. E. F.

state.commentary:
An angle is hard to carry about, but a triangle is only three lengths, which I.22 can set down anywhere: so Euclid copies the triangle DCE at A, and I.8 brings the angle with it. "This problem was, according to Eudemus (see Proclus, p. 333, 5), 'rather the discovery of Oenopides,' from which we must apparently infer, not that Oenopides was the first to find any solution of it, but that it was he who discovered the particular solution given by Euclid" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 295).

The editors, Heath notes, seem to have missed that the construction of the triangle here is "not exactly the construction given in I. 22": "We have here to construct a triangle on a certain finite straight line AG as base; in I. 22 we have only to construct a triangle with sides of given length without any restriction as to how it is to be placed" (vol. 1, p. 295). He suspects that Proclus felt it too, and so gave the construction over again "in a more instructive manner" (vol. 1, p. 295). Our I.22 is stated to close the gap, and our I.23 settles what Euclid's "on the given straight line AB" leaves open, for I.24, I.31 and I.42: as in Heath's figure, G is on the ray from A through B, and F on the side of AB where a given point P lies. Euclid's D and E, "taken at random", may be any points of the arms, since an angle depends only on its rays, and I.22's condition, which Euclid does not check, holds because the three lengths are the sides of the triangle DCE (I.20).

Proclus objects to Apollonius' way, which leans on Book III: circles of one radius about the vertex and about A, equal circumferences cut off on them, and the angles equal as standing on equal circumferences. As under I.11, Heath is kind to Apollonius: "It seems to me probable that his construction was only given from the point of view of *practical*, not theoretical, geometry" (vol. 1, p. 296). Done with compasses, as Heath reads it, the circumference cut off is measured by the straight line joining its ends, and the construction comes to Euclid's with an isosceles triangle: the way an angle is copied to this day.

**The modern way.** In the complex plane, multiplying by $w$ turns every direction through the angle $\arg w$. So the point $\mathrm{A} + \mathrm{(B - A)(E - C)/(D - C)}$ makes with AB, at A, an angle equal to DCE, and its mirror image in the straight line AB makes the same angle on the other side; which of the two lies on P's side is a matter of one sign.
state.lean_proof:
/-- On a given straight line and at a point on it to construct a rectilineal angle equal to a given
rectilineal angle. -/
theorem Prop23 {A B C D E P : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hDCE : Triangle D C E) (hP : ¬ Collinear A B P) :
    ∃ F G : Point, OnRay G A B ∧ SameSideOf F P A B ∧ ∠ F A G = ∠ D C E := by
  -- Let AB be the given straight line, A the point on it, and the angle DCE the given
  -- rectilineal angle;
  /- The given angle comes as the triangle DCE: its arms CD, CE are two straight
     lines through C, not one, so it is a true rectilineal angle. We shall need the
     straight line AB itself, to see that the angle we build is not flat either. -/
  obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B hAB
  -- thus it is required to construct on the given straight line AB, and at the point A on it,
  -- a rectilineal angle equal to the given rectilineal angle DCE.
  /- We build the angle on the ray from A through B, and on the side of AB where P
     is, so that later propositions can place it where they need it (I.24, I.31). -/
  -- On the straight lines CD, CE respectively let the points D, E be taken at random;
  /- The statement already names a point on each arm, D on CD and E on CE, so we
     take those. Any others would do as well: an angle depends only on its two rays
     (`angle_eq_of_onRay` in Book Zero). -/
  -- let DE be joined,
  /- Our proof uses only the points D and E; the straight line DE is drawn for the eye.
     Joined, it closes the triangle DCE, whose three sides are the three straight
     lines that I.22 is about to take. -/
  -- and out of three straight lines which are equal to the three straight lines CD, DE, CE let
  -- the triangle AFG be constructed in such a way that CD is equal to AF, CE to AG, and
  -- further DE to FG. [I. 22]
  /- I.22 asks that two of the three taken together in any manner be greater than the
     remaining one, and points to I.20 for it. The three are the sides of the
     triangle DCE, so I.20, applied to it named from C, says just that, once each sum
     is read in I.22's order. -/
  obtain ⟨hDE_lt, hCE_lt, hCD_lt⟩ := Prop20 hDCE.bac
  have h₁ : ‖D E‖ < ‖C D‖ + ‖C E‖ := by
    rw [← len_symm D C]
    exact hDE_lt
  have h₂ : ‖C E‖ < ‖C D‖ + ‖D E‖ := hCE_lt
  have h₃ : ‖C D‖ < ‖C E‖ + ‖D E‖ := by
    rw [add_comm, len_symm C E]
    exact hCD_lt
  /- I.22 puts the corner of its triangle at A, the side AG along the ray from A
     through B, and the third corner F on P's side of AB. Its lengths, in its own
     order and Euclid's, are CD, CE and DE. Heath notes that Euclid asks more of
     I.22 here than I.22, as Euclid gives it, provides: a triangle placed on a given
     straight line at a given point (vol. 1, p. 295). Our I.22 is stated so as to
     provide it. -/
  obtain ⟨G, F, hG, hF, hFA_CD, hAG_CE, hGF_DE⟩ :=
    Prop22 (A₁ := C) (A₂ := D) (B₁ := C) (B₂ := E) (C₁ := D) (C₂ := E) h₁ h₂ h₃ hAB hP
  /- Euclid calls AFG a triangle, and I.8 will need it to be one. G is on the
     straight line AB (a point of the ray from A through B, so not A itself), and F,
     being on one side of AB, is off it (`OnRay.onLine`, `SameSideOf.triangle`,
     `Triangle.off_line`, `Triangle.of_line` in Book Zero). -/
  have hG_AB : OnLine G AB := hG.onLine hA_AB hB_AB
  have hA_G : A ≠ G := hG.2.1.symm
  have hF_AB : ¬ OnLine F AB := hF.triangle.off_line hA_AB hB_AB
  have hAFG : Triangle A F G := (Triangle.of_line hA_AB hG_AB hA_G hF_AB).acb
  -- Then, since the two sides DC, CE are equal to the two sides FA, AG respectively,
  have hCD_AF : ‖C D‖ = ‖A F‖ := hFA_CD.symm.trans (len_symm F A)
  have hCE_AG : ‖C E‖ = ‖A G‖ := hAG_CE.symm
  -- and the base DE is equal to the base FG,
  have hDE_FG : ‖D E‖ = ‖F G‖ := hGF_DE.symm.trans (len_symm G F)
  -- the angle DCE is equal to the angle FAG. [I. 8]
  have hDCE_FAG : ∠ D C E = ∠ F A G := Prop8 hDCE.bac hAFG hCD_AF hCE_AG hDE_FG
  -- Therefore on the given straight line AB, and at the point A on it, the rectilineal angle
  -- FAG has been constructed equal to the given rectilineal angle DCE.
  exact ⟨F, G, hG, hF, hDCE_FAG.symm⟩
  -- Q. E. F.

statement.note: The angle FAG is built with G on the ray from A through B and F on the side of AB where a given point P lies, as I.24, I.31 and I.42 need.

state.heath_proof:
Let ABC, DEF be two triangles having the two sides AB, AC equal to the two sides DE, DF respectively, namely AB to DE, and AC to DF, and let the angle at A be greater than the angle at D;

I say that the base BC is also greater than the base EF.

For, since the angle BAC is greater than the angle EDF, let there be constructed, on the straight line DE, and at the point D on it, the angle EDG equal to the angle BAC; [I. 23]

let DG be made equal to either of the two straight lines AC, DF, and let EG, FG be joined.

Then, since AB is equal to DE, and AC to DG,

the two sides BA, AC are equal to the two sides ED, DG, respectively;

and the angle BAC is equal to the angle EDG;

therefore the base BC is equal to the base EG. [I. 4]

Again, since DF is equal to DG,

the angle DGF is also equal to the angle DFG; [I. 5]

therefore the angle DFG is greater than the angle EGF.

Therefore the angle EFG is much greater than the angle EGF.

And, since EFG is a triangle having the angle EFG greater than the angle EGF,

and the greater angle is subtended by the greater side, [I. 19]

the side EG is also greater than EF.

But EG is equal to BC.

Therefore BC is also greater than EF.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.

Then, since AB is equal to DE, and AC to DG,

the two sides BA, AC are equal to the two sides ED, DG, respectively;

and the angle BAC is equal to the angle EDG;

therefore the base BC is equal to the base EG. [I. 4]

Again, since DF is equal to DG,

the angle DGF is also equal to the angle DFG; [I. 5]

therefore the angle DFG is greater than the angle EGF.

Therefore the angle EFG is much greater than the angle EGF.

And, since EFG is a triangle having the angle EFG greater than the angle EGF,

and the greater angle is subtended by the greater side, [I. 19]

the side EG is also greater than EF.

But EG is equal to BC.

Therefore BC is also greater than EF.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, but have the one of the
angles contained by the equal straight lines greater than the other, they will also have the
base greater than the base. -/
theorem Prop24 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖D F‖) (h : ∠ E D F < ∠ B A C) :
    ‖E F‖ < ‖B C‖ := by
  -- Let ABC, DEF be two triangles having the two sides AB, AC equal to the two sides DE, DF
  -- respectively, namely AB to DE, and AC to DF, and let the angle at A be greater than the
  -- angle at D;
  have hDE : D ≠ E := hDEF.ne₁₂
  have hDF : D ≠ F := hDEF.ne₁₃
  -- I say that the base BC is also greater than the base EF.
  -- For, since the angle BAC is greater than the angle EDF, let there be constructed, on the
  -- straight line DE, and at the point D on it, the angle EDG equal to the angle BAC; [I. 23]
  /- I.23 builds the angle at D with one arm along the ray from D through E (it
     passes through a point E₁ of that ray) and the other through a point G₁ on
     whichever side of DE we ask for. We ask for F's side, as in Euclid's figure. -/
  obtain ⟨G₁, E₁, hE₁, hG₁F, hG₁DE₁⟩ := Prop23 hDE hABC.bac hDEF
  -- let DG be made equal to either of the two straight lines AC, DF, and let EG, FG be joined.
  /- G is laid along the arm DG₁ with a circle about D (`OnRay.exists_len_eq`). It is
     on F's side of DE, as G₁ is (`SameSideOf.of_onRay`), and the angle EDG is the angle
     E₁DG₁, its arms being the same rays (`angle_eq_of_onRay`). -/
  obtain ⟨G, hG, hDG_DF⟩ := OnRay.exists_len_eq hDF hG₁F.triangle.ne₁₃
  have hGF : SameSideOf G F D E := SameSideOf.of_onRay hG hG₁F
  have hEDG : ∠ E D G = ∠ B A C :=
    (angle_eq_of_onRay hE₁.symm hG).trans
      ((angle_symm hE₁.2.1 hG₁F.triangle.ne₁₃.symm).trans hG₁DE₁)
  /- Joining needs different points. G is off DE; and F, the angle EDF being the
     less, lies within the angle EDG (`Prop24.within`), so it is off DG. -/
  have hFE : SameSideOf F E D G := Prop24.within hGF (by rw [hEDG]; exact h)
  have hDEG : Triangle D E G := hGF.triangle
  have hDFG : Triangle D F G := hFE.triangle.acb
  -- Then, since AB is equal to DE, and AC to DG,
  have hAC_DG : ‖A C‖ = ‖D G‖ := hAC.trans hDG_DF.symm
  -- the two sides BA, AC are equal to the two sides ED, DG, respectively;
  -- and the angle BAC is equal to the angle EDG;
  have hBAC : ∠ B A C = ∠ E D G := hEDG.symm
  -- therefore the base BC is equal to the base EG. [I. 4]
  have hBC_EG : ‖B C‖ = ‖E G‖ := (Prop4 hABC hDEG hAB hAC_DG hBAC).1
  -- Again, since DF is equal to DG,
  have hDF_DG : ‖D F‖ = ‖D G‖ := hDG_DF.symm
  -- the angle DGF is also equal to the angle DFG; [I. 5]
  have hDGF : ∠ D G F = ∠ D F G := (Prop5.base hDFG hDF_DG).symm
  /- Euclid's figure has F beyond EG. Our statement, like his enunciation, covers
     every placing of F, so the proof takes as well the two cases he leaves to the
     reader (`Prop24.cases`), as Proclus does. -/
  have hEF_EG : ‖E F‖ < ‖E G‖ := by
    rcases Prop24.cases hGF hFE with hEFG | hF | ⟨X, hEXG, hDXF, hEGF⟩
    · /- F falls on EG: "it is then obvious that EG is greater than EF", the whole
         than the part. -/
      exact len_lt_of_between hEFG
    · /- F falls within the triangle DEG: "by I. 21, DF, FE are together less than
         DG, GE. But DF is equal to DG; therefore EF is less than EG." -/
      have hI21 : ‖D F‖ + ‖F E‖ < ‖D G‖ + ‖G E‖ := (Prop21 hDEG.cab hF).1
      rw [hDF_DG] at hI21
      rw [len_symm E F, len_symm E G]
      exact Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_left hI21
    · /- Euclid's figure has F beyond EG, which DF crosses at X. -/
      have hFG : F ≠ G := hDFG.ne₂₃
      have hEG : E ≠ G := hDEG.ne₂₃
      -- therefore the angle DFG is greater than the angle EGF.
      /- The angle EGF is the angle XGF, a part of the angle DGF, since X lies
         between D and F (`angle_lt_of_between`). -/
      have hEGF_DGF : ∠ E G F < ∠ D G F := by
        rw [← angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between (between_symm hEXG)) hFG]
        exact angle_lt_of_between hDFG hDXF
      have hEGF_DFG : ∠ E G F < ∠ D F G := by
        rw [← hDGF]
        exact hEGF_DGF
      -- Therefore the angle EFG is much greater than the angle EGF.
      /- The angle DFG is the angle XFG, a part of the angle EFG, since X lies
         between E and G. -/
      have hDFG_EFG : ∠ D F G < ∠ E F G := by
        rw [← angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between (between_symm hDXF)) hFG.symm]
        exact angle_lt_of_between hEGF hEXG
      have hmuch : ∠ E G F < ∠ E F G := lt_trans hEGF_DFG hDFG_EFG
      -- And, since EFG is a triangle having the angle EFG greater than the angle EGF,
      have hEFG : Triangle E F G := hEGF.acb
      -- and the greater angle is subtended by the greater side, [I. 19]
      -- the side EG is also greater than EF.
      exact Prop19 hEFG (by rw [angle_symm hFG hEG]; exact hmuch)
  -- But EG is equal to BC.
  rw [hBC_EG]
  -- Therefore BC is also greater than EF.
  exact hEF_EG
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.

helper_signatures.Elements.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop19:
/-- In any triangle the greater angle is subtended by the greater side. -/
theorem Prop19 {A B C : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (h : ∠ B C A < ∠ A B C) :
    ‖A B‖ < ‖A C‖
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop21:
/-- If on one of the sides of a triangle, from its extremities, there be constructed two straight
lines meeting within the triangle, the straight lines so constructed will be less than the
remaining two sides of the triangle, but will contain a greater angle. -/
theorem Prop21 {A B C D : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hD : InsideTriangle D A B C) :
    ‖B D‖ + ‖D C‖ < ‖B A‖ + ‖A C‖ ∧ ∠ B A C < ∠ B D C
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop23:
/-- On a given straight line and at a point on it to construct a rectilineal angle equal to a given
rectilineal angle. -/
theorem Prop23 {A B C D E P : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hDCE : Triangle D C E) (hP : ¬ Collinear A B P) :
    ∃ F G : Point, OnRay G A B ∧ SameSideOf F P A B ∧ ∠ F A G = ∠ D C E
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop24.cases:
/-- Where does F fall? Since F lies within the angle EDG, the straight line DF,
drawn on, crosses EG at some point X (`crossbar`). Then either F is X, and lies
on EG; or F is short of X, within the triangle DEG; or F is beyond X, on
the far side of EG from D, and EFG is a triangle. The last is Euclid's figure. -/
theorem Prop24.cases {D E F G : Point} (hGF : SameSideOf G F D E) (hFE : SameSideOf F E D G) :
    Between E F G ∨ InsideTriangle F G D E ∨
      ∃ X : Point, Between E X G ∧ Between D X F ∧ Triangle E G F
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop24.within:
/-- F lies within the angle EDG. Both are on one side of DE, and the angle EDF
is the less. If F were on DG, the angle EDF would be the angle EDG
(`angle_onRay_right`); if it were beyond DG, then G would lie within the angle
EDF (System E, Triple incidence 2), and the angle EDG would be a part of it
(`angle_add_of_within`, with the angle GDF something, `Triangle.angle_pos`), so the
greater would be less than the less. -/
theorem Prop24.within {D E F G : Point} (hGF : SameSideOf G F D E) (h : ∠ E D F < ∠ E D G) :
    SameSideOf F E D G
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop4:
/-- If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles
contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the base, the
triangle will be equal to the triangle, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining
angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend. -/
theorem Prop4 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖D F‖) (hA : ∠ B A C = ∠ E D F) :
    ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ ∧ △ A B C = △ D E F ∧ ∠ A B C = ∠ D E F ∧ ∠ A C B = ∠ D F E
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop5:
/-- In isosceles triangles the angles at the base are equal to one another, and, if the equal
straight lines be produced further, the angles under the base will be equal to one another. -/
theorem Prop5 {A B C D E : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖A C‖)
    (hD : Between A B D) (hE : Between A C E) :
    ∠ A B C = ∠ A C B ∧ ∠ C B D = ∠ B C E
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop5.base:
/-- The angles at the base, and only those. Our I.5 is stated as Euclid states it,
with the equal sides produced and the angles under the base as well, so a proof that
cites it must first produce AB and AC (Post. 2). When only the angles at the base are
wanted, as in I.7, I.9, I.18, I.19, I.20 and I.24, any points beyond B and C
will do, and this produces them once. [I. 5] -/
theorem Prop5.base {A B C : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (h : ‖A B‖ = ‖A C‖) :
    ∠ A B C = ∠ A C B
helper_signatures.Elements.CommonNotion5:
/-- **Common Notion 5.** The whole is greater than the part: if `b` is something
(not nothing), then `a + b` is greater than `a`. -/
theorem CommonNotion5 {a b : Magnitude k} (h : 0 < b) : a < a + b
helper_signatures.Elements.InsideTriangle:
/-- `D` lies within the triangle `ABC`. -/
def InsideTriangle (D A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_left:
/-- The same, with the common part first: if `a` and `b` together are less than `a`
and `c` together, then `b` is less than `c`. -/
theorem Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_left {k : Kind} {a b c : Magnitude k} (h : a + b < a + c) :
    b < c
helper_signatures.Elements.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.exists_len_eq:
/-- "Let DG be made equal to DF" (I.24): on the ray from D through any point P
there is a point G with DG equal to DF. Describe the circle with centre D and
distance DF (Post. 3); the straight line DP, which passes through its centre, cuts
it on P's side of D (System E, Intersections 5, with a point Q set out on the
other side); and DG is a radius [Def. 15]. -/
theorem OnRay.exists_len_eq {D F P : Point} (hDF : D ≠ F) (hDP : D ≠ P) :
    ∃ G : Point, OnRay G D P ∧ ‖D G‖ = ‖D F‖
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.of_between:
/-- A point between A and B is on the ray from A through B. -/
theorem OnRay.of_between (h : Between A P B) : OnRay P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.of_sameSideOf:
/-- Going the other way: a point P of the straight line DF, other than D, and
on the same side of the straight line DE as F, is on the ray from D through
F. It is not behind D, for then DE would separate it from F (System E,
Pasch 3). -/
theorem OnRay.of_sameSideOf {D E F P : Point} (h : SameSideOf P F D E) (hP : Collinear D F P)
    (hPD : P ≠ D) : OnRay P D F
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.symm:
/-- P is on the ray from A through B exactly when B is on the ray from A
through P: they are one and the same ray. -/
theorem OnRay.symm (h : OnRay P A B) : OnRay B A P
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate1:
/-- **Postulate 1.** To draw a straight line from any point to any point. -/
axiom Postulate1 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf:
/-- `P` and `Q` lie on the same side of the straight line `AB`. -/
def SameSideOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.of_line:
/-- Two points on the same side of a straight line L through A and B are on
the same side of the straight line AB, however that line is named: two points
fix one straight line. -/
theorem SameSideOf.of_line (hAB : A ≠ B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (h : SameSide P Q L) : SameSideOf P Q A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.of_onRay:
/-- A point G on the ray from D through P is on the same side of the straight
line DE as P: the ray leaves DE at D and never crosses it again (System E,
Pasch 4). -/
theorem SameSideOf.of_onRay {D E F G P : Point} (hG : OnRay G D P) (hP : SameSideOf P F D E) :
    SameSideOf G F D E
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.sameSide:
/-- Two points on the same side of the straight line AB are on the same side of
any straight line drawn through A and B. -/
theorem SameSideOf.sameSide (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    SameSide P Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.swap:
/-- "On the same side of AB" is the same as "on the same side of BA". -/
theorem SameSideOf.swap (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf P Q B A
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the same side of AB as Q, then Q is on the same side as P. -/
theorem SameSideOf.symm (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.trans:
/-- Points on the same side as a third are on the same side as each other. -/
theorem SameSideOf.trans (h₁ : SameSideOf P Q A B) (h₂ : SameSideOf Q R A B) :
    SameSideOf P R A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.triangle:
/-- A point on one side of the straight line AB is not on it, so ABP is a
triangle. -/
theorem SameSideOf.triangle (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : Triangle A B P
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.angle_symm:
/-- The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4) -/
axiom angle_symm (hAB : A ≠ B) (hCB : C ≠ B) : ∠ A B C = ∠ C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_cases:
/-- Of three different points on a straight line, one is between the other two.
(Between 6) -/
axiom between_cases (hAB : A ≠ B) (hBC : B ≠ C) (hAC : A ≠ C) (hA : OnLine A L)
    (hB : OnLine B L) (hC : OnLine C L) : Between A B C ∨ Between B A C ∨ Between A C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_symm:
/-- If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1) -/
axiom between_symm (h : Between A B C) : Between C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.len_symm:
/-- The straight line AB is the straight line BA. (Metric 3) -/
axiom len_symm (A B : Point) : ‖A B‖ = ‖B A‖
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.line_unique:
/-- Two points determine a straight line. (Generalities 1) -/
axiom line_unique (hAB : A ≠ B) (hAL : OnLine A L) (hBL : OnLine B L) (hAM : OnLine A M)
    (hBM : OnLine B M) : L = M
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.lt_irrefl:
/-- No magnitude is less than itself. (System E §3.5) -/
axiom lt_irrefl (a : Magnitude k) : ¬ a < a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.lt_trans:
/-- What is less than the less is less still. (System E §3.5) -/
axiom lt_trans {a b c : Magnitude k} : a < b → b < c → a < c
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.not_on_line_of_same_side:
/-- Points on one side of a straight line are not on it. (Same side 3) -/
axiom not_on_line_of_same_side (h : SameSide A B L) : ¬ OnLine A L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between_ends:
/-- A straight line through A and C passes through every point between them.
(Between 3) -/
axiom on_line_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hC : OnLine C L) :
    OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.pasch2:
/-- If B is between A and C, A is on L and B is off it, then B and C are
on the same side of L: a straight line that leaves L at A does not cross it
again. (Pasch 2) -/
axiom pasch2 (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : ¬ OnLine B L) : SameSide B C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.same_side_symm:
/-- If A is on the same side of a straight line as B, then B is on the same side
as A. (Same side 2) -/
axiom same_side_symm (h : SameSide A B L) : SameSide B A L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.triple_incidence2:
/-- Take B on L, C on M and D on N, three straight lines through A, with
B other than A and D off M. If C and D are on the same side of L, and B
and D are not on the same side of M, then B and C are on the same side of
N: C lies within the angle BAD. (Triple incidence 2) -/
axiom triple_incidence2 (hAL : OnLine A L) (hAM : OnLine A M) (hAN : OnLine A N)
    (hB : OnLine B L) (hC : OnLine C M) (hD : OnLine D N) (hCD : SameSide C D L)
    (hBD : ¬ SameSide B D M) (hDM : ¬ OnLine D M) (hBA : B ≠ A) : SameSide B C N
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.acb:
/-- The triangle ABC, named the other way round, as ACB. -/
theorem Triangle.acb (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle A C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.angle_pos:
/-- An angle of a triangle is something, not nothing: in the triangle ABC, were
the angle ABC nothing, C would lie on the straight line BA (System E,
Diagram-angle 1), and A, B, C would be on one straight line. -/
theorem Triangle.angle_pos (h : Triangle A B C) : 0 < ∠ A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.bac:
/-- The triangle ABC, named the other way round, as BAC. -/
theorem Triangle.bac (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.bca:
/-- The triangle ABC, named from B, as BCA. -/
theorem Triangle.bca (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle B C A
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.cab:
/-- The triangle ABC, named from C, as CAB. -/
theorem Triangle.cab (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle C A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₁₂:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₁₂ (h : Triangle A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₁₃:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₁₃ (h : Triangle A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₂₃:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₂₃ (h : Triangle A B C) : B ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.of_line:
/-- Two different points of a straight line, and a third point off it, make a
triangle. -/
theorem Triangle.of_line {P Q R : Point} (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L) (hPQ : P ≠ Q)
    (hR : ¬ OnLine R L) : Triangle P Q R
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.off_line:
/-- In the triangle ABC, the corner C is off every straight line through A
and B. -/
theorem Triangle.off_line (h : Triangle A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    ¬ OnLine C L
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_add_of_within:
/-- A straight line drawn from the corner of an angle through a point within it
cuts the angle into two. If R lies within the angle PVQ, on Q's side of VP
and on P's side of VQ, then the angle PVQ is made up of the angles PVR and
RVQ. This is System E's Diagram-angle 2, said of "the straight lines VP, VQ"
rather than of lines drawn and named. -/
theorem angle_add_of_within {V P Q R : Point} (hRQ : SameSideOf R Q V P)
    (hRP : SameSideOf R P V Q) : ∠ P V Q = ∠ P V R + ∠ R V Q
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_eq_of_onRay:
/-- An angle doesn't change when its arms are traced through other points of the
same rays: if B' is on the ray from A through B, and C' on the ray from A
through C, the angle B'AC' is the angle BAC. (System E, Diagram-angle 4) -/
theorem angle_eq_of_onRay {B' C' : Point} (hB : OnRay B' A B) (hC : OnRay C' A C) :
    ∠ B' A C' = ∠ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_lt_of_between:
/-- The part is less than the whole, for angles: if R lies between P and Q, and
V is off the straight line PQ, the angle RVQ is less than the angle PVQ. For
PVQ is made up of PVR and RVQ (`angle_add_of_between`), and PVR is
something, since R is off VP (`Triangle.angle_pos`). [C.N. 5] -/
theorem angle_lt_of_between {V P Q R : Point} (hPQV : Triangle P Q V) (h : Between P R Q) :
    ∠ R V Q < ∠ P V Q
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_onRay_left:
/-- One arm traced through another point of its ray: if B' is on the ray from A
through B, the angle B'AC is the angle BAC. (System E, Diagram-angle 4) -/
theorem angle_onRay_left {B' : Point} (hB : OnRay B' A B) (hCA : C ≠ A) :
    ∠ B' A C = ∠ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_onRay_right:
/-- The other arm traced through another point of its ray: if C' is on the ray
from A through C, the angle BAC' is the angle BAC. (System E,
Diagram-angle 4) -/
theorem angle_onRay_right {C' : Point} (hC : OnRay C' A C) (hBA : B ≠ A) :
    ∠ B A C' = ∠ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.crossbar:
