state.commentary:
Euclid's one figure has F below EG. Robert Simson added a sentence to make it the only case, "Of the two sides DE, DF let DE be the side which is not greater than the other", and Heath leaves it out: "I doubt whether Euclid could have been induced to insert the words himself, even if it had been represented to him that their omission meant leaving two possible cases out of consideration." Euclid gives one case, as under I.2, and leaves the others to the reader: "We have already seen one instance in I. 7" (vol. 1, p. 297).

Proclus supplies the other two, which are, says Heath, "decidedly simpler than the case taken by Euclid as typical, and could well be left to the ingenuity of the learner" (vol. 1, p. 297). If F falls on EG, EF is a part of EG; if within the triangle DEG, "by I. 21, DF, FE are together less than DG, GE. But DF is equal to DG; therefore EF is less than EG" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 297), with equals taken away by a law Euclid never states. Our proof takes all three. Since the angle EDF is the less, DF, produced if need be, crosses EG, and F lies beyond the crossing, on it, or short of it. In Euclid's case the crossing lies between D and F, and that is what makes each of his comparisons the whole greater than the part: the angle EGF is a part of DGF, and DFG a part of EFG.

Why not compare the areas, as in I.4? Proclus, as Heath reports him, answers before anyone asks: unequal angles need not give unequal areas, and "the areas cannot be compared without the help of the theory of parallels" (vol. 1, p. 298). When the angles at A and D together make two right angles, the triangles are equal; when more, "*that triangle which has the greater angle is less*"; when less, greater (Heath, vol. 1, p. 299). Heath proves it under I.38, where an-Nairīzī has Heron put it.

**The modern way.** With $\mathbf{b}$ and $\mathbf{c}$ along the two given sides from the vertex, and $\theta$ the angle between them, the base is $|\mathbf{b} - \mathbf{c}|$, and $|\mathbf{b} - \mathbf{c}|^2 = |\mathbf{b}|^2 + |\mathbf{c}|^2 - 2 \thinspace |\mathbf{b}| \thinspace |\mathbf{c}| \cos\theta$. As $\theta$ grows from $0$ to $\pi$, $\cos\theta$ falls and the base grows. The area, $\frac{1}{2} \thinspace |\mathbf{b}| \thinspace |\mathbf{c}| \sin\theta$, is the same at $\theta$ and at $\pi - \theta$: the heart of Proclus' answer.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABC, DEF be two triangles having the two sides AB, AC equal to the two sides DE, DF respectively, namely AB to DE, and AC to DF, and let the angle at A be greater than the angle at D;

I say that the base BC is also greater than the base EF.

For, since the angle BAC is greater than the angle EDF, let there be constructed, on the straight line DE, and at the point D on it, the angle EDG equal to the angle BAC; [I. 23]

let DG be made equal to either of the two straight lines AC, DF, and let EG, FG be joined.

Then, since AB is equal to DE, and AC to DG,

the two sides BA, AC are equal to the two sides ED, DG, respectively;

and the angle BAC is equal to the angle EDG;

therefore the base BC is equal to the base EG. [I. 4]

Again, since DF is equal to DG,

the angle DGF is also equal to the angle DFG; [I. 5]

therefore the angle DFG is greater than the angle EGF.

Therefore the angle EFG is much greater than the angle EGF.

And, since EFG is a triangle having the angle EFG greater than the angle EGF,

and the greater angle is subtended by the greater side, [I. 19]

the side EG is also greater than EF.

But EG is equal to BC.

Therefore BC is also greater than EF.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, but have the one of the
angles contained by the equal straight lines greater than the other, they will also have the
base greater than the base. -/
theorem Prop24 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖D F‖) (h : ∠ E D F < ∠ B A C) :
    ‖E F‖ < ‖B C‖ := by
  -- Let ABC, DEF be two triangles having the two sides AB, AC equal to the two sides DE, DF
  -- respectively, namely AB to DE, and AC to DF, and let the angle at A be greater than the
  -- angle at D;
  have hDE : D ≠ E := hDEF.ne₁₂
  have hDF : D ≠ F := hDEF.ne₁₃
  -- I say that the base BC is also greater than the base EF.
  -- For, since the angle BAC is greater than the angle EDF, let there be constructed, on the
  -- straight line DE, and at the point D on it, the angle EDG equal to the angle BAC; [I. 23]
  /- I.23 builds the angle at D with one arm along the ray from D through E (it
     passes through a point E₁ of that ray) and the other through a point G₁ on
     whichever side of DE we ask for. We ask for F's side, as in Euclid's figure. -/
  obtain ⟨G₁, E₁, hE₁, hG₁F, hG₁DE₁⟩ := Prop23 hDE hABC.bac hDEF
  -- let DG be made equal to either of the two straight lines AC, DF, and let EG, FG be joined.
  /- G is laid along the arm DG₁ with a circle about D (`OnRay.exists_len_eq`). It is
     on F's side of DE, as G₁ is (`SameSideOf.of_onRay`), and the angle EDG is the angle
     E₁DG₁, its arms being the same rays (`angle_eq_of_onRay`). -/
  obtain ⟨G, hG, hDG_DF⟩ := OnRay.exists_len_eq hDF hG₁F.triangle.ne₁₃
  have hGF : SameSideOf G F D E := SameSideOf.of_onRay hG hG₁F
  have hEDG : ∠ E D G = ∠ B A C :=
    (angle_eq_of_onRay hE₁.symm hG).trans
      ((angle_symm hE₁.2.1 hG₁F.triangle.ne₁₃.symm).trans hG₁DE₁)
  /- Joining needs different points. G is off DE; and F, the angle EDF being the
     less, lies within the angle EDG (`Prop24.within`), so it is off DG. -/
  have hFE : SameSideOf F E D G := Prop24.within hGF (by rw [hEDG]; exact h)
  have hDEG : Triangle D E G := hGF.triangle
  have hDFG : Triangle D F G := hFE.triangle.acb
  -- Then, since AB is equal to DE, and AC to DG,
  have hAC_DG : ‖A C‖ = ‖D G‖ := hAC.trans hDG_DF.symm
  -- the two sides BA, AC are equal to the two sides ED, DG, respectively;
  -- and the angle BAC is equal to the angle EDG;
  have hBAC : ∠ B A C = ∠ E D G := hEDG.symm
  -- therefore the base BC is equal to the base EG. [I. 4]
  have hBC_EG : ‖B C‖ = ‖E G‖ := (Prop4 hABC hDEG hAB hAC_DG hBAC).1
  -- Again, since DF is equal to DG,
  have hDF_DG : ‖D F‖ = ‖D G‖ := hDG_DF.symm
  -- the angle DGF is also equal to the angle DFG; [I. 5]
  have hDGF : ∠ D G F = ∠ D F G := (Prop5.base hDFG hDF_DG).symm
  /- Euclid's figure has F beyond EG. Our statement, like his enunciation, covers
     every placing of F, so the proof takes as well the two cases he leaves to the
     reader (`Prop24.cases`), as Proclus does. -/
  have hEF_EG : ‖E F‖ < ‖E G‖ := by
    rcases Prop24.cases hGF hFE with hEFG | hF | ⟨X, hEXG, hDXF, hEGF⟩
    · /- F falls on EG: "it is then obvious that EG is greater than EF", the whole
         than the part. -/
      exact len_lt_of_between hEFG
    · /- F falls within the triangle DEG: "by I. 21, DF, FE are together less than
         DG, GE. But DF is equal to DG; therefore EF is less than EG." -/
      have hI21 : ‖D F‖ + ‖F E‖ < ‖D G‖ + ‖G E‖ := (Prop21 hDEG.cab hF).1
      rw [hDF_DG] at hI21
      rw [len_symm E F, len_symm E G]
      exact Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_left hI21
    · /- Euclid's figure has F beyond EG, which DF crosses at X. -/
      have hFG : F ≠ G := hDFG.ne₂₃
      have hEG : E ≠ G := hDEG.ne₂₃
      -- therefore the angle DFG is greater than the angle EGF.
      /- The angle EGF is the angle XGF, a part of the angle DGF, since X lies
         between D and F (`angle_lt_of_between`). -/
      have hEGF_DGF : ∠ E G F < ∠ D G F := by
        rw [← angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between (between_symm hEXG)) hFG]
        exact angle_lt_of_between hDFG hDXF
      have hEGF_DFG : ∠ E G F < ∠ D F G := by
        rw [← hDGF]
        exact hEGF_DGF
      -- Therefore the angle EFG is much greater than the angle EGF.
      /- The angle DFG is the angle XFG, a part of the angle EFG, since X lies
         between E and G. -/
      have hDFG_EFG : ∠ D F G < ∠ E F G := by
        rw [← angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between (between_symm hDXF)) hFG.symm]
        exact angle_lt_of_between hEGF hEXG
      have hmuch : ∠ E G F < ∠ E F G := lt_trans hEGF_DFG hDFG_EFG
      -- And, since EFG is a triangle having the angle EFG greater than the angle EGF,
      have hEFG : Triangle E F G := hEGF.acb
      -- and the greater angle is subtended by the greater side, [I. 19]
      -- the side EG is also greater than EF.
      exact Prop19 hEFG (by rw [angle_symm hFG hEG]; exact hmuch)
  -- But EG is equal to BC.
  rw [hBC_EG]
  -- Therefore BC is also greater than EF.
  exact hEF_EG
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.

state.enunciation: If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, but have the base greater than the base, they will also have the one of the angles contained by the equal straight lines greater than the other.
state.lean_proof:
/-- If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, but have the base greater
than the base, they will also have the one of the angles contained by the equal straight lines
greater than the other. -/
theorem Prop25 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖D F‖) (h : ‖E F‖ < ‖B C‖) :
    ∠ E D F < ∠ B A C := by
  -- Let ABC, DEF be two triangles having the two sides AB, AC equal to the two sides DE, DF
  -- respectively, namely AB to DE, and AC to DF; and let the base BC be greater than the base
  -- EF;
  -- I say that the angle BAC is also greater than the angle EDF.
  -- For, if not, it is either equal to it or less.
  /- That an angle not greater than another is equal to it or less is the tacit
     rule of magnitudes `lt_trichotomy` (System E §3.5). -/
  have either : ¬ ∠ E D F < ∠ B A C → ∠ B A C = ∠ E D F ∨ ∠ B A C < ∠ E D F := by
    intro hnot
    rcases lt_trichotomy (∠ B A C) (∠ E D F) with hlt | heq | hgt
    · exact Or.inr hlt
    · exact Or.inl heq
    · exact absurd hgt hnot
  -- Now the angle BAC is not equal to the angle EDF;
  have not_equal : ∠ B A C ≠ ∠ E D F := by
    intro hA
    -- for then the base BC would also have been equal to the base EF, [I. 4]
    /- I.4 gives the bases equal, the triangles equal and the remaining angles
       equal; only the first is wanted here. -/
    have hBC_EF : ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ := (Prop4 hABC hDEF hAB hAC hA).1
    -- but it is not;
    /- It is greater, and a magnitude is not equal to one it is greater than
       (`Magnitude.ne_of_lt`). -/
    have hne : ‖B C‖ ≠ ‖E F‖ := fun heq => Magnitude.ne_of_lt h heq.symm
    -- therefore the angle BAC is not equal to the angle EDF.
    exact hne hBC_EF
  -- Neither again is the angle BAC less than the angle EDF;
  have not_less : ¬ ∠ B A C < ∠ E D F := by
    intro hA
    -- for then the base BC would also have been less than the base EF, [I. 24]
    /- This is I.24 with the triangles exchanged: in DEF the angle at D is
       now the greater, and its sides DE, DF are equal to AB, AC, the
       equalities read the other way round. -/
    have hBC_EF : ‖B C‖ < ‖E F‖ := Prop24 hDEF hABC hAB.symm hAC.symm hA
    -- but it is not;
    /- It is greater, and a magnitude cannot be both less and greater than
       another (`lt_trans`, `lt_irrefl`). -/
    have hnot : ¬ ‖B C‖ < ‖E F‖ := fun hlt => lt_irrefl _ (lt_trans hlt h)
    -- therefore the angle BAC is not less than the angle EDF.
    exact hnot hBC_EF
  -- But it was proved that it is not equal either;
  /- Both ways out are closed; Euclid's division is complete. -/
  have neither : ¬ (∠ B A C = ∠ E D F ∨ ∠ B A C < ∠ E D F) := fun hor =>
    hor.elim not_equal not_less
  -- therefore the angle BAC is greater than the angle EDF.
  /- Reductio ad absurdum: were the angle BAC not greater, the division above
     would make it equal or less, and it is neither. -/
  exact Classical.byContradiction fun hnot => neither (either hnot)
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.

state.commentary:
Euclid's proof constructs nothing. He argues by division, as in I.19: if the angle BAC is not greater than the angle EDF, it is equal to it or less. Equal angles would give equal bases, by I.4, and a less angle a less base, by I.24; but BC is greater than EF. So I.25 is I.24 turned round, and the two together say that when two triangles have two sides equal to two sides, the greater angle and the greater base go together.

Heath passes on Augustus De Morgan's view: "this proposition (as also I. 8) is a purely *logical* consequence of I. 4 and I. 24 in the same way as I. 19 and I. 6 are purely *logical* consequences of I. 18 and I. 5" (vol. 1, p. 300). Our proof bears him out. It builds no figure, and beyond I.4 and I.24 it uses only the three tacit rules of magnitude that carried I.19's division, `lt_trichotomy`, `lt_trans` and `lt_irrefl`. The logic covers I.8 as well, but Euclid could not have proved I.8 that way, since I.24 itself rests on I.8, through I.23. Heath also reports two direct proofs from Proclus, by Menelaus of Alexandria and by Heron, "and they are both interesting" (vol. 1, p. 300); each has to show where a new point falls before it can compare its angles, and Euclid's division never looks at a figure.

**The modern way.** With the sides $b$ and $c$ fixed, the law of cosines gives the angle $\theta$ they contain from the base $a$: $\theta = \arccos\left(\frac{b^{2} + c^{2} - a^{2}}{2bc}\right)$. As $a$ grows the fraction falls, and since the cosine falls as $\theta$ grows from $0$ to $\pi$, the angle rises: the greater base has the greater angle. Read the other way, the same formula is I.24.

state.heath_proof:
Let ABC, DEF be two triangles having the two angles ABC, BCA equal to the two angles DEF, EFD respectively, namely the angle ABC to the angle DEF, and the angle BCA to the angle EFD; and let them also have one side equal to one side, first that adjoining the equal angles, namely BC to EF;

I say that they will also have the remaining sides equal to the remaining sides respectively, namely AB to DE and AC to DF, and the remaining angle to the remaining angle, namely the angle BAC to the angle EDF.

For, if AB is unequal to DE, one of them is greater.

Let AB be greater, and let BG be made equal to DE; and let GC be joined.

Then, since BG is equal to DE, and BC to EF,

the two sides GB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively;

and the angle GBC is equal to the angle DEF;

therefore the base GC is equal to the base DF,

and the triangle GBC is equal to the triangle DEF,

and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles, namely those which the equal sides subtend; [I. 4]

therefore the angle GCB is equal to the angle DFE.

But the angle DFE is by hypothesis equal to the angle BCA;

therefore the angle BCG is equal to the angle BCA,

the less to the greater: which is impossible.

Therefore AB is not unequal to DE,

and is therefore equal to it.

But BC is also equal to EF;

therefore the two sides AB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively,

and the angle ABC is equal to the angle DEF;

therefore the base AC is equal to the base DF,

and the remaining angle BAC is equal to the remaining angle EDF. [I. 4]

Again, let sides subtending equal angles be equal, as AB to DE;

I say again that the remaining sides will be equal to the remaining sides, namely AC to DF and BC to EF, and further the remaining angle BAC is equal to the remaining angle EDF.

For, if BC is unequal to EF, one of them is greater.

Let BC be greater, if possible, and let BH be made equal to EF; let AH be joined.

Then, since BH is equal to EF, and AB to DE,

the two sides AB, BH are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively, and they contain equal angles;

therefore the base AH is equal to the base DF,

and the triangle ABH is equal to the triangle DEF,

and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles, namely those which the equal sides subtend; [I. 4]

therefore the angle BHA is equal to the angle EFD.

But the angle EFD is equal to the angle BCA;

therefore, in the triangle AHC, the exterior angle BHA is equal to the interior and opposite angle BCA:

which is impossible. [I. 16]

Therefore BC is not unequal to EF,

and is therefore equal to it.

But AB is also equal to DE;

therefore the two sides AB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively, and they contain equal angles;

therefore the base AC is equal to the base DF,

the triangle ABC equal to the triangle DEF,

and the remaining angle BAC equal to the remaining angle EDF. [I. 4]

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.

opaque Line : Type

state.enunciation: If two triangles have the two angles equal to two angles respectively, and one side equal to one side, namely, either the side adjoining the equal angles, or that subtending one of the equal angles, they will also have the remaining sides equal to the remaining sides and the remaining angle to the remaining angle.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABC, DEF be two triangles having the two angles ABC, BCA equal to the two angles DEF, EFD respectively, namely the angle ABC to the angle DEF, and the angle BCA to the angle EFD; and let them also have one side equal to one side, first that adjoining the equal angles, namely BC to EF;

I say that they will also have the remaining sides equal to the remaining sides respectively, namely AB to DE and AC to DF, and the remaining angle to the remaining angle, namely the angle BAC to the angle EDF.

For, if AB is unequal to DE, one of them is greater.

Let AB be greater, and let BG be made equal to DE; and let GC be joined.

Then, since BG is equal to DE, and BC to EF,

the two sides GB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively;

and the angle GBC is equal to the angle DEF;

therefore the base GC is equal to the base DF,

and the triangle GBC is equal to the triangle DEF,

and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles, namely those which the equal sides subtend; [I. 4]

therefore the angle GCB is equal to the angle DFE.

But the angle DFE is by hypothesis equal to the angle BCA;

therefore the angle BCG is equal to the angle BCA,

the less to the greater: which is impossible.

Therefore AB is not unequal to DE,

and is therefore equal to it.

But BC is also equal to EF;

therefore the two sides AB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively,

and the angle ABC is equal to the angle DEF;

therefore the base AC is equal to the base DF,

and the remaining angle BAC is equal to the remaining angle EDF. [I. 4]

Again, let sides subtending equal angles be equal, as AB to DE;

I say again that the remaining sides will be equal to the remaining sides, namely AC to DF and BC to EF, and further the remaining angle BAC is equal to the remaining angle EDF.

For, if BC is unequal to EF, one of them is greater.

Let BC be greater, if possible, and let BH be made equal to EF; let AH be joined.

Then, since BH is equal to EF, and AB to DE,

the two sides AB, BH are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively, and they contain equal angles;

therefore the base AH is equal to the base DF,

and the triangle ABH is equal to the triangle DEF,

and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles, namely those which the equal sides subtend; [I. 4]

therefore the angle BHA is equal to the angle EFD.

But the angle EFD is equal to the angle BCA;

therefore, in the triangle AHC, the exterior angle BHA is equal to the interior and opposite angle BCA:

which is impossible. [I. 16]

Therefore BC is not unequal to EF,

and is therefore equal to it.

But AB is also equal to DE;

therefore the two sides AB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively, and they contain equal angles;

therefore the base AC is equal to the base DF,

the triangle ABC equal to the triangle DEF,

and the remaining angle BAC equal to the remaining angle EDF. [I. 4]

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- If two triangles have the two angles equal to two angles respectively, and one side equal to one
side, namely, either the side adjoining the equal angles, or that subtending one of the equal
angles, they will also have the remaining sides equal to the remaining sides and the remaining
angle to the remaining angle. -/
theorem Prop26 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hB : ∠ A B C = ∠ D E F) (hC : ∠ B C A = ∠ E F D)
    (hside : ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ ∨ ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖D F‖ ∧ ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ E D F := by
  -- Let ABC, DEF be two triangles having the two angles ABC, BCA equal to the two angles DEF,
  -- EFD respectively, namely the angle ABC to the angle DEF, and the angle BCA to the angle
  -- EFD; and let them also have one side equal to one side, first that adjoining the equal
  -- angles, namely BC to EF;
  rcases hside with hBC | hAB
    -- I say that they will also have the remaining sides equal to the remaining sides
    -- respectively, namely AB to DE and AC to DF, and the remaining angle to the remaining
    -- angle, namely the angle BAC to the angle EDF.
    -- For, if AB is unequal to DE, one of them is greater.
  · /- The argument for the greater side works with the triangles named either
       way round. We write it once and exchange them below. -/
    have greater : ∀ {A B C D E F : Point}, Triangle A B C → Triangle D E F →
        ∠ A B C = ∠ D E F → ∠ B C A = ∠ E F D → ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ →
        ‖D E‖ < ‖A B‖ → False := by
      intro A B C D E F hABC hDEF hB hC hBC hlt
      -- Let AB be greater, and let BG be made equal to DE; and let GC be joined.
      /- I.3 supplies the cut and says explicitly that G is between B and A. -/
      obtain ⟨G, hBGA, hBG⟩ := Prop3 hDEF.ne₁₂ (by rwa [len_symm B A])
      obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B hABC.ne₁₂
      have hG_AB := on_line_of_between_ends hBGA hB_AB hA_AB
      have hBGC : Triangle B G C := Triangle.of_line hB_AB hG_AB
        (ne_of_between hBGA) (hABC.off_line hA_AB hB_AB)
      obtain ⟨GC, hG_GC, hC_GC⟩ := Postulate1 G C hBGC.ne₂₃
      -- Then, since BG is equal to DE, and BC to EF,
      -- the two sides GB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively;
      have hBG_ED : ‖B G‖ = ‖E D‖ := hBG.trans (len_symm D E)
      -- and the angle GBC is equal to the angle DEF;
      have hGBC : ∠ G B C = ∠ D E F :=
        (angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between hBGA) hABC.ne₂₃.symm).trans hB
      -- therefore the base GC is equal to the base DF,
      obtain ⟨hGC, harea, hG, hC'⟩ := Prop4 hBGC hDEF.bac hBG_ED hBC hGBC
      -- and the triangle GBC is equal to the triangle DEF,
      have : △ G B C = △ D E F := by
        rw [area_swap G B C, area_rotate G C B, area_swap D E F, area_rotate D F E]
        exact harea
      -- and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles, namely those which the
      -- equal sides subtend; [I. 4]
      have : ∠ B G C = ∠ E D F ∧ ∠ B C G = ∠ E F D := ⟨hG, hC'⟩
      -- therefore the angle GCB is equal to the angle DFE.
      have hGCB : ∠ G C B = ∠ D F E :=
        (angle_symm hBGC.ne₂₃ hBGC.ne₁₃).trans
          (hC'.trans (angle_symm hDEF.ne₂₃ hDEF.ne₁₃))
      -- But the angle DFE is by hypothesis equal to the angle BCA;
      have hDFE : ∠ D F E = ∠ B C A :=
        (angle_symm hDEF.ne₁₃ hDEF.ne₂₃).trans hC.symm
      -- therefore the angle BCG is equal to the angle BCA,
      have hBCG : ∠ B C G = ∠ B C A :=
        (angle_symm hBGC.ne₁₃ hBGC.ne₂₃).trans (hGCB.trans hDFE)
      -- the less to the greater: which is impossible.
      have hless := angle_lt_of_between hABC (between_symm hBGA)
      rw [← angle_symm hBGC.ne₁₃ hBGC.ne₂₃,
        ← angle_symm hABC.ne₂₃ hABC.ne₁₃, hBCG] at hless
      exact lt_irrefl _ hless
    -- Therefore AB is not unequal to DE,
    -- and is therefore equal to it.
    have hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖ := by
      rcases lt_trichotomy ‖A B‖ ‖D E‖ with hlt | heq | hgt
      · exact False.elim (greater hDEF hABC hB.symm hC.symm hBC.symm hlt)
      · exact heq
      · exact False.elim (greater hABC hDEF hB hC hBC hgt)
    -- But BC is also equal to EF;
    -- therefore the two sides AB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively,
    -- and the angle ABC is equal to the angle DEF;
    have hBA_ED : ‖B A‖ = ‖E D‖ :=
      (len_symm B A).trans (hAB.trans (len_symm D E))
    -- therefore the base AC is equal to the base DF,
    obtain ⟨hAC, -, hA, -⟩ := Prop4 hABC.bac hDEF.bac hBA_ED hBC hB
    -- and the remaining angle BAC is equal to the remaining angle EDF. [I. 4]
    exact ⟨hAB, hAC, hBC, hA⟩
    -- Again, let sides subtending equal angles be equal, as AB to DE;
    -- I say again that the remaining sides will be equal to the remaining sides, namely AC to DF
    -- and BC to EF, and further the remaining angle BAC is equal to the remaining angle EDF.
    -- For, if BC is unequal to EF, one of them is greater.
  · /- Again either triangle may have the greater side. -/
    have greater : ∀ {A B C D E F : Point}, Triangle A B C → Triangle D E F →
        ∠ A B C = ∠ D E F → ∠ B C A = ∠ E F D → ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖ →
        ‖E F‖ < ‖B C‖ → False := by
      intro A B C D E F hABC hDEF hB hC hAB hlt
      -- Let BC be greater, if possible, and let BH be made equal to EF; let AH be joined.
      obtain ⟨H, hBHC, hBH⟩ := Prop3 hDEF.ne₂₃ hlt
      obtain ⟨BC, hB_BC, hC_BC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hABC.ne₂₃
      have hH_BC := on_line_of_between_ends hBHC hB_BC hC_BC
      have hBHA : Triangle B H A := Triangle.of_line hB_BC hH_BC
        (ne_of_between hBHC) (hABC.bca.off_line hB_BC hC_BC)
      have hCHA : Triangle C H A := Triangle.of_line hC_BC hH_BC
        (ne_of_between (between_symm hBHC)) (hABC.bca.off_line hB_BC hC_BC)
      obtain ⟨AH, hA_AH, hH_AH⟩ := Postulate1 A H hBHA.ne₂₃.symm
      -- Then, since BH is equal to EF, and AB to DE,
      -- the two sides AB, BH are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively, and they contain
      -- equal angles;
      have hBA_ED : ‖B A‖ = ‖E D‖ :=
        (len_symm B A).trans (hAB.trans (len_symm D E))
      have hABH : ∠ A B H = ∠ D E F :=
        (angle_onRay_right (OnRay.of_between hBHC) hABC.ne₁₂).trans hB
      -- therefore the base AH is equal to the base DF,
      obtain ⟨hAH, harea, hA, hH⟩ := Prop4 hBHA.acb hDEF.bac hBA_ED hBH hABH
      -- and the triangle ABH is equal to the triangle DEF,
      have : △ A B H = △ D E F := by
        rw [area_swap A B H, area_rotate A H B, area_swap D E F, area_rotate D F E]
        exact harea
      -- and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles, namely those which the
      -- equal sides subtend; [I. 4]
      have : ∠ B A H = ∠ E D F ∧ ∠ B H A = ∠ E F D := ⟨hA, hH⟩
      -- therefore the angle BHA is equal to the angle EFD.
      have hBHA_EFD : ∠ B H A = ∠ E F D := hH
      -- But the angle EFD is equal to the angle BCA;
      have hEFD : ∠ E F D = ∠ B C A := hC.symm
      -- therefore, in the triangle AHC, the exterior angle BHA is equal to the interior and
      -- opposite angle BCA:
      have hBHA_BCA : ∠ B H A = ∠ B C A := hBHA_EFD.trans hEFD
      -- which is impossible. [I. 16]
      have hless := (Prop16 hCHA.cab (between_symm hBHC)).1
      rw [angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between (between_symm hBHC)) hABC.ne₁₃,
        angle_symm hBHA.ne₂₃.symm hBHA.ne₁₂, hBHA_BCA] at hless
      exact lt_irrefl _ hless
    -- Therefore BC is not unequal to EF,
    -- and is therefore equal to it.
    have hBC : ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ := by
      rcases lt_trichotomy ‖B C‖ ‖E F‖ with hlt | heq | hgt
      · exact False.elim (greater hDEF hABC hB.symm hC.symm hAB.symm hlt)
      · exact heq
      · exact False.elim (greater hABC hDEF hB hC hAB hgt)
    -- But AB is also equal to DE;
    -- therefore the two sides AB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively, and they
    -- contain equal angles;
    have hBA_ED : ‖B A‖ = ‖E D‖ :=
      (len_symm B A).trans (hAB.trans (len_symm D E))
    -- therefore the base AC is equal to the base DF,
    obtain ⟨hAC, harea, hA, -⟩ := Prop4 hABC.bac hDEF.bac hBA_ED hBC hB
    -- the triangle ABC equal to the triangle DEF,
    have : △ A B C = △ D E F := by
      rw [area_swap A B C, area_rotate A C B, area_swap D E F, area_rotate D F E]
      exact harea
    -- and the remaining angle BAC equal to the remaining angle EDF. [I. 4]
    have hBAC : ∠ B A C = ∠ E D F := hA
    -- Therefore etc.
    exact ⟨hAB, hAC, hBC, hBAC⟩
  -- Q. E. D.

helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop16:
/-- In any triangle, if one of the sides be produced, the exterior angle is greater than either of
the interior and opposite angles. -/
theorem Prop16 {A B C D : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hBCD : Between B C D) :
    ∠ C B A < ∠ A C D ∧ ∠ B A C < ∠ A C D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop3:
/-- Given two unequal straight lines, to cut off from the greater a straight line equal to the
less. -/
theorem Prop3 {A B C₁ C₂ : Point} (hC : C₁ ≠ C₂) (h : ‖C₁ C₂‖ < ‖A B‖) :
    ∃ E : Point, Between A E B ∧ ‖A E‖ = ‖C₁ C₂‖
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop4:
/-- If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles
contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the base, the
triangle will be equal to the triangle, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining
angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend. -/
theorem Prop4 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖D F‖) (hA : ∠ B A C = ∠ E D F) :
    ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ ∧ △ A B C = △ D E F ∧ ∠ A B C = ∠ D E F ∧ ∠ A C B = ∠ D F E
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.of_between:
/-- A point between A and B is on the ray from A through B. -/
theorem OnRay.of_between (h : Between A P B) : OnRay P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.symm:
/-- P is on the ray from A through B exactly when B is on the ray from A
through P: they are one and the same ray. -/
theorem OnRay.symm (h : OnRay P A B) : OnRay B A P
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate1:
/-- **Postulate 1.** To draw a straight line from any point to any point. -/
axiom Postulate1 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.angle_symm:
/-- The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4) -/
axiom angle_symm (hAB : A ≠ B) (hCB : C ≠ B) : ∠ A B C = ∠ C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.area_rotate:
/-- The triangle ABC is the triangle CAB. (Metric 8) -/
axiom area_rotate (A B C : Point) : △ A B C = △ C A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.area_swap:
/-- The triangle ABC is the triangle ACB. (Metric 8) -/
axiom area_swap (A B C : Point) : △ A B C = △ A C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_symm:

axiom between_symm (h : Between A B C) : Between C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.len_symm:

helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.lt_trichotomy:

helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between_ends:

def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.acb:

theorem Triangle.acb (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle A C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.bac:
/-- The triangle ABC, named the other way round, as BAC. -/
theorem Triangle.bac (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle B A C

theorem Triangle.bca (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle B C A
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.cab:
/-- The triangle ABC, named from C, as CAB. -/
theorem Triangle.cab (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle C A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₁₂:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₁₂ (h : Triangle A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₁₃:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₁₃ (h : Triangle A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₂₃:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₂₃ (h : Triangle A B C) : B ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.of_line:
/-- Two different points of a straight line, and a third point off it, make a
triangle. -/
theorem Triangle.of_line {P Q R : Point} (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L) (hPQ : P ≠ Q)
    (hR : ¬ OnLine R L) : Triangle P Q R
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.off_line:
/-- In the triangle ABC, the corner C is off every straight line through A
and B. -/
theorem Triangle.off_line (h : Triangle A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    ¬ OnLine C L
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_lt_of_between:
/-- The part is less than the whole, for angles: if R lies between P and Q, and
V is off the straight line PQ, the angle RVQ is less than the angle PVQ. For
PVQ is made up of PVR and RVQ (`angle_add_of_between`), and PVR is
something, since R is off VP (`Triangle.angle_pos`). [C.N. 5] -/
theorem angle_lt_of_between {V P Q R : Point} (hPQV : Triangle P Q V) (h : Between P R Q) :
    ∠ R V Q < ∠ P V Q
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_onRay_left:
/-- One arm traced through another point of its ray: if B' is on the ray from A
through B, the angle B'AC is the angle BAC. (System E, Diagram-angle 4) -/
theorem angle_onRay_left {B' : Point} (hB : OnRay B' A B) (hCA : C ≠ A) :
    ∠ B' A C = ∠ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_onRay_right:
/-- The other arm traced through another point of its ray: if C' is on the ray
from A through C, the angle BAC' is the angle BAC. (System E,
Diagram-angle 4) -/
theorem angle_onRay_right {C' : Point} (hC : OnRay C' A C) (hBA : B ≠ A) :
    ∠ B A C' = ∠ B A C

I.3.enunciation: Given two unequal straight lines, to cut off from the greater a straight line equal to the less.

I.4.enunciation: If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the base, the triangle will be equal to the triangle, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend.

definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area

state.commentary:
Euclid takes the equal side in each of its two places. When it adjoins the equal angles, he supposes AB greater than DE and cuts off BG equal to DE; I.4 then makes the angle BCG equal to BCA, "the less to the greater". When it subtends one of them, he supposes BC greater than EF and cuts off BH equal to EF; now I.4 makes the exterior angle BHA of the triangle AHC equal to the interior and opposite angle BCA, which I.16 forbids. Either way the sides are equal, and I.4 finishes. Heath's figure, and ours, shows G and H together, though each belongs to a supposition of its own.

Both contradictions want the cut point inside: BCG has to be a part of BCA, and BHA an exterior angle of the triangle AHC. I.3 gives that when it cuts BG off from BA and BH off from BC, putting G between B and A, and H between B and C. Euclid lets AB be the greater, though DE may as well be; we answer that case by exchanging the triangles.

**"The distance of ships in the sea."** Proclus tells a story: "Eudemus in his geometrical history refers this theorem to Thales. For he says that, in the method by which they say that Thales proved the distance of ships in the sea, it was necessary to make use of this theorem" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 304). Heath guesses that Thales stood on a tower with an upright stick and a cross-piece on a nail. He pointed the cross-piece at the ship, then turned the stick, still upright, until the cross-piece pointed at a mark on the shore. The two triangles share the tower and the angles at its ends, so the mark was as far off as the ship (vol. 1, p. 305).

The other way to prove I.26, by applying one triangle to the other, "was very early discovered", Heath says, at least for the side adjoining the equal angles; an-Nairīzī gives it, "observing that the proof is one which he had found, but of which he did not know the author" (vol. 1, p. 303). Euclid's proof moves nothing, and leaves superposition where it was, inside I.4.

**The modern way.** Write $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ for the angles at A, B, C and $a$, $b$, $c$ for the sides opposite them. The sine rule, $a/\sin\alpha = b/\sin\beta = c/\sin\gamma$, settles I.26 at once: two angles give the third, $\gamma = \pi - \alpha - \beta$, and the one side then gives the other two. But that third angle comes from I.32, whose proof uses Postulate 5, and Euclid's proof of I.26 does without it.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABC, DEF be two triangles having the two angles ABC, BCA equal to the two angles DEF, EFD respectively, namely the angle ABC to the angle DEF, and the angle BCA to the angle EFD; and let them also have one side equal to one side, first that adjoining the equal angles, namely BC to EF;

I say that they will also have the remaining sides equal to the remaining sides respectively, namely AB to DE and AC to DF, and the remaining angle to the remaining angle, namely the angle BAC to the angle EDF.

For, if AB is unequal to DE, one of them is greater.

Let AB be greater, and let BG be made equal to DE; and let GC be joined.

Then, since BG is equal to DE, and BC to EF,

the two sides GB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively;

and the angle GBC is equal to the angle DEF;

therefore the base GC is equal to the base DF,

and the triangle GBC is equal to the triangle DEF,

and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles, namely those which the equal sides subtend; [I. 4]

therefore the angle GCB is equal to the angle DFE.

But the angle DFE is by hypothesis equal to the angle BCA;

therefore the angle BCG is equal to the angle BCA,

the less to the greater: which is impossible.

Therefore AB is not unequal to DE,

and is therefore equal to it.

But BC is also equal to EF;

therefore the two sides AB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively,

and the angle ABC is equal to the angle DEF;

therefore the base AC is equal to the base DF,

and the remaining angle BAC is equal to the remaining angle EDF. [I. 4]

Again, let sides subtending equal angles be equal, as AB to DE;

I say again that the remaining sides will be equal to the remaining sides, namely AC to DF and BC to EF, and further the remaining angle BAC is equal to the remaining angle EDF.

For, if BC is unequal to EF, one of them is greater.

Let BC be greater, if possible, and let BH be made equal to EF; let AH be joined.

Then, since BH is equal to EF, and AB to DE,

the two sides AB, BH are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively, and they contain equal angles;

therefore the base AH is equal to the base DF,

and the triangle ABH is equal to the triangle DEF,

and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles, namely those which the equal sides subtend; [I. 4]

therefore the angle BHA is equal to the angle EFD.

But the angle EFD is equal to the angle BCA;

therefore, in the triangle AHC, the exterior angle BHA is equal to the interior and opposite angle BCA:

which is impossible. [I. 16]

Therefore BC is not unequal to EF,

and is therefore equal to it.

But AB is also equal to DE;

therefore the two sides AB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively, and they contain equal angles;

therefore the base AC is equal to the base DF,

the triangle ABC equal to the triangle DEF,

and the remaining angle BAC equal to the remaining angle EDF. [I. 4]

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- If two triangles have the two angles equal to two angles respectively, and one side equal to one
side, namely, either the side adjoining the equal angles, or that subtending one of the equal
angles, they will also have the remaining sides equal to the remaining sides and the remaining
angle to the remaining angle. -/
theorem Prop26 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hB : ∠ A B C = ∠ D E F) (hC : ∠ B C A = ∠ E F D)
    (hside : ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ ∨ ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖D F‖ ∧ ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ E D F := by
  -- Let ABC, DEF be two triangles having the two angles ABC, BCA equal to the two angles DEF,
  -- EFD respectively, namely the angle ABC to the angle DEF, and the angle BCA to the angle
  -- EFD; and let them also have one side equal to one side, first that adjoining the equal
  -- angles, namely BC to EF;
  rcases hside with hBC | hAB
    -- I say that they will also have the remaining sides equal to the remaining sides
    -- respectively, namely AB to DE and AC to DF, and the remaining angle to the remaining
    -- angle, namely the angle BAC to the angle EDF.
    -- For, if AB is unequal to DE, one of them is greater.
  · /- The argument for the greater side works with the triangles named either
       way round. We write it once and exchange them below. -/
    have greater : ∀ {A B C D E F : Point}, Triangle A B C → Triangle D E F →
        ∠ A B C = ∠ D E F → ∠ B C A = ∠ E F D → ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ →
        ‖D E‖ < ‖A B‖ → False := by
      intro A B C D E F hABC hDEF hB hC hBC hlt
      -- Let AB be greater, and let BG be made equal to DE; and let GC be joined.
      /- I.3 supplies the cut and says explicitly that G is between B and A. -/
      obtain ⟨G, hBGA, hBG⟩ := Prop3 hDEF.ne₁₂ (by rwa [len_symm B A])
      obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B hABC.ne₁₂
      have hG_AB := on_line_of_between_ends hBGA hB_AB hA_AB
      have hBGC : Triangle B G C := Triangle.of_line hB_AB hG_AB
        (ne_of_between hBGA) (hABC.off_line hA_AB hB_AB)
      obtain ⟨GC, hG_GC, hC_GC⟩ := Postulate1 G C hBGC.ne₂₃
      -- Then, since BG is equal to DE, and BC to EF,
      -- the two sides GB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively;
      have hBG_ED : ‖B G‖ = ‖E D‖ := hBG.trans (len_symm D E)
      -- and the angle GBC is equal to the angle DEF;
      have hGBC : ∠ G B C = ∠ D E F :=
        (angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between hBGA) hABC.ne₂₃.symm).trans hB
      -- therefore the base GC is equal to the base DF,
      obtain ⟨hGC, harea, hG, hC'⟩ := Prop4 hBGC hDEF.bac hBG_ED hBC hGBC
      -- and the triangle GBC is equal to the triangle DEF,
      have : △ G B C = △ D E F := by
        rw [area_swap G B C, area_rotate G C B, area_swap D E F, area_rotate D F E]
        exact harea
      -- and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles, namely those which the
      -- equal sides subtend; [I. 4]
      have : ∠ B G C = ∠ E D F ∧ ∠ B C G = ∠ E F D := ⟨hG, hC'⟩
      -- therefore the angle GCB is equal to the angle DFE.
      have hGCB : ∠ G C B = ∠ D F E :=
        (angle_symm hBGC.ne₂₃ hBGC.ne₁₃).trans
          (hC'.trans (angle_symm hDEF.ne₂₃ hDEF.ne₁₃))
      -- But the angle DFE is by hypothesis equal to the angle BCA;
      have hDFE : ∠ D F E = ∠ B C A :=
        (angle_symm hDEF.ne₁₃ hDEF.ne₂₃).trans hC.symm
      -- therefore the angle BCG is equal to the angle BCA,
      have hBCG : ∠ B C G = ∠ B C A :=
        (angle_symm hBGC.ne₁₃ hBGC.ne₂₃).trans (hGCB.trans hDFE)
      -- the less to the greater: which is impossible.
      have hless := angle_lt_of_between hABC (between_symm hBGA)
      rw [← angle_symm hBGC.ne₁₃ hBGC.ne₂₃,
        ← angle_symm hABC.ne₂₃ hABC.ne₁₃, hBCG] at hless
      exact lt_irrefl _ hless
    -- Therefore AB is not unequal to DE,
    -- and is therefore equal to it.
    have hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖ := by
      rcases lt_trichotomy ‖A B‖ ‖D E‖ with hlt | heq | hgt
      · exact False.elim (greater hDEF hABC hB.symm hC.symm hBC.symm hlt)
      · exact heq
      · exact False.elim (greater hABC hDEF hB hC hBC hgt)
    -- But BC is also equal to EF;
    -- therefore the two sides AB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively,
    -- and the angle ABC is equal to the angle DEF;
    have hBA_ED : ‖B A‖ = ‖E D‖ :=
      (len_symm B A).trans (hAB.trans (len_symm D E))
    -- therefore the base AC is equal to the base DF,
    obtain ⟨hAC, -, hA, -⟩ := Prop4 hABC.bac hDEF.bac hBA_ED hBC hB
    -- and the remaining angle BAC is equal to the remaining angle EDF. [I. 4]
    exact ⟨hAB, hAC, hBC, hA⟩
    -- Again, let sides subtending equal angles be equal, as AB to DE;
    -- I say again that the remaining sides will be equal to the remaining sides, namely AC to DF
    -- and BC to EF, and further the remaining angle BAC is equal to the remaining angle EDF.
    -- For, if BC is unequal to EF, one of them is greater.
  · /- Again either triangle may have the greater side. -/
    have greater : ∀ {A B C D E F : Point}, Triangle A B C → Triangle D E F →
        ∠ A B C = ∠ D E F → ∠ B C A = ∠ E F D → ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖ →
        ‖E F‖ < ‖B C‖ → False := by
      intro A B C D E F hABC hDEF hB hC hAB hlt
      -- Let BC be greater, if possible, and let BH be made equal to EF; let AH be joined.
      obtain ⟨H, hBHC, hBH⟩ := Prop3 hDEF.ne₂₃ hlt
      obtain ⟨BC, hB_BC, hC_BC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hABC.ne₂₃
      have hH_BC := on_line_of_between_ends hBHC hB_BC hC_BC
      have hBHA : Triangle B H A := Triangle.of_line hB_BC hH_BC
        (ne_of_between hBHC) (hABC.bca.off_line hB_BC hC_BC)
      have hCHA : Triangle C H A := Triangle.of_line hC_BC hH_BC
        (ne_of_between (between_symm hBHC)) (hABC.bca.off_line hB_BC hC_BC)
      obtain ⟨AH, hA_AH, hH_AH⟩ := Postulate1 A H hBHA.ne₂₃.symm
      -- Then, since BH is equal to EF, and AB to DE,
      -- the two sides AB, BH are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively, and they contain
      -- equal angles;
      have hBA_ED : ‖B A‖ = ‖E D‖ :=
        (len_symm B A).trans (hAB.trans (len_symm D E))
      have hABH : ∠ A B H = ∠ D E F :=
        (angle_onRay_right (OnRay.of_between hBHC) hABC.ne₁₂).trans hB
      -- therefore the base AH is equal to the base DF,
      obtain ⟨hAH, harea, hA, hH⟩ := Prop4 hBHA.acb hDEF.bac hBA_ED hBH hABH
      -- and the triangle ABH is equal to the triangle DEF,
      have : △ A B H = △ D E F := by
        rw [area_swap A B H, area_rotate A H B, area_swap D E F, area_rotate D F E]
        exact harea
      -- and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles, namely those which the
      -- equal sides subtend; [I. 4]
      have : ∠ B A H = ∠ E D F ∧ ∠ B H A = ∠ E F D := ⟨hA, hH⟩
      -- therefore the angle BHA is equal to the angle EFD.
      have hBHA_EFD : ∠ B H A = ∠ E F D := hH
      -- But the angle EFD is equal to the angle BCA;
      have hEFD : ∠ E F D = ∠ B C A := hC.symm
      -- therefore, in the triangle AHC, the exterior angle BHA is equal to the interior and
      -- opposite angle BCA:
      have hBHA_BCA : ∠ B H A = ∠ B C A := hBHA_EFD.trans hEFD
      -- which is impossible. [I. 16]
      have hless := (Prop16 hCHA.cab (between_symm hBHC)).1
      rw [angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between (between_symm hBHC)) hABC.ne₁₃,
        angle_symm hBHA.ne₂₃.symm hBHA.ne₁₂, hBHA_BCA] at hless
      exact lt_irrefl _ hless
    -- Therefore BC is not unequal to EF,
    -- and is therefore equal to it.
    have hBC : ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ := by
      rcases lt_trichotomy ‖B C‖ ‖E F‖ with hlt | heq | hgt
      · exact False.elim (greater hDEF hABC hB.symm hC.symm hAB.symm hlt)
      · exact heq
      · exact False.elim (greater hABC hDEF hB hC hAB hgt)
    -- But AB is also equal to DE;
    -- therefore the two sides AB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively, and they
    -- contain equal angles;
    have hBA_ED : ‖B A‖ = ‖E D‖ :=
      (len_symm B A).trans (hAB.trans (len_symm D E))
    -- therefore the base AC is equal to the base DF,
    obtain ⟨hAC, harea, hA, -⟩ := Prop4 hABC.bac hDEF.bac hBA_ED hBC hB
    -- the triangle ABC equal to the triangle DEF,
    have : △ A B C = △ D E F := by
      rw [area_swap A B C, area_rotate A C B, area_swap D E F, area_rotate D F E]
      exact harea
    -- and the remaining angle BAC equal to the remaining angle EDF. [I. 4]
    have hBAC : ∠ B A C = ∠ E D F := hA
    -- Therefore etc.
    exact ⟨hAB, hAC, hBC, hBAC⟩
  -- Q. E. D.

/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M

  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq

the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/

  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M

state.heath_proof:
For let the straight line EF falling on the two straight lines AB, CD make the alternate angles AEF, EFD equal to one another;

I say that AB is parallel to CD.

For, if not, AB, CD when produced will meet either in the direction of B, D or towards A, C.

Let them be produced and meet, in the direction of B, D, at G.

Then, in the triangle GEF,

the exterior angle AEF is equal to the interior and opposite angle EFG:

which is impossible. [I. 16]

Therefore AB, CD when produced will not meet in the direction of B, D.

state.lean_proof:
/-- If a straight line falling on two straight lines make the alternate angles equal to one another,
the straight lines will be parallel to one another. -/
theorem Prop27 {A B C D E F : Point} (hAEB : Between A E B) (hCFD : Between C F D)
    (hAD : OppositeSidesOf A D E F) (h : ∠ A E F = ∠ E F D) :
    AreParallel A B C D := by
  -- For let the straight line EF falling on the two straight lines AB, CD make the alternate
  -- angles AEF, EFD equal to one another;
  /- The straight lines AB, CD and EF, drawn whole (Post. 1). EF falls on AB at E and on
     CD at F, and A and D are on opposite sides of it, so neither is on it. -/
  have hAB : A ≠ B := ne_of_between_ends hAEB
  have hCD : C ≠ D := ne_of_between_ends hCFD
  have hEF : E ≠ F := hAD.1
  obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B hAB
  obtain ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD⟩ := Postulate1 C D hCD
  obtain ⟨EF, hE_EF, hF_EF⟩ := Postulate1 E F hEF
  have hE_AB : OnLine E AB := on_line_of_between_ends hAEB hA_AB hB_AB
  have hF_CD : OnLine F CD := on_line_of_between_ends hCFD hC_CD hD_CD
  have hAD_EF : OppositeSides A D EF := hAD.oppositeSides hE_EF hF_EF
  -- I say that AB is parallel to CD.
  -- For, if not, AB, CD when produced will meet either in the direction of B, D or towards A,
  -- C.
  /- A point where they meet lies on D's side of EF or on A's (System E,
     Generalities 1 and Same side 5): these are Euclid's two directions, for B lies
     on D's side, and C on A's. -/
  have either : ∀ G : Point, OnLine G AB → OnLine G CD →
      SameSideOf G D E F ∨ SameSideOf G A E F := by
    intro G hG_AB hG_CD
    have hG_EF : ¬ OnLine G EF := by
      intro hG_EF
      by_cases hGE : G = E
      · rw [hGE] at hG_CD
        exact hAD_EF.2.1 (line_unique hEF hG_CD hF_CD hE_EF hF_EF ▸ hD_CD)
      · exact hAD_EF.1 (line_unique hGE hG_AB hE_AB hG_EF hE_EF ▸ hA_AB)
    rcases same_side_or hAD_EF.2.1 hAD_EF.1 hG_EF (fun hs => hAD_EF.2.2 (same_side_symm hs))
      with hs | hs
    · exact Or.inl (SameSideOf.of_line hEF hE_EF hF_EF (same_side_symm hs))
    · exact Or.inr (SameSideOf.of_line hEF hE_EF hF_EF (same_side_symm hs))
  /- Euclid's argument, given once for any letters: if EF falls on AB and CD, making
     the alternate angles AEF, EFD equal, then AB and CD do not meet on D's side of
     EF. -/
  have not_meet : ∀ {A B C D E F G : Point}, Between A E B → Between C F D →
      OppositeSidesOf A D E F → ∠ A E F = ∠ E F D → Collinear A B G → Collinear C D G →
      ¬ SameSideOf G D E F := by
    -- Let them be produced and meet, in the direction of B, D, at G.
    rintro A B C D E F G hAEB hCFD hAD h ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB, hG_AB⟩ ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD, hG_CD⟩
      hG
    have hE_AB : OnLine E AB := on_line_of_between_ends hAEB hA_AB hB_AB
    have hF_CD : OnLine F CD := on_line_of_between_ends hCFD hC_CD hD_CD
    -- Then, in the triangle GEF,
    /- G is on one side of EF, so it is off EF, and GEF is a triangle. -/
    have hEFG : Triangle E F G := hG.triangle
    have hE_F : E ≠ F := hEFG.ne₁₂
    have hF_G : F ≠ G := hEFG.ne₂₃
    have hE_G : E ≠ G := hEFG.ne₁₃
    /- G lies on CD, on D's side of EF, so on the ray from F through D, and the angle
       EFG is the angle EFD (`OnRay.of_sameSideOf`, `angle_onRay_right`). -/
    have hG_FD : OnRay G F D := OnRay.of_sameSideOf hG.swap ⟨CD, hF_CD, hD_CD, hG_CD⟩ hF_G.symm
    have hEFG_EFD : ∠ E F G = ∠ E F D := angle_onRay_right hG_FD hE_F
    /- B is on D's side of EF too, for E lies between A and B, and A is on the other
       side. So G lies on the ray from E through B, and E between A and G: AE is GE
       produced, and the angle AEF is exterior to the triangle GEF (`OnRay.between`). -/
    have hBD : SameSideOf B D E F := hAD.sameSideOf_of_between hAEB
    have hG_EB : OnRay G E B :=
      OnRay.of_sameSideOf (hG.trans hBD.symm) ⟨AB, hE_AB, hB_AB, hG_AB⟩ hE_G.symm
    have hAEG : Between A E G := hG_EB.between hAEB
    -- the exterior angle AEF is equal to the interior and opposite angle EFG:
    have hAEF_EFG : ∠ A E F = ∠ E F G := h.trans hEFG_EFD.symm
    -- which is impossible. [I. 16]
    /- I.16, in the triangle FGE with GE produced to A: the exterior angle FEA is
       greater than the interior and opposite angle GFE. -/
    have hGFE_FEA : ∠ G F E < ∠ F E A := (Prop16 hEFG.bca (between_symm hAEG)).2
    rw [angle_symm hF_G.symm hE_F, angle_symm hE_F.symm (ne_of_between hAEB), hAEF_EFG]
      at hGFE_FEA
    exact lt_irrefl _ hGFE_FEA
  -- Therefore AB, CD when produced will not meet in the direction of B, D.
  have hBD : ∀ G : Point, OnLine G AB → OnLine G CD → ¬ SameSideOf G D E F :=
    fun G hG_AB hG_CD =>
      not_meet hAEB hCFD hAD h ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB, hG_AB⟩ ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD, hG_CD⟩
  -- Similarly it can be proved that neither will they meet towards A, C.
  /- The same argument, with the figure read from the other end: EF, as FE, falls on DC
     at F and on BA at E, and the alternate angles DFE, FEA are the angles EFD, AEF. -/
  have hDFE_FEA : ∠ D F E = ∠ F E A :=
    (angle_symm (ne_of_between (between_symm hCFD)) hEF).trans
      (h.symm.trans (angle_symm (ne_of_between hAEB) hEF.symm))
  have hAC : ∀ G : Point, OnLine G AB → OnLine G CD → ¬ SameSideOf G A F E :=
    fun G hG_AB hG_CD =>
      not_meet (between_symm hCFD) (between_symm hAEB) hAD.symm.swap hDFE_FEA
        ⟨CD, hD_CD, hC_CD, hG_CD⟩ ⟨AB, hB_AB, hA_AB, hG_AB⟩
  -- But straight lines which do not meet in either direction are parallel; [Def. 23]
  have hDef23 : (∀ G : Point, OnLine G AB → ¬ OnLine G CD) → AreParallel A B C D :=
    AreParallel.of_not_meet hAB hCD hA_AB hB_AB hC_CD hD_CD
  -- therefore AB is parallel to CD.
  exact hDef23 fun G hG_AB hG_CD =>
    (either G hG_AB hG_CD).elim (hBD G hG_AB hG_CD) (fun hGA => hAC G hG_AB hG_CD hGA.swap)
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.

state.commentary:
"With this proposition begins the second section of the first Book," Heath writes (vol. 1, p. 308): the section on parallels, which the areas to come will rest on. EF falls on AB and CD and makes the alternate angles AEF, EFD equal, on opposite sides of EF and between AB and CD. Were AB and CD to meet at G, they would close a triangle GEF whose exterior angle AEF is equal to the interior and opposite angle EFG, and I.16 forbids it. So they never meet, and Definition I.23 calls them parallel.

From two passages of Aristotle Heath concludes that the proposition is older than Euclid: "It seems clear then from Aristotle that I. 27, 28 at least are pre-Euclidean, and that it was only in I. 29 that Euclid made a change by using his Postulate" (vol. 1, p. 309). Augustus De Morgan saw that I.27 "is a *logical* equivalent of I. 16" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 309), the same fact turned round.

**"In the direction of B, D."** Literally, Heath notes, it is "towards the *parts* B, D or towards A, C" (vol. 1, p. 308), and we read the parts as the two sides of EF. A point where AB and CD meet is off EF, for AB meets EF at E alone, and were it E, CD would be EF itself; so it lies on one side of EF or the other. On D's side, G lies on the rays from E through B and from F through D, so AEF is exterior to the triangle GEF, and EFG is the given angle EFD; we prove both. Heath's figure can only suggest them: it draws AB and CD as though parallel and bends BG and DG to meet at G, since no straight lines can do what the supposition asks. Ours draws the supposition straight, A, E, B, G on one straight line and C, F, D, G on another, so the angles AEF and EFD, supposed equal, plainly are not.

**The modern way.** Let $\vec{u}$ and $\vec{v}$ be the unit vectors from E towards B and from F towards D, and $\vec{w} = \mathrm{E - F}$. The angle AEF is the angle between $\vec{u}$ and $\vec{w}$, and EFD the angle between $\vec{w}$ and $\vec{v}$; since B and D lie on one side of EF, equal angles make $\vec{u} = \vec{v}$. A common point $\mathrm{E} + s\vec{u} = \mathrm{F} + t\vec{u}$ would make $\vec{w}$ a multiple of $\vec{u}$ and put F on AB, so that EF, which falls on AB, would be AB itself.
state.heath_proof:
For let the straight line EF falling on the two straight lines AB, CD make the alternate angles AEF, EFD equal to one another;

I say that AB is parallel to CD.

For, if not, AB, CD when produced will meet either in the direction of B, D or towards A, C.

Let them be produced and meet, in the direction of B, D, at G.

Then, in the triangle GEF,

the exterior angle AEF is equal to the interior and opposite angle EFG:

which is impossible. [I. 16]

Therefore AB, CD when produced will not meet in the direction of B, D.

Similarly it can be proved that neither will they meet towards A, C.

But straight lines which do not meet in either direction are parallel; [Def. 23]

therefore AB is parallel to CD.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- If a straight line falling on two straight lines make the alternate angles equal to one another,
the straight lines will be parallel to one another. -/
theorem Prop27 {A B C D E F : Point} (hAEB : Between A E B) (hCFD : Between C F D)
    (hAD : OppositeSidesOf A D E F) (h : ∠ A E F = ∠ E F D) :
    AreParallel A B C D := by
  -- For let the straight line EF falling on the two straight lines AB, CD make the alternate
  -- angles AEF, EFD equal to one another;
  /- The straight lines AB, CD and EF, drawn whole (Post. 1). EF falls on AB at E and on
     CD at F, and A and D are on opposite sides of it, so neither is on it. -/
  have hAB : A ≠ B := ne_of_between_ends hAEB
  have hCD : C ≠ D := ne_of_between_ends hCFD
  have hEF : E ≠ F := hAD.1
  obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B hAB
  obtain ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD⟩ := Postulate1 C D hCD
  obtain ⟨EF, hE_EF, hF_EF⟩ := Postulate1 E F hEF
  have hE_AB : OnLine E AB := on_line_of_between_ends hAEB hA_AB hB_AB
  have hF_CD : OnLine F CD := on_line_of_between_ends hCFD hC_CD hD_CD
  have hAD_EF : OppositeSides A D EF := hAD.oppositeSides hE_EF hF_EF
  -- I say that AB is parallel to CD.
  -- For, if not, AB, CD when produced will meet either in the direction of B, D or towards A,
  -- C.
  /- A point where they meet lies on D's side of EF or on A's (System E,
     Generalities 1 and Same side 5): these are Euclid's two directions, for B lies
     on D's side, and C on A's. -/
  have either : ∀ G : Point, OnLine G AB → OnLine G CD →
      SameSideOf G D E F ∨ SameSideOf G A E F := by
    intro G hG_AB hG_CD
    have hG_EF : ¬ OnLine G EF := by
      intro hG_EF
      by_cases hGE : G = E
      · rw [hGE] at hG_CD
        exact hAD_EF.2.1 (line_unique hEF hG_CD hF_CD hE_EF hF_EF ▸ hD_CD)
      · exact hAD_EF.1 (line_unique hGE hG_AB hE_AB hG_EF hE_EF ▸ hA_AB)
    rcases same_side_or hAD_EF.2.1 hAD_EF.1 hG_EF (fun hs => hAD_EF.2.2 (same_side_symm hs))
      with hs | hs
    · exact Or.inl (SameSideOf.of_line hEF hE_EF hF_EF (same_side_symm hs))
    · exact Or.inr (SameSideOf.of_line hEF hE_EF hF_EF (same_side_symm hs))
  /- Euclid's argument, given once for any letters: if EF falls on AB and CD, making
     the alternate angles AEF, EFD equal, then AB and CD do not meet on D's side of
     EF. -/
  have not_meet : ∀ {A B C D E F G : Point}, Between A E B → Between C F D →
      OppositeSidesOf A D E F → ∠ A E F = ∠ E F D → Collinear A B G → Collinear C D G →
      ¬ SameSideOf G D E F := by
    -- Let them be produced and meet, in the direction of B, D, at G.
    rintro A B C D E F G hAEB hCFD hAD h ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB, hG_AB⟩ ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD, hG_CD⟩
      hG
    have hE_AB : OnLine E AB := on_line_of_between_ends hAEB hA_AB hB_AB
    have hF_CD : OnLine F CD := on_line_of_between_ends hCFD hC_CD hD_CD
    -- Then, in the triangle GEF,
    /- G is on one side of EF, so it is off EF, and GEF is a triangle. -/
    have hEFG : Triangle E F G := hG.triangle
    have hE_F : E ≠ F := hEFG.ne₁₂
    have hF_G : F ≠ G := hEFG.ne₂₃
    have hE_G : E ≠ G := hEFG.ne₁₃
    /- G lies on CD, on D's side of EF, so on the ray from F through D, and the angle
       EFG is the angle EFD (`OnRay.of_sameSideOf`, `angle_onRay_right`). -/
    have hG_FD : OnRay G F D := OnRay.of_sameSideOf hG.swap ⟨CD, hF_CD, hD_CD, hG_CD⟩ hF_G.symm
    have hEFG_EFD : ∠ E F G = ∠ E F D := angle_onRay_right hG_FD hE_F
    /- B is on D's side of EF too, for E lies between A and B, and A is on the other
       side. So G lies on the ray from E through B, and E between A and G: AE is GE
       produced, and the angle AEF is exterior to the triangle GEF (`OnRay.between`). -/
    have hBD : SameSideOf B D E F := hAD.sameSideOf_of_between hAEB
    have hG_EB : OnRay G E B :=
      OnRay.of_sameSideOf (hG.trans hBD.symm) ⟨AB, hE_AB, hB_AB, hG_AB⟩ hE_G.symm
    have hAEG : Between A E G := hG_EB.between hAEB
    -- the exterior angle AEF is equal to the interior and opposite angle EFG:
    have hAEF_EFG : ∠ A E F = ∠ E F G := h.trans hEFG_EFD.symm
    -- which is impossible. [I. 16]
    /- I.16, in the triangle FGE with GE produced to A: the exterior angle FEA is
       greater than the interior and opposite angle GFE. -/
    have hGFE_FEA : ∠ G F E < ∠ F E A := (Prop16 hEFG.bca (between_symm hAEG)).2
    rw [angle_symm hF_G.symm hE_F, angle_symm hE_F.symm (ne_of_between hAEB), hAEF_EFG]
      at hGFE_FEA
    exact lt_irrefl _ hGFE_FEA
  -- Therefore AB, CD when produced will not meet in the direction of B, D.
  have hBD : ∀ G : Point, OnLine G AB → OnLine G CD → ¬ SameSideOf G D E F :=
    fun G hG_AB hG_CD =>
      not_meet hAEB hCFD hAD h ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB, hG_AB⟩ ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD, hG_CD⟩
  -- Similarly it can be proved that neither will they meet towards A, C.
  /- The same argument, with the figure read from the other end: EF, as FE, falls on DC
     at F and on BA at E, and the alternate angles DFE, FEA are the angles EFD, AEF. -/
  have hDFE_FEA : ∠ D F E = ∠ F E A :=
    (angle_symm (ne_of_between (between_symm hCFD)) hEF).trans
      (h.symm.trans (angle_symm (ne_of_between hAEB) hEF.symm))
  have hAC : ∀ G : Point, OnLine G AB → OnLine G CD → ¬ SameSideOf G A F E :=
    fun G hG_AB hG_CD =>
      not_meet (between_symm hCFD) (between_symm hAEB) hAD.symm.swap hDFE_FEA
        ⟨CD, hD_CD, hC_CD, hG_CD⟩ ⟨AB, hB_AB, hA_AB, hG_AB⟩
  -- But straight lines which do not meet in either direction are parallel; [Def. 23]
  have hDef23 : (∀ G : Point, OnLine G AB → ¬ OnLine G CD) → AreParallel A B C D :=
    AreParallel.of_not_meet hAB hCD hA_AB hB_AB hC_CD hD_CD
  -- therefore AB is parallel to CD.
  exact hDef23 fun G hG_AB hG_CD =>
    (either G hG_AB hG_CD).elim (hBD G hG_AB hG_CD) (fun hGA => hAC G hG_AB hG_CD hGA.swap)
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.

state.enunciation: If a straight line falling on two straight lines make the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle on the same side, or the interior angles on the same side equal to two right angles, the straight lines will be parallel to one another.
state.lean_proof:
/-- If a straight line falling on two straight lines make the exterior angle equal to the interior
and opposite angle on the same side, or the interior angles on the same side equal to two right
angles, the straight lines will be parallel to one another. -/
theorem Prop28 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (hAGB : Between A G B) (hCHD : Between C H D)
    (hEGH : Between E G H) (hGHF : Between G H F) (hBD : SameSideOf B D E F)
    (h : ∠ E G B = ∠ G H D ∨ ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D = ∟ + ∟) :
    AreParallel A B C D := by
  -- For let the straight line EF falling on the two straight lines AB, CD make the exterior
  -- angle EGB equal to the interior and opposite angle GHD, or the interior angles on the same
  -- side, namely BGH, GHD, equal to two right angles;
  /- EF is the straight line GH, so B and D lie on one side of GH too
     (`SameSideOf.inner`); and B, on one side of it, is off it, which the angles
     below will need. -/
  have hBD_GH : SameSideOf B D G H := hBD.inner hEGH hGHF
  -- I say that AB is parallel to CD.
  rcases h with hext | hint
  -- For, since the angle EGB is equal to the angle GHD,
  · have hEGB_GHD : ∠ E G B = ∠ G H D := hext
    -- while the angle EGB is equal to the angle AGH, [I. 15]
    have hEHB : Triangle E H B := by
      rintro ⟨L, hE, hH, hB⟩
      exact hBD_GH.triangle ⟨L, on_line_of_between_ends hEGH hE hH, hH, hB⟩
    have hEGB_AGH : ∠ E G B = ∠ A G H :=
      (Prop15 hEGH (between_symm hAGB) hEHB).1
    -- the angle AGH is also equal to the angle GHD;
    have hAGH_GHD : ∠ A G H = ∠ G H D := CommonNotion1 hEGB_AGH.symm hEGB_GHD.symm
    -- and they are alternate;
    have hAD : OppositeSidesOf A D G H := hBD_GH.oppositeSidesOf_of_between hAGB
    -- therefore AB is parallel to CD. [I. 27]
    exact Prop27 hAGB hCHD hAD hAGH_GHD
  -- Again, since the angles BGH, GHD are equal to two right angles, and the angles AGH, BGH
  -- are also equal to two right angles, [I. 13]
  · have hABH : Triangle A B H := by
      rintro ⟨L, hA, hB, hH⟩
      exact hBD_GH.triangle ⟨L, on_line_of_between_ends hAGB hA hB, hH, hB⟩
    have htwo : ∠ A G H + ∠ B G H = ∟ + ∟ := by
      rw [angle_symm (ne_of_between (between_symm hAGB)) (ne_of_between hGHF).symm]
      exact Prop13 hAGB hABH
    -- the angles AGH, BGH are equal to the angles BGH, GHD.
    have hsums : ∠ A G H + ∠ B G H = ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D := CommonNotion1 htwo hint
    -- Let the angle BGH be subtracted from each;
    /- Each sum is written with the angle BGH last, for Common Notion 3 to take it
       away. -/
    have hsums' : ∠ A G H + ∠ B G H = ∠ G H D + ∠ B G H := hsums.trans (add_comm _ _)
    -- therefore the remaining angle AGH is equal to the remaining angle GHD;
    have hAGH_GHD : ∠ A G H = ∠ G H D := CommonNotion3 hsums' rfl
    -- and they are alternate;
    have hAD : OppositeSidesOf A D G H := hBD_GH.oppositeSidesOf_of_between hAGB
    -- therefore AB is parallel to CD. [I. 27]
    exact Prop27 hAGB hCHD hAD hAGH_GHD
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.

state.commentary:
Heath counts the tests so far: "One criterion of parallelism, the equality of alternate angles, is given in I. 27; here we have two more" (vol. 1, p. 310). Euclid brings each new one back to the alternate angles AGH, GHD. If the exterior angle EGB is equal to GHD, I.15 puts its vertical angle AGH in its place. If BGH and GHD make two right angles, so do AGH and BGH, by I.13, and when BGH is taken from each, AGH is left equal to GHD. Either way I.27 finishes. Each time Euclid says "and they are alternate", reading it from his figure. Our I.27 asks for A and D on opposite sides of GH, and the statement supplies it: B and D lie on one side of EF, which is the straight line GH, and G lies between A and B.

Aristotle knew the proposition, and used its second hypothesis to show what a general proof is. Two straight lines at right angles to a third do not meet, but a proof of that should not rest on the angles being right: it follows, in Heath's translation, "by virtue of their being equal (to two right angles) in any way whatever" (vol. 1, p. 309). The passage, Heath judges, "certainly refers to I. 28" (vol. 1, p. 309).

Heath reports Proclus' observation that "Euclid could have stated six criteria as well as three" (vol. 1, p. 310): pairs of angles on one side of EF or on opposite sides, interior or exterior, equal or together two right angles. The three left out, Heath says, "are of course equivalent but are not quite so easily expressed" (vol. 1, p. 311), and the three Euclid chose are the ones I.29 turns round. One Aigeias (or Aineias) of Hierapolis, known, it seems, only from Proclus' note here, made I.27 and I.28 one proposition in his abridgment of the *Elements* (Heath, vol. 1, p. 311).

For let the straight line EF fall on the parallel straight lines AB, CD;

I say that it makes the alternate angles AGH, GHD equal, the exterior angle EGB equal to the interior and opposite angle GHD, and the interior angles on the same side, namely BGH, GHD, equal to two right angles.

For, if the angle AGH is unequal to the angle GHD, one of them is greater.

Let the angle AGH be greater.

Let the angle BGH be added to each;

therefore the angles AGH, BGH are greater than the angles BGH, GHD.

But the angles AGH, BGH are equal to two right angles; [I. 13]

therefore the angles BGH, GHD are less than two right angles.

But straight lines produced indefinitely from angles less than two right angles meet; [Post. 5]

therefore AB, CD, if produced indefinitely, will meet;

but they do not meet, because they are by hypothesis parallel.

Therefore the angle AGH is not unequal to the angle GHD,

and is therefore equal to it.

Again, the angle AGH is equal to the angle EGB; [I. 15]

therefore the angle EGB is also equal to the angle GHD. [C.N. 1]

Let the angle BGH be added to each;

therefore the angles EGB, BGH are equal to the angles BGH, GHD. [C.N. 2]

But the angles EGB, BGH are equal to two right angles; [I. 13]

therefore the angles BGH, GHD are also equal to two right angles.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.

state.lean_proof:
/-- A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one
another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on
the same side equal to two right angles. -/
theorem Prop29 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (hpar : AreParallel A B C D) (hAGB : Between A G B)
    (hCHD : Between C H D) (hEGH : Between E G H) (hGHF : Between G H F)
    (hBD : SameSideOf B D E F) :
    ∠ A G H = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ E G B = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D = ∟ + ∟ := by
  -- For let the straight line EF fall on the parallel straight lines AB, CD;
  /- It falls on AB at G and on CD at H, with B and D on one side of it, and so
     on one side of GH, which is the same straight line (`SameSideOf.inner`). -/
  have hBD_GH : SameSideOf B D G H := hBD.inner hEGH hGHF
  -- I say that it makes the alternate angles AGH, GHD equal, the exterior angle EGB equal to
  -- the interior and opposite angle GHD, and the interior angles on the same side, namely BGH,
  -- GHD, equal to two right angles.
  -- For, if the angle AGH is unequal to the angle GHD, one of them is greater.
  /- Euclid lets the angle AGH be the greater and shows that it cannot be. If the angle
     GHD is the greater, the same argument runs from H's end: with D, C, B, A
     for A, B, C, D and H, G for G, H, the angles AGH, GHD change places,
     and A, C are the two on one side of GH. So we give his argument for any two
     parallels and any straight line falling on them, in his letters, and use it twice
     below. -/
  have not_greater : ∀ {A B C D G H : Point}, AreParallel A B C D → Between A G B →
      Between C H D → SameSideOf B D G H → ¬ ∠ G H D < ∠ A G H := by
    intro A B C D G H hpar hAGB hCHD hBD
    obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B hpar.1
    obtain ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD⟩ := Postulate1 C D hpar.2.1
    obtain ⟨GH, hG_GH, hH_GH⟩ := Postulate1 G H hBD.1
    have hG_AB : OnLine G AB := on_line_of_between_ends hAGB hA_AB hB_AB
    have hH_CD : OnLine H CD := on_line_of_between_ends hCHD hC_CD hD_CD
    -- Let the angle AGH be greater.
    intro hGHD_AGH
    -- Let the angle BGH be added to each;
    /- Adding the same thing to both keeps "less than", a tacit rule of magnitudes
       (`add_lt_add_right`), as in I.17. -/
    have hadd : ∠ G H D + ∠ B G H < ∠ A G H + ∠ B G H :=
      add_lt_add_right (∠ B G H) hGHD_AGH
    -- therefore the angles AGH, BGH are greater than the angles BGH, GHD.
    have hgreater : ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D < ∠ A G H + ∠ B G H := by
      rw [add_comm (∠ B G H)]
      exact hadd
    -- But the angles AGH, BGH are equal to two right angles; [I. 13]
    /- GH stands on AB at G: H is off AB, for otherwise G, B and H would
       be on one straight line, and B is off GH. The angle HGB of I.13 is the angle
       BGH, read the other way round. -/
    have hABH : Triangle A B H := by
      rintro ⟨L, hA, hB, hH⟩
      exact hBD.triangle.acb ⟨L, on_line_of_between_ends hAGB hA hB, hB, hH⟩
    have hAGH_BGH : ∠ A G H + ∠ B G H = ∟ + ∟ := by
      rw [← angle_symm hBD.1.symm (ne_of_between (between_symm hAGB))]
      exact Prop13 hAGB hABH
    -- therefore the angles BGH, GHD are less than two right angles.
    have hless : ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D < ∟ + ∟ := by
      rw [← hAGH_BGH]
      exact hgreater
    -- But straight lines produced indefinitely from angles less than two right angles
    -- meet; [Post. 5]
    -- therefore AB, CD, if produced indefinitely, will meet;
    /- Postulate 5 asks for what Euclid leaves to the figure: the straight lines GB and
       HD start from the points where GH meets them, and B and D lie on one side
       of GH. It also says on which side they meet, which is not needed here. -/
    have hmeet : ∃ P : Point, OnLine P AB ∧ OnLine P CD :=
      (Postulate5 hB_AB hG_AB hG_GH hH_GH hH_CD hD_CD hBD.1 (hBD.sameSide hG_GH hH_GH)
        hless).imp fun _ h => ⟨h.1, h.2.1⟩
    -- but they do not meet, because they are by hypothesis parallel.
    /- That is Definition 23, said of the straight lines AB and CD. -/
    exact (hpar.parallel hA_AB hB_AB hC_CD hD_CD).2 hmeet
  -- Therefore the angle AGH is not unequal to the angle GHD,
  /- Neither is the greater. The angle AGH is not, by Euclid's argument. Nor is the
     angle GHD, by the same argument from H's end: DC is parallel to BA, H lies
     between D and C, G between B and A, and C and A lie on one side of
     HG. For A is across GH from B, and so from D
     (`SameSideOf.oppositeSidesOf_of_between`), and C is across it from D too
     (`OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf_of_between`). The angles HGA, DHG are the angles
     AGH, GHD, read the other way round. -/
  have hnot_gt : ¬ ∠ G H D < ∠ A G H := not_greater hpar hAGB hCHD hBD_GH
  have hCA : SameSideOf C A H G :=
    (hBD_GH.oppositeSidesOf_of_between hAGB).symm.swap.sameSideOf_of_between
      (between_symm hCHD)
  have hnot_lt : ¬ ∠ A G H < ∠ G H D := by
    rw [angle_symm (ne_of_between hAGB) hBD_GH.1.symm,
      angle_symm hBD_GH.1 (ne_of_between (between_symm hCHD))]
    exact not_greater hpar.symm.swap_left.swap_right (between_symm hCHD) (between_symm hAGB)
      hCA
  -- and is therefore equal to it.
  have hAGH_GHD : ∠ A G H = ∠ G H D :=
    ((lt_trichotomy (∠ A G H) (∠ G H D)).resolve_left hnot_lt).resolve_right hnot_gt
  -- Again, the angle AGH is equal to the angle EGB; [I. 15]
  /- AB and HE cut one another at G, and H is off AB, as above. -/
  have hABH : Triangle A B H := by
    rintro ⟨L, hA, hB, hH⟩
    exact hBD_GH.triangle.acb ⟨L, on_line_of_between_ends hAGB hA hB, hB, hH⟩
  have hAGH_EGB : ∠ A G H = ∠ E G B := (Prop15 hAGB (between_symm hEGH) hABH).1
  -- therefore the angle EGB is also equal to the angle GHD. [C.N. 1]
  have hEGB_GHD : ∠ E G B = ∠ G H D := CommonNotion1 hAGH_EGB.symm hAGH_GHD.symm
  -- Let the angle BGH be added to each;
  -- therefore the angles EGB, BGH are equal to the angles BGH, GHD. [C.N. 2]
  have hsums : ∠ E G B + ∠ B G H = ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D := by
    rw [add_comm (∠ B G H)]
    exact CommonNotion2 hEGB_GHD rfl
  -- But the angles EGB, BGH are equal to two right angles; [I. 13]
  /- GB stands on EH at G: B is off EH, which is the straight line GH. -/
  have hEHB : Triangle E H B := by
    rintro ⟨L, hE, hH, hB⟩
    exact hBD_GH.triangle ⟨L, on_line_of_between_ends hEGH hE hH, hH, hB⟩
  have hEGB_BGH : ∠ E G B + ∠ B G H = ∟ + ∟ := Prop13 hEGH hEHB
  -- therefore the angles BGH, GHD are also equal to two right angles.
  have hBGH_GHD : ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D = ∟ + ∟ := hsums.symm.trans hEGB_BGH
  -- Therefore etc.
  exact ⟨hAGH_GHD, hEGB_GHD, hBGH_GHD⟩
  -- Q. E. D.

helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf:
/-- `P` and `Q` lie on the same side of the straight line `AB`. -/
def SameSideOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.inner:
/-- The straight line EF is the straight line GH, when G and H lie between E
and F in that order, as where EF falls on two straight lines at G and H
(I.27–I.29): two points on the same side of EF are on the same side of GH. -/
theorem SameSideOf.inner {E F G H : Point} (h : SameSideOf P Q E F) (hEGH : Between E G H)
    (hGHF : Between G H F) : SameSideOf P Q G H
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.oppositeSidesOf_of_b:
/-- Alternate sides. If B and D lie on the same side of the straight line GH,
and A lies on BG produced beyond G, then A and D lie on opposite sides
of GH. This is where the alternate angles AGH, GHD of I.27 and I.29 lie. (For a
straight line crossing at H, turn GH round with `.swap`.) -/
theorem SameSideOf.oppositeSidesOf_of_between {D G H : Point} (hBD : SameSideOf B D G H)
    (hAGB : Between A G B) : OppositeSidesOf A D G H
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.sameSide:
/-- Two points on the same side of the straight line AB are on the same side of
any straight line drawn through A and B. -/
theorem SameSideOf.sameSide (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    SameSide P Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.swap:
/-- "On the same side of AB" is the same as "on the same side of BA". -/
theorem SameSideOf.swap (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf P Q B A
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the same side of AB as Q, then Q is on the same side as P. -/
theorem SameSideOf.symm (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.trans:
/-- Points on the same side as a third are on the same side as each other. -/
theorem SameSideOf.trans (h₁ : SameSideOf P Q A B) (h₂ : SameSideOf Q R A B) :
    SameSideOf P R A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.triangle:
/-- A point on one side of the straight line AB is not on it, so ABP is a
triangle. -/
theorem SameSideOf.triangle (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : Triangle A B P
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.add_comm:
/-- The order of adding does not matter. (System E §3.5) -/
axiom add_comm (a b : Magnitude k) : a + b = b + a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.add_lt_add_right:
/-- Adding the same thing to both sides keeps "less than". (System E §3.5) -/
axiom add_lt_add_right {a b : Magnitude k} (c : Magnitude k) : a < b → a + c < b + c
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.angle_symm:
/-- The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4) -/
axiom angle_symm (hAB : A ≠ B) (hCB : C ≠ B) : ∠ A B C = ∠ C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_symm:
/-- If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1) -/
axiom between_symm (h : Between A B C) : Between C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.lt_trichotomy:
/-- Of two magnitudes, one is less, or they are equal, or the other is less.
(System E §3.5) -/
axiom lt_trichotomy (a b : Magnitude k) : a < b ∨ a = b ∨ b < a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between:
/-- A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between_ends:
/-- A straight line through A and C passes through every point between them.
(Between 3) -/
axiom on_line_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hC : OnLine C L) :
    OnLine B L
