/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.acb:
/-- The triangle ABC, named the other way round, as ACB. -/
theorem Triangle.acb (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle A C B

I.13.enunciation: If a straight line set up on a straight line make angles, it will make either two right angles or angles equal to two right angles.

I.15.enunciation: If two straight lines cut one another, they make the vertical angles equal to one another.
I.15.heath_porism: [PORISM. From this it is manifest that, if two straight lines cut one another, they will make the angles at the point of section equal to four right angles.]

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle

question.instructions:
Does every proposition called by the proof unit in `lean_proof` do work towards its conclusion or a substantive intermediate step of Euclid's argument? Also check for artificial hypothesis uses. Judge this unit's uses of the supplied helper signatures; helper bodies are outside this question. Heath's sentences stand as `--` lines and `cited` gives exact enunciations. In Lean, `have h : T := p` proves T by p and calls the result h; `obtain ⟨…⟩ := p` takes p apart into named pieces; `rw [h34, h37, …]` rewrites the goal by the equalities named. Follow uses through helper calls and tactics as well as explicit names. An anonymous binding or an unused hypothesis alone does not establish a defect. If both defects occur, choose `a dummy citation`.

docs/FORMALIZATION.md, section 5:
A checked intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid is legitimate, even if the
  final proof term could do without it.

criteria.cannot tell: What is given here is not enough to decide.
criteria.all do work: Every proposition call supports a later step or the conclusion, or establishes a substantive intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid. No hypothesis is mentioned merely to look used. With no proposition calls the citation part alone is vacuous; hypothesis use must still be inspected.
criteria.a dummy citation: Some proposition call does no substantive work: its result neither supports the argument nor establishes a substantive intermediate fact, and merely supplies a citation while the step is done another way.
criteria.an artificial hypothesis use: No dummy citation is established, but a hypothesis is mentioned only so that it looks used, and does no substantive work.

state.commentary:
**"Less than two right angles."** Here Euclid calls on Postulate 5 for the first time, and our proof calls on it at the same step. Heath honours the choice: "When we consider the countless successive attempts made through more than twenty centuries to prove the Postulate, many of them by geometers of ability, we cannot but admire the genius of the man who concluded that such a hypothesis, which he found necessary to the validity of his whole system of geometry, was really indemonstrable" (vol. 1, p. 202).

Euclid restates his postulate here in fewer words than its own, and Heath spells out what they leave unsaid, "namely that the straight lines begin from points at which they meet a transversal" (vol. 1, p. 312). Our `Postulate5` says every word: straight lines meeting GH at G and H, with B and D on one side of it and the angles BGH, GHD less than two right angles. What the postulate gives, a point on both AB and CD, is just what Definition I.23 rules out. Euclid supposes AGH the greater and passes over the case where GHD is; that is his argument read from H's end, on the side of A and C, with I.13 at H, and we use it so, as in I.16. After the proof, `Prop29.alternate`, `Prop29.interior` and `Prop29.exterior` state I.29 for any straight line falling on two parallels, for later propositions to cite.

Heath also proves I.29 from John Playfair's axiom, that through a given point only one parallel can be drawn to a given straight line, as modern textbooks usually do. Charles Dodgson, better known as Lewis Carroll, argued for keeping Euclid's postulate: it puts before the beginner "clear and *positive* conceptions", not straight lines that never meet, "a *negative* conception"; and it "gives a direct criterion for judging that two straight lines meet, a criterion which is constantly required, e.g. in I. 44" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 314).

**The modern way.** The coordinate plane has Postulate 5 built in. With $\vec{u} = (u_{1}, u_{2})$ pointing from A to B and $\vec{v} = (v_{1}, v_{2})$ from C to D, the straight lines AB and CD are the points $\mathrm{A} + s\vec{u}$ and $\mathrm{C} + t\vec{v}$, and they meet whenever the two equations of $\mathrm{A} + s\vec{u} = \mathrm{C} + t\vec{v}$ can be solved for $s$ and $t$, as they always can when $u_{1}v_{2} - u_{2}v_{1} \neq 0$. So straight lines that never meet have directions that are multiples of one another. Here the direction from H to D is a positive multiple of $\vec{u}$, since B and D lie on one side of EF, and with $\vec{w}$ pointing from G to H, the angles AGH and GHD both have cosine $-\vec{u} \cdot \vec{w}/(\lvert\vec{u}\rvert\lvert\vec{w}\rvert)$.
state.heath_proof:
For let the straight line EF fall on the parallel straight lines AB, CD;

I say that it makes the alternate angles AGH, GHD equal, the exterior angle EGB equal to the interior and opposite angle GHD, and the interior angles on the same side, namely BGH, GHD, equal to two right angles.

For, if the angle AGH is unequal to the angle GHD, one of them is greater.

Let the angle AGH be greater.

Let the angle BGH be added to each;

therefore the angles AGH, BGH are greater than the angles BGH, GHD.

But the angles AGH, BGH are equal to two right angles; [I. 13]

therefore the angles BGH, GHD are less than two right angles.

But straight lines produced indefinitely from angles less than two right angles meet; [Post. 5]

therefore AB, CD, if produced indefinitely, will meet;

but they do not meet, because they are by hypothesis parallel.

Therefore the angle AGH is not unequal to the angle GHD,

and is therefore equal to it.

Again, the angle AGH is equal to the angle EGB; [I. 15]

therefore the angle EGB is also equal to the angle GHD. [C.N. 1]

Let the angle BGH be added to each;

therefore the angles EGB, BGH are equal to the angles BGH, GHD. [C.N. 2]

But the angles EGB, BGH are equal to two right angles; [I. 13]

therefore the angles BGH, GHD are also equal to two right angles.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one
another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on
the same side equal to two right angles. -/
theorem Prop29 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (hpar : AreParallel A B C D) (hAGB : Between A G B)
    (hCHD : Between C H D) (hEGH : Between E G H) (hGHF : Between G H F)
    (hBD : SameSideOf B D E F) :
    ∠ A G H = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ E G B = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D = ∟ + ∟ := by
  -- For let the straight line EF fall on the parallel straight lines AB, CD;
  /- It falls on AB at G and on CD at H, with B and D on one side of it, and so
     on one side of GH, which is the same straight line (`SameSideOf.inner`). -/
  have hBD_GH : SameSideOf B D G H := hBD.inner hEGH hGHF
  -- I say that it makes the alternate angles AGH, GHD equal, the exterior angle EGB equal to
  -- the interior and opposite angle GHD, and the interior angles on the same side, namely BGH,
  -- GHD, equal to two right angles.
  -- For, if the angle AGH is unequal to the angle GHD, one of them is greater.
  /- Euclid lets the angle AGH be the greater and shows that it cannot be. If the angle
     GHD is the greater, the same argument runs from H's end: with D, C, B, A
     for A, B, C, D and H, G for G, H, the angles AGH, GHD change places,
     and A, C are the two on one side of GH. So we give his argument for any two
     parallels and any straight line falling on them, in his letters, and use it twice
     below. -/
  have not_greater : ∀ {A B C D G H : Point}, AreParallel A B C D → Between A G B →
      Between C H D → SameSideOf B D G H → ¬ ∠ G H D < ∠ A G H := by
    intro A B C D G H hpar hAGB hCHD hBD
    obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B hpar.1
    obtain ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD⟩ := Postulate1 C D hpar.2.1
    obtain ⟨GH, hG_GH, hH_GH⟩ := Postulate1 G H hBD.1
    have hG_AB : OnLine G AB := on_line_of_between_ends hAGB hA_AB hB_AB
    have hH_CD : OnLine H CD := on_line_of_between_ends hCHD hC_CD hD_CD
    -- Let the angle AGH be greater.
    intro hGHD_AGH
    -- Let the angle BGH be added to each;
    /- Adding the same thing to both keeps "less than", a tacit rule of magnitudes
       (`add_lt_add_right`), as in I.17. -/
    have hadd : ∠ G H D + ∠ B G H < ∠ A G H + ∠ B G H :=
      add_lt_add_right (∠ B G H) hGHD_AGH
    -- therefore the angles AGH, BGH are greater than the angles BGH, GHD.
    have hgreater : ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D < ∠ A G H + ∠ B G H := by
      rw [add_comm (∠ B G H)]
      exact hadd
    -- But the angles AGH, BGH are equal to two right angles; [I. 13]
    /- GH stands on AB at G: H is off AB, for otherwise G, B and H would
       be on one straight line, and B is off GH. The angle HGB of I.13 is the angle
       BGH, read the other way round. -/
    have hABH : Triangle A B H := by
      rintro ⟨L, hA, hB, hH⟩
      exact hBD.triangle.acb ⟨L, on_line_of_between_ends hAGB hA hB, hB, hH⟩
    have hAGH_BGH : ∠ A G H + ∠ B G H = ∟ + ∟ := by
      rw [← angle_symm hBD.1.symm (ne_of_between (between_symm hAGB))]
      exact Prop13 hAGB hABH
    -- therefore the angles BGH, GHD are less than two right angles.
    have hless : ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D < ∟ + ∟ := by
      rw [← hAGH_BGH]
      exact hgreater
    -- But straight lines produced indefinitely from angles less than two right angles
    -- meet; [Post. 5]
    -- therefore AB, CD, if produced indefinitely, will meet;
    /- Postulate 5 asks for what Euclid leaves to the figure: the straight lines GB and
       HD start from the points where GH meets them, and B and D lie on one side
       of GH. It also says on which side they meet, which is not needed here. -/
    have hmeet : ∃ P : Point, OnLine P AB ∧ OnLine P CD :=
      (Postulate5 hB_AB hG_AB hG_GH hH_GH hH_CD hD_CD hBD.1 (hBD.sameSide hG_GH hH_GH)
        hless).imp fun _ h => ⟨h.1, h.2.1⟩
    -- but they do not meet, because they are by hypothesis parallel.
    /- That is Definition 23, said of the straight lines AB and CD. -/
    exact (hpar.parallel hA_AB hB_AB hC_CD hD_CD).2 hmeet
  -- Therefore the angle AGH is not unequal to the angle GHD,
  /- Neither is the greater. The angle AGH is not, by Euclid's argument. Nor is the
     angle GHD, by the same argument from H's end: DC is parallel to BA, H lies
     between D and C, G between B and A, and C and A lie on one side of
     HG. For A is across GH from B, and so from D
     (`SameSideOf.oppositeSidesOf_of_between`), and C is across it from D too
     (`OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf_of_between`). The angles HGA, DHG are the angles
     AGH, GHD, read the other way round. -/
  have hnot_gt : ¬ ∠ G H D < ∠ A G H := not_greater hpar hAGB hCHD hBD_GH
  have hCA : SameSideOf C A H G :=
    (hBD_GH.oppositeSidesOf_of_between hAGB).symm.swap.sameSideOf_of_between
      (between_symm hCHD)
  have hnot_lt : ¬ ∠ A G H < ∠ G H D := by
    rw [angle_symm (ne_of_between hAGB) hBD_GH.1.symm,
      angle_symm hBD_GH.1 (ne_of_between (between_symm hCHD))]
    exact not_greater hpar.symm.swap_left.swap_right (between_symm hCHD) (between_symm hAGB)
      hCA
  -- and is therefore equal to it.
  have hAGH_GHD : ∠ A G H = ∠ G H D :=
    ((lt_trichotomy (∠ A G H) (∠ G H D)).resolve_left hnot_lt).resolve_right hnot_gt
  -- Again, the angle AGH is equal to the angle EGB; [I. 15]
  /- AB and HE cut one another at G, and H is off AB, as above. -/
  have hABH : Triangle A B H := by
    rintro ⟨L, hA, hB, hH⟩
    exact hBD_GH.triangle.acb ⟨L, on_line_of_between_ends hAGB hA hB, hB, hH⟩
  have hAGH_EGB : ∠ A G H = ∠ E G B := (Prop15 hAGB (between_symm hEGH) hABH).1
  -- therefore the angle EGB is also equal to the angle GHD. [C.N. 1]
  have hEGB_GHD : ∠ E G B = ∠ G H D := CommonNotion1 hAGH_EGB.symm hAGH_GHD.symm
  -- Let the angle BGH be added to each;
  -- therefore the angles EGB, BGH are equal to the angles BGH, GHD. [C.N. 2]
  have hsums : ∠ E G B + ∠ B G H = ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D := by
    rw [add_comm (∠ B G H)]
    exact CommonNotion2 hEGB_GHD rfl
  -- But the angles EGB, BGH are equal to two right angles; [I. 13]
  /- GB stands on EH at G: B is off EH, which is the straight line GH. -/
  have hEHB : Triangle E H B := by
    rintro ⟨L, hE, hH, hB⟩
    exact hBD_GH.triangle ⟨L, on_line_of_between_ends hEGH hE hH, hH, hB⟩
  have hEGB_BGH : ∠ E G B + ∠ B G H = ∟ + ∟ := Prop13 hEGH hEHB
  -- therefore the angles BGH, GHD are also equal to two right angles.
  have hBGH_GHD : ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D = ∟ + ∟ := hsums.symm.trans hEGB_BGH
  -- Therefore etc.
  exact ⟨hAGH_GHD, hEGB_GHD, hBGH_GHD⟩
  -- Q. E. D.
state.lean_statement:
theorem Prop29 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (hpar : AreParallel A B C D) (hAGB : Between A G B)
    (hCHD : Between C H D) (hEGH : Between E G H) (hGHF : Between G H F)
    (hBD : SameSideOf B D E F) :
    ∠ A G H = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ E G B = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D = ∟ + ∟

named_declarations.Elements.BookI.Prop29.alternate:
/-- The alternate angles. If the straight line PG is parallel to HQ, and P and
Q lie on opposite sides of GH, then the alternate angles PGH, GHQ are equal.
Euclid's figure is drawn about GH, each straight line produced beyond G and H
(`AreParallel.figure_alternate`), and I.29 does the rest. [I. 29] -/
theorem Prop29.alternate {P G H Q : Point} (hpar : AreParallel P G H Q)
    (hPQ : OppositeSidesOf P Q G H) : ∠ P G H = ∠ G H Q
named_declarations.Elements.BookI.Prop29.exterior:
/-- The exterior angle. If the straight line GP is parallel to HQ, P and Q lie
on one side of GH, and E lies on HG produced beyond G, then the exterior
angle EGP is equal to the interior and opposite angle GHQ. [I. 29] -/
theorem Prop29.exterior {P G H Q E : Point} (hpar : AreParallel G P H Q)
    (hPQ : SameSideOf P Q G H) (hEGH : Between E G H) : ∠ E G P = ∠ G H Q
named_declarations.Elements.BookI.Prop29.interior:
/-- The interior angles on the same side. If the straight line GP is parallel to
HQ, and P and Q lie on one side of GH, then the angles PGH, GHQ are
equal to two right angles. [I. 29] -/
theorem Prop29.interior {P G H Q : Point} (hpar : AreParallel G P H Q)
    (hPQ : SameSideOf P Q G H) : ∠ P G H + ∠ G H Q = ∟ + ∟
named_declarations.Elements.Postulate5:
/-- **Postulate 5.** If the straight line through `B` and `C` falls on the
straight lines `L` (through `A` and `B`) and `N` (through `C` and `D`), with `A`
and `D` on the same side of it, and the interior angles `ABC` and `BCD` together
are less than two right angles, then `L` and `N`, produced, meet on that side.

System E §3.6, diagram-angle transfer rule 5. -/

state.enunciation: A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on the same side equal to two right angles.
state.heath_proof:
For let the straight line EF fall on the parallel straight lines AB, CD;

I say that it makes the alternate angles AGH, GHD equal, the exterior angle EGB equal to the interior and opposite angle GHD, and the interior angles on the same side, namely BGH, GHD, equal to two right angles.

For, if the angle AGH is unequal to the angle GHD, one of them is greater.

Let the angle AGH be greater.

Let the angle BGH be added to each;

therefore the angles AGH, BGH are greater than the angles BGH, GHD.

But the angles AGH, BGH are equal to two right angles; [I. 13]

therefore the angles BGH, GHD are less than two right angles.

But straight lines produced indefinitely from angles less than two right angles meet; [Post. 5]

therefore AB, CD, if produced indefinitely, will meet;

but they do not meet, because they are by hypothesis parallel.

Therefore the angle AGH is not unequal to the angle GHD,

and is therefore equal to it.

Again, the angle AGH is equal to the angle EGB; [I. 15]

therefore the angle EGB is also equal to the angle GHD. [C.N. 1]

Let the angle BGH be added to each;

therefore the angles EGB, BGH are equal to the angles BGH, GHD. [C.N. 2]

But the angles EGB, BGH are equal to two right angles; [I. 13]

therefore the angles BGH, GHD are also equal to two right angles.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.

state.heath_proof:
Let each of the straight lines AB, CD be parallel to EF;

I say that AB is also parallel to CD.

For let the straight line GK fall upon them.

Then, since the straight line GK has fallen on the parallel straight lines AB, EF,

the angle AGK is equal to the angle GHF. [I. 29]

Again, since the straight line GK has fallen on the parallel straight lines EF, CD,

the angle GHF is equal to the angle GKD. [I. 29]

But the angle AGK was also proved equal to the angle GHF;

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another. -/
theorem Prop30 {A B C D E F : Point} (h₁ : AreParallel A B E F) (h₂ : AreParallel C D E F)
    (hC : ¬ Collinear A B C) :
    AreParallel A B C D := by
  -- Let each of the straight lines AB, CD be parallel to EF;
  obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B h₁.1
  obtain ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD⟩ := Postulate1 C D h₂.1
  obtain ⟨EF, hE_EF, hF_EF⟩ := Postulate1 E F h₁.2.1
  have hAB_EF := h₁.parallel hA_AB hB_AB hE_EF hF_EF
  have hCD_EF := h₂.parallel hC_CD hD_CD hE_EF hF_EF
  -- I say that AB is also parallel to CD.
  /- Heath's case, where EF separates G and K. The given points need not
     stand where his do, so we choose ends of each straight line on the sides of
     GK his figure wants, and return to the given names at the end: parallels
     are whole straight lines. -/
  have separated : ∀ {G K : Point}, OnLine G AB → OnLine K CD →
      OppositeSides G K EF → Parallel AB CD := by
    intro G K hG_AB hK_CD hGK
    -- For let the straight line GK fall upon them.
    obtain ⟨H, hH_EF, hGHK⟩ := hGK.exists_between
    have hG_K := ne_of_between_ends hGHK
    have hG_H := ne_of_between hGHK
    have hH_K := (ne_of_between (between_symm hGHK)).symm
    obtain ⟨GK, hG_GK, hK_GK⟩ := Postulate1 G K hG_K
    have hH_GK := on_line_of_between_ends hGHK hG_GK hK_GK
    have hEF_GK : EF ≠ GK := fun e => hGK.1 (e ▸ hG_GK)
    obtain ⟨F, hF_EF, hF_GK, -⟩ := exists_point_on_line_off_line hEF_GK []
    have hF_H : F ≠ H := fun e => hF_GK (e ▸ hH_GK)
    obtain ⟨E, hFHE⟩ := produce hF_H
    have hE_GK : ¬ OnLine E GK := fun h =>
      hF_GK (on_line_of_between (between_symm hFHE) h hH_GK)
    have hEF : OppositeSides E F GK :=
      ⟨hE_GK, hF_GK, pasch3 (between_symm hFHE) hH_GK⟩
    have hAB_GK : AB ≠ GK := fun e => hAB_EF.not_onLine (e ▸ hH_GK) hH_EF
    have hCD_GK : CD ≠ GK := fun e => hCD_EF.not_onLine (e ▸ hH_GK) hH_EF
    obtain ⟨A, hA_AB, hAE⟩ := Prop30.point_on_side hG_AB hG_GK hAB_GK hE_GK
    obtain ⟨D, hD_CD, hDF⟩ := Prop30.point_on_side hK_CD hK_GK hCD_GK hF_GK
    have hA_G : A ≠ G := fun e => not_on_line_of_same_side hAE (e ▸ hG_GK)
    have hD_K : D ≠ K := fun e => not_on_line_of_same_side hDF (e ▸ hK_GK)
    obtain ⟨B, hAGB⟩ := produce hA_G
    obtain ⟨C, hDKC⟩ := produce hD_K
    have hB_AB := on_line_of_between hAGB hA_AB hG_AB
    have hC_CD := on_line_of_between hDKC hD_CD hK_CD
    have hAF : OppositeSidesOf A F G H :=
      (SameSideOf.of_line hG_H hG_GK hH_GK hAE).trans_opposite
        (OppositeSidesOf.of_line hG_H hG_GK hH_GK hEF)
    have hFD : SameSideOf F D H K :=
      SameSideOf.of_line hH_K hH_GK hK_GK (same_side_symm hDF)
    -- Then, since the straight line GK has fallen on the parallel straight lines AB, EF,
    have hpar := AreParallel.of_parallel hA_G hF_H.symm hA_AB hG_AB hH_EF hF_EF hAB_EF
    -- the angle AGK is equal to the angle GHF. [I. 29]
    have hAGH : ∠ A G H = ∠ G H F := Prop29.alternate hpar hAF
    have hAGK : ∠ A G K = ∠ G H F :=
      (angle_onRay_right (OnRay.of_between hGHK) hA_G).symm.trans hAGH
    -- Again, since the straight line GK has fallen on the parallel straight lines EF, CD,
    have hpar' := AreParallel.of_parallel hF_H.symm hD_K.symm hH_EF hF_EF hK_CD hD_CD
      hCD_EF.symm
    -- the angle GHF is equal to the angle GKD. [I. 29]
    have hGHF : ∠ G H F = ∠ G K D :=
      (Prop29.exterior hpar' hFD hGHK).trans
        (angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between (between_symm hGHK)) hD_K)
    -- But the angle AGK was also proved equal to the angle GHF;
    have hsame : ∠ A G K = ∠ G H F := hAGK
    -- therefore the angle AGK is also equal to the angle GKD; [C.N. 1]
    have hequal : ∠ A G K = ∠ G K D := CommonNotion1 hsame hGHF.symm
    -- and they are alternate.
    have hAF_GK : OppositeSidesOf A F G K :=
      OppositeSidesOf.of_line hG_K hG_GK hK_GK (hAF.oppositeSides hG_GK hH_GK)
    have hDF_GK : SameSideOf D F G K := SameSideOf.of_line hG_K hG_GK hK_GK hDF
    have hAD : OppositeSidesOf A D G K := (hDF_GK.trans_opposite hAF_GK.symm).symm
    -- Therefore AB is parallel to CD.
    exact (Prop27 hAGB (between_symm hDKC) hAD hequal).parallel hA_AB hB_AB hC_CD hD_CD
  /- When EF lies outside AB and CD, a straight line from one to the other
     need not cross it. Then if AB and CD met, they would be two parallels to
     EF through one point, and so one straight line (`Prop30.unique`); but C
     is off AB. -/
  have hparallel : Parallel AB CD := by
    by_cases hs : SameSide A C EF
    · apply Parallel.of_not_meet hA_AB
      intro G hG_AB hG_CD
      have heq := Prop30.unique hAB_EF hCD_EF hG_AB hG_CD hE_EF
      exact hC ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB, heq ▸ hC_CD⟩
    · exact separated hA_AB hC_CD
        ⟨hAB_EF.not_onLine hA_AB, hCD_EF.not_onLine hC_CD, hs⟩
  exact AreParallel.of_parallel h₁.1 h₂.1 hA_AB hB_AB hC_CD hD_CD hparallel
  -- Q. E. D.

/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.of_parallel:
/-- Two different points of L, and two different points of M, are the ends of
parallel straight lines when L and M are parallel: two points fix one straight
line (System E, Generalities 1). With `AreParallel.parallel`, this says "AB is
parallel to CD" of any other two points P, Q of the straight line AB and R,
S of CD. -/
theorem AreParallel.of_parallel (hPQ : P ≠ Q) (hRS : R ≠ S) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L)
    (hR : OnLine R M) (hS : OnLine S M) (h : Parallel L M) : AreParallel P Q R S
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.parallel:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then a straight line through A and B is parallel
to one through C and D. -/
theorem AreParallel.parallel (h : AreParallel A B C D) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (hC : OnLine C M) (hD : OnLine D M) : Parallel L M
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.symm:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then CD is parallel to AB. -/
theorem AreParallel.symm (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop27:
/-- If a straight line falling on two straight lines make the alternate angles equal to one another,
the straight lines will be parallel to one another. -/
theorem Prop27 {A B C D E F : Point} (hAEB : Between A E B) (hCFD : Between C F D)
    (hAD : OppositeSidesOf A D E F) (h : ∠ A E F = ∠ E F D) :
    AreParallel A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29:
/-- A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one
another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on
the same side equal to two right angles. -/
theorem Prop29 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (hpar : AreParallel A B C D) (hAGB : Between A G B)
    (hCHD : Between C H D) (hEGH : Between E G H) (hGHF : Between G H F)
    (hBD : SameSideOf B D E F) :
    ∠ A G H = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ E G B = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D = ∟ + ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29.alternate:
/-- The alternate angles. If the straight line PG is parallel to HQ, and P and
Q lie on opposite sides of GH, then the alternate angles PGH, GHQ are equal.
Euclid's figure is drawn about GH, each straight line produced beyond G and H
(`AreParallel.figure_alternate`), and I.29 does the rest. [I. 29] -/
theorem Prop29.alternate {P G H Q : Point} (hpar : AreParallel P G H Q)
    (hPQ : OppositeSidesOf P Q G H) : ∠ P G H = ∠ G H Q
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29.exterior:
/-- The exterior angle. If the straight line GP is parallel to HQ, P and Q lie
on one side of GH, and E lies on HG produced beyond G, then the exterior
angle EGP is equal to the interior and opposite angle GHQ. [I. 29] -/
theorem Prop29.exterior {P G H Q E : Point} (hpar : AreParallel G P H Q)
    (hPQ : SameSideOf P Q G H) (hEGH : Between E G H) : ∠ E G P = ∠ G H Q
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29.interior:
/-- The interior angles on the same side. If the straight line GP is parallel to
HQ, and P and Q lie on one side of GH, then the angles PGH, GHQ are
equal to two right angles. [I. 29] -/
theorem Prop29.interior {P G H Q : Point} (hpar : AreParallel G P H Q)
    (hPQ : SameSideOf P Q G H) : ∠ P G H + ∠ G H Q = ∟ + ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30.point_on_side:
/-- Euclid's figure puts the ends of each straight line where the proof wants
them, on one side or the other of the straight line falling on it. A straight line
L through the point G of T, other than T, has a point on whichever side of
T we name: take a point of L off T, and if it is on the wrong side, produce
it through G to the other (System E, Points 2, Pasch 3 and Same side 5). -/
theorem Prop30.point_on_side {L T : Line} {G P : Point}
    (hGL : OnLine G L) (hGT : OnLine G T) (hLT : L ≠ T) (hP : ¬ OnLine P T) :
    ∃ A : Point, OnLine A L ∧ SameSide A P T
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30.unique:

straight line from one to the other need not cross it. For that case: two straight

straight line from the point to the third makes, with each, interior angles equal

theorem Prop30.unique {L M N : Line} {G H : Point}

    (hGL : OnLine G L) (hGM : OnLine G M) (hHN : OnLine H N) : L = M

helper_signatures.Elements.angle_onRay_right:
/-- The other arm traced through another point of its ray: if C' is on the ray
from A through C, the angle BAC' is the angle BAC. (System E,

theorem angle_onRay_right {C' : Point} (hC : OnRay C' A C) (hBA : B ≠ A) :
    ∠ B A C' = ∠ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.onRay_of_angle_eq:
/-- On one side of a straight line, only one ray from a point of it makes a given
angle with it. If P and F are on the same side of the straight line DE, and
the angle EDP is equal to the angle EDF, then P lies on the ray from D
through F.

Otherwise either P would lie within the angle EDF, or F within the angle
EDP (System E, Triple incidence 2 says which), and either way an angle would be
a part of an angle equal to it (Diagram-angle 1 and 2, with C.N. 5). Pasch 3
puts P on F's side of D rather than behind it. -/
theorem onRay_of_angle_eq {D E F P : Point} (hPF : SameSideOf P F D E)
    (h : ∠ E D P = ∠ E D F) : OnRay P D F

theorem produce (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ C : Point, Between A B C

theorem same_side_of_opposite_sides {C D E : Point} (h₁ : OppositeSides C D L)
    (h₂ : OppositeSides C E L) : SameSide D E L

I.27.enunciation: If a straight line falling on two straight lines make the alternate angles equal to one another, the straight lines will be parallel to one another.

I.29.enunciation: A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on the same side equal to two right angles.

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ P ≠ A ∧ Collinear A B P ∧ ¬ Between P A B
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle

question.instructions:
Does every proposition called by the proof unit in `lean_proof` do work towards its conclusion or a substantive intermediate step of Euclid's argument? Also check for artificial hypothesis uses. Judge this unit's uses of the supplied helper signatures; helper bodies are outside this question. Heath's sentences stand as `--` lines and `cited` gives exact enunciations. In Lean, `have h : T := p` proves T by p and calls the result h; `obtain ⟨…⟩ := p` takes p apart into named pieces; `rw [h34, h37, …]` rewrites the goal by the equalities named. Follow uses through helper calls and tactics as well as explicit names. An anonymous binding or an unused hypothesis alone does not establish a defect. If both defects occur, choose `a dummy citation`.

docs/FORMALIZATION.md, section 5:
A checked intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid is legitimate, even if the
  final proof term could do without it.

criteria.cannot tell: What is given here is not enough to decide.
criteria.all do work: Every proposition call supports a later step or the conclusion, or establishes a substantive intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid. No hypothesis is mentioned merely to look used. With no proposition calls the citation part alone is vacuous; hypothesis use must still be inspected.
criteria.a dummy citation: Some proposition call does no substantive work: its result neither supports the argument nor establishes a substantive intermediate fact, and merely supplies a citation while the step is done another way.
criteria.an artificial hypothesis use: No dummy citation is established, but a hypothesis is mentioned only so that it looks used, and does no substantive work.

state.commentary:
Heath's figure sets EF between AB and CD, so GK crosses EF at H. I.29 makes the alternate angles AGK, GHF equal, and the exterior angle GHF equal to the interior and opposite angle GKD; Common Notion 1 joins the two, and the alternate angles AGK, GKD make AB parallel to CD. That last step is I.27, though Heath gives no reference for it. Heath notes that the usual "Therefore etc." is, "curiously enough, wanting at the end of this proposition" (vol. 1, p. 314), and our Lean goes without it too.

**What if EF lies outside?** Euclid's enunciation allows it, and then a straight line from AB to CD may miss EF. So we first prove that two straight lines through one point, each parallel to a third, are one straight line (`Prop30.unique`): joined to the third, they make equal angles on one side of the straight line joining them, by I.29 and Common Notion 3, and so run along one ray. Were AB and CD to meet, they would be one. GK produced still meets EF, and I.29 would apply again. That meeting uses the rule that a straight line meeting one of two parallels meets the other. Our later proofs draw the rule from I.30 itself (`Prop30.meet`), so here we use uniqueness instead.

John Playfair's axiom says that two straight lines which cut one another are never both parallel to a third; I.30 says that two straight lines parallel to a third never cut one another. Heath credits Augustus De Morgan with seeing that these are one: "The proposition is, as De Morgan points out, the *logical* equivalent of 'Playfair's' axiom" (vol. 1, p. 314). So `Prop30.unique` is that axiom, proved here from I.29. De Morgan adds that another proposition is "much wanted", and Heath supplies it: when the sides of one angle are parallel, or perpendicular, to the sides of another, the two angles are equal or together make two right angles (vol. 1, p. 315).
state.heath_proof:
Let each of the straight lines AB, CD be parallel to EF;

I say that AB is also parallel to CD.

For let the straight line GK fall upon them.

Then, since the straight line GK has fallen on the parallel straight lines AB, EF,

the angle AGK is equal to the angle GHF. [I. 29]

Again, since the straight line GK has fallen on the parallel straight lines EF, CD,

the angle GHF is equal to the angle GKD. [I. 29]

But the angle AGK was also proved equal to the angle GHF;

therefore the angle AGK is also equal to the angle GKD; [C.N. 1]

and they are alternate.

Therefore AB is parallel to CD.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another. -/
theorem Prop30 {A B C D E F : Point} (h₁ : AreParallel A B E F) (h₂ : AreParallel C D E F)
    (hC : ¬ Collinear A B C) :
    AreParallel A B C D := by
  -- Let each of the straight lines AB, CD be parallel to EF;
  obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B h₁.1
  obtain ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD⟩ := Postulate1 C D h₂.1
  obtain ⟨EF, hE_EF, hF_EF⟩ := Postulate1 E F h₁.2.1
  have hAB_EF := h₁.parallel hA_AB hB_AB hE_EF hF_EF
  have hCD_EF := h₂.parallel hC_CD hD_CD hE_EF hF_EF
  -- I say that AB is also parallel to CD.
  /- Heath's case, where EF separates G and K. The given points need not
     stand where his do, so we choose ends of each straight line on the sides of
     GK his figure wants, and return to the given names at the end: parallels
     are whole straight lines. -/
  have separated : ∀ {G K : Point}, OnLine G AB → OnLine K CD →
      OppositeSides G K EF → Parallel AB CD := by
    intro G K hG_AB hK_CD hGK
    -- For let the straight line GK fall upon them.
    obtain ⟨H, hH_EF, hGHK⟩ := hGK.exists_between
    have hG_K := ne_of_between_ends hGHK
    have hG_H := ne_of_between hGHK
    have hH_K := (ne_of_between (between_symm hGHK)).symm
    obtain ⟨GK, hG_GK, hK_GK⟩ := Postulate1 G K hG_K
    have hH_GK := on_line_of_between_ends hGHK hG_GK hK_GK
    have hEF_GK : EF ≠ GK := fun e => hGK.1 (e ▸ hG_GK)
    obtain ⟨F, hF_EF, hF_GK, -⟩ := exists_point_on_line_off_line hEF_GK []
    have hF_H : F ≠ H := fun e => hF_GK (e ▸ hH_GK)
    obtain ⟨E, hFHE⟩ := produce hF_H
    have hE_GK : ¬ OnLine E GK := fun h =>
      hF_GK (on_line_of_between (between_symm hFHE) h hH_GK)
    have hEF : OppositeSides E F GK :=
      ⟨hE_GK, hF_GK, pasch3 (between_symm hFHE) hH_GK⟩
    have hAB_GK : AB ≠ GK := fun e => hAB_EF.not_onLine (e ▸ hH_GK) hH_EF
    have hCD_GK : CD ≠ GK := fun e => hCD_EF.not_onLine (e ▸ hH_GK) hH_EF
    obtain ⟨A, hA_AB, hAE⟩ := Prop30.point_on_side hG_AB hG_GK hAB_GK hE_GK
    obtain ⟨D, hD_CD, hDF⟩ := Prop30.point_on_side hK_CD hK_GK hCD_GK hF_GK
    have hA_G : A ≠ G := fun e => not_on_line_of_same_side hAE (e ▸ hG_GK)
    have hD_K : D ≠ K := fun e => not_on_line_of_same_side hDF (e ▸ hK_GK)
    obtain ⟨B, hAGB⟩ := produce hA_G
    obtain ⟨C, hDKC⟩ := produce hD_K
    have hB_AB := on_line_of_between hAGB hA_AB hG_AB
    have hC_CD := on_line_of_between hDKC hD_CD hK_CD
    have hAF : OppositeSidesOf A F G H :=
      (SameSideOf.of_line hG_H hG_GK hH_GK hAE).trans_opposite
        (OppositeSidesOf.of_line hG_H hG_GK hH_GK hEF)
    have hFD : SameSideOf F D H K :=
      SameSideOf.of_line hH_K hH_GK hK_GK (same_side_symm hDF)
    -- Then, since the straight line GK has fallen on the parallel straight lines AB, EF,
    have hpar := AreParallel.of_parallel hA_G hF_H.symm hA_AB hG_AB hH_EF hF_EF hAB_EF
    -- the angle AGK is equal to the angle GHF. [I. 29]
    have hAGH : ∠ A G H = ∠ G H F := Prop29.alternate hpar hAF
    have hAGK : ∠ A G K = ∠ G H F :=
      (angle_onRay_right (OnRay.of_between hGHK) hA_G).symm.trans hAGH
    -- Again, since the straight line GK has fallen on the parallel straight lines EF, CD,
    have hpar' := AreParallel.of_parallel hF_H.symm hD_K.symm hH_EF hF_EF hK_CD hD_CD
      hCD_EF.symm
    -- the angle GHF is equal to the angle GKD. [I. 29]
    have hGHF : ∠ G H F = ∠ G K D :=
      (Prop29.exterior hpar' hFD hGHK).trans
        (angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between (between_symm hGHK)) hD_K)
    -- But the angle AGK was also proved equal to the angle GHF;
    have hsame : ∠ A G K = ∠ G H F := hAGK
    -- therefore the angle AGK is also equal to the angle GKD; [C.N. 1]
    have hequal : ∠ A G K = ∠ G K D := CommonNotion1 hsame hGHF.symm
    -- and they are alternate.
    have hAF_GK : OppositeSidesOf A F G K :=
      OppositeSidesOf.of_line hG_K hG_GK hK_GK (hAF.oppositeSides hG_GK hH_GK)
    have hDF_GK : SameSideOf D F G K := SameSideOf.of_line hG_K hG_GK hK_GK hDF
    have hAD : OppositeSidesOf A D G K := (hDF_GK.trans_opposite hAF_GK.symm).symm
    -- Therefore AB is parallel to CD.
    exact (Prop27 hAGB (between_symm hDKC) hAD hequal).parallel hA_AB hB_AB hC_CD hD_CD
  /- When EF lies outside AB and CD, a straight line from one to the other
     need not cross it. Then if AB and CD met, they would be two parallels to
     EF through one point, and so one straight line (`Prop30.unique`); but C
     is off AB. -/
  have hparallel : Parallel AB CD := by
    by_cases hs : SameSide A C EF
    · apply Parallel.of_not_meet hA_AB
      intro G hG_AB hG_CD
      have heq := Prop30.unique hAB_EF hCD_EF hG_AB hG_CD hE_EF
      exact hC ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB, heq ▸ hC_CD⟩
    · exact separated hA_AB hC_CD
        ⟨hAB_EF.not_onLine hA_AB, hCD_EF.not_onLine hC_CD, hs⟩
  exact AreParallel.of_parallel h₁.1 h₂.1 hA_AB hB_AB hC_CD hD_CD hparallel
  -- Q. E. D.

named_declarations.Elements.BookI.Prop30.meet:
/-- A straight line meeting one of two parallels meets the other. If L is parallel
to M, and a straight line N, other than M, passes through a point P of M,
then N meets L. Otherwise N would be parallel to L too, and by I.30 M and
N would be parallel to one another, though both pass through P.

Euclid uses this whenever he draws a parallel and then names the point where it
meets another straight line: E and F in I.37, G and H in I.38, E in I.39,
F in I.40, F and G in I.42, H, L and M in I.44, E in I.46 and L in
I.47. It is the uniqueness of the parallel through a point, often called
Playfair's axiom; Heath reports under I.31 that Proclus draws it from I.30.
`Prop30.unique`, a step inside I.30's own proof, gives the same uniqueness from
I.29; later proofs cite this one, Proclus' route through I.30. [I. 30] -/
theorem Prop30.meet {L M N : Line} {P : Point} (hLM : Parallel L M) (hPM : OnLine P M)
    (hPN : OnLine P N) (hNM : N ≠ M) : ∃ Q : Point, OnLine Q N ∧ OnLine Q L
named_declarations.Elements.BookI.Prop30.unique:
/-- Euclid's enunciation also covers EF lying outside AB and CD, where a
straight line from one to the other need not cross it. For that case: two straight
lines through one point, each parallel to a third, are one straight line. A
straight line from the point to the third makes, with each, interior angles equal
to two right angles (I.29); Common Notion 3 takes away the angle they share, and
`onRay_of_angle_eq` makes the two rays one. This is the uniqueness of the
parallel, often called Playfair's axiom, proved here from I.29 rather than
assumed. Later proofs cite `Prop30.meet` instead: the same uniqueness, drawn
from I.30 itself, as Heath reports Proclus drawing it under I.31. -/
theorem Prop30.unique {L M N : Line} {G H : Point}
    (hLN : Parallel L N) (hMN : Parallel M N)
    (hGL : OnLine G L) (hGM : OnLine G M) (hHN : OnLine H N) : L = M

Let each of the straight lines AB, CD be parallel to EF;

I say that AB is also parallel to CD.

For let the straight line GK fall upon them.

the angle AGK is equal to the angle GHF. [I. 29]

Again, since the straight line GK has fallen on the parallel straight lines EF, CD,

the angle GHF is equal to the angle GKD. [I. 29]

But the angle AGK was also proved equal to the angle GHF;

therefore the angle AGK is also equal to the angle GKD; [C.N. 1]

and they are alternate.

Therefore AB is parallel to CD.

Q. E. D.

state.heath_proof:
Let A be the given point, and BC the given straight line;

thus it is required to draw through the point A a straight line parallel to the straight line BC.

Let a point D be taken at random on BC, and let AD be joined; on the straight line DA, and at the point A on it, let the angle DAE be constructed equal to the angle ADC [I. 23]; and let the straight line AF be produced in a straight line with EA.

Then, since the straight line AD falling on the two straight lines BC, EF has made the alternate angles EAD, ADC equal to one another,

therefore EAF is parallel to BC. [I. 27]

Therefore through the given point A the straight line EAF has been drawn parallel to the given straight line BC.

Q. E. F.
state.lean_proof:
/-- Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line. -/
theorem Prop31 {A B C : Point} (hBC : B ≠ C) (hA : ¬ Collinear B C A) :
    ∃ E F : Point, Between E A F ∧ AreParallel E F B C := by
  -- Let A be the given point, and BC the given straight line;
  /- The given point is off the given straight line: otherwise there would be no
     parallel through it. -/
  obtain ⟨BC, hB_BC, hC_BC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hBC
  have hA_BC : ¬ OnLine A BC := fun h => hA ⟨BC, hB_BC, hC_BC, h⟩
  -- thus it is required to draw through the point A a straight line parallel to the straight
  -- line BC.
  -- Let a point D be taken at random on BC,
  /- Taken between B and C, as Euclid's figure has it. -/
  obtain ⟨D, hD_BC, hBDC, -⟩ := exists_point_between hB_BC hC_BC hBC []
  -- and let AD be joined;
  /- Our proof uses only that A and D are two points: D is on BC and A is not.
     Then ADC and ADB are triangles, and B and C lie on either side of AD,
     since D is between them (`OppositeSidesOf.of_between`). -/
  have hAD : A ≠ D := fun h => hA_BC (h ▸ hD_BC)
  have hADC : Triangle A D C :=
    (Triangle.of_line hD_BC hC_BC (ne_of_between (between_symm hBDC)).symm hA_BC).cab
  have hADB : Triangle A D B :=
    (Triangle.of_line hD_BC hB_BC (ne_of_between hBDC).symm hA_BC).cab
  have hBC_AD : OppositeSidesOf B C A D := OppositeSidesOf.of_between hADB hBDC
  -- on the straight line DA, and at the point A on it, let the angle DAE be constructed equal
  -- to the angle ADC [I. 23];
  /- I.23 builds the angle at A with one arm along the ray from A through D (it
     passes through a point D₁ of that ray) and the other through a point E on
     whichever side of AD we ask for. We ask for B's side, away from C. The angle
     D₁AE is the angle DAE, its arms being the same rays (`angle_onRay_left`). -/
  obtain ⟨E, D₁, hD₁, hEB, hEAD₁⟩ := Prop23 hAD hADC hADB
  have hAE : A ≠ E := hEB.triangle.ne₁₃
  have hDAE : ∠ D A E = ∠ A D C :=
    (angle_onRay_left hD₁ hAE.symm).symm.trans ((angle_symm hD₁.2.1 hAE.symm).trans hEAD₁)
  -- and let the straight line AF be produced in a straight line with EA.
  obtain ⟨F, hEAF⟩ := produce hAE.symm
  -- Then, since the straight line AD falling on the two straight lines BC, EF has made the
  -- alternate angles EAD, ADC equal to one another,
  /- Alternate: E is on B's side of AD, and so on the other side from C
     (`SameSideOf.trans_opposite`). -/
  have hEC : OppositeSidesOf E C A D := hEB.trans_opposite hBC_AD
  have hEAD : ∠ E A D = ∠ A D C := (angle_symm hAE.symm hAD.symm).trans hDAE
  -- therefore EAF is parallel to BC. [I. 27]
  /- I.27 with EF for its AB, BC for its CD, and AD falling on them at A
     and D. -/
  have hpar : AreParallel E F B C := Prop27 hEAF hBDC hEC hEAD
  -- Therefore through the given point A the straight line EAF has been drawn parallel to the
  -- given straight line BC.
  exact ⟨E, F, hEAF, hpar⟩
  -- Q. E. F.

state.commentary:
Heath asks the question himself: "The construction, be it observed, depends only upon I. 27, and might therefore have come directly after that proposition. Why then did Euclid postpone it until after I. 29 and I. 30? Presumably because he considered it necessary, before giving the construction, to place beyond all doubt the fact that only one such parallel can be drawn" (vol. 1, p. 316). Our proof bears out his first sentence. Like Euclid's, it rests on I.23 and I.27 and not on Postulate 5, and in Book I it is the one proof after I.28 that does without the postulate.

**A parallel, or the parallel?** Proclus, Heath reports, draws the uniqueness from I.30: two straight lines through A, both parallel to BC, would be parallel to each other, though they meet at A. Heath thinks Euclid "deliberately determined that his own assumption was more appropriate to be made the subject of a Postulate than the assumption of the uniqueness of the parallel" (vol. 1, p. 316). That uniqueness later took John Playfair's name, though "it was of course not a new discovery. It is distinctly stated in Proclus' note to Eucl. I. 31" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 220). Our I.31 draws a parallel, as Euclid's does; that there is no other is `Prop30.unique`, proved from I.29.

Euclid's D is "taken at random on BC"; we take it between B and C, as his figure does, and copy the angle on B's side of AD, so that E falls across AD from C and the angles EAD, ADC are alternate.

**The modern way.** With coordinates no angle has to be copied: the parallel through A is the straight line of points $\mathrm{A} + t\mathrm{(C - B)}$, one for each real number $t$. Euclid's E is one of them with $t \lt 0$, on B's side of AD, and F one with $t \gt 0$.
state.heath_proof:
Let A be the given point, and BC the given straight line;

thus it is required to draw through the point A a straight line parallel to the straight line BC.

Let a point D be taken at random on BC, and let AD be joined; on the straight line DA, and at the point A on it, let the angle DAE be constructed equal to the angle ADC [I. 23]; and let the straight line AF be produced in a straight line with EA.

Then, since the straight line AD falling on the two straight lines BC, EF has made the alternate angles EAD, ADC equal to one another,

therefore EAF is parallel to BC. [I. 27]

Therefore through the given point A the straight line EAF has been drawn parallel to the given straight line BC.

Q. E. F.
state.lean_proof:
/-- Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line. -/
theorem Prop31 {A B C : Point} (hBC : B ≠ C) (hA : ¬ Collinear B C A) :
    ∃ E F : Point, Between E A F ∧ AreParallel E F B C := by
  -- Let A be the given point, and BC the given straight line;
  /- The given point is off the given straight line: otherwise there would be no
     parallel through it. -/
  obtain ⟨BC, hB_BC, hC_BC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hBC
  have hA_BC : ¬ OnLine A BC := fun h => hA ⟨BC, hB_BC, hC_BC, h⟩
  -- thus it is required to draw through the point A a straight line parallel to the straight
  -- line BC.
  -- Let a point D be taken at random on BC,
  /- Taken between B and C, as Euclid's figure has it. -/
  obtain ⟨D, hD_BC, hBDC, -⟩ := exists_point_between hB_BC hC_BC hBC []
  -- and let AD be joined;
  /- Our proof uses only that A and D are two points: D is on BC and A is not.
     Then ADC and ADB are triangles, and B and C lie on either side of AD,
     since D is between them (`OppositeSidesOf.of_between`). -/
  have hAD : A ≠ D := fun h => hA_BC (h ▸ hD_BC)
  have hADC : Triangle A D C :=
    (Triangle.of_line hD_BC hC_BC (ne_of_between (between_symm hBDC)).symm hA_BC).cab
  have hADB : Triangle A D B :=
    (Triangle.of_line hD_BC hB_BC (ne_of_between hBDC).symm hA_BC).cab
  have hBC_AD : OppositeSidesOf B C A D := OppositeSidesOf.of_between hADB hBDC
  -- on the straight line DA, and at the point A on it, let the angle DAE be constructed equal
  -- to the angle ADC [I. 23];
  /- I.23 builds the angle at A with one arm along the ray from A through D (it
     passes through a point D₁ of that ray) and the other through a point E on
     whichever side of AD we ask for. We ask for B's side, away from C. The angle
     D₁AE is the angle DAE, its arms being the same rays (`angle_onRay_left`). -/
  obtain ⟨E, D₁, hD₁, hEB, hEAD₁⟩ := Prop23 hAD hADC hADB
  have hAE : A ≠ E := hEB.triangle.ne₁₃
  have hDAE : ∠ D A E = ∠ A D C :=
    (angle_onRay_left hD₁ hAE.symm).symm.trans ((angle_symm hD₁.2.1 hAE.symm).trans hEAD₁)
  -- and let the straight line AF be produced in a straight line with EA.
  obtain ⟨F, hEAF⟩ := produce hAE.symm
  -- Then, since the straight line AD falling on the two straight lines BC, EF has made the
  -- alternate angles EAD, ADC equal to one another,
  /- Alternate: E is on B's side of AD, and so on the other side from C
     (`SameSideOf.trans_opposite`). -/
  have hEC : OppositeSidesOf E C A D := hEB.trans_opposite hBC_AD
  have hEAD : ∠ E A D = ∠ A D C := (angle_symm hAE.symm hAD.symm).trans hDAE
  -- therefore EAF is parallel to BC. [I. 27]
  /- I.27 with EF for its AB, BC for its CD, and AD falling on them at A
     and D. -/
  have hpar : AreParallel E F B C := Prop27 hEAF hBDC hEC hEAD
  -- Therefore through the given point A the straight line EAF has been drawn parallel to the
  -- given straight line BC.
  exact ⟨E, F, hEAF, hpar⟩
  -- Q. E. F.

statement.note: Draws a parallel through A, as asked; that there is no other, which Proclus remarks, is proved from I.29 as `Prop30.unique`.

named_declarations.Elements.BookI.Prop30.unique:
/-- Euclid's enunciation also covers EF lying outside AB and CD, where a
straight line from one to the other need not cross it. For that case: two straight
lines through one point, each parallel to a third, are one straight line. A
straight line from the point to the third makes, with each, interior angles equal
to two right angles (I.29); Common Notion 3 takes away the angle they share, and
`onRay_of_angle_eq` makes the two rays one. This is the uniqueness of the
parallel, often called Playfair's axiom, proved here from I.29 rather than
assumed. Later proofs cite `Prop30.meet` instead: the same uniqueness, drawn
from I.30 itself, as Heath reports Proclus drawing it under I.31. -/
theorem Prop30.unique {L M N : Line} {G H : Point}
    (hLN : Parallel L N) (hMN : Parallel M N)
    (hGL : OnLine G L) (hGM : OnLine G M) (hHN : OnLine H N) : L = M

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M

/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type

state.heath_proof:
Let ABC be a triangle, and let one side of it BC be produced to D;

I say that the exterior angle ACD is equal to the two interior and opposite angles CAB, ABC, and the three interior angles of the triangle ABC, BCA, CAB are equal to two right angles.

For let CE be drawn through the point C parallel to the straight line AB. [I. 31]

Then, since AB is parallel to CE,

and AC has fallen upon them,

the alternate angles BAC, ACE are equal to one another. [I. 29]

Again, since AB is parallel to CE,

and the straight line BD has fallen upon them,

the exterior angle ECD is equal to the interior and opposite angle ABC. [I. 29]

But the angle ACE was also proved equal to the angle BAC;

therefore the whole angle ACD is equal to the two interior and opposite angles BAC, ABC.

Let the angle ACB be added to each;

therefore the angles ACD, ACB are equal to the three angles ABC, BCA, CAB.

But the angles ACD, ACB are equal to two right angles; [I. 13]

therefore the angles ABC, BCA, CAB are also equal to two right angles.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- In any triangle, if one of the sides be produced, the exterior angle is equal to the two
interior and opposite angles, and the three interior angles of the triangle are equal to two
right angles. -/
theorem Prop32 {A B C D : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hBCD : Between B C D) :
    ∠ A C D = ∠ C A B + ∠ A B C ∧ ∠ A B C + ∠ B C A + ∠ C A B = ∟ + ∟ := by
  -- Let ABC be a triangle, and let one side of it BC be produced to D;
  obtain ⟨BC, hB_BC, hC_BC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hABC.ne₂₃
  have hD_BC : OnLine D BC := on_line_of_between hBCD hB_BC hC_BC
  have hCD : C ≠ D := (ne_of_between (between_symm hBCD)).symm
  -- I say that the exterior angle ACD is equal to the two interior and opposite angles CAB,
  -- ABC, and the three interior angles of the triangle ABC, BCA, CAB are equal to two right
  -- angles.
  -- For let CE be drawn through the point C parallel to the straight line AB. [I. 31]
  obtain ⟨P, Q, hPCQ, hPQ⟩ := Prop31 hABC.ne₁₂ hABC
  obtain ⟨E, hCE, hEA⟩ := Prop32.choose_end hABC hPCQ hPQ
  -- Then, since AB is parallel to CE,
  have hAB : AreParallel A B C E := hCE.symm
  -- and AC has fallen upon them,
  have hBE : OppositeSidesOf B E A C := hAB.swap_left.oppositeSidesOf hEA.symm
  -- the alternate angles BAC, ACE are equal to one another. [I. 29]
  have hBAC_ACE : ∠ B A C = ∠ A C E := Prop29.alternate hAB.swap_left hBE
  -- Again, since AB is parallel to CE,
  have hCE_BA : AreParallel C E B A := hCE.swap_right
  -- and the straight line BD has fallen upon them,
  -- the exterior angle ECD is equal to the interior and opposite angle ABC. [I. 29]
  have hECD_ABC : ∠ E C D = ∠ A B C := by
    have h := Prop29.exterior hCE_BA hEA.swap (between_symm hBCD)
    rw [angle_symm hCD.symm hCE.1.symm, angle_symm hABC.ne₂₃.symm hABC.ne₁₂] at h
    exact h
  -- But the angle ACE was also proved equal to the angle BAC;
  have hACE_BAC : ∠ A C E = ∠ B A C := hBAC_ACE.symm
  -- therefore the whole angle ACD is equal to the two interior and opposite angles BAC, ABC.
  /- E lies within ACD: both E and D are opposite B across AC,
     and E is on A's side of the straight line CD, which is BC. -/
  have hED : SameSideOf E D C A :=
    (hBE.sameSideOf (OppositeSidesOf.of_between hABC.acb hBCD)).swap
  have hEA_CD : SameSideOf E A C D :=
    SameSideOf.of_line hCD hC_BC hD_BC (hEA.sameSide hB_BC hC_BC)
  have hACD : ∠ A C D = ∠ C A B + ∠ A B C := by
    rw [angle_add_of_within hED hEA_CD, hACE_BAC, hECD_ABC,
      angle_symm hABC.ne₁₂.symm hABC.ne₁₃.symm]
  -- Let the angle ACB be added to each;
  have hadd := CommonNotion2 hACD (Eq.refl (∠ A C B))
  -- therefore the angles ACD, ACB are equal to the three angles ABC, BCA, CAB.
  have hthree : ∠ A C D + ∠ A C B = ∠ A B C + ∠ B C A + ∠ C A B := by
    rw [hadd, angle_symm hABC.ne₁₃ hABC.ne₂₃,
      add_comm (∠ C A B), add_assoc, add_comm (∠ C A B), ← add_assoc]
  -- But the angles ACD, ACB are equal to two right angles; [I. 13]
  have hright : ∠ A C D + ∠ A C B = ∟ + ∟ := by
    rw [add_comm, angle_symm hABC.ne₁₃ hABC.ne₂₃]
    exact Prop13 hBCD (Triangle.of_line hB_BC hD_BC (ne_of_between_ends hBCD)
      (hABC.bca.off_line hB_BC hC_BC))
  -- therefore the angles ABC, BCA, CAB are also equal to two right angles.
  have hsum : ∠ A B C + ∠ B C A + ∠ C A B = ∟ + ∟ := hthree.symm.trans hright
  -- Therefore etc.
  exact ⟨hACD, hsum⟩
  -- Q. E. D.

helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.of_parallel:
/-- Two different points of L, and two different points of M, are the ends of
parallel straight lines when L and M are parallel: two points fix one straight
line (System E, Generalities 1). With `AreParallel.parallel`, this says "AB is
parallel to CD" of any other two points P, Q of the straight line AB and R,
S of CD. -/
theorem AreParallel.of_parallel (hPQ : P ≠ Q) (hRS : R ≠ S) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L)
    (hR : OnLine R M) (hS : OnLine S M) (h : Parallel L M) : AreParallel P Q R S
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.oppositeSidesOf:
/-- Joining two parallels. If AB is parallel to CD, and B and D lie on the
same side of AC (the two "in the same directions", as I.33 says), then A and D
lie on opposite sides of BC: the angles ABC, BCD are alternate.

Were D on A's side of BC, it would lie within the angle ACB, and the straight
line CD, drawn within that angle, would cross AB (`crossbar`); but parallels do
not meet. -/
theorem AreParallel.oppositeSidesOf (h : AreParallel A B C D) (hBD : SameSideOf B D A C) :
    OppositeSidesOf A D B C
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.parallel:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then a straight line through A and B is parallel
to one through C and D. -/
theorem AreParallel.parallel (h : AreParallel A B C D) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (hC : OnLine C M) (hD : OnLine D M) : Parallel L M
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.sameSideOf:
/-- The ends of one parallel lie on one side of the other: if AB is parallel to
CD, then A and B are on the same side of CD (`Parallel.sameSide`). -/
theorem AreParallel.sameSideOf (h : AreParallel A B C D) : SameSideOf A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.swap_left:
/-- "AB is parallel to CD" is the same as "BA is parallel to CD". -/
theorem AreParallel.swap_left (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel B A C D
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.swap_right:
/-- "AB is parallel to CD" is the same as "AB is parallel to DC". -/
theorem AreParallel.swap_right (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel A B D C
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.symm:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then CD is parallel to AB. -/
theorem AreParallel.symm (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop13:
/-- If a straight line set up on a straight line make angles, it will make either two right angles
or angles equal to two right angles. -/
theorem Prop13 {A B C D : Point} (hCBD : Between C B D) (hA : ¬ Collinear C D A) :
    ∠ C B A + ∠ A B D = ∟ + ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29:
/-- A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one
another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on
the same side equal to two right angles. -/
theorem Prop29 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (hpar : AreParallel A B C D) (hAGB : Between A G B)
    (hCHD : Between C H D) (hEGH : Between E G H) (hGHF : Between G H F)
    (hBD : SameSideOf B D E F) :
    ∠ A G H = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ E G B = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D = ∟ + ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29.alternate:
/-- The alternate angles. If the straight line PG is parallel to HQ, and P and
Q lie on opposite sides of GH, then the alternate angles PGH, GHQ are equal.
Euclid's figure is drawn about GH, each straight line produced beyond G and H
(`AreParallel.figure_alternate`), and I.29 does the rest. [I. 29] -/
theorem Prop29.alternate {P G H Q : Point} (hpar : AreParallel P G H Q)
    (hPQ : OppositeSidesOf P Q G H) : ∠ P G H = ∠ G H Q
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29.exterior:
/-- The exterior angle. If the straight line GP is parallel to HQ, P and Q lie
on one side of GH, and E lies on HG produced beyond G, then the exterior
angle EGP is equal to the interior and opposite angle GHQ. [I. 29] -/
theorem Prop29.exterior {P G H Q E : Point} (hpar : AreParallel G P H Q)
    (hPQ : SameSideOf P Q G H) (hEGH : Between E G H) : ∠ E G P = ∠ G H Q
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31:
/-- Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line. -/
theorem Prop31 {A B C : Point} (hBC : B ≠ C) (hA : ¬ Collinear B C A) :
    ∃ E F : Point, Between E A F ∧ AreParallel E F B C
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop32.choose_end:
/-- Euclid's figure puts E, on the parallel through C, on A's side of BC.
The two points I.31 gives, one on either side of C, lie on opposite sides of
BC, which crosses their straight line at C; and a straight line has just two
sides, so one of them is on A's side (System E, Pasch 3 and Same side 5). It
cites no proposition. -/
theorem Prop32.choose_end {A B C P Q : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C)
    (hPCQ : Between P C Q) (hpar : AreParallel P Q A B) :
    ∃ E : Point, AreParallel C E A B ∧ SameSideOf E A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.CommonNotion2:
/-- **Common Notion 2.** If equals be added to equals, the wholes are equal. -/
theorem CommonNotion2 {a b c d : Magnitude k} (h₁ : a = b) (h₂ : c = d) :
    a + c = b + d
helper_signatures.Elements.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf:
/-- `P` and `Q` lie on opposite sides of the straight line `AB`. -/
def OppositeSidesOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.of_between:
/-- A straight line through a point of AB, from a point C off it, crosses to
the other side: if B lies between C and E, then E is on the other side
of the straight line AB from C. (System E, Pasch 3) -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.of_between {C E : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C)
    (h : Between C B E) : OppositeSidesOf C E A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf:
/-- The same, said of "the straight line AB": two points, each on the other side of
AB from C, are on the same side of AB as each other. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf {C D E : Point} (h₁ : OppositeSidesOf C D A B)
    (h₂ : OppositeSidesOf C E A B) : SameSideOf D E A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.swap:
/-- "On opposite sides of AB" is the same as "on opposite sides of BA". -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.swap (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : OppositeSidesOf P Q B A
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the other side of AB from Q, then Q is on the other side
from P. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.symm (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : OppositeSidesOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.off_transversal:
/-- A straight line T falling on two parallels, at G on L and at H on M,
meets L at G alone: every other point of L is off T. Otherwise T, through
two points of L, would be L itself (System E, Generalities 1), and H would lie
on both parallels. -/
theorem Parallel.off_transversal (h : Parallel L M) (hG : OnLine G L) (hH : OnLine H M)
    (hGT : OnLine G T) (hHT : OnLine H T) (hP : OnLine P L) (hPG : P ≠ G) : ¬ OnLine P T
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.sameSide:
/-- All the points of one parallel lie on one side of the other: two points of L
are on the same side of M. Were they on opposite sides, the straight line L
joining them would cross M (System E, Intersection 1). -/
theorem Parallel.sameSide (h : Parallel L M) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L) :
    SameSide P Q M
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.symm:
/-- If L is parallel to M, then M is parallel to L. -/
theorem Parallel.symm (h : Parallel L M) : Parallel M L
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate1:
/-- **Postulate 1.** To draw a straight line from any point to any point. -/
axiom Postulate1 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf:
/-- `P` and `Q` lie on the same side of the straight line `AB`. -/
def SameSideOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.of_line:
/-- Two points on the same side of a straight line L through A and B are on
the same side of the straight line AB, however that line is named: two points
fix one straight line. -/
theorem SameSideOf.of_line (hAB : A ≠ B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (h : SameSide P Q L) : SameSideOf P Q A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.sameSide:
/-- Two points on the same side of the straight line AB are on the same side of
any straight line drawn through A and B. -/
theorem SameSideOf.sameSide (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    SameSide P Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.swap:
/-- "On the same side of AB" is the same as "on the same side of BA". -/
theorem SameSideOf.swap (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf P Q B A
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the same side of AB as Q, then Q is on the same side as P. -/
theorem SameSideOf.symm (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.trans:
/-- Points on the same side as a third are on the same side as each other. -/
theorem SameSideOf.trans (h₁ : SameSideOf P Q A B) (h₂ : SameSideOf Q R A B) :
    SameSideOf P R A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.add_assoc:
/-- Adding three magnitudes in a row, it makes no difference whether the first two or the last
two are added first. (System E §3.5) -/
axiom add_assoc (a b c : Magnitude k) : a + b + c = a + (b + c)
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.add_comm:
/-- The order of adding does not matter. (System E §3.5) -/
axiom add_comm (a b : Magnitude k) : a + b = b + a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.angle_symm:
/-- The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4) -/
axiom angle_symm (hAB : A ≠ B) (hCB : C ≠ B) : ∠ A B C = ∠ C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_symm:
/-- If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1) -/
axiom between_symm (h : Between A B C) : Between C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between:
/-- A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between_ends:
/-- The ends of a finite straight line differ. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between:
/-- A straight line through A and B, with B between A and C, passes
through C. (Between 2) -/
axiom on_line_of_between (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    OnLine C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between_ends:
/-- A straight line through A and C passes through every point between them.
(Between 3) -/
axiom on_line_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hC : OnLine C L) :
    OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.pasch3:
/-- A straight line through a point between A and C separates them. (Pasch 3) -/
axiom pasch3 (h : Between A B C) (hB : OnLine B L) : ¬ SameSide A C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.same_side_or:
/-- A straight line has only two sides. (Same side 5) -/
axiom same_side_or (hA : ¬ OnLine A L) (hB : ¬ OnLine B L) (hC : ¬ OnLine C L)
    (h : ¬ SameSide A B L) : SameSide A C L ∨ SameSide B C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.acb:
/-- The triangle ABC, named the other way round, as ACB. -/
theorem Triangle.acb (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle A C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.bca:
/-- The triangle ABC, named from B, as BCA. -/
theorem Triangle.bca (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle B C A
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₁₂:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₁₂ (h : Triangle A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₁₃:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₁₃ (h : Triangle A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₂₃:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₂₃ (h : Triangle A B C) : B ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.of_line:
/-- Two different points of a straight line, and a third point off it, make a
triangle. -/
theorem Triangle.of_line {P Q R : Point} (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L) (hPQ : P ≠ Q)
    (hR : ¬ OnLine R L) : Triangle P Q R
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.off_line:
/-- In the triangle ABC, the corner C is off every straight line through A
and B. -/
theorem Triangle.off_line (h : Triangle A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    ¬ OnLine C L
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_add_of_within:
/-- A straight line drawn from the corner of an angle through a point within it
cuts the angle into two. If R lies within the angle PVQ, on Q's side of VP
and on P's side of VQ, then the angle PVQ is made up of the angles PVR and
RVQ. This is System E's Diagram-angle 2, said of "the straight lines VP, VQ"
rather than of lines drawn and named. -/
theorem angle_add_of_within {V P Q R : Point} (hRQ : SameSideOf R Q V P)
    (hRP : SameSideOf R P V Q) : ∠ P V Q = ∠ P V R + ∠ R V Q

I.13.enunciation: If a straight line set up on a straight line make angles, it will make either two right angles or angles equal to two right angles.

I.29.enunciation: A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on the same side equal to two right angles.

I.31.enunciation: Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line.

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle

question.instructions:
Does every proposition called by the proof unit in `lean_proof` do work towards its conclusion or a substantive intermediate step of Euclid's argument? Also check for artificial hypothesis uses. Judge this unit's uses of the supplied helper signatures; helper bodies are outside this question. Heath's sentences stand as `--` lines and `cited` gives exact enunciations. In Lean, `have h : T := p` proves T by p and calls the result h; `obtain ⟨…⟩ := p` takes p apart into named pieces; `rw [h34, h37, …]` rewrites the goal by the equalities named. Follow uses through helper calls and tactics as well as explicit names. An anonymous binding or an unused hypothesis alone does not establish a defect. If both defects occur, choose `a dummy citation`.

docs/FORMALIZATION.md, section 5:
A checked intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid is legitimate, even if the
  final proof term could do without it.

criteria.cannot tell: What is given here is not enough to decide.
criteria.all do work: Every proposition call supports a later step or the conclusion, or establishes a substantive intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid. No hypothesis is mentioned merely to look used. With no proposition calls the citation part alone is vacuous; hypothesis use must still be inspected.
criteria.a dummy citation: Some proposition call does no substantive work: its result neither supports the argument nor establishes a substantive intermediate fact, and merely supplies a citation while the step is done another way.
criteria.an artificial hypothesis use: No dummy citation is established, but a hypothesis is mentioned only so that it looks used, and does no substantive work.
