state.lean_proof:
/-- Parallelograms which are on the same base and in the same parallels are equal to one another. -/
theorem Prop35 {A B C D E F : Point} (h₁ : Parallelogram A B C D) (h₂ : Parallelogram E B C F)
    (hAF : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine D L ∧ OnLine E L ∧ OnLine F L) :
    quadArea A B C D = quadArea E B C F := by
  -- Let ABCD, EBCF be parallelograms on the same base BC and in the same parallels AF, BC;
  obtain ⟨AF, hA, hD, hE, hF⟩ := hAF
  obtain ⟨BC, hB, hC⟩ := Postulate1 B C h₁.2.1
  -- I say that ABCD is equal to the parallelogram EBCF.
  /- Euclid takes the case where AD and EF have no point in common, with D between
     A and E. We give his argument in his letters, then cover the other orders. -/
  have euclid : ∀ {A D E F : Point}, Parallelogram A B C D → Parallelogram E B C F →
      OnLine A AF → OnLine D AF → OnLine F AF → Between A D E →
      quadArea A B C D = quadArea E B C F := by
    intro A D E F h₁ h₂ hA hD hF hADE
    have hE : OnLine E AF := on_line_of_between hADE hA hD
    -- For, since ABCD is a parallelogram,
    have hAF_BC : Parallel AF BC := (h₁.2.parallel hB hC hD hA).symm
    -- AD is equal to BC. [I. 34]
    have hAD : ‖A D‖ = ‖B C‖ := (Prop34 (A := A) (B := D) (C := B) (D := C) h₁).1
    -- For the same reason also
    -- EF is equal to BC,
    have hEF : ‖E F‖ = ‖B C‖ := (Prop34 (A := E) (B := F) (C := B) (D := C) h₂).1
    -- so that AD is also equal to EF; [C.N. 1]
    have hAD_EF : ‖A D‖ = ‖E F‖ := CommonNotion1 hAD hEF
    -- and DE is common;
    /- G lies between E and B and between D and C; E lies between D and F.
       These are the orders Euclid reads from his figure. -/
    obtain ⟨G, hEGB, hDGC, hDEF⟩ := Prop35.figure h₁ h₂ hA hD hF hADE
    -- therefore the whole AE is equal to the whole DF. [C.N. 2]
    have hAE_DF : ‖A E‖ = ‖D F‖ := by
      have := CommonNotion2 hAD_EF (rfl : ‖D E‖ = ‖D E‖)
      rw [len_add_of_between hADE, add_comm, len_add_of_between hDEF] at this
      exact this
    -- But AB is also equal to DC; [I. 34]
    have hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖D C‖ := (Prop34 (A := A) (B := D) (C := B) (D := C) h₁).2.1
    -- therefore the two sides EA, AB are equal to the two sides FD, DC respectively,
    have hB_AF : ¬ OnLine B AF := hAF_BC.symm.not_onLine hB
    have hC_AF : ¬ OnLine C AF := hAF_BC.symm.not_onLine hC
    have hAEB : Triangle A E B := Triangle.of_line hA hE (ne_of_between_ends hADE) hB_AF
    have hDFC : Triangle D F C := Triangle.of_line hD hF (ne_of_between_ends hDEF) hC_AF
    -- and the angle FDC is equal to the angle EAB, the exterior to the interior; [I. 29]
    have hADF : Between A D F := between_of_between_right hADE hDEF
    have hFDC : ∠ F D C = ∠ E A B := by
      rw [Prop29.exterior h₁.1.symm.swap_left h₁.2.sameSideOf.symm (between_symm hADF),
        angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_beyond hADE) h₁.triangle.ne₁₂.symm]
    -- therefore the base EB is equal to the base FC,
    have h4 := Prop4 hAEB hDFC hAE_DF hAB hFDC.symm
    have hEB_FC : ‖E B‖ = ‖F C‖ := h4.1
    -- and the triangle EAB will be equal to the triangle FDC. [I. 4]
    have htri : △ A E B = △ D F C := h4.2.1
    -- Let DGE be subtracted from each;
    /- ABGD is named from B, so that its diameter is BD. Each taking away is
       written as a cutting: the larger triangle is the trapezium and DGE together. -/
    have e₁ : △ A E B = quadArea B G D A + △ D G E := by
      unfold quadArea
      rw [area_cab A E B, ← area_cut (A := B) hADE, area_bca B D E, ← area_cut (A := D) hEGB,
        area_cba B G D, area_acb B D A, area_acb D G E]
      ac_rfl
    have e₂ : △ D F C = quadArea E G C F + △ D G E := by
      unfold quadArea
      rw [area_cab D F C, ← area_cut (A := C) hDEF, area_cba C D E, ← area_cut (A := E) hDGC,
        area_bac E C F, area_cab D G E]
      ac_rfl
    -- therefore the trapezium ABGD which remains is equal to the trapezium EGCF which
    -- remains. [C.N. 3]
    have trap : quadArea B G D A = quadArea E G C F :=
      CommonNotion3 (e₁.symm.trans (htri.trans e₂)) rfl
    -- Let the triangle GBC be added to each;
    have hsum := CommonNotion2 trap (rfl : △ G B C = △ G B C)
    -- therefore the whole parallelogram ABCD is equal to the whole parallelogram EBCF. [C.N. 2]
    have hL : quadArea A B C D = quadArea B G D A + △ G B C := by
      rw [← h₁.quadArea_rotate]
      unfold quadArea
      rw [area_acb B C D, ← area_cut (A := B) hDGC, area_acb B G D, area_bac G B C]
      ac_rfl
    have hR : quadArea E B C F = quadArea E G C F + △ G B C := by
      unfold quadArea
      rw [area_cab E B C, ← area_cut (A := C) hEGB, area_cab E G C, area_cab G B C]
      ac_rfl
    rw [hL, hR, hsum]
  /- E may also fall between A and D, or at either end. The helpers add equal
     triangles to the common part, as Proclus does in the cases Heath reports.
     When E is A, equal lengths on the same ray make F equal to D. -/
  have oneway : ∀ {A D E F : Point}, Parallelogram A B C D → Parallelogram E B C F →
      OnLine A AF → OnLine D AF → OnLine E AF → OnLine F AF → (E = A ∨ SameSideOf C E A B) →
      quadArea A B C D = quadArea E B C F := by
    intro A D E F h₁ h₂ hA hD hE hF hdir
    obtain ⟨hAD, -, -, -, -⟩ := Prop34 (A := A) (B := D) (C := B) (D := C) h₁
    obtain ⟨hEF, -, -, -, -⟩ := Prop34 (A := E) (B := F) (C := B) (D := C) h₂
    rcases hdir with rfl | hCE
    · /- E is A, and so F is D. -/
      have hFray : OnRay F E D :=
        OnRay.of_sameSideOf (h₂.sameSideOf.symm.trans h₁.sameSideOf) ⟨AF, hE, hD, hF⟩
          (h₂.sameSideOf.symm.triangle.ne₁₃.symm)
      rw [hFray.eq_of_len_eq (hEF.trans hAD.symm)]
    · have hEA : E ≠ A := hCE.symm.triangle.ne₁₃.symm
      have hEray : OnRay E A D :=
        OnRay.of_sameSideOf (hCE.symm.trans h₁.sameSideOf) ⟨AF, hA, hD, hE⟩ hEA
      by_cases hED : E = D
      · subst hED
        exact Prop35.same h₁ h₂ hA hE hF
      · rcases between_cases hEray.1 (Ne.symm hED) hEA.symm hA hD hE with h | h | h
        · exact euclid h₁ h₂ hA hD hF h
        · exact absurd (between_symm h) hEray.2.2.2
        · exact Prop35.between h₁ h₂ hA hD hE hF h
  /- Exchanging the parallelograms covers the other direction along AF. -/
  have harea : quadArea A B C D = quadArea E B C F := by
    by_cases hEA : E = A
    · exact oneway h₁ h₂ hA hD hE hF (Or.inl hEA)
    · have hAF_BC : Parallel AF BC := (h₁.2.parallel hB hC hD hA).symm
      rcases (AreParallel.of_parallel (Ne.symm hEA) h₁.2.1 hA hE hB hC hAF_BC).sameSideOf_or with h | h
      · exact oneway h₁ h₂ hA hD hE hF (Or.inr h)
      · exact (oneway h₂ h₁ hE hF hA hD (Or.inr h)).symm
  -- Therefore etc.
  exact harea
  -- Q. E. D.

helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.cross_or:
/-- A four-sided figure between two parallels. If AD is parallel to BC, then
either the diameters AC and BD of the figure ABCD cross, or its sides AB and
DC cross: AD runs the same way as BC, or the other way.

The straight line AC either separates B from D or it does not. If it does, BD
crosses it, between the parallels, and so between A and C. If it does not, D
lies within the angle ACB, and the straight line CD crosses AB (`crossbar`),
again between the parallels (`Between.of_inside`). -/
theorem AreParallel.cross_or (h : AreParallel A D B C) :
    (∃ X : Point, Between A X C ∧ Between B X D) ∨
      (∃ X : Point, Between A X B ∧ Between D X C)
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.of_parallel:
/-- Two different points of L, and two different points of M, are the ends of
parallel straight lines when L and M are parallel: two points fix one straight
line (System E, Generalities 1). With `AreParallel.parallel`, this says "AB is
parallel to CD" of any other two points P, Q of the straight line AB and R,
S of CD. -/
theorem AreParallel.of_parallel (hPQ : P ≠ Q) (hRS : R ≠ S) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L)
    (hR : OnLine R M) (hS : OnLine S M) (h : Parallel L M) : AreParallel P Q R S
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.parallel:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then a straight line through A and B is parallel
to one through C and D. -/
theorem AreParallel.parallel (h : AreParallel A B C D) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (hC : OnLine C M) (hD : OnLine D M) : Parallel L M
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.sameSideOf:
/-- The ends of one parallel lie on one side of the other: if AB is parallel to
CD, then A and B are on the same side of CD (`Parallel.sameSide`). -/
theorem AreParallel.sameSideOf (h : AreParallel A B C D) : SameSideOf A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.sameSideOf_or:
/-- Which way two parallels run. If AD is parallel to BC, then either D lies on
C's side of AB (AD runs the same way as BC), or A lies on C's side of
DB (DA runs the same way as BC). This is `AreParallel.cross_or`, read with
`SameSideOf.of_cross`. -/
theorem AreParallel.sameSideOf_or (h : AreParallel A D B C) :
    SameSideOf C D A B ∨ SameSideOf C A D B
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.swap_left:
/-- "AB is parallel to CD" is the same as "BA is parallel to CD". -/
theorem AreParallel.swap_left (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel B A C D
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.symm:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then CD is parallel to AB. -/
theorem AreParallel.symm (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.triangle:
/-- An end of one parallel is off the other: if AB is parallel to CD, then C
is not on the straight line AB, and ABC is a triangle. (Turned round with
`AreParallel.symm` and `.swap_right`, the same holds of D, and of A and B
beside CD.) -/
theorem AreParallel.triangle (h : AreParallel A B C D) : Triangle A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29:
/-- A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one
another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on
the same side equal to two right angles. -/
theorem Prop29 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (hpar : AreParallel A B C D) (hAGB : Between A G B)
    (hCHD : Between C H D) (hEGH : Between E G H) (hGHF : Between G H F)
    (hBD : SameSideOf B D E F) :
    ∠ A G H = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ E G B = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D = ∟ + ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29.exterior:
/-- The exterior angle. If the straight line GP is parallel to HQ, P and Q lie
on one side of GH, and E lies on HG produced beyond G, then the exterior
angle EGP is equal to the interior and opposite angle GHQ. [I. 29] -/
theorem Prop29.exterior {P G H Q E : Point} (hpar : AreParallel G P H Q)
    (hPQ : SameSideOf P Q G H) (hEGH : Between E G H) : ∠ E G P = ∠ G H Q
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop34:
/-- In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the
diameter bisects the areas. -/
theorem Prop34 {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A C D B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ C D B ∧ ∠ A B D = ∠ A C D ∧
      △ A B C = △ D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop35.between:
/-- One case Euclid leaves out, which Proclus supplies, as Heath reports under I.35:
when E lies between A and D, D lies between E and F. The triangles
EAB, FDC are equal by I.34, I.29 and I.4; adding each to the trapezium EBCD
gives the two parallelograms. -/
theorem Prop35.between {A B C D E F : Point} (h₁ : Parallelogram A B C D) (h₂ : Parallelogram E B C F)
    {AF : Line} (hA : OnLine A AF) (hD : OnLine D AF) (hE : OnLine E AF) (hF : OnLine F AF)
    (hAED : Between A E D) :
    quadArea A B C D = quadArea E B C F
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop35.figure:
/-- Euclid's figure: with D between A and E, EB crosses DC at a point G
between the parallels, and E lies between D and F. -/
theorem Prop35.figure {A B C D E F : Point} (h₁ : Parallelogram A B C D)
    (h₂ : Parallelogram E B C F) {AF : Line} (hA : OnLine A AF) (hD : OnLine D AF)
    (hF : OnLine F AF) (hADE : Between A D E) :
    ∃ G : Point, Between E G B ∧ Between D G C ∧ Between D E F
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop35.same:
/-- The other case Euclid leaves out, which Proclus also supplies: when E is D,
that point lies between A and F. The triangles ADB, DFC are equal by I.34,
I.29 and I.4; adding the common triangle DBC to each gives the two
parallelograms. -/
theorem Prop35.same {A B C D F : Point} (h₁ : Parallelogram A B C D) (h₂ : Parallelogram D B C F)
    {AF : Line} (hA : OnLine A AF) (hD : OnLine D AF) (hF : OnLine F AF) :
    quadArea A B C D = quadArea D B C F
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop4:
/-- If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles
contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the base, the
triangle will be equal to the triangle, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining
angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend. -/
theorem Prop4 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖D F‖) (hA : ∠ B A C = ∠ E D F) :
    ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ ∧ △ A B C = △ D E F ∧ ∠ A B C = ∠ D E F ∧ ∠ A C B = ∠ D F E
helper_signatures.Elements.CommonNotion1:
/-- **Common Notion 1.** Things which are equal to the same thing are also equal
to one another. -/
theorem CommonNotion1 {α : Sort _} {a b c : α} (h₁ : a = c) (h₂ : b = c) : a = b
helper_signatures.Elements.CommonNotion2:
/-- **Common Notion 2.** If equals be added to equals, the wholes are equal. -/
theorem CommonNotion2 {a b c d : Magnitude k} (h₁ : a = b) (h₂ : c = d) :
    a + c = b + d
helper_signatures.Elements.CommonNotion3:
/-- **Common Notion 3.** If equals be subtracted from equals, the remainders
are equal. (From `a + c = b + d` and `c = d`, conclude `a = b`.) -/
theorem CommonNotion3 {a b c d : Magnitude k} (h₁ : a + c = b + d) (h₂ : c = d) :
    a = b
helper_signatures.Elements.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.between_of_len_lt:
/-- Of two points on a ray, the one nearer the start lies between the start and
the other. -/
theorem OnRay.between_of_len_lt (hP : OnRay P A B) (hQ : OnRay Q A B) (h : ‖A P‖ < ‖A Q‖) :
    Between A P Q
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.eq_of_len_eq:
/-- On a ray, only one point lies at a given distance from its start: a point P
on the ray from A through B, as far from A as B is, is B itself.

This is Sir Henry Savile's argument, which Heath reports on I.4 (vol. 1,
p. 250): otherwise P falls short of B or beyond it, and either way the less
would be equal to the greater. -/
theorem OnRay.eq_of_len_eq (hP : OnRay P A B) (h : ‖A P‖ = ‖A B‖) : P = B
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.of_between:
/-- A point between A and B is on the ray from A through B. -/
theorem OnRay.of_between (h : Between A P B) : OnRay P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.of_beyond:
/-- A point beyond B, on the straight line from A through B produced, is on
the ray from A through B. -/
theorem OnRay.of_beyond (h : Between A B P) : OnRay P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.of_sameSideOf:
/-- Going the other way: a point P of the straight line DF, other than D, and
on the same side of the straight line DE as F, is on the ray from D through
F. It is not behind D, for then DE would separate it from F (System E,
Pasch 3). -/
theorem OnRay.of_sameSideOf {D E F P : Point} (h : SameSideOf P F D E) (hP : Collinear D F P)
    (hPD : P ≠ D) : OnRay P D F
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.self:
/-- B itself is on the ray from A through B. -/
theorem OnRay.self (h : A ≠ B) : OnRay B A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.symm:
/-- P is on the ray from A through B exactly when B is on the ray from A
through P: they are one and the same ray. -/
theorem OnRay.symm (h : OnRay P A B) : OnRay B A P
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSides.exists_between:
/-- A finite straight line joining two points on opposite sides of a straight line
L crosses L, at a point between them (System E, Intersection 1 and Pasch 4). -/
theorem OppositeSides.exists_between (h : OppositeSides P Q L) :
    ∃ X : Point, OnLine X L ∧ Between P X Q
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.not_onLine:
/-- Parallels do not meet: a point of L is not on M. -/
theorem Parallel.not_onLine (h : Parallel L M) (hP : OnLine P L) : ¬ OnLine P M
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.sameSide:
/-- All the points of one parallel lie on one side of the other: two points of L
are on the same side of M. Were they on opposite sides, the straight line L
joining them would cross M (System E, Intersection 1). -/
theorem Parallel.sameSide (h : Parallel L M) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L) :
    SameSide P Q M
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.symm:
/-- If L is parallel to M, then M is parallel to L. -/
theorem Parallel.symm (h : Parallel L M) : Parallel M L
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.cross:
/-- The diameters of a parallelogram cross: in the parallelogram ABCD, some point
lies between A and C and between B and D. Its sides AB and DC are
parallel, so they do not cross, and `AreParallel.cross_or` leaves only the
diameters. -/
theorem Parallelogram.cross (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    ∃ X : Point, Between A X C ∧ Between B X D
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate:
/-- A parallelogram has the same area whichever diameter cuts it: the parallelogram
ABCD measured by BD, as BCDA, is the same as measured by AC. -/
theorem Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea B C D A = quadArea A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.sameSideOf:
/-- In the parallelogram ABCD, the far corners C and D lie on one side of the
side AB. (Named from another corner with `.rotate`, the same holds of every
side.) -/
theorem Parallelogram.sameSideOf (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : SameSideOf C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.triangle:
/-- In the parallelogram ABCD, the corner C is off the straight line AB, so
ABC is a triangle. -/
theorem Parallelogram.triangle (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Triangle A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate1:
/-- **Postulate 1.** To draw a straight line from any point to any point. -/
axiom Postulate1 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf:
/-- `P` and `Q` lie on the same side of the straight line `AB`. -/
def SameSideOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.of_cross:
/-- Diameters that cross make the figure convex: if the diameters AC and BD of
ABCD cross, then C and D lie on one side of AB. For the crossing point lies on
C's side of AB and on D's (System E, Pasch 2). -/
theorem SameSideOf.of_cross (hAXC : Between A X C) (hBXD : Between B X D)
    (hABC : Triangle A B C) : SameSideOf C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.sameSide:
/-- Two points on the same side of the straight line AB are on the same side of
any straight line drawn through A and B. -/
theorem SameSideOf.sameSide (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    SameSide P Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the same side of AB as Q, then Q is on the same side as P. -/
theorem SameSideOf.symm (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.trans:
/-- Points on the same side as a third are on the same side as each other. -/
theorem SameSideOf.trans (h₁ : SameSideOf P Q A B) (h₂ : SameSideOf Q R A B) :
    SameSideOf P R A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.triangle:
/-- A point on one side of the straight line AB is not on it, so ABP is a
triangle. -/
theorem SameSideOf.triangle (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : Triangle A B P
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.add_assoc:
/-- Adding three magnitudes in a row, it makes no difference whether the first two or the last
two are added first. (System E §3.5) -/
axiom add_assoc (a b c : Magnitude k) : a + b + c = a + (b + c)
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.add_comm:
/-- The order of adding does not matter. (System E §3.5) -/
axiom add_comm (a b : Magnitude k) : a + b = b + a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_cases:
/-- Of three different points on a straight line, one is between the other two.
(Between 6) -/
axiom between_cases (hAB : A ≠ B) (hBC : B ≠ C) (hAC : A ≠ C) (hA : OnLine A L)
    (hB : OnLine B L) (hC : OnLine C L) : Between A B C ∨ Between B A C ∨ Between A C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_of_between_right:
/-- If B is between A and C, and C is between B and D, then B is between
A and D. (Between 5) -/
axiom between_of_between_right (h₁ : Between A B C) (h₂ : Between B C D) : Between A B D
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_symm:
/-- If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1) -/
axiom between_symm (h : Between A B C) : Between C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.len_add_of_between:
/-- If B is between A and C, then AB and BC together make up AC.
(Diagram-segment 1) -/
axiom len_add_of_between (h : Between A B C) : ‖A B‖ + ‖B C‖ = ‖A C‖
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.len_symm:
/-- The straight line AB is the straight line BA. (Metric 3) -/
axiom len_symm (A B : Point) : ‖A B‖ = ‖B A‖
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.line_unique:
/-- Two points determine a straight line. (Generalities 1) -/
axiom line_unique (hAB : A ≠ B) (hAL : OnLine A L) (hBL : OnLine B L) (hAM : OnLine A M)
    (hBM : OnLine B M) : L = M
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between:
/-- A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between_ends:
/-- The ends of a finite straight line differ. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.not_on_line_of_same_side:
/-- Points on one side of a straight line are not on it. (Same side 3) -/
axiom not_on_line_of_same_side (h : SameSide A B L) : ¬ OnLine A L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between:
/-- A straight line through A and B, with B between A and C, passes
through C. (Between 2) -/
axiom on_line_of_between (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    OnLine C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between_ends:
/-- A straight line through A and C passes through every point between them.
(Between 3) -/
axiom on_line_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hC : OnLine C L) :
    OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.pasch2:
/-- If B is between A and C, A is on L and B is off it, then B and C are
on the same side of L: a straight line that leaves L at A does not cross it
again. (Pasch 2) -/
axiom pasch2 (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : ¬ OnLine B L) : SameSide B C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.pasch3:
/-- A straight line through a point between A and C separates them. (Pasch 3) -/
axiom pasch3 (h : Between A B C) (hB : OnLine B L) : ¬ SameSide A C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.same_side_symm:
/-- If A is on the same side of a straight line as B, then B is on the same side
as A. (Same side 2) -/
axiom same_side_symm (h : SameSide A B L) : SameSide B A L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.same_side_trans:
/-- Two points on the same side of a straight line as a third point are on the same
side as each other. (Same side 4) -/
axiom same_side_trans (h₁ : SameSide A B L) (h₂ : SameSide A C L) : SameSide B C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.cab:
/-- The triangle ABC, named from C, as CAB. -/
theorem Triangle.cab (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle C A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₁₂:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₁₂ (h : Triangle A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₁₃:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₁₃ (h : Triangle A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.of_line:
/-- Two different points of a straight line, and a third point off it, make a
triangle. -/
theorem Triangle.of_line {P Q R : Point} (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L) (hPQ : P ≠ Q)
    (hR : ¬ OnLine R L) : Triangle P Q R
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_onRay_left:
/-- One arm traced through another point of its ray: if B' is on the ray from A
through B, the angle B'AC is the angle BAC. (System E, Diagram-angle 4) -/
theorem angle_onRay_left {B' : Point} (hB : OnRay B' A B) (hCA : C ≠ A) :
    ∠ B' A C = ∠ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.area_acb:
/-- The triangle ABC is the triangle ACB. (System E, Metric 8) -/
theorem area_acb (A B C : Point) : △ A B C = △ A C B
helper_signatures.Elements.area_bac:
/-- The triangle ABC is the triangle BAC. (System E, Metric 8) -/
theorem area_bac (A B C : Point) : △ A B C = △ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.area_bca:
/-- The triangle ABC is the triangle BCA. (System E, Metric 8) -/
theorem area_bca (A B C : Point) : △ A B C = △ B C A
helper_signatures.Elements.area_cab:
/-- The triangle ABC is the triangle CAB. (System E, Metric 8) -/
theorem area_cab (A B C : Point) : △ A B C = △ C A B
helper_signatures.Elements.area_cba:
/-- The triangle ABC is the triangle CBA. (System E, Metric 8) -/
theorem area_cba (A B C : Point) : △ A B C = △ C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.area_cut:
/-- A straight line from a corner cuts a triangle into two which make up the
whole: if D lies between B and C, the triangles ABD and ADC together are
the triangle ABC. (System E, Diagram-area 2) When A is on the straight line
BC, all three are nothing, and it still holds. -/
theorem area_cut (h : Between B D C) : △ A B D + △ A D C = △ A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.len_lt_of_between:
/-- The part is less than the whole: if B lies between A and C, then AB is
less than AC, for AC is AB and BC together. (System E, Diagram-segment 1,
and C.N. 5) -/
theorem len_lt_of_between (h : Between A B C) : ‖A B‖ < ‖A C‖
helper_signatures.Elements.ne_of_len_eq:
/-- If a finite straight line AB has the length of one with different ends,
its own ends are different. -/
theorem ne_of_len_eq (h : ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖) (hCD : C ≠ D) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea_rotate_of_cross:
/-- A four-sided figure whose diameters cross has the same area whichever diameter
cuts it: if X lies between A and C and also between B and D, the figure
ABCD measured by AC is the figure BCDA measured by BD. Each diameter cuts
the figure into two triangles, and the other diameter cuts each of those into two
more; the four small triangles about X are the same either way (System E,
Diagram-area 2). -/
theorem quadArea_rotate_of_cross (hAXC : Between A X C) (hBXD : Between B X D) :
    quadArea B C D A = quadArea A B C D

I.4.enunciation: If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the base, the triangle will be equal to the triangle, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend.

I.29.enunciation: A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on the same side equal to two right angles.

I.34.enunciation: In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the diameter bisects the areas.

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ P ≠ A ∧ Collinear A B P ∧ ¬ Between P A B
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle

question.instructions:
Does every proposition called by the proof unit in `lean_proof` do work towards its conclusion or a substantive intermediate step of Euclid's argument? Also check for artificial hypothesis uses. Judge this unit's uses of the supplied helper signatures; helper bodies are outside this question. Heath's sentences stand as `--` lines and `cited` gives exact enunciations. In Lean, `have h : T := p` proves T by p and calls the result h; `obtain ⟨…⟩ := p` takes p apart into named pieces; `rw [h34, h37, …]` rewrites the goal by the equalities named. Follow uses through helper calls and tactics as well as explicit names. An anonymous binding or an unused hypothesis alone does not establish a defect. If both defects occur, choose `a dummy citation`.

criteria.all do work: Every proposition call supports a later step or the conclusion, or establishes a substantive intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid. criteria.a dummy citation: Some proposition call does no substantive work: its result neither supports the argument nor establishes a substantive intermediate fact, and merely supplies a citation while the step is done another way.
criteria.an artificial hypothesis use: No dummy citation is established, but a hypothesis is mentioned only so that it looks used, and does no substantive work.

bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34:
/-- In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the
diameter bisects the areas. -/
theorem Prop34 {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A C D B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ C D B ∧ ∠ A B D = ∠ A C D ∧
      △ A B C = △ D C B
bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34.bisect:
/-- The diameter bisects the parallelogram, said of its area: the parallelogram
ABCD, measured by its diameter AC, is double the triangle ABC. I.35–I.47 cite
I.34 for this ("the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram EBCA; for the diameter
AB bisects it"). To halve by the other diameter, name the parallelogram from the
next corner (`Parallelogram.rotate`) and turn its area round with
`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`. [I. 34] -/
theorem Prop34.bisect {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea A B C D = △ A B C + △ A B C
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.cross:
/-- The diameters of a parallelogram cross: in the parallelogram ABCD, some point
lies between A and C and between B and D. Its sides AB and DC are
parallel, so they do not cross, and `AreParallel.cross_or` leaves only the
diameters. -/
theorem Parallelogram.cross (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    ∃ X : Point, Between A X C ∧ Between B X D
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate:
/-- A parallelogram has the same area whichever diameter cuts it: the parallelogram
ABCD measured by BD, as BCDA, is the same as measured by AC. -/
theorem Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea B C D A = quadArea A B C D

state.commentary:
**"Equality in a new sense."** So Heath heads his note. Until now equal figures were congruent, but here figures "are inferred to be *equal* which are equal in *area* or in *content* but need not be of the same *form*" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 327). I.34, I.29 and I.4 make the triangles EAB, FDC equal; Euclid takes DGE from each and adds GBC to what remains. Beneath Common Notions 2 and 3 Heath finds "the further *tacit* assumption that it is indifferent to *what part* or from *what part* of the same or equal areas the same or equal areas are added or subtracted" (vol. 1, p. 328).

**"He allows this to appear from the figure simply."** Euclid names the triangle DGE without saying that, "in the case which he takes (where AD, EF have no point in common), BE, CD must meet at a point G between the two parallels" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 327). The rest of the proof depends on G. Taking DGE from EAB leaves the trapezium ABGD in his figure. Our areas are magnitudes, and a figure's area is the sum of the triangles it is cut into. To write EAB as ABGD and DGE together, we need D between A and E and G between E and B. We prove the crossing in `Prop35.figure`: D lies between A and E, so E is across DC from A and therefore from B. With ED parallel to BC, the diameters BE and CD of DBCE cross at G. The same step puts E between D and F, as "the whole DF" requires. Each subtraction and addition of areas then uses triangles cut in two by a straight line from a corner.

Proclus, "observing that Euclid has given only the most difficult of the three possible cases, adds the other two with separate proofs" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 328). When E falls between A and D, he adds the equal triangles to the trapezium EBCD, and so do we, and likewise when E falls at D; exchanging the parallelograms covers each case the other way round. Proclus also counts I.35 among the paradoxes of mathematics, "since the uninstructed might well regard it as impossible that the area of the parallelograms should remain the same while the length of the sides … may increase indefinitely" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 329). Following Geminus, he puts the cause in "the height of the parallels, which remains the same" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 331).

**The modern way.** For vectors $\vec{u}$ and $\vec{v}$ in the plane write $\vec{u} \times \vec{v} = u_{1}v_{2} - u_{2}v_{1}$, their cross product, the determinant of their coordinates. The parallelogram on $\vec{u}$ and $\vec{v}$ has area $\lvert\vec{u} \times \vec{v}\rvert$, and $\vec{u} \times \vec{u} = 0$. With E on AF, parallel to BC, $\mathrm{E - B} = \mathrm{(A - B)} + t\mathrm{(C - B)}$ for some real $t$, so $\lvert\mathrm{(C - B)} \times \mathrm{(E - B)}\rvert = \lvert\mathrm{(C - B)} \times \mathrm{(A - B)}\rvert$: one base, one height, one area.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABCD, EBCF be parallelograms on the same base BC and in the same parallels AF, BC;

I say that ABCD is equal to the parallelogram EBCF.

For, since ABCD is a parallelogram,

AD is equal to BC. [I. 34]

For the same reason also

EF is equal to BC,

so that AD is also equal to EF; [C.N. 1]

and DE is common;

therefore the whole AE is equal to the whole DF. [C.N. 2]

But AB is also equal to DC; [I. 34]

therefore the two sides EA, AB are equal to the two sides FD, DC respectively,

and the angle FDC is equal to the angle EAB, the exterior to the interior; [I. 29]

therefore the base EB is equal to the base FC,

and the triangle EAB will be equal to the triangle FDC. [I. 4]

Let DGE be subtracted from each;

therefore the trapezium ABGD which remains is equal to the trapezium EGCF which remains. [C.N. 3]

Let the triangle GBC be added to each;

therefore the whole parallelogram ABCD is equal to the whole parallelogram EBCF. [C.N. 2]

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- Parallelograms which are on the same base and in the same parallels are equal to one another. -/
theorem Prop35 {A B C D E F : Point} (h₁ : Parallelogram A B C D) (h₂ : Parallelogram E B C F)
    (hAF : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine D L ∧ OnLine E L ∧ OnLine F L) :
    quadArea A B C D = quadArea E B C F := by
  -- Let ABCD, EBCF be parallelograms on the same base BC and in the same parallels AF, BC;
  obtain ⟨AF, hA, hD, hE, hF⟩ := hAF
  obtain ⟨BC, hB, hC⟩ := Postulate1 B C h₁.2.1
  -- I say that ABCD is equal to the parallelogram EBCF.
  /- Euclid takes the case where AD and EF have no point in common, with D between
     A and E. We give his argument in his letters, then cover the other orders. -/
  have euclid : ∀ {A D E F : Point}, Parallelogram A B C D → Parallelogram E B C F →
      OnLine A AF → OnLine D AF → OnLine F AF → Between A D E →
      quadArea A B C D = quadArea E B C F := by
    intro A D E F h₁ h₂ hA hD hF hADE
    have hE : OnLine E AF := on_line_of_between hADE hA hD
    -- For, since ABCD is a parallelogram,
    have hAF_BC : Parallel AF BC := (h₁.2.parallel hB hC hD hA).symm
    -- AD is equal to BC. [I. 34]
    have hAD : ‖A D‖ = ‖B C‖ := (Prop34 (A := A) (B := D) (C := B) (D := C) h₁).1
    -- For the same reason also
    -- EF is equal to BC,
    have hEF : ‖E F‖ = ‖B C‖ := (Prop34 (A := E) (B := F) (C := B) (D := C) h₂).1
    -- so that AD is also equal to EF; [C.N. 1]
    have hAD_EF : ‖A D‖ = ‖E F‖ := CommonNotion1 hAD hEF
    -- and DE is common;
    /- G lies between E and B and between D and C; E lies between D and F.
       These are the orders Euclid reads from his figure. -/
    obtain ⟨G, hEGB, hDGC, hDEF⟩ := Prop35.figure h₁ h₂ hA hD hF hADE
    -- therefore the whole AE is equal to the whole DF. [C.N. 2]
    have hAE_DF : ‖A E‖ = ‖D F‖ := by
      have := CommonNotion2 hAD_EF (rfl : ‖D E‖ = ‖D E‖)
      rw [len_add_of_between hADE, add_comm, len_add_of_between hDEF] at this
      exact this
    -- But AB is also equal to DC; [I. 34]
    have hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖D C‖ := (Prop34 (A := A) (B := D) (C := B) (D := C) h₁).2.1
    -- therefore the two sides EA, AB are equal to the two sides FD, DC respectively,
    have hB_AF : ¬ OnLine B AF := hAF_BC.symm.not_onLine hB
    have hC_AF : ¬ OnLine C AF := hAF_BC.symm.not_onLine hC
    have hAEB : Triangle A E B := Triangle.of_line hA hE (ne_of_between_ends hADE) hB_AF
    have hDFC : Triangle D F C := Triangle.of_line hD hF (ne_of_between_ends hDEF) hC_AF
    -- and the angle FDC is equal to the angle EAB, the exterior to the interior; [I. 29]
    have hADF : Between A D F := between_of_between_right hADE hDEF
    have hFDC : ∠ F D C = ∠ E A B := by
      rw [Prop29.exterior h₁.1.symm.swap_left h₁.2.sameSideOf.symm (between_symm hADF),
        angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_beyond hADE) h₁.triangle.ne₁₂.symm]
    -- therefore the base EB is equal to the base FC,
    have h4 := Prop4 hAEB hDFC hAE_DF hAB hFDC.symm
    have hEB_FC : ‖E B‖ = ‖F C‖ := h4.1
    -- and the triangle EAB will be equal to the triangle FDC. [I. 4]
    have htri : △ A E B = △ D F C := h4.2.1
    -- Let DGE be subtracted from each;
    /- ABGD is named from B, so that its diameter is BD. Each taking away is
       written as a cutting: the larger triangle is the trapezium and DGE together. -/
    have e₁ : △ A E B = quadArea B G D A + △ D G E := by
      unfold quadArea
      rw [area_cab A E B, ← area_cut (A := B) hADE, area_bca B D E, ← area_cut (A := D) hEGB,
        area_cba B G D, area_acb B D A, area_acb D G E]
      ac_rfl
    have e₂ : △ D F C = quadArea E G C F + △ D G E := by
      unfold quadArea
      rw [area_cab D F C, ← area_cut (A := C) hDEF, area_cba C D E, ← area_cut (A := E) hDGC,
        area_bac E C F, area_cab D G E]
      ac_rfl
    -- therefore the trapezium ABGD which remains is equal to the trapezium EGCF which
    -- remains. [C.N. 3]
    have trap : quadArea B G D A = quadArea E G C F :=
      CommonNotion3 (e₁.symm.trans (htri.trans e₂)) rfl
    -- Let the triangle GBC be added to each;
    have hsum := CommonNotion2 trap (rfl : △ G B C = △ G B C)
    -- therefore the whole parallelogram ABCD is equal to the whole parallelogram EBCF. [C.N. 2]
    have hL : quadArea A B C D = quadArea B G D A + △ G B C := by
      rw [← h₁.quadArea_rotate]
      unfold quadArea
      rw [area_acb B C D, ← area_cut (A := B) hDGC, area_acb B G D, area_bac G B C]
      ac_rfl
    have hR : quadArea E B C F = quadArea E G C F + △ G B C := by
      unfold quadArea
      rw [area_cab E B C, ← area_cut (A := C) hEGB, area_cab E G C, area_cab G B C]
      ac_rfl
    rw [hL, hR, hsum]
  /- E may also fall between A and D, or at either end. The helpers add equal
     triangles to the common part, as Proclus does in the cases Heath reports.
     When E is A, equal lengths on the same ray make F equal to D. -/
  have oneway : ∀ {A D E F : Point}, Parallelogram A B C D → Parallelogram E B C F →
      OnLine A AF → OnLine D AF → OnLine E AF → OnLine F AF → (E = A ∨ SameSideOf C E A B) →
      quadArea A B C D = quadArea E B C F := by
    intro A D E F h₁ h₂ hA hD hE hF hdir
    obtain ⟨hAD, -, -, -, -⟩ := Prop34 (A := A) (B := D) (C := B) (D := C) h₁
    obtain ⟨hEF, -, -, -, -⟩ := Prop34 (A := E) (B := F) (C := B) (D := C) h₂
    rcases hdir with rfl | hCE
    · /- E is A, and so F is D. -/
      have hFray : OnRay F E D :=
        OnRay.of_sameSideOf (h₂.sameSideOf.symm.trans h₁.sameSideOf) ⟨AF, hE, hD, hF⟩

      rw [hFray.eq_of_len_eq (hEF.trans hAD.symm)]
    · have hEA : E ≠ A := hCE.symm.triangle.ne₁₃.symm
      have hEray : OnRay E A D :=
        OnRay.of_sameSideOf (hCE.symm.trans h₁.sameSideOf) ⟨AF, hA, hD, hE⟩ hEA

        · exact Prop35.between h₁ h₂ hA hD hE hF h

  have harea : quadArea A B C D = quadArea E B C F := by
    by_cases hEA : E = A
    · exact oneway h₁ h₂ hA hD hE hF (Or.inl hEA)
    · have hAF_BC : Parallel AF BC := (h₁.2.parallel hB hC hD hA).symm
      rcases (AreParallel.of_parallel (Ne.symm hEA) h₁.2.1 hA hE hB hC hAF_BC).sameSideOf_or with h | h
      · exact oneway h₁ h₂ hA hD hE hF (Or.inr h)
      · exact (oneway h₂ h₁ hE hF hA hD (Or.inr h)).symm

  exact harea
  -- Q. E. D.

Let ABCD, EBCF be parallelograms on the same base BC and in the same parallels AF, BC;

I say that ABCD is equal to the parallelogram EBCF.

For, since ABCD is a parallelogram,

AD is equal to BC. [I. 34]

For the same reason also

EF is equal to BC,

so that AD is also equal to EF; [C.N. 1]

and DE is common;

therefore the whole AE is equal to the whole DF. [C.N. 2]

But AB is also equal to DC; [I. 34]

therefore the two sides EA, AB are equal to the two sides FD, DC respectively,

and the angle FDC is equal to the angle EAB, the exterior to the interior; [I. 29]

therefore the base EB is equal to the base FC,

and the triangle EAB will be equal to the triangle FDC. [I. 4]

Let DGE be subtracted from each;

therefore the trapezium ABGD which remains is equal to the trapezium EGCF which remains. [C.N. 3]

Let the triangle GBC be added to each;

therefore the whole parallelogram ABCD is equal to the whole parallelogram EBCF. [C.N. 2]

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.

diameter bisects the areas. -/

ABCD, measured by its diameter AC, is double the triangle ABC. I.35–I.47 cite
I.34 for this ("the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram EBCA; for the diameter

`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`. [I. 34] -/

    quadArea A B C D = △ A B C + △ A B C

lies between A and C and between B and D. Its sides AB and DC are
parallel, so they do not cross, and `AreParallel.cross_or` leaves only the
diameters. -/

    ∃ X : Point, Between A X C ∧ Between B X D

ABCD measured by BD, as BCDA, is the same as measured by AC. -/
theorem Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea B C D A = quadArea A B C D

state.heath_proof:
Let ABCD, EFGH be parallelograms which are on equal bases BC, FG and in the same parallels AH, BG;

I say that the parallelogram ABCD is equal to EFGH.

For let BE, CH be joined.

Then, since BC is equal to FG,

while FG is equal to EH,

BC is also equal to EH. [C.N. 1]

But they are also parallel.

And EB, HC join them;

but straight lines joining equal and parallel straight lines (at the extremities which are) in the same directions (respectively) are equal and parallel. [I. 33]

Therefore EBCH is a parallelogram. [I. 34]

And it is equal to ABCD;

for it has the same base BC with it, and is in the same parallels BC, AH with it. [I. 35]

For the same reason also EFGH is equal to the same EBCH; [I. 35]

so that the parallelogram ABCD is also equal to EFGH. [C.N. 1]

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- Parallelograms which are on equal bases and in the same parallels are equal to one another. -/
theorem Prop36 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (h₁ : Parallelogram A B C D) (h₂ : Parallelogram E F G H)
    (hbase : ‖B C‖ = ‖F G‖)
    (hAH : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine D L ∧ OnLine E L ∧ OnLine H L)
    (hBG : ∃ L : Line, OnLine B L ∧ OnLine C L ∧ OnLine F L ∧ OnLine G L) :
    quadArea A B C D = quadArea E F G H := by
  -- Let ABCD, EFGH be parallelograms which are on equal bases BC, FG and in the same parallels
  -- AH, BG;
  obtain ⟨AH, hA, hD, hE, hH⟩ := hAH
  obtain ⟨BG, hB, hC, hF, hG⟩ := hBG
  have hpar : Parallel AH BG := (h₁.2.parallel hB hC hD hA).symm
  -- I say that the parallelogram ABCD is equal to EFGH.
  /- Euclid's case: EH runs the same way as BC, so C and H lie on one side of BE.
     We give his argument first, then turn the lettering round for the other case. -/
  have key : ∀ {E F G H : Point}, Parallelogram E F G H → ‖B C‖ = ‖F G‖ →
      OnLine E AH → OnLine H AH → OnLine F BG → OnLine G BG → SameSideOf C H B E →
      quadArea A B C D = quadArea E F G H := by
    intro E F G H h₂ hbase hE hH hF hG
    -- For let BE, CH be joined.
    -- Then, since BC is equal to FG,
    have hBC_FG : ‖B C‖ = ‖F G‖ := hbase
    -- while FG is equal to EH,
    have hEH : ‖E H‖ = ‖F G‖ := (Prop34 (A := E) (B := H) (C := F) (D := G) h₂).1
    -- BC is also equal to EH. [C.N. 1]
    have hBC_EH : ‖B C‖ = ‖E H‖ := CommonNotion1 hBC_FG hEH
    -- But they are also parallel.
    have hBCEH : AreParallel B C E H :=
      AreParallel.of_parallel h₁.2.1 h₂.2.2.1.symm hB hC hE hH hpar.symm
    -- And EB, HC join them;
    intro hdir
    -- but straight lines joining equal and parallel straight lines (at the extremities which
    -- are) in the same directions (respectively) are equal and parallel. [I. 33]
    have h33 := Prop33 hBCEH hBC_EH hdir
    -- Therefore EBCH is a parallelogram. [I. 34]
    /- Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, which is the definition of a
       parallelogram. -/
    have hEBCH : Parallelogram E B C H :=
      ⟨h33.2.swap_left,
        AreParallel.of_parallel h₁.2.1 h₂.2.2.1 hB hC hH hE hpar.symm⟩
    -- And it is equal to ABCD;
    have e₁ : quadArea A B C D = quadArea E B C H := by
      -- for it has the same base BC with it, and is in the same parallels BC, AH with it. [I. 35]
      exact Prop35 h₁ hEBCH ⟨AH, hA, hD, hE, hH⟩
    -- For the same reason also EFGH is equal to the same EBCH; [I. 35]
    have harea : quadArea F E H G = quadArea B E H C :=
      Prop35 h₂.reverse.rotate.rotate.rotate hEBCH.reverse.rotate.rotate.rotate
        ⟨BG, hF, hG, hB, hC⟩
    /- This time the common base is EH. Both areas are turned back to their given
       names: a parallelogram has one area, whichever diameter measures it. -/
    have e₂ : quadArea E F G H = quadArea E B C H := calc
      quadArea E F G H = quadArea F G H E := h₂.quadArea_rotate.symm
      _ = quadArea F E H G := (quadArea_reverse F G H E).symm
      _ = quadArea B E H C := harea
      _ = quadArea B C H E := quadArea_reverse B C H E
      _ = quadArea E B C H := hEBCH.quadArea_rotate
    -- so that the parallelogram ABCD is also equal to EFGH. [C.N. 1]
    exact CommonNotion1 e₁ e₂
  /- EH runs the same way as BC, or the other way. In the second case EFGH is
     read as HGFE, and the same argument applies without changing its area. -/
  have hEHBC : AreParallel E H B C :=
    AreParallel.of_parallel h₂.2.2.1.symm h₁.2.1 hE hH hB hC hpar
  have hequal : quadArea A B C D = quadArea E F G H := by
    rcases hEHBC.sameSideOf_or with hs | hs
    · exact key h₂ hbase hE hH hF hG hs.swap
    · rw [key h₂.reverse.rotate (hbase.trans (len_symm F G)) hH hE hG hF hs.swap,
        quadArea_reverse, quadArea_rotate₂, h₂.quadArea_rotate]
  -- Therefore etc.
  exact hequal
  -- Q. E. D.

/-- Two different points of L, and two different points of M, are the ends of
parallel straight lines when L and M are parallel: two points fix one straight

parallel to CD" of any other two points P, Q of the straight line AB and R,

theorem AreParallel.of_parallel (hPQ : P ≠ Q) (hRS : R ≠ S) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L)

    (hC : OnLine C M) (hD : OnLine D M) : Parallel L M

/-- Which way two parallels run. If AD is parallel to BC, then either D lies on

`SameSideOf.of_cross`. -/
theorem AreParallel.sameSideOf_or (h : AreParallel A D B C) :
    SameSideOf C D A B ∨ SameSideOf C A D B

theorem AreParallel.swap_left (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel B A C D

theorem AreParallel.symm (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel C D A B

Does every proposition called by the proof unit in `lean_proof` do work towards its conclusion or a substantive intermediate step of Euclid's argument? Also check for artificial hypothesis uses. Judge this unit's uses of the supplied helper signatures; helper bodies are outside this question. Heath's sentences stand as `--` lines and `cited` gives exact enunciations. In Lean, `have h : T := p` proves T by p and calls the result h; `obtain ⟨…⟩ := p` takes p apart into named pieces; `rw [h34, h37, …]` rewrites the goal by the equalities named. criteria.a dummy citation: Some proposition call does no substantive work: its result neither supports the argument nor establishes a substantive intermediate fact, and merely supplies a citation while the step is done another way.

criteria.all do work: Every proposition call supports a later step or the conclusion, or establishes a substantive intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid. state.commentary:
Euclid joins BE and CH, and the figure EBCH they close is a parallelogram with a base in common with each of the given ones: BC with ABCD, and EH with EFGH. I.35 makes it equal to each, and Common Notion 1 makes the two equal to one another. Equal bases do as well as one base, once a third parallelogram bridges them.

**Where does I.34 come in?** Heath's reference for "Therefore EBCH is a parallelogram" is I.34, but that step asks for no proposition: both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, and that is what a parallelogram is. The step that does use I.34 stands a few lines up, with no reference: "while FG is equal to EH", the opposite sides of EFGH. That equality is what lets I.33 make EB and HC equal and parallel, once C and H lie on one side of BE; when they do not, we read EFGH as HGFE.

Each use of I.35 may fall in any of its cases: on the base BC, the sides AD and EH may overlap or meet at an end, and on the base EH, so may BC and FG. So I.36 rests on the cases that Proclus adds under I.35 as well as on Euclid's, and our I.35 proves them all. Heath gives I.36 no note of its own, but among Heron's comments he finds "Distinctions of a number of particular *cases* of Euclid's propositions according as the figure is drawn in one way or in another. Of this class are the different cases of I. 35, 36" (vol. 1, p. 22).

Proclus' note on I.36 has lost its end, and his note on I.37 its beginning; the manuscripts run straight on "without regard to sense" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 332). In the lost lines, Heath gathers, Proclus remarked again that the sides stretching from one parallel to the other may grow to any length while the area stays the same. Proclus tells "of describers of countries … who drew conclusions regarding the size of cities from their perimeters" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 332).
state.heath_proof:
Let ABCD, EFGH be parallelograms which are on equal bases BC, FG and in the same parallels AH, BG;

I say that the parallelogram ABCD is equal to EFGH.

For let BE, CH be joined.

Then, since BC is equal to FG,

while FG is equal to EH,

BC is also equal to EH. [C.N. 1]

But they are also parallel.

And EB, HC join them;

but straight lines joining equal and parallel straight lines (at the extremities which are) in the same directions (respectively) are equal and parallel. [I. 33]

Therefore EBCH is a parallelogram. [I. 34]

And it is equal to ABCD;

for it has the same base BC with it, and is in the same parallels BC, AH with it. [I. 35]

For the same reason also EFGH is equal to the same EBCH; [I. 35]

so that the parallelogram ABCD is also equal to EFGH. [C.N. 1]

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- Parallelograms which are on equal bases and in the same parallels are equal to one another. -/
theorem Prop36 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (h₁ : Parallelogram A B C D) (h₂ : Parallelogram E F G H)
    (hbase : ‖B C‖ = ‖F G‖)
    (hAH : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine D L ∧ OnLine E L ∧ OnLine H L)
    (hBG : ∃ L : Line, OnLine B L ∧ OnLine C L ∧ OnLine F L ∧ OnLine G L) :
    quadArea A B C D = quadArea E F G H := by
  -- Let ABCD, EFGH be parallelograms which are on equal bases BC, FG and in the same parallels
  -- AH, BG;
  obtain ⟨AH, hA, hD, hE, hH⟩ := hAH
  obtain ⟨BG, hB, hC, hF, hG⟩ := hBG
  have hpar : Parallel AH BG := (h₁.2.parallel hB hC hD hA).symm
  -- I say that the parallelogram ABCD is equal to EFGH.
  /- Euclid's case: EH runs the same way as BC, so C and H lie on one side of BE.
     We give his argument first, then turn the lettering round for the other case. -/
  have key : ∀ {E F G H : Point}, Parallelogram E F G H → ‖B C‖ = ‖F G‖ →
      OnLine E AH → OnLine H AH → OnLine F BG → OnLine G BG → SameSideOf C H B E →
      quadArea A B C D = quadArea E F G H := by
    intro E F G H h₂ hbase hE hH hF hG
    -- For let BE, CH be joined.
    -- Then, since BC is equal to FG,
    have hBC_FG : ‖B C‖ = ‖F G‖ := hbase
    -- while FG is equal to EH,
    have hEH : ‖E H‖ = ‖F G‖ := (Prop34 (A := E) (B := H) (C := F) (D := G) h₂).1
    -- BC is also equal to EH. [C.N. 1]
    have hBC_EH : ‖B C‖ = ‖E H‖ := CommonNotion1 hBC_FG hEH
    -- But they are also parallel.
    have hBCEH : AreParallel B C E H :=
      AreParallel.of_parallel h₁.2.1 h₂.2.2.1.symm hB hC hE hH hpar.symm
    -- And EB, HC join them;
    intro hdir
    -- but straight lines joining equal and parallel straight lines (at the extremities which
    -- are) in the same directions (respectively) are equal and parallel. [I. 33]
    have h33 := Prop33 hBCEH hBC_EH hdir
    -- Therefore EBCH is a parallelogram. [I. 34]
    /- Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, which is the definition of a
       parallelogram. -/
    have hEBCH : Parallelogram E B C H :=
      ⟨h33.2.swap_left,
        AreParallel.of_parallel h₁.2.1 h₂.2.2.1 hB hC hH hE hpar.symm⟩
    -- And it is equal to ABCD;
    have e₁ : quadArea A B C D = quadArea E B C H := by
      -- for it has the same base BC with it, and is in the same parallels BC, AH with it. [I. 35]
      exact Prop35 h₁ hEBCH ⟨AH, hA, hD, hE, hH⟩
    -- For the same reason also EFGH is equal to the same EBCH; [I. 35]
    have harea : quadArea F E H G = quadArea B E H C :=
      Prop35 h₂.reverse.rotate.rotate.rotate hEBCH.reverse.rotate.rotate.rotate
        ⟨BG, hF, hG, hB, hC⟩
    /- This time the common base is EH. Both areas are turned back to their given
       names: a parallelogram has one area, whichever diameter measures it. -/
    have e₂ : quadArea E F G H = quadArea E B C H := calc
      quadArea E F G H = quadArea F G H E := h₂.quadArea_rotate.symm
      _ = quadArea F E H G := (quadArea_reverse F G H E).symm
      _ = quadArea B E H C := harea
      _ = quadArea B C H E := quadArea_reverse B C H E
      _ = quadArea E B C H := hEBCH.quadArea_rotate
    -- so that the parallelogram ABCD is also equal to EFGH. [C.N. 1]
    exact CommonNotion1 e₁ e₂
  /- EH runs the same way as BC, or the other way. In the second case EFGH is
     read as HGFE, and the same argument applies without changing its area. -/
  have hEHBC : AreParallel E H B C :=
    AreParallel.of_parallel h₂.2.2.1.symm h₁.2.1 hE hH hB hC hpar
  have hequal : quadArea A B C D = quadArea E F G H := by
    rcases hEHBC.sameSideOf_or with hs | hs

state.enunciation: Parallelograms which are on equal bases and in the same parallels are equal to one another.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABCD, EFGH be parallelograms which are on equal bases BC, FG and in the same parallels AH, BG;

I say that the parallelogram ABCD is equal to EFGH.

For let BE, CH be joined.

Then, since BC is equal to FG,

while FG is equal to EH,

BC is also equal to EH. [C.N. 1]

But they are also parallel.

And EB, HC join them;

but straight lines joining equal and parallel straight lines (at the extremities which are) in the same directions (respectively) are equal and parallel. [I. 33]

Therefore EBCH is a parallelogram. [I. 34]

And it is equal to ABCD;

for it has the same base BC with it, and is in the same parallels BC, AH with it. [I. 35]

For the same reason also EFGH is equal to the same EBCH; [I. 35]

so that the parallelogram ABCD is also equal to EFGH. [C.N. 1]

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.

state.heath_proof:
Let ABC, DBC be triangles on the same base BC and in the same parallels AD, BC;

I say that the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DBC.

Let AD be produced in both directions to E, F; through B let BE be drawn parallel to CA, [I. 31] and through C let CF be drawn parallel to BD. [I. 31]

Then each of the figures EBCA, DBCF is a parallelogram; and they are equal, for they are on the same base BC and in the same parallels BC, EF. [I. 35]

Moreover the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram EBCA; for the diameter AB bisects it. [I. 34]

And the triangle DBC is half of the parallelogram DBCF; for the diameter DC bisects it. [I. 34]

[But the halves of equal things are equal to one another.]

Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DBC.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- Triangles which are on the same base and in the same parallels are equal to one another. -/
theorem Prop37 {A B C D : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDBC : Triangle D B C)
    (hpar : ∃ L M : Line, Parallel L M ∧ OnLine A L ∧ OnLine D L ∧ OnLine B M ∧ OnLine C M) :
    △ A B C = △ D B C := by
  -- Let ABC, DBC be triangles on the same base BC and in the same parallels AD, BC;
  obtain ⟨AD, BC, hAD_BC, hA, hD, hB, hC⟩ := hpar
  -- I say that the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DBC.
  -- Let AD be produced in both directions to E, F; through B let BE be drawn parallel to
  -- CA, [I. 31] and through C let CF be drawn parallel to BD. [I. 31]
  /- E and F are where the parallels BE and CF meet the whole straight line AD
     (`Prop31.parallelogram`). -/
  obtain ⟨E, hE, hACBE⟩ := Prop31.parallelogram hAD_BC hA hC hB hABC.ne₂₃.symm
  obtain ⟨F, hF, hDBCF⟩ := Prop31.parallelogram hAD_BC hD hB hC hDBC.ne₂₃
  -- Then each of the figures EBCA, DBCF is a parallelogram; and they are equal, for they are
  -- on the same base BC and in the same parallels BC, EF. [I. 35]
  have hEBCA : Parallelogram E B C A := hACBE.reverse.rotate
  have h35 : quadArea E B C A = quadArea D B C F :=
    Prop35 hEBCA hDBCF ⟨AD, hE, hA, hD, hF⟩
  -- Moreover the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram EBCA; for the diameter AB bisects
  -- it. [I. 34]
  have h₁ : quadArea E B C A = △ A B C + △ A B C := by
    rw [← hEBCA.quadArea_rotate, area_bca A B C]
    exact Prop34.bisect hEBCA.rotate
  -- And the triangle DBC is half of the parallelogram DBCF; for the diameter DC bisects
  -- it. [I. 34]
  have h₂ : quadArea D B C F = △ D B C + △ D B C := Prop34.bisect hDBCF
  -- [But the halves of equal things are equal to one another.]
  have heq : △ A B C = △ D B C := Magnitude.eq_of_add_self_eq (h₁.symm.trans (h35.trans h₂))
  -- Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DBC.
  exact heq
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.

bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34:
/-- In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the
diameter bisects the areas. -/
theorem Prop34 {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A C D B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ C D B ∧ ∠ A B D = ∠ A C D ∧
      △ A B C = △ D C B
bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34.bisect:
/-- The diameter bisects the parallelogram, said of its area: the parallelogram
ABCD, measured by its diameter AC, is double the triangle ABC. I.35–I.47 cite
I.34 for this ("the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram EBCA; for the diameter
AB bisects it"). To halve by the other diameter, name the parallelogram from the
next corner (`Parallelogram.rotate`) and turn its area round with
`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`. [I. 34] -/
theorem Prop34.bisect {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea A B C D = △ A B C + △ A B C
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.cross:
/-- The diameters of a parallelogram cross: in the parallelogram ABCD, some point
lies between A and C and between B and D. Its sides AB and DC are
parallel, so they do not cross, and `AreParallel.cross_or` leaves only the
diameters. -/
theorem Parallelogram.cross (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    ∃ X : Point, Between A X C ∧ Between B X D
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate:
/-- A parallelogram has the same area whichever diameter cuts it: the parallelogram
ABCD measured by BD, as BCDA, is the same as measured by AC. -/
theorem Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea B C D A = quadArea A B C D

state.commentary:
Euclid completes each triangle to a parallelogram on BC, with parallels through B and C. I.35 makes the parallelograms equal, I.34 makes each triangle half of its own, and so the triangles are equal. J. L. Heiberg brackets that last step, and Heath gives his reason: "Here and in the next proposition Heiberg brackets the words 'But the halves of equal things are equal to one another' on the ground that, since the *Common Notion* which asserted this fact was interpolated at a very early date (before the time of Theon), it is probable that the words here were interpolated at the same time" (vol. 1, p. 332).

**"A little argument."** Heiberg took the halves to follow from Common Notion 3. Paul Tannery, Heath reports, "acutely observes" that they are no inference from it: they want a *reductio ad absurdum* through Common Notion 2. Even then, Heath adds, "a little argument would be necessary in addition to the reference to *Common Notion* 2" (vol. 1, p. 224), though he thinks Euclid would have taken it as obvious. Our tacit rules of magnitude say nothing of halves, so we prove the little argument in [Book Zero](../../Elements/Figure), as `Magnitude.eq_of_add_self_eq`: were one half less than the other, its double would be less too. Bracketed or not, the step has to be taken.

The area stays while the sides stretch, for triangles as for parallelograms: "Thus the *perimeter* in parallelograms or triangles is of itself no criterion as to their area" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 332). Proclus tells of members of communistic societies of his day "who cheated their fellow members by giving them land of greater perimeter but less area than they took themselves", and about 130 B.C. Polybius "said that there were people who could not understand that camps of the same periphery might have different capacities" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 333).

**What if A and D are one point?** Our statement reads "in the same parallels" as two whole straight lines, so A and D may coincide, as I.41 will want; the "AD" that Euclid produces is then the parallel through the vertices. He takes it from the figure that BE and CF meet it, and our I.35 covers wherever they fall.

**The modern way.** With the cross product of [I.35](35.md), twice the area of the triangle ABC is $\lvert\mathrm{(C - B)} \times \mathrm{(A - B)}\rvert$. Putting $\mathrm{D} = \mathrm{A} + t\mathrm{(C - B)}$ adds $t\mathrm{(C - B)} \times \mathrm{(C - B)} = 0$ to the cross product, so sliding the vertex along the parallel leaves the area alone.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABC, DBC be triangles on the same base BC and in the same parallels AD, BC;

I say that the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DBC.

Let AD be produced in both directions to E, F; through B let BE be drawn parallel to CA, [I. 31] and through C let CF be drawn parallel to BD. [I. 31]

Then each of the figures EBCA, DBCF is a parallelogram; and they are equal, for they are on the same base BC and in the same parallels BC, EF. [I. 35]

Moreover the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram EBCA; for the diameter AB bisects it. [I. 34]

And the triangle DBC is half of the parallelogram DBCF; for the diameter DC bisects it. [I. 34]

[But the halves of equal things are equal to one another.]

Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DBC.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- Triangles which are on the same base and in the same parallels are equal to one another. -/
theorem Prop37 {A B C D : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDBC : Triangle D B C)
    (hpar : ∃ L M : Line, Parallel L M ∧ OnLine A L ∧ OnLine D L ∧ OnLine B M ∧ OnLine C M) :
    △ A B C = △ D B C := by
  -- Let ABC, DBC be triangles on the same base BC and in the same parallels AD, BC;
  obtain ⟨AD, BC, hAD_BC, hA, hD, hB, hC⟩ := hpar
  -- I say that the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DBC.
  -- Let AD be produced in both directions to E, F; through B let BE be drawn parallel to
  -- CA, [I. 31] and through C let CF be drawn parallel to BD. [I. 31]
  /- E and F are where the parallels BE and CF meet the whole straight line AD
     (`Prop31.parallelogram`). -/
  obtain ⟨E, hE, hACBE⟩ := Prop31.parallelogram hAD_BC hA hC hB hABC.ne₂₃.symm
  obtain ⟨F, hF, hDBCF⟩ := Prop31.parallelogram hAD_BC hD hB hC hDBC.ne₂₃
  -- Then each of the figures EBCA, DBCF is a parallelogram; and they are equal, for they are
  -- on the same base BC and in the same parallels BC, EF. [I. 35]
  have hEBCA : Parallelogram E B C A := hACBE.reverse.rotate
  have h35 : quadArea E B C A = quadArea D B C F :=
    Prop35 hEBCA hDBCF ⟨AD, hE, hA, hD, hF⟩
  -- Moreover the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram EBCA; for the diameter AB bisects
  -- it. [I. 34]
  have h₁ : quadArea E B C A = △ A B C + △ A B C := by
    rw [← hEBCA.quadArea_rotate, area_bca A B C]
    exact Prop34.bisect hEBCA.rotate
  -- And the triangle DBC is half of the parallelogram DBCF; for the diameter DC bisects
  -- it. [I. 34]
  have h₂ : quadArea D B C F = △ D B C + △ D B C := Prop34.bisect hDBCF
  -- [But the halves of equal things are equal to one another.]
  have heq : △ A B C = △ D B C := Magnitude.eq_of_add_self_eq (h₁.symm.trans (h35.trans h₂))
  -- Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DBC.
  exact heq
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.

named_declarations.Elements.Magnitude.eq_of_add_self_eq:
/-- The halves of equal things are equal: if `a` and `a` together are equal to `b`
and `b` together, then `a` is equal to `b`. Were `a` less than `b`, then `a` and `a`
would be less than `b` and `b`; and the same the other way round. Heiberg brackets
these words in I.37 and I.38 as added later, but the step is needed all the same. -/
theorem Magnitude.eq_of_add_self_eq {a b : Magnitude k} (h : a + a = b + b) : a = b

state.enunciation: Triangles which are on equal bases and in the same parallels are equal to one another.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABC, DEF be triangles on equal bases BC, EF and in the same parallels BF, AD;

I say that the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DEF.

For let AD be produced in both directions to G, H; through B let BG be drawn parallel to CA, [I. 31] and through F let FH be drawn parallel to DE.

Then each of the figures GBCA, DEFH is a parallelogram; and GBCA is equal to DEFH; for they are on equal bases BC, EF and in the same parallels BF, GH. [I. 36]

Moreover the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram GBCA; for the diameter AB bisects it. [I. 34]

And the triangle FED is half of the parallelogram DEFH; for the diameter DF bisects it. [I. 34]

[But the halves of equal things are equal to one another.]

Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DEF.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.

      OnLine B M ∧ OnLine C M ∧ OnLine E M ∧ OnLine F M) :
    △ A B C = △ D E F

bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34:
/-- In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the
diameter bisects the areas. -/
theorem Prop34 {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A C D B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ C D B ∧ ∠ A B D = ∠ A C D ∧
      △ A B C = △ D C B
bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34.bisect:
/-- The diameter bisects the parallelogram, said of its area: the parallelogram
ABCD, measured by its diameter AC, is double the triangle ABC. I.35–I.47 cite
I.34 for this ("the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram EBCA; for the diameter
AB bisects it"). To halve by the other diameter, name the parallelogram from the
next corner (`Parallelogram.rotate`) and turn its area round with
`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`. [I. 34] -/
theorem Prop34.bisect {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea A B C D = △ A B C + △ A B C
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.cross:
/-- The diameters of a parallelogram cross: in the parallelogram ABCD, some point
lies between A and C and between B and D. Its sides AB and DC are
parallel, so they do not cross, and `AreParallel.cross_or` leaves only the
diameters. -/
theorem Parallelogram.cross (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    ∃ X : Point, Between A X C ∧ Between B X D
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate:
/-- A parallelogram has the same area whichever diameter cuts it: the parallelogram
ABCD measured by BD, as BCDA, is the same as measured by AC. -/
theorem Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea B C D A = quadArea A B C D

state.heath_proof:
Let ABC, DEF be triangles on equal bases BC, EF and in the same parallels BF, AD;

I say that the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DEF.

For let AD be produced in both directions to G, H; through B let BG be drawn parallel to CA, [I. 31] and through F let FH be drawn parallel to DE.

Then each of the figures GBCA, DEFH is a parallelogram; and GBCA is equal to DEFH; for they are on equal bases BC, EF and in the same parallels BF, GH. [I. 36]

Moreover the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram GBCA; for the diameter AB bisects it. [I. 34]

And the triangle FED is half of the parallelogram DEFH; for the diameter DF bisects it. [I. 34]

[But the halves of equal things are equal to one another.]

Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DEF.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- Triangles which are on equal bases and in the same parallels are equal to one another. -/
theorem Prop38 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hbase : ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖)
    (hpar : ∃ L M : Line, Parallel L M ∧ OnLine A L ∧ OnLine D L ∧
      OnLine B M ∧ OnLine C M ∧ OnLine E M ∧ OnLine F M) :
    △ A B C = △ D E F := by
  -- Let ABC, DEF be triangles on equal bases BC, EF and in the same parallels BF, AD;
  obtain ⟨AD, BF, hAD_BF, hA, hD, hB, hC, hE, hF⟩ := hpar
  -- I say that the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DEF.
  -- For let AD be produced in both directions to G, H; through B let BG be drawn parallel to
  -- CA, [I. 31] and through F let FH be drawn parallel to DE.
  /- G and H are where the parallels BG and FH meet AD (`Prop31.parallelogram`). -/
  obtain ⟨G, hG, hACBG⟩ := Prop31.parallelogram hAD_BF hA hC hB hABC.ne₂₃.symm
  obtain ⟨H, hH, hDEFH⟩ := Prop31.parallelogram hAD_BF hD hE hF hDEF.ne₂₃
  -- Then each of the figures GBCA, DEFH is a parallelogram; and GBCA is equal to DEFH; for
  -- they are on equal bases BC, EF and in the same parallels BF, GH. [I. 36]
  have hGBCA : Parallelogram G B C A := hACBG.reverse.rotate
  have h36 : quadArea G B C A = quadArea D E F H :=
    Prop36 hGBCA hDEFH hbase ⟨AD, hG, hA, hD, hH⟩ ⟨BF, hB, hC, hE, hF⟩
  -- Moreover the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram GBCA; for the diameter AB bisects
  -- it. [I. 34]
  have h₁ : quadArea G B C A = △ A B C + △ A B C := by
    rw [← hGBCA.quadArea_rotate, area_bca A B C]
    exact Prop34.bisect hGBCA.rotate
  -- And the triangle FED is half of the parallelogram DEFH; for the diameter DF bisects
  -- it. [I. 34]
  have h₂ : quadArea D E F H = △ F E D + △ F E D := by
    rw [area_cba F E D]
    exact Prop34.bisect hDEFH
  -- [But the halves of equal things are equal to one another.]
  have heq : △ A B C = △ F E D := Magnitude.eq_of_add_self_eq (h₁.symm.trans (h36.trans h₂))
  -- Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DEF.
  rw [heq, area_cba F E D]
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.

question.instructions:
Does every proposition called by the proof unit in `lean_proof` do work towards its conclusion or a substantive intermediate step of Euclid's argument? Also check for artificial hypothesis uses. Judge this unit's uses of the supplied helper signatures; helper bodies are outside this question. Heath's sentences stand as `--` lines and `cited` gives exact enunciations. In Lean, `have h : T := p` proves T by p and calls the result h; `obtain ⟨…⟩ := p` takes p apart into named pieces; `rw [h34, h37, …]` rewrites the goal by the equalities named. Follow uses through helper calls and tactics as well as explicit names. An anonymous binding or an unused hypothesis alone does not establish a defect. If both defects occur, choose `a dummy citation`.

docs/FORMALIZATION.md, section 5:
A checked intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid is legitimate, even if the
  final proof term could do without it.

criteria.cannot tell: What is given here is not enough to decide.
criteria.all do work: Every proposition call supports a later step or the conclusion, or establishes a substantive intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid. No hypothesis is mentioned merely to look used. With no proposition calls the citation part alone is vacuous; hypothesis use must still be inspected.
criteria.a dummy citation: Some proposition call does no substantive work: its result neither supports the argument nor establishes a substantive intermediate fact, and merely supplies a citation while the step is done another way.
criteria.an artificial hypothesis use: No dummy citation is established, but a hypothesis is mentioned only so that it looks used, and does no substantive work.

diameter bisects the areas. -/

bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34.bisect:
/-- The diameter bisects the parallelogram, said of its area: the parallelogram
ABCD, measured by its diameter AC, is double the triangle ABC. I.35–I.47 cite
I.34 for this ("the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram EBCA; for the diameter
AB bisects it"). To halve by the other diameter, name the parallelogram from the
next corner (`Parallelogram.rotate`) and turn its area round with
`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`. [I. 34] -/
theorem Prop34.bisect {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea A B C D = △ A B C + △ A B C
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.cross:
/-- The diameters of a parallelogram cross: in the parallelogram ABCD, some point
lies between A and C and between B and D. Its sides AB and DC are
parallel, so they do not cross, and `AreParallel.cross_or` leaves only the
diameters. -/

    ∃ X : Point, Between A X C ∧ Between B X D

/-- A parallelogram has the same area whichever diameter cuts it: the parallelogram
ABCD measured by BD, as BCDA, is the same as measured by AC. -/
theorem Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
