state.commentary:
I.38 is I.37 with the triangles set apart, on equal bases BC and EF. Euclid completes the parallelograms GBCA and DEFH, which I.36 now makes equal, and the diameters AB and DF halve them (I.34). J. L. Heiberg brackets the sentence on halves here too, as Heath notes under I.37, and the little argument proved for I.37 takes the step again.

**"Assumed in order to prove VI. 1."** Proclus thought Euclid had proved all four of I.35–I.38 at once in VI.1, where triangles and parallelograms of the same altitude are to one another as their bases, "for of course to be of the same altitude is equivalent to being in the same parallels"; most readers, he says, had missed it (Heath, vol. 1, p. 334). Heath answers: "It is true that VI. 1 generalises these propositions, but it must be observed that it does not prove the propositions themselves, as Proclus seems to imply; they are in fact assumed in order to prove VI. 1" (vol. 1, p. 334). The equalities come first, and Book VI's ratios are built on them.

Heron, in an-Nairīzī, places here a theorem Proclus gives under I.24. When two triangles have two sides equal to two sides, "*if the sum of the two angles contained by the equal sides is equal to two right angles, the two triangles are equal to one another*" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 334); if the sum is less, the one with the greater angle is the greater, and if more, the one with the less. For the first case Heron copies one triangle onto a side of the other, its vertex on the parallel to that side through the other's, and I.37 makes them equal. I.24 compared the bases of such triangles; Heron compares their areas.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABC, DEF be triangles on equal bases BC, EF and in the same parallels BF, AD;

I say that the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DEF.

For let AD be produced in both directions to G, H; through B let BG be drawn parallel to CA, [I. 31] and through F let FH be drawn parallel to DE.

Then each of the figures GBCA, DEFH is a parallelogram; and GBCA is equal to DEFH; for they are on equal bases BC, EF and in the same parallels BF, GH. [I. 36]

Moreover the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram GBCA; for the diameter AB bisects it. [I. 34]

And the triangle FED is half of the parallelogram DEFH; for the diameter DF bisects it. [I. 34]

[But the halves of equal things are equal to one another.]

Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DEF.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- Triangles which are on equal bases and in the same parallels are equal to one another. -/
theorem Prop38 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hbase : ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖)
    (hpar : ∃ L M : Line, Parallel L M ∧ OnLine A L ∧ OnLine D L ∧
      OnLine B M ∧ OnLine C M ∧ OnLine E M ∧ OnLine F M) :
    △ A B C = △ D E F := by
  -- Let ABC, DEF be triangles on equal bases BC, EF and in the same parallels BF, AD;
  obtain ⟨AD, BF, hAD_BF, hA, hD, hB, hC, hE, hF⟩ := hpar
  -- I say that the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DEF.
  -- For let AD be produced in both directions to G, H; through B let BG be drawn parallel to
  -- CA, [I. 31] and through F let FH be drawn parallel to DE.
  /- G and H are where the parallels BG and FH meet AD (`Prop31.parallelogram`). -/
  obtain ⟨G, hG, hACBG⟩ := Prop31.parallelogram hAD_BF hA hC hB hABC.ne₂₃.symm
  obtain ⟨H, hH, hDEFH⟩ := Prop31.parallelogram hAD_BF hD hE hF hDEF.ne₂₃
  -- Then each of the figures GBCA, DEFH is a parallelogram; and GBCA is equal to DEFH; for
  -- they are on equal bases BC, EF and in the same parallels BF, GH. [I. 36]
  have hGBCA : Parallelogram G B C A := hACBG.reverse.rotate
  have h36 : quadArea G B C A = quadArea D E F H :=
    Prop36 hGBCA hDEFH hbase ⟨AD, hG, hA, hD, hH⟩ ⟨BF, hB, hC, hE, hF⟩
  -- Moreover the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram GBCA; for the diameter AB bisects
  -- it. [I. 34]
  have h₁ : quadArea G B C A = △ A B C + △ A B C := by
    rw [← hGBCA.quadArea_rotate, area_bca A B C]
    exact Prop34.bisect hGBCA.rotate
  -- And the triangle FED is half of the parallelogram DEFH; for the diameter DF bisects
  -- it. [I. 34]
  have h₂ : quadArea D E F H = △ F E D + △ F E D := by
    rw [area_cba F E D]
    exact Prop34.bisect hDEFH
  -- [But the halves of equal things are equal to one another.]
  have heq : △ A B C = △ F E D := Magnitude.eq_of_add_self_eq (h₁.symm.trans (h36.trans h₂))
  -- Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DEF.
  rw [heq, area_cba F E D]
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.

/-- Equal triangles which are on the same base and on the same side are also in the same parallels. -/
theorem Prop39 {A B C D : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDBC : Triangle D B C)
    (heq : △ A B C = △ D B C) (hside : SameSideOf A D B C) (hAD : A ≠ D) :
    AreParallel A D B C := by
  -- Let ABC, DBC be equal triangles which are on the same base BC and on the same side of it;
  obtain ⟨BC, hB, hC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hABC.ne₂₃
  -- [I say that they are also in the same parallels.]
  -- And [For] let AD be joined;
  /- The parallel drawn through A will pass through D, and so be AD. -/
  -- I say that AD is parallel to BC.
  -- For, if not, let AE be drawn through the point A parallel to the straight line BC, [I. 31]
  /- The parallel through A is the straight line K (`Prop31.line`), which Euclid
     calls AE once E has been found. -/
  obtain ⟨K, hA_K, hKBC⟩ := Prop31.line (hABC.bca.off_line hB hC)
  -- and let EC be joined.
  /- E is where the parallel meets BD (`Prop30.meet`). -/
  obtain ⟨BD, hB_BD, hD_BD⟩ := Postulate1 B D hDBC.ne₁₂.symm
  have hD_BC : ¬ OnLine D BC := hDBC.bca.off_line hB hC
  have hBD_BC : BD ≠ BC := fun e => hD_BC (e ▸ hD_BD)
  obtain ⟨E, hE_BD, hE_K⟩ := Prop30.meet hKBC hB hB_BD hBD_BC
  have hE_BC : ¬ OnLine E BC := hKBC.not_onLine hE_K
  have hEBC : Triangle E B C := (Triangle.of_line hB hC hABC.ne₂₃ hE_BC).cab
  obtain ⟨EC, hE_EC, hC_EC⟩ := Postulate1 E C hEBC.ne₁₃
  -- Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle EBC; for it is on the same base BC
  -- with it and in the same parallels. [I. 37]
  have h37 : △ A B C = △ E B C :=
    Prop37 hABC hEBC ⟨K, BC, hKBC, hA_K, hE_K, hB, hC⟩
  -- But ABC is equal to DBC; therefore DBC is also equal to EBC, [C.N. 1] the greater to the
  -- less: which is impossible.
  have h1 : △ D B C = △ E B C := CommonNotion1 heq.symm h37.symm
  /- The parallel puts E on A's side of BC, hence on D's side. Since E is on
     BD, it lies on the ray from B through D. -/
  have hEB : E ≠ B := fun e => hE_BC (e ▸ hB)
  have hED_side : SameSideOf E D B C :=
    (SameSideOf.of_line hABC.ne₂₃ hB hC (hKBC.sameSide hE_K hA_K)).trans hside
  have hray : OnRay E B D :=
    OnRay.of_sameSideOf hED_side ⟨BD, hB_BD, hD_BD, hE_BD⟩ hEB
  /- In Heath's figure EBC is the less, in Proclus' other case DBC; either way
     only D itself will do (`OnRay.eq_of_area_eq`). -/
  have hED : E = D := hray.eq_of_area_eq hDBC h1.symm
  -- Therefore AE is not parallel to BC.
  /- A parallel meeting BD away from D has been excluded: the parallel
     through A must pass through D itself. -/
  have hD_K : OnLine D K := hED ▸ hE_K
  -- Similarly we can prove that neither is any other straight line except AD; therefore AD is
  -- parallel to BC.
  have hpar : AreParallel A D B C := AreParallel.of_parallel hAD hABC.ne₂₃ hA_K hD_K hB hC hKBC
  -- Therefore etc.
  exact hpar

/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.of_parallel:
/-- Two different points of L, and two different points of M, are the ends of
parallel straight lines when L and M are parallel: two points fix one straight
line (System E, Generalities 1). With `AreParallel.parallel`, this says "AB is
parallel to CD" of any other two points P, Q of the straight line AB and R,
S of CD. -/
theorem AreParallel.of_parallel (hPQ : P ≠ Q) (hRS : R ≠ S) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L)
    (hR : OnLine R M) (hS : OnLine S M) (h : Parallel L M) : AreParallel P Q R S
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.symm:

theorem AreParallel.symm (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30:
/-- Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another. -/
theorem Prop30 {A B C D E F : Point} (h₁ : AreParallel A B E F) (h₂ : AreParallel C D E F)
    (hC : ¬ Collinear A B C) :
    AreParallel A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30.meet:
/-- A straight line meeting one of two parallels meets the other. If L is parallel
to M, and a straight line N, other than M, passes through a point P of M,
then N meets L. Otherwise N would be parallel to L too, and by I.30 M and
N would be parallel to one another, though both pass through P.

Euclid uses this whenever he draws a parallel and then names the point where it
meets another straight line: E and F in I.37, G and H in I.38, E in I.39,
F in I.40, F and G in I.42, H, L and M in I.44, E in I.46 and L in
I.47. It is the uniqueness of the parallel through a point, often called
Playfair's axiom; Heath reports under I.31 that Proclus draws it from I.30.
`Prop30.unique`, a step inside I.30's own proof, gives the same uniqueness from
I.29; later proofs cite this one, Proclus' route through I.30. [I. 30] -/
theorem Prop30.meet {L M N : Line} {P : Point} (hLM : Parallel L M) (hPM : OnLine P M)
    (hPN : OnLine P N) (hNM : N ≠ M) : ∃ Q : Point, OnLine Q N ∧ OnLine Q L

/-- Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line. -/
theorem Prop31 {A B C : Point} (hBC : B ≠ C) (hA : ¬ Collinear B C A) :
    ∃ E F : Point, Between E A F ∧ AreParallel E F B C
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31.line:
/-- I.31 said of straight lines drawn and named: through a point A off the
straight line L there is a straight line K parallel to L. I.31 gives two points
of it, one on either side of A, and Postulate 1 joins them. [I. 31] -/
theorem Prop31.line {A : Point} {L : Line} (hA : ¬ OnLine A L) :
    ∃ K : Line, OnLine A K ∧ Parallel K L

    △ A B C = △ D B C

/-- "The greater to the less: which is impossible" (I.39, I.40). On the ray from B
through D, only D itself makes with the base BC a triangle equal to DBC. A
point E nearer to B makes EBC a part of DBC, and a point beyond D makes

  | length
  | angle
  | area

without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,

  A ≠ B ∧ P ≠ A ∧ Collinear A B P ∧ ¬ Between P A B

the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/

  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M

opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop

line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C

noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area

question.instructions:
Does every proposition called by the proof unit in `lean_proof` do work towards its conclusion or a substantive intermediate step of Euclid's argument? Also check for artificial hypothesis uses. Judge this unit's uses of the supplied helper signatures; helper bodies are outside this question. Heath's sentences stand as `--` lines and `cited` gives exact enunciations. In Lean, `have h : T := p` proves T by p and calls the result h; `obtain ⟨…⟩ := p` takes p apart into named pieces; `rw [h34, h37, …]` rewrites the goal by the equalities named. Follow uses through helper calls and tactics as well as explicit names. An anonymous binding or an unused hypothesis alone does not establish a defect. If both defects occur, choose `a dummy citation`.

docs/FORMALIZATION.md, section 5:
A checked intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid is legitimate, even if the
  final proof term could do without it.

criteria.all do work: Every proposition call supports a later step or the conclusion, or establishes a substantive intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid. No hypothesis is mentioned merely to look used. With no proposition calls the citation part alone is vacuous; hypothesis use must still be inspected.
criteria.a dummy citation: Some proposition call does no substantive work: its result neither supports the argument nor establishes a substantive intermediate fact, and merely supplies a citation while the step is done another way.
criteria.an artificial hypothesis use: No dummy citation is established, but a hypothesis is mentioned only so that it looks used, and does no substantive work.
criteria.cannot tell: What is given here is not enough to decide.

state.commentary:
In Heath's words, "This theorem is of course the *partial* converse of I. 37" (vol. 1, p. 337): I.37's base and its conclusion, equal areas, are the hypotheses here, and its parallels the conclusion. One hypothesis is new. "The additional qualification in this proposition that the triangles must be *on the same side* of the base is necessary because it is not, as in I. 37, involved in the other hypotheses" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 337): equal triangles on opposite sides of BC need not make AD parallel to BC.

Proclus remarks, Heath reports, "that Euclid only converts I. 37 and I. 38 relative to triangles, and omits the converses of I. 35, 36 about parallelograms as unnecessary because it is easy to see that the method would be the same, and therefore the reader may properly be left to prove them for himself" (vol. 1, p. 337). Proclus counts I.40 among Euclid's; its page tells why Heath prints it in brackets. One sentence of I.39 is in brackets too, "I say that they are also in the same parallels." J. L. Heiberg proved from a papyrus fragment, Heath reports, that it was added by someone "who did not observe that the words 'And let AD be joined' are part of the *setting-out*" (vol. 1, p. 337). Taking those words for the construction, the interpolator thought the thing to be proved should be stated first, and altered "And" into "For".

**"The greater to the less."** Before either triangle can be called the greater, we must know where E is. The parallel through A puts E on A's side of BC, and so on D's: on the ray from B through D. If E is between B and D, as in Heath's figure, EBC is a part of DBC and the less; if beyond D, a case Proclus finds equally easy (Heath, vol. 1, p. 337), DBC is the less. So E falls neither short of D nor beyond it: E is D, and the parallel through A is AD itself, with no other straight line left to refute. We keep the argument in [Book Zero](../../Elements/Figure) (`OnRay.eq_of_area_eq`), where I.40 finds it too.

**The modern way.** Put $\mathrm{B} = (0, 0)$ and $\mathrm{C} = (a, 0)$, with $a \gt 0$: a triangle on BC with its vertex at $(x, y)$ has area $\tfrac{1}{2}a\lvert y\rvert$. Equal areas give equal $\lvert y\rvert$, and the same side of BC gives $y$ one sign, so A and D are at one height and AD is parallel to BC.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABC, DBC be equal triangles which are on the same base BC and on the same side of it;

[I say that they are also in the same parallels.]

And [For] let AD be joined;

I say that AD is parallel to BC.

For, if not, let AE be drawn through the point A parallel to the straight line BC, [I. 31] and let EC be joined.

Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle EBC; for it is on the same base BC with it and in the same parallels. [I. 37]

But ABC is equal to DBC; therefore DBC is also equal to EBC, [C.N. 1] the greater to the less: which is impossible.

Therefore AE is not parallel to BC.

Similarly we can prove that neither is any other straight line except AD; therefore AD is parallel to BC.

Therefore etc.
state.lean_proof:
/-- Equal triangles which are on the same base and on the same side are also in the same parallels. -/
theorem Prop39 {A B C D : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDBC : Triangle D B C)
    (heq : △ A B C = △ D B C) (hside : SameSideOf A D B C) (hAD : A ≠ D) :
    AreParallel A D B C := by
  -- Let ABC, DBC be equal triangles which are on the same base BC and on the same side of it;
  obtain ⟨BC, hB, hC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hABC.ne₂₃
  -- [I say that they are also in the same parallels.]
  -- And [For] let AD be joined;
  /- The parallel drawn through A will pass through D, and so be AD. -/
  -- I say that AD is parallel to BC.
  -- For, if not, let AE be drawn through the point A parallel to the straight line BC, [I. 31]
  /- The parallel through A is the straight line K (`Prop31.line`), which Euclid
     calls AE once E has been found. -/
  obtain ⟨K, hA_K, hKBC⟩ := Prop31.line (hABC.bca.off_line hB hC)
  -- and let EC be joined.
  /- E is where the parallel meets BD (`Prop30.meet`). -/
  obtain ⟨BD, hB_BD, hD_BD⟩ := Postulate1 B D hDBC.ne₁₂.symm
  have hD_BC : ¬ OnLine D BC := hDBC.bca.off_line hB hC
  have hBD_BC : BD ≠ BC := fun e => hD_BC (e ▸ hD_BD)
  obtain ⟨E, hE_BD, hE_K⟩ := Prop30.meet hKBC hB hB_BD hBD_BC
  have hE_BC : ¬ OnLine E BC := hKBC.not_onLine hE_K
  have hEBC : Triangle E B C := (Triangle.of_line hB hC hABC.ne₂₃ hE_BC).cab
  obtain ⟨EC, hE_EC, hC_EC⟩ := Postulate1 E C hEBC.ne₁₃
  -- Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle EBC; for it is on the same base BC
  -- with it and in the same parallels. [I. 37]
  have h37 : △ A B C = △ E B C :=
    Prop37 hABC hEBC ⟨K, BC, hKBC, hA_K, hE_K, hB, hC⟩
  -- But ABC is equal to DBC; therefore DBC is also equal to EBC, [C.N. 1] the greater to the
  -- less: which is impossible.
  have h1 : △ D B C = △ E B C := CommonNotion1 heq.symm h37.symm
  /- The parallel puts E on A's side of BC, hence on D's side. Since E is on
     BD, it lies on the ray from B through D. -/
  have hEB : E ≠ B := fun e => hE_BC (e ▸ hB)
  have hED_side : SameSideOf E D B C :=
    (SameSideOf.of_line hABC.ne₂₃ hB hC (hKBC.sameSide hE_K hA_K)).trans hside
  have hray : OnRay E B D :=
    OnRay.of_sameSideOf hED_side ⟨BD, hB_BD, hD_BD, hE_BD⟩ hEB
  /- In Heath's figure EBC is the less, in Proclus' other case DBC; either way
     only D itself will do (`OnRay.eq_of_area_eq`). -/
  have hED : E = D := hray.eq_of_area_eq hDBC h1.symm
  -- Therefore AE is not parallel to BC.
  /- A parallel meeting BD away from D has been excluded: the parallel
     through A must pass through D itself. -/
  have hD_K : OnLine D K := hED ▸ hE_K
  -- Similarly we can prove that neither is any other straight line except AD; therefore AD is
  -- parallel to BC.
  have hpar : AreParallel A D B C := AreParallel.of_parallel hAD hABC.ne₂₃ hA_K hD_K hB hC hKBC
  -- Therefore etc.
  exact hpar

statement.note: "In the same parallels" is AD parallel to BC, so A and D are apart: on one base, ABC and DBC are two triangles only then.

route.note: Euclid's argument, made direct at its end: the parallel through A is shown to pass through D, so no other straight line needs refuting.

state.commentary:
In Heath's words, "This theorem is of course the *partial* converse of I. 37" (vol. 1, p. 337): I.37's base and its conclusion, equal areas, are the hypotheses here, and its parallels the conclusion. One hypothesis is new. "The additional qualification in this proposition that the triangles must be *on the same side* of the base is necessary because it is not, as in I. 37, involved in the other hypotheses" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 337): equal triangles on opposite sides of BC need not make AD parallel to BC.

Proclus remarks, Heath reports, "that Euclid only converts I. 37 and I. 38 relative to triangles, and omits the converses of I. 35, 36 about parallelograms as unnecessary because it is easy to see that the method would be the same, and therefore the reader may properly be left to prove them for himself" (vol. 1, p. 337). Proclus counts I.40 among Euclid's; its page tells why Heath prints it in brackets. One sentence of I.39 is in brackets too, "I say that they are also in the same parallels." J. L. Heiberg proved from a papyrus fragment, Heath reports, that it was added by someone "who did not observe that the words 'And let AD be joined' are part of the *setting-out*" (vol. 1, p. 337). Taking those words for the construction, the interpolator thought the thing to be proved should be stated first, and altered "And" into "For".

**"The greater to the less."** Before either triangle can be called the greater, we must know where E is. The parallel through A puts E on A's side of BC, and so on D's: on the ray from B through D. If E is between B and D, as in Heath's figure, EBC is a part of DBC and the less; if beyond D, a case Proclus finds equally easy (Heath, vol. 1, p. 337), DBC is the less. So E falls neither short of D nor beyond it: E is not D, and the parallel through A is AD itself, with no other straight line left to refute. We keep the argument in [Book Zero](../../Elements/Figure) (`OnRay.eq_of_area_eq`), where I.40 finds it too.

**The modern way.** Put $\mathrm{B} = (0, 0)$ and $\mathrm{C} = (a, 0)$, with $a \gt 0$: a triangle on BC with its vertex at $(x, y)$ has area $\tfrac{1}{2}a\lvert y\rvert$. Equal areas give equal $\lvert y\rvert$, and the same side of BC gives $y$ one sign, so A and D are at one height and AD is parallel to BC.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABC, DBC be equal triangles which are on the same base BC and on the same side of it;

[I say that they are also in the same parallels.]

And [For] let AD be joined;

I say that AD is parallel to BC.

For, if not, let AE be drawn through the point A parallel to the straight line BC, [I. 31] and let EC be joined.

Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle EBC; for it is on the same base BC with it and in the same parallels. [I. 37]

But ABC is equal to DBC; therefore DBC is also equal to EBC, [C.N. 1] the greater to the less: which is impossible.

Therefore AE is not parallel to BC.

Similarly we can prove that neither is any other straight line except AD; therefore AD is parallel to BC.

Therefore etc.
state.lean_proof:
/-- Equal triangles which are on the same base and on the same side are also in the same parallels. -/
theorem Prop39 {A B C D : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDBC : Triangle D B C)
    (heq : △ A B C = △ D B C) (hside : SameSideOf A D B C) (hAD : A ≠ D) :
    AreParallel A D B C := by
  -- Let ABC, DBC be equal triangles which are on the same base BC and on the same side of it;
  obtain ⟨BC, hB, hC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hABC.ne₂₃
  -- [I say that they are also in the same parallels.]
  -- And [For] let AD be joined;
  /- The parallel drawn through A will pass through D, and so be AD. -/
  -- I say that AD is parallel to BC.
  -- For, if not, let AE be drawn through the point A parallel to the straight line BC, [I. 31]
  /- The parallel through A is the straight line K (`Prop31.line`), which Euclid
     calls AE once E has been found. -/
  obtain ⟨K, hA_K, hKBC⟩ := Prop31.line (hABC.bca.off_line hB hC)
  -- and let EC be joined.
  /- E is where the parallel meets BD (`Prop30.meet`). -/
  obtain ⟨BD, hB_BD, hD_BD⟩ := Postulate1 B D hDBC.ne₁₂.symm
  have hD_BC : ¬ OnLine D BC := hDBC.bca.off_line hB hC
  have hBD_BC : BD ≠ BC := fun e => hD_BC (e ▸ hD_BD)
  obtain ⟨E, hE_BD, hE_K⟩ := Prop30.meet hKBC hB hB_BD hBD_BC
  have hE_BC : ¬ OnLine E BC := hKBC.not_onLine hE_K
  have hEBC : Triangle E B C := (Triangle.of_line hB hC hABC.ne₂₃ hE_BC).cab
  obtain ⟨EC, hE_EC, hC_EC⟩ := Postulate1 E C hEBC.ne₁₃
  -- Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle EBC; for it is on the same base BC
  -- with it and in the same parallels. [I. 37]
  have h37 : △ A B C = △ E B C :=
    Prop37 hABC hEBC ⟨K, BC, hKBC, hA_K, hE_K, hB, hC⟩
  -- But ABC is equal to DBC; therefore DBC is also equal to EBC, [C.N. 1] the greater to the
  -- less: which is impossible.
  have h1 : △ D B C = △ E B C := CommonNotion1 heq.symm h37.symm
  /- The parallel puts E on A's side of BC, hence on D's side. Since E is on
     BD, it lies on the ray from B through D. -/
  have hEB : E ≠ B := fun e => hE_BC (e ▸ hB)
  have hED_side : SameSideOf E D B C :=
    (SameSideOf.of_line hABC.ne₂₃ hB hC (hKBC.sameSide hE_K hA_K)).trans hside
  have hray : OnRay E B D :=
    OnRay.of_sameSideOf hED_side ⟨BD, hB_BD, hD_BD, hE_BD⟩ hEB
  /- In Heath's figure EBC is the less, in Proclus' other case DBC; either way
     only D itself will do (`OnRay.eq_of_area_eq`). -/
  have hED : E = D := hray.eq_of_area_eq hDBC h1.symm
  -- Therefore AE is not parallel to BC.
  /- A parallel meeting BD away from D has been excluded: the parallel
     through A must pass through D itself. -/
  have hD_K : OnLine D K := hED ▸ hE_K
  -- Similarly we can prove that neither is any other straight line except AD; therefore AD is
  -- parallel to BC.
  have hpar : AreParallel A D B C := AreParallel.of_parallel hAD hABC.ne₂₃ hA_K hD_K hB hC hKBC
  -- Therefore etc.
  exact hpar

statement.note: "In the same parallels" is AD parallel to BC, so A and D are apart: on one base, ABC and DBC are two triangles only then.

route.note: Euclid's argument, made direct at its end: the parallel through A is shown to pass through D, so no other straight line needs refuting.

named_declarations.Elements.OnRay.eq_of_area_eq:
/-- "The greater to the less: which is impossible" (I.39, I.40). On the ray from B
through D, only D itself makes with the base BC a triangle equal to DBC. A
point E nearer to B makes EBC a part of DBC, and a point beyond D makes
DBC a part of EBC; either way the part would be equal to the whole
(`area_lt_of_cut`, C.N. 5). If E is as far from B as D is, it is D
(`OnRay.eq_of_len_eq`). -/
theorem OnRay.eq_of_area_eq {E : Point} (hDBC : Triangle D B C) (hE : OnRay E B D)
    (h : △ E B C = △ D B C) : E = D

      (((SameSideOf.of_line hBE hB hE (hKBE.sameSide hF_K hA_K)).trans hside).sameSide hB hE)
  have hray : OnRay F C D :=
    OnRay.of_sameSideOf hFD_side ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD, hF_CD⟩ (fun e => hF_BE (e ▸ hC))
  /- Euclid's case has F between C and D; beyond D, DCE is the part and FCE
     the whole. Either way only D itself will do (`OnRay.eq_of_area_eq`). -/
  have hFD : F = D := hray.eq_of_area_eq hCDE.bac h1.symm
  -- Therefore AF is not parallel to BE.
  /- So the parallel through A meets CD at D itself, and is AD. -/
  have hD_K : OnLine D K := hFD ▸ hF_K
  -- Similarly we can prove that neither is any other straight line except AD; therefore AD is
  -- parallel to BE.
  have hpar : AreParallel A D B E := AreParallel.of_parallel hAD hBE hA_K hD_K hB hE hKBE
  -- Therefore etc.
  exact hpar
  -- Q. E. D.]

helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.of_parallel:
/-- Two different points of L, and two different points of M, are the ends of
parallel straight lines when L and M are parallel: two points fix one straight
line (System E, Generalities 1). With `AreParallel.parallel`, this says "AB is
parallel to CD" of any other two points P, Q of the straight line AB and R,
S of CD. -/
theorem AreParallel.of_parallel (hPQ : P ≠ Q) (hRS : R ≠ S) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L)
    (hR : OnLine R M) (hS : OnLine S M) (h : Parallel L M) : AreParallel P Q R S
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.symm:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then CD is parallel to AB. -/
theorem AreParallel.symm (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30:
/-- Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another. -/
theorem Prop30 {A B C D E F : Point} (h₁ : AreParallel A B E F) (h₂ : AreParallel C D E F)
    (hC : ¬ Collinear A B C) :
    AreParallel A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30.meet:
/-- A straight line meeting one of two parallels meets the other. If L is parallel
to M, and a straight line N, other than M, passes through a point P of M,
then N meets L. Otherwise N would be parallel to L too, and by I.30 M and
N would be parallel to one another, though both pass through P.

Euclid uses this whenever he draws a parallel and then names the point where it
meets another straight line: E and F in I.37, G and H in I.38, E in I.39,
F in I.40, F and G in I.42, H, L and M in I.44, E in I.46 and L in
I.47. It is the uniqueness of the parallel through a point, often called
Playfair's axiom; Heath reports under I.31 that Proclus draws it from I.30.
`Prop30.unique`, a step inside I.30's own proof, gives the same uniqueness from
I.29; later proofs cite this one, Proclus' route through I.30. [I. 30] -/
theorem Prop30.meet {L M N : Line} {P : Point} (hLM : Parallel L M) (hPM : OnLine P M)
    (hPN : OnLine P N) (hNM : N ≠ M) : ∃ Q : Point, OnLine Q N ∧ OnLine Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31:
/-- Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line. -/
theorem Prop31 {A B C : Point} (hBC : B ≠ C) (hA : ¬ Collinear B C A) :
    ∃ E F : Point, Between E A F ∧ AreParallel E F B C
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31.line:
/-- I.31 said of straight lines drawn and named: through a point A off the
straight line L there is a straight line K parallel to L. I.31 gives two points
of it, one on either side of A, and Postulate 1 joins them. [I. 31] -/
theorem Prop31.line {A : Point} {L : Line} (hA : ¬ OnLine A L) :
    ∃ K : Line, OnLine A K ∧ Parallel K L
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop38:
/-- Triangles which are on equal bases and in the same parallels are equal to one another. -/
theorem Prop38 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hbase : ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖)
    (hpar : ∃ L M : Line, Parallel L M ∧ OnLine A L ∧ OnLine D L ∧
      OnLine B M ∧ OnLine C M ∧ OnLine E M ∧ OnLine F M) :
    △ A B C = △ D E F
helper_signatures.Elements.CommonNotion1:
/-- **Common Notion 1.** Things which are equal to the same thing are also equal
to one another. -/
theorem CommonNotion1 {α : Sort _} {a b c : α} (h₁ : a = c) (h₂ : b = c) : a = b
helper_signatures.Elements.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.eq_of_area_eq:
/-- "The greater to the less: which is impossible" (I.39, I.40). On the ray from B
through D, only D itself makes with the base BC a triangle equal to DBC. A
point E nearer to B makes EBC a part of DBC, and a point beyond D makes
DBC a part of EBC; either way the part would be equal to the whole
(`area_lt_of_cut`, C.N. 5). If E is as far from B as D is, it is D
(`OnRay.eq_of_len_eq`). -/
theorem OnRay.eq_of_area_eq {E : Point} (hDBC : Triangle D B C) (hE : OnRay E B D)
    (h : △ E B C = △ D B C) : E = D
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.of_sameSideOf:
/-- Going the other way: a point P of the straight line DF, other than D, and
on the same side of the straight line DE as F, is on the ray from D through
F. It is not behind D, for then DE would separate it from F (System E,
Pasch 3). -/
theorem OnRay.of_sameSideOf {D E F P : Point} (h : SameSideOf P F D E) (hP : Collinear D F P)
    (hPD : P ≠ D) : OnRay P D F
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.symm:
/-- P is on the ray from A through B exactly when B is on the ray from A
through P: they are one and the same ray. -/
theorem OnRay.symm (h : OnRay P A B) : OnRay B A P
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.not_onLine:
/-- Parallels do not meet: a point of L is not on M. -/
theorem Parallel.not_onLine (h : Parallel L M) (hP : OnLine P L) : ¬ OnLine P M
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.sameSide:
/-- All the points of one parallel lie on one side of the other: two points of L
are on the same side of M. Were they on opposite sides, the straight line L
joining them would cross M (System E, Intersection 1). -/
theorem Parallel.sameSide (h : Parallel L M) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L) :
    SameSide P Q M
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.symm:
/-- If L is parallel to M, then M is parallel to L. -/
theorem Parallel.symm (h : Parallel L M) : Parallel M L
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate1:
/-- **Postulate 1.** To draw a straight line from any point to any point. -/
axiom Postulate1 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf:

def SameSideOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.of_line:

I.30.enunciation: Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another.

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ P ≠ A ∧ Collinear A B P ∧ ¬ Between P A B
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length

question.instructions:
Does every proposition called by the proof unit in `lean_proof` do work towards its conclusion or a substantive intermediate step of Euclid's argument? Also check for artificial hypothesis uses. Judge this unit's uses of the supplied helper signatures; helper bodies are outside this question. Heath's sentences stand as `--` lines and `cited` gives exact enunciations. In Lean, `have h : T := p` proves T by p and calls the result h; `obtain ⟨…⟩ := p` takes p apart into named pieces; `rw [h34, h37, …]` rewrites the goal by the equalities named. Follow uses through helper calls and tactics as well as explicit names. An anonymous binding or an unused hypothesis alone does not establish a defect. If both defects occur, choose `a dummy citation`.

docs/FORMALIZATION.md, section 5:
A checked intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid is legitimate, even if the
  final proof term could do without it.

criteria.all do work: Every proposition call supports a later step or the conclusion, or establishes a substantive intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid. No hypothesis is mentioned merely to look used. With no proposition calls the citation part alone is vacuous; hypothesis use must still be inspected.
criteria.a dummy citation: Some proposition call does no substantive work: its result neither supports the argument nor establishes a substantive intermediate fact, and merely supplies a citation while the step is done another way.
criteria.an artificial hypothesis use: No dummy citation is established, but a hypothesis is mentioned only so that it looks used, and does no substantive work.
criteria.cannot tell: What is given here is not enough to decide.

state.enunciation: Equal triangles which are on equal bases and on the same side are also in the same parallels.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABC, CDE be equal triangles on equal bases BC, CE and on the same side.

I say that they are also in the same parallels.

For let AD be joined;

I say that AD is parallel to BE.

For, if not, let AF be drawn through A parallel to BE [I. 31], and let FE be joined.

Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle FCE; for they are on equal bases BC, CE and in the same parallels BE, AF. [I. 38]

But the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DCE; therefore the triangle DCE is also equal to the triangle FCE, [C.N. 1] the greater to the less: which is impossible.

Therefore AF is not parallel to BE.

Similarly we can prove that neither is any other straight line except AD; therefore AD is parallel to BE.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.]
state.lean_proof:
/-- **I.40, general** (companion of I.40). Equal triangles ABC, DEF on equal bases BC, EF
of one straight line L, and on the same side of it, are in the same parallels: A and D lie
on one straight line parallel to L. The bases may be apart, touching, overlapping or one,
and named either way along L; the vertices may be one point, and then the parallel is the
one through it. -/
theorem Prop40.general {A B C D E F : Point} {L : Line} (hABC : Triangle A B C)
    (hDEF : Triangle D E F) (hB : OnLine B L) (hC : OnLine C L) (hE : OnLine E L)
    (hF : OnLine F L) (hbase : ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖) (heq : △ A B C = △ D E F)
    (hside : SameSide A D L) :
    ∃ M : Line, Parallel M L ∧ OnLine A M ∧ OnLine D M := by
  /- "Let ABC, CDE be equal triangles": here the second triangle is DEF,
     and both bases lie on L. Each vertex is off that straight line. -/
  have hA_L : ¬ OnLine A L := hABC.bca.off_line hB hC
  have hD_L : ¬ OnLine D L := hDEF.bca.off_line hE hF
  /- "let AF be drawn through A parallel to BE [I. 31]": K is the parallel
     through A to the straight line L carrying both bases. -/
  obtain ⟨K, hA_K, hKL⟩ := Prop31.line hA_L
  /- "and let FE be joined": G, playing Euclid's F, is where K meets ED, as
     his F lies on CD (`Prop30.meet`). His FE is our GF, which closes the
     triangle GEF, his FCE. -/
  obtain ⟨ED, hE_ED, hD_ED⟩ := Postulate1 E D hDEF.ne₁₂.symm
  obtain ⟨G, hG_ED, hG_K⟩ :=
    Prop30.meet hKL hE hE_ED (fun e => hD_L (e ▸ hD_ED))
  have hG_L : ¬ OnLine G L := hKL.not_onLine hG_K
  have hGEF : Triangle G E F := (Triangle.of_line hE hF hDEF.ne₂₃ hG_L).cab
  /- "the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle FCE": ABC and GEF have equal
     bases on L and their vertices on K, so I.38 gives equal areas. -/
  have h38 : △ A B C = △ G E F :=
    Prop38 hABC hGEF hbase ⟨K, L, hKL, hA_K, hG_K, hB, hC, hE, hF⟩
  /- "the triangle DCE is also equal to the triangle FCE, [C.N. 1]":
     DEF and GEF are each equal to ABC. -/
  have h1 : △ D E F = △ G E F := CommonNotion1 heq.symm h38.symm
  /- "the greater to the less: which is impossible": G and A lie on the
     same side of L, hence G is on D's side. On ED this puts G on the ray
     from E through D. -/
  have hGD_L : SameSide G D L := same_side_trans (hKL.sameSide hA_K hG_K) hside
  have hGD_side : SameSideOf G D E F := SameSideOf.of_line hDEF.ne₂₃ hE hF hGD_L
  have hray : OnRay G E D :=
    OnRay.of_sameSideOf hGD_side ⟨ED, hE_ED, hD_ED, hG_ED⟩ (fun e => hG_L (e ▸ hE))
  /- Between E and D, GEF would be the part of DEF; beyond D, DEF would be
     the part of GEF. Equal areas therefore put G at D itself. -/
  have hGD : G = D := hray.eq_of_area_eq hDEF h1.symm
  /- "they are also in the same parallels": the end of the reductio is direct.
     D lies on K, which is still the parallel through A when A and D coincide. -/
  have hD_K : OnLine D K := hGD ▸ hG_K
  exact ⟨K, hKL, hA_K, hD_K⟩

    (hC : ¬ Collinear A B C) :

helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30.meet:
/-- A straight line meeting one of two parallels meets the other. If L is parallel
to M, and a straight line N, other than M, passes through a point P of M,
then N meets L. Otherwise N would be parallel to L too, and by I.30 M and
N would be parallel to one another, though both pass through P.

meets another straight line: E and F in I.37, G and H in I.38, E in I.39,
F in I.40, F and G in I.42, H, L and M in I.44, E in I.46 and L in

    (hPN : OnLine P N) (hNM : N ≠ M) : ∃ Q : Point, OnLine Q N ∧ OnLine Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31:
/-- Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line. -/

    ∃ E F : Point, Between E A F ∧ AreParallel E F B C
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31.line:
/-- I.31 said of straight lines drawn and named: through a point A off the
straight line L there is a straight line K parallel to L. I.31 gives two points
of it, one on either side of A, and Postulate 1 joins them. [I. 31] -/

    ∃ K : Line, OnLine A K ∧ Parallel K L
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop38:
/-- Triangles which are on equal bases and in the same parallels are equal to one another. -/
theorem Prop38 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hbase : ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖)
    (hpar : ∃ L M : Line, Parallel L M ∧ OnLine A L ∧ OnLine D L ∧
      OnLine B M ∧ OnLine C M ∧ OnLine E M ∧ OnLine F M) :
    △ A B C = △ D E F

state.enunciation: Equal triangles which are on equal bases and on the same side are also in the same parallels.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABC, CDE be equal triangles on equal bases BC, CE and on the same side.

I say that they are also in the same parallels.

For let AD be joined;

I say that AD is parallel to BE.

For, if not, let AF be drawn through A parallel to BE [I. 31], and let FE be joined.

Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle FCE; for they are on equal bases BC, CE and in the same parallels BE, AF. [I. 38]

But the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DCE; therefore the triangle DCE is also equal to the triangle FCE, [C.N. 1] the greater to the less: which is impossible.

Therefore AF is not parallel to BE.

Similarly we can prove that neither is any other straight line except AD; therefore AD is parallel to BE.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.]
state.lean_proof:
/-- **I.40, the join** (companion of I.40). Under the hypotheses of `Prop40.general`, when
the vertices A and D are two points, the straight line AD joining them is parallel to the
base BC: Euclid's "AD is parallel to BE". -/
theorem Prop40.join {A B C D E F : Point} {L : Line} (hABC : Triangle A B C)
    (hDEF : Triangle D E F) (hB : OnLine B L) (hC : OnLine C L) (hE : OnLine E L)
    (hF : OnLine F L) (hbase : ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖) (heq : △ A B C = △ D E F)
    (hside : SameSide A D L) (hAD : A ≠ D) :
    AreParallel A D B C := by
  /- "For let AD be joined": the general statement puts A and D on one
     parallel M to L, and the two distinct vertices determine that straight line. -/
  obtain ⟨M, hM, hA_M, hD_M⟩ :=
    Prop40.general hABC hDEF hB hC hE hF hbase heq hside
  /- "therefore AD is parallel to BE": the distinct points A and D name M,
     and the distinct ends B and C of the first base name L. -/
  exact AreParallel.of_parallel hAD hABC.ne₂₃ hA_M hD_M hB hC hM

theorem Prop40.special {A B C D E : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hCDE : Triangle C D E)
    (hBCE : Between B C E) (hbase : ‖B C‖ = ‖C E‖) (heq : △ A B C = △ C D E)

Heath prints the whole proposition in square brackets, from its heading "[Proposition 40." to the closing "Q. E. D.]", and says why: "Heiberg has proved by means of the papyrus-fragment mentioned in the last note that this proposition is an interpolation by some one who thought that there should be a proposition following I. 39 and related to it in the same way as I. 38 is related to I. 37, and I. 36 to I. 35" (vol. 1, p. 338).

The fragment J. L. Heiberg used, of the second or third century, holds I.39 and I.41 one after the other, "showing that I. 40 was wanting, whereas it is found in all the MSS. and is recognised by Proclus"; it was added "although Euclid nowhere uses I. 40, and therefore was not likely to include it" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 51). Heath takes the same hand to have slipped the bracketed sentence into I.39, and I.40 repeats that sentence and its "For" with no brackets of their own. Heath prints the proposition, and so do we. The argument is I.39's again, with the equal bases BC, CE for the one base and I.38 for I.37.

**Two bases that touch.** Our main theorem takes the figure as it stands, with BC and CE meeting at C, though the enunciation, like I.38's, allows any two equal bases on one straight line. Its companion `Prop40.general` takes them so, apart, touching, overlapping or one, by the same argument. F is where the parallel through A meets CD, and our I.38 makes ABC equal to FCE while letting the bases share C and F be A, so neither needs a case of its own. The areas then put F at D, as they put E at D in I.39, and the parallel through A is AD.

**The modern way.** Let $\vec{u} = \mathrm{C - B}$, which is also $\mathrm{E - C}$, and take the cross product of [I.35](35.md). A and D lie on one side of BE, so the signed areas $\tfrac{1}{2}\vec{u} \times \mathrm{(A - B)}$ and $\tfrac{1}{2}\vec{u} \times \mathrm{(D - C)}$ have one sign. Their difference is $\tfrac{1}{2}\vec{u} \times \mathrm{(D - A)}$, since $\vec{u} \times \vec{u} = 0$, so equal areas make $\mathrm{D - A}$ a multiple of $\vec{u}$, and AD is parallel to BE.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABC, CDE be equal triangles on equal bases BC, CE and on the same side.

I say that they are also in the same parallels.

For let AD be joined;

I say that AD is parallel to BE.

For, if not, let AF be drawn through A parallel to BE [I. 31], and let FE be joined.

Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle FCE; for they are on equal bases BC, CE and in the same parallels BE, AF. [I. 38]

But the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DCE; therefore the triangle DCE is also equal to the triangle FCE, [C.N. 1] the greater to the less: which is impossible.

Therefore AF is not parallel to BE.

Similarly we can prove that neither is any other straight line except AD; therefore AD is parallel to BE.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.]
state.lean_proof:
/-- Equal triangles which are on equal bases and on the same side are also in the same parallels. -/
theorem Prop40 {A B C D E : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hCDE : Triangle C D E)
    (hBCE : Between B C E) (hbase : ‖B C‖ = ‖C E‖) (heq : △ A B C = △ C D E)
    (hside : SameSideOf A D B E) (hAD : A ≠ D) :
    AreParallel A D B E := by
  -- Let ABC, CDE be equal triangles on equal bases BC, CE and on the same side.
  have hBE : B ≠ E := ne_of_between_ends hBCE
  obtain ⟨BE, hB, hE⟩ := Postulate1 B E hBE
  have hC : OnLine C BE := on_line_of_between_ends hBCE hB hE
  have hA_BE : ¬ OnLine A BE := hABC.bca.off_line hB hC
  have hD_BE : ¬ OnLine D BE := hCDE.acb.off_line hC hE
  -- I say that they are also in the same parallels.
  -- For let AD be joined;
  /- The parallel drawn through A will pass through D, and so be AD. -/
  -- I say that AD is parallel to BE.
  -- For, if not, let AF be drawn through A parallel to BE [I. 31], and let FE be joined.
  /- The parallel through A is the straight line K (`Prop31.line`), and F is where
     it meets CD (`Prop30.meet`). -/
  obtain ⟨K, hA_K, hKBE⟩ := Prop31.line hA_BE
  obtain ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD⟩ := Postulate1 C D hCDE.ne₁₂
  obtain ⟨F, hF_CD, hF_K⟩ :=
    Prop30.meet hKBE hC hC_CD (fun e => hD_BE (e ▸ hD_CD))
  have hF_BE : ¬ OnLine F BE := hKBE.not_onLine hF_K
  have hFCE : Triangle F C E := (Triangle.of_line hC hE hCDE.ne₁₃ hF_BE).cab
  obtain ⟨FE, hF_FE, hE_FE⟩ := Postulate1 F E hFCE.ne₁₃
  -- Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle FCE; for they are on equal bases BC,
  -- CE and in the same parallels BE, AF. [I. 38]
  have h38 : △ A B C = △ F C E :=
    Prop38 hABC hFCE hbase ⟨K, BE, hKBE, hA_K, hF_K, hB, hC, hC, hE⟩
  -- But the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DCE; therefore the triangle DCE is also
  -- equal to the triangle FCE, [C.N. 1] the greater to the less: which is impossible.
  have h1 : △ D C E = △ F C E :=
    CommonNotion1 ((area_bac C D E).symm.trans heq.symm) h38.symm
  /- F and D lie on the same side of CE, which is the straight line BE.
     Thus F lies on the ray from C through D. -/
  have hFD_side : SameSideOf F D C E :=
    SameSideOf.of_line hCDE.ne₁₃ hC hE
      (((SameSideOf.of_line hBE hB hE (hKBE.sameSide hF_K hA_K)).trans hside).sameSide hB hE)
  have hray : OnRay F C D :=
    OnRay.of_sameSideOf hFD_side ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD, hF_CD⟩ (fun e => hF_BE (e ▸ hC))
  /- Euclid's case has F between C and D; beyond D, DCE is the part and FCE
     the whole. Either way only D itself will do (`OnRay.eq_of_area_eq`). -/
  have hFD : F = D := hray.eq_of_area_eq hCDE.bac h1.symm
  -- Therefore AF is not parallel to BE.
  /- So the parallel through A meets CD at D itself, and is AD. -/
  have hD_K : OnLine D K := hFD ▸ hF_K
  -- Similarly we can prove that neither is any other straight line except AD; therefore AD is
  -- parallel to BE.
  have hpar : AreParallel A D B E := AreParallel.of_parallel hAD hBE hA_K hD_K hB hE hKBE
  -- Therefore etc.
  exact hpar
  -- Q. E. D.]

  obtain ⟨FE, hF_FE, hE_FE⟩ := Postulate1 F E hFCE.ne₁₃
  -- Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle FCE; for they are on equal bases BC,
  -- CE and in the same parallels BE, AF. [I. 38]
  have h38 : △ A B C = △ F C E :=
    Prop38 hABC hFCE hbase ⟨K, BE, hKBE, hA_K, hF_K, hB, hC, hC, hE⟩
  -- But the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DCE; therefore the triangle DCE is also
  -- equal to the triangle FCE, [C.N. 1] the greater to the less: which is impossible.
  have h1 : △ D C E = △ F C E :=
    CommonNotion1 ((area_bac C D E).symm.trans heq.symm) h38.symm
  /- F and D lie on the same side of CE, which is the straight line BE.
     Thus F lies on the ray from C through D. -/
  have hFD_side : SameSideOf F D C E :=
    SameSideOf.of_line hCDE.ne₁₃ hC hE
      (((SameSideOf.of_line hBE hB hE (hKBE.sameSide hF_K hA_K)).trans hside).sameSide hB hE)
  have hray : OnRay F C D :=
    OnRay.of_sameSideOf hFD_side ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD, hF_CD⟩ (fun e => hF_BE (e ▸ hC))
  /- Euclid's case has F between C and D; beyond D, DCE is the part and FCE
     the whole. Either way only D itself will do (`OnRay.eq_of_area_eq`). -/
  have hFD : F = D := hray.eq_of_area_eq hCDE.bac h1.symm
  -- Therefore AF is not parallel to BE.
  /- So the parallel through A meets CD at D itself, and is AD. -/
  have hD_K : OnLine D K := hFD ▸ hF_K
  -- Similarly we can prove that neither is any other straight line except AD; therefore AD is
  -- parallel to BE.
  have hpar : AreParallel A D B E := AreParallel.of_parallel hAD hBE hA_K hD_K hB hE hKBE
  -- Therefore etc.
  exact hpar
  -- Q. E. D.]

state.heath_proof:
Let ABC, CDE be equal triangles on equal bases BC, CE and on the same side.

I say that they are also in the same parallels.

For let AD be joined;

I say that AD is parallel to BE.

For, if not, let AF be drawn through A parallel to BE [I. 31], and let FE be joined.

Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle FCE; for they are on equal bases BC, CE and in the same parallels BE, AF. [I. 38]

But the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DCE; therefore the triangle DCE is also equal to the triangle FCE, [C.N. 1] the greater to the less: which is impossible.

Therefore AF is not parallel to BE.

Similarly we can prove that neither is any other straight line except AD; therefore AD is parallel to BE.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.]

    quadArea A B C D = △ A B C + △ A B C

lies between A and C and between B and D. Its sides AB and DC are
parallel, so they do not cross, and `AreParallel.cross_or` leaves only the

    ∃ X : Point, Between A X C ∧ Between B X D

state.enunciation: If a parallelogram have the same base with a triangle and be in the same parallels, the parallelogram is double of the triangle.
state.heath_proof:
For let the parallelogram ABCD have the same base BC with the triangle EBC, and let it be in the same parallels BC, AE;

I say that the parallelogram ABCD is double of the triangle BEC.

For let AC be joined.

Then the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle EBC; for it is on the same base BC with it and in the same parallels BC, AE. [I. 37]

But the parallelogram ABCD is double of the triangle ABC; for the diameter AC bisects it; [I. 34] so that the parallelogram ABCD is also double of the triangle EBC.

state.lean_proof:
/-- If a parallelogram have the same base with a triangle and be in the same parallels, the
parallelogram is double of the triangle. -/
theorem Prop41 {A B C D E : Point} (hABCD : Parallelogram A B C D) (hE : Collinear A D E) :
    quadArea A B C D = △ B E C + △ B E C := by
  -- For let the parallelogram ABCD have the same base BC with the triangle EBC,
  -- and let it be in the same parallels BC, AE;
  obtain ⟨AE, hA_AE, hD_AE, hE_AE⟩ := hE
  obtain ⟨BC, hB, hC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hABCD.2.1
  have hpar : Parallel AE BC := (hABCD.2.parallel hB hC hD_AE hA_AE).symm
  -- I say that the parallelogram ABCD is double of the triangle BEC.
  -- For let AC be joined.
  /- The area `quadArea A B C D` already measures ABCD by its diameter AC,
     as the triangles ABC and ACD together. -/
  -- Then the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle EBC;
  -- for it is on the same base BC with it and in the same parallels BC, AE. [I. 37]
  have hEBC : Triangle E B C :=
    (Triangle.of_line hB hC hABCD.2.1 (hpar.not_onLine hE_AE)).cab
  have h37 : △ A B C = △ E B C :=
    Prop37 hABCD.triangle hEBC ⟨AE, BC, hpar, hA_AE, hE_AE, hB, hC⟩
  -- But the parallelogram ABCD is double of the triangle ABC;
  -- for the diameter AC bisects it; [I. 34]
  have h34 : quadArea A B C D = △ A B C + △ A B C := Prop34.bisect hABCD
  -- so that the parallelogram ABCD is also double of the triangle EBC.
  rw [h34, h37, area_bac E B C]
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.

state.enunciation: If a parallelogram have the same base with a triangle and be in the same parallels, the parallelogram is double of the triangle.
state.heath_proof:
For let the parallelogram ABCD have the same base BC with the triangle EBC, and let it be in the same parallels BC, AE;

I say that the parallelogram ABCD is double of the triangle BEC.

For let AC be joined.

Then the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle EBC; for it is on the same base BC with it and in the same parallels BC, AE. [I. 37]

But the parallelogram ABCD is double of the triangle ABC; for the diameter AC bisects it; [I. 34] so that the parallelogram ABCD is also double of the triangle EBC.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- If a parallelogram have the same base with a triangle and be in the same parallels, the
parallelogram is double of the triangle. -/
theorem Prop41 {A B C D E : Point} (hABCD : Parallelogram A B C D) (hE : Collinear A D E) :
    quadArea A B C D = △ B E C + △ B E C := by
  have unrelated := @Elements.BookI.Prop15
  -- For let the parallelogram ABCD have the same base BC with the triangle EBC,
  -- and let it be in the same parallels BC, AE;
  obtain ⟨AE, hA_AE, hD_AE, hE_AE⟩ := hE
  obtain ⟨BC, hB, hC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hABCD.2.1
  have hpar : Parallel AE BC := (hABCD.2.parallel hB hC hD_AE hA_AE).symm
  -- I say that the parallelogram ABCD is double of the triangle BEC.
  -- For let AC be joined.
  /- The area `quadArea A B C D` already measures ABCD by its diameter AC,
     as the triangles ABC and ACD together. -/
  -- Then the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle EBC;
  -- for it is on the same base BC with it and in the same parallels BC, AE. [I. 37]
  have hEBC : Triangle E B C :=
    (Triangle.of_line hB hC hABCD.2.1 (hpar.not_onLine hE_AE)).cab
  have h37 : △ A B C = △ E B C :=
    Prop37 hABCD.triangle hEBC ⟨AE, BC, hpar, hA_AE, hE_AE, hB, hC⟩
  -- But the parallelogram ABCD is double of the triangle ABC;
  -- for the diameter AC bisects it; [I. 34]
  have h34 : quadArea A B C D = △ A B C + △ A B C := Prop34.bisect hABCD
  -- so that the parallelogram ABCD is also double of the triangle EBC.
  rw [h34, h37, area_bac E B C]
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.

/-- In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the
diameter bisects the areas. -/
theorem Prop34 {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A C D B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ C D B ∧ ∠ A B D = ∠ A C D ∧
      △ A B C = △ D C B
bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34.bisect:
/-- The diameter bisects the parallelogram, said of its area: the parallelogram
ABCD, measured by its diameter AC, is double the triangle ABC. I.35–I.47 cite
I.34 for this ("the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram EBCA; for the diameter
AB bisects it"). To halve by the other diameter, name the parallelogram from the
next corner (`Parallelogram.rotate`) and turn its area round with
`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`. [I. 34] -/
theorem Prop34.bisect {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea A B C D = △ A B C + △ A B C
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.cross:
/-- The diameters of a parallelogram cross: in the parallelogram ABCD, some point
lies between A and C and between B and D. Its sides AB and DC are
parallel, so they do not cross, and `AreParallel.cross_or` leaves only the
diameters. -/
theorem Parallelogram.cross (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    ∃ X : Point, Between A X C ∧ Between B X D
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate:
/-- A parallelogram has the same area whichever diameter cuts it: the parallelogram
ABCD measured by BD, as BCDA, is the same as measured by AC. -/
theorem Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea B C D A = quadArea A B C D

state.commentary:
Joining AC, Euclid needs just two steps: I.37 slides the triangle's vertex from E to A along the parallel, and the diameter AC halves the parallelogram, by I.34. He uses the result at once. I.42 builds a parallelogram equal to a triangle with it, and in I.47 it makes each square on the sides, and each piece of the square on the base, double of a triangle. Our figure is Euclid's, with E on AD produced beyond D, but our statement lets E fall anywhere on the straight line AD, at A or at D among them. One argument serves for all, since our I.37 was stated with those cases in mind, and joining AC costs nothing: our area of a four-sided figure is already measured by a diameter.

On this proposition, Heath reports, Proclus considers "the area of a *trapezium* (a quadrilateral with only one pair of opposite sides parallel)", and proves this: "*If a triangle be formed by joining the middle point of either of the non-parallel sides to the extremities of the opposite side, the area of the trapezium is always double of that of the triangle*" (vol. 1, p. 338). He produces a straight line from one end of the opposite side through the middle point until it meets the other parallel side, produced; the two small triangles at the middle point are equal (I.26), so the trapezium is equal to one large triangle, and the triangle of the theorem is half of it, by I.38 (Heath, vol. 1, p. 339). The end of his note is lost, as Heath remarks under I.43.
state.heath_proof:
For let the parallelogram ABCD have the same base BC with the triangle EBC, and let it be in the same parallels BC, AE;

I say that the parallelogram ABCD is double of the triangle BEC.

For let AC be joined.

Then the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle EBC; for it is on the same base BC with it and in the same parallels BC, AE. [I. 37]

But the parallelogram ABCD is double of the triangle ABC; for the diameter AC bisects it; [I. 34] so that the parallelogram ABCD is also double of the triangle EBC.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- If a parallelogram have the same base with a triangle and be in the same parallels, the
parallelogram is double of the triangle. -/
theorem Prop41 {A B C D E : Point} (hABCD : Parallelogram A B C D) (hE : Collinear A D E) :
    quadArea A B C D = △ B E C + △ B E C := by
  -- For let the parallelogram ABCD have the same base BC with the triangle EBC,
  -- and let it be in the same parallels BC, AE;
  obtain ⟨AE, hA_AE, hD_AE, hE_AE⟩ := hE
  obtain ⟨BC, hB, hC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hABCD.2.1
  have hpar : Parallel AE BC := (hABCD.2.parallel hB hC hD_AE hA_AE).symm
  -- I say that the parallelogram ABCD is double of the triangle BEC.
  -- For let AC be joined.
  /- The area `quadArea A B C D` already measures ABCD by its diameter AC,
     as the triangles ABC and ACD together. -/
  -- Then the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle EBC;
  -- for it is on the same base BC with it and in the same parallels BC, AE. [I. 37]
  have hEBC : Triangle E B C :=
    (Triangle.of_line hB hC hABCD.2.1 (hpar.not_onLine hE_AE)).cab
  have h37 : △ A B C = △ E B C :=
    Prop37 hABCD.triangle hEBC ⟨AE, BC, hpar, hA_AE, hE_AE, hB, hC⟩
  -- But the parallelogram ABCD is double of the triangle ABC;
  -- for the diameter AC bisects it; [I. 34]
  have h34 : quadArea A B C D = △ A B C + △ A B C := Prop34.bisect hABCD
  -- so that the parallelogram ABCD is also double of the triangle EBC.
  rw [h34, h37, area_bac E B C]
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.

state.enunciation: To construct, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given triangle.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABC be the given triangle, and D the given rectilineal angle; thus it is required to construct in the rectilineal angle D a parallelogram equal to the triangle ABC.

Let BC be bisected at E, and let AE be joined; on the straight line EC, and at the point E on it, let the angle CEF be constructed equal to the angle D; [I. 23] through A let AG be drawn parallel to EC, and [I. 31] through C let CG be drawn parallel to EF.

Then FECG is a parallelogram.

And, since BE is equal to EC, the triangle ABE is also equal to the triangle AEC, for they are on equal bases BE, EC and in the same parallels BC, AG; [I. 38] therefore the triangle ABC is double of the triangle AEC.

But the parallelogram FECG is also double of the triangle AEC, for it has the same base with it and is in the same parallels with it; [I. 41] therefore the parallelogram FECG is equal to the triangle ABC.

And it has the angle CEF equal to the given angle D.

Therefore the parallelogram FECG has been constructed equal to the given triangle ABC, in the angle CEF which is equal to D.

Q. E. F.

      ∠ C E F = ∠ D₁ D D₂ ∧ quadArea F E C G = △ A B C

diameter bisects the areas. -/
theorem Prop34 {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A C D B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ C D B ∧ ∠ A B D = ∠ A C D ∧
      △ A B C = △ D C B
bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34.bisect:
/-- The diameter bisects the parallelogram, said of its area: the parallelogram
ABCD, measured by its diameter AC, is double the triangle ABC. I.35–I.47 cite
I.34 for this ("the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram EBCA; for the diameter
AB bisects it"). To halve by the other diameter, name the parallelogram from the
next corner (`Parallelogram.rotate`) and turn its area round with
`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`. [I. 34] -/
theorem Prop34.bisect {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea A B C D = △ A B C + △ A B C
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.cross:
/-- The diameters of a parallelogram cross: in the parallelogram ABCD, some point
lies between A and C and between B and D. Its sides AB and DC are
parallel, so they do not cross, and `AreParallel.cross_or` leaves only the
diameters. -/
theorem Parallelogram.cross (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    ∃ X : Point, Between A X C ∧ Between B X D
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate:
/-- A parallelogram has the same area whichever diameter cuts it: the parallelogram
ABCD measured by BD, as BCDA, is the same as measured by AC. -/
theorem Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea B C D A = quadArea A B C D

Elements.Parallelogram.cross: variable {A B C D E F X A' B' C' : Point} {L M N L₁ L₃ : Line}
Elements.Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate: variable {A B C D E F X A' B' C' : Point} {L M N L₁ L₃ : Line}

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
