state.enunciation: To construct, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given triangle.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABC be the given triangle, and D the given rectilineal angle; thus it is required to construct in the rectilineal angle D a parallelogram equal to the triangle ABC.

Let BC be bisected at E, and let AE be joined; on the straight line EC, and at the point E on it, let the angle CEF be constructed equal to the angle D; [I. 23] through A let AG be drawn parallel to EC, and [I. 31] through C let CG be drawn parallel to EF.

Then FECG is a parallelogram.

And, since BE is equal to EC, the triangle ABE is also equal to the triangle AEC, for they are on equal bases BE, EC and in the same parallels BC, AG; [I. 38] therefore the triangle ABC is double of the triangle AEC.

But the parallelogram FECG is also double of the triangle AEC, for it has the same base with it and is in the same parallels with it; [I. 41] therefore the parallelogram FECG is equal to the triangle ABC.

And it has the angle CEF equal to the given angle D.

Therefore the parallelogram FECG has been constructed equal to the given triangle ABC, in the angle CEF which is equal to D.

Q. E. F.
state.lean_proof:
/-- To construct, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given triangle. -/
theorem Prop42 {A B C D₁ D D₂ : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hD : Triangle D₁ D D₂) :
    ∃ E F G : Point, Between B E C ∧ SameSideOf F A B C ∧ Parallelogram F E C G ∧
      ∠ C E F = ∠ D₁ D D₂ ∧ quadArea F E C G = △ A B C := by
  -- Let ABC be the given triangle, and D the given rectilineal angle; thus it is required to
  -- construct in the rectilineal angle D a parallelogram equal to the triangle ABC.
  -- Let BC be bisected at E,
  obtain ⟨E, hBEC, hBE⟩ := Prop10 hABC.ne₂₃
  obtain ⟨BC, hB, hC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hABC.ne₂₃
  have hA_BC : ¬ OnLine A BC := hABC.bca.off_line hB hC
  have hE : OnLine E BC := on_line_of_between_ends hBEC hB hC
  have hEC : E ≠ C := (ne_of_between (between_symm hBEC)).symm
  -- and let AE be joined;
  /- The triangles ABE and AEC are named by their corners; the join needs no
     further object in Lean. -/
  -- on the straight line EC, and at the point E on it, let the angle CEF be constructed equal
  -- to the angle D; [I. 23]
  have hECA : Triangle E C A := Triangle.of_line hE hC hEC hA_BC
  obtain ⟨F₁, C₁, hC₁, hF₁, hang⟩ := Prop23 hEC hD hECA
  /- C₁ lies on the ray EC, and F₁ on A's side of EC. The parallel through A
     will determine F on the ray from E through F₁. -/
  -- through A let AG be drawn parallel to EC, and [I. 31]
  obtain ⟨AG, hA_AG, hAG⟩ := Prop31.line hA_BC
  /- The straight line through E and F₁ meets AG by I.30. Both F and F₁ lie on
     A's side of BC, so F is on the constructed ray. -/
  have hEF₁ : E ≠ F₁ := hF₁.triangle.ne₁₃
  obtain ⟨EF, hE_EF, hF₁_EF⟩ := Postulate1 E F₁ hEF₁
  have hEF_BC : EF ≠ BC := fun e => (hF₁.triangle.off_line hE hC) (e ▸ hF₁_EF)
  obtain ⟨F, hF_EF, hF_AG⟩ := Prop30.meet hAG hE hE_EF hEF_BC
  have hFA : SameSide F A BC := hAG.sameSide hF_AG hA_AG
  have hFE : F ≠ E := fun e => hAG.not_onLine hF_AG (e ▸ hE)
  have hFray : OnRay F E F₁ :=
    OnRay.of_sameSideOf ((SameSideOf.of_line hEC hE hC hFA).trans hF₁.symm)
      ⟨EF, hE_EF, hF₁_EF, hF_EF⟩ hFE
  -- through C let CG be drawn parallel to EF.
  /- It meets AG at G (`Prop31.parallelogram`). -/
  obtain ⟨G, hG_AG, hpar⟩ := Prop31.parallelogram hAG hF_AG hE hC hEC
  -- Then FECG is a parallelogram.
  have hFECG : Parallelogram F E C G := hpar
  -- And, since BE is equal to EC, the triangle ABE is also equal to the triangle AEC, for they
  -- are on equal bases BE, EC and in the same parallels BC, AG; [I. 38]
  have hABE : Triangle A B E := (Triangle.of_line hB hE (ne_of_between hBEC) hA_BC).cab
  have hAEC : Triangle A E C := hECA.cab
  have h38 : △ A B E = △ A E C :=
    Prop38 hABE hAEC hBE ⟨AG, BC, hAG, hA_AG, hA_AG, hB, hE, hE, hC⟩
  -- therefore the triangle ABC is double of the triangle AEC.
  have hABC_double : △ A B C = △ A E C + △ A E C := by
    rw [← area_cut (A := A) hBEC, h38]
  -- But the parallelogram FECG is also double of the triangle AEC, for it has the same base
  -- with it and is in the same parallels with it; [I. 41]
  have h41 : quadArea F E C G = △ E A C + △ E A C :=
    Prop41 hFECG ⟨AG, hF_AG, hG_AG, hA_AG⟩
  have hFECG_double : quadArea F E C G = △ A E C + △ A E C := by
    rw [h41, ← area_bac A E C]
  -- therefore the parallelogram FECG is equal to the triangle ABC.
  have hequal : quadArea F E C G = △ A B C := CommonNotion1 hFECG_double hABC_double
  -- And it has the angle CEF equal to the given angle D.
  have hCEF : ∠ C E F = ∠ D₁ D D₂ :=
    (angle_eq_of_onRay hC₁.symm hFray).trans ((angle_symm hC₁.2.1 hEF₁.symm).trans hang)
  -- Therefore the parallelogram FECG has been constructed equal to the given triangle ABC, in
  -- the angle CEF which is equal to D.
  exact ⟨E, F, G, hBEC, SameSideOf.of_line hABC.ne₂₃ hB hC hFA, hFECG, hCEF, hequal⟩
  -- Q. E. F.

helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.symm:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then CD is parallel to AB. -/
theorem AreParallel.symm (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.triangle:
/-- An end of one parallel is off the other: if AB is parallel to CD, then C
is not on the straight line AB, and ABC is a triangle. (Turned round with
`AreParallel.symm` and `.swap_right`, the same holds of D, and of A and B
beside CD.) -/
theorem AreParallel.triangle (h : AreParallel A B C D) : Triangle A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop10:
/-- To bisect a given finite straight line. -/
theorem Prop10 {A B : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) :
    ∃ D : Point, Between A D B ∧ ‖A D‖ = ‖D B‖
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop23:
/-- On a given straight line and at a point on it to construct a rectilineal angle equal to a given
rectilineal angle. -/
theorem Prop23 {A B C D E P : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hDCE : Triangle D C E) (hP : ¬ Collinear A B P) :
    ∃ F G : Point, OnRay G A B ∧ SameSideOf F P A B ∧ ∠ F A G = ∠ D C E
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30:
/-- Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another. -/
theorem Prop30 {A B C D E F : Point} (h₁ : AreParallel A B E F) (h₂ : AreParallel C D E F)
    (hC : ¬ Collinear A B C) :
    AreParallel A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30.meet:
/-- A straight line meeting one of two parallels meets the other. If L is parallel
to M, and a straight line N, other than M, passes through a point P of M,
then N meets L. Otherwise N would be parallel to L too, and by I.30 M and
N would be parallel to one another, though both pass through P.

Euclid uses this whenever he draws a parallel and then names the point where it
meets another straight line: E and F in I.37, G and H in I.38, E in I.39,
F in I.40, F and G in I.42, H, L and M in I.44, E in I.46 and L in
I.47. It is the uniqueness of the parallel through a point, often called
Playfair's axiom; Heath reports under I.31 that Proclus draws it from I.30.
`Prop30.unique`, a step inside I.30's own proof, gives the same uniqueness from
I.29; later proofs cite this one, Proclus' route through I.30. [I. 30] -/
theorem Prop30.meet {L M N : Line} {P : Point} (hLM : Parallel L M) (hPM : OnLine P M)
    (hPN : OnLine P N) (hNM : N ≠ M) : ∃ Q : Point, OnLine Q N ∧ OnLine Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31:
/-- Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line. -/
theorem Prop31 {A B C : Point} (hBC : B ≠ C) (hA : ¬ Collinear B C A) :
    ∃ E F : Point, Between E A F ∧ AreParallel E F B C
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31.line:
/-- I.31 said of straight lines drawn and named: through a point A off the
straight line L there is a straight line K parallel to L. I.31 gives two points
of it, one on either side of A, and Postulate 1 joins them. [I. 31] -/
theorem Prop31.line {A : Point} {L : Line} (hA : ¬ OnLine A L) :
    ∃ K : Line, OnLine A K ∧ Parallel K L
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31.parallelogram:
/-- Completing the parallelogram. If X lies on L, and Y and Z on M, which is
parallel to L, the straight line drawn through Z parallel to XY [I. 31] meets
L at a point W (`Prop30.meet`), and XYZW is a parallelogram. Euclid draws such
a parallel in I.37, I.38, I.42, I.44 and I.46, and reads the point where it meets
L, and the parallelogram, off his figure. [I. 30, I. 31] -/
theorem Prop31.parallelogram {X Y Z : Point} {L M : Line} (hLM : Parallel L M)
    (hX : OnLine X L) (hY : OnLine Y M) (hZ : OnLine Z M) (hYZ : Y ≠ Z) :
    ∃ W : Point, OnLine W L ∧ Parallelogram X Y Z W
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop38:
/-- Triangles which are on equal bases and in the same parallels are equal to one another. -/
theorem Prop38 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hbase : ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖)
    (hpar : ∃ L M : Line, Parallel L M ∧ OnLine A L ∧ OnLine D L ∧
      OnLine B M ∧ OnLine C M ∧ OnLine E M ∧ OnLine F M) :
    △ A B C = △ D E F
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop41:
/-- If a parallelogram have the same base with a triangle and be in the same parallels, the
parallelogram is double of the triangle. -/
theorem Prop41 {A B C D E : Point} (hABCD : Parallelogram A B C D) (hE : Collinear A D E) :
    quadArea A B C D = △ B E C + △ B E C
helper_signatures.Elements.CommonNotion1:
/-- **Common Notion 1.** Things which are equal to the same thing are also equal
to one another. -/
theorem CommonNotion1 {α : Sort _} {a b c : α} (h₁ : a = c) (h₂ : b = c) : a = b
helper_signatures.Elements.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.of_sameSideOf:
/-- Going the other way: a point P of the straight line DF, other than D, and
on the same side of the straight line DE as F, is on the ray from D through
F. It is not behind D, for then DE would separate it from F (System E,
Pasch 3). -/
theorem OnRay.of_sameSideOf {D E F P : Point} (h : SameSideOf P F D E) (hP : Collinear D F P)
    (hPD : P ≠ D) : OnRay P D F
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.symm:
/-- P is on the ray from A through B exactly when B is on the ray from A
through P: they are one and the same ray. -/
theorem OnRay.symm (h : OnRay P A B) : OnRay B A P
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.not_onLine:
/-- Parallels do not meet: a point of L is not on M. -/
theorem Parallel.not_onLine (h : Parallel L M) (hP : OnLine P L) : ¬ OnLine P M
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.sameSide:
/-- All the points of one parallel lie on one side of the other: two points of L
are on the same side of M. Were they on opposite sides, the straight line L
joining them would cross M (System E, Intersection 1). -/
theorem Parallel.sameSide (h : Parallel L M) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L) :
    SameSide P Q M
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.symm:
/-- If L is parallel to M, then M is parallel to L. -/
theorem Parallel.symm (h : Parallel L M) : Parallel M L
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.triangle:
/-- In the parallelogram ABCD, the corner C is off the straight line AB, so
ABC is a triangle. -/
theorem Parallelogram.triangle (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Triangle A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate1:
/-- **Postulate 1.** To draw a straight line from any point to any point. -/
axiom Postulate1 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf:
/-- `P` and `Q` lie on the same side of the straight line `AB`. -/
def SameSideOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.of_line:
/-- Two points on the same side of a straight line L through A and B are on
the same side of the straight line AB, however that line is named: two points
fix one straight line. -/
theorem SameSideOf.of_line (hAB : A ≠ B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (h : SameSide P Q L) : SameSideOf P Q A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.sameSide:
/-- Two points on the same side of the straight line AB are on the same side of
any straight line drawn through A and B. -/
theorem SameSideOf.sameSide (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    SameSide P Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the same side of AB as Q, then Q is on the same side as P. -/
theorem SameSideOf.symm (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.trans:
/-- Points on the same side as a third are on the same side as each other. -/
theorem SameSideOf.trans (h₁ : SameSideOf P Q A B) (h₂ : SameSideOf Q R A B) :
    SameSideOf P R A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.triangle:
/-- A point on one side of the straight line AB is not on it, so ABP is a
triangle. -/
theorem SameSideOf.triangle (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : Triangle A B P
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.angle_symm:
/-- The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4) -/
axiom angle_symm (hAB : A ≠ B) (hCB : C ≠ B) : ∠ A B C = ∠ C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_symm:
/-- If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1) -/
axiom between_symm (h : Between A B C) : Between C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between:
/-- A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between_ends:
/-- A straight line through A and C passes through every point between them.
(Between 3) -/
axiom on_line_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hC : OnLine C L) :
    OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.bca:
/-- The triangle ABC, named from B, as BCA. -/
theorem Triangle.bca (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle B C A
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.cab:
/-- The triangle ABC, named from C, as CAB. -/
theorem Triangle.cab (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle C A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₁₃:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₁₃ (h : Triangle A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₂₃:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₂₃ (h : Triangle A B C) : B ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.of_line:

/-- In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the
diameter bisects the areas. -/
theorem Prop34 {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A C D B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ C D B ∧ ∠ A B D = ∠ A C D ∧
      △ A B C = △ D C B
bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34.bisect:
/-- The diameter bisects the parallelogram, said of its area: the parallelogram
ABCD, measured by its diameter AC, is double the triangle ABC. I.35–I.47 cite
I.34 for this ("the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram EBCA; for the diameter
AB bisects it"). To halve by the other diameter, name the parallelogram from the
next corner (`Parallelogram.rotate`) and turn its area round with
`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`. [I. 34] -/
theorem Prop34.bisect {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea A B C D = △ A B C + △ A B C
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.cross:
/-- The diameters of a parallelogram cross: in the parallelogram ABCD, some point
lies between A and C and between B and D. Its sides AB and DC are
parallel, so they do not cross, and `AreParallel.cross_or` leaves only the
diameters. -/
theorem Parallelogram.cross (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    ∃ X : Point, Between A X C ∧ Between B X D
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate:
/-- A parallelogram has the same area whichever diameter cuts it: the parallelogram
ABCD measured by BD, as BCDA, is the same as measured by AC. -/
theorem Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea B C D A = quadArea A B C D

state.commentary:
Here Euclid turns a triangle into a parallelogram of the same size, in any angle he is given. He halves the base BC at E (Heath gives no reference here: it is I.10) and builds the parallelogram FECG on EC, in the given angle and between the same parallels as the triangle. FECG is double of the triangle AEC, by I.41; so is ABC, since its halves ABE and AEC are equal, by I.38. I.44 will carry such a parallelogram onto any straight line, and I.45 will make one equal to any rectilineal figure, any figure bounded by straight lines.

**Why are the two doubles equal?** Euclid gives no reason. Some manuscripts give this a Common Notion of its own, that things double of the same thing are equal; Proclus excludes it, Heath reports, because it follows from Common Notion 1 (vol. 1, p. 223). We follow Proclus: each double is AEC added to itself, and Common Notion 1 makes them equal. Heath, agreeing with Paul Tannery, sees no reason to strike out the like words in I.47: "If they were interpolated, we should have expected to find the same interpolation in I. 42, where the axiom is *tacitly* assumed" (vol. 1, p. 224).

Our I.23 makes the angle at E on A's side of EC, and F is where its arm, produced, meets the parallel through A. F lies on A's side of BC, so `OnRay.of_sameSideOf` puts it on the arm itself, and CEF is the very angle I.23 made. A may fall at F or at G, for I.41 asks only that A lie on the straight line FG.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABC be the given triangle, and D the given rectilineal angle; thus it is required to construct in the rectilineal angle D a parallelogram equal to the triangle ABC.

Let BC be bisected at E, and let AE be joined; on the straight line EC, and at the point E on it, let the angle CEF be constructed equal to the angle D; [I. 23] through A let AG be drawn parallel to EC, and [I. 31] through C let CG be drawn parallel to EF.

Then FECG is a parallelogram.

And, since BE is equal to EC, the triangle ABE is also equal to the triangle AEC, for they are on equal bases BE, EC and in the same parallels BC, AG; [I. 38] therefore the triangle ABC is double of the triangle AEC.

But the parallelogram FECG is also double of the triangle AEC, for it has the same base with it and is in the same parallels with it; [I. 41] therefore the parallelogram FECG is equal to the triangle ABC.

And it has the angle CEF equal to the given angle D.

Therefore the parallelogram FECG has been constructed equal to the given triangle ABC, in the angle CEF which is equal to D.

Q. E. F.
state.lean_proof:
/-- To construct, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given triangle. -/
theorem Prop42 {A B C D₁ D D₂ : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hD : Triangle D₁ D D₂) :
    ∃ E F G : Point, Between B E C ∧ SameSideOf F A B C ∧ Parallelogram F E C G ∧
      ∠ C E F = ∠ D₁ D D₂ ∧ quadArea F E C G = △ A B C := by
  -- Let ABC be the given triangle, and D the given rectilineal angle; thus it is required to
  -- construct in the rectilineal angle D a parallelogram equal to the triangle ABC.
  -- Let BC be bisected at E,
  obtain ⟨E, hBEC, hBE⟩ := Prop10 hABC.ne₂₃
  obtain ⟨BC, hB, hC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hABC.ne₂₃
  have hA_BC : ¬ OnLine A BC := hABC.bca.off_line hB hC
  have hE : OnLine E BC := on_line_of_between_ends hBEC hB hC
  have hEC : E ≠ C := (ne_of_between (between_symm hBEC)).symm
  -- and let AE be joined;
  /- The triangles ABE and AEC are named by their corners; the join needs no
     further object in Lean. -/
  -- on the straight line EC, and at the point E on it, let the angle CEF be constructed equal
  -- to the angle D; [I. 23]
  have hECA : Triangle E C A := Triangle.of_line hE hC hEC hA_BC
  obtain ⟨F₁, C₁, hC₁, hF₁, hang⟩ := Prop23 hEC hD hECA
  /- C₁ lies on the ray EC, and F₁ on A's side of EC. The parallel through A
     will determine F on the ray from E through F₁. -/
  -- through A let AG be drawn parallel to EC, and [I. 31]
  obtain ⟨AG, hA_AG, hAG⟩ := Prop31.line hA_BC
  /- The straight line through E and F₁ meets AG by I.30. Both F and F₁ lie on
     A's side of BC, so F is on the constructed ray. -/
  have hEF₁ : E ≠ F₁ := hF₁.triangle.ne₁₃
  obtain ⟨EF, hE_EF, hF₁_EF⟩ := Postulate1 E F₁ hEF₁
  have hEF_BC : EF ≠ BC := fun e => (hF₁.triangle.off_line hE hC) (e ▸ hF₁_EF)
  obtain ⟨F, hF_EF, hF_AG⟩ := Prop30.meet hAG hE hE_EF hEF_BC
  have hFA : SameSide F A BC := hAG.sameSide hF_AG hA_AG
  have hFE : F ≠ E := fun e => hAG.not_onLine hF_AG (e ▸ hE)
  have hFray : OnRay F E F₁ :=
    OnRay.of_sameSideOf ((SameSideOf.of_line hEC hE hC hFA).trans hF₁.symm)
      ⟨EF, hE_EF, hF₁_EF, hF_EF⟩ hFE
  -- through C let CG be drawn parallel to EF.
  /- It meets AG at G (`Prop31.parallelogram`). -/
  obtain ⟨G, hG_AG, hpar⟩ := Prop31.parallelogram hAG hF_AG hE hC hEC
  -- Then FECG is a parallelogram.
  have hFECG : Parallelogram F E C G := hpar
  -- And, since BE is equal to EC, the triangle ABE is also equal to the triangle AEC, for they
  -- are on equal bases BE, EC and in the same parallels BC, AG; [I. 38]
  have hABE : Triangle A B E := (Triangle.of_line hB hE (ne_of_between hBEC) hA_BC).cab
  have hAEC : Triangle A E C := hECA.cab
  have h38 : △ A B E = △ A E C :=
    Prop38 hABE hAEC hBE ⟨AG, BC, hAG, hA_AG, hA_AG, hB, hE, hE, hC⟩
  -- therefore the triangle ABC is double of the triangle AEC.
  have hABC_double : △ A B C = △ A E C + △ A E C := by
    rw [← area_cut (A := A) hBEC, h38]
  -- But the parallelogram FECG is also double of the triangle AEC, for it has the same base
  -- with it and is in the same parallels with it; [I. 41]
  have h41 : quadArea F E C G = △ E A C + △ E A C :=
    Prop41 hFECG ⟨AG, hF_AG, hG_AG, hA_AG⟩
  have hFECG_double : quadArea F E C G = △ A E C + △ A E C := by
    rw [h41, ← area_bac A E C]
  -- therefore the parallelogram FECG is equal to the triangle ABC.
  have hequal : quadArea F E C G = △ A B C := CommonNotion1 hFECG_double hABC_double
  -- And it has the angle CEF equal to the given angle D.
  have hCEF : ∠ C E F = ∠ D₁ D D₂ :=
    (angle_eq_of_onRay hC₁.symm hFray).trans ((angle_symm hC₁.2.1 hEF₁.symm).trans hang)
  -- Therefore the parallelogram FECG has been constructed equal to the given triangle ABC, in
  -- the angle CEF which is equal to D.
  exact ⟨E, F, G, hBEC, SameSideOf.of_line hABC.ne₂₃ hB hC hFA, hFECG, hCEF, hequal⟩
  -- Q. E. F.

theorem Prop42 {A B C D₁ D D₂ : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hD : Triangle D₁ D D₂) :
    ∃ E F G : Point, Between B E C ∧ SameSideOf F A B C ∧ Parallelogram F E C G ∧

state.enunciation: To construct, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given triangle.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABC be the given triangle, and D the given rectilineal angle; thus it is required to construct in the rectilineal angle D a parallelogram equal to the triangle ABC.

Let BC be bisected at E, and let AE be joined; on the straight line EC, and at the point E on it, let the angle CEF be constructed equal to the angle D; [I. 23] through A let AG be drawn parallel to EC, and [I. 31] through C let CG be drawn parallel to EF.

Then FECG is a parallelogram.

And, since BE is equal to EC, the triangle ABE is also equal to the triangle AEC, for they are on equal bases BE, EC and in the same parallels BC, AG; [I. 38] therefore the triangle ABC is double of the triangle AEC.

But the parallelogram FECG is also double of the triangle AEC, for it has the same base with it and is in the same parallels with it; [I. 41] therefore the parallelogram FECG is equal to the triangle ABC.

And it has the angle CEF equal to the given angle D.

Therefore the parallelogram FECG has been constructed equal to the given triangle ABC, in the angle CEF which is equal to D.

Q. E. F.

`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`. [I. 34] -/

    quadArea A B C D = △ A B C + △ A B C

state.heath_proof:
Let ABCD be a parallelogram, and AC its diameter; and about AC let EH, FG be parallelograms, and BK, KD the so-called complements;

I say that the complement BK is equal to the complement KD.

For, since ABCD is a parallelogram, and AC its diameter, the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle ACD. [I. 34]

Again, since EH is a parallelogram, and AK is its diameter, the triangle AEK is equal to the triangle AHK.

For the same reason the triangle KFC is also equal to KGC.

Now, since the triangle AEK is equal to the triangle AHK, and KFC to KGC, the triangle AEK together with KGC is equal to the triangle AHK together with KFC. [C.N. 2]

And the whole triangle ABC is also equal to the whole ADC; therefore the complement BK which remains is equal to the complement KD which remains. [C.N. 3]

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- In any parallelogram the complements of the parallelograms about the diameter are equal to one
another. -/
theorem Prop43 {A B C D E F G H K : Point} (hABCD : Parallelogram A B C D) (hK : Between A K C)
    (hE : Between A E B) (hG : Between B G C) (hF : Between C F D) (hH : Between D H A)
    (hEH : Parallelogram A E K H) (hFG : Parallelogram K G C F) :
    quadArea E B G K = quadArea H K F D := by
  -- Let ABCD be a parallelogram, and AC its diameter; and about AC let EH, FG be
  -- parallelograms, and BK, KD the so-called complements;
  -- I say that the complement BK is equal to the complement KD.
  -- For, since ABCD is a parallelogram, and AC its diameter, the triangle ABC is equal to the
  -- triangle ACD. [I. 34]
  have hABC_ACD : △ A B C = △ A C D := by
    have h := (Prop34 (A := B) (B := A) (C := C) (D := D) hABCD.rotate).2.2.2.2
    rw [area_bac B A C, area_cba D C A] at h
    exact h
  -- Again, since EH is a parallelogram, and AK is its diameter, the triangle AEK is equal to
  -- the triangle AHK.
  have hAEK_AHK : △ A E K = △ A H K := by
    have h := (Prop34 (A := E) (B := A) (C := K) (D := H) hEH.rotate).2.2.2.2
    rw [area_bac E A K, area_cab H K A] at h
    exact h
  -- For the same reason the triangle KFC is also equal to KGC.
  have hKFC_KGC : △ K F C = △ K G C := by
    have h := (Prop34 (A := G) (B := K) (C := C) (D := F) hFG.rotate).2.2.2.2
    rw [area_bac G K C, area_cab F C K] at h
    exact h.symm
  -- Now, since the triangle AEK is equal to the triangle AHK, and KFC to KGC, the triangle AEK
  -- together with KGC is equal to the triangle AHK together with KFC. [C.N. 2]
  have hsum : △ A E K + △ K G C = △ A H K + △ K F C :=
    CommonNotion2 hAEK_AHK hKFC_KGC.symm
  -- And the whole triangle ABC is also equal to the whole ADC; therefore the complement BK
  -- which remains is equal to the complement KD which remains. [C.N. 3]
  have hABC_ADC : △ A B C = △ A D C := hABC_ACD.trans (area_acb A C D)
  have hABC := Prop43.cut hABCD.triangle hK hE hG
  have hADC := Prop43.cut hABCD.reverse.triangle hK (between_symm hH) (between_symm hF)
  rw [quadArea_reverse H K F D] at hADC
  refine CommonNotion3 (c := △ A E K + △ K G C) (d := △ A H K + △ K F C) ?_ hsum
  calc
    quadArea E B G K + (△ A E K + △ K G C) = △ A B C := by rw [hABC]; ac_rfl
    _ = △ A D C := hABC_ADC
    _ = quadArea H K F D + (△ A H K + △ K F C) := by rw [hADC]; ac_rfl
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D

question.instructions:
Does every proposition called by the proof unit in `lean_proof` do work towards its conclusion or a substantive intermediate step of Euclid's argument? Also check for artificial hypothesis uses. Judge this unit's uses of the supplied helper signatures; helper bodies are outside this question. Heath's sentences stand as `--` lines and `cited` gives exact enunciations. In Lean, `have h : T := p` proves T by p and calls the result h; `obtain ⟨…⟩ := p` takes p apart into named pieces; `rw [h34, h37, …]` rewrites the goal by the equalities named. Follow uses through helper calls and tactics as well as explicit names. An anonymous binding or an unused hypothesis alone does not establish a defect. If both defects occur, choose `a dummy citation`.

criteria.a dummy citation: Some proposition call does no substantive work: its result neither supports the argument nor establishes a substantive intermediate fact, and merely supplies a citation while the step is done another way.
criteria.an artificial hypothesis use: No dummy citation is established, but a hypothesis is mentioned only so that it looks used, and does no substantive work.
criteria.cannot tell: What is given here is not enough to decide.
criteria.all do work: Every proposition call supports a later step or the conclusion, or establishes a substantive intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid. No hypothesis is mentioned merely to look used. With no proposition calls the citation part alone is vacuous; hypothesis use must still be inspected.

bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34:
/-- In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the
diameter bisects the areas. -/
theorem Prop34 {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A C D B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ C D B ∧ ∠ A B D = ∠ A C D ∧
      △ A B C = △ D C B
bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34.bisect:
/-- The diameter bisects the parallelogram, said of its area: the parallelogram
ABCD, measured by its diameter AC, is double the triangle ABC. I.35–I.47 cite
I.34 for this ("the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram EBCA; for the diameter
AB bisects it"). To halve by the other diameter, name the parallelogram from the
next corner (`Parallelogram.rotate`) and turn its area round with
`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`. [I. 34] -/
theorem Prop34.bisect {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea A B C D = △ A B C + △ A B C
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.cross:
/-- The diameters of a parallelogram cross: in the parallelogram ABCD, some point
lies between A and C and between B and D. Its sides AB and DC are
parallel, so they do not cross, and `AreParallel.cross_or` leaves only the
diameters. -/
theorem Parallelogram.cross (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    ∃ X : Point, Between A X C ∧ Between B X D
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate:
/-- A parallelogram has the same area whichever diameter cuts it: the parallelogram
ABCD measured by BD, as BCDA, is the same as measured by AC. -/
theorem Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea B C D A = quadArea A B C D

state.commentary:
About the diameter AC of the parallelogram ABCD stand two smaller parallelograms, EH and FG, meeting at a point K of AC, and the complements BK and KD fill up the rest. Their Greek name means, in Heath's rendering, "the figures put in to fill up (interstices)", and Euclid's "so-called" tells Heath that the term "was not new, though it might not be universally known" (vol. 1, p. 341). The proof is I.34 three times over: AC halves ABCD, AK halves EH, and KC halves FG. Common Notion 2 adds the two small halves on each side of AC, Common Notion 3 takes them from the halves of the whole, and the complements are left equal. I.44 is built on this.

Euclid takes for granted that the triangle ABC is made up of the triangle AEK, the complement BK and the triangle KGC, so that BK is what remains. We prove it from the order of the points alone (`Prop43.cut`). Our area of a four-sided figure is measured along a diameter, while the cut runs along the other one, BK; but the two diameters of the complement cross, at a point Euclid never needed to name, so either will do, and the proof of the cut never uses that the complements are parallelograms.

**Must the complements be parallelograms?** In Euclid's figure the parallelograms about the diameter meet at K, and our statement asks for that. Proclus lets them stand apart or overlap, and then, Heath notes, "the complements need not be parallelograms" (vol. 1, p. 341): apart, they have five sides; overlapping, each is, as Heath counts it, a parallelogram less a triangle. Proclus says Euclid needed no definition of a complement, the name being "simply suggested by the facts", and Heath sums up: "In all the cases it is easy to show, as Proclus does, that the complements are still equal" (vol. 1, p. 341).

**The modern way.** Put A at the origin, with $\vec{u} = \mathrm{B - A}$, $\vec{v} = \mathrm{D - A}$ and $\mathrm{K} = s\vec{u} + t\vec{v}$, where $s$ and $t$ lie between $0$ and $1$. With the cross product of [I.35](35.md), the complements BK and KD have areas $(1 - s)t\lvert\vec{u} \times \vec{v}\rvert$ and $s(1 - t)\lvert\vec{u} \times \vec{v}\rvert$, equal exactly when $s = t$, that is, when K lies on AC. Euclid proves that K on AC makes them equal; the converse is not his.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABCD be a parallelogram, and AC its diameter; and about AC let EH, FG be parallelograms, and BK, KD the so-called complements;

I say that the complement BK is equal to the complement KD.

For, since ABCD is a parallelogram, and AC its diameter, the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle ACD. [I. 34]

Again, since EH is a parallelogram, and AK is its diameter, the triangle AEK is equal to the triangle AHK.

For the same reason the triangle KFC is also equal to KGC.

Now, since the triangle AEK is equal to the triangle AHK, and KFC to KGC, the triangle AEK together with KGC is equal to the triangle AHK together with KFC. [C.N. 2]

And the whole triangle ABC is also equal to the whole ADC; therefore the complement BK which remains is equal to the complement KD which remains. [C.N. 3]

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- In any parallelogram the complements of the parallelograms about the diameter are equal to one
another. -/
theorem Prop43 {A B C D E F G H K : Point} (hABCD : Parallelogram A B C D) (hK : Between A K C)
    (hE : Between A E B) (hG : Between B G C) (hF : Between C F D) (hH : Between D H A)
    (hEH : Parallelogram A E K H) (hFG : Parallelogram K G C F) :
    quadArea E B G K = quadArea H K F D := by
  -- Let ABCD be a parallelogram, and AC its diameter; and about AC let EH, FG be
  -- parallelograms, and BK, KD the so-called complements;
  -- I say that the complement BK is equal to the complement KD.
  -- For, since ABCD is a parallelogram, and AC its diameter, the triangle ABC is equal to the
  -- triangle ACD. [I. 34]
  have hABC_ACD : △ A B C = △ A C D := by
    have h := (Prop34 (A := B) (B := A) (C := C) (D := D) hABCD.rotate).2.2.2.2
    rw [area_bac B A C, area_cba D C A] at h
    exact h
  -- Again, since EH is a parallelogram, and AK is its diameter, the triangle AEK is equal to
  -- the triangle AHK.
  have hAEK_AHK : △ A E K = △ A H K := by
    have h := (Prop34 (A := E) (B := A) (C := K) (D := H) hEH.rotate).2.2.2.2
    rw [area_bac E A K, area_cab H K A] at h
    exact h
  -- For the same reason the triangle KFC is also equal to KGC.
  have hKFC_KGC : △ K F C = △ K G C := by
    have h := (Prop34 (A := G) (B := K) (C := C) (D := F) hFG.rotate).2.2.2.2
    rw [area_bac G K C, area_cab F C K] at h
    exact h.symm
  -- Now, since the triangle AEK is equal to the triangle AHK, and KFC to KGC, the triangle AEK
  -- together with KGC is equal to the triangle AHK together with KFC. [C.N. 2]
  have hsum : △ A E K + △ K G C = △ A H K + △ K F C :=
    CommonNotion2 hAEK_AHK hKFC_KGC.symm
  -- And the whole triangle ABC is also equal to the whole ADC; therefore the complement BK
  -- which remains is equal to the complement KD which remains. [C.N. 3]
  have hABC_ADC : △ A B C = △ A D C := hABC_ACD.trans (area_acb A C D)
  have hABC := Prop43.cut hABCD.triangle hK hE hG
  have hADC := Prop43.cut hABCD.reverse.triangle hK (between_symm hH) (between_symm hF)
  rw [quadArea_reverse H K F D] at hADC
  refine CommonNotion3 (c := △ A E K + △ K G C) (d := △ A H K + △ K F C) ?_ hsum
  calc
    quadArea E B G K + (△ A E K + △ K G C) = △ A B C := by rw [hABC]; ac_rfl
    _ = △ A D C := hABC_ADC
    _ = quadArea H K F D + (△ A H K + △ K F C) := by rw [hADC]; ac_rfl
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.

/-- Euclid takes for granted that the triangle ABC is made up of AEK, the
complement BK and KGC. The diameters EG and BK of the complement cross, so either
measures its area; cutting the triangle then gives the three pieces. Only the
three betweennesses are needed, with no parallels. -/

    (hE : Between A E B) (hG : Between B G C) :
    △ A B C = △ A E K + quadArea E B G K + △ K G C

Let ABCD be a parallelogram, and AC its diameter; and about AC let EH, FG be parallelograms, and BK, KD the so-called complements;

Let AB be the given straight line, C the given triangle and D the given rectilineal angle; thus it is required to apply to the given straight line AB, in an angle equal to the angle D, a parallelogram equal to the given triangle C.

Therefore the angles BHG, GFE are less than two right angles; and straight lines produced indefinitely from angles less than two right angles meet; [Post. 5] therefore HB, FE, when produced, will meet.

Let them be produced and meet at K; through the point K let KL be drawn parallel to either EA or FH, [I. 31] and let HA, GB be produced to the points L, M.

Then HLKF is a parallelogram, HK is its diameter, and AG, ME are parallelograms, and LB, BF the so-called complements, about HK; therefore LB is equal to BF. [I. 43]

But BF is equal to the triangle C; therefore LB is also equal to C. [C.N. 1]

And, since the angle GBE is equal to the angle ABM, [I. 15] while the angle GBE is equal to D, the angle ABM is also equal to the angle D.

Therefore the parallelogram LB equal to the given triangle C has been applied to the given straight line AB, in the angle ABM which is equal to D.

bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34:
/-- In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the
diameter bisects the areas. -/
theorem Prop34 {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A C D B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ C D B ∧ ∠ A B D = ∠ A C D ∧
      △ A B C = △ D C B
bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34.bisect:
/-- The diameter bisects the parallelogram, said of its area: the parallelogram
ABCD, measured by its diameter AC, is double the triangle ABC. I.35–I.47 cite
I.34 for this ("the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram EBCA; for the diameter
AB bisects it"). To halve by the other diameter, name the parallelogram from the
next corner (`Parallelogram.rotate`) and turn its area round with
`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`. [I. 34] -/
theorem Prop34.bisect {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea A B C D = △ A B C + △ A B C
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.cross:
/-- The diameters of a parallelogram cross: in the parallelogram ABCD, some point
lies between A and C and between B and D. Its sides AB and DC are
parallel, so they do not cross, and `AreParallel.cross_or` leaves only the
diameters. -/
theorem Parallelogram.cross (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    ∃ X : Point, Between A X C ∧ Between B X D
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate:
/-- A parallelogram has the same area whichever diameter cuts it: the parallelogram
ABCD measured by BD, as BCDA, is the same as measured by AC. -/
theorem Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea B C D A = quadArea A B C D
