state.lean_proof:
/-- To a given straight line to apply, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a
given triangle. -/
theorem Prop44 {A B C₁ C₂ C₃ D₁ D D₂ P : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hC : Triangle C₁ C₂ C₃)
    (hD : Triangle D₁ D D₂) (hP : ¬ Collinear A B P) :
    ∃ L M : Point, SameSideOf M P A B ∧ Parallelogram A B M L ∧
      ∠ A B M = ∠ D₁ D D₂ ∧ quadArea A B M L = △ C₁ C₂ C₃ := by
  -- Let AB be the given straight line, C the given triangle and D the given rectilineal angle;
  -- thus it is required to apply to the given straight line AB, in an angle equal to the angle
  -- D, a parallelogram equal to the given triangle C.
  obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B hAB
  -- Let the parallelogram BEFG be constructed equal to the triangle C, in the angle EBG which
  -- is equal to D [I. 42];
  obtain ⟨E₀, F₀, G₀, -, -, h42, hang42, harea42⟩ := Prop42 hC hD
  -- let it be placed so that BE is in a straight line with AB;
  /- G goes on the side away from P, so that the complement will stand on P's side. -/
  obtain ⟨X, hXP, -⟩ := exists_oppositeSidesOf (show Triangle A B P from hP) []
  obtain ⟨E, F, G, hABE, hGX, hBEFG, hEBG, harea⟩ := Prop44.place hAB hXP.triangle h42
  have hE_AB : OnLine E AB := on_line_of_between hABE hA_AB hB_AB
  have hBE : B ≠ E := (ne_of_between (between_symm hABE)).symm
  have hBG : B ≠ G := hBEFG.2.2.1.symm
  obtain ⟨BG, hB_BG, hG_BG⟩ := Postulate1 B G hBG
  obtain ⟨EF, hE_EF, hF_EF⟩ := Postulate1 E F hBEFG.2.1
  obtain ⟨FG, hF_FG, hG_FG⟩ := Postulate1 F G hBEFG.1.2.1
  have hAB_FG : Parallel AB FG := hBEFG.1.parallel hB_AB hE_AB hF_FG hG_FG
  have hEF_BG : Parallel EF BG := hBEFG.2.parallel hE_EF hF_EF hG_BG hB_BG
  have hG_AB : ¬ OnLine G AB := hAB_FG.symm.not_onLine hG_FG
  -- let FG be drawn through to H, and let AH be drawn through A parallel to either BG or EF.
  -- [I. 31]
  have hA_BG : ¬ OnLine A BG := fun h =>
    hG_AB ((line_unique hAB.symm hB_BG h hB_AB hA_AB) ▸ hG_BG)
  obtain ⟨AH, hA_AH, hAH_BG⟩ := Prop31.line hA_BG
  have hFG_BG : FG ≠ BG := fun e => hAB_FG.not_onLine hB_AB (e ▸ hB_BG)
  obtain ⟨H, hH_FG, hH_AH⟩ := Prop30.meet hAH_BG hG_BG hG_FG hFG_BG
  have hHGF : Between H G F := hABE.of_sameSide hB_BG (hAH_BG.sameSide hH_AH hA_AH)
    (hEF_BG.sameSide hF_EF hE_EF) hG_BG ⟨FG, hH_FG, hG_FG, hF_FG⟩
  have hAE : A ≠ E := ne_of_between_ends hABE
  have hAH_EF_ne : AH ≠ EF := fun e =>
    hAB_FG.not_onLine ((line_unique hAE hA_AB hE_AB (e ▸ hA_AH) hE_EF) ▸ hF_EF) hF_FG
  have hAH_EF : Parallel AH EF := Prop30.parallel hAH_BG hEF_BG hAH_EF_ne
  have hAH : A ≠ H := fun e => hAB_FG.not_onLine hA_AB (e ▸ hH_FG)
  have hHF : H ≠ F := fun e => hAH_EF.not_onLine hH_AH (e ▸ hF_EF)
  -- Let HB be joined.
  have hHB : H ≠ B := fun e => hAB_FG.not_onLine hB_AB (e ▸ hH_FG)
  obtain ⟨HB, hH_HB, hB_HB⟩ := Postulate1 H B hHB
  -- Then, since the straight line HF falls upon the parallels AH, EF, the angles AHF, HFE are
  -- equal to two right angles. [I. 29]
  have hAE_FG : SameSide A E FG := hAB_FG.sameSide hA_AB hE_AB
  have hAHFE : AreParallel H A F E :=
    AreParallel.of_parallel hAH.symm hBEFG.2.1.symm hH_AH hA_AH hF_EF hE_EF hAH_EF
  have h29 : ∠ A H F + ∠ H F E = ∟ + ∟ :=
    Prop29.interior hAHFE (SameSideOf.of_line hHF hH_FG hF_FG hAE_FG)
  -- Therefore the angles BHG, GFE are less than two right angles;
  have hBE_AH : SameSide B E AH := pasch2 hABE hA_AH (fun h => hAH_BG.not_onLine h hB_BG)
  have hEF_AH : SameSide E F AH := hAH_EF.symm.sameSide hE_EF hF_EF
  have hBF_HA : SameSideOf B F H A :=
    SameSideOf.of_line hAH.symm hH_AH hA_AH (same_side_trans (same_side_symm hBE_AH) hEF_AH)
  have hBA_HF : SameSideOf B A H F :=
    SameSideOf.of_line hHF hH_FG hF_FG (hAB_FG.sameSide hB_AB hA_AB)
  have hAHF : ∠ A H F = ∠ A H B + ∠ B H F := angle_add_of_within hBF_HA hBA_HF
  have hlt : ∠ B H F + ∠ H F E < ∟ + ∟ :=
    calc ∠ B H F + ∠ H F E < (∠ B H F + ∠ H F E) + ∠ A H B :=
          CommonNotion5 hBF_HA.triangle.bac.angle_pos
      _ = ∟ + ∟ := by rw [← h29, hAHF]; ac_rfl
  have hBHG : ∠ B H G = ∠ B H F := angle_onRay_right (OnRay.of_between hHGF) hHB.symm
  have hGFE : ∠ G F E = ∠ H F E := angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between (between_symm hHGF)) hBEFG.2.1
  have hlt' : ∠ B H G + ∠ G F E < ∟ + ∟ := by rw [hBHG, hGFE]; exact hlt
  -- and straight lines produced indefinitely from angles less than two right angles meet;
  -- [Post. 5] therefore HB, FE, when produced, will meet.
  have hmeet : ∃ K : Point, OnLine K HB ∧ OnLine K EF ∧ SameSide K B FG :=
    Postulate5 hB_HB hH_HB hH_FG hF_FG hF_EF hE_EF hHF
      (hAB_FG.sameSide hB_AB hE_AB) (by rw [← hBHG, ← hGFE]; exact hlt')
  -- Let them be produced and meet at K;
  obtain ⟨K, hK_HB, hK_EF, hKB⟩ := hmeet
  have hH_AB : ¬ OnLine H AB := hAB_FG.symm.not_onLine hH_FG
  have hH_BG : ¬ OnLine H BG := hAH_BG.not_onLine hH_AH
  have hK_BG : ¬ OnLine K BG := hEF_BG.not_onLine hK_EF
  have hK_FG : ¬ OnLine K FG := not_on_line_of_same_side hKB
  have hK_AB : ¬ OnLine K AB := fun hK => by
    by_cases hKE : K = E
    · subst hKE
      exact hH_AB ((line_unique hBE hB_HB hK_HB hB_AB hK) ▸ hH_HB)
    · exact hAB_FG.not_onLine ((line_unique hKE hK_EF hE_EF hK hE_AB) ▸ hF_EF) hF_FG
  -- through the point K let KL be drawn parallel to either EA or FH, [I. 31]
  obtain ⟨KL, hK_KL, hKL_FG⟩ := Prop31.line hK_FG
  have hKL_AB : Parallel KL AB :=
    Prop30.parallel hKL_FG hAB_FG (fun e => hK_AB (e ▸ hK_KL))
  -- and let HA, GB be produced to the points L, M.
  have hAH_FG : AH ≠ FG := fun e => hAH_BG.not_onLine (e ▸ hG_FG) hG_BG
  obtain ⟨L, hL_AH, hL_KL⟩ := Prop30.meet hKL_FG hH_FG hH_AH hAH_FG
  obtain ⟨M, hM_BG, hM_KL⟩ := Prop30.meet hKL_FG hG_FG hG_BG hFG_BG.symm
  /- The parallels carry the order A, B, E to every crossing straight line. -/
  have hHBK : Between H B K := hHGF.of_sameSide hG_BG (same_side_refl hH_BG)
    (hEF_BG.sameSide hK_EF hF_EF) hB_BG ⟨HB, hH_HB, hB_HB, hK_HB⟩
  have hFEK : Between F E K := hHBK.of_sameSide hB_AB (hAB_FG.symm.sameSide hF_FG hH_FG)
    (same_side_refl hK_AB) hE_AB ⟨EF, hF_EF, hE_EF, hK_EF⟩
  have hKML : Between K M L := (between_symm hHBK).of_sameSide hB_BG (same_side_refl hK_BG)
    (hAH_BG.sameSide hL_AH hH_AH) hM_BG ⟨KL, hK_KL, hM_KL, hL_KL⟩
  have hLAH : Between L A H := (between_symm hHBK).of_sameSide hB_AB
    (hKL_AB.sameSide hL_KL hK_KL) (same_side_refl hH_AB) hA_AB ⟨AH, hL_AH, hA_AH, hH_AH⟩
  have hGBM : Between G B M := hHBK.of_sameSide hB_AB (hAB_FG.symm.sameSide hG_FG hH_FG)
    (hKL_AB.sameSide hM_KL hK_KL) hB_AB ⟨BG, hG_BG, hB_BG, hM_BG⟩
  -- Then HLKF is a parallelogram, HK is its diameter, and AG, ME are parallelograms, and LB,
  -- BF the so-called complements, about HK;
  have hKL : K ≠ L := fun e => hAH_EF.not_onLine (e ▸ hL_AH) hK_EF
  have hLH : L ≠ H := fun e => hKL_FG.not_onLine hL_KL (e ▸ hH_FG)
  have hHG : H ≠ G := fun e => hAH_BG.not_onLine hH_AH (e ▸ hG_BG)
  have hKM : K ≠ M := fun e => hK_BG (e ▸ hM_BG)
  have hMB : M ≠ B := fun e => hKL_AB.not_onLine hM_KL (e ▸ hB_AB)
  have hML : M ≠ L := fun e => hAH_BG.not_onLine (e ▸ hL_AH) hM_BG
  have hLA' : L ≠ A := fun e => hKL_AB.not_onLine hL_KL (e ▸ hA_AB)
  have hHLKF : Parallelogram H L K F :=
    ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel hLH.symm (ne_of_between_ends hFEK).symm
        hH_AH hL_AH hK_EF hF_EF hAH_EF,
      AreParallel.of_parallel hKL.symm hHF.symm hL_KL hK_KL hF_FG hH_FG hKL_FG⟩
  have hHABG : Parallelogram H A B G :=
    ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel hAH.symm hBG hH_AH hA_AH hB_BG hG_BG hAH_BG,
      AreParallel.of_parallel hAB hHG.symm hA_AB hB_AB hG_FG hH_FG hAB_FG⟩
  have hBMKE : Parallelogram B M K E :=
    ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel hMB.symm (ne_of_between (between_symm hFEK))
        hB_BG hM_BG hK_EF hE_EF hEF_BG.symm,
      AreParallel.of_parallel hKM.symm hBE.symm hM_KL hK_KL hE_AB hB_AB hKL_AB⟩
  have hABML : Parallelogram A B M L :=
    ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel hAB hML hA_AB hB_AB hM_KL hL_KL hKL_AB.symm,
      AreParallel.of_parallel hMB.symm hLA' hB_BG hM_BG hL_AH hA_AH hAH_BG.symm⟩
  -- therefore LB is equal to BF. [I. 43]
  have h43 : quadArea A L M B = quadArea G B E F :=
    Prop43 hHLKF hHBK (between_symm hLAH) (between_symm hKML) (between_symm hFEK)
      (between_symm hHGF) hHABG hBMKE
  have hLB_BF : quadArea A B M L = quadArea B E F G := by
    rw [← quadArea_reverse A B M L, h43, quadArea_rotate₂ E F G B, hBEFG.quadArea_rotate]
  -- But BF is equal to the triangle C;
  have hBF_C : quadArea B E F G = △ C₁ C₂ C₃ := harea.trans harea42
  -- therefore LB is also equal to C. [C.N. 1]
  have hLB_C : quadArea A B M L = △ C₁ C₂ C₃ := CommonNotion1 hLB_BF hBF_C.symm
  -- And, since the angle GBE is equal to the angle ABM, [I. 15]
  have hGBE_ABM : ∠ G B E = ∠ A B M := (Prop15 hABE hGBM fun ⟨ℓ, hA_ℓ, hE_ℓ, hG_ℓ⟩ =>
    hG_AB ((line_unique hAE hA_ℓ hE_ℓ hA_AB hE_AB) ▸ hG_ℓ)).2
  -- while the angle GBE is equal to D,
  have hGBE_D : ∠ G B E = ∠ D₁ D D₂ := by
    rw [angle_symm hBG.symm hBE.symm, hEBG, hang42]
  -- the angle ABM is also equal to the angle D.
  have hABM_D : ∠ A B M = ∠ D₁ D D₂ := hGBE_ABM.symm.trans hGBE_D
  -- Therefore the parallelogram LB equal to the given triangle C has been applied to the given
  -- straight line AB, in the angle ABM which is equal to D.
  have hGP : OppositeSidesOf G P A B := hGX.trans_opposite hXP
  have hGM : OppositeSidesOf G M A B :=
    OppositeSidesOf.of_between (Triangle.of_line hA_AB hB_AB hAB hG_AB) hGBM
  exact ⟨L, M, OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf hGM hGP, hABML, hABM_D, hLB_C⟩
  -- Q. E. F.

helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.of_parallel:
/-- Two different points of L, and two different points of M, are the ends of
parallel straight lines when L and M are parallel: two points fix one straight
line (System E, Generalities 1). With `AreParallel.parallel`, this says "AB is
parallel to CD" of any other two points P, Q of the straight line AB and R,
S of CD. -/
theorem AreParallel.of_parallel (hPQ : P ≠ Q) (hRS : R ≠ S) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L)
    (hR : OnLine R M) (hS : OnLine S M) (h : Parallel L M) : AreParallel P Q R S
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.parallel:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then a straight line through A and B is parallel
to one through C and D. -/
theorem AreParallel.parallel (h : AreParallel A B C D) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (hC : OnLine C M) (hD : OnLine D M) : Parallel L M
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.symm:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then CD is parallel to AB. -/
theorem AreParallel.symm (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.triangle:
/-- An end of one parallel is off the other: if AB is parallel to CD, then C
is not on the straight line AB, and ABC is a triangle. (Turned round with
`AreParallel.symm` and `.swap_right`, the same holds of D, and of A and B
beside CD.) -/
theorem AreParallel.triangle (h : AreParallel A B C D) : Triangle A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Between.of_sameSide:
/-- Order kept across a straight line. If B, on the straight line L, lies
between A and C, and A', C' lie on the same sides of L as A, C, then a
point B' of L on one straight line with A' and C' lies between them: A' and
C' are on opposite sides of L, so the straight line joining them crosses L
between them, and it crosses L only once (System E, Pasch 3 and 4). -/
theorem Between.of_sameSide (hABC : Between A B C) (hB : OnLine B L) (hA : SameSide A' A L)
    (hC : SameSide C' C L) (hB' : OnLine B' L) (hcol : Collinear A' B' C') :
    Between A' B' C'
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop15:
/-- If two straight lines cut one another, they make the vertical angles equal to one another. -/
theorem Prop15 {A B C D E : Point} (hAEB : Between A E B) (hCED : Between C E D)
    (hC : ¬ Collinear A B C) :
    ∠ A E C = ∠ D E B ∧ ∠ C E B = ∠ A E D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop2:
/-- To place at a given point (as an extremity) a straight line equal to a given straight
line. -/
theorem Prop2 (A B C : Point) (hBC : B ≠ C) :
    ∃ L : Point, ‖A L‖ = ‖B C‖
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop23:
/-- On a given straight line and at a point on it to construct a rectilineal angle equal to a given
rectilineal angle. -/
theorem Prop23 {A B C D E P : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hDCE : Triangle D C E) (hP : ¬ Collinear A B P) :
    ∃ F G : Point, OnRay G A B ∧ SameSideOf F P A B ∧ ∠ F A G = ∠ D C E
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29:
/-- A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one
another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on
the same side equal to two right angles. -/
theorem Prop29 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (hpar : AreParallel A B C D) (hAGB : Between A G B)
    (hCHD : Between C H D) (hEGH : Between E G H) (hGHF : Between G H F)
    (hBD : SameSideOf B D E F) :
    ∠ A G H = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ E G B = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D = ∟ + ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29.interior:
/-- The interior angles on the same side. If the straight line GP is parallel to
HQ, and P and Q lie on one side of GH, then the angles PGH, GHQ are
equal to two right angles. [I. 29] -/
theorem Prop29.interior {P G H Q : Point} (hpar : AreParallel G P H Q)
    (hPQ : SameSideOf P Q G H) : ∠ P G H + ∠ G H Q = ∟ + ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30:
/-- Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another. -/
theorem Prop30 {A B C D E F : Point} (h₁ : AreParallel A B E F) (h₂ : AreParallel C D E F)
    (hC : ¬ Collinear A B C) :
    AreParallel A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30.meet:
/-- A straight line meeting one of two parallels meets the other. If L is parallel
to M, and a straight line N, other than M, passes through a point P of M,
then N meets L. Otherwise N would be parallel to L too, and by I.30 M and
N would be parallel to one another, though both pass through P.

Euclid uses this whenever he draws a parallel and then names the point where it
meets another straight line: E and F in I.37, G and H in I.38, E in I.39,
F in I.40, F and G in I.42, H, L and M in I.44, E in I.46 and L in
I.47. It is the uniqueness of the parallel through a point, often called
Playfair's axiom; Heath reports under I.31 that Proclus draws it from I.30.
`Prop30.unique`, a step inside I.30's own proof, gives the same uniqueness from
I.29; later proofs cite this one, Proclus' route through I.30. [I. 30] -/
theorem Prop30.meet {L M N : Line} {P : Point} (hLM : Parallel L M) (hPM : OnLine P M)
    (hPN : OnLine P N) (hNM : N ≠ M) : ∃ Q : Point, OnLine Q N ∧ OnLine Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30.parallel:
/-- I.30 said of straight lines drawn and named: two different straight lines L and
M, each parallel to N, are parallel to one another. Euclid uses it without a
bracket in I.44 and I.47, where a straight line drawn "parallel to either" of two
parallels is parallel to both; in I.45 he brackets it. [I. 30] -/
theorem Prop30.parallel {L M N : Line} (hL : Parallel L N) (hM : Parallel M N) (hLM : L ≠ M) :
    Parallel L M
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31:
/-- Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line. -/
theorem Prop31 {A B C : Point} (hBC : B ≠ C) (hA : ¬ Collinear B C A) :
    ∃ E F : Point, Between E A F ∧ AreParallel E F B C
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31.line:
/-- I.31 said of straight lines drawn and named: through a point A off the
straight line L there is a straight line K parallel to L. I.31 gives two points
of it, one on either side of A, and Postulate 1 joins them. [I. 31] -/
theorem Prop31.line {A : Point} {L : Line} (hA : ¬ OnLine A L) :
    ∃ K : Line, OnLine A K ∧ Parallel K L
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31.parallelogram:
/-- Completing the parallelogram. If X lies on L, and Y and Z on M, which is
parallel to L, the straight line drawn through Z parallel to XY [I. 31] meets
L at a point W (`Prop30.meet`), and XYZW is a parallelogram. Euclid draws such
a parallel in I.37, I.38, I.42, I.44 and I.46, and reads the point where it meets
L, and the parallelogram, off his figure. [I. 30, I. 31] -/
theorem Prop31.parallelogram {X Y Z : Point} {L M : Line} (hLM : Parallel L M)
    (hX : OnLine X L) (hY : OnLine Y M) (hZ : OnLine Z M) (hYZ : Y ≠ Z) :
    ∃ W : Point, OnLine W L ∧ Parallelogram X Y Z W
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop34:
/-- In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the
diameter bisects the areas. -/
theorem Prop34 {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A C D B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ C D B ∧ ∠ A B D = ∠ A C D ∧
      △ A B C = △ D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop34.bisect:
/-- The diameter bisects the parallelogram, said of its area: the parallelogram
ABCD, measured by its diameter AC, is double the triangle ABC. I.35–I.47 cite
I.34 for this ("the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram EBCA; for the diameter
AB bisects it"). To halve by the other diameter, name the parallelogram from the
next corner (`Parallelogram.rotate`) and turn its area round with
`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`. [I. 34] -/
theorem Prop34.bisect {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea A B C D = △ A B C + △ A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop4:
/-- If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles
contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the base, the
triangle will be equal to the triangle, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining
angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend. -/
theorem Prop4 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖D F‖) (hA : ∠ B A C = ∠ E D F) :
    ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ ∧ △ A B C = △ D E F ∧ ∠ A B C = ∠ D E F ∧ ∠ A C B = ∠ D F E
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop42:
/-- To construct, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given triangle. -/
theorem Prop42 {A B C D₁ D D₂ : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hD : Triangle D₁ D D₂) :
    ∃ E F G : Point, Between B E C ∧ SameSideOf F A B C ∧ Parallelogram F E C G ∧
      ∠ C E F = ∠ D₁ D D₂ ∧ quadArea F E C G = △ A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop43:
/-- In any parallelogram the complements of the parallelograms about the diameter are equal to one
another. -/
theorem Prop43 {A B C D E F G H K : Point} (hABCD : Parallelogram A B C D) (hK : Between A K C)
    (hE : Between A E B) (hG : Between B G C) (hF : Between C F D) (hH : Between D H A)
    (hEH : Parallelogram A E K H) (hFG : Parallelogram K G C F) :
    quadArea E B G K = quadArea H K F D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop44.place:
/-- "Let it be placed so that BE is in a straight line with AB." Euclid moves the
parallelogram made by I.42 into place without a word, as if picking it up. Our
foundations move a figure only by superposition, kept for I.4 and I.8, so we
build an equal one where Euclid puts his. Given the
parallelogram PQRS, with its angle RQP, and a straight line AB: produce AB to
E, making BE equal to QR [I. 2]; at B on BE construct the angle EBG equal
to the angle RQP, on the side of X [I. 23], with BG equal to QP [I. 2];
through G and E draw parallels to BE and BG [I. 31], meeting at F
(`Prop30.meet`). Then BEFG is a parallelogram, and it is equal to PQRS, for each
is double a triangle [I. 34], and the triangles GBE and PQR are equal [I. 4]. -/
theorem Prop44.place {A B X P Q R S : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hX : ¬ Collinear A B X)
    (h : Parallelogram P Q R S) :
    ∃ E F G : Point, Between A B E ∧ SameSideOf G X A B ∧ Parallelogram B E F G ∧
      ∠ E B G = ∠ R Q P ∧ quadArea B E F G = quadArea P Q R S
helper_signatures.Elements.Collinear:
/-- `A`, `B`, `C` lie on one straight line. -/
def Collinear (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.CommonNotion1:
/-- **Common Notion 1.** Things which are equal to the same thing are also equal
to one another. -/
theorem CommonNotion1 {α : Sort _} {a b c : α} (h₁ : a = c) (h₂ : b = c) : a = b
helper_signatures.Elements.CommonNotion5:
/-- **Common Notion 5.** The whole is greater than the part: if `b` is something
(not nothing), then `a + b` is greater than `a`. -/
theorem CommonNotion5 {a b : Magnitude k} (h : 0 < b) : a < a + b
helper_signatures.Elements.Magnitude.instAssociative:
/-- Adding magnitudes is associative (System E §3.5), told to `ac_rfl`. -/
instance Magnitude.instAssociative : Std.Associative (α := Magnitude k) (· + ·)
helper_signatures.Elements.Magnitude.instCommutative:
/-- Adding magnitudes is commutative (System E §3.5), told to `ac_rfl`. -/
instance Magnitude.instCommutative : Std.Commutative (α := Magnitude k) (· + ·)
helper_signatures.Elements.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.between:
/-- Beyond the start of a ray. If CB is produced beyond B to E, every point D
of the ray from B through E lies beyond B from C as well. Of the three points
C, B, D on one straight line one is between the other two (System E,
Between 6); were it C or D, then B would lie between D and E, and D
would be off the ray. -/
theorem OnRay.between {C D E : Point} (hD : OnRay D B E) (hCBE : Between C B E) :
    Between C B D
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.exists_len_eq:
/-- "Let DG be made equal to DF" (I.24): on the ray from D through any point P
there is a point G with DG equal to DF. Describe the circle with centre D and
distance DF (Post. 3); the straight line DP, which passes through its centre, cuts
it on P's side of D (System E, Intersections 5, with a point Q set out on the
other side); and DG is a radius [Def. 15]. -/
theorem OnRay.exists_len_eq {D F P : Point} (hDF : D ≠ F) (hDP : D ≠ P) :
    ∃ G : Point, OnRay G D P ∧ ‖D G‖ = ‖D F‖
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.of_between:
/-- A point between A and B is on the ray from A through B. -/
theorem OnRay.of_between (h : Between A P B) : OnRay P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.symm:
/-- P is on the ray from A through B exactly when B is on the ray from A
through P: they are one and the same ray. -/
theorem OnRay.symm (h : OnRay P A B) : OnRay B A P
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf:
/-- `P` and `Q` lie on opposite sides of the straight line `AB`. -/
def OppositeSidesOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.of_between:
/-- A straight line through a point of AB, from a point C off it, crosses to
the other side: if B lies between C and E, then E is on the other side
of the straight line AB from C. (System E, Pasch 3) -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.of_between {C E : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C)
    (h : Between C B E) : OppositeSidesOf C E A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf:
/-- The same, said of "the straight line AB": two points, each on the other side of
AB from C, are on the same side of AB as each other. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf {C D E : Point} (h₁ : OppositeSidesOf C D A B)
    (h₂ : OppositeSidesOf C E A B) : SameSideOf D E A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the other side of AB from Q, then Q is on the other side
from P. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.symm (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : OppositeSidesOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.triangle:
/-- A point on either side of the straight line AB is not on it, so ABP is a
triangle. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.triangle (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : Triangle A B P
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.between:
/-- Parallels keep order. Let three straight lines be crossed by two others: if B
lies between A and C on one crossing straight line, then B' lies between A'
and C' on the other, when A, A' lie on L₁, B, B' on L, and C, C' on
L₃, and L₁ and L₃ are each parallel to L. All of L₁ lies on one side of
L, and all of L₃ on the other (`Parallel.sameSide`). Book II's figures use it
(`Parallelogram.figure`), where the parallels through the points of section meet the
far side of the square in the same order. -/
theorem Parallel.between (h₁ : Parallel L₁ L) (h₃ : Parallel L₃ L) (hA : OnLine A L₁)
    (hB : OnLine B L) (hC : OnLine C L₃) (hABC : Between A B C) (hA' : OnLine A' L₁)
    (hB' : OnLine B' L) (hC' : OnLine C' L₃) (hcol : Collinear A' B' C') :
    Between A' B' C'
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.not_onLine:
/-- Parallels do not meet: a point of L is not on M. -/
theorem Parallel.not_onLine (h : Parallel L M) (hP : OnLine P L) : ¬ OnLine P M
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.sameSide:
/-- All the points of one parallel lie on one side of the other: two points of L
are on the same side of M. Were they on opposite sides, the straight line L
joining them would cross M (System E, Intersection 1). -/
theorem Parallel.sameSide (h : Parallel L M) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L) :
    SameSide P Q M
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.symm:
/-- If L is parallel to M, then M is parallel to L. -/
theorem Parallel.symm (h : Parallel L M) : Parallel M L
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate:
/-- A parallelogram has the same area whichever diameter cuts it: the parallelogram
ABCD measured by BD, as BCDA, is the same as measured by AC. -/
theorem Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea B C D A = quadArea A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.rotate:
/-- The parallelogram ABCD, named from B, is the parallelogram BCDA. -/
theorem Parallelogram.rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Parallelogram B C D A
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.triangle:
/-- In the parallelogram ABCD, the corner C is off the straight line AB, so
ABC is a triangle. -/
theorem Parallelogram.triangle (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Triangle A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate1:
/-- **Postulate 1.** To draw a straight line from any point to any point. -/
axiom Postulate1 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate5:
/-- **Postulate 5.** If the straight line through `B` and `C` falls on the
straight lines `L` (through `A` and `B`) and `N` (through `C` and `D`), with `A`
and `D` on the same side of it, and the interior angles `ABC` and `BCD` together
are less than two right angles, then `L` and `N`, produced, meet on that side.

System E §3.6, diagram-angle transfer rule 5. -/
axiom Postulate5 {A B C D : Point} {L M N : Line}
    (hA : OnLine A L) (hBL : OnLine B L) (hBM : OnLine B M) (hCM : OnLine C M)
    (hCN : OnLine C N) (hD : OnLine D N) (hBC : B ≠ C) (hAD : SameSide A D M)
    (hsum : ∠ A B C + ∠ B C D < ∟ + ∟) :
    ∃ E : Point, OnLine E L ∧ OnLine E N ∧ SameSide E A M
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf:
/-- `P` and `Q` lie on the same side of the straight line `AB`. -/
def SameSideOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.of_line:
/-- Two points on the same side of a straight line L through A and B are on
the same side of the straight line AB, however that line is named: two points
fix one straight line. -/
theorem SameSideOf.of_line (hAB : A ≠ B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (h : SameSide P Q L) : SameSideOf P Q A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.of_onRay:
/-- A point G on the ray from D through P is on the same side of the straight
line DE as P: the ray leaves DE at D and never crosses it again (System E,
Pasch 4). -/
theorem SameSideOf.of_onRay {D E F G P : Point} (hG : OnRay G D P) (hP : SameSideOf P F D E) :
    SameSideOf G F D E
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.sameSide:
/-- Two points on the same side of the straight line AB are on the same side of
any straight line drawn through A and B. -/
theorem SameSideOf.sameSide (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    SameSide P Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the same side of AB as Q, then Q is on the same side as P. -/
theorem SameSideOf.symm (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.trans:
/-- Points on the same side as a third are on the same side as each other. -/
theorem SameSideOf.trans (h₁ : SameSideOf P Q A B) (h₂ : SameSideOf Q R A B) :
    SameSideOf P R A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.trans_opposite:
/-- A point on Q's side of the straight line AB, where Q is on the other side
from R, is itself on the other side from R. -/
theorem SameSideOf.trans_opposite (h₁ : SameSideOf P Q A B) (h₂ : OppositeSidesOf Q R A B) :
    OppositeSidesOf P R A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.triangle:
/-- A point on one side of the straight line AB is not on it, so ABP is a
triangle. -/
theorem SameSideOf.triangle (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : Triangle A B P
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.angle_symm:
/-- The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4) -/
axiom angle_symm (hAB : A ≠ B) (hCB : C ≠ B) : ∠ A B C = ∠ C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_symm:
/-- If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1) -/
axiom between_symm (h : Between A B C) : Between C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.line_unique:
/-- Two points determine a straight line. (Generalities 1) -/
axiom line_unique (hAB : A ≠ B) (hAL : OnLine A L) (hBL : OnLine B L) (hAM : OnLine A M)
    (hBM : OnLine B M) : L = M
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between:
/-- A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between_ends:
/-- The ends of a finite straight line differ. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.not_on_line_of_same_side:
/-- Points on one side of a straight line are not on it. (Same side 3) -/
axiom not_on_line_of_same_side (h : SameSide A B L) : ¬ OnLine A L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between:
/-- A straight line through A and B, with B between A and C, passes
through C. (Between 2) -/
axiom on_line_of_between (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    OnLine C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.pasch2:
/-- If B is between A and C, A is on L and B is off it, then B and C are
on the same side of L: a straight line that leaves L at A does not cross it
again. (Pasch 2) -/
axiom pasch2 (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : ¬ OnLine B L) : SameSide B C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.same_side_refl:
/-- A point off a straight line is on the same side of it as itself. (Same side 1) -/
axiom same_side_refl (h : ¬ OnLine A L) : SameSide A A L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.same_side_symm:
/-- If A is on the same side of a straight line as B, then B is on the same side
as A. (Same side 2) -/
axiom same_side_symm (h : SameSide A B L) : SameSide B A L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.same_side_trans:
/-- Two points on the same side of a straight line as a third point are on the same
side as each other. (Same side 4) -/
axiom same_side_trans (h₁ : SameSide A B L) (h₂ : SameSide A C L) : SameSide B C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.acb:
/-- The triangle ABC, named the other way round, as ACB. -/
theorem Triangle.acb (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle A C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.angle_pos:
/-- An angle of a triangle is something, not nothing: in the triangle ABC, were
the angle ABC nothing, C would lie on the straight line BA (System E,
Diagram-angle 1), and A, B, C would be on one straight line. -/
theorem Triangle.angle_pos (h : Triangle A B C) : 0 < ∠ A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.bac:
/-- The triangle ABC, named the other way round, as BAC. -/
theorem Triangle.bac (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.cba:
/-- The triangle ABC, named the other way round, as CBA. -/
theorem Triangle.cba (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₁₂:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₁₂ (h : Triangle A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₁₃:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₁₃ (h : Triangle A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₂₃:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₂₃ (h : Triangle A B C) : B ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.of_line:
/-- Two different points of a straight line, and a third point off it, make a
triangle. -/
theorem Triangle.of_line {P Q R : Point} (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L) (hPQ : P ≠ Q)
    (hR : ¬ OnLine R L) : Triangle P Q R
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.off_line:
/-- In the triangle ABC, the corner C is off every straight line through A
and B. -/
theorem Triangle.off_line (h : Triangle A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    ¬ OnLine C L
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_add_of_within:
/-- A straight line drawn from the corner of an angle through a point within it
cuts the angle into two. If R lies within the angle PVQ, on Q's side of VP
and on P's side of VQ, then the angle PVQ is made up of the angles PVR and
RVQ. This is System E's Diagram-angle 2, said of "the straight lines VP, VQ"
rather than of lines drawn and named. -/
theorem angle_add_of_within {V P Q R : Point} (hRQ : SameSideOf R Q V P)
    (hRP : SameSideOf R P V Q) : ∠ P V Q = ∠ P V R + ∠ R V Q
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_eq_of_onRay:
/-- An angle doesn't change when its arms are traced through other points of the
same rays: if B' is on the ray from A through B, and C' on the ray from A
through C, the angle B'AC' is the angle BAC. (System E, Diagram-angle 4) -/
theorem angle_eq_of_onRay {B' C' : Point} (hB : OnRay B' A B) (hC : OnRay C' A C) :
    ∠ B' A C' = ∠ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_onRay_left:
/-- One arm traced through another point of its ray: if B' is on the ray from A
through B, the angle B'AC is the angle BAC. (System E, Diagram-angle 4) -/
theorem angle_onRay_left {B' : Point} (hB : OnRay B' A B) (hCA : C ≠ A) :
    ∠ B' A C = ∠ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_onRay_right:
/-- The other arm traced through another point of its ray: if C' is on the ray
from A through C, the angle BAC' is the angle BAC. (System E,
Diagram-angle 4) -/
theorem angle_onRay_right {C' : Point} (hC : OnRay C' A C) (hBA : B ≠ A) :
    ∠ B A C' = ∠ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.area_bac:
/-- The triangle ABC is the triangle BAC. (System E, Metric 8) -/
theorem area_bac (A B C : Point) : △ A B C = △ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.exists_oppositeSidesOf:
/-- "Let a point be taken at random on the other side of the straight line AB"
(I.12): if P is off the straight line AB, there is a point on the other side
of it from P, which may be chosen different from any points already in the
figure. (System E, Points 6) -/
theorem exists_oppositeSidesOf (hP : Triangle A B P) (avoid : List Point) :
    ∃ Q : Point, OppositeSidesOf Q P A B ∧ Q ∉ avoid
helper_signatures.Elements.ne_of_len_eq:
/-- If a finite straight line AB has the length of one with different ends,
its own ends are different. -/
theorem ne_of_len_eq (h : ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖) (hCD : C ≠ D) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.produce:
/-- A finite straight line AB can be produced beyond B. [Post. 1, Post. 2] -/
theorem produce (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ C : Point, Between A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea_reverse:
/-- The figure ABCD read the other way round, as ADCB, has the same diameter
AC, and the same area. -/
theorem quadArea_reverse (A B C D : Point) : quadArea A D C B = quadArea A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea_rotate₂:
/-- The figure ABCD read from C, as CDAB, has the same diameter CA, and the
same area. -/
theorem quadArea_rotate₂ (A B C D : Point) : quadArea C D A B = quadArea A B C D

I.2.enunciation: To place at a given point (as an extremity) a straight line equal to a given straight line.

I.4.enunciation: If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the base, the triangle will be equal to the triangle, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend.

I.15.enunciation: If two straight lines cut one another, they make the vertical angles equal to one another.
I.15.heath_porism: [PORISM. From this it is manifest that, if two straight lines cut one another, they will make the angles at the point of section equal to four right angles.]

I.23.enunciation: On a given straight line and at a point on it to construct a rectilineal angle equal to a given rectilineal angle.

I.29.enunciation: A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on the same side equal to two right angles.

I.30.enunciation: Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another.

I.31.enunciation: Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line.

I.34.enunciation: In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the diameter bisects the areas.

I.42.enunciation: To construct, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given triangle.

I.43.enunciation: In any parallelogram the complements of the parallelograms about the diameter are equal to one another.

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ P ≠ A ∧ Collinear A B P ∧ ¬ Between P A B
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle

question.instructions:
Does every proposition called by the proof unit in `lean_proof` do work towards its conclusion or a substantive intermediate step of Euclid's argument? Also check for artificial hypothesis uses. Judge this unit's uses of the supplied helper signatures; helper bodies are outside this question. Heath's sentences stand as `--` lines and `cited` gives exact enunciations. In Lean, `have h : T := p` proves T by p and calls the result h; `obtain ⟨…⟩ := p` takes p apart into named pieces; `rw [h34, h37, …]` rewrites the goal by the equalities named. Follow uses through helper calls and tactics as well as explicit names. An anonymous binding or an unused hypothesis alone does not establish a defect. If both defects occur, choose `a dummy citation`.

docs/FORMALIZATION.md, section 5:
A checked intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid is legitimate, even if the
  final proof term could do without it.

criteria.an artificial hypothesis use: No dummy citation is established, but a hypothesis is mentioned only so that it looks used, and does no substantive work.
criteria.cannot tell: What is given here is not enough to decide.
criteria.all do work: Every proposition call supports a later step or the conclusion, or establishes a substantive intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid. No hypothesis is mentioned merely to look used. With no proposition calls the citation part alone is vacuous; hypothesis use must still be inspected.
criteria.a dummy citation: Some proposition call does no substantive work: its result neither supports the argument nor establishes a substantive intermediate fact, and merely supplies a citation while the step is done another way.

bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34:
/-- In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the
diameter bisects the areas. -/
theorem Prop34 {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A C D B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ C D B ∧ ∠ A B D = ∠ A C D ∧
      △ A B C = △ D C B
bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34.bisect:
/-- The diameter bisects the parallelogram, said of its area: the parallelogram
ABCD, measured by its diameter AC, is double the triangle ABC. I.35–I.47 cite
I.34 for this ("the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram EBCA; for the diameter
AB bisects it"). To halve by the other diameter, name the parallelogram from the
next corner (`Parallelogram.rotate`) and turn its area round with
`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`. [I. 34] -/
theorem Prop34.bisect {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea A B C D = △ A B C + △ A B C
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.cross:
/-- The diameters of a parallelogram cross: in the parallelogram ABCD, some point
lies between A and C and between B and D. Its sides AB and DC are
parallel, so they do not cross, and `AreParallel.cross_or` leaves only the
diameters. -/
theorem Parallelogram.cross (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    ∃ X : Point, Between A X C ∧ Between B X D
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate:
/-- A parallelogram has the same area whichever diameter cuts it: the parallelogram
ABCD measured by BD, as BCDA, is the same as measured by AC. -/
theorem Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea B C D A = quadArea A B C D

Elements.Parallelogram.cross: variable {A B C D E F X A' B' C' : Point} {L M N L₁ L₃ : Line}
Elements.Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate: variable {A B C D E F X A' B' C' : Point} {L M N L₁ L₃ : Line}

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D

state.commentary:
To apply a parallelogram to a straight line is to build it on that whole straight line. Euclid sets the parallelogram of I.42 beside AB as one complement in a larger parallelogram, HLKF, and I.43 makes the other complement, the one standing on AB, equal to it. Heath judges that this proposition "will always remain one of the most impressive in all geometry" (vol. 1, p. 342), for the simplicity of its means and for what they achieve: a parallelogram of any shape remade on a side "of any given length, e.g. a *unit* length" (vol. 1, p. 343).

**"Let it be placed."** Euclid simply moves I.42's parallelogram to B. Superposition is one rule in our foundations, kept for I.4 and I.8, so we build an equal parallelogram where Euclid puts his, with constructions Book I already has (`Prop44.place`). A given point says on which side of AB the parallelogram is to stand, and the parallels carry the order of A, B, E to the straight lines crossing them.

Then, for the second and last time in Book I, Euclid calls on Postulate 5: "HB, FE, when produced, will meet." I.29 makes the angles AHF, HFE together two right angles; HB splits the angle AHF, so BHG and GFE are less, by Common Notion 5, and the postulate gives K on B's side of FG. Charles Dodgson, defending Euclid's postulate, gave I.44 as an example of its use, as Heath reports under I.29.

Proclus, citing Eudemus, calls the application of areas, with its exceeding and its falling-short, "discoveries of the Muse of the Pythagoreans" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 343). An area that overruns the straight line exceeds; one that leaves some of it over falls short. Apollonius took the names for the curves we still call conic sections, "designating one of these a *parabola* (application), another a *hyperbola* (exceeding) and another an *ellipse* (falling-short)" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 343). Proclus' own example is in numbers: an area of twelve feet, applied in a right angle to a straight line of four feet, has a breadth of three.

**The modern way.** A parallelogram with sides $a$ and $b$ in the angle $\theta$ has area $ab\sin\theta$, so an area $q$ applied in that angle to a straight line of length $a$ has breadth $q/(a\sin\theta)$. In Euclid's figure, take oblique axes along BE and BM with B at the origin: $\mathrm{H} = (-\mathrm{AB}, -\mathrm{BG})$ and $\mathrm{K} = (\mathrm{BE}, \mathrm{BM})$ lie on one straight line through B, so $\mathrm{BM} = \mathrm{BE} \cdot \mathrm{BG}/\mathrm{AB}$, and $\mathrm{AB} \cdot \mathrm{BM} = \mathrm{BE} \cdot \mathrm{BG}$.
state.heath_proof:
Let AB be the given straight line, C the given triangle and D the given rectilineal angle; thus it is required to apply to the given straight line AB, in an angle equal to the angle D, a parallelogram equal to the given triangle C.

Let the parallelogram BEFG be constructed equal to the triangle C, in the angle EBG which is equal to D [I. 42]; let it be placed so that BE is in a straight line with AB; let FG be drawn through to H, and let AH be drawn through A parallel to either BG or EF. [I. 31]

Let HB be joined.

Then, since the straight line HF falls upon the parallels AH, EF, the angles AHF, HFE are equal to two right angles. [I. 29]

Therefore the angles BHG, GFE are less than two right angles; and straight lines produced indefinitely from angles less than two right angles meet; [Post. 5] therefore HB, FE, when produced, will meet.

Let them be produced and meet at K; through the point K let KL be drawn parallel to either EA or FH, [I. 31] and let HA, GB be produced to the points L, M.

Then HLKF is a parallelogram, HK is its diameter, and AG, ME are parallelograms, and LB, BF the so-called complements, about HK; therefore LB is equal to BF. [I. 43]

But BF is equal to the triangle C; therefore LB is also equal to C. [C.N. 1]

And, since the angle GBE is equal to the angle ABM, [I. 15] while the angle GBE is equal to D, the angle ABM is also equal to the angle D.

Therefore the parallelogram LB equal to the given triangle C has been applied to the given straight line AB, in the angle ABM which is equal to D.

Q. E. F.
state.lean_proof:
/-- To a given straight line to apply, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a
given triangle. -/
theorem Prop44 {A B C₁ C₂ C₃ D₁ D D₂ P : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hC : Triangle C₁ C₂ C₃)
    (hD : Triangle D₁ D D₂) (hP : ¬ Collinear A B P) :
    ∃ L M : Point, SameSideOf M P A B ∧ Parallelogram A B M L ∧
      ∠ A B M = ∠ D₁ D D₂ ∧ quadArea A B M L = △ C₁ C₂ C₃ := by
  -- Let AB be the given straight line, C the given triangle and D the given rectilineal angle;
  -- thus it is required to apply to the given straight line AB, in an angle equal to the angle
  -- D, a parallelogram equal to the given triangle C.
  obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B hAB
  -- Let the parallelogram BEFG be constructed equal to the triangle C, in the angle EBG which
  -- is equal to D [I. 42];
  obtain ⟨E₀, F₀, G₀, -, -, h42, hang42, harea42⟩ := Prop42 hC hD
  -- let it be placed so that BE is in a straight line with AB;
  /- G goes on the side away from P, so that the complement will stand on P's side. -/
  obtain ⟨X, hXP, -⟩ := exists_oppositeSidesOf (show Triangle A B P from hP) []
  obtain ⟨E, F, G, hABE, hGX, hBEFG, hEBG, harea⟩ := Prop44.place hAB hXP.triangle h42
  have hE_AB : OnLine E AB := on_line_of_between hABE hA_AB hB_AB
  have hBE : B ≠ E := (ne_of_between (between_symm hABE)).symm
  have hBG : B ≠ G := hBEFG.2.2.1.symm
  obtain ⟨BG, hB_BG, hG_BG⟩ := Postulate1 B G hBG
  obtain ⟨EF, hE_EF, hF_EF⟩ := Postulate1 E F hBEFG.2.1
  obtain ⟨FG, hF_FG, hG_FG⟩ := Postulate1 F G hBEFG.1.2.1
  have hAB_FG : Parallel AB FG := hBEFG.1.parallel hB_AB hE_AB hF_FG hG_FG
  have hEF_BG : Parallel EF BG := hBEFG.2.parallel hE_EF hF_EF hG_BG hB_BG
  have hG_AB : ¬ OnLine G AB := hAB_FG.symm.not_onLine hG_FG
  -- let FG be drawn through to H, and let AH be drawn through A parallel to either BG or EF.
  -- [I. 31]
  have hA_BG : ¬ OnLine A BG := fun h =>
    hG_AB ((line_unique hAB.symm hB_BG h hB_AB hA_AB) ▸ hG_BG)
  obtain ⟨AH, hA_AH, hAH_BG⟩ := Prop31.line hA_BG
  have hFG_BG : FG ≠ BG := fun e => hAB_FG.not_onLine hB_AB (e ▸ hB_BG)
  obtain ⟨H, hH_FG, hH_AH⟩ := Prop30.meet hAH_BG hG_BG hG_FG hFG_BG
  have hHGF : Between H G F := hABE.of_sameSide hB_BG (hAH_BG.sameSide hH_AH hA_AH)
    (hEF_BG.sameSide hF_EF hE_EF) hG_BG ⟨FG, hH_FG, hG_FG, hF_FG⟩
  have hAE : A ≠ E := ne_of_between_ends hABE
  have hAH_EF_ne : AH ≠ EF := fun e =>
    hAB_FG.not_onLine ((line_unique hAE hA_AB hE_AB (e ▸ hA_AH) hE_EF) ▸ hF_EF) hF_FG
  have hAH_EF : Parallel AH EF := Prop30.parallel hAH_BG hEF_BG hAH_EF_ne
  have hAH : A ≠ H := fun e => hAB_FG.not_onLine hA_AB (e ▸ hH_FG)
  have hHF : H ≠ F := fun e => hAH_EF.not_onLine hH_AH (e ▸ hF_EF)
  -- Let HB be joined.
  have hHB : H ≠ B := fun e => hAB_FG.not_onLine hB_AB (e ▸ hH_FG)
  obtain ⟨HB, hH_HB, hB_HB⟩ := Postulate1 H B hHB
  -- Then, since the straight line HF falls upon the parallels AH, EF, the angles AHF, HFE are
  -- equal to two right angles. [I. 29]
  have hAE_FG : SameSide A E FG := hAB_FG.sameSide hA_AB hE_AB
  have hAHFE : AreParallel H A F E :=
    AreParallel.of_parallel hAH.symm hBEFG.2.1.symm hH_AH hA_AH hF_EF hE_EF hAH_EF
  have h29 : ∠ A H F + ∠ H F E = ∟ + ∟ :=
    Prop29.interior hAHFE (SameSideOf.of_line hHF hH_FG hF_FG hAE_FG)
  -- Therefore the angles BHG, GFE are less than two right angles;
  have hBE_AH : SameSide B E AH := pasch2 hABE hA_AH (fun h => hAH_BG.not_onLine h hB_BG)
  have hEF_AH : SameSide E F AH := hAH_EF.symm.sameSide hE_EF hF_EF
  have hBF_HA : SameSideOf B F H A :=
    SameSideOf.of_line hAH.symm hH_AH hA_AH (same_side_trans (same_side_symm hBE_AH) hEF_AH)
  have hBA_HF : SameSideOf B A H F :=
    SameSideOf.of_line hHF hH_FG hF_FG (hAB_FG.sameSide hB_AB hA_AB)
  have hAHF : ∠ A H F = ∠ A H B + ∠ B H F := angle_add_of_within hBF_HA hBA_HF
  have hlt : ∠ B H F + ∠ H F E < ∟ + ∟ :=
    calc ∠ B H F + ∠ H F E < (∠ B H F + ∠ H F E) + ∠ A H B :=
          CommonNotion5 hBF_HA.triangle.bac.angle_pos
      _ = ∟ + ∟ := by rw [← h29, hAHF]; ac_rfl
  have hBHG : ∠ B H G = ∠ B H F := angle_onRay_right (OnRay.of_between hHGF) hHB.symm
  have hGFE : ∠ G F E = ∠ H F E := angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between (between_symm hHGF)) hBEFG.2.1
  have hlt' : ∠ B H G + ∠ G F E < ∟ + ∟ := by rw [hBHG, hGFE]; exact hlt
  -- and straight lines produced indefinitely from angles less than two right angles meet;
  -- [Post. 5] therefore HB, FE, when produced, will meet.
  have hmeet : ∃ K : Point, OnLine K HB ∧ OnLine K EF ∧ SameSide K B FG :=
    Postulate5 hB_HB hH_HB hH_FG hF_FG hF_EF hE_EF hHF
      (hAB_FG.sameSide hB_AB hE_AB) (by rw [← hBHG, ← hGFE]; exact hlt')
  -- Let them be produced and meet at K;
  obtain ⟨K, hK_HB, hK_EF, hKB⟩ := hmeet
  have hH_AB : ¬ OnLine H AB := hAB_FG.symm.not_onLine hH_FG
  have hH_BG : ¬ OnLine H BG := hAH_BG.not_onLine hH_AH
  have hK_BG : ¬ OnLine K BG := hEF_BG.not_onLine hK_EF
  have hK_FG : ¬ OnLine K FG := not_on_line_of_same_side hKB
  have hK_AB : ¬ OnLine K AB := fun hK => by
    by_cases hKE : K = E
    · subst hKE
      exact hH_AB ((line_unique hBE hB_HB hK_HB hB_AB hK) ▸ hH_HB)
    · exact hAB_FG.not_onLine ((line_unique hKE hK_EF hE_EF hK hE_AB) ▸ hF_EF) hF_FG
  -- through the point K let KL be drawn parallel to either EA or FH, [I. 31]
  obtain ⟨KL, hK_KL, hKL_FG⟩ := Prop31.line hK_FG
  have hKL_AB : Parallel KL AB :=
    Prop30.parallel hKL_FG hAB_FG (fun e => hK_AB (e ▸ hK_KL))
  -- and let HA, GB be produced to the points L, M.
  have hAH_FG : AH ≠ FG := fun e => hAH_BG.not_onLine (e ▸ hG_FG) hG_BG
  obtain ⟨L, hL_AH, hL_KL⟩ := Prop30.meet hKL_FG hH_FG hH_AH hAH_FG
  obtain ⟨M, hM_BG, hM_KL⟩ := Prop30.meet hKL_FG hG_FG hG_BG hFG_BG.symm
  /- The parallels carry the order A, B, E to every crossing straight line. -/
  have hHBK : Between H B K := hHGF.of_sameSide hG_BG (same_side_refl hH_BG)
    (hEF_BG.sameSide hK_EF hF_EF) hB_BG ⟨HB, hH_HB, hB_HB, hK_HB⟩
  have hFEK : Between F E K := hHBK.of_sameSide hB_AB (hAB_FG.symm.sameSide hF_FG hH_FG)
    (same_side_refl hK_AB) hE_AB ⟨EF, hF_EF, hE_EF, hK_EF⟩
  have hKML : Between K M L := (between_symm hHBK).of_sameSide hB_BG (same_side_refl hK_BG)
    (hAH_BG.sameSide hL_AH hH_AH) hM_BG ⟨KL, hK_KL, hM_KL, hL_KL⟩
  have hLAH : Between L A H := (between_symm hHBK).of_sameSide hB_AB
    (hKL_AB.sameSide hL_KL hK_KL) (same_side_refl hH_AB) hA_AB ⟨AH, hL_AH, hA_AH, hH_AH⟩
  have hGBM : Between G B M := hHBK.of_sameSide hB_AB (hAB_FG.symm.sameSide hG_FG hH_FG)
    (hKL_AB.sameSide hM_KL hK_KL) hB_AB ⟨BG, hG_BG, hB_BG, hM_BG⟩
  -- Then HLKF is a parallelogram, HK is its diameter, and AG, ME are parallelograms, and LB,
  -- BF the so-called complements, about HK;
  have hKL : K ≠ L := fun e => hAH_EF.not_onLine (e ▸ hL_AH) hK_EF
  have hLH : L ≠ H := fun e => hKL_FG.not_onLine hL_KL (e ▸ hH_FG)
  have hHG : H ≠ G := fun e => hAH_BG.not_onLine hH_AH (e ▸ hG_BG)
  have hKM : K ≠ M := fun e => hK_BG (e ▸ hM_BG)
  have hMB : M ≠ B := fun e => hKL_AB.not_onLine hM_KL (e ▸ hB_AB)
  have hML : M ≠ L := fun e => hAH_BG.not_onLine (e ▸ hL_AH) hM_BG
  have hLA' : L ≠ A := fun e => hKL_AB.not_onLine hL_KL (e ▸ hA_AB)
  have hHLKF : Parallelogram H L K F :=
    ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel hLH.symm (ne_of_between_ends hFEK).symm
        hH_AH hL_AH hK_EF hF_EF hAH_EF,
      AreParallel.of_parallel hKL.symm hHF.symm hL_KL hK_KL hF_FG hH_FG hKL_FG⟩
  have hHABG : Parallelogram H A B G :=
    ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel hAH.symm hBG hH_AH hA_AH hB_BG hG_BG hAH_BG,
      AreParallel.of_parallel hAB hHG.symm hA_AB hB_AB hG_FG hH_FG hAB_FG⟩
  have hBMKE : Parallelogram B M K E :=
    ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel hMB.symm (ne_of_between (between_symm hFEK))
        hB_BG hM_BG hK_EF hE_EF hEF_BG.symm,
      AreParallel.of_parallel hKM.symm hBE.symm hM_KL hK_KL hE_AB hB_AB hKL_AB⟩
  have hABML : Parallelogram A B M L :=
    ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel hAB hML hA_AB hB_AB hM_KL hL_KL hKL_AB.symm,
      AreParallel.of_parallel hMB.symm hLA' hB_BG hM_BG hL_AH hA_AH hAH_BG.symm⟩
  -- therefore LB is equal to BF. [I. 43]
  have h43 : quadArea A L M B = quadArea G B E F :=
    Prop43 hHLKF hHBK (between_symm hLAH) (between_symm hKML) (between_symm hFEK)
      (between_symm hHGF) hHABG hBMKE
  have hLB_BF : quadArea A B M L = quadArea B E F G := by
    rw [← quadArea_reverse A B M L, h43, quadArea_rotate₂ E F G B, hBEFG.quadArea_rotate]
  -- But BF is equal to the triangle C;
  have hBF_C : quadArea B E F G = △ C₁ C₂ C₃ := harea.trans harea42
  -- therefore LB is also equal to C. [C.N. 1]
  have hLB_C : quadArea A B M L = △ C₁ C₂ C₃ := CommonNotion1 hLB_BF hBF_C.symm
  -- And, since the angle GBE is equal to the angle ABM, [I. 15]
  have hGBE_ABM : ∠ G B E = ∠ A B M := (Prop15 hABE hGBM fun ⟨ℓ, hA_ℓ, hE_ℓ, hG_ℓ⟩ =>
    hG_AB ((line_unique hAE hA_ℓ hE_ℓ hA_AB hE_AB) ▸ hG_ℓ)).2
  -- while the angle GBE is equal to D,
  have hGBE_D : ∠ G B E = ∠ D₁ D D₂ := by
    rw [angle_symm hBG.symm hBE.symm, hEBG, hang42]
  -- the angle ABM is also equal to the angle D.
  have hABM_D : ∠ A B M = ∠ D₁ D D₂ := hGBE_ABM.symm.trans hGBE_D
  -- Therefore the parallelogram LB equal to the given triangle C has been applied to the given
  -- straight line AB, in the angle ABM which is equal to D.
  have hGP : OppositeSidesOf G P A B := hGX.trans_opposite hXP
  have hGM : OppositeSidesOf G M A B :=
    OppositeSidesOf.of_between (Triangle.of_line hA_AB hB_AB hAB hG_AB) hGBM
  exact ⟨L, M, OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf hGM hGP, hABML, hABM_D, hLB_C⟩
  -- Q. E. F.

theorem Prop44 {A B C₁ C₂ C₃ D₁ D D₂ P : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hC : Triangle C₁ C₂ C₃)

named_declarations.Elements.BookI.Prop44.place:
/-- "Let it be placed so that BE is in a straight line with AB." Euclid moves the
parallelogram made by I.42 into place without a word, as if picking it up. Our
foundations move a figure only by superposition, kept for I.4 and I.8, so we
build an equal one where Euclid puts his. Given the
parallelogram PQRS, with its angle RQP, and a straight line AB: produce AB to
E, making BE equal to QR [I. 2]; at B on BE construct the angle EBG equal
to the angle RQP, on the side of X [I. 23], with BG equal to QP [I. 2];
through G and E draw parallels to BE and BG [I. 31], meeting at F
(`Prop30.meet`). Then BEFG is a parallelogram, and it is equal to PQRS, for each
is double a triangle [I. 34], and the triangles GBE and PQR are equal [I. 4]. -/
theorem Prop44.place {A B X P Q R S : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hX : ¬ Collinear A B X)
    (h : Parallelogram P Q R S) :
    ∃ E F G : Point, Between A B E ∧ SameSideOf G X A B ∧ Parallelogram B E F G ∧
      ∠ E B G = ∠ R Q P ∧ quadArea B E F G = quadArea P Q R S

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D

state.enunciation: To a given straight line to apply, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given triangle.
state.heath_proof:
Let AB be the given straight line, C the given triangle and D the given rectilineal angle; thus it is required to apply to the given straight line AB, in an angle equal to the angle D, a parallelogram equal to the given triangle C.

Let the parallelogram BEFG be constructed equal to the triangle C, in the angle EBG which is equal to D [I. 42]; let it be placed so that BE is in a straight line with AB; let FG be drawn through to H, and let AH be drawn through A parallel to either BG or EF. [I. 31]

Let HB be joined.

Then, since the straight line HF falls upon the parallels AH, EF, the angles AHF, HFE are equal to two right angles. [I. 29]

Therefore the angles BHG, GFE are less than two right angles; and straight lines produced indefinitely from angles less than two right angles meet; [Post. 5] therefore HB, FE, when produced, will meet.

Let them be produced and meet at K; through the point K let KL be drawn parallel to either EA or FH, [I. 31] and let HA, GB be produced to the points L, M.

Then HLKF is a parallelogram, HK is its diameter, and AG, ME are parallelograms, and LB, BF the so-called complements, about HK; therefore LB is equal to BF. [I. 43]

But BF is equal to the triangle C; therefore LB is also equal to C. [C.N. 1]

And, since the angle GBE is equal to the angle ABM, [I. 15] while the angle GBE is equal to D, the angle ABM is also equal to the angle D.

Therefore the parallelogram LB equal to the given triangle C has been applied to the given straight line AB, in the angle ABM which is equal to D.

Q. E. F.

state.enunciation: To construct, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given rectilineal figure.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABCD be the given rectilineal figure and E the given rectilineal angle; thus it is required to construct, in the given angle E, a parallelogram equal to the rectilineal figure ABCD.

Let DB be joined, and let the parallelogram FH be constructed equal to the triangle ABD, in the angle HKF which is equal to E; [I. 42] let the parallelogram GM equal to the triangle DBC be applied to the straight line GH, in the angle GHM which is equal to E. [I. 44]

Then, since the angle E is equal to each of the angles HKF, GHM, the angle HKF is also equal to the angle GHM. [C.N. 1]

Let the angle KHG be added to each; therefore the angles FKH, KHG are equal to the angles KHG, GHM.

But the angles FKH, KHG are equal to two right angles; [I. 29] therefore the angles KHG, GHM are also equal to two right angles.

Thus, with a straight line GH, and at the point H on it, two straight lines KH, HM not lying on the same side make the adjacent angles equal to two right angles; therefore KH is in a straight line with HM. [I. 14]

And, since the straight line HG falls upon the parallels KM, FG, the alternate angles MHG, HGF are equal to one another. [I. 29]

Let the angle HGL be added to each; therefore the angles MHG, HGL are equal to the angles HGF, HGL. [C.N. 2]

But the angles MHG, HGL are equal to two right angles; [I. 29] therefore the angles HGF, HGL are also equal to two right angles. [C.N. 1]

Therefore FG is in a straight line with GL. [I. 14]

And, since FK is equal and parallel to HG, [I. 34] and HG to ML also, KF is also equal and parallel to ML; [C.N. 1; I. 30] and the straight lines KM, FL join them (at their extremities); therefore KM, FL are also equal and parallel. [I. 33]

Therefore KFLM is a parallelogram.

And, since the triangle ABD is equal to the parallelogram FH, and DBC to GM, the whole rectilineal figure ABCD is equal to the whole parallelogram KFLM.

Therefore the parallelogram KFLM has been constructed equal to the given rectilineal figure ABCD, in the angle FKM which is equal to the given angle E.

Q. E. F.

theorem Prop45 {A B C D E₁ E E₂ : Point} (hABD : Triangle A B D) (hDBC : Triangle D B C)

statement.note: With its companions: `Prop45.apart` takes any figure given with triangles that lie apart, `Prop45.fan` Euclid's division from one corner; `Prop45` his ABD, DBC.

representation.note: A rectilineal figure is given with its division into triangles, and the division is checked: as triangles that lie apart, no point inside two of them, for any figure, a figure with a hole among them (`Prop45.apart`); as triangles glued edge to edge in a suitable order, for a figure with one boundary (`Prop45.figure`); or as Euclid and Oliver Byrne divide it, from one corner, neighbours on opposite sides of the straight line they share and the angles at that corner together less than four right angles, the triangles then shown to fit together (`Prop45.fan`, by `Fitted.fan`). Equal to the figure means equal to those triangles together. That every figure can be so divided, and that another division gives the same sum, are not proved here; David Hilbert proved the second, for his measure of area. In `Prop45.fan`, `Fitted.fan` proves that the triangles fit together; the Lean does not state that their figure is bounded by the closed line through the corners in order, though this is true in the plane. The construction does not use that the triangles lie apart, which is what makes their sum the figure's: it is `Prop45.sum`'s, for any triangles. The main theorem is an area-sum theorem: it takes ABD and DBC unchecked, and they may overlap. It represents Euclid's pictured division when A and C lie on opposite sides of DB; that checked case is `Prop45.fan` for the corners D, A, B, C. Full coverage is carried by `Prop45.apart`, for any figure given with any division into triangles that lie apart.

figure-with-dissection.meaning: A rectilineal figure is given with its division into triangles, checked: any division, as triangles that lie apart, no point inside two of them, so that the figure may have a hole; or, for a figure with one boundary, triangles glued edge to edge in a suitable order, each across a side of an earlier one and meeting the earlier ones only along it; or, as Euclid and Byrne divide it, the triangles from one corner, neighbours on opposite sides of the straight line they share and the angles at that corner together less than four right angles. Equal to the figure means equal to those triangles together. That every figure can be so divided, and that another division gives the same sum, are not proved here; Hilbert proved the second, for his measure of area (I.45, II.14).

bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34:
/-- In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the
diameter bisects the areas. -/
theorem Prop34 {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A C D B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ C D B ∧ ∠ A B D = ∠ A C D ∧
      △ A B C = △ D C B
bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34.bisect:
/-- The diameter bisects the parallelogram, said of its area: the parallelogram
ABCD, measured by its diameter AC, is double the triangle ABC. I.35–I.47 cite
I.34 for this ("the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram EBCA; for the diameter
AB bisects it"). To halve by the other diameter, name the parallelogram from the
next corner (`Parallelogram.rotate`) and turn its area round with
`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`. [I. 34] -/
theorem Prop34.bisect {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea A B C D = △ A B C + △ A B C
bridges.Elements.Fitted.fan:
/-- **Euclid's and Oliver Byrne's division is a figure, when it is checked.** A figure given
by its corners A₀, A₁, A₂, …, Aₙ, the list `ps` being A₃, …, Aₙ, and divided by the straight
lines from A₀ into the triangles A₀A₁A₂, A₀A₂A₃, …, A₀Aₙ₋₁Aₙ, one on each side
`segments (A₁ :: A₂ :: ps)`. Suppose each is a triangle; each two neighbouring triangles,
A₀Aᵢ₋₁Aᵢ and A₀AᵢAᵢ₊₁, lie on opposite sides of the straight line A₀Aᵢ they share, that is,
Aᵢ₋₁ and Aᵢ₊₁ are on opposite sides of it (one condition for each of
`triples (A₁ :: A₂ :: ps)`); and the angles A₁A₀A₂, A₂A₀A₃, …, Aₙ₋₁A₀Aₙ at A₀ together are
less than four right angles. Then those triangles, in that order, are fitted together into
one figure: each is laid across the straight line A₀Aᵢ against the one before it, and meets
the earlier ones only along that straight line. The figure they make is read as the figure
with corners A₀, A₁, …, Aₙ in order round it; that its boundary is the closed line A₀A₁…AₙA₀
is not stated in Lean.

The two conditions are what make the triangles turn one way round A₀ and not come round on
themselves, so that they do not overlap. Euclid's ABCD, divided from D by DB, is the figure
with corners D, A, B, C: A and C are on opposite sides of DB, and the two angles at D,
each less than two right angles, are together less than four. -/
theorem Fitted.fan {A₀ A₁ A₂ : Point} {ps : List Point}
    (htri : ∀ s ∈ segments (A₁ :: A₂ :: ps), Triangle A₀ s.1 s.2)
    (hopp : ∀ t ∈ triples (A₁ :: A₂ :: ps), OppositeSidesOf t.1 t.2.2 A₀ t.2.1)
    (hA₀ : Magnitude.sum ((segments (A₁ :: A₂ :: ps)).map fun s => ∠ s.1 A₀ s.2) <
      ∟ + ∟ + (∟ + ∟)) :
    Fitted ((segments (A₁ :: A₂ :: ps)).map fun s => (A₀, s.1, s.2))
bridges.Elements.Fitted.inside_pairwise:
/-- **The triangles of a figure do not overlap**: no point is inside two of them. Each new
triangle meets the earlier ones only along the side it is glued to, and a point inside a
triangle is off its sides. This is what makes the sum of the triangles the area of the figure
they make up (`Rectilineal.area`), and it pins that meaning of `Fitted` against a later
change of the definition. -/
theorem Fitted.inside_pairwise {ps : List (Point × Point × Point)} (h : Fitted ps) :
    ps.Pairwise (fun s s' => ∀ Y : Point,
      InsideTriangle Y s.1 s.2.1 s.2.2 → ¬ InsideTriangle Y s'.1 s'.2.1 s'.2.2)
bridges.Elements.Fitted.triangle:
/-- Each piece of a figure is a triangle: its corners are not on one straight line. -/
theorem Fitted.triangle {ps : List (Point × Point × Point)} (h : Fitted ps) :
    ∀ t ∈ ps, Triangle t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.cross:
/-- The diameters of a parallelogram cross: in the parallelogram ABCD, some point
lies between A and C and between B and D. Its sides AB and DC are
parallel, so they do not cross, and `AreParallel.cross_or` leaves only the
diameters. -/
theorem Parallelogram.cross (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    ∃ X : Point, Between A X C ∧ Between B X D
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate:
/-- A parallelogram has the same area whichever diameter cuts it: the parallelogram
ABCD measured by BD, as BCDA, is the same as measured by AC. -/
theorem Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea B C D A = quadArea A B C D
bridges.Elements.Rectilineal.area_toApart:
/-- **The area is the same sum**: the area of a glued figure taken with triangles that lie
apart is its area as a glued figure. Lean checks it by unfolding, so the two definitions of
the sum, `Apart.area` and `Rectilineal.area`, cannot drift apart. -/
theorem Rectilineal.area_toApart (R : Rectilineal) : R.toApart.area = R.area
bridges.Elements.Rectilineal.toApart:
/-- **A figure glued together, taken with triangles that lie apart**: the same triangles,
which lie apart by `Fitted.inside_pairwise`. A companion that takes `Apart` takes a glued
figure R as `R.toApart`: `Prop45.figure` and `Prop14.figure` are `Prop45.apart` and
`Prop14.apart` for it, and `Prop14.square R.toApart` draws its square. -/
def Rectilineal.toApart (R : Rectilineal) : Apart :=
  ⟨R.pieces, R.fitted.ne_nil, R.fitted.triangle, R.fitted.inside_pairwise⟩
