definitions.Apart:
/-- **A rectilineal figure, given with triangles that lie apart** (Definition I.14: a figure
is "that which is contained by any boundary or boundaries"; Definition I.19: rectilineal
figures are "those which are contained by straight lines"): any division of it into
triangles, each named by its three corners, at least one; each a triangle; and no point
inside two of them. The figure is the triangles together. It may have a hole, as a square
with a smaller square cut from its middle has, may touch itself at a corner, and may be in
more than one piece. No order of the triangles is asked, and a triangle may lie against part
of a side of another. A figure given by gluing is one of these, its triangles lying apart by
`Fitted.inside_pairwise`. That every rectilineal figure, with any boundaries, can be cut
into triangles that lie apart is not stated in Lean. -/
structure Apart where
  /-- The triangles the figure is cut into. -/
  pieces : List (Point × Point × Point)
  /-- There is at least one. -/
  ne : pieces ≠ []
  /-- Each is a triangle: its corners are not on one straight line. -/
  triangle : ∀ t ∈ pieces, Triangle t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2
  /-- No point is inside two of them. -/
  apart : pieces.Pairwise fun s s' => ∀ Y : Point,
    InsideTriangle Y s.1 s.2.1 s.2.2 → ¬ InsideTriangle Y s'.1 s'.2.1 s'.2.2
definitions.Apart.area:
/-- **The area of a figure given with triangles that lie apart, as given**: the sum of its
triangles. As with `Rectilineal.area`, that another division of the same figure gives the
same sum is not proved here (Book I's gap catalogue, under I.45), so this is the area of the
figure with its division, not yet a measure of the figure alone. -/
noncomputable def Apart.area (R : Apart) : Area :=
  Magnitude.sum (R.pieces.map fun t => △ t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2)
definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Corners:
/-- The triangle `t` has the corners `P`, `Q`, `R`: read from some corner, one way round or
the other, it is `(P, Q, R)`. So `PQ` is one of its sides, and `R` the corner opposite. -/
def Corners (t : Point × Point × Point) (P Q R : Point) : Prop :=
  t = (P, Q, R) ∨ t = (Q, R, P) ∨ t = (R, P, Q) ∨ t = (Q, P, R) ∨ t = (P, R, Q) ∨
    t = (R, Q, P)
definitions.Fitted:
/-- **Triangles fitted together into one rectilineal figure**, in the order listed.

* `single`: one triangle is a figure.
* `glue`: a figure, with a new triangle `PQX` laid against the side `PQ` of one of its
  triangles `t`, whose third corner is `R`. The new triangle lies across that side, `X` being
  on the other side of `PQ` from `R`; and it meets the triangles already there only along
  `PQ`: a point within or on the new triangle, and within or on one of the earlier ones,
  lies on the finite straight line `PQ`.

The new triangle goes at the end of the list. A figure made this way may be convex or not.
Every figure made this way is bounded by one closed line that neither crosses nor touches
itself, with no hole; and every such figure can be cut this way, since it can be cut into
triangles by straight lines joining its corners, and those triangles, listed so that each
after the first shares a side with one before it, with each later triangle named so that
its attached side is its first two corners, satisfy the rule: a later triangle meets an
earlier one that is not its neighbour only at an end of the side it is glued along.
Neither fact is stated in Lean. That no point is inside two of the triangles is stated, and
proved (`Fitted.inside_pairwise`). So every such figure has a division that is fitted, but
not every division of it is: a ring of triangles round a point inside it is not (below),
nor is a list whose later triangle is named from the wrong corner, as the square ABCD cut
along AC and listed ABC, ADC (the second must be named with AC as its first two corners,
ACD or CAD).

A ring of triangles closing up round a point, or round a hole, is not made this way, for its
last triangle would meet the others along two sides. A triangle laid against part of a
side, or against two sides in line, is not glued this way either; its figure is cut
differently. A figure with a hole cannot be cut so as to be glued. Any division of any
figure, with a hole or without, is taken given with triangles that lie apart (`Apart`), and
a fitted figure's triangles lie apart too. -/
inductive Fitted : List (Point × Point × Point) → Prop
  | single {A B C : Point} (h : Triangle A B C) : Fitted [(A, B, C)]
  | glue {ps : List (Point × Point × Point)} {t : Point × Point × Point} {P Q R X : Point}
      (hps : Fitted ps) (ht : t ∈ ps) (hside : Corners t P Q R)
      (hX : OppositeSidesOf X R P Q)
      (hmeet : ∀ Y : Point, OnOrInsideTriangle Y P Q X →
        ∀ s ∈ ps, OnOrInsideTriangle Y s.1 s.2.1 s.2.2 → OnFiniteLine Y P Q) :
      Fitted (ps ++ [(P, Q, X)])
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.Magnitude.sum:
/-- **The sum of a list of magnitudes** of one kind: nothing for the empty list, and
otherwise the first added to the sum of the rest. So `Magnitude.sum [a, b, c]` is
`a + (b + (c + 0))`, which is `a + b + c`. -/
noncomputable def Magnitude.sum {k : Kind} : List (Magnitude k) → Magnitude k
  | [] => 0
  | a :: as => a + Magnitude.sum as
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnFiniteLine:
/-- `Y` lies on the finite straight line `PQ`: it is one of the ends, or between them. -/
def OnFiniteLine (Y P Q : Point) : Prop := Y = P ∨ Y = Q ∨ Between P Y Q
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.OnOrInsideTriangle:
/-- `Y` lies within the triangle `ABC` or on its boundary: inside it, on one of its sides
between two corners, or at a corner. -/
def OnOrInsideTriangle (Y A B C : Point) : Prop :=
  InsideTriangle Y A B C ∨ Between A Y B ∨ Between B Y C ∨ Between C Y A ∨
    Y = A ∨ Y = B ∨ Y = C
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.Rectilineal:
/-- **A rectilineal figure with one boundary, given with its triangles fitted together**
(Definition I.19: "Rectilineal figures are those which are contained by straight lines"):
the triangles it is cut into, each named by its three corners, in an order in which they
fit together, with the proof that they do. The figure is the triangles together. -/
structure Rectilineal where
  /-- The triangles the figure is cut into, in the order they were fitted. -/
  pieces : List (Point × Point × Point)
  /-- They fit together into one figure. -/
  fitted : Fitted pieces
definitions.Rectilineal.area:
/-- **The area of a rectilineal figure, as given**: the sum of the triangles it is given
with, which do not overlap (`Fitted.inside_pairwise`) and make up the figure. That another
division of the same figure gives the same sum is not proved here (Book I's gap catalogue,
under I.45), so this is the area of the figure with its division, not yet a measure of the
figure alone. -/
noncomputable def Rectilineal.area (R : Rectilineal) : Area :=
  Magnitude.sum (R.pieces.map fun t => △ t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2)
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle
definitions.segments:
/-- **The segments** of a straight line cut at points in order: each point of the list with
the next, as the ends of one segment. The segments of `[B, D, E, C]` are BD, DE and EC. The
points need not be in order, or on one straight line: in the companions of I.45 and II.14
for a checked fan (`Prop45.fan`, `Prop14.fan`), the segments of a figure's corners A₁, A₂,
…, Aₙ are its sides A₁A₂, …, Aₙ₋₁Aₙ, those away from the corner A₀, and each side with A₀
makes one of the triangles into which the straight lines from A₀ divide the figure, when the
fan's conditions hold. -/
def segments : List Point → List (Point × Point)
  | p :: q :: rest => (p, q) :: segments (q :: rest)
  | _ => []
definitions.triples:
/-- **The corners three at a time**: each corner of the list with the next two. The triples
of `[A₁, A₂, A₃, A₄]` are A₁A₂A₃ and A₂A₃A₄. In a division from one corner A₀, the middle
corner of each triple is the far end of the straight line A₀Aᵢ that two neighbouring
triangles share, and the other two are their third corners. -/
def triples : List Point → List (Point × Point × Point)
  | p :: q :: r :: rest => (p, q, r) :: triples (q :: r :: rest)
  | _ => []

state.enunciation: To construct, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given rectilineal figure.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABCD be the given rectilineal figure and E the given rectilineal angle; thus it is required to construct, in the given angle E, a parallelogram equal to the rectilineal figure ABCD.

Let DB be joined, and let the parallelogram FH be constructed equal to the triangle ABD, in the angle HKF which is equal to E; [I. 42] let the parallelogram GM equal to the triangle DBC be applied to the straight line GH, in the angle GHM which is equal to E. [I. 44]

Then, since the angle E is equal to each of the angles HKF, GHM, the angle HKF is also equal to the angle GHM. [C.N. 1]

Let the angle KHG be added to each; therefore the angles FKH, KHG are equal to the angles KHG, GHM.

But the angles FKH, KHG are equal to two right angles; [I. 29] therefore the angles KHG, GHM are also equal to two right angles.

Thus, with a straight line GH, and at the point H on it, two straight lines KH, HM not lying on the same side make the adjacent angles equal to two right angles; therefore KH is in a straight line with HM. [I. 14]

And, since the straight line HG falls upon the parallels KM, FG, the alternate angles MHG, HGF are equal to one another. [I. 29]

Let the angle HGL be added to each; therefore the angles MHG, HGL are equal to the angles HGF, HGL. [C.N. 2]

But the angles MHG, HGL are equal to two right angles; [I. 29] therefore the angles HGF, HGL are also equal to two right angles. [C.N. 1]

Therefore FG is in a straight line with GL. [I. 14]

And, since FK is equal and parallel to HG, [I. 34] and HG to ML also, KF is also equal and parallel to ML; [C.N. 1; I. 30] and the straight lines KM, FL join them (at their extremities); therefore KM, FL are also equal and parallel. [I. 33]

Therefore KFLM is a parallelogram.

And, since the triangle ABD is equal to the parallelogram FH, and DBC to GM, the whole rectilineal figure ABCD is equal to the whole parallelogram KFLM.

Therefore the parallelogram KFLM has been constructed equal to the given rectilineal figure ABCD, in the angle FKM which is equal to the given angle E.

Q. E. F.
state.lean_proof:
/-- To construct, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given rectilineal figure. -/
theorem Prop45 {A B C D E₁ E E₂ : Point} (hABD : Triangle A B D) (hDBC : Triangle D B C)
    (hE : Triangle E₁ E E₂) :
    ∃ K F L M : Point, Parallelogram K F L M ∧ ∠ F K M = ∠ E₁ E E₂ ∧
      quadArea K F L M = △ A B D + △ D B C := by
  -- Let ABCD be the given rectilineal figure and E the given rectilineal angle; thus it is
  -- required to construct, in the given angle E, a parallelogram equal to the rectilineal
  -- figure ABCD.
  -- Let DB be joined, and let the parallelogram FH be constructed equal to the triangle ABD,
  -- in the angle HKF which is equal to E; [I. 42] let the parallelogram GM equal to the
  -- triangle DBC be applied to the straight line GH, in the angle GHM which is equal to
  -- E. [I. 44]
  /- I.42 builds on half of the triangle's own base, so KH lies along BD and H
     falls on D: the Lean writes D wherever Euclid writes H, and in our figure KFLM
     overlaps ABCD. K lies between B and D, and F is on A's side of BD. -/
  obtain ⟨K, F, G, hBKD, hFA, hFKHG, hHKF, hFH⟩ := Prop42 hABD hE
  have hGHK : Triangle G D K := hFKHG.1.symm.swap_right.triangle.bac
  /- I.44's point for the side is taken across GH from K, so that KH and HM are
     "not lying on the same side", as I.14 will ask. -/
  obtain ⟨P, hPK, -⟩ := exists_oppositeSidesOf hGHK []
  obtain ⟨L, M, hMP, hGHML, hGHM, hGM⟩ := Prop44 hGHK.ne₁₂ hDBC hE hPK.triangle
  have hMK : OppositeSidesOf M K G D := hMP.trans_opposite hPK
  have hKD : K ≠ D := hGHK.ne₂₃.symm
  have hGD : G ≠ D := hGHK.ne₁₂
  have hFK : F ≠ K := hFKHG.1.1
  -- Then, since the angle E is equal to each of the angles HKF, GHM, the angle HKF is also
  -- equal to the angle GHM. [C.N. 1]
  have hHKF_GHM : ∠ D K F = ∠ G D M := CommonNotion1 hHKF hGHM
  -- Let the angle KHG be added to each; therefore the angles FKH, KHG are equal to the angles
  -- KHG, GHM.
  have hsum₁ : ∠ F K D + ∠ K D G = ∠ K D G + ∠ G D M := by
    rw [angle_symm hFK hKD.symm, hHKF_GHM, add_comm]
  -- But the angles FKH, KHG are equal to two right angles; [I. 29] therefore the angles KHG,
  -- GHM are also equal to two right angles.
  have hFG_KH : SameSideOf F G K D := hFKHG.rotate.sameSideOf.symm
  have h29a : ∠ F K D + ∠ K D G = ∟ + ∟ := Prop29.interior hFKHG.1.swap_left hFG_KH
  have hKHG_GHM : ∠ K D G + ∠ G D M = ∟ + ∟ := hsum₁.symm.trans h29a
  -- Thus, with a straight line GH, and at the point H on it, two straight lines KH, HM not
  -- lying on the same side make the adjacent angles equal to two right angles; therefore KH is
  -- in a straight line with HM. [I. 14]
  have hKHM : Between K D M := Prop14 hMK.symm (by
    rw [angle_symm hGD hKD]
    exact hKHG_GHM)
  -- And, since the straight line HG falls upon the parallels KM, FG, the alternate angles MHG,
  -- HGF are equal to one another. [I. 29]
  have hFK_HG : SameSideOf F K D G := hFKHG.rotate.rotate.sameSideOf
  have hMD : M ≠ D := ne_of_between (between_symm hKHM)
  obtain ⟨KM, hK_KM, hM_KM⟩ := Postulate1 K M (ne_of_between_ends hKHM)
  have hD_KM : OnLine D KM := on_line_of_between_ends hKHM hK_KM hM_KM
  obtain ⟨FG, hF_FG, hG_FG⟩ := Postulate1 F G hFKHG.2.2.1.symm
  have hKM_FG : Parallel KM FG := hFKHG.2.parallel hK_KM hD_KM hG_FG hF_FG
  have hMHGF : AreParallel M D G F :=
    AreParallel.of_parallel hMD hFKHG.2.2.1 hM_KM hD_KM hG_FG hF_FG hKM_FG
  have hMF : OppositeSidesOf M F D G := (hFK_HG.trans_opposite hMK.symm.swap).symm
  have hMHG_HGF : ∠ M D G = ∠ D G F := Prop29.alternate hMHGF hMF
  -- Let the angle HGL be added to each; therefore the angles MHG, HGL are equal to the angles
  -- HGF, HGL. [C.N. 2]
  have hsum₂ : ∠ M D G + ∠ D G L = ∠ D G F + ∠ D G L := CommonNotion2 hMHG_HGF rfl
  -- But the angles MHG, HGL are equal to two right angles; [I. 29] therefore the angles HGF,
  -- HGL are also equal to two right angles. [C.N. 1]
  have hML_HG : SameSideOf M L D G := hGHML.sameSideOf.swap
  have h29c : ∠ M D G + ∠ D G L = ∟ + ∟ := Prop29.interior hGHML.2.swap_right hML_HG
  have hHGF_HGL : ∠ D G F + ∠ D G L = ∟ + ∟ := CommonNotion1 hsum₂.symm h29c.symm
  -- Therefore FG is in a straight line with GL. [I. 14]
  have hFL : OppositeSidesOf F L D G :=
    hFK_HG.trans_opposite (hML_HG.symm.trans_opposite hMK.swap).symm
  have hFGL : Between F G L := Prop14 hFL hHGF_HGL
  -- And, since FK is equal and parallel to HG, [I. 34] and HG to ML also, KF is also equal and
  -- parallel to ML; [C.N. 1; I. 30] and the straight lines KM, FL join them (at their
  -- extremities); therefore KM, FL are also equal and parallel. [I. 33]
  obtain ⟨-, hFK_GH, -, -, -⟩ := Prop34 (A := F) (B := G) (C := K) (D := D) hFKHG
  obtain ⟨-, hGH_LM, -, -, -⟩ := Prop34 (A := G) (B := L) (C := D) (D := M) hGHML
  have hlen : ‖K F‖ = ‖M L‖ :=
    CommonNotion1 ((len_symm K F).trans hFK_GH) (hGH_LM.trans (len_symm L M)).symm
  obtain ⟨KF, hK_KF, hF_KF⟩ := Postulate1 K F hFK.symm
  obtain ⟨ML, hM_ML, hL_ML⟩ := Postulate1 M L hGHML.1.2.1
  obtain ⟨GD, hG_GD, hD_GD⟩ := Postulate1 G D hGD
  have hKF_GD : Parallel KF GD := hFKHG.1.swap_left.parallel hK_KF hF_KF hD_GD hG_GD
  have hML_GD : Parallel ML GD := hGHML.1.symm.parallel hM_ML hL_ML hG_GD hD_GD
  have hKF_ML : KF ≠ ML := fun e => by
    have hK_ML : OnLine K ML := e ▸ hK_KF
    have : ML = KM := line_unique (ne_of_between_ends hKHM) hK_ML hM_ML hK_KM hM_KM
    exact hML_GD.not_onLine (this ▸ hD_KM) hD_GD
  have hpar : AreParallel K F M L :=
    AreParallel.of_parallel hFK.symm hGHML.1.2.1 hK_KF hF_KF hM_ML hL_ML
      (Prop30.parallel hKF_GD hML_GD hKF_ML)
  have hdir : SameSideOf F L K M := by
    have hF : SameSide F G KM := hFG_KH.sameSide hK_KM hD_KM
    have hL : SameSide L G KM := hGHML.rotate.sameSideOf.sameSide hD_KM hM_KM
    exact SameSideOf.of_line (ne_of_between_ends hKHM) hK_KM hM_KM
      (same_side_trans (same_side_symm hF) (same_side_symm hL))
  obtain ⟨-, h33⟩ := Prop33 hpar hlen hdir
  -- Therefore KFLM is a parallelogram.
  have hKFLM : Parallelogram K F L M := ⟨hpar.swap_right, h33.symm.swap_right⟩
  -- And, since the triangle ABD is equal to the parallelogram FH, and DBC to GM, the whole
  -- rectilineal figure ABCD is equal to the whole parallelogram KFLM.
  have hwhole : quadArea K F L M = △ A B D + △ D B C := by
    rw [quadArea_add_of_parallelograms hFKHG.rotate.reverse hGHML.rotate.reverse hKHM hFGL,
      quadArea_reverse K D G F, hFKHG.quadArea_rotate, hFH,
      quadArea_reverse D M L G, hGHML.quadArea_rotate, hGM]
  -- Therefore the parallelogram KFLM has been constructed equal to the given rectilineal
  -- figure ABCD, in the angle FKM which is equal to the given angle E.
  refine ⟨K, F, L, M, hKFLM, ?_, hwhole⟩
  rw [angle_onRay_right (OnRay.of_beyond hKHM) hFK, angle_symm hFK hKD.symm]
  exact hHKF
  -- Q. E. F.

helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.of_parallel:
/-- Two different points of L, and two different points of M, are the ends of
parallel straight lines when L and M are parallel: two points fix one straight
line (System E, Generalities 1). With `AreParallel.parallel`, this says "AB is
parallel to CD" of any other two points P, Q of the straight line AB and R,
S of CD. -/
theorem AreParallel.of_parallel (hPQ : P ≠ Q) (hRS : R ≠ S) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L)
    (hR : OnLine R M) (hS : OnLine S M) (h : Parallel L M) : AreParallel P Q R S
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.parallel:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then a straight line through A and B is parallel
to one through C and D. -/
theorem AreParallel.parallel (h : AreParallel A B C D) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (hC : OnLine C M) (hD : OnLine D M) : Parallel L M
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.sameSideOf:
/-- The ends of one parallel lie on one side of the other: if AB is parallel to
CD, then A and B are on the same side of CD (`Parallel.sameSide`). -/
theorem AreParallel.sameSideOf (h : AreParallel A B C D) : SameSideOf A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.swap_left:
/-- "AB is parallel to CD" is the same as "BA is parallel to CD". -/
theorem AreParallel.swap_left (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel B A C D
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.swap_right:
/-- "AB is parallel to CD" is the same as "AB is parallel to DC". -/
theorem AreParallel.swap_right (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel A B D C
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.symm:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then CD is parallel to AB. -/
theorem AreParallel.symm (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.triangle:
/-- An end of one parallel is off the other: if AB is parallel to CD, then C
is not on the straight line AB, and ABC is a triangle. (Turned round with
`AreParallel.symm` and `.swap_right`, the same holds of D, and of A and B
beside CD.) -/
theorem AreParallel.triangle (h : AreParallel A B C D) : Triangle A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop14:
/-- If with any straight line, and at a point on it, two straight lines not lying on the same side
make the adjacent angles equal to two right angles, the two straight lines will be in a straight
line with one another. -/
theorem Prop14 {A B C D : Point} (hCD : OppositeSidesOf C D A B) (h : ∠ A B C + ∠ A B D = ∟ + ∟) :
    Between C B D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29:
/-- A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one
another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on
the same side equal to two right angles. -/
theorem Prop29 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (hpar : AreParallel A B C D) (hAGB : Between A G B)
    (hCHD : Between C H D) (hEGH : Between E G H) (hGHF : Between G H F)
    (hBD : SameSideOf B D E F) :
    ∠ A G H = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ E G B = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D = ∟ + ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29.alternate:
/-- The alternate angles. If the straight line PG is parallel to HQ, and P and
Q lie on opposite sides of GH, then the alternate angles PGH, GHQ are equal.
Euclid's figure is drawn about GH, each straight line produced beyond G and H
(`AreParallel.figure_alternate`), and I.29 does the rest. [I. 29] -/
theorem Prop29.alternate {P G H Q : Point} (hpar : AreParallel P G H Q)
    (hPQ : OppositeSidesOf P Q G H) : ∠ P G H = ∠ G H Q
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29.interior:
/-- The interior angles on the same side. If the straight line GP is parallel to
HQ, and P and Q lie on one side of GH, then the angles PGH, GHQ are
equal to two right angles. [I. 29] -/
theorem Prop29.interior {P G H Q : Point} (hpar : AreParallel G P H Q)
    (hPQ : SameSideOf P Q G H) : ∠ P G H + ∠ G H Q = ∟ + ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30:
/-- Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another. -/
theorem Prop30 {A B C D E F : Point} (h₁ : AreParallel A B E F) (h₂ : AreParallel C D E F)
    (hC : ¬ Collinear A B C) :
    AreParallel A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30.parallel:
/-- I.30 said of straight lines drawn and named: two different straight lines L and
M, each parallel to N, are parallel to one another. Euclid uses it without a
bracket in I.44 and I.47, where a straight line drawn "parallel to either" of two
parallels is parallel to both; in I.45 he brackets it. [I. 30] -/
theorem Prop30.parallel {L M N : Line} (hL : Parallel L N) (hM : Parallel M N) (hLM : L ≠ M) :
    Parallel L M
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop33:
/-- The straight lines joining equal and parallel straight lines (at the extremities which are) in
the same directions (respectively) are themselves also equal and parallel. -/
theorem Prop33 {A B C D : Point} (hpar : AreParallel A B C D) (heq : ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖)
    (hdir : SameSideOf B D A C) :
    ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ AreParallel A C B D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop34:
/-- In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the
diameter bisects the areas. -/
theorem Prop34 {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A C D B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ C D B ∧ ∠ A B D = ∠ A C D ∧
      △ A B C = △ D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop42:
/-- To construct, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given triangle. -/
theorem Prop42 {A B C D₁ D D₂ : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hD : Triangle D₁ D D₂) :
    ∃ E F G : Point, Between B E C ∧ SameSideOf F A B C ∧ Parallelogram F E C G ∧
      ∠ C E F = ∠ D₁ D D₂ ∧ quadArea F E C G = △ A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop44:
/-- To a given straight line to apply, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a
given triangle. -/
theorem Prop44 {A B C₁ C₂ C₃ D₁ D D₂ P : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hC : Triangle C₁ C₂ C₃)
    (hD : Triangle D₁ D D₂) (hP : ¬ Collinear A B P) :
    ∃ L M : Point, SameSideOf M P A B ∧ Parallelogram A B M L ∧
      ∠ A B M = ∠ D₁ D D₂ ∧ quadArea A B M L = △ C₁ C₂ C₃
helper_signatures.Elements.CommonNotion1:
/-- **Common Notion 1.** Things which are equal to the same thing are also equal
to one another. -/
theorem CommonNotion1 {α : Sort _} {a b c : α} (h₁ : a = c) (h₂ : b = c) : a = b
helper_signatures.Elements.CommonNotion2:
/-- **Common Notion 2.** If equals be added to equals, the wholes are equal. -/
theorem CommonNotion2 {a b c d : Magnitude k} (h₁ : a = b) (h₂ : c = d) :
    a + c = b + d
helper_signatures.Elements.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.of_beyond:
/-- A point beyond B, on the straight line from A through B produced, is on
the ray from A through B. -/
theorem OnRay.of_beyond (h : Between A B P) : OnRay P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.symm:
/-- P is on the ray from A through B exactly when B is on the ray from A
through P: they are one and the same ray. -/
theorem OnRay.symm (h : OnRay P A B) : OnRay B A P
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf:
/-- `P` and `Q` lie on opposite sides of the straight line `AB`. -/
def OppositeSidesOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf:
/-- The same, said of "the straight line AB": two points, each on the other side of
AB from C, are on the same side of AB as each other. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf {C D E : Point} (h₁ : OppositeSidesOf C D A B)
    (h₂ : OppositeSidesOf C E A B) : SameSideOf D E A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.swap:
/-- "On opposite sides of AB" is the same as "on opposite sides of BA". -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.swap (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : OppositeSidesOf P Q B A
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the other side of AB from Q, then Q is on the other side
from P. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.symm (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : OppositeSidesOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.triangle:
/-- A point on either side of the straight line AB is not on it, so ABP is a
triangle. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.triangle (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : Triangle A B P
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.not_onLine:
/-- Parallels do not meet: a point of L is not on M. -/
theorem Parallel.not_onLine (h : Parallel L M) (hP : OnLine P L) : ¬ OnLine P M
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.sameSide:
/-- All the points of one parallel lie on one side of the other: two points of L
are on the same side of M. Were they on opposite sides, the straight line L
joining them would cross M (System E, Intersection 1). -/
theorem Parallel.sameSide (h : Parallel L M) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L) :
    SameSide P Q M
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.symm:
/-- If L is parallel to M, then M is parallel to L. -/
theorem Parallel.symm (h : Parallel L M) : Parallel M L
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate:
/-- A parallelogram has the same area whichever diameter cuts it: the parallelogram
ABCD measured by BD, as BCDA, is the same as measured by AC. -/
theorem Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea B C D A = quadArea A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.reverse:
/-- The parallelogram ABCD, read the other way round from A, is the
parallelogram ADCB. -/
theorem Parallelogram.reverse (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Parallelogram A D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.rotate:
/-- The parallelogram ABCD, named from B, is the parallelogram BCDA. -/
theorem Parallelogram.rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Parallelogram B C D A
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.sameSideOf:
/-- In the parallelogram ABCD, the far corners C and D lie on one side of the
side AB. (Named from another corner with `.rotate`, the same holds of every
side.) -/
theorem Parallelogram.sameSideOf (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : SameSideOf C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.triangle:
/-- In the parallelogram ABCD, the corner C is off the straight line AB, so
ABC is a triangle. -/
theorem Parallelogram.triangle (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Triangle A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate1:
/-- **Postulate 1.** To draw a straight line from any point to any point. -/
axiom Postulate1 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf:
/-- `P` and `Q` lie on the same side of the straight line `AB`. -/
def SameSideOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.of_line:
/-- Two points on the same side of a straight line L through A and B are on
the same side of the straight line AB, however that line is named: two points
fix one straight line. -/
theorem SameSideOf.of_line (hAB : A ≠ B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (h : SameSide P Q L) : SameSideOf P Q A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.sameSide:
/-- Two points on the same side of the straight line AB are on the same side of
any straight line drawn through A and B. -/
theorem SameSideOf.sameSide (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    SameSide P Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.swap:
/-- "On the same side of AB" is the same as "on the same side of BA". -/
theorem SameSideOf.swap (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf P Q B A
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the same side of AB as Q, then Q is on the same side as P. -/
theorem SameSideOf.symm (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.trans:
/-- Points on the same side as a third are on the same side as each other. -/
theorem SameSideOf.trans (h₁ : SameSideOf P Q A B) (h₂ : SameSideOf Q R A B) :
    SameSideOf P R A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.trans_opposite:
/-- A point on Q's side of the straight line AB, where Q is on the other side
from R, is itself on the other side from R. -/
theorem SameSideOf.trans_opposite (h₁ : SameSideOf P Q A B) (h₂ : OppositeSidesOf Q R A B) :
    OppositeSidesOf P R A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.triangle:
/-- A point on one side of the straight line AB is not on it, so ABP is a
triangle. -/
theorem SameSideOf.triangle (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : Triangle A B P
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.add_comm:
/-- The order of adding does not matter. (System E §3.5) -/
axiom add_comm (a b : Magnitude k) : a + b = b + a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.angle_symm:
/-- The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4) -/
axiom angle_symm (hAB : A ≠ B) (hCB : C ≠ B) : ∠ A B C = ∠ C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_symm:
/-- If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1) -/
axiom between_symm (h : Between A B C) : Between C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.len_symm:
/-- The straight line AB is the straight line BA. (Metric 3) -/
axiom len_symm (A B : Point) : ‖A B‖ = ‖B A‖
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.line_unique:
/-- Two points determine a straight line. (Generalities 1) -/
axiom line_unique (hAB : A ≠ B) (hAL : OnLine A L) (hBL : OnLine B L) (hAM : OnLine A M)
    (hBM : OnLine B M) : L = M
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between:
/-- A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between_ends:
/-- The ends of a finite straight line differ. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between_ends:
/-- A straight line through A and C passes through every point between them.
(Between 3) -/
axiom on_line_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hC : OnLine C L) :
    OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.same_side_symm:
/-- If A is on the same side of a straight line as B, then B is on the same side
as A. (Same side 2) -/
axiom same_side_symm (h : SameSide A B L) : SameSide B A L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.same_side_trans:
/-- Two points on the same side of a straight line as a third point are on the same
side as each other. (Same side 4) -/
axiom same_side_trans (h₁ : SameSide A B L) (h₂ : SameSide A C L) : SameSide B C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.bac:
/-- The triangle ABC, named the other way round, as BAC. -/
theorem Triangle.bac (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₁₂:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₁₂ (h : Triangle A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₂₃:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₂₃ (h : Triangle A B C) : B ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_onRay_right:
/-- The other arm traced through another point of its ray: if C' is on the ray
from A through C, the angle BAC' is the angle BAC. (System E,
Diagram-angle 4) -/
theorem angle_onRay_right {C' : Point} (hC : OnRay C' A C) (hBA : B ≠ A) :
    ∠ B A C' = ∠ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.exists_oppositeSidesOf:
/-- "Let a point be taken at random on the other side of the straight line AB"
(I.12): if P is off the straight line AB, there is a point on the other side
of it from P, which may be chosen different from any points already in the
figure. (System E, Points 6) -/
theorem exists_oppositeSidesOf (hP : Triangle A B P) (avoid : List Point) :
    ∃ Q : Point, OppositeSidesOf Q P A B ∧ Q ∉ avoid
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea_add_of_parallelograms:
/-- A parallelogram cut by a straight line parallel to two of its sides is the two
parallelograms it is cut into. If E lies between A and D, F between B and
C, and ABFE, EFCD are parallelograms, then the figure ABCD is ABFE and
EFCD together. Cut each piece and the whole into triangles from A and C; the
four-sided figure AFCE is measured by AC in the whole and by FE in the pieces,
and its diameters cross, for A and C lie on either side of EF. -/
theorem quadArea_add_of_parallelograms (h₁ : Parallelogram A B F E) (h₂ : Parallelogram E F C D)
    (hAED : Between A E D) (hBFC : Between B F C) :
    quadArea A B C D = quadArea A B F E + quadArea E F C D
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea_reverse:
/-- The figure ABCD read the other way round, as ADCB, has the same diameter
AC, and the same area. -/
theorem quadArea_reverse (A B C D : Point) : quadArea A D C B = quadArea A B C D

I.14.enunciation: If with any straight line, and at a point on it, two straight lines not lying on the same side make the adjacent angles equal to two right angles, the two straight lines will be in a straight line with one another.

I.29.enunciation: A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on the same side equal to two right angles.

I.30.enunciation: Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another.

I.33.enunciation: The straight lines joining equal and parallel straight lines (at the extremities which are) in the same directions (respectively) are themselves also equal and parallel.

I.34.enunciation: In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the diameter bisects the areas.

I.42.enunciation: To construct, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given triangle.

I.44.enunciation: To a given straight line to apply, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given triangle.

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ P ≠ A ∧ Collinear A B P ∧ ¬ Between P A B
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rightAngle:

state.enunciation: To construct, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given rectilineal figure.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABCD be the given rectilineal figure and E the given rectilineal angle; thus it is required to construct, in the given angle E, a parallelogram equal to the rectilineal figure ABCD.

Let DB be joined, and let the parallelogram FH be constructed equal to the triangle ABD, in the angle HKF which is equal to E; [I. 42] let the parallelogram GM equal to the triangle DBC be applied to the straight line GH, in the angle GHM which is equal to E. [I. 44]

Then, since the angle E is equal to each of the angles HKF, GHM, the angle HKF is also equal to the angle GHM. [C.N. 1]

Let the angle KHG be added to each; therefore the angles FKH, KHG are equal to the angles KHG, GHM.

But the angles FKH, KHG are equal to two right angles; [I. 29] therefore the angles KHG, GHM are also equal to two right angles.

Thus, with a straight line GH, and at the point H on it, two straight lines KH, HM not lying on the same side make the adjacent angles equal to two right angles; therefore KH is in a straight line with HM. [I. 14]

And, since the straight line HG falls upon the parallels KM, FG, the alternate angles MHG, HGF are equal to one another. [I. 29]

Let the angle HGL be added to each; therefore the angles MHG, HGL are equal to the angles HGF, HGL. [C.N. 2]

But the angles MHG, HGL are equal to two right angles; [I. 29] therefore the angles HGF, HGL are also equal to two right angles. [C.N. 1]

Therefore FG is in a straight line with GL. [I. 14]

And, since FK is equal and parallel to HG, [I. 34] and HG to ML also, KF is also equal and parallel to ML; [C.N. 1; I. 30] and the straight lines KM, FL join them (at their extremities); therefore KM, FL are also equal and parallel. [I. 33]

Therefore KFLM is a parallelogram.

And, since the triangle ABD is equal to the parallelogram FH, and DBC to GM, the whole rectilineal figure ABCD is equal to the whole parallelogram KFLM.

Therefore the parallelogram KFLM has been constructed equal to the given rectilineal figure ABCD, in the angle FKM which is equal to the given angle E.

Q. E. F.
state.lean_proof:
/-- **I.45, for any rectilineal figure, with any boundaries** (companion of I.45). To
construct, in a given rectilineal angle E, a parallelogram KFLM, its angle at K equal to E,
equal to a given rectilineal figure: the figure given with any division of it into
triangles, no point inside two of them (`Apart`), and "equal to the figure" meaning equal
to those triangles taken together (`Apart.area`). The figure may have a hole, touch itself
at a corner, or be in more than one piece. It is `Prop45.sum` for the figure's triangles;
lying apart is what makes their sum the figure's. Nothing is claimed of another division of
the figure. -/
theorem Prop45.apart {E₁ E E₂ : Point} (R : Apart) (hE : Triangle E₁ E E₂) :
    ∃ K F L M : Point, Parallelogram K F L M ∧ ∠ F K M = ∠ E₁ E E₂ ∧
      quadArea K F L M = R.area :=
  Prop45.sum R.pieces R.ne R.triangle hE

helper_signatures.Elements.Apart:
/-- **A rectilineal figure, given with triangles that lie apart** (Definition I.14: a figure
is "that which is contained by any boundary or boundaries"; Definition I.19: rectilineal
figures are "those which are contained by straight lines"): any division of it into
triangles, each named by its three corners, at least one; each a triangle; and no point
inside two of them. The figure is the triangles together. It may have a hole, as a square
with a smaller square cut from its middle has, may touch itself at a corner, and may be in
more than one piece. No order of the triangles is asked, and a triangle may lie against part
of a side of another. A figure given by gluing is one of these, its triangles lying apart by
`Fitted.inside_pairwise`. That every rectilineal figure, with any boundaries, can be cut
into triangles that lie apart is not stated in Lean. -/
structure Apart where
  /-- The triangles the figure is cut into. -/
  pieces : List (Point × Point × Point)
  /-- There is at least one. -/
  ne : pieces ≠ []
  /-- Each is a triangle: its corners are not on one straight line. -/
  triangle : ∀ t ∈ pieces, Triangle t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2
  /-- No point is inside two of them. -/
  apart : pieces.Pairwise fun s s' => ∀ Y : Point,
    InsideTriangle Y s.1 s.2.1 s.2.2 → ¬ InsideTriangle Y s'.1 s'.2.1 s'.2.2
helper_signatures.Elements.Apart.area:
/-- **The area of a figure given with triangles that lie apart, as given**: the sum of its
triangles. As with `Rectilineal.area`, that another division of the same figure gives the
same sum is not proved here (Book I's gap catalogue, under I.45), so this is the area of the
figure with its division, not yet a measure of the figure alone. -/
noncomputable def Apart.area (R : Apart) : Area
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.triangle:
/-- An end of one parallel is off the other: if AB is parallel to CD, then C
is not on the straight line AB, and ABC is a triangle. (Turned round with
`AreParallel.symm` and `.swap_right`, the same holds of D, and of A and B
beside CD.) -/
theorem AreParallel.triangle (h : AreParallel A B C D) : Triangle A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop45.sum:
/-- **I.45, any number of triangles** (companion of I.45). To construct, in a given
rectilineal angle E, a parallelogram equal to any number of given triangles taken together,
at least one: I.42 for the first, then `Prop45.append` for each of the rest, in order. The
triangles are any triangles, each with its corners off one straight line; they need not fit
together into one figure, and the statement claims nothing of a figure. -/
theorem Prop45.sum {E₁ E E₂ : Point} (ts : List (Point × Point × Point)) (hne : ts ≠ [])
    (hts : ∀ t ∈ ts, Triangle t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2) (hE : Triangle E₁ E E₂) :
    ∃ K F L M : Point, Parallelogram K F L M ∧ ∠ F K M = ∠ E₁ E E₂ ∧
      quadArea K F L M = Magnitude.sum (ts.map fun t => △ t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2)
helper_signatures.Elements.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.triangle:
/-- In the parallelogram ABCD, the corner C is off the straight line AB, so
ABC is a triangle. -/
theorem Parallelogram.triangle (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Triangle A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.triangle:
/-- A point on one side of the straight line AB is not on it, so ABP is a
triangle. -/
theorem SameSideOf.triangle (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : Triangle A B P
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area

I.14.enunciation: If with any straight line, and at a point on it, two straight lines not lying on the same side make the adjacent angles equal to two right angles, the two straight lines will be in a straight line with one another.

I.29.enunciation: A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on the same side equal to two right angles.

I.30.enunciation: Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another.

I.33.enunciation: The straight lines joining equal and parallel straight lines (at the extremities which are) in the same directions (respectively) are themselves also equal and parallel.

I.34.enunciation: In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the diameter bisects the areas.

I.42.enunciation: To construct, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given triangle.

I.44.enunciation: To a given straight line to apply, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given triangle.

I.45 sum.enunciation: To construct, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given rectilineal figure.

definitions.Apart:
/-- **A rectilineal figure, given with triangles that lie apart** (Definition I.14: a figure
is "that which is contained by any boundary or boundaries"; Definition I.19: rectilineal
figures are "those which are contained by straight lines"): any division of it into
triangles, each named by its three corners, at least one; each a triangle; and no point
inside two of them. The figure is the triangles together. It may have a hole, as a square
with a smaller square cut from its middle has, may touch itself at a corner, and may be in
more than one piece. No order of the triangles is asked, and a triangle may lie against part
of a side of another. A figure given by gluing is one of these, its triangles lying apart by
`Fitted.inside_pairwise`. That every rectilineal figure, with any boundaries, can be cut
into triangles that lie apart is not stated in Lean. -/
structure Apart where
  /-- The triangles the figure is cut into. -/
  pieces : List (Point × Point × Point)
  /-- There is at least one. -/
  ne : pieces ≠ []
  /-- Each is a triangle: its corners are not on one straight line. -/
  triangle : ∀ t ∈ pieces, Triangle t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2
  /-- No point is inside two of them. -/
  apart : pieces.Pairwise fun s s' => ∀ Y : Point,
    InsideTriangle Y s.1 s.2.1 s.2.2 → ¬ InsideTriangle Y s'.1 s'.2.1 s'.2.2
definitions.Apart.area:
/-- **The area of a figure given with triangles that lie apart, as given**: the sum of its
triangles. As with `Rectilineal.area`, that another division of the same figure gives the
same sum is not proved here (Book I's gap catalogue, under I.45), so this is the area of the
figure with its division, not yet a measure of the figure alone. -/
noncomputable def Apart.area (R : Apart) : Area :=
  Magnitude.sum (R.pieces.map fun t => △ t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2)
definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.Magnitude.sum:
/-- **The sum of a list of magnitudes** of one kind: nothing for the empty list, and
otherwise the first added to the sum of the rest. So `Magnitude.sum [a, b, c]` is
`a + (b + (c + 0))`, which is `a + b + c`. -/
noncomputable def Magnitude.sum {k : Kind} : List (Magnitude k) → Magnitude k
  | [] => 0
  | a :: as => a + Magnitude.sum as
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D

state.lean_proof:
/-- **I.45, one more triangle** (companion of I.45). Given a parallelogram KFLM in the
given rectilineal angle E, and a triangle ABC, to construct a parallelogram in the same
angle equal to KFLM and ABC together: the second half of Euclid's proof, which applies a
parallelogram equal to the triangle to a side of the first [I. 44] and shows that the two
make one. -/
theorem Prop45.append {A B C K F L M E₁ E E₂ : Point} (hKFLM : Parallelogram K F L M)
    (hang : ∠ F K M = ∠ E₁ E E₂) (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hE : Triangle E₁ E E₂) :
    ∃ K' F' L' M' : Point, Parallelogram K' F' L' M' ∧ ∠ F' K' M' = ∠ E₁ E E₂ ∧
      quadArea K' F' L' M' = quadArea K F L M + △ A B C := by
  /- Here M is Euclid's H and L is G; the new corners L', M' are his L, M.
     Read the given parallelogram as FKML, and apply the new one to LM across
     that side from K, so that I.14 can join KM to MM'. -/
  have hFKML : Parallelogram F K M L := hKFLM.rotate.reverse
  have hLMK : Triangle L M K := hFKML.1.symm.swap_right.triangle.bac
  obtain ⟨P, hPK, -⟩ := exists_oppositeSidesOf hLMK []
  obtain ⟨L', M', hM'P, hLMM'L', hLMM', hadded⟩ :=
    Prop44 hLMK.ne₁₂ hABC hE hPK.triangle
  have hM'K : OppositeSidesOf M' K L M := hM'P.trans_opposite hPK
  have hKM : K ≠ M := hLMK.ne₂₃.symm
  have hLM : L ≠ M := hLMK.ne₁₂
  have hFK : F ≠ K := hFKML.1.1
  /- The angles FKM and LMM' both equal E. Add KML to each; I.29 makes
     the first pair two right angles, hence the second pair also. -/
  have hFKM_LMM' : ∠ F K M = ∠ L M M' := CommonNotion1 hang hLMM'
  have hsum₁ : ∠ F K M + ∠ K M L = ∠ K M L + ∠ L M M' := by
    rw [hFKM_LMM', add_comm]
  have hFL_KM : SameSideOf F L K M := hFKML.rotate.sameSideOf.symm
  have hFKM_KML : ∠ F K M + ∠ K M L = ∟ + ∟ :=
    Prop29.interior hFKML.1.swap_left hFL_KM
  have hKML_LMM' : ∠ K M L + ∠ L M M' = ∟ + ∟ :=
    hsum₁.symm.trans hFKM_KML
  /- K and M' lie on opposite sides of LM, and the angles KML, LMM' are two
     right angles, so I.14 puts KM in a straight line with MM', with M
     between K and M'. -/
  have hKMM' : Between K M M' := Prop14 hM'K.symm (by
    rw [angle_symm hLM hKM]
    exact hKML_LMM')
  /- ML falls on the parallels KM' and FL, so I.29 equates the alternate
     angles M'ML and MLF. -/
  have hFK_ML : SameSideOf F K M L := hFKML.rotate.rotate.sameSideOf
  have hM'M : M' ≠ M := ne_of_between (between_symm hKMM')
  obtain ⟨KM', hK_KM', hM'_KM'⟩ := Postulate1 K M' (ne_of_between_ends hKMM')
  have hM_KM' : OnLine M KM' := on_line_of_between_ends hKMM' hK_KM' hM'_KM'
  obtain ⟨FL, hF_FL, hL_FL⟩ := Postulate1 F L hFKML.2.2.1.symm
  have hKM'_FL : Parallel KM' FL := hFKML.2.parallel hK_KM' hM_KM' hL_FL hF_FL
  have hM'MLF : AreParallel M' M L F :=
    AreParallel.of_parallel hM'M hFKML.2.2.1 hM'_KM' hM_KM' hL_FL hF_FL hKM'_FL
  have hM'F : OppositeSidesOf M' F M L := (hFK_ML.trans_opposite hM'K.symm.swap).symm
  have hM'ML_MLF : ∠ M' M L = ∠ M L F := Prop29.alternate hM'MLF hM'F
  /- Add MLL' to each. I.29 makes M'ML and MLL' two right angles,
     so MLF and MLL' are two right angles too. -/
  have hsum₂ : ∠ M' M L + ∠ M L L' = ∠ M L F + ∠ M L L' :=
    CommonNotion2 hM'ML_MLF rfl
  have hM'L'_ML : SameSideOf M' L' M L := hLMM'L'.sameSideOf.swap
  have hM'ML_MLL' : ∠ M' M L + ∠ M L L' = ∟ + ∟ :=
    Prop29.interior hLMM'L'.2.swap_right hM'L'_ML
  have hMLF_MLL' : ∠ M L F + ∠ M L L' = ∟ + ∟ :=
    CommonNotion1 hsum₂.symm hM'ML_MLL'.symm
  /- F and L' lie on opposite sides of ML, so I.14 puts FL and LL'
     in one straight line. -/
  have hFL' : OppositeSidesOf F L' M L :=
    hFK_ML.trans_opposite (hM'L'_ML.symm.trans_opposite hM'K.swap).symm
  have hFLL' : Between F L L' := Prop14 hFL' hMLF_MLL'
  /- I.34 gives FK equal to LM and LM equal to L'M'. The outer sides FK
     and L'M' are parallel to LM, and are not one straight line, for that
     line would be KM', which meets LM at M; I.30 makes KF parallel to M'L'. -/
  obtain ⟨-, hFK_LM, -, -, -⟩ := Prop34 (A := F) (B := L) (C := K) (D := M) hFKML
  obtain ⟨-, hLM_L'M', -, -, -⟩ :=
    Prop34 (A := L) (B := L') (C := M) (D := M') hLMM'L'
  have hlen : ‖K F‖ = ‖M' L'‖ :=
    CommonNotion1 ((len_symm K F).trans hFK_LM) (hLM_L'M'.trans (len_symm L' M')).symm
  obtain ⟨KF, hK_KF, hF_KF⟩ := Postulate1 K F hFK.symm
  obtain ⟨M'L', hM'_M'L', hL'_M'L'⟩ := Postulate1 M' L' hLMM'L'.1.2.1
  obtain ⟨LM, hL_LM, hM_LM⟩ := Postulate1 L M hLM
  have hKF_LM : Parallel KF LM := hFKML.1.swap_left.parallel hK_KF hF_KF hM_LM hL_LM
  have hM'L'_LM : Parallel M'L' LM :=
    hLMM'L'.1.symm.parallel hM'_M'L' hL'_M'L' hL_LM hM_LM
  have hKF_M'L' : KF ≠ M'L' := fun e => by
    have hK_M'L' : OnLine K M'L' := e ▸ hK_KF
    have hline : M'L' = KM' :=
      line_unique (ne_of_between_ends hKMM') hK_M'L' hM'_M'L' hK_KM' hM'_KM'
    exact hM'L'_LM.not_onLine (hline ▸ hM_KM') hM_LM
  have hpar : AreParallel K F M' L' :=
    AreParallel.of_parallel hFK.symm hLMM'L'.1.2.1 hK_KF hF_KF hM'_M'L' hL'_M'L'
      (Prop30.parallel hKF_LM hM'L'_LM hKF_M'L')
  /- KM' and FL' join the equal parallels in the same direction. By I.33
     they too are parallel, completing the parallelogram KFL'M'. -/
  have hdir : SameSideOf F L' K M' := by
    have hF : SameSide F L KM' := hFL_KM.sameSide hK_KM' hM_KM'
    have hL' : SameSide L' L KM' := hLMM'L'.rotate.sameSideOf.sameSide hM_KM' hM'_KM'
    exact SameSideOf.of_line (ne_of_between_ends hKMM') hK_KM' hM'_KM'
      (same_side_trans (same_side_symm hF) (same_side_symm hL'))
  obtain ⟨-, h33⟩ := Prop33 hpar hlen hdir
  have hwhole : Parallelogram K F L' M' := ⟨hpar.swap_right, h33.symm.swap_right⟩
  /- The whole is the two parallelograms together, and the added one equals
     ABC. The ray KM' is the ray KM, so the angle at K remains E. -/
  have harea : quadArea K F L' M' = quadArea K F L M + △ A B C := by
    rw [quadArea_add_of_parallelograms hKFLM hLMM'L'.rotate.reverse hKMM' hFLL',
      quadArea_reverse M M' L' L, hLMM'L'.quadArea_rotate, hadded]
  refine ⟨K, F, L', M', hwhole, ?_, harea⟩
  rw [angle_onRay_right (OnRay.of_beyond hKMM') hFK]
  exact hang

helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.of_parallel:
/-- Two different points of L, and two different points of M, are the ends of
parallel straight lines when L and M are parallel: two points fix one straight
line (System E, Generalities 1). With `AreParallel.parallel`, this says "AB is
parallel to CD" of any other two points P, Q of the straight line AB and R,
S of CD. -/
theorem AreParallel.of_parallel (hPQ : P ≠ Q) (hRS : R ≠ S) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L)
    (hR : OnLine R M) (hS : OnLine S M) (h : Parallel L M) : AreParallel P Q R S
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.parallel:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then a straight line through A and B is parallel
to one through C and D. -/
theorem AreParallel.parallel (h : AreParallel A B C D) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (hC : OnLine C M) (hD : OnLine D M) : Parallel L M
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.sameSideOf:
/-- The ends of one parallel lie on one side of the other: if AB is parallel to
CD, then A and B are on the same side of CD (`Parallel.sameSide`). -/
theorem AreParallel.sameSideOf (h : AreParallel A B C D) : SameSideOf A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.swap_left:
/-- "AB is parallel to CD" is the same as "BA is parallel to CD". -/
theorem AreParallel.swap_left (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel B A C D
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.swap_right:
/-- "AB is parallel to CD" is the same as "AB is parallel to DC". -/
theorem AreParallel.swap_right (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel A B D C
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.symm:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then CD is parallel to AB. -/
theorem AreParallel.symm (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.triangle:
/-- An end of one parallel is off the other: if AB is parallel to CD, then C
is not on the straight line AB, and ABC is a triangle. (Turned round with
`AreParallel.symm` and `.swap_right`, the same holds of D, and of A and B
beside CD.) -/
theorem AreParallel.triangle (h : AreParallel A B C D) : Triangle A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop14:
/-- If with any straight line, and at a point on it, two straight lines not lying on the same side
make the adjacent angles equal to two right angles, the two straight lines will be in a straight
line with one another. -/
theorem Prop14 {A B C D : Point} (hCD : OppositeSidesOf C D A B) (h : ∠ A B C + ∠ A B D = ∟ + ∟) :
    Between C B D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29:
/-- A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one
another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on
the same side equal to two right angles. -/
theorem Prop29 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (hpar : AreParallel A B C D) (hAGB : Between A G B)
    (hCHD : Between C H D) (hEGH : Between E G H) (hGHF : Between G H F)
    (hBD : SameSideOf B D E F) :
    ∠ A G H = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ E G B = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D = ∟ + ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29.alternate:
/-- The alternate angles. If the straight line PG is parallel to HQ, and P and
Q lie on opposite sides of GH, then the alternate angles PGH, GHQ are equal.
Euclid's figure is drawn about GH, each straight line produced beyond G and H
(`AreParallel.figure_alternate`), and I.29 does the rest. [I. 29] -/
theorem Prop29.alternate {P G H Q : Point} (hpar : AreParallel P G H Q)
    (hPQ : OppositeSidesOf P Q G H) : ∠ P G H = ∠ G H Q
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29.interior:
/-- The interior angles on the same side. If the straight line GP is parallel to
HQ, and P and Q lie on one side of GH, then the angles PGH, GHQ are
equal to two right angles. [I. 29] -/
theorem Prop29.interior {P G H Q : Point} (hpar : AreParallel G P H Q)
    (hPQ : SameSideOf P Q G H) : ∠ P G H + ∠ G H Q = ∟ + ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30:
/-- Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another. -/
theorem Prop30 {A B C D E F : Point} (h₁ : AreParallel A B E F) (h₂ : AreParallel C D E F)
    (hC : ¬ Collinear A B C) :
    AreParallel A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30.parallel:
/-- I.30 said of straight lines drawn and named: two different straight lines L and
M, each parallel to N, are parallel to one another. Euclid uses it without a
bracket in I.44 and I.47, where a straight line drawn "parallel to either" of two
parallels is parallel to both; in I.45 he brackets it. [I. 30] -/
theorem Prop30.parallel {L M N : Line} (hL : Parallel L N) (hM : Parallel M N) (hLM : L ≠ M) :
    Parallel L M
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop33:
/-- The straight lines joining equal and parallel straight lines (at the extremities which are) in
the same directions (respectively) are themselves also equal and parallel. -/
theorem Prop33 {A B C D : Point} (hpar : AreParallel A B C D) (heq : ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖)
    (hdir : SameSideOf B D A C) :
    ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ AreParallel A C B D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop34:
/-- In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the
diameter bisects the areas. -/
theorem Prop34 {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A C D B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ C D B ∧ ∠ A B D = ∠ A C D ∧
      △ A B C = △ D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop44:
/-- To a given straight line to apply, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a
given triangle. -/
theorem Prop44 {A B C₁ C₂ C₃ D₁ D D₂ P : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hC : Triangle C₁ C₂ C₃)
    (hD : Triangle D₁ D D₂) (hP : ¬ Collinear A B P) :
    ∃ L M : Point, SameSideOf M P A B ∧ Parallelogram A B M L ∧
      ∠ A B M = ∠ D₁ D D₂ ∧ quadArea A B M L = △ C₁ C₂ C₃
helper_signatures.Elements.CommonNotion1:
/-- **Common Notion 1.** Things which are equal to the same thing are also equal
to one another. -/
theorem CommonNotion1 {α : Sort _} {a b c : α} (h₁ : a = c) (h₂ : b = c) : a = b
helper_signatures.Elements.CommonNotion2:
/-- **Common Notion 2.** If equals be added to equals, the wholes are equal. -/
theorem CommonNotion2 {a b c d : Magnitude k} (h₁ : a = b) (h₂ : c = d) :
    a + c = b + d
helper_signatures.Elements.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.of_beyond:
/-- A point beyond B, on the straight line from A through B produced, is on
the ray from A through B. -/
theorem OnRay.of_beyond (h : Between A B P) : OnRay P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.symm:
/-- P is on the ray from A through B exactly when B is on the ray from A
through P: they are one and the same ray. -/
theorem OnRay.symm (h : OnRay P A B) : OnRay B A P
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf:
/-- `P` and `Q` lie on opposite sides of the straight line `AB`. -/
def OppositeSidesOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf:
/-- The same, said of "the straight line AB": two points, each on the other side of
AB from C, are on the same side of AB as each other. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf {C D E : Point} (h₁ : OppositeSidesOf C D A B)
    (h₂ : OppositeSidesOf C E A B) : SameSideOf D E A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.swap:
/-- "On opposite sides of AB" is the same as "on opposite sides of BA". -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.swap (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : OppositeSidesOf P Q B A
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the other side of AB from Q, then Q is on the other side
from P. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.symm (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : OppositeSidesOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.triangle:
/-- A point on either side of the straight line AB is not on it, so ABP is a
triangle. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.triangle (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : Triangle A B P
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.not_onLine:
/-- Parallels do not meet: a point of L is not on M. -/
theorem Parallel.not_onLine (h : Parallel L M) (hP : OnLine P L) : ¬ OnLine P M
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.sameSide:
/-- All the points of one parallel lie on one side of the other: two points of L
are on the same side of M. Were they on opposite sides, the straight line L
joining them would cross M (System E, Intersection 1). -/
theorem Parallel.sameSide (h : Parallel L M) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L) :
    SameSide P Q M
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.symm:
/-- If L is parallel to M, then M is parallel to L. -/
theorem Parallel.symm (h : Parallel L M) : Parallel M L
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate:
/-- A parallelogram has the same area whichever diameter cuts it: the parallelogram
ABCD measured by BD, as BCDA, is the same as measured by AC. -/
theorem Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea B C D A = quadArea A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.reverse:
/-- The parallelogram ABCD, read the other way round from A, is the
parallelogram ADCB. -/
theorem Parallelogram.reverse (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Parallelogram A D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.rotate:
/-- The parallelogram ABCD, named from B, is the parallelogram BCDA. -/
theorem Parallelogram.rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Parallelogram B C D A
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.sameSideOf:
/-- In the parallelogram ABCD, the far corners C and D lie on one side of the
side AB. (Named from another corner with `.rotate`, the same holds of every
side.) -/
theorem Parallelogram.sameSideOf (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : SameSideOf C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.triangle:
/-- In the parallelogram ABCD, the corner C is off the straight line AB, so
ABC is a triangle. -/
theorem Parallelogram.triangle (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Triangle A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate1:
/-- **Postulate 1.** To draw a straight line from any point to any point. -/
axiom Postulate1 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf:
/-- `P` and `Q` lie on the same side of the straight line `AB`. -/
def SameSideOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.of_line:
/-- Two points on the same side of a straight line L through A and B are on
the same side of the straight line AB, however that line is named: two points
fix one straight line. -/
theorem SameSideOf.of_line (hAB : A ≠ B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (h : SameSide P Q L) : SameSideOf P Q A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.sameSide:
/-- Two points on the same side of the straight line AB are on the same side of
any straight line drawn through A and B. -/
theorem SameSideOf.sameSide (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    SameSide P Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.swap:
/-- "On the same side of AB" is the same as "on the same side of BA". -/
theorem SameSideOf.swap (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf P Q B A
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the same side of AB as Q, then Q is on the same side as P. -/
theorem SameSideOf.symm (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.trans:
/-- Points on the same side as a third are on the same side as each other. -/
theorem SameSideOf.trans (h₁ : SameSideOf P Q A B) (h₂ : SameSideOf Q R A B) :
    SameSideOf P R A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.trans_opposite:
/-- A point on Q's side of the straight line AB, where Q is on the other side
from R, is itself on the other side from R. -/
theorem SameSideOf.trans_opposite (h₁ : SameSideOf P Q A B) (h₂ : OppositeSidesOf Q R A B) :
    OppositeSidesOf P R A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.triangle:
/-- A point on one side of the straight line AB is not on it, so ABP is a
triangle. -/
theorem SameSideOf.triangle (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : Triangle A B P
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.add_comm:
/-- The order of adding does not matter. (System E §3.5) -/
axiom add_comm (a b : Magnitude k) : a + b = b + a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.angle_symm:
/-- The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4) -/
axiom angle_symm (hAB : A ≠ B) (hCB : C ≠ B) : ∠ A B C = ∠ C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_symm:
/-- If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1) -/
axiom between_symm (h : Between A B C) : Between C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.len_symm:
/-- The straight line AB is the straight line BA. (Metric 3) -/
axiom len_symm (A B : Point) : ‖A B‖ = ‖B A‖
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.line_unique:
/-- Two points determine a straight line. (Generalities 1) -/
axiom line_unique (hAB : A ≠ B) (hAL : OnLine A L) (hBL : OnLine B L) (hAM : OnLine A M)
    (hBM : OnLine B M) : L = M
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between:
/-- A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between_ends:
/-- The ends of a finite straight line differ. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between_ends:
/-- A straight line through A and C passes through every point between them.
(Between 3) -/
axiom on_line_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hC : OnLine C L) :
    OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.same_side_symm:
/-- If A is on the same side of a straight line as B, then B is on the same side
as A. (Same side 2) -/
axiom same_side_symm (h : SameSide A B L) : SameSide B A L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.same_side_trans:
/-- Two points on the same side of a straight line as a third point are on the same
side as each other. (Same side 4) -/
axiom same_side_trans (h₁ : SameSide A B L) (h₂ : SameSide A C L) : SameSide B C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.bac:
/-- The triangle ABC, named the other way round, as BAC. -/
theorem Triangle.bac (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₁₂:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₁₂ (h : Triangle A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₂₃:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₂₃ (h : Triangle A B C) : B ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_onRay_right:
/-- The other arm traced through another point of its ray: if C' is on the ray
from A through C, the angle BAC' is the angle BAC. (System E,
Diagram-angle 4) -/
theorem angle_onRay_right {C' : Point} (hC : OnRay C' A C) (hBA : B ≠ A) :
    ∠ B A C' = ∠ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.exists_oppositeSidesOf:
/-- "Let a point be taken at random on the other side of the straight line AB"
(I.12): if P is off the straight line AB, there is a point on the other side
of it from P, which may be chosen different from any points already in the
figure. (System E, Points 6) -/
theorem exists_oppositeSidesOf (hP : Triangle A B P) (avoid : List Point) :
    ∃ Q : Point, OppositeSidesOf Q P A B ∧ Q ∉ avoid
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea_add_of_parallelograms:
/-- A parallelogram cut by a straight line parallel to two of its sides is the two
parallelograms it is cut into. If E lies between A and D, F between B and
C, and ABFE, EFCD are parallelograms, then the figure ABCD is ABFE and
EFCD together. Cut each piece and the whole into triangles from A and C; the
four-sided figure AFCE is measured by AC in the whole and by FE in the pieces,
and its diameters cross, for A and C lie on either side of EF. -/
theorem quadArea_add_of_parallelograms (h₁ : Parallelogram A B F E) (h₂ : Parallelogram E F C D)
    (hAED : Between A E D) (hBFC : Between B F C) :
    quadArea A B C D = quadArea A B F E + quadArea E F C D
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea_reverse:
/-- The figure ABCD read the other way round, as ADCB, has the same diameter
AC, and the same area. -/
theorem quadArea_reverse (A B C D : Point) : quadArea A D C B = quadArea A B C D
