state.enunciation: In right-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the right angle is equal to the squares on the sides containing the right angle.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABC be a right-angled triangle having the angle BAC right;

I say that the square on BC is equal to the squares on BA, AC.

For let there be described on BC the square BDEC, and on BA, AC the squares GB, HC; [I. 46] through A let AL be drawn parallel to either BD or CE, and let AD, FC be joined.

Then, since each of the angles BAC, BAG is right, it follows that with a straight line BA, and at the point A on it, the two straight lines AC, AG not lying on the same side make the adjacent angles equal to two right angles; therefore CA is in a straight line with AG. [I. 14]

For the same reason BA is also in a straight line with AH.

And, since the angle DBC is equal to the angle FBA: for each is right: let the angle ABC be added to each; therefore the whole angle DBA is equal to the whole angle FBC. [C.N. 2]

And, since DB is equal to BC, and FB to BA, the two sides AB, BD are equal to the two sides FB, BC respectively; and the angle ABD is equal to the angle FBC; therefore the base AD is equal to the base FC, and the triangle ABD is equal to the triangle FBC. [I. 4]

Now the parallelogram BL is double of the triangle ABD, for they have the same base BD and are in the same parallels BD, AL. [I. 41]

And the square GB is double of the triangle FBC, for they again have the same base FB and are in the same parallels FB, GC. [I. 41]

[But the doubles of equals are equal to one another.]

Therefore the parallelogram BL is also equal to the square GB.

Similarly, if AE, BK be joined, the parallelogram CL can also be proved equal to the square HC; therefore the whole square BDEC is equal to the two squares GB, HC. [C.N. 2]

And the square BDEC is described on BC, and the squares GB, HC on BA, AC.

Therefore the square on the side BC is equal to the squares on the sides BA, AC.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- In right-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the right angle is equal to the
squares on the sides containing the right angle. -/
theorem Prop47 {A B C D E F G H K : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hright : ∠ B A C = ∟)
    (hBDEC : Square B D E C) (hD : OppositeSidesOf D A B C) (hE : OppositeSidesOf E A B C)
    (hABFG : Square A B F G) (hF : OppositeSidesOf F C A B) (hG : OppositeSidesOf G C A B)
    (hACKH : Square A C K H) (hK : OppositeSidesOf K B A C) (hH : OppositeSidesOf H B A C) :
    quadArea B D E C = quadArea A B F G + quadArea A C K H := by
  -- Let ABC be a right-angled triangle having the angle BAC right;
  -- I say that the square on BC is equal to the squares on BA, AC.
  -- For let there be described on BC the square BDEC, and on BA, AC the squares GB,
  -- HC; [I. 46]
  /- The three squares are given in the statement, so I.46 is not cited. Their
     opposite sides are parallel by `Prop28.square`. -/
  have hpsq : Parallelogram B D E C :=
    (Prop28.square hBDEC.rotate.rotate.rotate
      (OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf hD.symm hE.symm).swap).rotate
  have hABFGpar : Parallelogram A B F G :=
    Prop28.square hABFG (OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf hF.symm hG.symm)
  have hACKHpar : Parallelogram A C K H :=
    Prop28.square hACKH (OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf hK.symm hH.symm)
  obtain ⟨hBD_DE, hDE_EC, hEC_CB, hCBD, -, -, hECB⟩ := id hBDEC
  have hBD_BC : ‖B D‖ = ‖B C‖ :=
    hBD_DE.trans (hDE_EC.trans (hEC_CB.trans (len_symm C B)))
  have hCE_CB : ‖C E‖ = ‖C B‖ := (len_symm C E).trans hEC_CB
  have hBCE : ∠ B C E = ∟ :=
    (angle_symm hABC.ne₂₃ hE.triangle.ne₂₃.symm).trans hECB
  have hright' : ∠ C A B = ∟ :=
    (angle_symm hABC.ne₁₃.symm hABC.ne₁₂.symm).trans hright
  /- I.17 makes the angles at B and C acute. With the outward squares,
     `Prop47.within` puts A between the straight lines BD and CE. -/
  have hacB : ∠ A B C < ∟ := by
    have h17 := (Prop17 hABC).2.2
    rw [hright'] at h17
    exact Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_left h17
  have hacC : ∠ A C B < ∟ := by
    have h17 := (Prop17 hABC).2.1
    rw [hright] at h17
    exact Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_left h17
  obtain ⟨hCA_BD, -⟩ := Prop47.within hABC hD hCBD hacB
  obtain ⟨hBA_CE, -⟩ := Prop47.within hABC.acb hE.swap hBCE hacC
  -- through A let AL be drawn parallel to either BD or CE,
  have hBD : B ≠ D := hCA_BD.1
  have hCE : C ≠ E := hBA_CE.1
  obtain ⟨BD, hB_BD, hD_BD⟩ := Postulate1 B D hBD
  obtain ⟨CE, hC_CE, hE_CE⟩ := Postulate1 C E hCE
  obtain ⟨BC, hB_BC, hC_BC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hABC.ne₂₃
  obtain ⟨DE, hD_DE, hE_DE⟩ := Postulate1 D E hpsq.2.1
  have hBD_CE : Parallel BD CE := hpsq.1.parallel hB_BD hD_BD hE_CE hC_CE
  have hDE_BC : Parallel DE BC := hpsq.2.parallel hD_DE hE_DE hC_BC hB_BC
  have hA_BD : ¬ OnLine A BD :=
    not_on_line_of_same_side (same_side_symm (hCA_BD.sameSide hB_BD hD_BD))
  obtain ⟨AL, hA_AL, hAL_BD⟩ := Prop31.line hA_BD
  have hA_CE : ¬ OnLine A CE :=
    not_on_line_of_same_side (same_side_symm (hBA_CE.sameSide hC_CE hE_CE))
  have hAL_CE : Parallel AL CE :=
    Prop30.parallel hAL_BD hBD_CE.symm (fun e => hA_CE (e ▸ hA_AL))
  /- The parallel meets DE at L and BC at its unlettered foot (`Prop30.meet`). -/
  have hDE_BD : DE ≠ BD := fun e => hDE_BC.not_onLine (e ▸ hB_BD) hB_BC
  obtain ⟨L, hL_DE, hL_AL⟩ := Prop30.meet hAL_BD hD_BD hD_DE hDE_BD
  have hBC_BD : BC ≠ BD := fun e => hD.triangle.off_line hB_BC hC_BC (e ▸ hD_BD)
  obtain ⟨X, hX_BC, hX_AL⟩ := Prop30.meet hAL_BD hB_BD hB_BC hBC_BD
  have hXL : X ≠ L := fun e => hDE_BC.not_onLine (e ▸ hL_DE) hX_BC
  have hDL : D ≠ L := fun e => hAL_BD.not_onLine (e ▸ hL_AL) hD_BD
  have hXB : X ≠ B := fun e => hAL_BD.not_onLine (e ▸ hX_AL) hB_BD
  have hLE : L ≠ E := fun e => hAL_CE.not_onLine hL_AL (e ▸ hE_CE)
  have hCX : C ≠ X := fun e => hAL_CE.not_onLine hX_AL (e ▸ hC_CE)
  have P₁ : Parallelogram B D L X :=
    ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel hBD hXL.symm hB_BD hD_BD hL_AL hX_AL hAL_BD.symm,
      AreParallel.of_parallel hDL hXB hD_DE hL_DE hX_BC hB_BC hDE_BC⟩
  have P₂ : Parallelogram X L E C :=
    ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel hXL hCE.symm hX_AL hL_AL hE_CE hC_CE hAL_CE,
      AreParallel.of_parallel hLE hCX hL_DE hE_DE hC_BC hX_BC hDE_BC⟩
  have hXLA : Collinear X L A := ⟨AL, hX_AL, hL_AL, hA_AL⟩
  -- and let AD, FC be joined.
  /- The joined straight lines are the sides of the triangles in I.4 below. -/
  -- Then, since each of the angles BAC, BAG is right, it follows that with a straight line BA,
  -- and at the point A on it, the two straight lines AC, AG not lying on the same side make
  -- the adjacent angles equal to two right angles; therefore CA is in a straight line with
  -- AG. [I. 14]
  have hCAG : Between C A G := Prop14 hG.symm.swap (by
    rw [hright, angle_symm hABC.ne₁₂.symm hG.triangle.ne₁₃.symm, hABFG.2.2.2.1])
  -- For the same reason BA is also in a straight line with AH.
  have hBAH : Between B A H := Prop14 hH.symm.swap (by
    rw [hright', angle_symm hABC.ne₁₃.symm hH.triangle.ne₁₃.symm, hACKH.2.2.2.1])
  /- Euclid proves one half and then says "similarly". We give these sentences
     once over any letters, using the straightness and acute angle already
     proved, and apply them at B and at C. -/
  have half : ∀ {A B C D F G X L : Point}, Triangle A B C →
      ‖B D‖ = ‖B C‖ → ∠ C B D = ∟ → OppositeSidesOf D A B C →
      Square A B F G → OppositeSidesOf F C A B → Parallelogram A B F G →
      Between C A G → ∠ A B C < ∟ → Parallelogram X B D L → Collinear X L A →
      quadArea X B D L = quadArea A B F G := by
    intro A B C D F G X L hABC hBD hCBD hD hsq hF hpsq hCAG hacute hp hX
    obtain ⟨hAB_BF, -, -, -, hABF, -, -⟩ := hsq
    -- And, since the angle DBC is equal to the angle FBA: for each is right: let the angle ABC
    -- be added to each; therefore the whole angle DBA is equal to the whole angle FBC. [C.N. 2]
    obtain ⟨hCA_BD, hCD_BA⟩ := Prop47.within hABC hD hCBD hacute
    obtain ⟨hAC_BF, hAF_BC⟩ := Prop47.within hABC.cba hF.swap hABF
      (by rw [angle_symm hABC.ne₂₃.symm hABC.ne₁₂]; exact hacute)
    have hDBA : ∠ D B A = ∠ D B C + ∠ C B A :=
      angle_add_of_within hCA_BD hCD_BA
    have hFBC : ∠ F B C = ∠ F B A + ∠ A B C :=
      angle_add_of_within hAC_BF hAF_BC
    have hBD_ne : B ≠ D := hCA_BD.1
    have hBF_ne : B ≠ F := hAC_BF.1
    have hrights : ∠ D B C = ∠ F B A := by
      rw [angle_symm hBD_ne.symm hABC.ne₂₃.symm, hCBD,
        angle_symm hBF_ne.symm hABC.ne₁₂, hABF]
    have hadd := CommonNotion2 hrights (Eq.refl (∠ A B C))
    have hang : ∠ D B A = ∠ F B C := by
      rw [hDBA, hFBC, angle_symm hABC.ne₂₃.symm hABC.ne₁₂]
      exact hadd
    -- And, since DB is equal to BC, and FB to BA, the two sides AB, BD are equal to the two
    -- sides FB, BC respectively; and the angle ABD is equal to the angle FBC; therefore the base
    -- AD is equal to the base FC, and the triangle ABD is equal to the triangle FBC. [I. 4]
    have hABD : ∠ A B D = ∠ F B C :=
      (angle_symm hABC.ne₁₂ hBD_ne.symm).trans hang
    obtain ⟨hAD_FC, h4, -, -⟩ :=
      Prop4 hCD_BA.symm.triangle hAC_BF.symm.triangle
        ((len_symm B A).trans hAB_BF) hBD hABD
    -- Now the parallelogram BL is double of the triangle ABD, for they have the same base BD and
    -- are in the same parallels BD, AL. [I. 41]
    have h41a : quadArea X B D L = △ B A D + △ B A D := Prop41 hp hX
    -- And the square GB is double of the triangle FBC, for they again have the same base FB and
    -- are in the same parallels FB, GC. [I. 41]
    obtain ⟨GC, hC_GC, hA_GC, hG_GC⟩ := collinear_of_between hCAG
    have h41b : quadArea G F B A = △ F C B + △ F C B :=
      Prop41 hpsq.rotate.rotate.rotate.reverse ⟨GC, hG_GC, hA_GC, hC_GC⟩
    -- [But the doubles of equals are equal to one another.]
    have hdouble := CommonNotion2 h4 h4
    -- Therefore the parallelogram BL is also equal to the square GB.
    calc
      quadArea X B D L = △ B A D + △ B A D := h41a
      _ = △ B F C + △ B F C := hdouble
      _ = △ F C B + △ F C B := by rw [area_bca B F C]
      _ = quadArea G F B A := h41b.symm
      _ = quadArea A B F G := by
        rw [quadArea_reverse, hpsq.rotate.rotate.rotate.quadArea_rotate]
  have h₁ : quadArea X B D L = quadArea A B F G :=
    half hABC hBD_BC hCBD hD hABFG hF hABFGpar hCAG hacB P₁.rotate.rotate.rotate hXLA
  -- Similarly, if AE, BK be joined, the parallelogram CL can also be proved equal to the
  -- square HC; therefore the whole square BDEC is equal to the two squares GB, HC. [C.N. 2]
  have h₂ : quadArea X C E L = quadArea A C K H :=
    half hABC.acb hCE_CB hBCE hE.swap hACKH hK hACKHpar hBAH hacC P₂.reverse hXLA
  /- The foot of AL lies between B and C, and L between D and E: A lies
     between BD and CE, and AL is parallel to both (`Between.of_inside`). -/
  have ss : ∀ {P Q R : Point} {N : Line},
      SameSide P Q N → SameSide Q R N → SameSide P R N :=
    fun h₁ h₂ => same_side_trans (same_side_symm h₁) h₂
  have hAC_BD : SameSide A C BD := same_side_symm (hCA_BD.sameSide hB_BD hD_BD)
  have hAB_CE : SameSide A B CE := same_side_symm (hBA_CE.sameSide hC_CE hE_CE)
  have hBXC : Between B X C :=
    Between.of_inside hB_BD hC_CE ⟨BC, hB_BC, hX_BC, hC_BC⟩
      (ss (hAL_BD.sameSide hX_AL hA_AL) hAC_BD)
      (ss (hAL_CE.sameSide hX_AL hA_AL) hAB_CE)
  have hCE_BD : SameSide C E BD :=
    same_side_symm (hpsq.sameSideOf.sameSide hB_BD hD_BD)
  have hBD_CE' : SameSide B D CE := hpsq.rotate.rotate.sameSideOf.sameSide hE_CE hC_CE
  have hDLE : Between D L E :=
    Between.of_inside hD_BD hE_CE ⟨DE, hD_DE, hL_DE, hE_DE⟩
      (ss (ss (hAL_BD.sameSide hL_AL hA_AL) hAC_BD) hCE_BD)
      (ss (ss (hAL_CE.sameSide hL_AL hA_AL) hAB_CE) hBD_CE')
  have hwhole : quadArea B D E C = quadArea X B D L + quadArea X C E L := by
    rw [quadArea_add_of_parallelograms P₁ P₂ hBXC hDLE,
      P₁.rotate.rotate.rotate.quadArea_rotate, quadArea_reverse X C E L]
  have hequal := hwhole.trans (CommonNotion2 h₁ h₂)
  -- And the square BDEC is described on BC, and the squares GB, HC on BA, AC.
  /- These are the three given squares. -/
  -- Therefore the square on the side BC is equal to the squares on the sides BA, AC.
  -- Therefore etc.
  exact hequal
  -- Q. E. D.

helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.of_parallel:
/-- Two different points of L, and two different points of M, are the ends of
parallel straight lines when L and M are parallel: two points fix one straight
line (System E, Generalities 1). With `AreParallel.parallel`, this says "AB is
parallel to CD" of any other two points P, Q of the straight line AB and R,
S of CD. -/
theorem AreParallel.of_parallel (hPQ : P ≠ Q) (hRS : R ≠ S) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L)
    (hR : OnLine R M) (hS : OnLine S M) (h : Parallel L M) : AreParallel P Q R S
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.parallel:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then a straight line through A and B is parallel
to one through C and D. -/
theorem AreParallel.parallel (h : AreParallel A B C D) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (hC : OnLine C M) (hD : OnLine D M) : Parallel L M
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.sameSideOf:
/-- The ends of one parallel lie on one side of the other: if AB is parallel to
CD, then A and B are on the same side of CD (`Parallel.sameSide`). -/
theorem AreParallel.sameSideOf (h : AreParallel A B C D) : SameSideOf A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.symm:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then CD is parallel to AB. -/
theorem AreParallel.symm (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.triangle:
/-- An end of one parallel is off the other: if AB is parallel to CD, then C
is not on the straight line AB, and ABC is a triangle. (Turned round with
`AreParallel.symm` and `.swap_right`, the same holds of D, and of A and B
beside CD.) -/
theorem AreParallel.triangle (h : AreParallel A B C D) : Triangle A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Between.of_inside:
/-- A point on the straight line AC, on C's side of a straight line L through
A and on A's side of a straight line M through C, lies between A and C.
Were A between it and C, L would separate it from C; were C between it and
A, M would separate it from A (System E, Between 6 and Pasch 3). So a point
of a straight line joining two parallels, lying between the parallels, lies
between the points where it meets them. `Between.of_sameSide`, below, is another
matter: it carries the order of three points across a straight line. -/
theorem Between.of_inside (hA : OnLine A L) (hC : OnLine C M) (hX : Collinear A X C)
    (hXL : SameSide X C L) (hXM : SameSide X A M) : Between A X C
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop13:
/-- If a straight line set up on a straight line make angles, it will make either two right angles
or angles equal to two right angles. -/
theorem Prop13 {A B C D : Point} (hCBD : Between C B D) (hA : ¬ Collinear C D A) :
    ∠ C B A + ∠ A B D = ∟ + ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop14:
/-- If with any straight line, and at a point on it, two straight lines not lying on the same side
make the adjacent angles equal to two right angles, the two straight lines will be in a straight
line with one another. -/
theorem Prop14 {A B C D : Point} (hCD : OppositeSidesOf C D A B) (h : ∠ A B C + ∠ A B D = ∟ + ∟) :
    Between C B D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop17:
/-- In any triangle two angles taken together in any manner are less than two right angles. -/
theorem Prop17 {A B C : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) :
    ∠ A B C + ∠ B C A < ∟ + ∟ ∧ ∠ B A C + ∠ A C B < ∟ + ∟ ∧ ∠ C A B + ∠ A B C < ∟ + ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop28:
/-- If a straight line falling on two straight lines make the exterior angle equal to the interior
and opposite angle on the same side, or the interior angles on the same side equal to two right
angles, the straight lines will be parallel to one another. -/
theorem Prop28 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (hAGB : Between A G B) (hCHD : Between C H D)
    (hEGH : Between E G H) (hGHF : Between G H F) (hBD : SameSideOf B D E F)
    (h : ∠ E G B = ∠ G H D ∨ ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D = ∟ + ∟) :
    AreParallel A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop28.square:
/-- A square is a parallelogram. If ABCD is a square (Def. 22) whose far corners
C, D lie on one side of AB, its opposite sides are parallel: the right angles
at A and B make AD parallel to BC, and those at B and C make AB parallel
to CD. Euclid's squares are those I.46 describes, which are parallelograms by
construction; a square given in a statement has to be shown one. [I. 28] -/
theorem Prop28.square {A B C D : Point} (h : Square A B C D) (hCD : SameSideOf C D A B) :
    Parallelogram A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30:
/-- Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another. -/
theorem Prop30 {A B C D E F : Point} (h₁ : AreParallel A B E F) (h₂ : AreParallel C D E F)
    (hC : ¬ Collinear A B C) :
    AreParallel A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30.meet:
/-- A straight line meeting one of two parallels meets the other. If L is parallel
to M, and a straight line N, other than M, passes through a point P of M,
then N meets L. Otherwise N would be parallel to L too, and by I.30 M and
N would be parallel to one another, though both pass through P.

Euclid uses this whenever he draws a parallel and then names the point where it
meets another straight line: E and F in I.37, G and H in I.38, E in I.39,
F in I.40, F and G in I.42, H, L and M in I.44, E in I.46 and L in
I.47. It is the uniqueness of the parallel through a point, often called
Playfair's axiom; Heath reports under I.31 that Proclus draws it from I.30.
`Prop30.unique`, a step inside I.30's own proof, gives the same uniqueness from
I.29; later proofs cite this one, Proclus' route through I.30. [I. 30] -/
theorem Prop30.meet {L M N : Line} {P : Point} (hLM : Parallel L M) (hPM : OnLine P M)
    (hPN : OnLine P N) (hNM : N ≠ M) : ∃ Q : Point, OnLine Q N ∧ OnLine Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30.parallel:
/-- I.30 said of straight lines drawn and named: two different straight lines L and
M, each parallel to N, are parallel to one another. Euclid uses it without a
bracket in I.44 and I.47, where a straight line drawn "parallel to either" of two
parallels is parallel to both; in I.45 he brackets it. [I. 30] -/
theorem Prop30.parallel {L M N : Line} (hL : Parallel L N) (hM : Parallel M N) (hLM : L ≠ M) :
    Parallel L M
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31:
/-- Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line. -/
theorem Prop31 {A B C : Point} (hBC : B ≠ C) (hA : ¬ Collinear B C A) :
    ∃ E F : Point, Between E A F ∧ AreParallel E F B C
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31.line:
/-- I.31 said of straight lines drawn and named: through a point A off the
straight line L there is a straight line K parallel to L. I.31 gives two points
of it, one on either side of A, and Postulate 1 joins them. [I. 31] -/
theorem Prop31.line {A : Point} {L : Line} (hA : ¬ OnLine A L) :
    ∃ K : Line, OnLine A K ∧ Parallel K L
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop4:
/-- If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles
contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the base, the
triangle will be equal to the triangle, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining
angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend. -/
theorem Prop4 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖D F‖) (hA : ∠ B A C = ∠ E D F) :
    ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ ∧ △ A B C = △ D E F ∧ ∠ A B C = ∠ D E F ∧ ∠ A C B = ∠ D F E
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop41:
/-- If a parallelogram have the same base with a triangle and be in the same parallels, the
parallelogram is double of the triangle. -/
theorem Prop41 {A B C D E : Point} (hABCD : Parallelogram A B C D) (hE : Collinear A D E) :
    quadArea A B C D = △ B E C + △ B E C
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop47.within:
/-- Where the squares fall. If the angle ABC is less than a right angle, and BD
stands at right angles to BC on the other side of it from A, then C lies within
the angle ABD: on A's side of BD, and on D's side of BA. Euclid reads this
off his figure when he adds the angle ABC to the right angles DBC, FBA, and
again when he takes the parallelograms BL, CL to make up the square BDEC.

The straight line AD crosses BC, since it joins points on either side of it. Not
at B, for then the angles ABC, CBD would make two right angles [I. 13], and
CBD alone is right. Not beyond B from C, for then the angle ABD would be
greater than two right angles: the angle on the far side of AB from C is
greater than right [I. 13], and to it is added the right angle on the far side of
BD. So it crosses on the ray from B through C, and C lies where the crossing
point does. [I. 13] -/
theorem Prop47.within {A B C D : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hD : OppositeSidesOf D A B C)
    (hCBD : ∠ C B D = ∟) (hacute : ∠ A B C < ∟) :
    SameSideOf C A B D ∧ SameSideOf C D B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Collinear:
/-- `A`, `B`, `C` lie on one straight line. -/
def Collinear (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.CommonNotion2:
/-- **Common Notion 2.** If equals be added to equals, the wholes are equal. -/
theorem CommonNotion2 {a b c d : Magnitude k} (h₁ : a = b) (h₂ : c = d) :
    a + c = b + d
helper_signatures.Elements.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_left:
/-- The same, with the common part first: if `a` and `b` together are less than `a`
and `c` together, then `b` is less than `c`. -/
theorem Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_left {k : Kind} {a b c : Magnitude k} (h : a + b < a + c) :
    b < c
helper_signatures.Elements.Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_righ:
/-- Take the same thing away from two unequal magnitudes, and the less remains the
less: if `x` and `a` together are less than `y` and `a` together, then `x` is less
than `y`. Otherwise `y` would be equal to `x` or less, and adding `a` to each would
keep it so (the laws of magnitudes, System E §3.5). -/
theorem Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_right {k : Kind} {a x y : Magnitude k} (h : x + a < y + a) :
    x < y
helper_signatures.Elements.Magnitude.ne_of_lt:
/-- Unequal magnitudes, if one is less. -/
theorem Magnitude.ne_of_lt {k : Kind} {a b : Magnitude k} (h : a < b) : a ≠ b
helper_signatures.Elements.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.symm:
/-- P is on the ray from A through B exactly when B is on the ray from A
through P: they are one and the same ray. -/
theorem OnRay.symm (h : OnRay P A B) : OnRay B A P
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSides:
/-- `A` and `B` lie on opposite sides of the straight line `L`. -/
def OppositeSides (A B : Point) (L : Line) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSides.exists_between:
/-- A finite straight line joining two points on opposite sides of a straight line
L crosses L, at a point between them (System E, Intersection 1 and Pasch 4). -/
theorem OppositeSides.exists_between (h : OppositeSides P Q L) :
    ∃ X : Point, OnLine X L ∧ Between P X Q
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf:
/-- `P` and `Q` lie on opposite sides of the straight line `AB`. -/
def OppositeSidesOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.oppositeSides:
/-- Two points on opposite sides of the straight line AB are on opposite sides of
any straight line drawn through A and B. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.oppositeSides (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) (hA : OnLine A L)
    (hB : OnLine B L) : OppositeSides P Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf:
/-- The same, said of "the straight line AB": two points, each on the other side of
AB from C, are on the same side of AB as each other. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf {C D E : Point} (h₁ : OppositeSidesOf C D A B)
    (h₂ : OppositeSidesOf C E A B) : SameSideOf D E A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.swap:
/-- "On opposite sides of AB" is the same as "on opposite sides of BA". -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.swap (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : OppositeSidesOf P Q B A
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the other side of AB from Q, then Q is on the other side
from P. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.symm (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : OppositeSidesOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.triangle:
/-- A point on either side of the straight line AB is not on it, so ABP is a
triangle. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.triangle (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : Triangle A B P
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.not_onLine:
/-- Parallels do not meet: a point of L is not on M. -/
theorem Parallel.not_onLine (h : Parallel L M) (hP : OnLine P L) : ¬ OnLine P M
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.sameSide:
/-- All the points of one parallel lie on one side of the other: two points of L
are on the same side of M. Were they on opposite sides, the straight line L
joining them would cross M (System E, Intersection 1). -/
theorem Parallel.sameSide (h : Parallel L M) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L) :
    SameSide P Q M
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.symm:
/-- If L is parallel to M, then M is parallel to L. -/
theorem Parallel.symm (h : Parallel L M) : Parallel M L
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate:
/-- A parallelogram has the same area whichever diameter cuts it: the parallelogram
ABCD measured by BD, as BCDA, is the same as measured by AC. -/
theorem Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea B C D A = quadArea A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.reverse:
/-- The parallelogram ABCD, read the other way round from A, is the
parallelogram ADCB. -/
theorem Parallelogram.reverse (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Parallelogram A D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.rotate:
/-- The parallelogram ABCD, named from B, is the parallelogram BCDA. -/
theorem Parallelogram.rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Parallelogram B C D A
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.sameSideOf:
/-- In the parallelogram ABCD, the far corners C and D lie on one side of the
side AB. (Named from another corner with `.rotate`, the same holds of every
side.) -/
theorem Parallelogram.sameSideOf (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : SameSideOf C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.triangle:
/-- In the parallelogram ABCD, the corner C is off the straight line AB, so
ABC is a triangle. -/
theorem Parallelogram.triangle (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Triangle A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate1:
/-- **Postulate 1.** To draw a straight line from any point to any point. -/
axiom Postulate1 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf:
/-- `P` and `Q` lie on the same side of the straight line `AB`. -/
def SameSideOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.of_line:
/-- Two points on the same side of a straight line L through A and B are on
the same side of the straight line AB, however that line is named: two points
fix one straight line. -/
theorem SameSideOf.of_line (hAB : A ≠ B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (h : SameSide P Q L) : SameSideOf P Q A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.of_onRay:
/-- A point G on the ray from D through P is on the same side of the straight
line DE as P: the ray leaves DE at D and never crosses it again (System E,
Pasch 4). -/
theorem SameSideOf.of_onRay {D E F G P : Point} (hG : OnRay G D P) (hP : SameSideOf P F D E) :
    SameSideOf G F D E
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.sameSide:
/-- Two points on the same side of the straight line AB are on the same side of
any straight line drawn through A and B. -/
theorem SameSideOf.sameSide (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    SameSide P Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.swap:
/-- "On the same side of AB" is the same as "on the same side of BA". -/
theorem SameSideOf.swap (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf P Q B A
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the same side of AB as Q, then Q is on the same side as P. -/
theorem SameSideOf.symm (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.trans:
/-- Points on the same side as a third are on the same side as each other. -/
theorem SameSideOf.trans (h₁ : SameSideOf P Q A B) (h₂ : SameSideOf Q R A B) :
    SameSideOf P R A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.triangle:
/-- A point on one side of the straight line AB is not on it, so ABP is a
triangle. -/
theorem SameSideOf.triangle (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : Triangle A B P
helper_signatures.Elements.Square:
/-- **Definition 22.** "Of quadrilateral figures, a square is that which is both
equilateral and right-angled." The corners are `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, in order. -/
def Square (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Square.reverse:
/-- The square ABCD, read the other way round from A, is the square ADCB. -/
theorem Square.reverse (h : Square A B C D) (hp : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    Square A D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Square.rotate:
/-- The square ABCD, named from B, is the square BCDA. -/
theorem Square.rotate (h : Square A B C D) : Square B C D A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.add_comm:
/-- The order of adding does not matter. (System E §3.5) -/
axiom add_comm (a b : Magnitude k) : a + b = b + a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.add_lt_add_right:
/-- Adding the same thing to both sides keeps "less than". (System E §3.5) -/
axiom add_lt_add_right {a b : Magnitude k} (c : Magnitude k) : a < b → a + c < b + c
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.angle_le_two_right:
/-- No angle exceeds two right angles. (Metric 5) -/
axiom angle_le_two_right (A B C : Point) : ∠ A B C ≤ ∟ + ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.angle_symm:
/-- The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4) -/
axiom angle_symm (hAB : A ≠ B) (hCB : C ≠ B) : ∠ A B C = ∠ C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_symm:
/-- If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1) -/
axiom between_symm (h : Between A B C) : Between C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.len_symm:
/-- The straight line AB is the straight line BA. (Metric 3) -/
axiom len_symm (A B : Point) : ‖A B‖ = ‖B A‖
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.line_unique:
/-- Two points determine a straight line. (Generalities 1) -/
axiom line_unique (hAB : A ≠ B) (hAL : OnLine A L) (hBL : OnLine B L) (hAM : OnLine A M)
    (hBM : OnLine B M) : L = M
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.lt_trichotomy:
/-- Of two magnitudes, one is less, or they are equal, or the other is less.
(System E §3.5) -/
axiom lt_trichotomy (a b : Magnitude k) : a < b ∨ a = b ∨ b < a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between:
/-- A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between_ends:
/-- The ends of a finite straight line differ. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.not_on_line_of_same_side:
/-- Points on one side of a straight line are not on it. (Same side 3) -/
axiom not_on_line_of_same_side (h : SameSide A B L) : ¬ OnLine A L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between_ends:
/-- A straight line through A and C passes through every point between them.
(Between 3) -/
axiom on_line_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hC : OnLine C L) :
    OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.pasch2:
/-- If B is between A and C, A is on L and B is off it, then B and C are
on the same side of L: a straight line that leaves L at A does not cross it
again. (Pasch 2) -/
axiom pasch2 (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : ¬ OnLine B L) : SameSide B C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.same_side_symm:
/-- If A is on the same side of a straight line as B, then B is on the same side
as A. (Same side 2) -/
axiom same_side_symm (h : SameSide A B L) : SameSide B A L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.same_side_trans:
/-- Two points on the same side of a straight line as a third point are on the same
side as each other. (Same side 4) -/
axiom same_side_trans (h₁ : SameSide A B L) (h₂ : SameSide A C L) : SameSide B C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.acb:
/-- The triangle ABC, named the other way round, as ACB. -/
theorem Triangle.acb (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle A C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.cba:
/-- The triangle ABC, named the other way round, as CBA. -/
theorem Triangle.cba (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₁₂:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₁₂ (h : Triangle A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₁₃:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₁₃ (h : Triangle A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₂₃:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₂₃ (h : Triangle A B C) : B ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.off_line:
/-- In the triangle ABC, the corner C is off every straight line through A
and B. -/
theorem Triangle.off_line (h : Triangle A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    ¬ OnLine C L
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_add_of_between:
/-- If R lies between P and Q, and V is off the straight line PQ, then VR
falls within the angle PVQ, and that angle is made up of the angles PVR and
RVQ. (System E, Pasch 2 and Diagram-angle 2) -/
theorem angle_add_of_between {V P Q R : Point} (hPQV : Triangle P Q V) (h : Between P R Q) :
    ∠ P V Q = ∠ P V R + ∠ R V Q
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_add_of_within:
/-- A straight line drawn from the corner of an angle through a point within it
cuts the angle into two. If R lies within the angle PVQ, on Q's side of VP
and on P's side of VQ, then the angle PVQ is made up of the angles PVR and
RVQ. This is System E's Diagram-angle 2, said of "the straight lines VP, VQ"
rather than of lines drawn and named. -/
theorem angle_add_of_within {V P Q R : Point} (hRQ : SameSideOf R Q V P)
    (hRP : SameSideOf R P V Q) : ∠ P V Q = ∠ P V R + ∠ R V Q
helper_signatures.Elements.area_bca:
/-- The triangle ABC is the triangle BCA. (System E, Metric 8) -/
theorem area_bca (A B C : Point) : △ A B C = △ B C A
helper_signatures.Elements.collinear_of_between:
/-- Three points, one between the other two, lie on one straight line. -/
theorem collinear_of_between (h : Between A B C) : Collinear A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea_add_of_parallelograms:
/-- A parallelogram cut by a straight line parallel to two of its sides is the two
parallelograms it is cut into. If E lies between A and D, F between B and
C, and ABFE, EFCD are parallelograms, then the figure ABCD is ABFE and
EFCD together. Cut each piece and the whole into triangles from A and C; the
four-sided figure AFCE is measured by AC in the whole and by FE in the pieces,
and its diameters cross, for A and C lie on either side of EF. -/
theorem quadArea_add_of_parallelograms (h₁ : Parallelogram A B F E) (h₂ : Parallelogram E F C D)
    (hAED : Between A E D) (hBFC : Between B F C) :
    quadArea A B C D = quadArea A B F E + quadArea E F C D
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea_reverse:
/-- The figure ABCD read the other way round, as ADCB, has the same diameter
AC, and the same area. -/
theorem quadArea_reverse (A B C D : Point) : quadArea A D C B = quadArea A B C D

I.4.enunciation: If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the base, the triangle will be equal to the triangle, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend.

I.13.enunciation: If a straight line set up on a straight line make angles, it will make either two right angles or angles equal to two right angles.

I.14.enunciation: If with any straight line, and at a point on it, two straight lines not lying on the same side make the adjacent angles equal to two right angles, the two straight lines will be in a straight line with one another.

I.17.enunciation: In any triangle two angles taken together in any manner are less than two right angles.

I.28.enunciation: If a straight line falling on two straight lines make the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle on the same side, or the interior angles on the same side equal to two right angles, the straight lines will be parallel to one another.

I.30.enunciation: Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another.

I.31.enunciation: Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line.

I.41.enunciation: If a parallelogram have the same base with a triangle and be in the same parallels, the parallelogram is double of the triangle.

I.46.enunciation: On a given straight line to describe a square.

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ P ≠ A ∧ Collinear A B P ∧ ¬ Between P A B
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Square:
/-- **Definition 22.** "Of quadrilateral figures, a square is that which is both
equilateral and right-angled." The corners are `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, in order. -/
def Square (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  ‖A B‖ = ‖B C‖ ∧ ‖B C‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖C D‖ = ‖D A‖ ∧
    ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle

question.instructions:
Does every proposition called by the proof unit in `lean_proof` do work towards its conclusion or a substantive intermediate step of Euclid's argument? Also check for artificial hypothesis uses. Judge this unit's uses of the supplied helper signatures; helper bodies are outside this question. Heath's sentences stand as `--` lines and `cited` gives exact enunciations. In Lean, `have h : T := p` proves T by p and calls the result h; `obtain ⟨…⟩ := p` takes p apart into named pieces; `rw [h34, h37, …]` rewrites the goal by the equalities named. Follow uses through helper calls and tactics as well as explicit names. An anonymous binding or an unused hypothesis alone does not establish a defect. If both defects occur, choose `a dummy citation`.

docs/FORMALIZATION.md, section 5:
A checked intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid is legitimate, even if the
  final proof term could do without it.

criteria.an artificial hypothesis use: No dummy citation is established, but a hypothesis is mentioned only so that it looks used, and does no substantive work.
criteria.cannot tell: What is given here is not enough to decide.
criteria.all do work: Every proposition call supports a later step or the conclusion, or establishes a substantive intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid. No hypothesis is mentioned merely to look used. With no proposition calls the citation part alone is vacuous; hypothesis use must still be inspected.
criteria.a dummy citation: Some proposition call does no substantive work: its result neither supports the argument nor establishes a substantive intermediate fact, and merely supplies a citation while the step is done another way.

theorem Prop47 {A B C D E F G H K : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hright : ∠ B A C = ∟)
    (hBDEC : Square B D E C) (hD : OppositeSidesOf D A B C) (hE : OppositeSidesOf E A B C)
    (hABFG : Square A B F G) (hF : OppositeSidesOf F C A B) (hG : OppositeSidesOf G C A B)
    (hACKH : Square A C K H) (hK : OppositeSidesOf K B A C) (hH : OppositeSidesOf H B A C) :

bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34:
/-- In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the
diameter bisects the areas. -/
theorem Prop34 {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A C D B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ C D B ∧ ∠ A B D = ∠ A C D ∧
      △ A B C = △ D C B
bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34.bisect:
/-- The diameter bisects the parallelogram, said of its area: the parallelogram
ABCD, measured by its diameter AC, is double the triangle ABC. I.35–I.47 cite
I.34 for this ("the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram EBCA; for the diameter
AB bisects it"). To halve by the other diameter, name the parallelogram from the
next corner (`Parallelogram.rotate`) and turn its area round with
`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`. [I. 34] -/
theorem Prop34.bisect {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea A B C D = △ A B C + △ A B C
bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop46.square_eq:
/-- Squares described on equal straight lines are equal. Euclid assumes this in
I.48 ("since DA is equal to AB, the square on DA is also equal to the square on
AB"). Heath reports, under I.46, that Proclus proves it. Each square is a
parallelogram (`Prop28.square`), so the diameter AC cuts it into the triangles
ABC and ACD, right-angled at B and D; and I.4 makes these equal to the triangles
A'B'C' and A'C'D'. Here a square ABCD is "described on AB" when its far corners
C, D lie on one side of AB. [I. 4, I. 28] -/
theorem Prop46.square_eq {A B C D A' B' C' D' : Point} (h : Square A B C D)
    (hCD : SameSideOf C D A B) (h' : Square A' B' C' D') (hCD' : SameSideOf C' D' A' B')
    (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖A' B'‖) : quadArea A B C D = quadArea A' B' C' D'
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.cross:
/-- The diameters of a parallelogram cross: in the parallelogram ABCD, some point
lies between A and C and between B and D. Its sides AB and DC are
parallel, so they do not cross, and `AreParallel.cross_or` leaves only the
diameters. -/
theorem Parallelogram.cross (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    ∃ X : Point, Between A X C ∧ Between B X D
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate:
/-- A parallelogram has the same area whichever diameter cuts it: the parallelogram
ABCD measured by BD, as BCDA, is the same as measured by AC. -/
theorem Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea B C D A = quadArea A B C D

state.commentary:
"If we listen," says Proclus, "to those who wish to recount ancient history, we may find some of them referring this theorem to Pythagoras and saying that he sacrificed an ox in honour of his discovery. But for my part, while I admire those who first observed the truth of this theorem, I marvel more at the writer of the Elements" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 350). His reason follows on the same page: in Book VI Euclid proves the theorem for any similar figures, similarly situated, on the three sides (VI.31).

Euclid describes a square on each side, the figure often called the windmill, and draws AL through A parallel to BD. It cuts the square on BC into two parallelograms, BL and CL. BL is double of the triangle ABD, and the square GB double of the triangle FBC, each pair on one base and in the same parallels (I.41); and I.4 makes those triangles equal. So BL is equal to the square on AB, CL likewise to the square on AC, and together they fill the square on BC.

"Let the angle ABC be added to each": the sum makes the angle DBA only if C lies within it, and the angle FBC only if A lies within that. Euclid reads both off his figure. We find the reason in I.17 and I.13: the angles at B and C are less than right, and our statement stands the squares outward (`Prop47.within`). The same step puts the foot of AL between B and C, a point Euclid never names, since he calls the pieces BL and CL by their opposite corners.

Turn the square on BC inward, over the triangle, and the angle ABC would have to be taken from the right angle DBC. The text first says only that the squares are "described on" the sides. Its next step puts AC and AG "not lying on the same side" of BA, and the figure stands all three squares outward. The right angle at A ensures this arrangement for every right-angled triangle with outward squares, so there is no further case to leave to the reader.

**"Which compels admiration."** Heath thinks a proof by proportions suggested Euclid's: the perpendicular from the right angle cuts the triangle into two similar to the whole, so each smaller square is equal to the rectangle contained by the base and the piece of it beside that square, "whence the result follows by addition" (vol. 1, p. 353). Proportions wait for Book VI, so Euclid recast the proof on Book I alone, and Heath calls the result "a veritable *tour de force* which compels admiration, notwithstanding the ignorant strictures of Schopenhauer" (vol. 1, p. 354). Arthur Schopenhauer had called it "a mouse-trap proof" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 354).

**The modern way.** Put $\mathrm{A} = (0, 0)$, $\mathrm{B} = (c, 0)$ and $\mathrm{C} = (0, b)$, and write $a$ for the length of BC, so that $a$, $b$, $c$ are the sides opposite A, B, C. The foot of AL divides BC into pieces of length $c^{2}/a$, next to B, and $b^{2}/a$, so the rectangles BL and CL, of height $a$, have areas $c^{2}$ and $b^{2}$, and together they make the square on BC: $b^{2} + c^{2} = a^{2}$.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABC be a right-angled triangle having the angle BAC right;

I say that the square on BC is equal to the squares on BA, AC.

For let there be described on BC the square BDEC, and on BA, AC the squares GB, HC; [I. 46] through A let AL be drawn parallel to either BD or CE, and let AD, FC be joined.

Then, since each of the angles BAC, BAG is right, it follows that with a straight line BA, and at the point A on it, the two straight lines AC, AG not lying on the same side make the adjacent angles equal to two right angles; therefore CA is in a straight line with AG. [I. 14]

For the same reason BA is also in a straight line with AH.

And, since the angle DBC is equal to the angle FBA: for each is right: let the angle ABC be added to each; therefore the whole angle DBA is equal to the whole angle FBC. [C.N. 2]

And, since DB is equal to BC, and FB to BA, the two sides AB, BD are equal to the two sides FB, BC respectively; and the angle ABD is equal to the angle FBC; therefore the base AD is equal to the base FC, and the triangle ABD is equal to the triangle FBC. [I. 4]

Now the parallelogram BL is double of the triangle ABD, for they have the same base BD and are in the same parallels BD, AL. [I. 41]

And the square GB is double of the triangle FBC, for they again have the same base FB and are in the same parallels FB, GC. [I. 41]

[But the doubles of equals are equal to one another.]

Therefore the parallelogram BL is also equal to the square GB.

Similarly, if AE, BK be joined, the parallelogram CL can also be proved equal to the square HC; therefore the whole square BDEC is equal to the two squares GB, HC. [C.N. 2]

And the square BDEC is described on BC, and the squares GB, HC on BA, AC.

Therefore the square on the side BC is equal to the squares on the sides BA, AC.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- In right-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the right angle is equal to the
squares on the sides containing the right angle. -/
theorem Prop47 {A B C D E F G H K : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hright : ∠ B A C = ∟)
    (hBDEC : Square B D E C) (hD : OppositeSidesOf D A B C) (hE : OppositeSidesOf E A B C)
    (hABFG : Square A B F G) (hF : OppositeSidesOf F C A B) (hG : OppositeSidesOf G C A B)
    (hACKH : Square A C K H) (hK : OppositeSidesOf K B A C) (hH : OppositeSidesOf H B A C) :
    quadArea B D E C = quadArea A B F G + quadArea A C K H := by
  -- Let ABC be a right-angled triangle having the angle BAC right;
  -- I say that the square on BC is equal to the squares on BA, AC.
  -- For let there be described on BC the square BDEC, and on BA, AC the squares GB,
  -- HC; [I. 46]
  /- The three squares are given in the statement, so I.46 is not cited. Their
     opposite sides are parallel by `Prop28.square`. -/
  have hpsq : Parallelogram B D E C :=
    (Prop28.square hBDEC.rotate.rotate.rotate
      (OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf hD.symm hE.symm).swap).rotate
  have hABFGpar : Parallelogram A B F G :=
    Prop28.square hABFG (OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf hF.symm hG.symm)
  have hACKHpar : Parallelogram A C K H :=
    Prop28.square hACKH (OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf hK.symm hH.symm)
  obtain ⟨hBD_DE, hDE_EC, hEC_CB, hCBD, -, -, hECB⟩ := id hBDEC
  have hBD_BC : ‖B D‖ = ‖B C‖ :=
    hBD_DE.trans (hDE_EC.trans (hEC_CB.trans (len_symm C B)))
  have hCE_CB : ‖C E‖ = ‖C B‖ := (len_symm C E).trans hEC_CB
  have hBCE : ∠ B C E = ∟ :=
    (angle_symm hABC.ne₂₃ hE.triangle.ne₂₃.symm).trans hECB
  have hright' : ∠ C A B = ∟ :=
    (angle_symm hABC.ne₁₃.symm hABC.ne₁₂.symm).trans hright
  /- I.17 makes the angles at B and C acute. With the outward squares,
     `Prop47.within` puts A between the straight lines BD and CE. -/
  have hacB : ∠ A B C < ∟ := by
    have h17 := (Prop17 hABC).2.2
    rw [hright'] at h17
    exact Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_left h17
  have hacC : ∠ A C B < ∟ := by
    have h17 := (Prop17 hABC).2.1
    rw [hright] at h17
    exact Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_left h17
  obtain ⟨hCA_BD, -⟩ := Prop47.within hABC hD hCBD hacB
  obtain ⟨hBA_CE, -⟩ := Prop47.within hABC.acb hE.swap hBCE hacC
  -- through A let AL be drawn parallel to either BD or CE,
  have hBD : B ≠ D := hCA_BD.1
  have hCE : C ≠ E := hBA_CE.1
  obtain ⟨BD, hB_BD, hD_BD⟩ := Postulate1 B D hBD
  obtain ⟨CE, hC_CE, hE_CE⟩ := Postulate1 C E hCE
  obtain ⟨BC, hB_BC, hC_BC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hABC.ne₂₃
  obtain ⟨DE, hD_DE, hE_DE⟩ := Postulate1 D E hpsq.2.1
  have hBD_CE : Parallel BD CE := hpsq.1.parallel hB_BD hD_BD hE_CE hC_CE
  have hDE_BC : Parallel DE BC := hpsq.2.parallel hD_DE hE_DE hC_BC hB_BC
  have hA_BD : ¬ OnLine A BD :=
    not_on_line_of_same_side (same_side_symm (hCA_BD.sameSide hB_BD hD_BD))
  obtain ⟨AL, hA_AL, hAL_BD⟩ := Prop31.line hA_BD
  have hA_CE : ¬ OnLine A CE :=
    not_on_line_of_same_side (same_side_symm (hBA_CE.sameSide hC_CE hE_CE))
  have hAL_CE : Parallel AL CE :=
    Prop30.parallel hAL_BD hBD_CE.symm (fun e => hA_CE (e ▸ hA_AL))
  /- The parallel meets DE at L and BC at its unlettered foot (`Prop30.meet`). -/
  have hDE_BD : DE ≠ BD := fun e => hDE_BC.not_onLine (e ▸ hB_BD) hB_BC
  obtain ⟨L, hL_DE, hL_AL⟩ := Prop30.meet hAL_BD hD_BD hD_DE hDE_BD
  have hBC_BD : BC ≠ BD := fun e => hD.triangle.off_line hB_BC hC_BC (e ▸ hD_BD)
  obtain ⟨X, hX_BC, hX_AL⟩ := Prop30.meet hAL_BD hB_BD hB_BC hBC_BD
  have hXL : X ≠ L := fun e => hDE_BC.not_onLine (e ▸ hL_DE) hX_BC
  have hDL : D ≠ L := fun e => hAL_BD.not_onLine (e ▸ hL_AL) hD_BD
  have hXB : X ≠ B := fun e => hAL_BD.not_onLine (e ▸ hX_AL) hB_BD
  have hLE : L ≠ E := fun e => hAL_CE.not_onLine hL_AL (e ▸ hE_CE)
  have hCX : C ≠ X := fun e => hAL_CE.not_onLine hX_AL (e ▸ hC_CE)
  have P₁ : Parallelogram B D L X :=
    ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel hBD hXL.symm hB_BD hD_BD hL_AL hX_AL hAL_BD.symm,
      AreParallel.of_parallel hDL hXB hD_DE hL_DE hX_BC hB_BC hDE_BC⟩
  have P₂ : Parallelogram X L E C :=
    ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel hXL hCE.symm hX_AL hL_AL hE_CE hC_CE hAL_CE,
      AreParallel.of_parallel hLE hCX hL_DE hE_DE hC_BC hX_BC hDE_BC⟩
  have hXLA : Collinear X L A := ⟨AL, hX_AL, hL_AL, hA_AL⟩
  -- and let AD, FC be joined.
  /- The joined straight lines are the sides of the triangles in I.4 below. -/
  -- Then, since each of the angles BAC, BAG is right, it follows that with a straight line BA,
  -- and at the point A on it, the two straight lines AC, AG not lying on the same side make
  -- the adjacent angles equal to two right angles; therefore CA is in a straight line with
  -- AG. [I. 14]
  have hCAG : Between C A G := Prop14 hG.symm.swap (by
    rw [hright, angle_symm hABC.ne₁₂.symm hG.triangle.ne₁₃.symm, hABFG.2.2.2.1])
  -- For the same reason BA is also in a straight line with AH.
  have hBAH : Between B A H := Prop14 hH.symm.swap (by
    rw [hright', angle_symm hABC.ne₁₃.symm hH.triangle.ne₁₃.symm, hACKH.2.2.2.1])
  /- Euclid proves one half and then says "similarly". We give these sentences
     once over any letters, using the straightness and acute angle already
     proved, and apply them at B and at C. -/
  have half : ∀ {A B C D F G X L : Point}, Triangle A B C →
      ‖B D‖ = ‖B C‖ → ∠ C B D = ∟ → OppositeSidesOf D A B C →
      Square A B F G → OppositeSidesOf F C A B → Parallelogram A B F G →
      Between C A G → ∠ A B C < ∟ → Parallelogram X B D L → Collinear X L A →
      quadArea X B D L = quadArea A B F G := by
    intro A B C D F G X L hABC hBD hCBD hD hsq hF hpsq hCAG hacute hp hX
    obtain ⟨hAB_BF, -, -, -, hABF, -, -⟩ := hsq
    -- And, since the angle DBC is equal to the angle FBA: for each is right: let the angle ABC
    -- be added to each; therefore the whole angle DBA is equal to the whole angle FBC. [C.N. 2]
    obtain ⟨hCA_BD, hCD_BA⟩ := Prop47.within hABC hD hCBD hacute
    obtain ⟨hAC_BF, hAF_BC⟩ := Prop47.within hABC.cba hF.swap hABF
      (by rw [angle_symm hABC.ne₂₃.symm hABC.ne₁₂]; exact hacute)
    have hDBA : ∠ D B A = ∠ D B C + ∠ C B A :=
      angle_add_of_within hCA_BD hCD_BA
    have hFBC : ∠ F B C = ∠ F B A + ∠ A B C :=
      angle_add_of_within hAC_BF hAF_BC
    have hBD_ne : B ≠ D := hCA_BD.1
    have hBF_ne : B ≠ F := hAC_BF.1
    have hrights : ∠ D B C = ∠ F B A := by
      rw [angle_symm hBD_ne.symm hABC.ne₂₃.symm, hCBD,
        angle_symm hBF_ne.symm hABC.ne₁₂, hABF]
    have hadd := CommonNotion2 hrights (Eq.refl (∠ A B C))
    have hang : ∠ D B A = ∠ F B C := by
      rw [hDBA, hFBC, angle_symm hABC.ne₂₃.symm hABC.ne₁₂]
      exact hadd
    -- And, since DB is equal to BC, and FB to BA, the two sides AB, BD are equal to the two
    -- sides FB, BC respectively; and the angle ABD is equal to the angle FBC; therefore the base
    -- AD is equal to the base FC, and the triangle ABD is equal to the triangle FBC. [I. 4]
    have hABD : ∠ A B D = ∠ F B C :=
      (angle_symm hABC.ne₁₂ hBD_ne.symm).trans hang
    obtain ⟨hAD_FC, h4, -, -⟩ :=
      Prop4 hCD_BA.symm.triangle hAC_BF.symm.triangle
        ((len_symm B A).trans hAB_BF) hBD hABD
    -- Now the parallelogram BL is double of the triangle ABD, for they have the same base BD and
    -- are in the same parallels BD, AL. [I. 41]
    have h41a : quadArea X B D L = △ B A D + △ B A D := Prop41 hp hX
    -- And the square GB is double of the triangle FBC, for they again have the same base FB and
    -- are in the same parallels FB, GC. [I. 41]
    obtain ⟨GC, hC_GC, hA_GC, hG_GC⟩ := collinear_of_between hCAG
    have h41b : quadArea G F B A = △ F C B + △ F C B :=
      Prop41 hpsq.rotate.rotate.rotate.reverse ⟨GC, hG_GC, hA_GC, hC_GC⟩
    -- [But the doubles of equals are equal to one another.]
    have hdouble := CommonNotion2 h4 h4
    -- Therefore the parallelogram BL is also equal to the square GB.
    calc
      quadArea X B D L = △ B A D + △ B A D := h41a
      _ = △ B F C + △ B F C := hdouble
      _ = △ F C B + △ F C B := by rw [area_bca B F C]
      _ = quadArea G F B A := h41b.symm
      _ = quadArea A B F G := by
        rw [quadArea_reverse, hpsq.rotate.rotate.rotate.quadArea_rotate]
  have h₁ : quadArea X B D L = quadArea A B F G :=
    half hABC hBD_BC hCBD hD hABFG hF hABFGpar hCAG hacB P₁.rotate.rotate.rotate hXLA
  -- Similarly, if AE, BK be joined, the parallelogram CL can also be proved equal to the
  -- square HC; therefore the whole square BDEC is equal to the two squares GB, HC. [C.N. 2]
  have h₂ : quadArea X C E L = quadArea A C K H :=
    half hABC.acb hCE_CB hBCE hE.swap hACKH hK hACKHpar hBAH hacC P₂.reverse hXLA
  /- The foot of AL lies between B and C, and L between D and E: A lies
     between BD and CE, and AL is parallel to both (`Between.of_inside`). -/
  have ss : ∀ {P Q R : Point} {N : Line},
      SameSide P Q N → SameSide Q R N → SameSide P R N :=
    fun h₁ h₂ => same_side_trans (same_side_symm h₁) h₂
  have hAC_BD : SameSide A C BD := same_side_symm (hCA_BD.sameSide hB_BD hD_BD)
  have hAB_CE : SameSide A B CE := same_side_symm (hBA_CE.sameSide hC_CE hE_CE)
  have hBXC : Between B X C :=
    Between.of_inside hB_BD hC_CE ⟨BC, hB_BC, hX_BC, hC_BC⟩
      (ss (hAL_BD.sameSide hX_AL hA_AL) hAC_BD)
      (ss (hAL_CE.sameSide hX_AL hA_AL) hAB_CE)
  have hCE_BD : SameSide C E BD :=
    same_side_symm (hpsq.sameSideOf.sameSide hB_BD hD_BD)
  have hBD_CE' : SameSide B D CE := hpsq.rotate.rotate.sameSideOf.sameSide hE_CE hC_CE
  have hDLE : Between D L E :=
    Between.of_inside hD_BD hE_CE ⟨DE, hD_DE, hL_DE, hE_DE⟩
      (ss (ss (hAL_BD.sameSide hL_AL hA_AL) hAC_BD) hCE_BD)
      (ss (ss (hAL_CE.sameSide hL_AL hA_AL) hAB_CE) hBD_CE')
  have hwhole : quadArea B D E C = quadArea X B D L + quadArea X C E L := by
    rw [quadArea_add_of_parallelograms P₁ P₂ hBXC hDLE,
      P₁.rotate.rotate.rotate.quadArea_rotate, quadArea_reverse X C E L]
  have hequal := hwhole.trans (CommonNotion2 h₁ h₂)
  -- And the square BDEC is described on BC, and the squares GB, HC on BA, AC.
  /- These are the three given squares. -/
  -- Therefore the square on the side BC is equal to the squares on the sides BA, AC.
  -- Therefore etc.
  exact hequal
  -- Q. E. D.

statement.note: Proved for squares standing outward, as Euclid describes them; inward squares on the same sides are equal to these, as proved after I.46.

state.lean_statement:
theorem Prop47 {A B C D E F G H K : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hright : ∠ B A C = ∟)
    (hBDEC : Square B D E C) (hD : OppositeSidesOf D A B C) (hE : OppositeSidesOf E A B C)
    (hABFG : Square A B F G) (hF : OppositeSidesOf F C A B) (hG : OppositeSidesOf G C A B)
    (hACKH : Square A C K H) (hK : OppositeSidesOf K B A C) (hH : OppositeSidesOf H B A C) :
    quadArea B D E C = quadArea A B F G + quadArea A C K H

named_declarations.Elements.BookI.Prop47.within:
/-- Where the squares fall. If the angle ABC is less than a right angle, and BD
stands at right angles to BC on the other side of it from A, then C lies within
the angle ABD: on A's side of BD, and on D's side of BA. Euclid reads this
off his figure when he adds the angle ABC to the right angles DBC, FBA, and
again when he takes the parallelograms BL, CL to make up the square BDEC.

The straight line AD crosses BC, since it joins points on either side of it. Not
at B, for then the angles ABC, CBD would make two right angles [I. 13], and
CBD alone is right. Not beyond B from C, for then the angle ABD would be
greater than two right angles: the angle on the far side of AB from C is
greater than right [I. 13], and to it is added the right angle on the far side of
BD. So it crosses on the ray from B through C, and C lies where the crossing
point does. [I. 13] -/
theorem Prop47.within {A B C D : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hD : OppositeSidesOf D A B C)
    (hCBD : ∠ C B D = ∟) (hacute : ∠ A B C < ∟) :
    SameSideOf C A B D ∧ SameSideOf C D B A

definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Square:
/-- **Definition 22.** "Of quadrilateral figures, a square is that which is both
equilateral and right-angled." The corners are `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, in order. -/
def Square (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  ‖A B‖ = ‖B C‖ ∧ ‖B C‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖C D‖ = ‖D A‖ ∧
    ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle

state.enunciation: In right-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the right angle is equal to the squares on the sides containing the right angle.
state.heath_proof:
Let ABC be a right-angled triangle having the angle BAC right;

I say that the square on BC is equal to the squares on BA, AC.

For let there be described on BC the square BDEC, and on BA, AC the squares GB, HC; [I. 46] through A let AL be drawn parallel to either BD or CE, and let AD, FC be joined.

Then, since each of the angles BAC, BAG is right, it follows that with a straight line BA, and at the point A on it, the two straight lines AC, AG not lying on the same side make the adjacent angles equal to two right angles; therefore CA is in a straight line with AG. [I. 14]

For the same reason BA is also in a straight line with AH.

And, since the angle DBC is equal to the angle FBA: for each is right: let the angle ABC be added to each; therefore the whole angle DBA is equal to the whole angle FBC. [C.N. 2]

And, since DB is equal to BC, and FB to BA, the two sides AB, BD are equal to the two sides FB, BC respectively; and the angle ABD is equal to the angle FBC; therefore the base AD is equal to the base FC, and the triangle ABD is equal to the triangle FBC. [I. 4]

Now the parallelogram BL is double of the triangle ABD, for they have the same base BD and are in the same parallels BD, AL. [I. 41]

And the square GB is double of the triangle FBC, for they again have the same base FB and are in the same parallels FB, GC. [I. 41]

[But the doubles of equals are equal to one another.]

Therefore the parallelogram BL is also equal to the square GB.

Similarly, if AE, BK be joined, the parallelogram CL can also be proved equal to the square HC; therefore the whole square BDEC is equal to the two squares GB, HC. [C.N. 2]

And the square BDEC is described on BC, and the squares GB, HC on BA, AC.

Therefore the square on the side BC is equal to the squares on the sides BA, AC.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_statement:
theorem Prop47 {A B C D E F G H K : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hright : ∠ B A C = ∟)
    (hBDEC : Square B D E C) (hD : OppositeSidesOf D A B C) (hE : OppositeSidesOf E A B C)
    (hABFG : Square A B F G) (hF : OppositeSidesOf F C A B) (hG : OppositeSidesOf G C A B)
    (hACKH : Square A C K H) (hK : OppositeSidesOf K B A C) (hH : OppositeSidesOf H B A C) :
    quadArea B D E C = quadArea A B F G + quadArea A C K H

state.enunciation: If in a triangle the square on one of the sides be equal to the squares on the remaining two sides of the triangle, the angle contained by the remaining two sides of the triangle is right.
state.heath_proof:
For in the triangle ABC let the square on one side BC be equal to the squares on the sides BA, AC;

I say that the angle BAC is right.

For let AD be drawn from the point A at right angles to the straight line AC, let AD be made equal to BA, and let DC be joined.

Since DA is equal to AB, the square on DA is also equal to the square on AB.

Let the square on AC be added to each; therefore the squares on DA, AC are equal to the squares on BA, AC.

But the square on DC is equal to the squares on DA, AC, for the angle DAC is right; [I. 47] and the square on BC is equal to the squares on BA, AC, for this is the hypothesis; therefore the square on DC is equal to the square on BC, so that the side DC is also equal to BC.

And, since DA is equal to AB, and AC is common, the two sides DA, AC are equal to the two sides BA, AC; and the base DC is equal to the base BC; therefore the angle DAC is equal to the angle BAC. [I. 8]

But the angle DAC is right; therefore the angle BAC is also right.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.

theorem Prop48 {A B C P Q R S T U : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C)
    (hBC : Square B P Q C) (hPQ : SameSideOf P Q B C)
    (hBA : Square A B R S) (hRS : SameSideOf R S A B)
    (hAC : Square A C T U) (hTU : SameSideOf T U A C)
    (h : quadArea B P Q C = quadArea A B R S + quadArea A C T U) :
    ∠ B A C = ∟

statement.note: The three given squares may each stand on either side of its side.

bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34:
/-- In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the
diameter bisects the areas. -/
theorem Prop34 {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A C D B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ C D B ∧ ∠ A B D = ∠ A C D ∧
      △ A B C = △ D C B
bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop34.bisect:
/-- The diameter bisects the parallelogram, said of its area: the parallelogram
ABCD, measured by its diameter AC, is double the triangle ABC. I.35–I.47 cite
I.34 for this ("the triangle ABC is half of the parallelogram EBCA; for the diameter
AB bisects it"). To halve by the other diameter, name the parallelogram from the
next corner (`Parallelogram.rotate`) and turn its area round with
`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`. [I. 34] -/
theorem Prop34.bisect {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea A B C D = △ A B C + △ A B C
bridges.Elements.BookI.Prop46.square_eq:
/-- Squares described on equal straight lines are equal. Euclid assumes this in
I.48 ("since DA is equal to AB, the square on DA is also equal to the square on
AB"). Heath reports, under I.46, that Proclus proves it. Each square is a
parallelogram (`Prop28.square`), so the diameter AC cuts it into the triangles
ABC and ACD, right-angled at B and D; and I.4 makes these equal to the triangles
A'B'C' and A'C'D'. Here a square ABCD is "described on AB" when its far corners
C, D lie on one side of AB. [I. 4, I. 28] -/
theorem Prop46.square_eq {A B C D A' B' C' D' : Point} (h : Square A B C D)
    (hCD : SameSideOf C D A B) (h' : Square A' B' C' D') (hCD' : SameSideOf C' D' A' B')
    (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖A' B'‖) : quadArea A B C D = quadArea A' B' C' D'
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.cross:
/-- The diameters of a parallelogram cross: in the parallelogram ABCD, some point
lies between A and C and between B and D. Its sides AB and DC are
parallel, so they do not cross, and `AreParallel.cross_or` leaves only the
diameters. -/
theorem Parallelogram.cross (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    ∃ X : Point, Between A X C ∧ Between B X D
bridges.Elements.Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate:
/-- A parallelogram has the same area whichever diameter cuts it: the parallelogram
ABCD measured by BD, as BCDA, is the same as measured by AC. -/
theorem Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea B C D A = quadArea A B C D

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Square:
/-- **Definition 22.** "Of quadrilateral figures, a square is that which is both
equilateral and right-angled." The corners are `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, in order. -/
def Square (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  ‖A B‖ = ‖B C‖ ∧ ‖B C‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖C D‖ = ‖D A‖ ∧
    ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle
