I.2.enunciation: To place at a given point (as an extremity) a straight line equal to a given straight line.

I.3.enunciation: Given two unequal straight lines, to cut off from the greater a straight line equal to the less.

I.4.enunciation: If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the base, the triangle will be equal to the triangle, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend.

I.11.enunciation: To draw a straight line at right angles to a given straight line from a given point on it.

I.29.enunciation: A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on the same side equal to two right angles.

I.30.enunciation: Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another.

I.31.enunciation: Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line.

I.34.enunciation: In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the diameter bisects the areas.

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Contain:
/-- The lengths `a` and `b` contain the area `x`: some rectangle `PQRS` has `PQ` equal
to `a`, `PS` equal to `b`, and is equal to `x`; or one of `a`, `b` is nothing, and so
is `x`. -/
def Contain (a b : Length) (x : Area) : Prop :=
  ((a = 0 ∨ b = 0) ∧ x = 0) ∨
    ∃ P Q R S : Point, Rectangle P Q R S ∧ ‖P Q‖ = a ∧ ‖P S‖ = b ∧ quadArea P Q R S = x
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ P ≠ A ∧ Collinear A B P ∧ ¬ Between P A B
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.Rectangle:
/-- **Definition II.1.** A rectangular parallelogram: the parallelogram `ABCD`, its
corners taken in order, with all four of its angles right. Euclid says "rectangular",
as Definition 22 says "right-angled" of the square. -/
def Rectangle (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  Parallelogram A B C D ∧ ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rect:
/-- **The rectangle contained by `AB`, `CD`** (Definition II.1): the area of any
rectangle whose sides about a right angle are equal to `AB` and `CD`. Lean chooses one
such area (`Classical.epsilon`); `Rectangle.contained` shows that every such
rectangle is equal to it. -/
noncomputable def rect (A B C D : Point) : Area :=
  Classical.epsilon (Contain ‖A B‖ ‖C D‖)
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle

state.enunciation: If there be two straight lines, and one of them be cut into any number of segments whatever, the rectangle contained by the two straight lines is equal to the rectangles contained by the uncut straight line and each of the segments.
state.heath_proof:
Let A, BC be two straight lines, and let BC be cut at random at the points D, E;

I say that the rectangle contained by A, BC is equal to the rectangle contained by A, BD, that contained by A, DE and that contained by A, EC.

For let BF be drawn from B at right angles to BC; [I. 11]

let BG be made equal to A, [I. 3]

through G let GH be drawn parallel to BC, [I. 31]

and through D, E, C let DK, EL, CH be drawn parallel to BG.

Then BH is equal to BK, DL, EH.

Now BH is the rectangle A, BC, for it is contained by GB, BC, and BG is equal to A;

BK is the rectangle A, BD, for it is contained by GB, BD, and BG is equal to A;

and DL is the rectangle A, DE, for DK, that is BG [I. 34], is equal to A.

Similarly also EH is the rectangle A, EC.

Therefore the rectangle A, BC is equal to the rectangle A, BD, the rectangle A, DE and the rectangle A, EC.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- **II.1, any number of segments** (companion of II.1). If the straight line from B to its
end is cut at any number of points in order, the rectangle contained by A₁A₂ and the whole
is equal to the rectangles contained by A₁A₂ and each of the segments. The list `ps` is
the points of section followed by the end; with no points of section it is the whole
straight line alone, and with no points at all the straight line is nothing and so is each
side. -/
theorem Prop1.general {A₁ A₂ B : Point} {ps : List Point} (h : InOrder (B :: ps)) :
    rect A₁ A₂ B (endOf B ps) =
      Magnitude.sum ((segments (B :: ps)).map fun s => rect A₁ A₂ s.1 s.2) := by
  /- Repeat the one-cut construction, taking the first segment at each step. -/
  induction ps generalizing B with
  | nil =>
      /- With no end point, both the rectangle on BB and the sum are nothing. -/
      simp only [endOf, segments, List.map, Magnitude.sum, rect_self_right]
  | cons P ps ih =>
      cases ps with
      | nil =>
          /- With no cut, BP is the whole straight line and its only segment. -/
          simp only [endOf, segments, List.map, Magnitude.sum, add_zero]
      | cons Q rest =>
          /- Cut off BP, then apply the same argument to the remaining segments. -/
          have hBP : Between B P (endOf P (Q :: rest)) :=
            InOrder.between_end h (List.cons_ne_nil Q rest)
          have hrest := ih h.2.2
          calc
            rect A₁ A₂ B (endOf B (P :: Q :: rest)) =
                rect A₁ A₂ B P + rect A₁ A₂ P (endOf P (Q :: rest)) := Prop1.two hBP
            _ = rect A₁ A₂ B P +
                Magnitude.sum ((segments (P :: Q :: rest)).map fun s => rect A₁ A₂ s.1 s.2) := by
              rw [hrest]
            _ = Magnitude.sum
                ((segments (B :: P :: Q :: rest)).map fun s => rect A₁ A₂ s.1 s.2) := rfl

/-- **II.1, one cut** (companion of II.1). If the straight line BC is cut at D, the

cut at the points D and E. A list of one point, or of none, is in order. -/
def InOrder : List Point → Prop

rectangle whose sides about a right angle are equal to `AB` and `CD`. Lean chooses one

def segments : List Point → List (Point × Point)

I.3.enunciation: Given two unequal straight lines, to cut off from the greater a straight line equal to the less.

I.11.enunciation: To draw a straight line at right angles to a given straight line from a given point on it.

I.31.enunciation: Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line.

I.34.enunciation: In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the diameter bisects the areas.

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Contain:
/-- The lengths `a` and `b` contain the area `x`: some rectangle `PQRS` has `PQ` equal
to `a`, `PS` equal to `b`, and is equal to `x`; or one of `a`, `b` is nothing, and so
is `x`. -/
def Contain (a b : Length) (x : Area) : Prop :=
  ((a = 0 ∨ b = 0) ∧ x = 0) ∨
    ∃ P Q R S : Point, Rectangle P Q R S ∧ ‖P Q‖ = a ∧ ‖P S‖ = b ∧ quadArea P Q R S = x
definitions.InOrder:
/-- **Points in order.** `InOrder ps`: each point of the list `ps` differs from the next,
and of any three in a row the middle one lies between the other two. So the points lie on
one straight line, in the order listed: `InOrder [B, D, E, C]` is II.1's straight line BC
cut at the points D and E. A list of one point, or of none, is in order. -/
def InOrder : List Point → Prop
  | [] => True
  | [_] => True
  | [p, q] => p ≠ q
  | p :: q :: r :: rest => p ≠ q ∧ Between p q r ∧ InOrder (q :: r :: rest)
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.Magnitude.sum:
/-- **The sum of a list of magnitudes** of one kind: nothing for the empty list, and
otherwise the first added to the sum of the rest. So `Magnitude.sum [a, b, c]` is
`a + (b + (c + 0))`, which is `a + b + c`. -/
noncomputable def Magnitude.sum {k : Kind} : List (Magnitude k) → Magnitude k
  | [] => 0
  | a :: as => a + Magnitude.sum as
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.Rectangle:
/-- **Definition II.1.** A rectangular parallelogram: the parallelogram `ABCD`, its
corners taken in order, with all four of its angles right. Euclid says "rectangular",
as Definition 22 says "right-angled" of the square. -/
def Rectangle (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  Parallelogram A B C D ∧ ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.endOf:
/-- **The end** of the straight line that starts at `B` and runs through the points `ps`:
the last of them, or `B` itself if there are none. `endOf B [D, E, C]` is C. -/
def endOf (B : Point) : List Point → Point
  | [] => B
  | p :: ps => endOf p ps
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rect:
/-- **The rectangle contained by `AB`, `CD`** (Definition II.1): the area of any
rectangle whose sides about a right angle are equal to `AB` and `CD`. Lean chooses one
such area (`Classical.epsilon`); `Rectangle.contained` shows that every such
rectangle is equal to it. -/
noncomputable def rect (A B C D : Point) : Area :=
  Classical.epsilon (Contain ‖A B‖ ‖C D‖)
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle
definitions.segments:
/-- **The segments** of a straight line cut at points in order: each point of the list with
the next, as the ends of one segment. The segments of `[B, D, E, C]` are BD, DE and EC. The
points need not be in order, or on one straight line: in the companions of I.45 and II.14
for a checked fan (`Prop45.fan`, `Prop14.fan`), the segments of a figure's corners A₁, A₂,
…, Aₙ are its sides A₁A₂, …, Aₙ₋₁Aₙ, those away from the corner A₀, and each side with A₀
makes one of the triangles into which the straight lines from A₀ divide the figure, when the
fan's conditions hold. -/
def segments : List Point → List (Point × Point)
  | p :: q :: rest => (p, q) :: segments (q :: rest)
  | _ => []

state.lean_proof:
/-- **II.1, one cut** (companion of II.1). If the straight line BC is cut at D, the
rectangle contained by A₁A₂ and BC is equal to the rectangles contained by A₁A₂ and each
of BD, DC. II.1's construction, with one parallel drawn through D. The uncut straight line
A₁A₂ may be nothing, and then every rectangle is nothing. -/
theorem Prop1.two {A₁ A₂ B C D : Point} (h : Between B D C) :
    rect A₁ A₂ B C = rect A₁ A₂ B D + rect A₁ A₂ D C := by
  /- If A₁A₂ is nothing, all three rectangles are nothing. -/
  by_cases hA : A₁ = A₂
  · subst A₂
    simp only [rect_self_left, add_zero]
  have hBC : B ≠ C := ne_of_between_ends h
  obtain ⟨BC, hB_BC, hC_BC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hBC
  have hD_BC : OnLine D BC := on_line_of_between_ends h hB_BC hC_BC
  /- Draw BF at right angles to BC by I.11. -/
  obtain ⟨Q, hQ, -⟩ := exists_off_line hBC []
  obtain ⟨F, hFQ, hright⟩ := BookI.Prop11 hBC ⟨BC, hB_BC, hC_BC, hB_BC⟩ hQ
  have hCBF : ∠ C B F = ∟ := hright C ⟨BC, hB_BC, hC_BC, hC_BC⟩ hBC.symm
  /- Place A₁A₂ at B by I.2 and produce BF far enough along its ray.
     I.3 then cuts off BG equal to A₁A₂. -/
  obtain ⟨P, hP⟩ := BookI.Prop2 B A₁ A₂ hA
  have hBP : B ≠ P := ne_of_len_eq hP hA
  have hBF : B ≠ F := hFQ.triangle.ne₁₃
  obtain ⟨Y, hFBY⟩ := produce hBF.symm
  obtain ⟨X, hYBX, hlt⟩ := produce_longer (ne_of_between (between_symm hFBY)) hBP
  have hX : OnRay X B F := OnRay.of_between_between (between_symm hFBY) hYBX
  obtain ⟨G, hBGX, hBG⟩ := BookI.Prop3 hA (hP ▸ hlt)
  have hCBG : ∠ C B G = ∟ := by
    rw [angle_onRay_right (OnRay.of_between hBGX) hBC.symm, angle_onRay_right hX hBC.symm]
    exact hCBF
  have hGQ : SameSideOf G Q B C :=
    SameSideOf.of_onRay (OnRay.of_between hBGX) (SameSideOf.of_onRay hX hFQ)
  have hG_BC : ¬ OnLine G BC := not_on_line_of_same_side (hGQ.sameSide hB_BC hC_BC)
  /- Draw GH parallel to BC, and DK and CH parallel to BG, by I.31. -/
  obtain ⟨GH, hG_GH, hGH_BC⟩ := BookI.Prop31.line hG_BC
  obtain ⟨K, hK_GH, hGBDK⟩ :=
    BookI.Prop31.parallelogram hGH_BC hG_GH hB_BC hD_BC (ne_of_between h)
  obtain ⟨H, hH_GH, hGBCH⟩ := BookI.Prop31.parallelogram hGH_BC hG_GH hB_BC hC_BC hBC
  obtain ⟨BG, hB_BG, hG_BG⟩ := Postulate1 B G (ne_of_between hBGX)
  obtain ⟨DK, hD_DK, hK_DK⟩ := Postulate1 D K hGBDK.1.2.1
  obtain ⟨CH, hC_CH, hH_CH⟩ := Postulate1 C H hGBCH.1.2.1
  have hDK_BG : Parallel DK BG := (hGBDK.1.parallel hG_BG hB_BG hD_DK hK_DK).symm
  have hCH_BG : Parallel CH BG := (hGBCH.1.parallel hG_BG hB_BG hC_CH hH_CH).symm
  have hDC : D ≠ C := (ne_of_between (between_symm h)).symm
  /- DK meets BC only at D. It is distinct from CH, and I.30 makes them parallel. -/
  have hC_DK : ¬ OnLine C DK :=
    hGH_BC.symm.off_transversal hD_BC hK_GH hD_DK hK_DK hC_BC hDC.symm
  have hDK_CH : Parallel DK CH :=
    BookI.Prop30.parallel hDK_BG hCH_BG (fun e => hC_DK (e.symm ▸ hC_CH))
  /- The parallels put K between G and H, so BH divides into BK and DH. -/
  have hGKH : Between G K H := Parallel.between hDK_BG.symm hDK_CH.symm hB_BG hD_DK hC_CH
    h hG_BG hK_DK hH_CH ⟨GH, hG_GH, hK_GH, hH_GH⟩
  have hBGKD : Parallelogram B G K D := hGBDK.reverse.rotate.rotate.rotate
  have hBGHC : Parallelogram B G H C := hGBCH.reverse.rotate.rotate.rotate
  have hDKHC : Parallelogram D K H C :=
    ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel hGBDK.1.2.1 hGBCH.1.2.1.symm hD_DK hK_DK hH_CH hC_CH hDK_CH,
      AreParallel.of_parallel (ne_of_between (between_symm hGKH)).symm hDC.symm
        hK_GH hH_GH hC_BC hD_BC hGH_BC⟩
  have hparts : quadArea B G H C = quadArea B G K D + quadArea D K H C :=
    quadArea_add_of_parallelograms hBGKD hDKHC h hGKH
  /- BH and BK are contained by BG with BC and BD, respectively. -/
  have hBH : quadArea B G H C = rect A₁ A₂ B C :=
    (Rectangle.of_right hBGHC hCBG).eq_rect hBG rfl
  have hBK_rect : Rectangle B G K D := by
    refine Rectangle.of_right hBGKD ?_
    rw [angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between h) (ne_of_between hBGX).symm]
    exact hCBG
  have hBK : quadArea B G K D = rect A₁ A₂ B D := hBK_rect.eq_rect hBG rfl
  /- By I.34, DK equals BG and hence A₁A₂. The adjacent angle CDK is right,
     so DH is the rectangle contained by A₁A₂ and DC. -/
  have hDK : ‖D K‖ = ‖A₁ A₂‖ := by
    rw [len_symm D K, ← (BookI.Prop34 hGBDK).2.1, len_symm G B]
    exact hBG
  have hK_BC : ¬ OnLine K BC := hGH_BC.not_onLine hK_GH
  have hCDK : ∠ C D K = ∟ := by
    have hBDK := hBK_rect.2.2.2.2
    rw [angle_symm hGBDK.1.2.1.symm (ne_of_between h)] at hBDK
    rw [angle_symm hDC.symm hGBDK.1.2.1.symm,
      ← adjacent_eq_of_right hB_BC hC_BC h hK_BC hBDK]
    exact hBDK
  have hDH : quadArea D K H C = rect A₁ A₂ D C :=
    (Rectangle.of_right hDKHC hCDK).eq_rect hDK rfl
  rw [← hBH, hparts, hBK, hDH]

helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.of_parallel:
/-- Two different points of L, and two different points of M, are the ends of
parallel straight lines when L and M are parallel: two points fix one straight
line (System E, Generalities 1). With `AreParallel.parallel`, this says "AB is
parallel to CD" of any other two points P, Q of the straight line AB and R,
S of CD. -/
theorem AreParallel.of_parallel (hPQ : P ≠ Q) (hRS : R ≠ S) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L)
    (hR : OnLine R M) (hS : OnLine S M) (h : Parallel L M) : AreParallel P Q R S
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.parallel:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then a straight line through A and B is parallel
to one through C and D. -/
theorem AreParallel.parallel (h : AreParallel A B C D) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (hC : OnLine C M) (hD : OnLine D M) : Parallel L M
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.symm:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then CD is parallel to AB. -/
theorem AreParallel.symm (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.triangle:
/-- An end of one parallel is off the other: if AB is parallel to CD, then C
is not on the straight line AB, and ABC is a triangle. (Turned round with
`AreParallel.symm` and `.swap_right`, the same holds of D, and of A and B
beside CD.) -/
theorem AreParallel.triangle (h : AreParallel A B C D) : Triangle A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop11:
/-- To draw a straight line at right angles to a given straight line from a given point on it. -/
theorem Prop11 {A B C Q : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hC : Collinear A B C) (hQ : ¬ Collinear A B Q) :
    ∃ F : Point, SameSideOf F Q A B ∧ ∀ P : Point, Collinear A B P → P ≠ C → ∠ P C F = ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop2:
/-- To place at a given point (as an extremity) a straight line equal to a given straight
line. -/
theorem Prop2 (A B C : Point) (hBC : B ≠ C) :
    ∃ L : Point, ‖A L‖ = ‖B C‖
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29:
/-- A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one
another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on
the same side equal to two right angles. -/
theorem Prop29 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (hpar : AreParallel A B C D) (hAGB : Between A G B)
    (hCHD : Between C H D) (hEGH : Between E G H) (hGHF : Between G H F)
    (hBD : SameSideOf B D E F) :
    ∠ A G H = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ E G B = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D = ∟ + ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop3:
/-- Given two unequal straight lines, to cut off from the greater a straight line equal to the
less. -/
theorem Prop3 {A B C₁ C₂ : Point} (hC : C₁ ≠ C₂) (h : ‖C₁ C₂‖ < ‖A B‖) :
    ∃ E : Point, Between A E B ∧ ‖A E‖ = ‖C₁ C₂‖
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30:
/-- Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another. -/
theorem Prop30 {A B C D E F : Point} (h₁ : AreParallel A B E F) (h₂ : AreParallel C D E F)
    (hC : ¬ Collinear A B C) :
    AreParallel A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30.parallel:
/-- I.30 said of straight lines drawn and named: two different straight lines L and
M, each parallel to N, are parallel to one another. Euclid uses it without a
bracket in I.44 and I.47, where a straight line drawn "parallel to either" of two
parallels is parallel to both; in I.45 he brackets it. [I. 30] -/
theorem Prop30.parallel {L M N : Line} (hL : Parallel L N) (hM : Parallel M N) (hLM : L ≠ M) :
    Parallel L M
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31:
/-- Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line. -/
theorem Prop31 {A B C : Point} (hBC : B ≠ C) (hA : ¬ Collinear B C A) :
    ∃ E F : Point, Between E A F ∧ AreParallel E F B C
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31.line:
/-- I.31 said of straight lines drawn and named: through a point A off the
straight line L there is a straight line K parallel to L. I.31 gives two points
of it, one on either side of A, and Postulate 1 joins them. [I. 31] -/
theorem Prop31.line {A : Point} {L : Line} (hA : ¬ OnLine A L) :
    ∃ K : Line, OnLine A K ∧ Parallel K L
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31.parallelogram:
/-- Completing the parallelogram. If X lies on L, and Y and Z on M, which is
parallel to L, the straight line drawn through Z parallel to XY [I. 31] meets
L at a point W (`Prop30.meet`), and XYZW is a parallelogram. Euclid draws such
a parallel in I.37, I.38, I.42, I.44 and I.46, and reads the point where it meets
L, and the parallelogram, off his figure. [I. 30, I. 31] -/
theorem Prop31.parallelogram {X Y Z : Point} {L M : Line} (hLM : Parallel L M)
    (hX : OnLine X L) (hY : OnLine Y M) (hZ : OnLine Z M) (hYZ : Y ≠ Z) :
    ∃ W : Point, OnLine W L ∧ Parallelogram X Y Z W
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop34:
/-- In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the
diameter bisects the areas. -/
theorem Prop34 {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A C D B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ C D B ∧ ∠ A B D = ∠ A C D ∧
      △ A B C = △ D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop4:
/-- If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles
contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the base, the
triangle will be equal to the triangle, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining
angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend. -/
theorem Prop4 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖D F‖) (hA : ∠ B A C = ∠ E D F) :
    ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ ∧ △ A B C = △ D E F ∧ ∠ A B C = ∠ D E F ∧ ∠ A C B = ∠ D F E
helper_signatures.Elements.Contain.symm:
/-- Read either way round, two lengths contain the same areas: the rectangle PQRS
read as PSRQ has its sides about the angle at P in the other order. -/
theorem Contain.symm (h : Contain a b x) : Contain b a x
helper_signatures.Elements.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.of_between:
/-- A point between A and B is on the ray from A through B. -/
theorem OnRay.of_between (h : Between A P B) : OnRay P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.of_between_between:
/-- Two points beyond C from B lie on one ray from C: if C is between B and
D, and also between B and E, then E is on the ray from C through D
(System E, Between 7). So when a straight line is produced twice beyond the same
point, the angles made at that point by the two produced parts are the same. -/
theorem OnRay.of_between_between {C D E : Point} (hBCD : Between B C D) (hBCE : Between B C E) :
    OnRay E C D
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.symm:
/-- P is on the ray from A through B exactly when B is on the ray from A
through P: they are one and the same ray. -/
theorem OnRay.symm (h : OnRay P A B) : OnRay B A P
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.between:
/-- Parallels keep order. Let three straight lines be crossed by two others: if B
lies between A and C on one crossing straight line, then B' lies between A'
and C' on the other, when A, A' lie on L₁, B, B' on L, and C, C' on
L₃, and L₁ and L₃ are each parallel to L. All of L₁ lies on one side of
L, and all of L₃ on the other (`Parallel.sameSide`). Book II's figures use it
(`Parallelogram.figure`), where the parallels through the points of section meet the
far side of the square in the same order. -/
theorem Parallel.between (h₁ : Parallel L₁ L) (h₃ : Parallel L₃ L) (hA : OnLine A L₁)
    (hB : OnLine B L) (hC : OnLine C L₃) (hABC : Between A B C) (hA' : OnLine A' L₁)
    (hB' : OnLine B' L) (hC' : OnLine C' L₃) (hcol : Collinear A' B' C') :
    Between A' B' C'
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.not_onLine:
/-- Parallels do not meet: a point of L is not on M. -/
theorem Parallel.not_onLine (h : Parallel L M) (hP : OnLine P L) : ¬ OnLine P M
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.off_transversal:
/-- A straight line T falling on two parallels, at G on L and at H on M,
meets L at G alone: every other point of L is off T. Otherwise T, through
two points of L, would be L itself (System E, Generalities 1), and H would lie
on both parallels. -/
theorem Parallel.off_transversal (h : Parallel L M) (hG : OnLine G L) (hH : OnLine H M)
    (hGT : OnLine G T) (hHT : OnLine H T) (hP : OnLine P L) (hPG : P ≠ G) : ¬ OnLine P T
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.sameSide:
/-- All the points of one parallel lie on one side of the other: two points of L
are on the same side of M. Were they on opposite sides, the straight line L
joining them would cross M (System E, Intersection 1). -/
theorem Parallel.sameSide (h : Parallel L M) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L) :
    SameSide P Q M
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.symm:
/-- If L is parallel to M, then M is parallel to L. -/
theorem Parallel.symm (h : Parallel L M) : Parallel M L
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.reverse:
/-- The parallelogram ABCD, read the other way round from A, is the
parallelogram ADCB. -/
theorem Parallelogram.reverse (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Parallelogram A D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.rotate:
/-- The parallelogram ABCD, named from B, is the parallelogram BCDA. -/
theorem Parallelogram.rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Parallelogram B C D A
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.triangle:
/-- In the parallelogram ABCD, the corner C is off the straight line AB, so
ABC is a triangle. -/
theorem Parallelogram.triangle (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Triangle A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate1:
/-- **Postulate 1.** To draw a straight line from any point to any point. -/
axiom Postulate1 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Rectangle:
/-- **Definition II.1.** A rectangular parallelogram: the parallelogram `ABCD`, its
corners taken in order, with all four of its angles right. Euclid says "rectangular",
as Definition 22 says "right-angled" of the square. -/
def Rectangle (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Rectangle.eq_rect:
/-- Euclid's way of naming a rectangle: "BH is the rectangle A, BC, for it is contained
by GB, BC, and BG is equal to A" (II.1). If the sides PQ, PS of the rectangle
PQRS are equal to AB, CD, it is the rectangle contained by AB, CD.
[I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Rectangle.eq_rect (h : Rectangle P Q R S) (h₁ : ‖P Q‖ = ‖A B‖) (h₂ : ‖P S‖ = ‖C D‖) :
    quadArea P Q R S = rect A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.Rectangle.of_right:
/-- One right angle makes a rectangle: a parallelogram ABCD whose angle at A is
right has all four of its angles right. The angles DAB, ABC stand on the parallels
AD, BC, so together they make two right angles [I. 29], and the angle at B is
right; in the same way so are the angles at C and D. Euclid says so in II.4 ("the
angles KBC, GCB are equal to two right angles"), and elsewhere in Book II takes it
for granted, as Heath remarks of II.4 that "there can be no need to repeat exactly
that part of the proof of I. 46 which shows that all the angles of the figure there
constructed are right when one is" (vol. 1, p. 381). [I. 29] -/
theorem Rectangle.of_right (h : Parallelogram A B C D) (hA : ∠ D A B = ∟) :
    Rectangle A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.Rectangle.reverse:
/-- The rectangle ABCD, read the other way round from A, is the rectangle ADCB. -/
theorem Rectangle.reverse (h : Rectangle A B C D) : Rectangle A D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Rectangle.rotate:
/-- The rectangle ABCD, named from B, is the rectangle BCDA. -/
theorem Rectangle.rotate (h : Rectangle A B C D) : Rectangle B C D A
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf:
/-- `P` and `Q` lie on the same side of the straight line `AB`. -/
def SameSideOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.of_onRay:
/-- A point G on the ray from D through P is on the same side of the straight
line DE as P: the ray leaves DE at D and never crosses it again (System E,
Pasch 4). -/
theorem SameSideOf.of_onRay {D E F G P : Point} (hG : OnRay G D P) (hP : SameSideOf P F D E) :
    SameSideOf G F D E
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.sameSide:
/-- Two points on the same side of the straight line AB are on the same side of
any straight line drawn through A and B. -/
theorem SameSideOf.sameSide (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    SameSide P Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the same side of AB as Q, then Q is on the same side as P. -/
theorem SameSideOf.symm (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.triangle:
/-- A point on one side of the straight line AB is not on it, so ABP is a
triangle. -/
theorem SameSideOf.triangle (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : Triangle A B P
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.add_zero:
/-- Adding nothing changes nothing. (System E §3.5) -/
axiom add_zero (a : Magnitude k) : a + 0 = a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.adjacent_eq_of_right:
/-- A right angle is equal to the angle adjacent to it. (Diagram-angle 3; the
other half is Definition 10 together with Postulate 4) -/
axiom adjacent_eq_of_right (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) (h : Between A C B)
    (hD : ¬ OnLine D L) (hright : ∠ A C D = ∟) : ∠ A C D = ∠ D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.angle_symm:
/-- The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4) -/
axiom angle_symm (hAB : A ≠ B) (hCB : C ≠ B) : ∠ A B C = ∠ C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_symm:
/-- If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1) -/
axiom between_symm (h : Between A B C) : Between C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.len_symm:
/-- The straight line AB is the straight line BA. (Metric 3) -/
axiom len_symm (A B : Point) : ‖A B‖ = ‖B A‖
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between:
/-- A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between_ends:
/-- The ends of a finite straight line differ. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.not_on_line_of_same_side:
/-- Points on one side of a straight line are not on it. (Same side 3) -/
axiom not_on_line_of_same_side (h : SameSide A B L) : ¬ OnLine A L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between_ends:
/-- A straight line through A and C passes through every point between them.
(Between 3) -/
axiom on_line_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hC : OnLine C L) :
    OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₁₃:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₁₃ (h : Triangle A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_onRay_left:
/-- One arm traced through another point of its ray: if B' is on the ray from A
through B, the angle B'AC is the angle BAC. (System E, Diagram-angle 4) -/
theorem angle_onRay_left {B' : Point} (hB : OnRay B' A B) (hCA : C ≠ A) :
    ∠ B' A C = ∠ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_onRay_right:
/-- The other arm traced through another point of its ray: if C' is on the ray
from A through C, the angle BAC' is the angle BAC. (System E,
Diagram-angle 4) -/
theorem angle_onRay_right {C' : Point} (hC : OnRay C' A C) (hBA : B ≠ A) :
    ∠ B A C' = ∠ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.exists_off_line:
/-- There is a point off the straight line AB, avoiding any points already in the
figure. The circles with centres A and B through each other cut one another
(System E, Intersection 5), and a point where they cut is off AB: on AB it would be
as far from A as B is, and as far from B as A is, and one of the three points
would lie between the other two (Definition 15; System E, Between 6 and Diagram-segment
1). Then any point on its side will do (System E, Points 5). -/
theorem exists_off_line (hAB : A ≠ B) (avoid : List Point) :
    ∃ P : Point, Triangle A B P ∧ P ∉ avoid
helper_signatures.Elements.ne_of_len_eq:
/-- If a finite straight line AB has the length of one with different ends,
its own ends are different. -/
theorem ne_of_len_eq (h : ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖) (hCD : C ≠ D) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.produce:
/-- A finite straight line AB can be produced beyond B. [Post. 1, Post. 2] -/
theorem produce (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ C : Point, Between A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.produce_longer:
/-- Room to cut off. A finite straight line AB can be produced beyond B further
than a given straight line BC from B. Postulate 2 produces a straight line but
never says how far, and I.3 cuts off only from a *greater* straight line; so Euclid's
"let CE be made equal to CD [I. 3]", on a straight line produced, needs this first
(I.11, I.16, I.20, I.22). Describe the circle with centre B and distance BC
[Post. 3]; the straight line AB, produced beyond the centre, cuts it at some Y
(System E, Intersections 5); and BY, produced a little further still to X
[Post. 2], is greater than BY, that is, than BC [Def. 15, C.N. 5]. -/
theorem produce_longer (hAB : A ≠ B) (hBC : B ≠ C) :
    ∃ X : Point, Between A B X ∧ ‖B C‖ < ‖B X‖
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea_add_of_parallelograms:
/-- A parallelogram cut by a straight line parallel to two of its sides is the two
parallelograms it is cut into. If E lies between A and D, F between B and
C, and ABFE, EFCD are parallelograms, then the figure ABCD is ABFE and
EFCD together. Cut each piece and the whole into triangles from A and C; the
four-sided figure AFCE is measured by AC in the whole and by FE in the pieces,
and its diameters cross, for A and C lie on either side of EF. -/
theorem quadArea_add_of_parallelograms (h₁ : Parallelogram A B F E) (h₂ : Parallelogram E F C D)
    (hAED : Between A E D) (hBFC : Between B F C) :
    quadArea A B C D = quadArea A B F E + quadArea E F C D
helper_signatures.Elements.rect:
/-- **The rectangle contained by `AB`, `CD`** (Definition II.1): the area of any
rectangle whose sides about a right angle are equal to `AB` and `CD`. Lean chooses one
such area (`Classical.epsilon`); `Rectangle.contained` shows that every such
rectangle is equal to it. -/
noncomputable def rect (A B C D : Point) : Area
helper_signatures.Elements.rect_self_left:
/-- A rectangle with a side that is nothing is nothing: the rectangle contained by AA,
CD has no area. -/
theorem rect_self_left (A C D : Point) : rect A A C D = 0

I.2.enunciation: To place at a given point (as an extremity) a straight line equal to a given straight line.

I.3.enunciation: Given two unequal straight lines, to cut off from the greater a straight line equal to the less.

I.4.enunciation: If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the base, the triangle will be equal to the triangle, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend.

I.11.enunciation: To draw a straight line at right angles to a given straight line from a given point on it.

I.29.enunciation: A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on the same side equal to two right angles.

I.30.enunciation: Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another.

I.31.enunciation: Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line.

I.34.enunciation: In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the diameter bisects the areas.

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Contain:
/-- The lengths `a` and `b` contain the area `x`: some rectangle `PQRS` has `PQ` equal
to `a`, `PS` equal to `b`, and is equal to `x`; or one of `a`, `b` is nothing, and so
is `x`. -/
def Contain (a b : Length) (x : Area) : Prop :=
  ((a = 0 ∨ b = 0) ∧ x = 0) ∨
    ∃ P Q R S : Point, Rectangle P Q R S ∧ ‖P Q‖ = a ∧ ‖P S‖ = b ∧ quadArea P Q R S = x
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ P ≠ A ∧ Collinear A B P ∧ ¬ Between P A B
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.Rectangle:
/-- **Definition II.1.** A rectangular parallelogram: the parallelogram `ABCD`, its
corners taken in order, with all four of its angles right. Euclid says "rectangular",
as Definition 22 says "right-angled" of the square. -/
def Rectangle (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  Parallelogram A B C D ∧ ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rect:
/-- **The rectangle contained by `AB`, `CD`** (Definition II.1): the area of any
rectangle whose sides about a right angle are equal to `AB` and `CD`. Lean chooses one
such area (`Classical.epsilon`); `Rectangle.contained` shows that every such
rectangle is equal to it. -/
noncomputable def rect (A B C D : Point) : Area :=
  Classical.epsilon (Contain ‖A B‖ ‖C D‖)
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle

question.instructions:
Does every proposition called by the proof unit in `lean_proof` do work towards its conclusion or a substantive intermediate step of Euclid's argument? Also check for artificial hypothesis uses. Judge this unit's uses of the supplied helper signatures; helper bodies are outside this question. Heath's sentences stand as `--` lines and `cited` gives exact enunciations. In Lean, `have h : T := p` proves T by p and calls the result h; `obtain ⟨…⟩ := p` takes p apart into named pieces; `rw [h34, h37, …]` rewrites the goal by the equalities named. Follow uses through helper calls and tactics as well as explicit names. An anonymous binding or an unused hypothesis alone does not establish a defect. If both defects occur, choose `a dummy citation`.

criteria.an artificial hypothesis use: No dummy citation is established, but a hypothesis is mentioned only so that it looks used, and does no substantive work.
criteria.cannot tell: What is given here is not enough to decide.
criteria.all do work: Every proposition call supports a later step or the conclusion, or establishes a substantive intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid. No hypothesis is mentioned merely to look used. With no proposition calls the citation part alone is vacuous; hypothesis use must still be inspected.
criteria.a dummy citation: Some proposition call does no substantive work: its result neither supports the argument nor establishes a substantive intermediate fact, and merely supplies a citation while the step is done another way.

state.enunciation: If there be two straight lines, and one of them be cut into any number of segments whatever, the rectangle contained by the two straight lines is equal to the rectangles contained by the uncut straight line and each of the segments.
state.lean_statement:
theorem Prop1 {A₁ A₂ B C D E : Point} (hA : A₁ ≠ A₂) (hBDE : Between B D E) (hDEC : Between D E C) :
    rect A₁ A₂ B C = rect A₁ A₂ B D + rect A₁ A₂ D E + rect A₁ A₂ E C

attached_statements.II.1 general:
theorem Prop1.general {A₁ A₂ B : Point} {ps : List Point} (h : InOrder (B :: ps)) :
    rect A₁ A₂ B (endOf B ps) =
      Magnitude.sum ((segments (B :: ps)).map fun s => rect A₁ A₂ s.1 s.2)
attached_statements.II.1 two:
theorem Prop1.two {A₁ A₂ B C D : Point} (h : Between B D C) :
    rect A₁ A₂ B C = rect A₁ A₂ B D + rect A₁ A₂ D C

statement.note: With its companions: `Prop1.general` cuts the straight line at any number of points in order, `Prop1.two` at one; `Prop1` keeps Euclid's two, D and E.

representation.note: The straight line A is named by its two ends, A₁ and A₂, and the main theorem asks them to differ. The companions do not: A₁A₂ may be nothing, and then every rectangle is nothing, so they claim a little more than Euclid's two straight lines. `Prop1.general` takes the straight line from B cut at points given in order along it (`InOrder`), and adds the rectangles on its segments as a sum over the list; with no point of section the one segment is the whole, and with no point at all the straight line and each rectangle are nothing.

hypothesis-dropped.meaning: A hypothesis of Euclid's enunciation is left out of the statement, which so claims more than he does (III.9's point need not be within the circle).

bridges.Elements.InOrder.between_end:
/-- Of three or more points in order, the second lies between the first and the last. -/
theorem InOrder.between_end {B P : Point} {ps : List Point} (h : InOrder (B :: P :: ps))
    (hps : ps ≠ []) : Between B P (endOf P ps)
bridges.Elements.Rectangle.congr:
/-- Rectangles contained by equal straight lines are equal: if the rectangles PQRS,
P'Q'R'S' have PQ equal to P'Q' and PS to P'S', they are equal. The diameter
QS cuts off the triangle SPQ, right-angled at P, which is half the rectangle
[I. 34]; and the two halves are equal [I. 4]. Euclid takes this for granted whenever
he names a rectangle by its sides. [I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Rectangle.congr (h : Rectangle P Q R S) (h' : Rectangle P' Q' R' S')
    (h₁ : ‖P Q‖ = ‖P' Q'‖) (h₂ : ‖P S‖ = ‖P' S'‖) :
    quadArea P Q R S = quadArea P' Q' R' S'
bridges.Elements.Rectangle.contained:
/-- **A rectangle is contained by its sides** (Definition II.1): the rectangle PQRS is
the rectangle contained by PQ, PS, the two straight lines containing its right
angle at P. `rect` chose some rectangle contained by straight lines equal to these,
and by `Rectangle.congr` the two are equal. [I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Rectangle.contained (h : Rectangle P Q R S) : quadArea P Q R S = rect P Q P S
bridges.Elements.Rectangle.eq_rect:
/-- Euclid's way of naming a rectangle: "BH is the rectangle A, BC, for it is contained
by GB, BC, and BG is equal to A" (II.1). If the sides PQ, PS of the rectangle
PQRS are equal to AB, CD, it is the rectangle contained by AB, CD.
[I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Rectangle.eq_rect (h : Rectangle P Q R S) (h₁ : ‖P Q‖ = ‖A B‖) (h₂ : ‖P S‖ = ‖C D‖) :
    quadArea P Q R S = rect A B C D
bridges.Elements.Square.described:
/-- The square ADEB that I.46 describes on AB, with D and E on the side of AB
where P is, is a parallelogram [I. 28], and it is the square on AB: "AE is the
square on AB" (II.2). [I. 4, I. 28, I. 34] -/
theorem Square.described (h : Square A D E B) (hD : SameSideOf D P A B)
    (hE : SameSideOf E P A B) : Parallelogram A D E B ∧ quadArea A D E B = sq A B
bridges.Elements.Square.eq_sq:
/-- A square is the square on its side: the square ABCD, a parallelogram, is the
square on AB. [I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Square.eq_sq (h : Square A B C D) (hp : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea A B C D = sq A B
bridges.Elements.rect_self_left:
/-- A rectangle with a side that is nothing is nothing: the rectangle contained by AA,
CD has no area. -/
theorem rect_self_left (A C D : Point) : rect A A C D = 0
bridges.Elements.rect_self_right:
/-- The rectangle contained by AB, CC has no area. -/
theorem rect_self_right (A B C : Point) : rect A B C C = 0
bridges.Elements.sq_self:
/-- The square on AA has no area. -/
theorem sq_self (A : Point) : sq A A = 0

  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Contain:
/-- The lengths `a` and `b` contain the area `x`: some rectangle `PQRS` has `PQ` equal
to `a`, `PS` equal to `b`, and is equal to `x`; or one of `a`, `b` is nothing, and so
is `x`. -/

  ((a = 0 ∨ b = 0) ∧ x = 0) ∨

definitions.InOrder:
/-- **Points in order.** `InOrder ps`: each point of the list `ps` differs from the next,
and of any three in a row the middle one lies between the other two. So the points lie on
one straight line, in the order listed: `InOrder [B, D, E, C]` is II.1's straight line BC
cut at the points D and E. A list of one point, or of none, is in order. -/
def InOrder : List Point → Prop
  | [] => True
  | [_] => True
  | [p, q] => p ≠ q
  | p :: q :: r :: rest => p ≠ q ∧ Between p q r ∧ InOrder (q :: r :: rest)
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.Magnitude.sum:
/-- **The sum of a list of magnitudes** of one kind: nothing for the empty list, and
otherwise the first added to the sum of the rest. So `Magnitude.sum [a, b, c]` is
`a + (b + (c + 0))`, which is `a + b + c`. -/
noncomputable def Magnitude.sum {k : Kind} : List (Magnitude k) → Magnitude k
  | [] => 0
  | a :: as => a + Magnitude.sum as
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.Rectangle:
/-- **Definition II.1.** A rectangular parallelogram: the parallelogram `ABCD`, its
corners taken in order, with all four of its angles right. Euclid says "rectangular",
as Definition 22 says "right-angled" of the square. -/
def Rectangle (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  Parallelogram A B C D ∧ ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Square:
/-- **Definition 22.** "Of quadrilateral figures, a square is that which is both
equilateral and right-angled." The corners are `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, in order. -/
def Square (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  ‖A B‖ = ‖B C‖ ∧ ‖B C‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖C D‖ = ‖D A‖ ∧
    ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.endOf:
/-- **The end** of the straight line that starts at `B` and runs through the points `ps`:
the last of them, or `B` itself if there are none. `endOf B [D, E, C]` is C. -/
def endOf (B : Point) : List Point → Point
  | [] => B
  | p :: ps => endOf p ps
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rect:
/-- **The rectangle contained by `AB`, `CD`** (Definition II.1): the area of any
rectangle whose sides about a right angle are equal to `AB` and `CD`. Lean chooses one
such area (`Classical.epsilon`); `Rectangle.contained` shows that every such
rectangle is equal to it. -/
noncomputable def rect (A B C D : Point) : Area :=
  Classical.epsilon (Contain ‖A B‖ ‖C D‖)
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle
definitions.segments:
/-- **The segments** of a straight line cut at points in order: each point of the list with
the next, as the ends of one segment. The segments of `[B, D, E, C]` are BD, DE and EC. The
points need not be in order, or on one straight line: in the companions of I.45 and II.14
for a checked fan (`Prop45.fan`, `Prop14.fan`), the segments of a figure's corners A₁, A₂,
…, Aₙ are its sides A₁A₂, …, Aₙ₋₁Aₙ, those away from the corner A₀, and each side with A₀
makes one of the triangles into which the straight lines from A₀ divide the figure, when the
fan's conditions hold. -/
def segments : List Point → List (Point × Point)
  | p :: q :: rest => (p, q) :: segments (q :: rest)
  | _ => []
definitions.sq:
/-- **The square on `AB`**: the rectangle contained by `AB`, `AB`, the area of any
square described on a straight line equal to `AB` (`Square.eq_sq`). -/
noncomputable def sq (A B : Point) : Area := rect A B A B

state.commentary:
Book II multiplies with rectangles, and II.1 cuts one into strips. Euclid names a rectangle as he names an angle, by the two straight lines that contain it, and the Greek can shorten both names the same way: "In both cases the substantive and participle can be omitted because the feminine or neuter of the article enables us to distinguish whether an angle or a rectangle is meant" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 370). From here on, where Euclid leaves out "contained", Heath writes simply "the rectangle A, BC". Augustus De Morgan advised "the rectangle *under* two lines" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 376). Heath declines it, since it might suggest that the Greek word means "under", which it does not.

The enunciation cuts BC into "any number of segments whatever"; the setting-out cuts it at two points, D and E. Our main theorem keeps Euclid's two points, and names the ends of his straight line A as A₁ and A₂; its companion `Prop1.general` cuts BC at any number of points taken in order. A sum times a sum needs only a fuller figure, Heath adds, in which "a series of parallels to BC would have to be drawn as well as the series of parallels to BF" (vol. 1, p. 376). Euclid never uses II.1 again, as Heath remarks under II.2. Heron did: he proved the propositions after it as its consequences, and, according to an-Nairīzī, explained "that it is not possible to prove II. 1 without drawing a number of lines (i.e. without actually drawing the rectangles), but that the following propositions up to II. 10 inclusive can be proved by merely drawing one line" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 373).

"Now BH is the rectangle A, BC, for it is contained by GB, BC, and BG is equal to A." Here Euclid takes for granted that a rectangle drawn is the rectangle contained by its sides, or by straight lines equal to them. Our `rect` is the rectangle contained, an area defined from the two lengths, and `Rectangle.eq_rect` proves the step from I.4 and I.34. II.2 to II.8, II.11 and II.14 use it again, and [Book II's introduction](index.md#areas) tells how.
state.heath_proof:
Let A, BC be two straight lines, and let BC be cut at random at the points D, E;

I say that the rectangle contained by A, BC is equal to the rectangle contained by A, BD, that contained by A, DE and that contained by A, EC.

For let BF be drawn from B at right angles to BC; [I. 11]

let BG be made equal to A, [I. 3]

through G let GH be drawn parallel to BC, [I. 31]

and through D, E, C let DK, EL, CH be drawn parallel to BG.

Then BH is equal to BK, DL, EH.

Now BH is the rectangle A, BC, for it is contained by GB, BC, and BG is equal to A;

BK is the rectangle A, BD, for it is contained by GB, BD, and BG is equal to A;

and DL is the rectangle A, DE, for DK, that is BG [I. 34], is equal to A.

Similarly also EH is the rectangle A, EC.

Therefore the rectangle A, BC is equal to the rectangle A, BD, the rectangle A, DE and the rectangle A, EC.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- If there be two straight lines, and one of them be cut into any number of segments whatever, the
rectangle contained by the two straight lines is equal to the rectangles contained by the uncut
straight line and each of the segments. -/
theorem Prop1 {A₁ A₂ B C D E : Point} (hA : A₁ ≠ A₂) (hBDE : Between B D E) (hDEC : Between D E C) :
    rect A₁ A₂ B C = rect A₁ A₂ B D + rect A₁ A₂ D E + rect A₁ A₂ E C := by
  -- Let A, BC be two straight lines, and let BC be cut at random at the points D, E;
  have hBDC : Between B D C := between_of_between_right hBDE hDEC
  have hBEC : Between B E C :=
    between_symm (between_of_between_right (between_symm hDEC) (between_symm hBDE))
  have hBC : B ≠ C := ne_of_between_ends hBDC
  obtain ⟨BC, hB_BC, hC_BC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hBC
  have hD_BC : OnLine D BC := on_line_of_between_ends hBDC hB_BC hC_BC
  have hE_BC : OnLine E BC := on_line_of_between_ends hBEC hB_BC hC_BC
  -- I say that the rectangle contained by A, BC is equal to the rectangle contained by A, BD,
  -- that contained by A, DE and that contained by A, EC.
  -- For let BF be drawn from B at right angles to BC; [I. 11]
  obtain ⟨Q, hQ, -⟩ := exists_off_line hBC []
  obtain ⟨F, hFQ, hright⟩ := BookI.Prop11 hBC ⟨BC, hB_BC, hC_BC, hB_BC⟩ hQ
  have hCBF : ∠ C B F = ∟ := hright C ⟨BC, hB_BC, hC_BC, hC_BC⟩ hBC.symm
  -- let BG be made equal to A, [I. 3]
  /- I.3 needs a greater straight line. Place A at B by I.2 and produce BF
     far enough along its ray before cutting off BG. -/
  obtain ⟨P, hP⟩ := BookI.Prop2 B A₁ A₂ hA
  have hBP : B ≠ P := ne_of_len_eq hP hA
  have hBF : B ≠ F := hFQ.triangle.ne₁₃
  obtain ⟨Y, hFBY⟩ := produce hBF.symm
  obtain ⟨X, hYBX, hlt⟩ := produce_longer (ne_of_between (between_symm hFBY)) hBP
  have hX : OnRay X B F := OnRay.of_between_between (between_symm hFBY) hYBX
  obtain ⟨G, hBGX, hBG⟩ := BookI.Prop3 hA (hP ▸ hlt)
  have hCBG : ∠ C B G = ∟ := by
    rw [angle_onRay_right (OnRay.of_between hBGX) hBC.symm, angle_onRay_right hX hBC.symm]
    exact hCBF
  have hGQ : SameSideOf G Q B C :=
    SameSideOf.of_onRay (OnRay.of_between hBGX) (SameSideOf.of_onRay hX hFQ)
  have hG_BC : ¬ OnLine G BC := not_on_line_of_same_side (hGQ.sameSide hB_BC hC_BC)
  -- through G let GH be drawn parallel to BC, [I. 31]
  obtain ⟨GH, hG_GH, hGH_BC⟩ := BookI.Prop31.line hG_BC
  -- and through D, E, C let DK, EL, CH be drawn parallel to BG.
  obtain ⟨K, hK_GH, hGBDK⟩ :=
    BookI.Prop31.parallelogram hGH_BC hG_GH hB_BC hD_BC (ne_of_between hBDC)
  obtain ⟨L, hL_GH, hGBEL⟩ :=
    BookI.Prop31.parallelogram hGH_BC hG_GH hB_BC hE_BC (ne_of_between hBEC)
  obtain ⟨H, hH_GH, hGBCH⟩ := BookI.Prop31.parallelogram hGH_BC hG_GH hB_BC hC_BC hBC
  obtain ⟨BG, hB_BG, hG_BG⟩ := Postulate1 B G (ne_of_between hBGX)
  obtain ⟨DK, hD_DK, hK_DK⟩ := Postulate1 D K hGBDK.1.2.1
  obtain ⟨EL, hE_EL, hL_EL⟩ := Postulate1 E L hGBEL.1.2.1
  obtain ⟨CH, hC_CH, hH_CH⟩ := Postulate1 C H hGBCH.1.2.1
  have hDK_BG : Parallel DK BG := (hGBDK.1.parallel hG_BG hB_BG hD_DK hK_DK).symm
  have hEL_BG : Parallel EL BG := (hGBEL.1.parallel hG_BG hB_BG hE_EL hL_EL).symm
  have hCH_BG : Parallel CH BG := (hGBCH.1.parallel hG_BG hB_BG hC_CH hH_CH).symm
  -- Then BH is equal to BK, DL, EH.
  have hDE : D ≠ E := ne_of_between hDEC
  have hDC : D ≠ C := (ne_of_between (between_symm hBDC)).symm
  have hEC : E ≠ C := (ne_of_between (between_symm hBEC)).symm
  /- Each upright meets BC at its own point alone, so these are distinct
     straight lines (`Parallel.off_transversal`). I.30 makes them parallel. -/
  have hE_DK : ¬ OnLine E DK :=
    hGH_BC.symm.off_transversal hD_BC hK_GH hD_DK hK_DK hE_BC hDE.symm
  have hC_DK : ¬ OnLine C DK :=
    hGH_BC.symm.off_transversal hD_BC hK_GH hD_DK hK_DK hC_BC hDC.symm
  have hC_EL : ¬ OnLine C EL :=
    hGH_BC.symm.off_transversal hE_BC hL_GH hE_EL hL_EL hC_BC hEC.symm
  have hDK_EL : Parallel DK EL :=
    BookI.Prop30.parallel hDK_BG hEL_BG (fun e => hE_DK (e.symm ▸ hE_EL))
  have hDK_CH : Parallel DK CH :=
    BookI.Prop30.parallel hDK_BG hCH_BG (fun e => hC_DK (e.symm ▸ hC_CH))
  have hEL_CH : Parallel EL CH :=
    BookI.Prop30.parallel hEL_BG hCH_BG (fun e => hC_EL (e.symm ▸ hC_CH))
  /- The parallels keep the order of B, D, E, C on GH. -/
  have hGKL : Between G K L := Parallel.between hDK_BG.symm hDK_EL.symm hB_BG hD_DK hE_EL
    hBDE hG_BG hK_DK hL_EL ⟨GH, hG_GH, hK_GH, hL_GH⟩
  have hKLH : Between K L H := Parallel.between hDK_EL hEL_CH.symm hD_DK hE_EL hC_CH
    hDEC hK_DK hL_EL hH_CH ⟨GH, hK_GH, hL_GH, hH_GH⟩
  have hGKH : Between G K H := between_of_between_right hGKL hKLH
  have hBGKD : Parallelogram B G K D := hGBDK.reverse.rotate.rotate.rotate
  have hBGLE : Parallelogram B G L E := hGBEL.reverse.rotate.rotate.rotate
  have hBGHC : Parallelogram B G H C := hGBCH.reverse.rotate.rotate.rotate
  have hDKHC : Parallelogram D K H C :=
    ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel hGBDK.1.2.1 hGBCH.1.2.1.symm hD_DK hK_DK hH_CH hC_CH hDK_CH,
      AreParallel.of_parallel (ne_of_between_ends hKLH) hDC.symm hK_GH hH_GH hC_BC hD_BC hGH_BC⟩
  have hDKLE : Parallelogram D K L E :=
    ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel hGBDK.1.2.1 hGBEL.1.2.1.symm hD_DK hK_DK hL_EL hE_EL hDK_EL,
      AreParallel.of_parallel (ne_of_between hKLH) hDE.symm hK_GH hL_GH hE_BC hD_BC hGH_BC⟩
  have hELHC : Parallelogram E L H C :=
    ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel hGBEL.1.2.1 hGBCH.1.2.1.symm hE_EL hL_EL hH_CH hC_CH hEL_CH,
      AreParallel.of_parallel (ne_of_between (between_symm hKLH)).symm hEC.symm hL_GH hH_GH
        hC_BC hE_BC hGH_BC⟩
  have h₁ : quadArea B G H C = quadArea B G K D + quadArea D K H C :=
    quadArea_add_of_parallelograms hBGKD hDKHC hBDC hGKH
  have h₂ : quadArea D K H C = quadArea D K L E + quadArea E L H C :=
    quadArea_add_of_parallelograms hDKLE hELHC hDEC hKLH
  -- Now BH is the rectangle A, BC, for it is contained by GB, BC, and BG is equal to A;
  have hBH : quadArea B G H C = rect A₁ A₂ B C :=
    (Rectangle.of_right hBGHC hCBG).eq_rect hBG rfl
  -- BK is the rectangle A, BD, for it is contained by GB, BD, and BG is equal to A;
  have hBK_rect : Rectangle B G K D := by
    refine Rectangle.of_right hBGKD ?_
    rw [angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between hBDC) (ne_of_between hBGX).symm]
    exact hCBG
  have hBK : quadArea B G K D = rect A₁ A₂ B D := hBK_rect.eq_rect hBG rfl
  -- and DL is the rectangle A, DE, for DK, that is BG [I. 34], is equal to A.
  have hDK : ‖D K‖ = ‖A₁ A₂‖ := by
    rw [len_symm D K, ← (BookI.Prop34 hGBDK).2.1, len_symm G B]; exact hBG
  have hK_BC : ¬ OnLine K BC := hGH_BC.not_onLine hK_GH
  have hEDK : ∠ E D K = ∟ := by
    have h := hBK_rect.2.2.2.2
    rw [angle_symm hGBDK.1.2.1.symm (ne_of_between hBDE)] at h
    rw [angle_symm hDE.symm hGBDK.1.2.1.symm, ← adjacent_eq_of_right hB_BC hE_BC hBDE hK_BC h]
    exact h
  have hDL : quadArea D K L E = rect A₁ A₂ D E :=
    (Rectangle.of_right hDKLE hEDK).eq_rect hDK rfl
  -- Similarly also EH is the rectangle A, EC.
  have hEL : ‖E L‖ = ‖A₁ A₂‖ := by
    rw [len_symm E L, ← (BookI.Prop34 hGBEL).2.1, len_symm G B]; exact hBG
  have hL_BC : ¬ OnLine L BC := hGH_BC.not_onLine hL_GH
  have hBGLE_rect : Rectangle B G L E := by
    refine Rectangle.of_right hBGLE ?_
    rw [angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between hBEC) (ne_of_between hBGX).symm]
    exact hCBG
  have hCEL : ∠ C E L = ∟ := by
    have h := hBGLE_rect.2.2.2.2
    rw [angle_symm hGBEL.1.2.1.symm (ne_of_between hBEC)] at h
    rw [angle_symm hEC.symm hGBEL.1.2.1.symm, ← adjacent_eq_of_right hB_BC hC_BC hBEC hL_BC h]
    exact h
  have hEH : quadArea E L H C = rect A₁ A₂ E C :=
    (Rectangle.of_right hELHC hCEL).eq_rect hEL rfl
  -- Therefore the rectangle A, BC is equal to the rectangle A, BD, the rectangle A, DE and the
  -- rectangle A, EC.
  have hequal : rect A₁ A₂ B C = rect A₁ A₂ B D + rect A₁ A₂ D E + rect A₁ A₂ E C := by
    rw [← hBH, h₁, h₂, hBK, hDL, hEH]
    ac_rfl
  -- Therefore etc.
  exact hequal
  -- Q. E. D.

statement.note: With its companions: `Prop1.general` cuts the straight line at any number of points in order, `Prop1.two` at one; `Prop1` keeps Euclid's two, D and E.

route.note: Euclid draws every parallel in one figure. The companions draw one at a time: `Prop1.two` is his construction for one point of section, and `Prop1.general` repeats it, cutting off one segment after another (`InOrder.between_end`).

named_declarations.Elements.BookII.Prop1.general:
/-- **II.1, any number of segments** (companion of II.1). If the straight line from B to its
end is cut at any number of points in order, the rectangle contained by A₁A₂ and the whole
is equal to the rectangles contained by A₁A₂ and each of the segments. The list `ps` is
the points of section followed by the end; with no points of section it is the whole
straight line alone, and with no points at all the straight line is nothing and so is each
side. -/
theorem Prop1.general {A₁ A₂ B : Point} {ps : List Point} (h : InOrder (B :: ps)) :
    rect A₁ A₂ B (endOf B ps) =
      Magnitude.sum ((segments (B :: ps)).map fun s => rect A₁ A₂ s.1 s.2)
named_declarations.Elements.Rectangle.eq_rect:
/-- Euclid's way of naming a rectangle: "BH is the rectangle A, BC, for it is contained
by GB, BC, and BG is equal to A" (II.1). If the sides PQ, PS of the rectangle
PQRS are equal to AB, CD, it is the rectangle contained by AB, CD.
[I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Rectangle.eq_rect (h : Rectangle P Q R S) (h₁ : ‖P Q‖ = ‖A B‖) (h₂ : ‖P S‖ = ‖C D‖) :
    quadArea P Q R S = rect A B C D
named_declarations.Elements.rect:
/-- **The rectangle contained by `AB`, `CD`** (Definition II.1): the area of any
rectangle whose sides about a right angle are equal to `AB` and `CD`. Lean chooses one
such area (`Classical.epsilon`); `Rectangle.contained` shows that every such
rectangle is equal to it. -/
noncomputable def rect (A B C D : Point) : Area

Elements.Rectangle.eq_rect: variable {A B C D E F G H K P Q R S P' Q' R' S' : Point}

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Contain:
/-- The lengths `a` and `b` contain the area `x`: some rectangle `PQRS` has `PQ` equal
to `a`, `PS` equal to `b`, and is equal to `x`; or one of `a`, `b` is nothing, and so
is `x`. -/
def Contain (a b : Length) (x : Area) : Prop :=
  ((a = 0 ∨ b = 0) ∧ x = 0) ∨
    ∃ P Q R S : Point, Rectangle P Q R S ∧ ‖P Q‖ = a ∧ ‖P S‖ = b ∧ quadArea P Q R S = x
definitions.InOrder:
/-- **Points in order.** `InOrder ps`: each point of the list `ps` differs from the next,
and of any three in a row the middle one lies between the other two. So the points lie on
one straight line, in the order listed: `InOrder [B, D, E, C]` is II.1's straight line BC
cut at the points D and E. A list of one point, or of none, is in order. -/
def InOrder : List Point → Prop
  | [] => True
  | [_] => True
  | [p, q] => p ≠ q
  | p :: q :: r :: rest => p ≠ q ∧ Between p q r ∧ InOrder (q :: r :: rest)
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.Magnitude.sum:
/-- **The sum of a list of magnitudes** of one kind: nothing for the empty list, and
otherwise the first added to the sum of the rest. So `Magnitude.sum [a, b, c]` is
`a + (b + (c + 0))`, which is `a + b + c`. -/
noncomputable def Magnitude.sum {k : Kind} : List (Magnitude k) → Magnitude k
  | [] => 0
  | a :: as => a + Magnitude.sum as
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.Rectangle:
/-- **Definition II.1.** A rectangular parallelogram: the parallelogram `ABCD`, its
corners taken in order, with all four of its angles right. Euclid says "rectangular",
as Definition 22 says "right-angled" of the square. -/
def Rectangle (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  Parallelogram A B C D ∧ ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.endOf:
/-- **The end** of the straight line that starts at `B` and runs through the points `ps`:
the last of them, or `B` itself if there are none. `endOf B [D, E, C]` is C. -/
def endOf (B : Point) : List Point → Point
  | [] => B
  | p :: ps => endOf p ps
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rect:
/-- **The rectangle contained by `AB`, `CD`** (Definition II.1): the area of any
rectangle whose sides about a right angle are equal to `AB` and `CD`. Lean chooses one
such area (`Classical.epsilon`); `Rectangle.contained` shows that every such
rectangle is equal to it. -/
noncomputable def rect (A B C D : Point) : Area :=
  Classical.epsilon (Contain ‖A B‖ ‖C D‖)
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle
definitions.segments:
/-- **The segments** of a straight line cut at points in order: each point of the list with
the next, as the ends of one segment. The segments of `[B, D, E, C]` are BD, DE and EC. The
points need not be in order, or on one straight line: in the companions of I.45 and II.14
for a checked fan (`Prop45.fan`, `Prop14.fan`), the segments of a figure's corners A₁, A₂,
…, Aₙ are its sides A₁A₂, …, Aₙ₋₁Aₙ, those away from the corner A₀, and each side with A₀
makes one of the triangles into which the straight lines from A₀ divide the figure, when the
fan's conditions hold. -/
def segments : List Point → List (Point × Point)
  | p :: q :: rest => (p, q) :: segments (q :: rest)
  | _ => []

bridges.Elements.Rectangle.congr:
/-- Rectangles contained by equal straight lines are equal: if the rectangles PQRS,
P'Q'R'S' have PQ equal to P'Q' and PS to P'S', they are equal. The diameter
QS cuts off the triangle SPQ, right-angled at P, which is half the rectangle
[I. 34]; and the two halves are equal [I. 4]. Euclid takes this for granted whenever
he names a rectangle by its sides. [I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Rectangle.congr (h : Rectangle P Q R S) (h' : Rectangle P' Q' R' S')
    (h₁ : ‖P Q‖ = ‖P' Q'‖) (h₂ : ‖P S‖ = ‖P' S'‖) :
    quadArea P Q R S = quadArea P' Q' R' S'
bridges.Elements.Rectangle.contained:
/-- **A rectangle is contained by its sides** (Definition II.1): the rectangle PQRS is
the rectangle contained by PQ, PS, the two straight lines containing its right
angle at P. `rect` chose some rectangle contained by straight lines equal to these,
and by `Rectangle.congr` the two are equal. [I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Rectangle.contained (h : Rectangle P Q R S) : quadArea P Q R S = rect P Q P S
bridges.Elements.Rectangle.eq_rect:
/-- Euclid's way of naming a rectangle: "BH is the rectangle A, BC, for it is contained
by GB, BC, and BG is equal to A" (II.1). If the sides PQ, PS of the rectangle
PQRS are equal to AB, CD, it is the rectangle contained by AB, CD.
[I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Rectangle.eq_rect (h : Rectangle P Q R S) (h₁ : ‖P Q‖ = ‖A B‖) (h₂ : ‖P S‖ = ‖C D‖) :
    quadArea P Q R S = rect A B C D
bridges.Elements.Square.described:
/-- The square ADEB that I.46 describes on AB, with D and E on the side of AB
where P is, is a parallelogram [I. 28], and it is the square on AB: "AE is the
square on AB" (II.2). [I. 4, I. 28, I. 34] -/
theorem Square.described (h : Square A D E B) (hD : SameSideOf D P A B)
    (hE : SameSideOf E P A B) : Parallelogram A D E B ∧ quadArea A D E B = sq A B
bridges.Elements.Square.eq_sq:
/-- A square is the square on its side: the square ABCD, a parallelogram, is the
square on AB. [I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Square.eq_sq (h : Square A B C D) (hp : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea A B C D = sq A B
