def Contain (a b : Length) (x : Area) : Prop :=
  ((a = 0 ∨ b = 0) ∧ x = 0) ∨
    ∃ P Q R S : Point, Rectangle P Q R S ∧ ‖P Q‖ = a ∧ ‖P S‖ = b ∧ quadArea P Q R S = x
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.Rectangle:
/-- **Definition II.1.** A rectangular parallelogram: the parallelogram `ABCD`, its
corners taken in order, with all four of its angles right. Euclid says "rectangular",
as Definition 22 says "right-angled" of the square. -/
def Rectangle (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  Parallelogram A B C D ∧ ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Square:
/-- **Definition 22.** "Of quadrilateral figures, a square is that which is both
equilateral and right-angled." The corners are `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, in order. -/
def Square (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  ‖A B‖ = ‖B C‖ ∧ ‖B C‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖C D‖ = ‖D A‖ ∧
    ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rect:
/-- **The rectangle contained by `AB`, `CD`** (Definition II.1): the area of any
rectangle whose sides about a right angle are equal to `AB` and `CD`. Lean chooses one
such area (`Classical.epsilon`); `Rectangle.contained` shows that every such
rectangle is equal to it. -/
noncomputable def rect (A B C D : Point) : Area :=
  Classical.epsilon (Contain ‖A B‖ ‖C D‖)
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle
definitions.sq:
/-- **The square on `AB`**: the rectangle contained by `AB`, `AB`, the area of any
square described on a straight line equal to `AB` (`Square.eq_sq`). -/
noncomputable def sq (A B : Point) : Area := rect A B A B

state.enunciation: If a straight line be cut into equal and unequal segments, the rectangle contained by the unequal segments of the whole together with the square on the straight line between the points of section is equal to the square on the half.
state.heath_proof:
For let a straight line AB be cut into equal segments at C and into unequal segments at D;

I say that the rectangle contained by AD, DB together with the square on CD is equal to the square on CB.

For let the square CEFB be described on CB, [I. 46]

and let BE be joined;

through D let DG be drawn parallel to either CE or BF,

through H again let KM be drawn parallel to either AB or EF,

and again through A let AK be drawn parallel to either CL or BM. [I. 31]

Then, since the complement CH is equal to the complement HF, [I. 43]

let DM be added to each;

therefore the whole CM is equal to the whole DF.

But CM is equal to AL,

since AC is also equal to CB; [I. 36]

therefore AL is also equal to DF.

Let CH be added to each;

therefore the whole AH is equal to the gnomon NOP.

But AH is the rectangle AD, DB, for DH is equal to DB,

therefore the gnomon NOP is also equal to the rectangle AD, DB.

Let LG, which is equal to the square on CD, be added to each;

therefore the gnomon NOP and LG are equal to the rectangle contained by AD, DB and the square on CD.

But the gnomon NOP and LG are the whole square CEFB, which is described on CB;

therefore the rectangle contained by AD, DB together with the square on CD is equal to the square on CB.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- If a straight line be cut into equal and unequal segments, the rectangle contained by the
unequal segments of the whole together with the square on the straight line between the points
of section is equal to the square on the half. -/
theorem Prop5 {A B C D : Point} (hACB : Between A C B) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖C B‖) (hADB : Between A D B)
    (hDC : D ≠ C) :
    rect A D D B + sq C D = sq C B := by
  -- For let a straight line AB be cut into equal segments at C and into unequal segments at D;
  -- I say that the rectangle contained by AD, DB together with the square on CD is equal to
  -- the square on CB.
  /- Euclid's figure puts D between C and B; the other side is the same with A
     and B exchanged. -/
  have euclid : ∀ {A B C D : Point}, Between A C B → ‖A C‖ = ‖C B‖ → Between C D B →
      rect A D D B + sq C D = sq C B := by
    intro A B C D hACB hAC hCDB
    have hCB : C ≠ B := ne_of_between_ends hCDB
    -- For let the square CEFB be described on CB, [I. 46]
    obtain ⟨X, hX, -⟩ := exists_off_line hCB []
    obtain ⟨E, F, hsq, hE, hF⟩ := BookI.Prop46 hCB hX
    obtain ⟨hp, hCEFB⟩ := Square.described hsq hE hF
    -- and let BE be joined;
    -- through D let DG be drawn parallel to either CE or BF,
    -- through H again let KM be drawn parallel to either AB or EF,
    obtain ⟨G, H, L, M, hBHE, hEGF, hCLE, hFMB, hDHG, hLHM, hBDHM, hHLEG⟩ := hp.figure hCDB
    -- and again through A let AK be drawn parallel to either CL or BM. [I. 31]
    obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B (ne_of_between_ends hACB)
    have hC_AB : OnLine C AB := on_line_of_between_ends hACB hA_AB hB_AB
    have hD_AB : OnLine D AB := on_line_of_between_ends hCDB hC_AB hB_AB
    obtain ⟨KM, hL_KM, hM_KM⟩ := Postulate1 L M (ne_of_between_ends hLHM)
    have hH_KM : OnLine H KM := on_line_of_between_ends hLHM hL_KM hM_KM
    have hKM_AB : Parallel KM AB := (hBDHM.1.parallel hB_AB hD_AB hH_KM hM_KM).symm
    obtain ⟨K, hK_KM, hLCAK⟩ :=
      BookI.Prop31.parallelogram hKM_AB hL_KM hC_AB hA_AB (ne_of_between hACB).symm
    -- Then, since the complement CH is equal to the complement HF, [I. 43]
    have hBCEF : Parallelogram B C E F := hp.rotate.rotate.rotate
    have hBDC : Between B D C := between_symm hCDB
    have h43 : quadArea D C L H = quadArea M H G F :=
      BookI.Prop43 hBCEF hBHE hBDC hCLE hEGF hFMB hBDHM hHLEG
    obtain ⟨hDCLH, hMHGF⟩ := hBCEF.complements hBHE hBDC hCLE hEGF hFMB hBDHM hHLEG
    -- let DM be added to each;
    have hadd := CommonNotion2 h43 (rfl : quadArea B D H M = quadArea B D H M)
    -- therefore the whole CM is equal to the whole DF.
    have hCM : quadArea L C B M = quadArea L C D H + quadArea H D B M :=
      quadArea_add_of_parallelograms hDCLH.rotate.rotate.reverse hBDHM.rotate.rotate.reverse hLHM
        hCDB
    have hDF : quadArea D B F G = quadArea D B M H + quadArea H M F G :=
      quadArea_add_of_parallelograms hBDHM.rotate.reverse hMHGF.rotate.reverse hDHG
        (between_symm hFMB)
    have hCM_DF : quadArea L C B M = quadArea D B F G := by
      rw [hCM, hDF, quadArea_reverse L H D C, hDCLH.rotate.quadArea_rotate, hDCLH.quadArea_rotate,
        quadArea_reverse H M B D, hBDHM.rotate.quadArea_rotate, hBDHM.quadArea_rotate,
        quadArea_reverse D H M B, hBDHM.quadArea_rotate, quadArea_reverse H G F M,
        hMHGF.quadArea_rotate]
      exact hadd.trans (add_comm _ _)
    -- But CM is equal to AL,
    -- since AC is also equal to CB; [I. 36]
    obtain ⟨CE, hC_CE, hE_CE⟩ := Postulate1 C E hp.1.1
    obtain ⟨BF, hB_BF, hF_BF⟩ := Postulate1 B F hp.1.2.1.symm
    have hL_CE : OnLine L CE := on_line_of_between_ends hCLE hC_CE hE_CE
    have hM_BF : OnLine M BF := on_line_of_between_ends hFMB hF_BF hB_BF
    have hCE_BF : Parallel CE BF := hp.1.parallel hC_CE hE_CE hF_BF hB_BF
    have hLCBM : Parallelogram L C B M :=
      ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel (ne_of_between hCLE).symm (ne_of_between (between_symm hFMB))
          hL_CE hC_CE hB_BF hM_BF hCE_BF,
        AreParallel.of_parallel hCB (ne_of_between_ends hLHM).symm hC_AB hB_AB hM_KM hL_KM
          hKM_AB.symm⟩
    have h36 : quadArea L C B M = quadArea K A C L :=
      BookI.Prop36 hLCBM hLCAK.rotate.rotate.rotate.reverse hAC.symm
        ⟨KM, hL_KM, hM_KM, hK_KM, hL_KM⟩ ⟨AB, hC_AB, hB_AB, hA_AB, hC_AB⟩
    -- therefore AL is also equal to DF.
    have hAL_DF : quadArea K A C L = quadArea D B F G := CommonNotion1 h36.symm hCM_DF.symm
    -- Let CH be added to each;
    have hadd₂ := CommonNotion2 hAL_DF (rfl : quadArea D C L H = quadArea D C L H)
    -- therefore the whole AH is equal to the gnomon NOP.
    /- AH is AL and CH together: C lies between A and D, and L between K and H,
       the parallels AK, CL, DH keeping order. -/
    have hACD : Between A C D := between_cut hACB hCDB
    obtain ⟨AK, hA_AK, hK_AK⟩ := Postulate1 A K hLCAK.1.2.1
    obtain ⟨DG, hD_DG, hG_DG⟩ := Postulate1 D G (ne_of_between_ends hDHG)
    have hH_DG : OnLine H DG := on_line_of_between_ends hDHG hD_DG hG_DG
    have hAK_CE : Parallel AK CE := (hLCAK.1.parallel hL_CE hC_CE hA_AK hK_AK).symm
    have hDG_CE : Parallel DG CE := (hDCLH.2.parallel hC_CE hL_CE hH_DG hD_DG).symm
    have hKLH : Between K L H := Parallel.between hAK_CE hDG_CE hA_AK hC_CE hD_DG hACD hK_AK
      hL_CE hH_DG ⟨KM, hK_KM, hL_KM, hH_KM⟩
    have hAH : quadArea A K H D = quadArea A K L C + quadArea C L H D :=
      quadArea_add_of_parallelograms hLCAK.rotate.rotate hDCLH.rotate hACD hKLH
    have hgnomon : quadArea A K H D = quadArea D C L H + quadArea B D H M + quadArea M H G F := by
      calc
        quadArea A K H D = quadArea K A C L + quadArea D C L H := by
          rw [hAH, ← hLCAK.rotate.rotate.quadArea_rotate, quadArea_reverse K A C L,
            hDCLH.quadArea_rotate]
        _ = quadArea D B F G + quadArea D C L H := hadd₂
        _ = quadArea D C L H + quadArea B D H M + quadArea M H G F := by
          rw [hDF, quadArea_reverse D H M B, hBDHM.quadArea_rotate,
            quadArea_reverse H G F M, hMHGF.quadArea_rotate]
          ac_rfl
    -- But AH is the rectangle AD, DB, for DH is equal to DB,
    have hDM : Square B D H M :=
      hsq.rotate.rotate.rotate.about_diameter hBCEF hBHE hBDC (between_symm hFMB) hBDHM
    have hDH_DB : ‖D H‖ = ‖D B‖ := hDM.1.symm.trans (len_symm B D)
    have hAD : A ≠ D := ne_of_between_ends hACD
    have hAK_DG : Parallel AK DG := BookI.Prop30.parallel hAK_CE hDG_CE fun e => by
      have hAB_DG : AB = DG := line_unique hAD hA_AB hD_AB (e ▸ hA_AK) hD_DG
      exact hKM_AB.not_onLine hH_KM (hAB_DG ▸ hH_DG)
    have hDAKH : Parallelogram D A K H :=
      ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel hAD.symm (ne_of_between_ends hKLH) hD_AB hA_AB hK_KM hH_KM
          hKM_AB.symm,
        AreParallel.of_parallel hLCAK.1.2.1 (ne_of_between hDHG).symm hA_AK hK_AK hH_DG hD_DG
          hAK_DG⟩
    have hH_AB : ¬ OnLine H AB := fun h => hKM_AB.not_onLine hH_KM h
    have hright : ∠ H D A = ∟ := by
      have h := hDM.2.2.2.2.1
      rw [adjacent_eq_of_right hB_AB hA_AB (between_of_between_left (between_symm hACB) hBDC)
        hH_AB h] at h
      exact h
    have hAHrect : quadArea D A K H = rect A D D B :=
      (Rectangle.of_right hDAKH hright).eq_rect (len_symm D A) hDH_DB
    -- therefore the gnomon NOP is also equal to the rectangle AD, DB.
    have hNOP : quadArea D C L H + quadArea B D H M + quadArea M H G F = rect A D D B :=
      (hgnomon.symm.trans hDAKH.quadArea_rotate).trans hAHrect
    -- Let LG, which is equal to the square on CD, be added to each;
    have hLG : Square E G H L :=
      hsq.rotate.about_diameter hp.rotate (between_symm hBHE) hEGF (between_symm hCLE)
        hHLEG.rotate.rotate
    obtain ⟨-, hDC_HL, -, -, -⟩ := BookI.Prop34 (A := D) (B := H) (C := C) (D := L) hDCLH
    have hLGsq : quadArea H L E G = sq C D := by
      rw [quadArea_rotate₂ E G H L, hLG.eq_sq hHLEG.rotate.rotate]
      exact sq_congr ((hLG.1.trans hLG.2.1).trans (hDC_HL.symm.trans (len_symm D C)))
    -- therefore the gnomon NOP and LG are equal to the rectangle contained by AD, DB and the
    -- square on CD.
    have hadd₃ := CommonNotion2 hNOP hLGsq
    -- But the gnomon NOP and LG are the whole square CEFB, which is described on CB;
    have hwhole := hBCEF.about_diameter hBHE hBDC hCLE hEGF hFMB hBDHM hHLEG
    -- therefore the rectangle contained by AD, DB together with the square on CD is equal to the
    -- square on CB.
    rw [← hadd₃, ← hCEFB, hBCEF.quadArea_rotate, hwhole]
    ac_rfl
  /- D falls between A and C, or between C and B, for it cannot be C itself, the
     segments being unequal. The second is Euclid's case; for the first we exchange
     A and B. -/
  have hCray : OnRay C A B := OnRay.of_between hACB
  have hDray : OnRay D A B := OnRay.of_between hADB
  rcases lt_trichotomy ‖A D‖ ‖A C‖ with h | h | h
  · have hADC : Between A D C := hDray.between_of_len_lt hCray h
    have := euclid (between_symm hACB) (by rw [len_symm B C, len_symm C A]; exact hAC.symm)
      (between_symm hADC)
    rw [rect_comm, rect_congr (len_symm D A) (len_symm B D),
      sq_congr ((len_symm C A).trans hAC)] at this
    exact this
  · obtain ⟨AB, hA, hB⟩ := Postulate1 A B (ne_of_between_ends hACB)
    have hDray' : OnRay D A C := ⟨ne_of_between hACB, (ne_of_between hADB).symm,
      ⟨AB, hA, on_line_of_between_ends hACB hA hB, on_line_of_between_ends hADB hA hB⟩,
      hDray.not_between hCray⟩
    exact absurd (hDray'.eq_of_len_eq h) hDC
  · exact euclid hACB hAC (between_inner (hCray.between_of_len_lt hDray h) hADB)
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.

helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.of_parallel:
/-- Two different points of L, and two different points of M, are the ends of
parallel straight lines when L and M are parallel: two points fix one straight
line (System E, Generalities 1). With `AreParallel.parallel`, this says "AB is
parallel to CD" of any other two points P, Q of the straight line AB and R,
S of CD. -/
theorem AreParallel.of_parallel (hPQ : P ≠ Q) (hRS : R ≠ S) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L)
    (hR : OnLine R M) (hS : OnLine S M) (h : Parallel L M) : AreParallel P Q R S
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.parallel:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then a straight line through A and B is parallel
to one through C and D. -/
theorem AreParallel.parallel (h : AreParallel A B C D) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (hC : OnLine C M) (hD : OnLine D M) : Parallel L M
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.symm:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then CD is parallel to AB. -/
theorem AreParallel.symm (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop28:
/-- If a straight line falling on two straight lines make the exterior angle equal to the interior
and opposite angle on the same side, or the interior angles on the same side equal to two right
angles, the straight lines will be parallel to one another. -/
theorem Prop28 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (hAGB : Between A G B) (hCHD : Between C H D)
    (hEGH : Between E G H) (hGHF : Between G H F) (hBD : SameSideOf B D E F)
    (h : ∠ E G B = ∠ G H D ∨ ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D = ∟ + ∟) :
    AreParallel A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29:
/-- A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one
another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on
the same side equal to two right angles. -/
theorem Prop29 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (hpar : AreParallel A B C D) (hAGB : Between A G B)
    (hCHD : Between C H D) (hEGH : Between E G H) (hGHF : Between G H F)
    (hBD : SameSideOf B D E F) :
    ∠ A G H = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ E G B = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D = ∟ + ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30:
/-- Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another. -/
theorem Prop30 {A B C D E F : Point} (h₁ : AreParallel A B E F) (h₂ : AreParallel C D E F)
    (hC : ¬ Collinear A B C) :
    AreParallel A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30.parallel:
/-- I.30 said of straight lines drawn and named: two different straight lines L and
M, each parallel to N, are parallel to one another. Euclid uses it without a
bracket in I.44 and I.47, where a straight line drawn "parallel to either" of two
parallels is parallel to both; in I.45 he brackets it. [I. 30] -/
theorem Prop30.parallel {L M N : Line} (hL : Parallel L N) (hM : Parallel M N) (hLM : L ≠ M) :
    Parallel L M
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31:
/-- Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line. -/
theorem Prop31 {A B C : Point} (hBC : B ≠ C) (hA : ¬ Collinear B C A) :
    ∃ E F : Point, Between E A F ∧ AreParallel E F B C
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31.parallelogram:
/-- Completing the parallelogram. If X lies on L, and Y and Z on M, which is
parallel to L, the straight line drawn through Z parallel to XY [I. 31] meets
L at a point W (`Prop30.meet`), and XYZW is a parallelogram. Euclid draws such
a parallel in I.37, I.38, I.42, I.44 and I.46, and reads the point where it meets
L, and the parallelogram, off his figure. [I. 30, I. 31] -/
theorem Prop31.parallelogram {X Y Z : Point} {L M : Line} (hLM : Parallel L M)
    (hX : OnLine X L) (hY : OnLine Y M) (hZ : OnLine Z M) (hYZ : Y ≠ Z) :
    ∃ W : Point, OnLine W L ∧ Parallelogram X Y Z W
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop34:
/-- In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the
diameter bisects the areas. -/
theorem Prop34 {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A C D B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ C D B ∧ ∠ A B D = ∠ A C D ∧
      △ A B C = △ D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop36:
/-- Parallelograms which are on equal bases and in the same parallels are equal to one another. -/
theorem Prop36 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (h₁ : Parallelogram A B C D) (h₂ : Parallelogram E F G H)
    (hbase : ‖B C‖ = ‖F G‖)
    (hAH : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine D L ∧ OnLine E L ∧ OnLine H L)
    (hBG : ∃ L : Line, OnLine B L ∧ OnLine C L ∧ OnLine F L ∧ OnLine G L) :
    quadArea A B C D = quadArea E F G H
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop4:
/-- If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles
contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the base, the
triangle will be equal to the triangle, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining
angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend. -/
theorem Prop4 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖D F‖) (hA : ∠ B A C = ∠ E D F) :
    ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ ∧ △ A B C = △ D E F ∧ ∠ A B C = ∠ D E F ∧ ∠ A C B = ∠ D F E
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop43:
/-- In any parallelogram the complements of the parallelograms about the diameter are equal to one
another. -/
theorem Prop43 {A B C D E F G H K : Point} (hABCD : Parallelogram A B C D) (hK : Between A K C)
    (hE : Between A E B) (hG : Between B G C) (hF : Between C F D) (hH : Between D H A)
    (hEH : Parallelogram A E K H) (hFG : Parallelogram K G C F) :
    quadArea E B G K = quadArea H K F D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop46:
/-- On a given straight line to describe a square. -/
theorem Prop46 {A B P : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hP : ¬ Collinear A B P) :
    ∃ D E : Point, Square A D E B ∧ SameSideOf D P A B ∧ SameSideOf E P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop5:
/-- In isosceles triangles the angles at the base are equal to one another, and, if the equal
straight lines be produced further, the angles under the base will be equal to one another. -/
theorem Prop5 {A B C D E : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖A C‖)
    (hD : Between A B D) (hE : Between A C E) :
    ∠ A B C = ∠ A C B ∧ ∠ C B D = ∠ B C E
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop6:
/-- If in a triangle two angles be equal to one another, the sides which subtend the equal angles
will also be equal to one another. -/
theorem Prop6 {A B C : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (h : ∠ A B C = ∠ A C B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖A C‖
helper_signatures.Elements.CommonNotion1:
/-- **Common Notion 1.** Things which are equal to the same thing are also equal
to one another. -/
theorem CommonNotion1 {α : Sort _} {a b c : α} (h₁ : a = c) (h₂ : b = c) : a = b
helper_signatures.Elements.CommonNotion2:
/-- **Common Notion 2.** If equals be added to equals, the wholes are equal. -/
theorem CommonNotion2 {a b c d : Magnitude k} (h₁ : a = b) (h₂ : c = d) :
    a + c = b + d
helper_signatures.Elements.Contain.symm:
/-- Read either way round, two lengths contain the same areas: the rectangle PQRS
read as PSRQ has its sides about the angle at P in the other order. -/
theorem Contain.symm (h : Contain a b x) : Contain b a x
helper_signatures.Elements.Magnitude.instAssociative:
/-- Adding magnitudes is associative (System E §3.5), told to `ac_rfl`. -/
instance Magnitude.instAssociative : Std.Associative (α := Magnitude k) (· + ·)
helper_signatures.Elements.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.between_of_len_lt:
/-- Of two points on a ray, the one nearer the start lies between the start and
the other. -/
theorem OnRay.between_of_len_lt (hP : OnRay P A B) (hQ : OnRay Q A B) (h : ‖A P‖ < ‖A Q‖) :
    Between A P Q
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.eq_of_len_eq:
/-- On a ray, only one point lies at a given distance from its start: a point P
on the ray from A through B, as far from A as B is, is B itself.

This is Sir Henry Savile's argument, which Heath reports on I.4 (vol. 1,
p. 250): otherwise P falls short of B or beyond it, and either way the less
would be equal to the greater. -/
theorem OnRay.eq_of_len_eq (hP : OnRay P A B) (h : ‖A P‖ = ‖A B‖) : P = B
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.not_between:
/-- Two points of one ray are never on opposite sides of its start: A does not
lie between them. -/
theorem OnRay.not_between (hP : OnRay P A B) (hQ : OnRay Q A B) : ¬ Between P A Q
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.of_between:
/-- A point between A and B is on the ray from A through B. -/
theorem OnRay.of_between (h : Between A P B) : OnRay P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.symm:
/-- P is on the ray from A through B exactly when B is on the ray from A
through P: they are one and the same ray. -/
theorem OnRay.symm (h : OnRay P A B) : OnRay B A P
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.between:
/-- Parallels keep order. Let three straight lines be crossed by two others: if B
lies between A and C on one crossing straight line, then B' lies between A'
and C' on the other, when A, A' lie on L₁, B, B' on L, and C, C' on
L₃, and L₁ and L₃ are each parallel to L. All of L₁ lies on one side of
L, and all of L₃ on the other (`Parallel.sameSide`). Book II's figures use it
(`Parallelogram.figure`), where the parallels through the points of section meet the
far side of the square in the same order. -/
theorem Parallel.between (h₁ : Parallel L₁ L) (h₃ : Parallel L₃ L) (hA : OnLine A L₁)
    (hB : OnLine B L) (hC : OnLine C L₃) (hABC : Between A B C) (hA' : OnLine A' L₁)
    (hB' : OnLine B' L) (hC' : OnLine C' L₃) (hcol : Collinear A' B' C') :
    Between A' B' C'
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.not_onLine:
/-- Parallels do not meet: a point of L is not on M. -/
theorem Parallel.not_onLine (h : Parallel L M) (hP : OnLine P L) : ¬ OnLine P M
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.symm:
/-- If L is parallel to M, then M is parallel to L. -/
theorem Parallel.symm (h : Parallel L M) : Parallel M L
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.about_diameter:
/-- **The gnomon and the rest are the whole.** In I.43's figure, the parallelogram
ABCD is the two parallelograms AEKH, KGCF about its diameter AC together with
the two complements EBGK, HKFD. So a gnomon (Definition II.2), one parallelogram
about the diameter with the two complements, makes the whole together with the other
parallelogram about the diameter: "the gnomon NOP and LG are the whole square CEFB"
(II.5). The complements are parallelograms (`Parallelogram.complements`), HKG and
EKF are straight lines, and the whole is cut along each in turn
(`quadArea_add_of_parallelograms`). [I. 30] -/
theorem Parallelogram.about_diameter (hABCD : Parallelogram A B C D) (hK : Between A K C)
    (hE : Between A E B) (hG : Between B G C) (hF : Between C F D) (hH : Between D H A)
    (hEH : Parallelogram A E K H) (hFG : Parallelogram K G C F) :
    quadArea A B C D =
      quadArea A E K H + quadArea E B G K + quadArea K G C F + quadArea H K F D
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.complements:
/-- The complements are parallelograms. In I.43's figure, the parallelogram ABCD with
the parallelograms AEKH, KGCF about its diameter AC, the complements EBGK and
HKFD are parallelograms too: each straight line through K is parallel to the side
it runs beside, both being parallel to the opposite side [I. 30]. [I. 30] -/
theorem Parallelogram.complements (hABCD : Parallelogram A B C D) (hK : Between A K C)
    (hE : Between A E B) (hG : Between B G C) (hF : Between C F D) (hH : Between D H A)
    (hEH : Parallelogram A E K H) (hFG : Parallelogram K G C F) :
    Parallelogram E B G K ∧ Parallelogram H K F D
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.figure:
/-- **"Let the figure be drawn."** In the parallelogram ADEB, with C on its side AB,
draw the diameter BD; through C the parallel CF to AD, cutting BD at G and
DE at F; and through G the parallel HK to AB, cutting AD at H and BE at K
[I. 31]. Each point where a parallel is cut is found by `Prop30.meet`. Then G lies
between B and D, each other point between the ends of its side, G between C and
F and between H and K, and CGKB, GHDF are the parallelograms about the diameter:
everything I.43 asks for, and `Parallelogram.about_diameter` with it.

This is the figure of Book II. II.4 draws it line by line in these letters; II.7 says only
"let the figure be drawn"; II.5 and II.6 draw it in a square on CB and on CD, and II.8
draws it twice ("let the figure be drawn double"). [I. 30, I. 31] -/
theorem Parallelogram.figure (hp : Parallelogram A D E B) (hACB : Between A C B) :
    ∃ F G H K : Point, Between B G D ∧ Between D F E ∧ Between A H D ∧ Between E K B ∧
      Between C G F ∧ Between H G K ∧ Parallelogram B C G K ∧ Parallelogram G H D F
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate:
/-- A parallelogram has the same area whichever diameter cuts it: the parallelogram
ABCD measured by BD, as BCDA, is the same as measured by AC. -/
theorem Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea B C D A = quadArea A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.reverse:
/-- The parallelogram ABCD, read the other way round from A, is the
parallelogram ADCB. -/
theorem Parallelogram.reverse (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Parallelogram A D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.rotate:
/-- The parallelogram ABCD, named from B, is the parallelogram BCDA. -/
theorem Parallelogram.rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Parallelogram B C D A
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate1:
/-- **Postulate 1.** To draw a straight line from any point to any point. -/
axiom Postulate1 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Rectangle.eq_rect:
/-- Euclid's way of naming a rectangle: "BH is the rectangle A, BC, for it is contained
by GB, BC, and BG is equal to A" (II.1). If the sides PQ, PS of the rectangle
PQRS are equal to AB, CD, it is the rectangle contained by AB, CD.
[I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Rectangle.eq_rect (h : Rectangle P Q R S) (h₁ : ‖P Q‖ = ‖A B‖) (h₂ : ‖P S‖ = ‖C D‖) :
    quadArea P Q R S = rect A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.Rectangle.of_right:
/-- One right angle makes a rectangle: a parallelogram ABCD whose angle at A is
right has all four of its angles right. The angles DAB, ABC stand on the parallels
AD, BC, so together they make two right angles [I. 29], and the angle at B is
right; in the same way so are the angles at C and D. Euclid says so in II.4 ("the
angles KBC, GCB are equal to two right angles"), and elsewhere in Book II takes it
for granted, as Heath remarks of II.4 that "there can be no need to repeat exactly
that part of the proof of I. 46 which shows that all the angles of the figure there
constructed are right when one is" (vol. 1, p. 381). [I. 29] -/
theorem Rectangle.of_right (h : Parallelogram A B C D) (hA : ∠ D A B = ∟) :
    Rectangle A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.Rectangle.reverse:
/-- The rectangle ABCD, read the other way round from A, is the rectangle ADCB. -/
theorem Rectangle.reverse (h : Rectangle A B C D) : Rectangle A D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Rectangle.rotate:
/-- The rectangle ABCD, named from B, is the rectangle BCDA. -/
theorem Rectangle.rotate (h : Rectangle A B C D) : Rectangle B C D A
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the same side of AB as Q, then Q is on the same side as P. -/
theorem SameSideOf.symm (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.trans:
/-- Points on the same side as a third are on the same side as each other. -/
theorem SameSideOf.trans (h₁ : SameSideOf P Q A B) (h₂ : SameSideOf Q R A B) :
    SameSideOf P R A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Square:
/-- **Definition 22.** "Of quadrilateral figures, a square is that which is both
equilateral and right-angled." The corners are `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, in order. -/
def Square (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Square.about_diameter:
/-- **In square areas the parallelograms about the diameter are squares.** If ABCD is a
square and a parallelogram, K lies on its diameter AC, and AEKH is a
parallelogram with E on AB and H on AD, then AEKH is a square.

Heath's note on II.4 quotes this from the Greek text, where it stands as a porism,
"undoubtedly interpolated" (vol. 1, p. 381), and his 1908 text leaves it out. Euclid
proves its first case inside II.4 ("CGKB is equilateral ... it is also
right-angled"), says "for the same reason" for the second, and in II.5–II.8 takes it
for granted: "LG, which is equal to the square on CD".

The angle EKA is equal to the alternate angle KAH [I. 29], that is to CAD, which
is equal to the alternate angle ACB [I. 29], and so to BAC [I. 5]. So the angles
EAK, EKA are equal, and EK is equal to EA [I. 6]; the opposite sides are
equal [I. 34]; and the angle at A is the square's, so all four are right
(`Rectangle.of_right`). [I. 5, I. 6, I. 29, I. 34] -/
theorem Square.about_diameter (h : Square A B C D) (hp : Parallelogram A B C D)
    (hK : Between A K C) (hE : Between A E B) (hH : Between A H D)
    (hAEKH : Parallelogram A E K H) : Square A E K H
helper_signatures.Elements.Square.described:
/-- The square ADEB that I.46 describes on AB, with D and E on the side of AB
where P is, is a parallelogram [I. 28], and it is the square on AB: "AE is the
square on AB" (II.2). [I. 4, I. 28, I. 34] -/
theorem Square.described (h : Square A D E B) (hD : SameSideOf D P A B)
    (hE : SameSideOf E P A B) : Parallelogram A D E B ∧ quadArea A D E B = sq A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Square.eq_sq:
/-- A square is the square on its side: the square ABCD, a parallelogram, is the
square on AB. [I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Square.eq_sq (h : Square A B C D) (hp : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea A B C D = sq A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Square.reverse:
/-- The square ABCD, read the other way round from A, is the square ADCB. -/
theorem Square.reverse (h : Square A B C D) (hp : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    Square A D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Square.rotate:
/-- The square ABCD, named from B, is the square BCDA. -/
theorem Square.rotate (h : Square A B C D) : Square B C D A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.add_comm:
/-- The order of adding does not matter. (System E §3.5) -/
axiom add_comm (a b : Magnitude k) : a + b = b + a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.adjacent_eq_of_right:
/-- A right angle is equal to the angle adjacent to it. (Diagram-angle 3; the
other half is Definition 10 together with Postulate 4) -/
axiom adjacent_eq_of_right (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) (h : Between A C B)
    (hD : ¬ OnLine D L) (hright : ∠ A C D = ∟) : ∠ A C D = ∠ D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_of_between_left:
/-- If B is between A and C, and D is between A and B, then D is between
A and C. (Between 4) -/
axiom between_of_between_left (h₁ : Between A B C) (h₂ : Between A D B) : Between A D C
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_symm:
/-- If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1) -/
axiom between_symm (h : Between A B C) : Between C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.len_symm:
/-- The straight line AB is the straight line BA. (Metric 3) -/
axiom len_symm (A B : Point) : ‖A B‖ = ‖B A‖
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.line_unique:
/-- Two points determine a straight line. (Generalities 1) -/
axiom line_unique (hAB : A ≠ B) (hAL : OnLine A L) (hBL : OnLine B L) (hAM : OnLine A M)
    (hBM : OnLine B M) : L = M
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.lt_trichotomy:
/-- Of two magnitudes, one is less, or they are equal, or the other is less.
(System E §3.5) -/
axiom lt_trichotomy (a b : Magnitude k) : a < b ∨ a = b ∨ b < a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between:
/-- A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between_ends:
/-- The ends of a finite straight line differ. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between_ends:
/-- A straight line through A and C passes through every point between them.
(Between 3) -/
axiom on_line_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hC : OnLine C L) :
    OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.between_cut:
/-- Cutting off beyond a point: if B is between A and C, and D between B and
C, then B is between A and D. This is the step after "let CE be made equal to
CD [I. 3]" on a straight line produced: what is cut off from BC still lies beyond
B. -/
theorem between_cut (h₁ : Between A B C) (h₂ : Between B D C) : Between A B D
helper_signatures.Elements.between_inner:
/-- Order on a straight line: if B is between A and C, and C is between A
and D, then C is between B and D. -/
theorem between_inner (h₁ : Between A B C) (h₂ : Between A C D) : Between B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.exists_off_line:
/-- There is a point off the straight line AB, avoiding any points already in the
figure. The circles with centres A and B through each other cut one another
(System E, Intersection 5), and a point where they cut is off AB: on AB it would be
as far from A as B is, and as far from B as A is, and one of the three points
would lie between the other two (Definition 15; System E, Between 6 and Diagram-segment
1). Then any point on its side will do (System E, Points 5). -/
theorem exists_off_line (hAB : A ≠ B) (avoid : List Point) :
    ∃ P : Point, Triangle A B P ∧ P ∉ avoid
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea_add_of_parallelograms:
/-- A parallelogram cut by a straight line parallel to two of its sides is the two
parallelograms it is cut into. If E lies between A and D, F between B and
C, and ABFE, EFCD are parallelograms, then the figure ABCD is ABFE and
EFCD together. Cut each piece and the whole into triangles from A and C; the
four-sided figure AFCE is measured by AC in the whole and by FE in the pieces,
and its diameters cross, for A and C lie on either side of EF. -/
theorem quadArea_add_of_parallelograms (h₁ : Parallelogram A B F E) (h₂ : Parallelogram E F C D)
    (hAED : Between A E D) (hBFC : Between B F C) :
    quadArea A B C D = quadArea A B F E + quadArea E F C D
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea_reverse:
/-- The figure ABCD read the other way round, as ADCB, has the same diameter
AC, and the same area. -/
theorem quadArea_reverse (A B C D : Point) : quadArea A D C B = quadArea A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.quadArea_rotate₂:
/-- The figure ABCD read from C, as CDAB, has the same diameter CA, and the
same area. -/
theorem quadArea_rotate₂ (A B C D : Point) : quadArea C D A B = quadArea A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.rect:
/-- **The rectangle contained by `AB`, `CD`** (Definition II.1): the area of any
rectangle whose sides about a right angle are equal to `AB` and `CD`. Lean chooses one
such area (`Classical.epsilon`); `Rectangle.contained` shows that every such
rectangle is equal to it. -/
noncomputable def rect (A B C D : Point) : Area
helper_signatures.Elements.rect_comm:
/-- The rectangle contained by AB, CD is the rectangle contained by CD, AB. -/
theorem rect_comm (A B C D : Point) : rect A B C D = rect C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.rect_congr:
/-- The rectangle contained by AB, CD depends only on the lengths of AB and CD:
straight lines equal to them contain the same rectangle. -/
theorem rect_congr (h₁ : ‖A B‖ = ‖A' B'‖) (h₂ : ‖C D‖ = ‖C' D'‖) :
    rect A B C D = rect A' B' C' D'
helper_signatures.Elements.sq:
/-- **The square on `AB`**: the rectangle contained by `AB`, `AB`, the area of any
square described on a straight line equal to `AB` (`Square.eq_sq`). -/
noncomputable def sq (A B : Point) : Area
helper_signatures.Elements.sq_congr:
/-- Squares on equal straight lines are equal: "since AC is equal to CE, the square on
AC is also equal to the square on CE" (II.9). -/
theorem sq_congr (h : ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖) : sq A B = sq C D

I.4.enunciation: If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the base, the triangle will be equal to the triangle, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend.

I.5.enunciation: In isosceles triangles the angles at the base are equal to one another, and, if the equal straight lines be produced further, the angles under the base will be equal to one another.

I.6.enunciation: If in a triangle two angles be equal to one another, the sides which subtend the equal angles will also be equal to one another.

I.28.enunciation: If a straight line falling on two straight lines make the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle on the same side, or the interior angles on the same side equal to two right angles, the straight lines will be parallel to one another.

I.29.enunciation: A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on the same side equal to two right angles.

I.30.enunciation: Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another.

I.31.enunciation: Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line.

I.34.enunciation: In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the diameter bisects the areas.

I.36.enunciation: Parallelograms which are on equal bases and in the same parallels are equal to one another.

I.43.enunciation: In any parallelogram the complements of the parallelograms about the diameter are equal to one another.

I.46.enunciation: On a given straight line to describe a square.

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Contain:
/-- The lengths `a` and `b` contain the area `x`: some rectangle `PQRS` has `PQ` equal
to `a`, `PS` equal to `b`, and is equal to `x`; or one of `a`, `b` is nothing, and so
is `x`. -/
def Contain (a b : Length) (x : Area) : Prop :=
  ((a = 0 ∨ b = 0) ∧ x = 0) ∨
    ∃ P Q R S : Point, Rectangle P Q R S ∧ ‖P Q‖ = a ∧ ‖P S‖ = b ∧ quadArea P Q R S = x
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ P ≠ A ∧ Collinear A B P ∧ ¬ Between P A B
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.Rectangle:
/-- **Definition II.1.** A rectangular parallelogram: the parallelogram `ABCD`, its
corners taken in order, with all four of its angles right. Euclid says "rectangular",
as Definition 22 says "right-angled" of the square. -/
def Rectangle (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  Parallelogram A B C D ∧ ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Square:
/-- **Definition 22.** "Of quadrilateral figures, a square is that which is both
equilateral and right-angled." The corners are `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, in order. -/
def Square (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  ‖A B‖ = ‖B C‖ ∧ ‖B C‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖C D‖ = ‖D A‖ ∧
    ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rect:
/-- **The rectangle contained by `AB`, `CD`** (Definition II.1): the area of any
rectangle whose sides about a right angle are equal to `AB` and `CD`. Lean chooses one
such area (`Classical.epsilon`); `Rectangle.contained` shows that every such
rectangle is equal to it. -/
noncomputable def rect (A B C D : Point) : Area :=
  Classical.epsilon (Contain ‖A B‖ ‖C D‖)
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle
definitions.sq:
/-- **The square on `AB`**: the rectangle contained by `AB`, `AB`, the area of any
square described on a straight line equal to `AB` (`Square.eq_sq`). -/
noncomputable def sq (A B : Point) : Area := rect A B A B

question.instructions:
Does every proposition called by the proof unit in `lean_proof` do work towards its conclusion or a substantive intermediate step of Euclid's argument? Also check for artificial hypothesis uses. Judge this unit's uses of the supplied helper signatures; helper bodies are outside this question. Heath's sentences stand as `--` lines and `cited` gives exact enunciations. In Lean, `have h : T := p` proves T by p and calls the result h; `obtain ⟨…⟩ := p` takes p apart into named pieces; `rw [h34, h37, …]` rewrites the goal by the equalities named. Follow uses through helper calls and tactics as well as explicit names. An anonymous binding or an unused hypothesis alone does not establish a defect. If both defects occur, choose `a dummy citation`.

docs/FORMALIZATION.md, section 5:
A checked intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid is legitimate, even if the
  final proof term could do without it.

criteria.an artificial hypothesis use: No dummy citation is established, but a hypothesis is mentioned only so that it looks used, and does no substantive work.
criteria.cannot tell: What is given here is not enough to decide.
criteria.all do work: Every proposition call supports a later step or the conclusion, or establishes a substantive intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid. No hypothesis is mentioned merely to look used. With no proposition calls the citation part alone is vacuous; hypothesis use must still be inspected.
criteria.a dummy citation: Some proposition call does no substantive work: its result neither supports the argument nor establishes a substantive intermediate fact, and merely supplies a citation while the step is done another way.

bridges.Elements.Rectangle.congr:
/-- Rectangles contained by equal straight lines are equal: if the rectangles PQRS,
P'Q'R'S' have PQ equal to P'Q' and PS to P'S', they are equal. The diameter
QS cuts off the triangle SPQ, right-angled at P, which is half the rectangle
[I. 34]; and the two halves are equal [I. 4]. Euclid takes this for granted whenever
he names a rectangle by its sides. [I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Rectangle.congr (h : Rectangle P Q R S) (h' : Rectangle P' Q' R' S')
    (h₁ : ‖P Q‖ = ‖P' Q'‖) (h₂ : ‖P S‖ = ‖P' S'‖) :
    quadArea P Q R S = quadArea P' Q' R' S'
bridges.Elements.Rectangle.contained:
/-- **A rectangle is contained by its sides** (Definition II.1): the rectangle PQRS is
the rectangle contained by PQ, PS, the two straight lines containing its right
angle at P. `rect` chose some rectangle contained by straight lines equal to these,
and by `Rectangle.congr` the two are equal. [I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Rectangle.contained (h : Rectangle P Q R S) : quadArea P Q R S = rect P Q P S
bridges.Elements.Rectangle.eq_rect:
/-- Euclid's way of naming a rectangle: "BH is the rectangle A, BC, for it is contained
by GB, BC, and BG is equal to A" (II.1). If the sides PQ, PS of the rectangle
PQRS are equal to AB, CD, it is the rectangle contained by AB, CD.
[I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Rectangle.eq_rect (h : Rectangle P Q R S) (h₁ : ‖P Q‖ = ‖A B‖) (h₂ : ‖P S‖ = ‖C D‖) :
    quadArea P Q R S = rect A B C D
bridges.Elements.Square.described:
/-- The square ADEB that I.46 describes on AB, with D and E on the side of AB
where P is, is a parallelogram [I. 28], and it is the square on AB: "AE is the
square on AB" (II.2). [I. 4, I. 28, I. 34] -/
theorem Square.described (h : Square A D E B) (hD : SameSideOf D P A B)
    (hE : SameSideOf E P A B) : Parallelogram A D E B ∧ quadArea A D E B = sq A B
bridges.Elements.Square.eq_sq:
/-- A square is the square on its side: the square ABCD, a parallelogram, is the
square on AB. [I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Square.eq_sq (h : Square A B C D) (hp : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea A B C D = sq A B

state.commentary:
The gnomon of Definition II.2 enters Euclid's proofs here and stays for four propositions. In a square it is what is left when a smaller square is cut from one corner, the shape of a carpenter's square, and a scholium explains the name: "from it the whole is known, whether of the whole area or of the remainder, when it is either placed round or taken away" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 371). Euclid's gnomon NOP is CH, DM and HF together, marked "by three separate letters and a dotted curve" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 383), the curve running round H. The manuscripts' figure had two M's, and Heath relettered it; we keep his letters. NOP names an area, not three points, so our Lean writes it as the sum of its three parallelograms, as [Book II's introduction](index.md#areas) explains.

Heath recalls here Proclus' account of "the application of areas, their exceeding and their falling-short", met under I.44 (vol. 1, p. 384). II.5 is the falling-short: AH, the rectangle AD, DB, applied to AB, falls short of it by the square DM. So Heath reads II.5 as a problem, to apply to a given straight line a rectangle equal to a given square and falling short by a square figure, and the problem has two solutions, with D on either side of C. "Euclid's figure corresponds to one only of the two solutions," he writes (vol. 1, p. 384), though he has no doubt that Euclid knew both. Euclid's setting-out names no side, so our statement lets D fall on either: we prove his case, D between C and B, and get the other by exchanging A and B.

**The modern way.** Heath's problem, with $\mathrm{AB} = a$ and $\mathrm{DB} = x$, is the quadratic $ax - x^2 = b^2$ (vol. 1, p. 383). Its two roots put D at equal distances from C, one on each side, and they are real only when $b \le a/2$: by II.5 the rectangle AD, DB is the square on CB less the square on CD, so it is greatest when D is at C. At $b = a/2$ the two roots meet and D falls on C, where the segments are no longer unequal, so II.5's own case is $b \lt a/2$. Heath also writes II.5 in algebra (vol. 1, p. 385); with $\mathrm{AD} = p$ and $\mathrm{DB} = q$ (his $a$ and $b$, renamed to keep our earlier $a$ and $b$ free), it is $((p + q)/2)^2 - ((p - q)/2)^2 = pq$, and from it he draws the two rules, attributed to the Pythagoreans and to Plato, for a square number equal to two square numbers: $p = n^2$ and $q = 1$, with $n$ odd, give $((n^2 + 1)/2)^2 = ((n^2 - 1)/2)^2 + n^2$, and $p = 2n^2$ and $q = 2$ give $(n^2 + 1)^2 = (n^2 - 1)^2 + (2n)^2$.
state.heath_proof:
For let a straight line AB be cut into equal segments at C and into unequal segments at D;

I say that the rectangle contained by AD, DB together with the square on CD is equal to the square on CB.

For let the square CEFB be described on CB, [I. 46]

and let BE be joined;

through D let DG be drawn parallel to either CE or BF,

through H again let KM be drawn parallel to either AB or EF,

and again through A let AK be drawn parallel to either CL or BM. [I. 31]

Then, since the complement CH is equal to the complement HF, [I. 43]

let DM be added to each;

therefore the whole CM is equal to the whole DF.

But CM is equal to AL,

since AC is also equal to CB; [I. 36]

therefore AL is also equal to DF.

Let CH be added to each;

therefore the whole AH is equal to the gnomon NOP.

But AH is the rectangle AD, DB, for DH is equal to DB,

therefore the gnomon NOP is also equal to the rectangle AD, DB.

Let LG, which is equal to the square on CD, be added to each;

therefore the gnomon NOP and LG are equal to the rectangle contained by AD, DB and the square on CD.

But the gnomon NOP and LG are the whole square CEFB, which is described on CB;

therefore the rectangle contained by AD, DB together with the square on CD is equal to the square on CB.

state.lean_proof:
/-- If a straight line be cut into equal and unequal segments, the rectangle contained by the
unequal segments of the whole together with the square on the straight line between the points
of section is equal to the square on the half. -/
theorem Prop5 {A B C D : Point} (hACB : Between A C B) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖C B‖) (hADB : Between A D B)
    (hDC : D ≠ C) :
    rect A D D B + sq C D = sq C B := by
  -- For let a straight line AB be cut into equal segments at C and into unequal segments at D;
  -- I say that the rectangle contained by AD, DB together with the square on CD is equal to
  -- the square on CB.
  /- Euclid's figure puts D between C and B; the other side is the same with A
     and B exchanged. -/
  have euclid : ∀ {A B C D : Point}, Between A C B → ‖A C‖ = ‖C B‖ → Between C D B →
      rect A D D B + sq C D = sq C B := by
    intro A B C D hACB hAC hCDB
    have hCB : C ≠ B := ne_of_between_ends hCDB
    -- For let the square CEFB be described on CB, [I. 46]
    obtain ⟨X, hX, -⟩ := exists_off_line hCB []
    obtain ⟨E, F, hsq, hE, hF⟩ := BookI.Prop46 hCB hX
    obtain ⟨hp, hCEFB⟩ := Square.described hsq hE hF
    -- and let BE be joined;
    -- through D let DG be drawn parallel to either CE or BF,
    -- through H again let KM be drawn parallel to either AB or EF,
    obtain ⟨G, H, L, M, hBHE, hEGF, hCLE, hFMB, hDHG, hLHM, hBDHM, hHLEG⟩ := hp.figure hCDB
    -- and again through A let AK be drawn parallel to either CL or BM. [I. 31]
    obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B (ne_of_between_ends hACB)
    have hC_AB : OnLine C AB := on_line_of_between_ends hACB hA_AB hB_AB
    have hD_AB : OnLine D AB := on_line_of_between_ends hCDB hC_AB hB_AB
    obtain ⟨KM, hL_KM, hM_KM⟩ := Postulate1 L M (ne_of_between_ends hLHM)
    have hH_KM : OnLine H KM := on_line_of_between_ends hLHM hL_KM hM_KM
    have hKM_AB : Parallel KM AB := (hBDHM.1.parallel hB_AB hD_AB hH_KM hM_KM).symm
    obtain ⟨K, hK_KM, hLCAK⟩ :=
      BookI.Prop31.parallelogram hKM_AB hL_KM hC_AB hA_AB (ne_of_between hACB).symm
    -- Then, since the complement CH is equal to the complement HF, [I. 43]
    have hBCEF : Parallelogram B C E F := hp.rotate.rotate.rotate
    have hBDC : Between B D C := between_symm hCDB
    have h43 : quadArea D C L H = quadArea M H G F :=
      BookI.Prop43 hBCEF hBHE hBDC hCLE hEGF hFMB hBDHM hHLEG
    obtain ⟨hDCLH, hMHGF⟩ := hBCEF.complements hBHE hBDC hCLE hEGF hFMB hBDHM hHLEG
    -- let DM be added to each;
    have hadd := CommonNotion2 h43 (rfl : quadArea B D H M = quadArea B D H M)
    -- therefore the whole CM is equal to the whole DF.
    have hCM : quadArea L C B M = quadArea L C D H + quadArea H D B M :=
      quadArea_add_of_parallelograms hDCLH.rotate.rotate.reverse hBDHM.rotate.rotate.reverse hLHM
        hCDB
    have hDF : quadArea D B F G = quadArea D B M H + quadArea H M F G :=
      quadArea_add_of_parallelograms hBDHM.rotate.reverse hMHGF.rotate.reverse hDHG
        (between_symm hFMB)
    have hCM_DF : quadArea L C B M = quadArea D B F G := by
      rw [hCM, hDF, quadArea_reverse L H D C, hDCLH.rotate.quadArea_rotate, hDCLH.quadArea_rotate,
        quadArea_reverse H M B D, hBDHM.rotate.quadArea_rotate, hBDHM.quadArea_rotate,
        quadArea_reverse D H M B, hBDHM.quadArea_rotate, quadArea_reverse H G F M,
        hMHGF.quadArea_rotate]
      exact hadd.trans (add_comm _ _)
    -- But CM is equal to AL,
    -- since AC is also equal to CB; [I. 36]
    obtain ⟨CE, hC_CE, hE_CE⟩ := Postulate1 C E hp.1.1
    obtain ⟨BF, hB_BF, hF_BF⟩ := Postulate1 B F hp.1.2.1.symm
    have hL_CE : OnLine L CE := on_line_of_between_ends hCLE hC_CE hE_CE
    have hM_BF : OnLine M BF := on_line_of_between_ends hFMB hF_BF hB_BF
    have hCE_BF : Parallel CE BF := hp.1.parallel hC_CE hE_CE hF_BF hB_BF
    have hLCBM : Parallelogram L C B M :=
      ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel (ne_of_between hCLE).symm (ne_of_between (between_symm hFMB))
          hL_CE hC_CE hB_BF hM_BF hCE_BF,
        AreParallel.of_parallel hCB (ne_of_between_ends hLHM).symm hC_AB hB_AB hM_KM hL_KM
          hKM_AB.symm⟩
    have h36 : quadArea L C B M = quadArea K A C L :=
      BookI.Prop36 hLCBM hLCAK.rotate.rotate.rotate.reverse hAC.symm
        ⟨KM, hL_KM, hM_KM, hK_KM, hL_KM⟩ ⟨AB, hC_AB, hB_AB, hA_AB, hC_AB⟩
    -- therefore AL is also equal to DF.
    have hAL_DF : quadArea K A C L = quadArea D B F G := CommonNotion1 h36.symm hCM_DF.symm
    -- Let CH be added to each;
    have hadd₂ := CommonNotion2 hAL_DF (rfl : quadArea D C L H = quadArea D C L H)
    -- therefore the whole AH is equal to the gnomon NOP.
    /- AH is AL and CH together: C lies between A and D, and L between K and H,
       the parallels AK, CL, DH keeping order. -/
    have hACD : Between A C D := between_cut hACB hCDB
    obtain ⟨AK, hA_AK, hK_AK⟩ := Postulate1 A K hLCAK.1.2.1
    obtain ⟨DG, hD_DG, hG_DG⟩ := Postulate1 D G (ne_of_between_ends hDHG)
    have hH_DG : OnLine H DG := on_line_of_between_ends hDHG hD_DG hG_DG
    have hAK_CE : Parallel AK CE := (hLCAK.1.parallel hL_CE hC_CE hA_AK hK_AK).symm
    have hDG_CE : Parallel DG CE := (hDCLH.2.parallel hC_CE hL_CE hH_DG hD_DG).symm
    have hKLH : Between K L H := Parallel.between hAK_CE hDG_CE hA_AK hC_CE hD_DG hACD hK_AK
      hL_CE hH_DG ⟨KM, hK_KM, hL_KM, hH_KM⟩
    have hAH : quadArea A K H D = quadArea A K L C + quadArea C L H D :=
      quadArea_add_of_parallelograms hLCAK.rotate.rotate hDCLH.rotate hACD hKLH
    have hgnomon : quadArea A K H D = quadArea D C L H + quadArea B D H M + quadArea M H G F := by
      calc
        quadArea A K H D = quadArea K A C L + quadArea D C L H := by
          rw [hAH, ← hLCAK.rotate.rotate.quadArea_rotate, quadArea_reverse K A C L,
            hDCLH.quadArea_rotate]
        _ = quadArea D B F G + quadArea D C L H := hadd₂
        _ = quadArea D C L H + quadArea B D H M + quadArea M H G F := by
          rw [hDF, quadArea_reverse D H M B, hBDHM.quadArea_rotate,
            quadArea_reverse H G F M, hMHGF.quadArea_rotate]
          ac_rfl
    -- But AH is the rectangle AD, DB, for DH is equal to DB,
    have hDM : Square B D H M :=
      hsq.rotate.rotate.rotate.about_diameter hBCEF hBHE hBDC (between_symm hFMB) hBDHM
    have hDH_DB : ‖D H‖ = ‖D B‖ := hDM.1.symm.trans (len_symm B D)
    have hAD : A ≠ D := ne_of_between_ends hACD
    have hAK_DG : Parallel AK DG := BookI.Prop30.parallel hAK_CE hDG_CE fun e => by
      have hAB_DG : AB = DG := line_unique hAD hA_AB hD_AB (e ▸ hA_AK) hD_DG
      exact hKM_AB.not_onLine hH_KM (hAB_DG ▸ hH_DG)
    have hDAKH : Parallelogram D A K H :=
      ⟨AreParallel.of_parallel hAD.symm (ne_of_between_ends hKLH) hD_AB hA_AB hK_KM hH_KM
          hKM_AB.symm,
        AreParallel.of_parallel hLCAK.1.2.1 (ne_of_between hDHG).symm hA_AK hK_AK hH_DG hD_DG
          hAK_DG⟩
    have hH_AB : ¬ OnLine H AB := fun h => hKM_AB.not_onLine hH_KM h
    have hright : ∠ H D A = ∟ := by
      have h := hDM.2.2.2.2.1
      rw [adjacent_eq_of_right hB_AB hA_AB (between_of_between_left (between_symm hACB) hBDC)
        hH_AB h] at h
      exact h
    have hAHrect : quadArea D A K H = rect A D D B :=
      (Rectangle.of_right hDAKH hright).eq_rect (len_symm D A) hDH_DB
    -- therefore the gnomon NOP is also equal to the rectangle AD, DB.
    have hNOP : quadArea D C L H + quadArea B D H M + quadArea M H G F = rect A D D B :=
      (hgnomon.symm.trans hDAKH.quadArea_rotate).trans hAHrect
    -- Let LG, which is equal to the square on CD, be added to each;
    have hLG : Square E G H L :=
      hsq.rotate.about_diameter hp.rotate (between_symm hBHE) hEGF (between_symm hCLE)
        hHLEG.rotate.rotate
    obtain ⟨-, hDC_HL, -, -, -⟩ := BookI.Prop34 (A := D) (B := H) (C := C) (D := L) hDCLH
    have hLGsq : quadArea H L E G = sq C D := by
      rw [quadArea_rotate₂ E G H L, hLG.eq_sq hHLEG.rotate.rotate]
      exact sq_congr ((hLG.1.trans hLG.2.1).trans (hDC_HL.symm.trans (len_symm D C)))
    -- therefore the gnomon NOP and LG are equal to the rectangle contained by AD, DB and the
    -- square on CD.
    have hadd₃ := CommonNotion2 hNOP hLGsq
    -- But the gnomon NOP and LG are the whole square CEFB, which is described on CB;
    have hwhole := hBCEF.about_diameter hBHE hBDC hCLE hEGF hFMB hBDHM hHLEG
    -- therefore the rectangle contained by AD, DB together with the square on CD is equal to the
    -- square on CB.
    rw [← hadd₃, ← hCEFB, hBCEF.quadArea_rotate, hwhole]
    ac_rfl
  /- D falls between A and C, or between C and B, for it cannot be C itself, the
     segments being unequal. The second is Euclid's case; for the first we exchange
     A and B. -/
  have hCray : OnRay C A B := OnRay.of_between hACB
  have hDray : OnRay D A B := OnRay.of_between hADB
  rcases lt_trichotomy ‖A D‖ ‖A C‖ with h | h | h
  · have hADC : Between A D C := hDray.between_of_len_lt hCray h
    have := euclid (between_symm hACB) (by rw [len_symm B C, len_symm C A]; exact hAC.symm)
      (between_symm hADC)
    rw [rect_comm, rect_congr (len_symm D A) (len_symm B D),
      sq_congr ((len_symm C A).trans hAC)] at this
    exact this
  · obtain ⟨AB, hA, hB⟩ := Postulate1 A B (ne_of_between_ends hACB)
    have hDray' : OnRay D A C := ⟨ne_of_between hACB, (ne_of_between hADB).symm,
      ⟨AB, hA, on_line_of_between_ends hACB hA hB, on_line_of_between_ends hADB hA hB⟩,
      hDray.not_between hCray⟩
    exact absurd (hDray'.eq_of_len_eq h) hDC
  · exact euclid hACB hAC (between_inner (hCray.between_of_len_lt hDray h) hADB)
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.

statement.note: For D on either side of C: Euclid's figure puts D between C and B, and the other side follows by exchanging A and B.

state.lean_statement:
theorem Prop5 {A B C D : Point} (hACB : Between A C B) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖C B‖) (hADB : Between A D B)
    (hDC : D ≠ C) :
    rect A D D B + sq C D = sq C B

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Contain:
/-- The lengths `a` and `b` contain the area `x`: some rectangle `PQRS` has `PQ` equal
to `a`, `PS` equal to `b`, and is equal to `x`; or one of `a`, `b` is nothing, and so
is `x`. -/
def Contain (a b : Length) (x : Area) : Prop :=
  ((a = 0 ∨ b = 0) ∧ x = 0) ∨
    ∃ P Q R S : Point, Rectangle P Q R S ∧ ‖P Q‖ = a ∧ ‖P S‖ = b ∧ quadArea P Q R S = x
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.Rectangle:
/-- **Definition II.1.** A rectangular parallelogram: the parallelogram `ABCD`, its
corners taken in order, with all four of its angles right. Euclid says "rectangular",
as Definition 22 says "right-angled" of the square. -/
def Rectangle (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  Parallelogram A B C D ∧ ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rect:
/-- **The rectangle contained by `AB`, `CD`** (Definition II.1): the area of any
rectangle whose sides about a right angle are equal to `AB` and `CD`. Lean chooses one
such area (`Classical.epsilon`); `Rectangle.contained` shows that every such
rectangle is equal to it. -/
noncomputable def rect (A B C D : Point) : Area :=
  Classical.epsilon (Contain ‖A B‖ ‖C D‖)
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle
definitions.sq:
/-- **The square on `AB`**: the rectangle contained by `AB`, `AB`, the area of any
square described on a straight line equal to `AB` (`Square.eq_sq`). -/
noncomputable def sq (A B : Point) : Area := rect A B A B

For let a straight line AB be bisected at the point C, and let a straight line BD be added to it in a straight line;

I say that the rectangle contained by AD, DB together with the square on CB is equal to the square on CD.

For let the square CEFD be described on CD, [I. 46]

and let DE be joined;

through the point B let BG be drawn parallel to either EC or DF,

through the point H let KM be drawn parallel to either AB or EF,

and further through A let AK be drawn parallel to either CL or DM. [I. 31]

Then, since AC is equal to CB,

AL is also equal to CH. [I. 36]

But CH is equal to HF. [I. 43]

Therefore AL is also equal to HF.

Let CM be added to each;

therefore the whole AM is equal to the gnomon NOP.

But AM is the rectangle AD, DB,

for DM is equal to DB;

therefore the gnomon NOP is also equal to the rectangle AD, DB.

Let LG, which is equal to the square on BC, be added to each;

therefore the rectangle contained by AD, DB together with the square on CB is equal to the gnomon NOP and LG.

But the gnomon NOP and LG are the whole square CEFD, which is described on CD;

therefore the rectangle contained by AD, DB together with the square on CB is equal to the square on CD.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.

bridges.Elements.Rectangle.congr:
/-- Rectangles contained by equal straight lines are equal: if the rectangles PQRS,
P'Q'R'S' have PQ equal to P'Q' and PS to P'S', they are equal. The diameter
QS cuts off the triangle SPQ, right-angled at P, which is half the rectangle
[I. 34]; and the two halves are equal [I. 4]. Euclid takes this for granted whenever
he names a rectangle by its sides. [I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Rectangle.congr (h : Rectangle P Q R S) (h' : Rectangle P' Q' R' S')
    (h₁ : ‖P Q‖ = ‖P' Q'‖) (h₂ : ‖P S‖ = ‖P' S'‖) :
    quadArea P Q R S = quadArea P' Q' R' S'
bridges.Elements.Rectangle.contained:
/-- **A rectangle is contained by its sides** (Definition II.1): the rectangle PQRS is
the rectangle contained by PQ, PS, the two straight lines containing its right
angle at P. `rect` chose some rectangle contained by straight lines equal to these,
and by `Rectangle.congr` the two are equal. [I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Rectangle.contained (h : Rectangle P Q R S) : quadArea P Q R S = rect P Q P S
bridges.Elements.Rectangle.eq_rect:
/-- Euclid's way of naming a rectangle: "BH is the rectangle A, BC, for it is contained
by GB, BC, and BG is equal to A" (II.1). If the sides PQ, PS of the rectangle
PQRS are equal to AB, CD, it is the rectangle contained by AB, CD.
[I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Rectangle.eq_rect (h : Rectangle P Q R S) (h₁ : ‖P Q‖ = ‖A B‖) (h₂ : ‖P S‖ = ‖C D‖) :
    quadArea P Q R S = rect A B C D
bridges.Elements.Square.described:
/-- The square ADEB that I.46 describes on AB, with D and E on the side of AB
where P is, is a parallelogram [I. 28], and it is the square on AB: "AE is the
square on AB" (II.2). [I. 4, I. 28, I. 34] -/
theorem Square.described (h : Square A D E B) (hD : SameSideOf D P A B)
    (hE : SameSideOf E P A B) : Parallelogram A D E B ∧ quadArea A D E B = sq A B
bridges.Elements.Square.eq_sq:
/-- A square is the square on its side: the square ABCD, a parallelogram, is the
square on AB. [I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Square.eq_sq (h : Square A B C D) (hp : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea A B C D = sq A B

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Contain:
/-- The lengths `a` and `b` contain the area `x`: some rectangle `PQRS` has `PQ` equal
to `a`, `PS` equal to `b`, and is equal to `x`; or one of `a`, `b` is nothing, and so
is `x`. -/
def Contain (a b : Length) (x : Area) : Prop :=
  ((a = 0 ∨ b = 0) ∧ x = 0) ∨
    ∃ P Q R S : Point, Rectangle P Q R S ∧ ‖P Q‖ = a ∧ ‖P S‖ = b ∧ quadArea P Q R S = x
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.Rectangle:
/-- **Definition II.1.** A rectangular parallelogram: the parallelogram `ABCD`, its
corners taken in order, with all four of its angles right. Euclid says "rectangular",
as Definition 22 says "right-angled" of the square. -/
def Rectangle (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  Parallelogram A B C D ∧ ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Square:
/-- **Definition 22.** "Of quadrilateral figures, a square is that which is both
equilateral and right-angled." The corners are `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, in order. -/
def Square (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  ‖A B‖ = ‖B C‖ ∧ ‖B C‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖C D‖ = ‖D A‖ ∧
    ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rect:
/-- **The rectangle contained by `AB`, `CD`** (Definition II.1): the area of any
rectangle whose sides about a right angle are equal to `AB` and `CD`. Lean chooses one
such area (`Classical.epsilon`); `Rectangle.contained` shows that every such
rectangle is equal to it. -/
noncomputable def rect (A B C D : Point) : Area :=
  Classical.epsilon (Contain ‖A B‖ ‖C D‖)
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle
definitions.sq:
/-- **The square on `AB`**: the rectangle contained by `AB`, `AB`, the area of any
square described on a straight line equal to `AB` (`Square.eq_sq`). -/
noncomputable def sq (A B : Point) : Area := rect A B A B
