state.enunciation: If a straight line be cut into equal and unequal segments, the squares on the unequal segments of the whole are double of the square on the half and of the square on the straight line between the points of section.
state.heath_proof:
For let a straight line AB be cut into equal segments at C, and into unequal segments at D;

I say that the squares on AD, DB are double of the squares on AC, CD.

For let CE be drawn from C at right angles to AB, and let it be made equal to either AC or CB;

let EA, EB be joined,

let DF be drawn through D parallel to EC,

and FG through F parallel to AB,

and let AF be joined.

Then, since AC is equal to CE,

the angle EAC is also equal to the angle AEC.

And, since the angle at C is right,

the remaining angles EAC, AEC are equal to one right angle. [I. 32]

And they are equal;

therefore each of the angles CEA, CAE is half a right angle.

For the same reason

each of the angles CEB, EBC is also half a right angle;

therefore the whole angle AEB is right.

And, since the angle GEF is half a right angle,

and the angle EGF is right, for it is equal to the interior and opposite angle ECB, [I. 29]

the remaining angle EFG is half a right angle; [I. 32]

therefore the angle GEF is equal to the angle EFG,

so that the side EG is also equal to GF. [I. 6]

Again, since the angle at B is half a right angle,

and the angle FDB is right, for it is again equal to the interior and opposite angle ECB, [I. 29]

the remaining angle BFD is half a right angle; [I. 32]

therefore the angle at B is equal to the angle DFB,

so that the side FD is also equal to the side DB. [I. 6]

Now, since AC is equal to CE,

the square on AC is also equal to the square on CE;

therefore the squares on AC, CE are double of the square on AC.

But the square on EA is equal to the squares on AC, CE, for the angle ACE is right; [I. 47]

therefore the square on EA is double of the square on AC.

Again, since EG is equal to GF,

the square on EG is also equal to the square on GF;

therefore the squares on EG, GF are double of the square on GF.

But the square on EF is equal to the squares on EG, GF;

therefore the square on EF is double of the square on GF.

But GF is equal to CD; [I. 34]

therefore the square on EF is double of the square on CD.

But the square on EA is also double of the square on AC;

therefore the squares on AE, EF are double of the squares on AC, CD.

And the square on AF is equal to the squares on AE, EF, for the angle AEF is right; [I. 47]

therefore the square on AF is double of the squares on AC, CD.

But the squares on AD, DF are equal to the square on AF, for the angle at D is right; [I. 47]

therefore the squares on AD, DF are double of the squares on AC, CD.

And DF is equal to DB;

therefore the squares on AD, DB are double of the squares on AC, CD.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.
state.lean_proof:
/-- If a straight line be cut into equal and unequal segments, the squares on the unequal segments
of the whole are double of the square on the half and of the square on the straight line between
the points of section. -/
theorem Prop9 {A B C D : Point} (hACB : Between A C B) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖C B‖) (hADB : Between A D B)
    (hDC : D ≠ C) :
    sq A D + sq D B = sq A C + sq C D + (sq A C + sq C D) := by
  -- For let a straight line AB be cut into equal segments at C, and into unequal segments at
  -- D;
  -- I say that the squares on AD, DB are double of the squares on AC, CD.
  /- As in II.5, D may fall on either side of C. Euclid's figure puts it between C
     and B, and we prove that case for any letters; the other is the same with A and B
     exchanged. Half a right angle is an angle that, added to itself, makes a right
     angle, and two such halves are equal (`Magnitude.eq_of_add_self_eq`). -/
  have euclid : ∀ {A B C D : Point}, Between A C B → ‖A C‖ = ‖C B‖ → Between C D B →
      sq A D + sq D B = sq A C + sq C D + (sq A C + sq C D) := by
    intro A B C D hACB hAC hCDB
    have hAB : A ≠ B := ne_of_between_ends hACB
    have hAC' : A ≠ C := ne_of_between hACB
    have hCB : C ≠ B := ne_of_between_ends hCDB
    have hCD : C ≠ D := ne_of_between hCDB
    have hDB : D ≠ B := ne_of_between (between_symm hCDB) |>.symm
    have hADB : Between A D B :=
      between_symm (between_of_between_left (between_symm hACB) (between_symm hCDB))
    obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B hAB
    have hC_AB : OnLine C AB := on_line_of_between_ends hACB hA_AB hB_AB
    have hD_AB : OnLine D AB := on_line_of_between_ends hADB hA_AB hB_AB
    have col : ∀ {P : Point}, OnLine P AB → Collinear A B P := fun h => ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB, h⟩
    -- For let CE be drawn from C at right angles to AB, and let it be made equal to either AC or
    -- CB;
    obtain ⟨Q, hQ, -⟩ := exists_off_line hAB []
    obtain ⟨X, hXQ, hright⟩ := BookI.Prop11 hAB (col hC_AB) hQ
    have hX_AB : ¬ OnLine X AB := not_on_line_of_same_side (hXQ.sameSide hA_AB hB_AB)
    have hCX : C ≠ X := fun e => hX_AB (e ▸ hC_AB)
    obtain ⟨E, hE, hCE⟩ := OnRay.exists_len_eq hAC'.symm hCX
    have hE_AB : ¬ OnLine E AB := fun h => by
      obtain ⟨-, hEC, ⟨M, hC_M, hX_M, hE_M⟩, -⟩ := hE
      exact hX_AB ((line_unique hEC.symm hC_M hE_M hC_AB h) ▸ hX_M)
    have hCE' : C ≠ E := fun e => hE_AB (e ▸ hC_AB)
    have rightAt : ∀ {P : Point}, OnLine P AB → P ≠ C → ∠ P C E = ∟ := fun hP hPC => by
      rw [angle_onRay_right hE hPC]; exact hright _ (col hP) hPC
    obtain ⟨CE, hC_CE, hE_CE⟩ := Postulate1 C E hCE'
    -- let EA, EB be joined,
    have hCAE : Triangle C A E := Triangle.of_line hC_AB hA_AB hAC'.symm hE_AB
    have hCBE : Triangle C B E := Triangle.of_line hC_AB hB_AB hCB hE_AB
    obtain ⟨EB, hE_EB, hB_EB⟩ := Postulate1 E B (fun e => hE_AB (e ▸ hB_AB))
    -- let DF be drawn through D parallel to EC,
    have hD_CE : ¬ OnLine D CE := fun h =>
      hE_AB ((line_unique hCD hC_CE h hC_AB hD_AB) ▸ hE_CE)
    obtain ⟨DF, hD_DF, hDF_CE⟩ := BookI.Prop31.line hD_CE
    have hEB_CE : EB ≠ CE := fun e =>
      hE_AB ((line_unique hCB hC_CE (e ▸ hB_EB) hC_AB hB_AB) ▸ hE_CE)
    obtain ⟨F, hF_EB, hF_DF⟩ := BookI.Prop30.meet hDF_CE hE_CE hE_EB hEB_CE
    have hB_DF : ¬ OnLine B DF := fun h =>
      hDF_CE.not_onLine ((line_unique hDB hD_AB hB_AB hD_DF h).symm ▸ hC_AB) hC_CE
    have hEFB : Between E F B :=
      Between.of_sameSide hCDB hD_DF (hDF_CE.symm.sameSide hE_CE hC_CE) (same_side_refl hB_DF)
        hF_DF ⟨EB, hE_EB, hF_EB, hB_EB⟩
    have hD_EB : ¬ OnLine D EB := fun h =>
      hE_AB ((line_unique hDB h hB_EB hD_AB hB_AB) ▸ hE_EB)
    have hDF : D ≠ F := fun e => hD_EB (e ▸ hF_EB)
    -- and FG through F parallel to AB,
    obtain ⟨G, hG_CE, hpG⟩ := BookI.Prop31.parallelogram hDF_CE.symm hC_CE hD_DF hF_DF hDF
    obtain ⟨FG, hF_FG, hG_FG⟩ := Postulate1 F G hpG.1.2.1
    have hFG_AB : Parallel AB FG := hpG.1.parallel hC_AB hD_AB hF_FG hG_FG
    have hE_FG : ¬ OnLine E FG := fun h =>
      hFG_AB.not_onLine hB_AB (on_line_of_between hEFB h hF_FG)
    have hEGC : Between E G C :=
      Between.of_sameSide hEFB hF_FG (same_side_refl hE_FG) (hFG_AB.sameSide hC_AB hB_AB)
        hG_FG ⟨CE, hE_CE, hG_CE, hC_CE⟩
    -- and let AF be joined.
    have hF_AB : ¬ OnLine F AB := fun h =>
      hE_AB (on_line_of_between (between_symm hEFB) hB_AB h)
    have hDA : D ≠ A := (ne_of_between hADB).symm
    have hDAF : Triangle D A F := Triangle.of_line hD_AB hA_AB hDA hF_AB
    -- Then, since AC is equal to CE,
    have hAC_CE : ‖A C‖ = ‖C E‖ := by rw [hCE, len_symm]
    -- the angle EAC is also equal to the angle AEC.
    have h5a : ∠ C A E = ∠ C E A :=
      BookI.Prop5.base hCAE ((len_symm C A).trans hAC_CE)
    -- And, since the angle at C is right,
    have hACE : ∠ A C E = ∟ := rightAt hA_AB hAC'
    -- the remaining angles EAC, AEC are equal to one right angle. [I. 32]
    have h32a := (BookI.Prop32 hCAE.cba hACB).2
    rw [hACE] at h32a
    have hrem_a : ∠ E A C + ∠ C E A = ∟ :=
      CommonNotion3 (c := ∟) (d := ∟) (by rw [← h32a]; ac_rfl) rfl
    -- And they are equal;
    have hEA : E ≠ A := hCAE.ne₂₃.symm
    have hEAC_CEA : ∠ E A C = ∠ C E A :=
      (angle_symm hEA hAC'.symm).trans h5a
    -- therefore each of the angles CEA, CAE is half a right angle.
    have hhalf_CEA : ∠ C E A + ∠ C E A = ∟ := by
      rw [hEAC_CEA] at hrem_a; exact hrem_a
    have hhalf_CAE : ∠ C A E + ∠ C A E = ∟ := by
      rw [h5a]; exact hhalf_CEA
    -- For the same reason
    -- each of the angles CEB, EBC is also half a right angle;
    have h5b : ∠ C B E = ∠ C E B := BookI.Prop5.base hCBE (by rw [hCE, len_symm C A, hAC])
    have hBCE : ∠ B C E = ∟ := rightAt hB_AB hCB.symm
    have h32b := (BookI.Prop32 hCBE.cba (between_symm hACB)).2
    rw [hBCE] at h32b
    have hEB : E ≠ B := fun e => hE_AB (e ▸ hB_AB)
    have hrem_b : ∠ E B C + ∠ C E B = ∟ :=
      CommonNotion3 (c := ∟) (d := ∟) (by rw [← h32b]; ac_rfl) rfl
    have hhalf_CEB : ∠ C E B + ∠ C E B = ∟ := by
      rw [← hrem_b, angle_symm hEB hCB, h5b]
    have hhalf_EBC : ∠ E B C + ∠ E B C = ∟ := by
      rw [angle_symm hEB hCB, h5b]; exact hhalf_CEB
    -- therefore the whole angle AEB is right.
    have hAEB : ∠ A E B = ∟ := by
      have hsplit := angle_add_of_between (Triangle.of_line hA_AB hB_AB hAB hE_AB) hACB
      have heq : ∠ C E A = ∠ C E B :=
        Magnitude.eq_of_add_self_eq (hhalf_CEA.trans hhalf_CEB.symm)
      rw [hsplit, angle_symm hEA.symm hCE', heq]; exact hhalf_CEB
    -- And, since the angle GEF is half a right angle,
    have hGEF : ∠ G E F = ∠ C E B :=
      angle_eq_of_onRay (OnRay.of_between hEGC) (OnRay.of_between hEFB)
    have hhalf_GEF : ∠ G E F + ∠ G E F = ∟ := by
      rw [hGEF]; exact hhalf_CEB
    -- and the angle EGF is right, for it is equal to the interior and opposite angle
    -- ECB, [I. 29]
    have hEGF : ∠ E G F = ∟ := by
      have h29 := BookI.Prop29.exterior hpG.1.symm.swap_left
        hpG.rotate.rotate.rotate.sameSideOf.symm hEGC
      rw [h29, angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between (between_symm hEGC)) hCD.symm,
        angle_onRay_right (OnRay.of_between hCDB) hCE'.symm, angle_symm hCE'.symm hCB.symm]
      exact hBCE
    -- the remaining angle EFG is half a right angle; [I. 32]
    have hFEG : Triangle F E G := by
      refine Triangle.of_line hF_EB hE_EB (ne_of_between hEFB).symm fun h => ?_
      exact hE_AB ((line_unique hCB hC_CE ((line_unique (ne_of_between hEGC) hE_CE
        (on_line_of_between_ends hEGC hE_CE hC_CE) hE_EB h) ▸ hB_EB) hC_AB hB_AB) ▸ hE_CE)
    have h32c := (BookI.Prop32 hFEG hEGC).2
    rw [hEGF] at h32c
    have hFE : F ≠ E := (ne_of_between hEFB).symm
    have hGE : G ≠ E := (ne_of_between hEGC).symm
    have hGF : G ≠ F := fun e => hDF_CE.not_onLine hF_DF (e ▸ hG_CE)
    have hhalf_EFG : ∠ E F G + ∠ E F G = ∟ := by
      rw [angle_symm hFE hGE, angle_symm hGF hFE.symm] at h32c
      have hsum : ∠ G E F + ∠ E F G = ∟ :=
        CommonNotion3 (c := ∟) (d := ∟) (by rw [← h32c]; ac_rfl) rfl
      have := hsum.trans hhalf_GEF.symm
      have heq : ∠ E F G = ∠ G E F :=
        CommonNotion3 (by rw [add_comm]; exact this) rfl
      rw [heq]; exact hhalf_GEF
    -- therefore the angle GEF is equal to the angle EFG,
    have hEFG : ∠ E F G = ∠ G E F :=
      Magnitude.eq_of_add_self_eq (hhalf_EFG.trans hhalf_GEF.symm)
    -- so that the side EG is also equal to GF. [I. 6]
    have hEG_GF : ‖G E‖ = ‖G F‖ := by
      refine BookI.Prop6 hFEG.cba ?_
      rw [angle_symm hGF hFE.symm, hEFG]
    -- Again, since the angle at B is half a right angle,
    have hFBD : ∠ F B D = ∠ E B C :=
      angle_eq_of_onRay (OnRay.of_between (between_symm hEFB))
        (OnRay.of_between (between_symm hCDB))
    have hhalf_FBD : ∠ F B D + ∠ F B D = ∟ := by
      rw [hFBD]; exact hhalf_EBC
    -- and the angle FDB is right, for it is again equal to the interior and opposite angle
    -- ECB, [I. 29]
    have hFDB : ∠ F D B = ∟ := by
      have h29 := BookI.Prop29.exterior hpG.2.swap_right hpG.sameSideOf.swap (between_symm hCDB)
      rw [angle_symm hDF.symm hDB.symm, h29,
        angle_onRay_right (OnRay.of_between (between_symm hEGC)) hCD.symm,
        angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between hCDB) hCE'.symm]
      exact hBCE
    have hBDF : ∠ B D F = ∟ := (angle_symm hDB.symm hDF.symm).trans hFDB
    -- the remaining angle BFD is half a right angle; [I. 32]
    have hFB : F ≠ B := ne_of_between (between_symm hEFB) |>.symm
    have hFBDt : Triangle F B D := Triangle.of_line hF_EB hB_EB hFB hD_EB
    have h32d := (BookI.Prop32 hFBDt (between_symm hCDB)).2
    rw [hBDF] at h32d
    have hhalf_DFB : ∠ D F B + ∠ D F B = ∟ := by
      have hsum : ∠ F B D + ∠ D F B = ∟ :=
        CommonNotion3 (c := ∟) (d := ∟) (by rw [← h32d]; ac_rfl) rfl
      have := hsum.trans hhalf_FBD.symm
      have heq : ∠ D F B = ∠ F B D :=
        CommonNotion3 (by rw [add_comm]; exact this) rfl
      rw [heq]; exact hhalf_FBD
    -- therefore the angle at B is equal to the angle DFB,
    have hDFB : ∠ D F B = ∠ F B D :=
      Magnitude.eq_of_add_self_eq (hhalf_DFB.trans hhalf_FBD.symm)
    -- so that the side FD is also equal to the side DB. [I. 6]
    have hDB_DF : ‖D B‖ = ‖D F‖ := by
      refine BookI.Prop6 hFBDt.cba ?_
      rw [angle_symm hDB hFB, hDFB]
    -- Now, since AC is equal to CE,
    -- the square on AC is also equal to the square on CE;
    have hsqAC : sq A C = sq C E := sq_congr hAC_CE
    -- therefore the squares on AC, CE are double of the square on AC.
    have h1 : sq A C + sq C E = sq A C + sq A C := by rw [hsqAC]
    -- But the square on EA is equal to the squares on AC, CE, for the angle ACE is
    -- right; [I. 47]
    have h47a : sq A E = sq A C + sq C E := BookI.Prop47.sq hCAE hACE
    -- therefore the square on EA is double of the square on AC.
    have h2 : sq E A = sq A C + sq A C := (sq_symm E A).trans (h47a.trans h1)
    -- Again, since EG is equal to GF,
    -- the square on EG is also equal to the square on GF;
    have hsqEG : sq E G = sq G F := sq_congr (by rw [len_symm]; exact hEG_GF)
    -- therefore the squares on EG, GF are double of the square on GF.
    have h3 : sq E G + sq G F = sq G F + sq G F := by rw [hsqEG]
    -- But the square on EF is equal to the squares on EG, GF;
    have h47b : sq E F = sq E G + sq G F := BookI.Prop47.sq hFEG.cba hEGF
    -- therefore the square on EF is double of the square on GF.
    have hEFdouble : sq E F = sq G F + sq G F := h47b.trans h3
    -- But GF is equal to CD; [I. 34]
    have hGF_CD : ‖G F‖ = ‖C D‖ := (BookI.Prop34 hpG.rotate.rotate.rotate).1
    -- therefore the square on EF is double of the square on CD.
    have h4 : sq E F = sq C D + sq C D := by rw [hEFdouble, sq_congr hGF_CD]
    -- But the square on EA is also double of the square on AC;
    -- therefore the squares on AE, EF are double of the squares on AC, CD.
    have h5 : sq A E + sq E F = sq A C + sq C D + (sq A C + sq C D) := by
      rw [sq_symm A E, h2, h4]; ac_rfl
    -- And the square on AF is equal to the squares on AE, EF, for the angle AEF is
    -- right; [I. 47]
    have hAEF : ∠ A E F = ∟ := by
      rw [angle_onRay_right (OnRay.of_between hEFB) hEA.symm]; exact hAEB
    have hA_EB : ¬ OnLine A EB := fun h =>
      hE_AB ((line_unique hAB h hB_EB hA_AB hB_AB) ▸ hE_EB)
    have h47c : sq A F = sq A E + sq E F :=
      BookI.Prop47.sq (Triangle.of_line hE_EB hF_EB hFE.symm hA_EB).acb hAEF
    -- therefore the square on AF is double of the squares on AC, CD.
    have hAFdouble : sq A F = sq A C + sq C D + (sq A C + sq C D) := h47c.trans h5
    -- But the squares on AD, DF are equal to the square on AF, for the angle at D is
    -- right; [I. 47]
    /- "The angle at D" is two angles: FDB, which I.29 makes right, and ADF beside
       it, which I.47 needs here; an angle beside a right angle is right. -/
    have hADF : ∠ A D F = ∟ := by
      have := adjacent_eq_of_right hB_AB hA_AB (between_symm hADB) hF_AB hBDF
      rw [angle_symm hDA.symm hDF.symm, ← this, hBDF]
    have h47d : sq A F = sq A D + sq D F :=
      BookI.Prop47.sq hDAF hADF
    -- therefore the squares on AD, DF are double of the squares on AC, CD.
    have hADDF : sq A D + sq D F = sq A C + sq C D + (sq A C + sq C D) :=
      h47d.symm.trans hAFdouble
    -- And DF is equal to DB;
    have hDF_DB : ‖D F‖ = ‖D B‖ := hDB_DF.symm
    -- therefore the squares on AD, DB are double of the squares on AC, CD.
    rw [← sq_congr hDF_DB]; exact hADDF
  -- Therefore etc.
  /- Otherwise D lies between A and C, and we exchange A and B. -/
  have hCray : OnRay C A B := OnRay.of_between hACB
  have hDray : OnRay D A B := OnRay.of_between hADB
  rcases lt_trichotomy ‖A D‖ ‖A C‖ with h | h | h
  · have hADC : Between A D C := hDray.between_of_len_lt hCray h
    have := euclid (between_symm hACB) (by rw [len_symm B C, len_symm C A]; exact hAC.symm)
      (between_symm hADC)
    rw [sq_symm B D, sq_symm D A, sq_congr (len_symm B C ▸ hAC.symm : ‖B C‖ = ‖A C‖),
      add_comm (sq D B)] at this
    exact this
  · obtain ⟨L, hA, hB⟩ := Postulate1 A B (ne_of_between_ends hACB)
    have hDray' : OnRay D A C := ⟨ne_of_between hACB, (ne_of_between hADB).symm,
      ⟨L, hA, on_line_of_between_ends hACB hA hB, on_line_of_between_ends hADB hA hB⟩,
      hDray.not_between hCray⟩
    exact absurd (hDray'.eq_of_len_eq h) hDC
  · exact euclid hACB hAC (between_inner (hCray.between_of_len_lt hDray h) hADB)
  -- Q. E. D.

helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.parallel:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then a straight line through A and B is parallel
to one through C and D. -/
theorem AreParallel.parallel (h : AreParallel A B C D) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L)
    (hC : OnLine C M) (hD : OnLine D M) : Parallel L M
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.sameSideOf:
/-- The ends of one parallel lie on one side of the other: if AB is parallel to
CD, then A and B are on the same side of CD (`Parallel.sameSide`). -/
theorem AreParallel.sameSideOf (h : AreParallel A B C D) : SameSideOf A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.swap_left:
/-- "AB is parallel to CD" is the same as "BA is parallel to CD". -/
theorem AreParallel.swap_left (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel B A C D
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.swap_right:
/-- "AB is parallel to CD" is the same as "AB is parallel to DC". -/
theorem AreParallel.swap_right (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel A B D C
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.symm:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then CD is parallel to AB. -/
theorem AreParallel.symm (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Between.of_sameSide:
/-- Order kept across a straight line. If B, on the straight line L, lies
between A and C, and A', C' lie on the same sides of L as A, C, then a
point B' of L on one straight line with A' and C' lies between them: A' and
C' are on opposite sides of L, so the straight line joining them crosses L
between them, and it crosses L only once (System E, Pasch 3 and 4). -/
theorem Between.of_sameSide (hABC : Between A B C) (hB : OnLine B L) (hA : SameSide A' A L)
    (hC : SameSide C' C L) (hB' : OnLine B' L) (hcol : Collinear A' B' C') :
    Between A' B' C'
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop11:
/-- To draw a straight line at right angles to a given straight line from a given point on it. -/
theorem Prop11 {A B C Q : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hC : Collinear A B C) (hQ : ¬ Collinear A B Q) :
    ∃ F : Point, SameSideOf F Q A B ∧ ∀ P : Point, Collinear A B P → P ≠ C → ∠ P C F = ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop28:
/-- If a straight line falling on two straight lines make the exterior angle equal to the interior
and opposite angle on the same side, or the interior angles on the same side equal to two right
angles, the straight lines will be parallel to one another. -/
theorem Prop28 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (hAGB : Between A G B) (hCHD : Between C H D)
    (hEGH : Between E G H) (hGHF : Between G H F) (hBD : SameSideOf B D E F)
    (h : ∠ E G B = ∠ G H D ∨ ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D = ∟ + ∟) :
    AreParallel A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29:
/-- A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one
another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on
the same side equal to two right angles. -/
theorem Prop29 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (hpar : AreParallel A B C D) (hAGB : Between A G B)
    (hCHD : Between C H D) (hEGH : Between E G H) (hGHF : Between G H F)
    (hBD : SameSideOf B D E F) :
    ∠ A G H = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ E G B = ∠ G H D ∧ ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D = ∟ + ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop29.exterior:
/-- The exterior angle. If the straight line GP is parallel to HQ, P and Q lie
on one side of GH, and E lies on HG produced beyond G, then the exterior
angle EGP is equal to the interior and opposite angle GHQ. [I. 29] -/
theorem Prop29.exterior {P G H Q E : Point} (hpar : AreParallel G P H Q)
    (hPQ : SameSideOf P Q G H) (hEGH : Between E G H) : ∠ E G P = ∠ G H Q
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30:
/-- Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another. -/
theorem Prop30 {A B C D E F : Point} (h₁ : AreParallel A B E F) (h₂ : AreParallel C D E F)
    (hC : ¬ Collinear A B C) :
    AreParallel A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop30.meet:
/-- A straight line meeting one of two parallels meets the other. If L is parallel
to M, and a straight line N, other than M, passes through a point P of M,
then N meets L. Otherwise N would be parallel to L too, and by I.30 M and
N would be parallel to one another, though both pass through P.

Euclid uses this whenever he draws a parallel and then names the point where it
meets another straight line: E and F in I.37, G and H in I.38, E in I.39,
F in I.40, F and G in I.42, H, L and M in I.44, E in I.46 and L in
I.47. It is the uniqueness of the parallel through a point, often called
Playfair's axiom; Heath reports under I.31 that Proclus draws it from I.30.
`Prop30.unique`, a step inside I.30's own proof, gives the same uniqueness from
I.29; later proofs cite this one, Proclus' route through I.30. [I. 30] -/
theorem Prop30.meet {L M N : Line} {P : Point} (hLM : Parallel L M) (hPM : OnLine P M)
    (hPN : OnLine P N) (hNM : N ≠ M) : ∃ Q : Point, OnLine Q N ∧ OnLine Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31:
/-- Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line. -/
theorem Prop31 {A B C : Point} (hBC : B ≠ C) (hA : ¬ Collinear B C A) :
    ∃ E F : Point, Between E A F ∧ AreParallel E F B C
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31.line:
/-- I.31 said of straight lines drawn and named: through a point A off the
straight line L there is a straight line K parallel to L. I.31 gives two points
of it, one on either side of A, and Postulate 1 joins them. [I. 31] -/
theorem Prop31.line {A : Point} {L : Line} (hA : ¬ OnLine A L) :
    ∃ K : Line, OnLine A K ∧ Parallel K L
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop31.parallelogram:
/-- Completing the parallelogram. If X lies on L, and Y and Z on M, which is
parallel to L, the straight line drawn through Z parallel to XY [I. 31] meets
L at a point W (`Prop30.meet`), and XYZW is a parallelogram. Euclid draws such
a parallel in I.37, I.38, I.42, I.44 and I.46, and reads the point where it meets
L, and the parallelogram, off his figure. [I. 30, I. 31] -/
theorem Prop31.parallelogram {X Y Z : Point} {L M : Line} (hLM : Parallel L M)
    (hX : OnLine X L) (hY : OnLine Y M) (hZ : OnLine Z M) (hYZ : Y ≠ Z) :
    ∃ W : Point, OnLine W L ∧ Parallelogram X Y Z W
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop32:
/-- In any triangle, if one of the sides be produced, the exterior angle is equal to the two
interior and opposite angles, and the three interior angles of the triangle are equal to two
right angles. -/
theorem Prop32 {A B C D : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hBCD : Between B C D) :
    ∠ A C D = ∠ C A B + ∠ A B C ∧ ∠ A B C + ∠ B C A + ∠ C A B = ∟ + ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop34:
/-- In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the
diameter bisects the areas. -/
theorem Prop34 {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A C D B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ C D B ∧ ∠ A B D = ∠ A C D ∧
      △ A B C = △ D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop4:
/-- If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles
contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the base, the
triangle will be equal to the triangle, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining
angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend. -/
theorem Prop4 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖D F‖) (hA : ∠ B A C = ∠ E D F) :
    ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ ∧ △ A B C = △ D E F ∧ ∠ A B C = ∠ D E F ∧ ∠ A C B = ∠ D F E
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop46:
/-- On a given straight line to describe a square. -/
theorem Prop46 {A B P : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hP : ¬ Collinear A B P) :
    ∃ D E : Point, Square A D E B ∧ SameSideOf D P A B ∧ SameSideOf E P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop47:
/-- In right-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the right angle is equal to the
squares on the sides containing the right angle. -/
theorem Prop47 {A B C D E F G H K : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hright : ∠ B A C = ∟)
    (hBDEC : Square B D E C) (hD : OppositeSidesOf D A B C) (hE : OppositeSidesOf E A B C)
    (hABFG : Square A B F G) (hF : OppositeSidesOf F C A B) (hG : OppositeSidesOf G C A B)
    (hACKH : Square A C K H) (hK : OppositeSidesOf K B A C) (hH : OppositeSidesOf H B A C) :
    quadArea B D E C = quadArea A B F G + quadArea A C K H
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop47.sq:
/-- **I.47 for the squares on straight lines.** In the triangle ABC right-angled at
A, the square on BC is equal to the squares on BA, AC. Book II cites I.47 in
this form: "the square on EA is equal to the squares on AC, CE, for the angle ACE is
right" (II.9). The three squares are described outward [I. 46], I.47 compares them,
and each is the square on its side (`Square.described`).
[I. 4, I. 28, I. 34, I. 46, I. 47] -/
theorem BookI.Prop47.sq (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hright : ∠ B A C = ∟) :
    sq B C = sq B A + sq A C
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop5:
/-- In isosceles triangles the angles at the base are equal to one another, and, if the equal
straight lines be produced further, the angles under the base will be equal to one another. -/
theorem Prop5 {A B C D E : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖A C‖)
    (hD : Between A B D) (hE : Between A C E) :
    ∠ A B C = ∠ A C B ∧ ∠ C B D = ∠ B C E
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop5.base:
/-- The angles at the base, and only those. Our I.5 is stated as Euclid states it,
with the equal sides produced and the angles under the base as well, so a proof that
cites it must first produce AB and AC (Post. 2). When only the angles at the base are
wanted, as in I.7, I.9, I.18, I.19, I.20 and I.24, any points beyond B and C
will do, and this produces them once. [I. 5] -/
theorem Prop5.base {A B C : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (h : ‖A B‖ = ‖A C‖) :
    ∠ A B C = ∠ A C B
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop6:
/-- If in a triangle two angles be equal to one another, the sides which subtend the equal angles
will also be equal to one another. -/
theorem Prop6 {A B C : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (h : ∠ A B C = ∠ A C B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖A C‖
helper_signatures.Elements.Collinear:
/-- `A`, `B`, `C` lie on one straight line. -/
def Collinear (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.CommonNotion3:
/-- **Common Notion 3.** If equals be subtracted from equals, the remainders
are equal. (From `a + c = b + d` and `c = d`, conclude `a = b`.) -/
theorem CommonNotion3 {a b c d : Magnitude k} (h₁ : a + c = b + d) (h₂ : c = d) :
    a = b
helper_signatures.Elements.Contain.symm:
/-- Read either way round, two lengths contain the same areas: the rectangle PQRS
read as PSRQ has its sides about the angle at P in the other order. -/
theorem Contain.symm (h : Contain a b x) : Contain b a x
helper_signatures.Elements.Magnitude.eq_of_add_self_eq:
/-- The halves of equal things are equal: if `a` and `a` together are equal to `b`
and `b` together, then `a` is equal to `b`. Were `a` less than `b`, then `a` and `a`
would be less than `b` and `b`; and the same the other way round. Heiberg brackets
these words in I.37 and I.38 as added later, but the step is needed all the same. -/
theorem Magnitude.eq_of_add_self_eq {a b : Magnitude k} (h : a + a = b + b) : a = b
helper_signatures.Elements.Magnitude.instAssociative:
/-- Adding magnitudes is associative (System E §3.5), told to `ac_rfl`. -/
instance Magnitude.instAssociative : Std.Associative (α := Magnitude k) (· + ·)
helper_signatures.Elements.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.between_of_len_lt:
/-- Of two points on a ray, the one nearer the start lies between the start and
the other. -/
theorem OnRay.between_of_len_lt (hP : OnRay P A B) (hQ : OnRay Q A B) (h : ‖A P‖ < ‖A Q‖) :
    Between A P Q
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.eq_of_len_eq:
/-- On a ray, only one point lies at a given distance from its start: a point P
on the ray from A through B, as far from A as B is, is B itself.

This is Sir Henry Savile's argument, which Heath reports on I.4 (vol. 1,
p. 250): otherwise P falls short of B or beyond it, and either way the less
would be equal to the greater. -/
theorem OnRay.eq_of_len_eq (hP : OnRay P A B) (h : ‖A P‖ = ‖A B‖) : P = B
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.exists_len_eq:
/-- "Let DG be made equal to DF" (I.24): on the ray from D through any point P
there is a point G with DG equal to DF. Describe the circle with centre D and
distance DF (Post. 3); the straight line DP, which passes through its centre, cuts
it on P's side of D (System E, Intersections 5, with a point Q set out on the
other side); and DG is a radius [Def. 15]. -/
theorem OnRay.exists_len_eq {D F P : Point} (hDF : D ≠ F) (hDP : D ≠ P) :
    ∃ G : Point, OnRay G D P ∧ ‖D G‖ = ‖D F‖
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.not_between:
/-- Two points of one ray are never on opposite sides of its start: A does not
lie between them. -/
theorem OnRay.not_between (hP : OnRay P A B) (hQ : OnRay Q A B) : ¬ Between P A Q
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.of_between:
/-- A point between A and B is on the ray from A through B. -/
theorem OnRay.of_between (h : Between A P B) : OnRay P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.symm:
/-- P is on the ray from A through B exactly when B is on the ray from A
through P: they are one and the same ray. -/
theorem OnRay.symm (h : OnRay P A B) : OnRay B A P
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf:
/-- The same, said of "the straight line AB": two points, each on the other side of
AB from C, are on the same side of AB as each other. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.sameSideOf {C D E : Point} (h₁ : OppositeSidesOf C D A B)
    (h₂ : OppositeSidesOf C E A B) : SameSideOf D E A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.swap:
/-- "On opposite sides of AB" is the same as "on opposite sides of BA". -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.swap (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : OppositeSidesOf P Q B A
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the other side of AB from Q, then Q is on the other side
from P. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.symm (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : OppositeSidesOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.not_onLine:
/-- Parallels do not meet: a point of L is not on M. -/
theorem Parallel.not_onLine (h : Parallel L M) (hP : OnLine P L) : ¬ OnLine P M
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.sameSide:
/-- All the points of one parallel lie on one side of the other: two points of L
are on the same side of M. Were they on opposite sides, the straight line L
joining them would cross M (System E, Intersection 1). -/
theorem Parallel.sameSide (h : Parallel L M) (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L) :
    SameSide P Q M
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.symm:
/-- If L is parallel to M, then M is parallel to L. -/
theorem Parallel.symm (h : Parallel L M) : Parallel M L
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.rotate:
/-- The parallelogram ABCD, named from B, is the parallelogram BCDA. -/
theorem Parallelogram.rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Parallelogram B C D A
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.sameSideOf:
/-- In the parallelogram ABCD, the far corners C and D lie on one side of the
side AB. (Named from another corner with `.rotate`, the same holds of every
side.) -/
theorem Parallelogram.sameSideOf (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : SameSideOf C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate1:
/-- **Postulate 1.** To draw a straight line from any point to any point. -/
axiom Postulate1 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Rectangle.rotate:
/-- The rectangle ABCD, named from B, is the rectangle BCDA. -/
theorem Rectangle.rotate (h : Rectangle A B C D) : Rectangle B C D A
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.sameSide:
/-- Two points on the same side of the straight line AB are on the same side of
any straight line drawn through A and B. -/
theorem SameSideOf.sameSide (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    SameSide P Q L
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.swap:
/-- "On the same side of AB" is the same as "on the same side of BA". -/
theorem SameSideOf.swap (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf P Q B A
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the same side of AB as Q, then Q is on the same side as P. -/
theorem SameSideOf.symm (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.trans:
/-- Points on the same side as a third are on the same side as each other. -/
theorem SameSideOf.trans (h₁ : SameSideOf P Q A B) (h₂ : SameSideOf Q R A B) :
    SameSideOf P R A B
helper_signatures.Elements.Square.rotate:
/-- The square ABCD, named from B, is the square BCDA. -/
theorem Square.rotate (h : Square A B C D) : Square B C D A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.add_comm:
/-- The order of adding does not matter. (System E §3.5) -/
axiom add_comm (a b : Magnitude k) : a + b = b + a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.adjacent_eq_of_right:
/-- A right angle is equal to the angle adjacent to it. (Diagram-angle 3; the
other half is Definition 10 together with Postulate 4) -/
axiom adjacent_eq_of_right (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) (h : Between A C B)
    (hD : ¬ OnLine D L) (hright : ∠ A C D = ∟) : ∠ A C D = ∠ D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.angle_symm:
/-- The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4) -/
axiom angle_symm (hAB : A ≠ B) (hCB : C ≠ B) : ∠ A B C = ∠ C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_of_between_left:
/-- If B is between A and C, and D is between A and B, then D is between
A and C. (Between 4) -/
axiom between_of_between_left (h₁ : Between A B C) (h₂ : Between A D B) : Between A D C
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_symm:
/-- If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1) -/
axiom between_symm (h : Between A B C) : Between C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.len_symm:
/-- The straight line AB is the straight line BA. (Metric 3) -/
axiom len_symm (A B : Point) : ‖A B‖ = ‖B A‖
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.line_unique:
/-- Two points determine a straight line. (Generalities 1) -/
axiom line_unique (hAB : A ≠ B) (hAL : OnLine A L) (hBL : OnLine B L) (hAM : OnLine A M)
    (hBM : OnLine B M) : L = M
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.lt_trichotomy:
/-- Of two magnitudes, one is less, or they are equal, or the other is less.
(System E §3.5) -/
axiom lt_trichotomy (a b : Magnitude k) : a < b ∨ a = b ∨ b < a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between:
/-- A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between_ends:
/-- The ends of a finite straight line differ. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.not_on_line_of_same_side:
/-- Points on one side of a straight line are not on it. (Same side 3) -/
axiom not_on_line_of_same_side (h : SameSide A B L) : ¬ OnLine A L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between:
/-- A straight line through A and B, with B between A and C, passes
through C. (Between 2) -/
axiom on_line_of_between (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) :
    OnLine C L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between_ends:
/-- A straight line through A and C passes through every point between them.
(Between 3) -/
axiom on_line_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) (hA : OnLine A L) (hC : OnLine C L) :
    OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.same_side_refl:
/-- A point off a straight line is on the same side of it as itself. (Same side 1) -/
axiom same_side_refl (h : ¬ OnLine A L) : SameSide A A L
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.acb:
/-- The triangle ABC, named the other way round, as ACB. -/
theorem Triangle.acb (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle A C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.cba:
/-- The triangle ABC, named the other way round, as CBA. -/
theorem Triangle.cba (h : Triangle A B C) : Triangle C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.ne₂₃:
/-- The corners of a triangle are different points. -/
theorem Triangle.ne₂₃ (h : Triangle A B C) : B ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle.of_line:
/-- Two different points of a straight line, and a third point off it, make a
triangle. -/
theorem Triangle.of_line {P Q R : Point} (hP : OnLine P L) (hQ : OnLine Q L) (hPQ : P ≠ Q)
    (hR : ¬ OnLine R L) : Triangle P Q R
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_add_of_between:
/-- If R lies between P and Q, and V is off the straight line PQ, then VR
falls within the angle PVQ, and that angle is made up of the angles PVR and
RVQ. (System E, Pasch 2 and Diagram-angle 2) -/
theorem angle_add_of_between {V P Q R : Point} (hPQV : Triangle P Q V) (h : Between P R Q) :
    ∠ P V Q = ∠ P V R + ∠ R V Q
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_eq_of_onRay:
/-- An angle doesn't change when its arms are traced through other points of the
same rays: if B' is on the ray from A through B, and C' on the ray from A
through C, the angle B'AC' is the angle BAC. (System E, Diagram-angle 4) -/
theorem angle_eq_of_onRay {B' C' : Point} (hB : OnRay B' A B) (hC : OnRay C' A C) :
    ∠ B' A C' = ∠ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_onRay_left:
/-- One arm traced through another point of its ray: if B' is on the ray from A
through B, the angle B'AC is the angle BAC. (System E, Diagram-angle 4) -/
theorem angle_onRay_left {B' : Point} (hB : OnRay B' A B) (hCA : C ≠ A) :
    ∠ B' A C = ∠ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.angle_onRay_right:
/-- The other arm traced through another point of its ray: if C' is on the ray
from A through C, the angle BAC' is the angle BAC. (System E,
Diagram-angle 4) -/
theorem angle_onRay_right {C' : Point} (hC : OnRay C' A C) (hBA : B ≠ A) :
    ∠ B A C' = ∠ B A C
helper_signatures.Elements.between_inner:
/-- Order on a straight line: if B is between A and C, and C is between A
and D, then C is between B and D. -/
theorem between_inner (h₁ : Between A B C) (h₂ : Between A C D) : Between B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.exists_off_line:
/-- There is a point off the straight line AB, avoiding any points already in the
figure. The circles with centres A and B through each other cut one another
(System E, Intersection 5), and a point where they cut is off AB: on AB it would be
as far from A as B is, and as far from B as A is, and one of the three points
would lie between the other two (Definition 15; System E, Between 6 and Diagram-segment
1). Then any point on its side will do (System E, Points 5). -/
theorem exists_off_line (hAB : A ≠ B) (avoid : List Point) :
    ∃ P : Point, Triangle A B P ∧ P ∉ avoid
helper_signatures.Elements.sq:
/-- **The square on `AB`**: the rectangle contained by `AB`, `AB`, the area of any
square described on a straight line equal to `AB` (`Square.eq_sq`). -/
noncomputable def sq (A B : Point) : Area
helper_signatures.Elements.sq_congr:
/-- Squares on equal straight lines are equal: "since AC is equal to CE, the square on
AC is also equal to the square on CE" (II.9). -/
theorem sq_congr (h : ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖) : sq A B = sq C D
helper_signatures.Elements.sq_symm:
/-- The square on AB is the square on BA. -/
theorem sq_symm (A B : Point) : sq A B = sq B A

I.4.enunciation: If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the base, the triangle will be equal to the triangle, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend.

I.5.enunciation: In isosceles triangles the angles at the base are equal to one another, and, if the equal straight lines be produced further, the angles under the base will be equal to one another.

I.6.enunciation: If in a triangle two angles be equal to one another, the sides which subtend the equal angles will also be equal to one another.

I.11.enunciation: To draw a straight line at right angles to a given straight line from a given point on it.

I.28.enunciation: If a straight line falling on two straight lines make the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle on the same side, or the interior angles on the same side equal to two right angles, the straight lines will be parallel to one another.

I.29.enunciation: A straight line falling on parallel straight lines makes the alternate angles equal to one another, the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle, and the interior angles on the same side equal to two right angles.

I.30.enunciation: Straight lines parallel to the same straight line are also parallel to one another.

I.31.enunciation: Through a given point to draw a straight line parallel to a given straight line.

I.32.enunciation: In any triangle, if one of the sides be produced, the exterior angle is equal to the two interior and opposite angles, and the three interior angles of the triangle are equal to two right angles.

I.34.enunciation: In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the diameter bisects the areas.

I.46.enunciation: On a given straight line to describe a square.

I.47.enunciation: In right-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the right angle is equal to the squares on the sides containing the right angle.

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Contain:
/-- The lengths `a` and `b` contain the area `x`: some rectangle `PQRS` has `PQ` equal
to `a`, `PS` equal to `b`, and is equal to `x`; or one of `a`, `b` is nothing, and so
is `x`. -/
def Contain (a b : Length) (x : Area) : Prop :=
  ((a = 0 ∨ b = 0) ∧ x = 0) ∨
    ∃ P Q R S : Point, Rectangle P Q R S ∧ ‖P Q‖ = a ∧ ‖P S‖ = b ∧ quadArea P Q R S = x
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ P ≠ A ∧ Collinear A B P ∧ ¬ Between P A B
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.Rectangle:
/-- **Definition II.1.** A rectangular parallelogram: the parallelogram `ABCD`, its
corners taken in order, with all four of its angles right. Euclid says "rectangular",
as Definition 22 says "right-angled" of the square. -/
def Rectangle (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  Parallelogram A B C D ∧ ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Square:
/-- **Definition 22.** "Of quadrilateral figures, a square is that which is both
equilateral and right-angled." The corners are `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, in order. -/
def Square (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  ‖A B‖ = ‖B C‖ ∧ ‖B C‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖C D‖ = ‖D A‖ ∧
    ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rect:
/-- **The rectangle contained by `AB`, `CD`** (Definition II.1): the area of any
rectangle whose sides about a right angle are equal to `AB` and `CD`. Lean chooses one
such area (`Classical.epsilon`); `Rectangle.contained` shows that every such
rectangle is equal to it. -/
noncomputable def rect (A B C D : Point) : Area :=
  Classical.epsilon (Contain ‖A B‖ ‖C D‖)
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle
definitions.sq:
/-- **The square on `AB`**: the rectangle contained by `AB`, `AB`, the area of any
square described on a straight line equal to `AB` (`Square.eq_sq`). -/
noncomputable def sq (A B : Point) : Area := rect A B A B

question.instructions:
Does every proposition called by the proof unit in `lean_proof` do work towards its conclusion or a substantive intermediate step of Euclid's argument? Also check for artificial hypothesis uses. Judge this unit's uses of the supplied helper signatures; helper bodies are outside this question. Heath's sentences stand as `--` lines and `cited` gives exact enunciations. In Lean, `have h : T := p` proves T by p and calls the result h; `obtain ⟨…⟩ := p` takes p apart into named pieces; `rw [h34, h37, …]` rewrites the goal by the equalities named. Follow uses through helper calls and tactics as well as explicit names. An anonymous binding or an unused hypothesis alone does not establish a defect. If both defects occur, choose `a dummy citation`.

docs/FORMALIZATION.md, section 5:
A checked intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid is legitimate, even if the
  final proof term could do without it.

criteria.an artificial hypothesis use: No dummy citation is established, but a hypothesis is mentioned only so that it looks used, and does no substantive work.
criteria.cannot tell: What is given here is not enough to decide.
criteria.all do work: Every proposition call supports a later step or the conclusion, or establishes a substantive intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid. No hypothesis is mentioned merely to look used. With no proposition calls the citation part alone is vacuous; hypothesis use must still be inspected.
criteria.a dummy citation: Some proposition call does no substantive work: its result neither supports the argument nor establishes a substantive intermediate fact, and merely supplies a citation while the step is done another way.

state.enunciation: If a straight line be cut into equal and unequal segments, the squares on the unequal segments of the whole are double of the square on the half and of the square on the straight line between the points of section.
state.lean_statement:
theorem Prop9 {A B C D : Point} (hACB : Between A C B) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖C B‖) (hADB : Between A D B)
    (hDC : D ≠ C) :
    sq A D + sq D B = sq A C + sq C D + (sq A C + sq C D)

statement.note: For D on either side of C: Euclid's figure puts D between C and B, and the other side follows by exchanging A and B.

bridges.Elements.Rectangle.congr:
/-- Rectangles contained by equal straight lines are equal: if the rectangles PQRS,
P'Q'R'S' have PQ equal to P'Q' and PS to P'S', they are equal. The diameter
QS cuts off the triangle SPQ, right-angled at P, which is half the rectangle
[I. 34]; and the two halves are equal [I. 4]. Euclid takes this for granted whenever
he names a rectangle by its sides. [I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Rectangle.congr (h : Rectangle P Q R S) (h' : Rectangle P' Q' R' S')
    (h₁ : ‖P Q‖ = ‖P' Q'‖) (h₂ : ‖P S‖ = ‖P' S'‖) :
    quadArea P Q R S = quadArea P' Q' R' S'
bridges.Elements.Rectangle.contained:
/-- **A rectangle is contained by its sides** (Definition II.1): the rectangle PQRS is
the rectangle contained by PQ, PS, the two straight lines containing its right
angle at P. `rect` chose some rectangle contained by straight lines equal to these,
and by `Rectangle.congr` the two are equal. [I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Rectangle.contained (h : Rectangle P Q R S) : quadArea P Q R S = rect P Q P S
bridges.Elements.Rectangle.eq_rect:
/-- Euclid's way of naming a rectangle: "BH is the rectangle A, BC, for it is contained
by GB, BC, and BG is equal to A" (II.1). If the sides PQ, PS of the rectangle
PQRS are equal to AB, CD, it is the rectangle contained by AB, CD.
[I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Rectangle.eq_rect (h : Rectangle P Q R S) (h₁ : ‖P Q‖ = ‖A B‖) (h₂ : ‖P S‖ = ‖C D‖) :
    quadArea P Q R S = rect A B C D
bridges.Elements.Square.described:
/-- The square ADEB that I.46 describes on AB, with D and E on the side of AB
where P is, is a parallelogram [I. 28], and it is the square on AB: "AE is the
square on AB" (II.2). [I. 4, I. 28, I. 34] -/
theorem Square.described (h : Square A D E B) (hD : SameSideOf D P A B)
    (hE : SameSideOf E P A B) : Parallelogram A D E B ∧ quadArea A D E B = sq A B
bridges.Elements.Square.eq_sq:
/-- A square is the square on its side: the square ABCD, a parallelogram, is the
square on AB. [I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Square.eq_sq (h : Square A B C D) (hp : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    quadArea A B C D = sq A B

Elements.Rectangle.congr: variable {A B C D E F G H K P Q R S P' Q' R' S' : Point}

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Contain:
/-- The lengths `a` and `b` contain the area `x`: some rectangle `PQRS` has `PQ` equal
to `a`, `PS` equal to `b`, and is equal to `x`; or one of `a`, `b` is nothing, and so
is `x`. -/
def Contain (a b : Length) (x : Area) : Prop :=
  ((a = 0 ∨ b = 0) ∧ x = 0) ∨
    ∃ P Q R S : Point, Rectangle P Q R S ∧ ‖P Q‖ = a ∧ ‖P S‖ = b ∧ quadArea P Q R S = x
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.Rectangle:
/-- **Definition II.1.** A rectangular parallelogram: the parallelogram `ABCD`, its
corners taken in order, with all four of its angles right. Euclid says "rectangular",
as Definition 22 says "right-angled" of the square. -/
def Rectangle (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  Parallelogram A B C D ∧ ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Square:
/-- **Definition 22.** "Of quadrilateral figures, a square is that which is both
equilateral and right-angled." The corners are `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, in order. -/
def Square (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  ‖A B‖ = ‖B C‖ ∧ ‖B C‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖C D‖ = ‖D A‖ ∧
    ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rect:
/-- **The rectangle contained by `AB`, `CD`** (Definition II.1): the area of any
rectangle whose sides about a right angle are equal to `AB` and `CD`. Lean chooses one
such area (`Classical.epsilon`); `Rectangle.contained` shows that every such
rectangle is equal to it. -/
noncomputable def rect (A B C D : Point) : Area :=
  Classical.epsilon (Contain ‖A B‖ ‖C D‖)
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle
definitions.sq:
/-- **The square on `AB`**: the rectangle contained by `AB`, `AB`, the area of any
square described on a straight line equal to `AB` (`Square.eq_sq`). -/
noncomputable def sq (A B : Point) : Area := rect A B A B
