state.enunciation: To construct a square equal to a given rectilineal figure.
state.heath_proof:
Let A be the given rectilineal figure;

thus it is required to construct a square equal to the rectilineal figure A.

For let there be constructed the rectangular parallelogram BD equal to the rectilineal figure A. [I. 45]

Then, if BE is equal to ED, that which was enjoined will have been done; for a square BD has been constructed equal to the rectilineal figure A.

But, if not, one of the straight lines BE, ED is greater.

Let BE be greater, and let it be produced to F;

let EF be made equal to ED, and let BF be bisected at G.

With centre G and distance one of the straight lines GB, GF let the semicircle BHF be described; let DE be produced to H, and let GH be joined.

Then, since the straight line BF has been cut into equal segments at G, and into unequal segments at E,

the rectangle contained by BE, EF together with the square on EG is equal to the square on GF. [II. 5]

But GF is equal to GH;

therefore the rectangle BE, EF together with the square on GE is equal to the square on GH.

But the squares on HE, EG are equal to the square on GH; [I. 47]

therefore the rectangle BE, EF together with the square on GE is equal to the squares on HE, EG.

Let the square on GE be subtracted from each;

therefore the rectangle contained by BE, EF which remains is equal to the square on EH.

But the rectangle BE, EF is BD, for EF is equal to ED;

therefore the parallelogram BD is equal to the square on HE.

And BD is equal to the rectilineal figure A.

Therefore the rectilineal figure A is also equal to the square which can be described on EH.

Therefore a square, namely that which can be described on EH, has been constructed equal to the given rectilineal figure A.

Q. E. F.
state.lean_proof:
/-- **II.14, for any rectilineal figure, with any boundaries** (companion of II.14). To
construct a square equal to a given rectilineal figure, given with any division of it into
triangles, no point inside two of them (`Apart`), as in `Prop45.apart`: the square on PQ is
equal to those triangles taken together (`Apart.area`). The figure may have a hole, touch
itself at a corner, or be in more than one piece. It is `Prop14.sum` for the figure's
triangles. Nothing is claimed of another division of the figure. -/
theorem Prop14.apart (R : Apart) : ∃ P Q : Point, sq P Q = R.area :=
  Prop14.sum R.pieces R.ne R.triangle

helper_signatures.Elements.Apart:
/-- **A rectilineal figure, given with triangles that lie apart** (Definition I.14: a figure
is "that which is contained by any boundary or boundaries"; Definition I.19: rectilineal
figures are "those which are contained by straight lines"): any division of it into
triangles, each named by its three corners, at least one; each a triangle; and no point
inside two of them. The figure is the triangles together. It may have a hole, as a square
with a smaller square cut from its middle has, may touch itself at a corner, and may be in
more than one piece. No order of the triangles is asked, and a triangle may lie against part
of a side of another. A figure given by gluing is one of these, its triangles lying apart by
`Fitted.inside_pairwise`. That every rectilineal figure, with any boundaries, can be cut
into triangles that lie apart is not stated in Lean. -/
structure Apart where
  /-- The triangles the figure is cut into. -/
  pieces : List (Point × Point × Point)
  /-- There is at least one. -/
  ne : pieces ≠ []
  /-- Each is a triangle: its corners are not on one straight line. -/
  triangle : ∀ t ∈ pieces, Triangle t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2
  /-- No point is inside two of them. -/
  apart : pieces.Pairwise fun s s' => ∀ Y : Point,
    InsideTriangle Y s.1 s.2.1 s.2.2 → ¬ InsideTriangle Y s'.1 s'.2.1 s'.2.2
helper_signatures.Elements.Apart.area:
/-- **The area of a figure given with triangles that lie apart, as given**: the sum of its
triangles. As with `Rectilineal.area`, that another division of the same figure gives the
same sum is not proved here (Book I's gap catalogue, under I.45), so this is the area of the
figure with its division, not yet a measure of the figure alone. -/
noncomputable def Apart.area (R : Apart) : Area
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.triangle:
/-- An end of one parallel is off the other: if AB is parallel to CD, then C
is not on the straight line AB, and ABC is a triangle. (Turned round with
`AreParallel.symm` and `.swap_right`, the same holds of D, and of A and B
beside CD.) -/
theorem AreParallel.triangle (h : AreParallel A B C D) : Triangle A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.BookII.Prop14.sum:
/-- **II.14, any number of triangles** (companion of II.14). To construct a square equal to
any number of given triangles taken together, at least one: a rectangle equal to them
[I. 45, `Prop45.sum`, in a right angle from I.11 at a corner A of the first triangle ABC, on
AB], then a square equal to the rectangle (`Prop14.rectangle`). The triangles are any
triangles; they need not fit together into one figure, and the statement claims nothing of
a figure. The square is the square on PQ. -/
theorem Prop14.sum (ts : List (Point × Point × Point)) (hne : ts ≠ [])
    (hts : ∀ t ∈ ts, Triangle t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2) :
    ∃ P Q : Point, sq P Q = Magnitude.sum (ts.map fun t => △ t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2)
helper_signatures.Elements.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.triangle:
/-- In the parallelogram ABCD, the corner C is off the straight line AB, so
ABC is a triangle. -/
theorem Parallelogram.triangle (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Triangle A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.triangle:
/-- A point on one side of the straight line AB is not on it, so ABP is a
triangle. -/
theorem SameSideOf.triangle (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : Triangle A B P

square described on a straight line equal to `AB` (`Square.eq_sq`). -/
noncomputable def sq (A B : Point) : Area

definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.Rectangle:
/-- **Definition II.1.** A rectangular parallelogram: the parallelogram `ABCD`, its
corners taken in order, with all four of its angles right. Euclid says "rectangular",
as Definition 22 says "right-angled" of the square. -/
def Rectangle (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  Parallelogram A B C D ∧ ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rect:
/-- **The rectangle contained by `AB`, `CD`** (Definition II.1): the area of any
rectangle whose sides about a right angle are equal to `AB` and `CD`. Lean chooses one
such area (`Classical.epsilon`); `Rectangle.contained` shows that every such
rectangle is equal to it. -/
noncomputable def rect (A B C D : Point) : Area :=
  Classical.epsilon (Contain ‖A B‖ ‖C D‖)
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle
definitions.sq:
/-- **The square on `AB`**: the rectangle contained by `AB`, `AB`, the area of any
square described on a straight line equal to `AB` (`Square.eq_sq`). -/
noncomputable def sq (A B : Point) : Area := rect A B A B

question.instructions:
Does every proposition called by the proof unit in `lean_proof` do work towards its conclusion or a substantive intermediate step of Euclid's argument? Also check for artificial hypothesis uses. Judge this unit's uses of the supplied helper signatures; helper bodies are outside this question. Heath's sentences stand as `--` lines and `cited` gives exact enunciations. In Lean, `have h : T := p` proves T by p and calls the result h; `obtain ⟨…⟩ := p` takes p apart into named pieces; `rw [h34, h37, …]` rewrites the goal by the equalities named. Follow uses through helper calls and tactics as well as explicit names. An anonymous binding or an unused hypothesis alone does not establish a defect. If both defects occur, choose `a dummy citation`.

docs/FORMALIZATION.md, section 5:
A checked intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid is legitimate, even if the
  final proof term could do without it.

criteria.all do work: Every proposition call supports a later step or the conclusion, or establishes a substantive intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid. No hypothesis is mentioned merely to look used. With no proposition calls the citation part alone is vacuous; hypothesis use must still be inspected.
criteria.a dummy citation: Some proposition call does no substantive work: its result neither supports the argument nor establishes a substantive intermediate fact, and merely supplies a citation while the step is done another way.
criteria.an artificial hypothesis use: No dummy citation is established, but a hypothesis is mentioned only so that it looks used, and does no substantive work.
criteria.cannot tell: What is given here is not enough to decide.

state.enunciation: To construct a square equal to a given rectilineal figure.
state.heath_proof:
Let A be the given rectilineal figure;

thus it is required to construct a square equal to the rectilineal figure A.

For let there be constructed the rectangular parallelogram BD equal to the rectilineal figure A. [I. 45]

Then, if BE is equal to ED, that which was enjoined will have been done; for a square BD has been constructed equal to the rectilineal figure A.

But, if not, one of the straight lines BE, ED is greater.

Let BE be greater, and let it be produced to F;

let EF be made equal to ED, and let BF be bisected at G.

With centre G and distance one of the straight lines GB, GF let the semicircle BHF be described; let DE be produced to H, and let GH be joined.

Then, since the straight line BF has been cut into equal segments at G, and into unequal segments at E,

the rectangle contained by BE, EF together with the square on EG is equal to the square on GF. [II. 5]

But GF is equal to GH;

therefore the rectangle BE, EF together with the square on GE is equal to the square on GH.

But the squares on HE, EG are equal to the square on GH; [I. 47]

therefore the rectangle BE, EF together with the square on GE is equal to the squares on HE, EG.

Let the square on GE be subtracted from each;

therefore the rectangle contained by BE, EF which remains is equal to the square on EH.

But the rectangle BE, EF is BD, for EF is equal to ED;

therefore the parallelogram BD is equal to the square on HE.

And BD is equal to the rectilineal figure A.

Therefore the rectilineal figure A is also equal to the square which can be described on EH.

Therefore a square, namely that which can be described on EH, has been constructed equal to the given rectilineal figure A.

Q. E. F.
state.lean_proof:
/-- **II.14, for a figure divided from one corner** (companion of II.14), as Euclid and
Oliver Byrne divide it. A figure with corners A₀, A₁, A₂, …, Aₙ, divided by the straight
lines from A₀ into the triangles A₀A₁A₂, …, A₀Aₙ₋₁Aₙ, with the division checked as in
`Prop45.fan`: each piece a triangle, each two neighbouring triangles on opposite sides of
the straight line A₀Aᵢ they share, and the angles at A₀ together less than four right
angles. Then those triangles, in that order, are fitted together into one figure
(`Fitted.fan`), and the square on PQ is equal to that figure, that is, to the triangles
taken together. The figure is read as the one with corners A₀, A₁, …, Aₙ in order round it
(that its boundary is that closed line is not stated in Lean). The square drawn is
`Prop14.square R.toApart`, for the glued figure `R` returned.

As in `Prop45.fan`, the first conclusion is what the two conditions are for; the square
alone would follow from each piece being a triangle, by `Prop14.sum`. -/
theorem Prop14.fan {A₀ A₁ A₂ : Point} {ps : List Point}
    (htri : ∀ s ∈ segments (A₁ :: A₂ :: ps), Triangle A₀ s.1 s.2)
    (hopp : ∀ t ∈ triples (A₁ :: A₂ :: ps), OppositeSidesOf t.1 t.2.2 A₀ t.2.1)
    (hA₀ : Magnitude.sum ((segments (A₁ :: A₂ :: ps)).map fun s => ∠ s.1 A₀ s.2) <
      ∟ + ∟ + (∟ + ∟)) :
    ∃ R : Rectilineal,
      R.pieces = (segments (A₁ :: A₂ :: ps)).map (fun s => (A₀, s.1, s.2)) ∧
      ∃ P Q : Point, sq P Q = R.area :=
  ⟨⟨_, Fitted.fan htri hopp hA₀⟩, rfl, Prop14.figure _⟩

helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop13:
/-- If a straight line set up on a straight line make angles, it will make either two right angles
or angles equal to two right angles. -/
theorem Prop13 {A B C D : Point} (hCBD : Between C B D) (hA : ¬ Collinear C D A) :
    ∠ C B A + ∠ A B D = ∟ + ∟
helper_signatures.Elements.BookII.Prop14.figure:
/-- **II.14, for any rectilineal figure with one boundary** (companion of II.14). To
construct a square equal to a given rectilineal figure, given with triangles fitted together
in a suitable order, each glued across a side of an earlier one and meeting the earlier ones
only along it (`Rectilineal`), as in `Prop45.figure`: the square on PQ is equal to those
triangles taken together (`Rectilineal.area`). It is `Prop14.apart` for the figure's
triangles, which lie apart (`Fitted.inside_pairwise`, `Rectilineal.toApart`). Nothing is
claimed of another division of the figure. -/
theorem Prop14.figure (R : Rectilineal) : ∃ P Q : Point, sq P Q = R.area
helper_signatures.Elements.Fitted.fan:
/-- **Euclid's and Oliver Byrne's division is a figure, when it is checked.** A figure given
by its corners A₀, A₁, A₂, …, Aₙ, the list `ps` being A₃, …, Aₙ, and divided by the straight
lines from A₀ into the triangles A₀A₁A₂, A₀A₂A₃, …, A₀Aₙ₋₁Aₙ, one on each side
`segments (A₁ :: A₂ :: ps)`. Suppose each is a triangle; each two neighbouring triangles,
A₀Aᵢ₋₁Aᵢ and A₀AᵢAᵢ₊₁, lie on opposite sides of the straight line A₀Aᵢ they share, that is,
Aᵢ₋₁ and Aᵢ₊₁ are on opposite sides of it (one condition for each of
`triples (A₁ :: A₂ :: ps)`); and the angles A₁A₀A₂, A₂A₀A₃, …, Aₙ₋₁A₀Aₙ at A₀ together are
less than four right angles. Then those triangles, in that order, are fitted together into
one figure: each is laid across the straight line A₀Aᵢ against the one before it, and meets
the earlier ones only along that straight line. The figure they make is read as the figure
with corners A₀, A₁, …, Aₙ in order round it; that its boundary is the closed line A₀A₁…AₙA₀
is not stated in Lean.

The two conditions are what make the triangles turn one way round A₀ and not come round on
themselves, so that they do not overlap. Euclid's ABCD, divided from D by DB, is the figure
with corners D, A, B, C: A and C are on opposite sides of DB, and the two angles at D,
each less than two right angles, are together less than four. -/
theorem Fitted.fan {A₀ A₁ A₂ : Point} {ps : List Point}
    (htri : ∀ s ∈ segments (A₁ :: A₂ :: ps), Triangle A₀ s.1 s.2)
    (hopp : ∀ t ∈ triples (A₁ :: A₂ :: ps), OppositeSidesOf t.1 t.2.2 A₀ t.2.1)
    (hA₀ : Magnitude.sum ((segments (A₁ :: A₂ :: ps)).map fun s => ∠ s.1 A₀ s.2) <
      ∟ + ∟ + (∟ + ∟)) :
    Fitted ((segments (A₁ :: A₂ :: ps)).map fun s => (A₀, s.1, s.2))
helper_signatures.Elements.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
helper_signatures.Elements.Magnitude.sum:
/-- **The sum of a list of magnitudes** of one kind: nothing for the empty list, and
otherwise the first added to the sum of the rest. So `Magnitude.sum [a, b, c]` is
`a + (b + (c + 0))`, which is `a + b + c`. -/
noncomputable def Magnitude.sum {k : Kind} : List (Magnitude k) → Magnitude k
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf:
/-- `P` and `Q` lie on opposite sides of the straight line `AB`. -/
def OppositeSidesOf (P Q A B : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Rectilineal:
/-- **A rectilineal figure with one boundary, given with its triangles fitted together**
(Definition I.19: "Rectilineal figures are those which are contained by straight lines"):
the triangles it is cut into, each named by its three corners, in an order in which they
fit together, with the proof that they do. The figure is the triangles together. -/
structure Rectilineal where
  /-- The triangles the figure is cut into, in the order they were fitted. -/
  pieces : List (Point × Point × Point)
  /-- They fit together into one figure. -/
  fitted : Fitted pieces
helper_signatures.Elements.Rectilineal.area:
/-- **The area of a rectilineal figure, as given**: the sum of the triangles it is given
with, which do not overlap (`Fitted.inside_pairwise`) and make up the figure. That another
division of the same figure gives the same sum is not proved here (Book I's gap catalogue,
under I.45), so this is the area of the figure with its division, not yet a measure of the
figure alone. -/
noncomputable def Rectilineal.area (R : Rectilineal) : Area
helper_signatures.Elements.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.segments:
/-- **The segments** of a straight line cut at points in order: each point of the list with
the next, as the ends of one segment. The segments of `[B, D, E, C]` are BD, DE and EC. The
points need not be in order, or on one straight line: in the companions of I.45 and II.14
for a checked fan (`Prop45.fan`, `Prop14.fan`), the segments of a figure's corners A₁, A₂,
…, Aₙ are its sides A₁A₂, …, Aₙ₋₁Aₙ, those away from the corner A₀, and each side with A₀
makes one of the triangles into which the straight lines from A₀ divide the figure, when the
fan's conditions hold. -/
def segments : List Point → List (Point × Point)
helper_signatures.Elements.sq:
/-- **The square on `AB`**: the rectangle contained by `AB`, `AB`, the area of any
square described on a straight line equal to `AB` (`Square.eq_sq`). -/
noncomputable def sq (A B : Point) : Area
helper_signatures.Elements.triples:
/-- **The corners three at a time**: each corner of the list with the next two. The triples
of `[A₁, A₂, A₃, A₄]` are A₁A₂A₃ and A₂A₃A₄. In a division from one corner A₀, the middle
corner of each triple is the far end of the straight line A₀Aᵢ that two neighbouring
triangles share, and the other two are their third corners. -/
def triples : List Point → List (Point × Point × Point)

I.13.enunciation: If a straight line set up on a straight line make angles, it will make either two right angles or angles equal to two right angles.

I.45.enunciation: To construct, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given rectilineal figure.

I.47.enunciation: In right-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the right angle is equal to the squares on the sides containing the right angle.

II.5.enunciation: If a straight line be cut into equal and unequal segments, the rectangle contained by the unequal segments of the whole together with the square on the straight line between the points of section is equal to the square on the half.

II.14 figure.enunciation: To construct a square equal to a given rectilineal figure.

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Contain:
/-- The lengths `a` and `b` contain the area `x`: some rectangle `PQRS` has `PQ` equal
to `a`, `PS` equal to `b`, and is equal to `x`; or one of `a`, `b` is nothing, and so
is `x`. -/
def Contain (a b : Length) (x : Area) : Prop :=
  ((a = 0 ∨ b = 0) ∧ x = 0) ∨
    ∃ P Q R S : Point, Rectangle P Q R S ∧ ‖P Q‖ = a ∧ ‖P S‖ = b ∧ quadArea P Q R S = x
definitions.Corners:
/-- The triangle `t` has the corners `P`, `Q`, `R`: read from some corner, one way round or
the other, it is `(P, Q, R)`. So `PQ` is one of its sides, and `R` the corner opposite. -/
def Corners (t : Point × Point × Point) (P Q R : Point) : Prop :=
  t = (P, Q, R) ∨ t = (Q, R, P) ∨ t = (R, P, Q) ∨ t = (Q, P, R) ∨ t = (P, R, Q) ∨
    t = (R, Q, P)
definitions.Fitted:
/-- **Triangles fitted together into one rectilineal figure**, in the order listed.

* `single`: one triangle is a figure.
* `glue`: a figure, with a new triangle `PQX` laid against the side `PQ` of one of its
  triangles `t`, whose third corner is `R`. The new triangle lies across that side, `X` being
  on the other side of `PQ` from `R`; and it meets the triangles already there only along
  `PQ`: a point within or on the new triangle, and within or on one of the earlier ones,
  lies on the finite straight line `PQ`.

The new triangle goes at the end of the list. A figure made this way may be convex or not.
Every figure made this way is bounded by one closed line that neither crosses nor touches
itself, with no hole; and every such figure can be cut this way, since it can be cut into
triangles by straight lines joining its corners, and those triangles, listed so that each
after the first shares a side with one before it, with each later triangle named so that
its attached side is its first two corners, satisfy the rule: a later triangle meets an
earlier one that is not its neighbour only at an end of the side it is glued along.
Neither fact is stated in Lean. That no point is inside two of the triangles is stated, and
proved (`Fitted.inside_pairwise`). So every such figure has a division that is fitted, but
not every division of it is: a ring of triangles round a point inside it is not (below),
nor is a list whose later triangle is named from the wrong corner, as the square ABCD cut
along AC and listed ABC, ADC (the second must be named with AC as its first two corners,
ACD or CAD).

A ring of triangles closing up round a point, or round a hole, is not made this way, for its
last triangle would meet the others along two sides. A triangle laid against part of a
side, or against two sides in line, is not glued this way either; its figure is cut
differently. A figure with a hole cannot be cut so as to be glued. Any division of any
figure, with a hole or without, is taken given with triangles that lie apart (`Apart`), and
a fitted figure's triangles lie apart too. -/
inductive Fitted : List (Point × Point × Point) → Prop
  | single {A B C : Point} (h : Triangle A B C) : Fitted [(A, B, C)]
  | glue {ps : List (Point × Point × Point)} {t : Point × Point × Point} {P Q R X : Point}
      (hps : Fitted ps) (ht : t ∈ ps) (hside : Corners t P Q R)
      (hX : OppositeSidesOf X R P Q)
      (hmeet : ∀ Y : Point, OnOrInsideTriangle Y P Q X →
        ∀ s ∈ ps, OnOrInsideTriangle Y s.1 s.2.1 s.2.2 → OnFiniteLine Y P Q) :
      Fitted (ps ++ [(P, Q, X)])
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.Magnitude.sum:
/-- **The sum of a list of magnitudes** of one kind: nothing for the empty list, and
otherwise the first added to the sum of the rest. So `Magnitude.sum [a, b, c]` is
`a + (b + (c + 0))`, which is `a + b + c`. -/
noncomputable def Magnitude.sum {k : Kind} : List (Magnitude k) → Magnitude k
  | [] => 0
  | a :: as => a + Magnitude.sum as
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnFiniteLine:
/-- `Y` lies on the finite straight line `PQ`: it is one of the ends, or between them. -/
def OnFiniteLine (Y P Q : Point) : Prop := Y = P ∨ Y = Q ∨ Between P Y Q
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.OnOrInsideTriangle:
/-- `Y` lies within the triangle `ABC` or on its boundary: inside it, on one of its sides
between two corners, or at a corner. -/
def OnOrInsideTriangle (Y A B C : Point) : Prop :=
  InsideTriangle Y A B C ∨ Between A Y B ∨ Between B Y C ∨ Between C Y A ∨
    Y = A ∨ Y = B ∨ Y = C
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.Rectangle:
/-- **Definition II.1.** A rectangular parallelogram: the parallelogram `ABCD`, its
corners taken in order, with all four of its angles right. Euclid says "rectangular",
as Definition 22 says "right-angled" of the square. -/
def Rectangle (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  Parallelogram A B C D ∧ ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.Rectilineal:
/-- **A rectilineal figure with one boundary, given with its triangles fitted together**
(Definition I.19: "Rectilineal figures are those which are contained by straight lines"):
the triangles it is cut into, each named by its three corners, in an order in which they
fit together, with the proof that they do. The figure is the triangles together. -/
structure Rectilineal where
  /-- The triangles the figure is cut into, in the order they were fitted. -/
  pieces : List (Point × Point × Point)
  /-- They fit together into one figure. -/
  fitted : Fitted pieces
definitions.Rectilineal.area:
/-- **The area of a rectilineal figure, as given**: the sum of the triangles it is given
with, which do not overlap (`Fitted.inside_pairwise`) and make up the figure. That another
division of the same figure gives the same sum is not proved here (Book I's gap catalogue,
under I.45), so this is the area of the figure with its division, not yet a measure of the
figure alone. -/
noncomputable def Rectilineal.area (R : Rectilineal) : Area :=
  Magnitude.sum (R.pieces.map fun t => △ t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2)
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rect:
/-- **The rectangle contained by `AB`, `CD`** (Definition II.1): the area of any
rectangle whose sides about a right angle are equal to `AB` and `CD`. Lean chooses one
such area (`Classical.epsilon`); `Rectangle.contained` shows that every such
rectangle is equal to it. -/
noncomputable def rect (A B C D : Point) : Area :=
  Classical.epsilon (Contain ‖A B‖ ‖C D‖)
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle
definitions.segments:
/-- **The segments** of a straight line cut at points in order: each point of the list with
the next, as the ends of one segment. The segments of `[B, D, E, C]` are BD, DE and EC. The
points need not be in order, or on one straight line: in the companions of I.45 and II.14
for a checked fan (`Prop45.fan`, `Prop14.fan`), the segments of a figure's corners A₁, A₂,
…, Aₙ are its sides A₁A₂, …, Aₙ₋₁Aₙ, those away from the corner A₀, and each side with A₀

state.enunciation: To construct a square equal to a given rectilineal figure.
state.heath_proof:
Let A be the given rectilineal figure;

thus it is required to construct a square equal to the rectilineal figure A.

For let there be constructed the rectangular parallelogram BD equal to the rectilineal figure A. [I. 45]

Then, if BE is equal to ED, that which was enjoined will have been done; for a square BD has been constructed equal to the rectilineal figure A.

But, if not, one of the straight lines BE, ED is greater.

Let BE be greater, and let it be produced to F;

let EF be made equal to ED, and let BF be bisected at G.

With centre G and distance one of the straight lines GB, GF let the semicircle BHF be described; let DE be produced to H, and let GH be joined.

Then, since the straight line BF has been cut into equal segments at G, and into unequal segments at E,

the rectangle contained by BE, EF together with the square on EG is equal to the square on GF. [II. 5]

But GF is equal to GH;

therefore the rectangle BE, EF together with the square on GE is equal to the square on GH.

But the squares on HE, EG are equal to the square on GH; [I. 47]

therefore the rectangle BE, EF together with the square on GE is equal to the squares on HE, EG.

Let the square on GE be subtracted from each;

therefore the rectangle contained by BE, EF which remains is equal to the square on EH.

But the rectangle BE, EF is BD, for EF is equal to ED;

therefore the parallelogram BD is equal to the square on HE.

And BD is equal to the rectilineal figure A.

Therefore the rectilineal figure A is also equal to the square which can be described on EH.

Therefore a square, namely that which can be described on EH, has been constructed equal to the given rectilineal figure A.

Q. E. F.

definitions.Apart:
/-- **A rectilineal figure, given with triangles that lie apart** (Definition I.14: a figure
is "that which is contained by any boundary or boundaries"; Definition I.19: rectilineal
figures are "those which are contained by straight lines"): any division of it into
triangles, each named by its three corners, at least one; each a triangle; and no point
inside two of them. The figure is the triangles together. It may have a hole, as a square
with a smaller square cut from its middle has, may touch itself at a corner, and may be in
more than one piece. No order of the triangles is asked, and a triangle may lie against part
of a side of another. A figure given by gluing is one of these, its triangles lying apart by
`Fitted.inside_pairwise`. That every rectilineal figure, with any boundaries, can be cut
into triangles that lie apart is not stated in Lean. -/
structure Apart where
  /-- The triangles the figure is cut into. -/
  pieces : List (Point × Point × Point)
  /-- There is at least one. -/
  ne : pieces ≠ []
  /-- Each is a triangle: its corners are not on one straight line. -/
  triangle : ∀ t ∈ pieces, Triangle t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2
  /-- No point is inside two of them. -/
  apart : pieces.Pairwise fun s s' => ∀ Y : Point,
    InsideTriangle Y s.1 s.2.1 s.2.2 → ¬ InsideTriangle Y s'.1 s'.2.1 s'.2.2
definitions.Apart.area:
/-- **The area of a figure given with triangles that lie apart, as given**: the sum of its
triangles. As with `Rectilineal.area`, that another division of the same figure gives the
same sum is not proved here (Book I's gap catalogue, under I.45), so this is the area of the
figure with its division, not yet a measure of the figure alone. -/
noncomputable def Apart.area (R : Apart) : Area :=
  Magnitude.sum (R.pieces.map fun t => △ t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2)
definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Contain:
/-- The lengths `a` and `b` contain the area `x`: some rectangle `PQRS` has `PQ` equal
to `a`, `PS` equal to `b`, and is equal to `x`; or one of `a`, `b` is nothing, and so
is `x`. -/
def Contain (a b : Length) (x : Area) : Prop :=
  ((a = 0 ∨ b = 0) ∧ x = 0) ∨
    ∃ P Q R S : Point, Rectangle P Q R S ∧ ‖P Q‖ = a ∧ ‖P S‖ = b ∧ quadArea P Q R S = x
definitions.Corners:
/-- The triangle `t` has the corners `P`, `Q`, `R`: read from some corner, one way round or
the other, it is `(P, Q, R)`. So `PQ` is one of its sides, and `R` the corner opposite. -/
def Corners (t : Point × Point × Point) (P Q R : Point) : Prop :=
  t = (P, Q, R) ∨ t = (Q, R, P) ∨ t = (R, P, Q) ∨ t = (Q, P, R) ∨ t = (P, R, Q) ∨
    t = (R, Q, P)
definitions.Fitted:
/-- **Triangles fitted together into one rectilineal figure**, in the order listed.

* `single`: one triangle is a figure.
* `glue`: a figure, with a new triangle `PQX` laid against the side `PQ` of one of its
  triangles `t`, whose third corner is `R`. The new triangle lies across that side, `X` being
  on the other side of `PQ` from `R`; and it meets the triangles already there only along
  `PQ`: a point within or on the new triangle, and within or on one of the earlier ones,
  lies on the finite straight line `PQ`.

The new triangle goes at the end of the list. A figure made this way may be convex or not.
Every figure made this way is bounded by one closed line that neither crosses nor touches
itself, with no hole; and every such figure can be cut this way, since it can be cut into
triangles by straight lines joining its corners, and those triangles, listed so that each
after the first shares a side with one before it, with each later triangle named so that
its attached side is its first two corners, satisfy the rule: a later triangle meets an
earlier one that is not its neighbour only at an end of the side it is glued along.
Neither fact is stated in Lean. That no point is inside two of the triangles is stated, and
proved (`Fitted.inside_pairwise`). So every such figure has a division that is fitted, but
not every division of it is: a ring of triangles round a point inside it is not (below),
nor is a list whose later triangle is named from the wrong corner, as the square ABCD cut
along AC and listed ABC, ADC (the second must be named with AC as its first two corners,
ACD or CAD).

A ring of triangles closing up round a point, or round a hole, is not made this way, for its
last triangle would meet the others along two sides. A triangle laid against part of a
side, or against two sides in line, is not glued this way either; its figure is cut
differently. A figure with a hole cannot be cut so as to be glued. Any division of any
figure, with a hole or without, is taken given with triangles that lie apart (`Apart`), and
a fitted figure's triangles lie apart too. -/
inductive Fitted : List (Point × Point × Point) → Prop
  | single {A B C : Point} (h : Triangle A B C) : Fitted [(A, B, C)]
  | glue {ps : List (Point × Point × Point)} {t : Point × Point × Point} {P Q R X : Point}
      (hps : Fitted ps) (ht : t ∈ ps) (hside : Corners t P Q R)
      (hX : OppositeSidesOf X R P Q)
      (hmeet : ∀ Y : Point, OnOrInsideTriangle Y P Q X →
        ∀ s ∈ ps, OnOrInsideTriangle Y s.1 s.2.1 s.2.2 → OnFiniteLine Y P Q) :
      Fitted (ps ++ [(P, Q, X)])
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.Magnitude.sum:
/-- **The sum of a list of magnitudes** of one kind: nothing for the empty list, and
otherwise the first added to the sum of the rest. So `Magnitude.sum [a, b, c]` is
`a + (b + (c + 0))`, which is `a + b + c`. -/
noncomputable def Magnitude.sum {k : Kind} : List (Magnitude k) → Magnitude k
  | [] => 0
  | a :: as => a + Magnitude.sum as
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnFiniteLine:
/-- `Y` lies on the finite straight line `PQ`: it is one of the ends, or between them. -/
def OnFiniteLine (Y P Q : Point) : Prop := Y = P ∨ Y = Q ∨ Between P Y Q
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.OnOrInsideTriangle:
/-- `Y` lies within the triangle `ABC` or on its boundary: inside it, on one of its sides
between two corners, or at a corner. -/
def OnOrInsideTriangle (Y A B C : Point) : Prop :=
  InsideTriangle Y A B C ∨ Between A Y B ∨ Between B Y C ∨ Between C Y A ∨
    Y = A ∨ Y = B ∨ Y = C
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.Rectangle:
/-- **Definition II.1.** A rectangular parallelogram: the parallelogram `ABCD`, its
corners taken in order, with all four of its angles right. Euclid says "rectangular",
as Definition 22 says "right-angled" of the square. -/
def Rectangle (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  Parallelogram A B C D ∧ ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.Rectilineal:
/-- **A rectilineal figure with one boundary, given with its triangles fitted together**
(Definition I.19: "Rectilineal figures are those which are contained by straight lines"):
the triangles it is cut into, each named by its three corners, in an order in which they
fit together, with the proof that they do. The figure is the triangles together. -/
structure Rectilineal where
  /-- The triangles the figure is cut into, in the order they were fitted. -/
  pieces : List (Point × Point × Point)
  /-- They fit together into one figure. -/
  fitted : Fitted pieces
definitions.Rectilineal.area:
/-- **The area of a rectilineal figure, as given**: the sum of the triangles it is given
with, which do not overlap (`Fitted.inside_pairwise`) and make up the figure. That another
division of the same figure gives the same sum is not proved here (Book I's gap catalogue,
under I.45), so this is the area of the figure with its division, not yet a measure of the
figure alone. -/
noncomputable def Rectilineal.area (R : Rectilineal) : Area :=
  Magnitude.sum (R.pieces.map fun t => △ t.1 t.2.1 t.2.2)
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rect:
/-- **The rectangle contained by `AB`, `CD`** (Definition II.1): the area of any
rectangle whose sides about a right angle are equal to `AB` and `CD`. Lean chooses one
such area (`Classical.epsilon`); `Rectangle.contained` shows that every such
rectangle is equal to it. -/
noncomputable def rect (A B C D : Point) : Area :=
  Classical.epsilon (Contain ‖A B‖ ‖C D‖)
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle
definitions.sq:
/-- **The square on `AB`**: the rectangle contained by `AB`, `AB`, the area of any
square described on a straight line equal to `AB` (`Square.eq_sq`). -/
noncomputable def sq (A B : Point) : Area := rect A B A B

state.lean_proof:
/-- **II.14, for a rectangle** (companion of II.14). To construct a square equal to a given
rectangle EBCD: the second part of Euclid's proof, with both of its cases. If BE is equal to
ED, the rectangle is a square already. If not, the greater, say BE, is produced to F with EF
equal to ED, BF is bisected at G, the semicircle BHF is described with centre G, and DE is
produced to H; then the rectangle BE, EF with the square on EG is the square on GF [II. 5],
which is the squares on HE, EG [I. 47], and the rectangle is the square on EH. This is
the proof of `Prop14` after the rectangle is made, written out again, for it does not cite
II.14. The square is the square on PQ. -/
theorem Prop14.rectangle {E B C D : Point} (h : Rectangle E B C D) :
    ∃ P Q : Point, sq P Q = quadArea E B C D := by
  /- If BE equals ED, the rectangle is already the square on EB. -/
  by_cases heq : ‖B E‖ = ‖E D‖
  · exact ⟨E, B, (h.eq_rect rfl ((len_symm E B).trans heq).symm).symm⟩
  /- Otherwise one side is greater. -/
  have hlt : ‖E D‖ < ‖E B‖ ∨ ‖E B‖ < ‖E D‖ := by
    rcases lt_trichotomy ‖E D‖ ‖E B‖ with h' | h' | h'
    · exact Or.inl h'
    · exact False.elim (heq ((len_symm B E).trans h'.symm))
    · exact Or.inr h'
  /- Euclid's figure has BE greater. The same construction serves when ED is
     greater, by reading the rectangle the other way round. -/
  have greater : ∀ {E B C D : Point}, Rectangle E B C D → ‖E D‖ < ‖E B‖ →
      ∃ P Q : Point, sq P Q = quadArea E B C D := by
    intro E B C D h hlt
    /- Produce BE beyond E, and take EF equal to ED on that ray. -/
    have hEB : E ≠ B := h.1.1.1
    have hDE : D ≠ E := h.1.2.2.1
    obtain ⟨X, hBEX⟩ := produce hEB.symm
    obtain ⟨F, hF, hEF⟩ :=
      OnRay.exists_len_eq hDE.symm (ne_of_between (between_symm hBEX)).symm
    have hBEF : Between B E F := hF.between hBEX
    /- Bisect BF at G [I. 10]. -/
    obtain ⟨G, hBGF, hBG⟩ := BookI.Prop10 (ne_of_between_ends hBEF)
    /- Describe the circle with centre G through B (Postulate 3); it passes
       through F too, since GF equals GB. -/
    obtain ⟨BHF, hG_BHF, hB_BHF⟩ := Postulate3 G B (ne_of_between hBGF).symm
    have hF_BHF : OnCircle F BHF :=
      on_circle_of_len_eq hG_BHF hB_BHF (by rw [← hBG, len_symm G B])
    /- G lies between B and E: the half BG of BF is less than BE, since BE is
       greater than the remaining part EF. Thus E is the unequal cut of BF that
       II.5 needs, distinct from the midpoint G. -/
    have hlt' : ‖E F‖ < ‖B E‖ := by rw [hEF, len_symm B E]; exact hlt
    have hBGE : Between B G E := by
      have hBF : ‖B F‖ = ‖B G‖ + ‖B G‖ := by
        rw [← len_add_of_between hBGF, ← hBG]
      have hBF' : ‖B F‖ = ‖B E‖ + ‖E F‖ := (len_add_of_between hBEF).symm
      refine OnRay.between_of_len_lt (OnRay.of_between hBGF) (OnRay.of_between hBEF) ?_
      rcases lt_trichotomy ‖B G‖ ‖B E‖ with h' | h' | h'
      · exact h'
      · exfalso
        rw [h', hBF'] at hBF
        have : ‖E F‖ = ‖B E‖ := CommonNotion3 (by rw [add_comm]; exact hBF) rfl
        exact lt_irrefl _ (this ▸ hlt')
      · exfalso
        have := Magnitude.add_self_lt_add_self h'
        rw [← hBF, hBF'] at this
        exact lt_irrefl _ (lt_trans hlt' (Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_left this))
    have hEG : E ≠ G := ne_of_between (between_symm hBGE)
    /- E is inside the circle: it lies between the centre G and F
       (Definition I.15). -/
    have hE_BHF : InsideCircle E BHF :=
      InsideCircle.of_between_centre hG_BHF hF_BHF (between_inner hBGE hBEF)
    /- Produce DE to H beyond E, on the semicircle BHF away from the rectangle. -/
    obtain ⟨DE, hD_DE, hE_DE⟩ := Postulate1 D E hDE
    obtain ⟨H, hH_BHF, hH_DE, hHED⟩ := line_circle_beyond hE_BHF hE_DE hD_DE hDE
    /- BF is cut equally at G and unequally at E: the rectangle BE, EF with the
       square on GE equals the square on GF [II. 5]. -/
    have h5 : rect B E E F + sq G E = sq G F := Prop5 hBGF hBG hBEF hEG
    /- GF and GH are radii of the same circle (Definition I.15), so the same sum
       equals the square on GH. -/
    have hGF_GH : ‖G F‖ = ‖G H‖ := Definition15 hG_BHF hF_BHF hH_BHF
    have hsum : rect B E E F + sq G E = sq G H := h5.trans (sq_congr hGF_GH)
    /- H is off BF: otherwise the straight line through H and E would be BF, and
       D on it, contrary to the rectangle's triangle DEB. So HEG is a triangle,
       with GH as its third side. -/
    obtain ⟨BF, hB_BF, hF_BF⟩ := Postulate1 B F (ne_of_between_ends hBEF)
    have hE_BF : OnLine E BF := on_line_of_between_ends hBEF hB_BF hF_BF
    have hG_BF : OnLine G BF := on_line_of_between_ends hBGF hB_BF hF_BF
    have hDEB : Triangle D E B := h.1.rotate.rotate.rotate.triangle
    have hD_BF : ¬ OnLine D BF := hDEB.bca.off_line hE_BF hB_BF
    have hHE : H ≠ E := ne_of_between hHED
    have hH_BF : ¬ OnLine H BF := fun hH =>
      hD_BF ((line_unique hHE hH_DE hE_DE hH hE_BF) ▸ hD_DE)
    /- HEG is right: HEB is adjacent to the rectangle's right angle DEB,
       and G lies on the ray EB. -/
    have hBEH : ∠ B E H = ∟ := by
      rw [← adjacent_eq_of_right hD_DE hH_DE (between_symm hHED)
        (hDEB.off_line hD_DE hE_DE) h.2.1]
      exact h.2.1
    have hHEG : ∠ H E G = ∟ := by
      rw [angle_symm hHE (Ne.symm hEG),
        angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between (between_symm hBGE)) hHE]
      exact hBEH
    /- The squares on HE and EG equal the square on GH [I. 47]. Thus they
       equal the rectangle BE, EF together with the square on GE. -/
    have h47 := BookI.Prop47.sq (Triangle.of_line hE_BF hG_BF hEG hH_BF).acb hHEG
    have hequal : rect B E E F + sq G E = sq H E + sq E G :=
      hsum.trans ((sq_symm G H).trans h47)
    /- Subtract the square on GE from each: the rectangle BE, EF is the square
       on HE, hence on EH (Common Notion 3). -/
    have hrem : rect B E E F = sq H E := CommonNotion3 hequal (sq_symm G E)
    have hEH : rect B E E F = sq E H := hrem.trans (sq_symm H E)
    /- EF equals ED, so the rectangle BE, EF is the given rectangle EBCD. -/
    have hrectangle : quadArea E B C D = rect B E E F :=
      h.eq_rect (len_symm E B) hEF.symm
    exact ⟨E, H, (hrectangle.trans hEH).symm⟩
  rcases hlt with hlt | hlt
  · exact greater h hlt
  · obtain ⟨P, Q, hPQ⟩ := greater h.reverse hlt
    exact ⟨P, Q, hPQ.trans (quadArea_reverse E B C D)⟩

helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.symm:
/-- If AB is parallel to CD, then CD is parallel to AB. -/
theorem AreParallel.symm (h : AreParallel A B C D) : AreParallel C D A B
helper_signatures.Elements.AreParallel.triangle:
/-- An end of one parallel is off the other: if AB is parallel to CD, then C
is not on the straight line AB, and ABC is a triangle. (Turned round with
`AreParallel.symm` and `.swap_right`, the same holds of D, and of A and B
beside CD.) -/
theorem AreParallel.triangle (h : AreParallel A B C D) : Triangle A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop10:
/-- To bisect a given finite straight line. -/
theorem Prop10 {A B : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) :
    ∃ D : Point, Between A D B ∧ ‖A D‖ = ‖D B‖
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop28:
/-- If a straight line falling on two straight lines make the exterior angle equal to the interior
and opposite angle on the same side, or the interior angles on the same side equal to two right
angles, the straight lines will be parallel to one another. -/
theorem Prop28 {A B C D E F G H : Point} (hAGB : Between A G B) (hCHD : Between C H D)
    (hEGH : Between E G H) (hGHF : Between G H F) (hBD : SameSideOf B D E F)
    (h : ∠ E G B = ∠ G H D ∨ ∠ B G H + ∠ G H D = ∟ + ∟) :
    AreParallel A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop34:
/-- In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the
diameter bisects the areas. -/
theorem Prop34 {A B C D : Point} (h : Parallelogram A C D B) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖B D‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ C D B ∧ ∠ A B D = ∠ A C D ∧
      △ A B C = △ D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop4:
/-- If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles
contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the base, the
triangle will be equal to the triangle, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining
angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend. -/
theorem Prop4 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖D F‖) (hA : ∠ B A C = ∠ E D F) :
    ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ ∧ △ A B C = △ D E F ∧ ∠ A B C = ∠ D E F ∧ ∠ A C B = ∠ D F E
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop46:
/-- On a given straight line to describe a square. -/
theorem Prop46 {A B P : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hP : ¬ Collinear A B P) :
    ∃ D E : Point, Square A D E B ∧ SameSideOf D P A B ∧ SameSideOf E P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop47:
/-- In right-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the right angle is equal to the
squares on the sides containing the right angle. -/
theorem Prop47 {A B C D E F G H K : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hright : ∠ B A C = ∟)
    (hBDEC : Square B D E C) (hD : OppositeSidesOf D A B C) (hE : OppositeSidesOf E A B C)
    (hABFG : Square A B F G) (hF : OppositeSidesOf F C A B) (hG : OppositeSidesOf G C A B)
    (hACKH : Square A C K H) (hK : OppositeSidesOf K B A C) (hH : OppositeSidesOf H B A C) :
    quadArea B D E C = quadArea A B F G + quadArea A C K H
helper_signatures.Elements.BookI.Prop47.sq:
/-- **I.47 for the squares on straight lines.** In the triangle ABC right-angled at
A, the square on BC is equal to the squares on BA, AC. Book II cites I.47 in
this form: "the square on EA is equal to the squares on AC, CE, for the angle ACE is
right" (II.9). The three squares are described outward [I. 46], I.47 compares them,
and each is the square on its side (`Square.described`).
[I. 4, I. 28, I. 34, I. 46, I. 47] -/
theorem BookI.Prop47.sq (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hright : ∠ B A C = ∟) :
    sq B C = sq B A + sq A C
helper_signatures.Elements.BookII.Prop5:
/-- If a straight line be cut into equal and unequal segments, the rectangle contained by the
unequal segments of the whole together with the square on the straight line between the points
of section is equal to the square on the half. -/
theorem Prop5 {A B C D : Point} (hACB : Between A C B) (hAC : ‖A C‖ = ‖C B‖) (hADB : Between A D B)
    (hDC : D ≠ C) :
    rect A D D B + sq C D = sq C B
helper_signatures.Elements.CommonNotion3:
/-- **Common Notion 3.** If equals be subtracted from equals, the remainders
are equal. (From `a + c = b + d` and `c = d`, conclude `a = b`.) -/
theorem CommonNotion3 {a b c d : Magnitude k} (h₁ : a + c = b + d) (h₂ : c = d) :
    a = b
helper_signatures.Elements.Contain.symm:
/-- Read either way round, two lengths contain the same areas: the rectangle PQRS
read as PSRQ has its sides about the angle at P in the other order. -/
theorem Contain.symm (h : Contain a b x) : Contain b a x
helper_signatures.Elements.Definition15:
/-- **Definition 15.** "A circle is a plane figure contained by one line such
that all the straight lines falling upon it from one point among those lying
within the figure are equal to one another."

So any two radii of a circle are equal. -/
axiom Definition15 {A B C : Point} {α : Circle} (hA : Centre A α) (hB : OnCircle B α)
    (hC : OnCircle C α) : ‖A B‖ = ‖A C‖
helper_signatures.Elements.InsideCircle:
/-- `InsideCircle A α`: the point `A` lies inside the circle `α`. -/
opaque InsideCircle : Point → Circle → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.InsideCircle.of_between_centre:
/-- A point between the centre and a point on the circle is within it. It is nearer the
centre than that point is, as the part is less than the whole, and so nearer than the
circumference by Definition 15 and the transfer rules. No proposition is needed, and not
System E's Circle 2, which contains III.2. -/
theorem InsideCircle.of_between_centre {O P : Point} (hO : Centre O α)
    (hP : OnCircle P α) (h : Between O C P) : InsideCircle C α
helper_signatures.Elements.Magnitude.add_self_lt_add_self:
/-- The doubles of unequal things are unequal, the less to the less: if `a` is less
than `b`, then `a` and `a` together are less than `b` and `b` together. (System E
§3.5) -/
theorem Magnitude.add_self_lt_add_self {a b : Magnitude k} (h : a < b) : a + a < b + b
helper_signatures.Elements.Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_left:
/-- The same, with the common part first: if `a` and `b` together are less than `a`
and `c` together, then `b` is less than `c`. -/
theorem Magnitude.lt_of_add_lt_add_left {k : Kind} {a b c : Magnitude k} (h : a + b < a + c) :
    b < c
helper_signatures.Elements.OnCircle:
/-- `OnCircle A α`: the point `A` lies on the circumference of the circle `α`. -/
opaque OnCircle : Point → Circle → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.between:
/-- Beyond the start of a ray. If CB is produced beyond B to E, every point D
of the ray from B through E lies beyond B from C as well. Of the three points
C, B, D on one straight line one is between the other two (System E,
Between 6); were it C or D, then B would lie between D and E, and D
would be off the ray. -/
theorem OnRay.between {C D E : Point} (hD : OnRay D B E) (hCBE : Between C B E) :
    Between C B D
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.between_of_len_lt:
/-- Of two points on a ray, the one nearer the start lies between the start and
the other. -/
theorem OnRay.between_of_len_lt (hP : OnRay P A B) (hQ : OnRay Q A B) (h : ‖A P‖ < ‖A Q‖) :
    Between A P Q
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.exists_len_eq:
/-- "Let DG be made equal to DF" (I.24): on the ray from D through any point P
there is a point G with DG equal to DF. Describe the circle with centre D and
distance DF (Post. 3); the straight line DP, which passes through its centre, cuts
it on P's side of D (System E, Intersections 5, with a point Q set out on the
other side); and DG is a radius [Def. 15]. -/
theorem OnRay.exists_len_eq {D F P : Point} (hDF : D ≠ F) (hDP : D ≠ P) :
    ∃ G : Point, OnRay G D P ∧ ‖D G‖ = ‖D F‖
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.of_between:
/-- A point between A and B is on the ray from A through B. -/
theorem OnRay.of_between (h : Between A P B) : OnRay P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OnRay.symm:
/-- P is on the ray from A through B exactly when B is on the ray from A
through P: they are one and the same ray. -/
theorem OnRay.symm (h : OnRay P A B) : OnRay B A P
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the other side of AB from Q, then Q is on the other side
from P. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.symm (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : OppositeSidesOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.OppositeSidesOf.triangle:
/-- A point on either side of the straight line AB is not on it, so ABP is a
triangle. -/
theorem OppositeSidesOf.triangle (h : OppositeSidesOf P Q A B) : Triangle A B P
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.between:
/-- Parallels keep order. Let three straight lines be crossed by two others: if B
lies between A and C on one crossing straight line, then B' lies between A'
and C' on the other, when A, A' lie on L₁, B, B' on L, and C, C' on
L₃, and L₁ and L₃ are each parallel to L. All of L₁ lies on one side of
L, and all of L₃ on the other (`Parallel.sameSide`). Book II's figures use it
(`Parallelogram.figure`), where the parallels through the points of section meet the
far side of the square in the same order. -/
theorem Parallel.between (h₁ : Parallel L₁ L) (h₃ : Parallel L₃ L) (hA : OnLine A L₁)
    (hB : OnLine B L) (hC : OnLine C L₃) (hABC : Between A B C) (hA' : OnLine A' L₁)
    (hB' : OnLine B' L) (hC' : OnLine C' L₃) (hcol : Collinear A' B' C') :
    Between A' B' C'
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallel.symm:
/-- If L is parallel to M, then M is parallel to L. -/
theorem Parallel.symm (h : Parallel L M) : Parallel M L
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.reverse:
/-- The parallelogram ABCD, read the other way round from A, is the
parallelogram ADCB. -/
theorem Parallelogram.reverse (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Parallelogram A D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.rotate:
/-- The parallelogram ABCD, named from B, is the parallelogram BCDA. -/
theorem Parallelogram.rotate (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Parallelogram B C D A
helper_signatures.Elements.Parallelogram.triangle:
/-- In the parallelogram ABCD, the corner C is off the straight line AB, so
ABC is a triangle. -/
theorem Parallelogram.triangle (h : Parallelogram A B C D) : Triangle A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate1:
/-- **Postulate 1.** To draw a straight line from any point to any point. -/
axiom Postulate1 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ L : Line, OnLine A L ∧ OnLine B L
helper_signatures.Elements.Postulate3:
/-- **Postulate 3.** To describe a circle with any centre and distance.

Like Euclid's own compass, this one "collapses": the circle has centre `A` and
passes through `B`. Carrying a distance from one place to another is
Proposition 2's job. -/
axiom Postulate3 (A B : Point) (h : A ≠ B) : ∃ α : Circle, Centre A α ∧ OnCircle B α
helper_signatures.Elements.Rectangle:
/-- **Definition II.1.** A rectangular parallelogram: the parallelogram `ABCD`, its
corners taken in order, with all four of its angles right. Euclid says "rectangular",
as Definition 22 says "right-angled" of the square. -/
def Rectangle (A B C D : Point) : Prop
helper_signatures.Elements.Rectangle.eq_rect:
/-- Euclid's way of naming a rectangle: "BH is the rectangle A, BC, for it is contained
by GB, BC, and BG is equal to A" (II.1). If the sides PQ, PS of the rectangle
PQRS are equal to AB, CD, it is the rectangle contained by AB, CD.
[I. 4, I. 34] -/
theorem Rectangle.eq_rect (h : Rectangle P Q R S) (h₁ : ‖P Q‖ = ‖A B‖) (h₂ : ‖P S‖ = ‖C D‖) :
    quadArea P Q R S = rect A B C D
helper_signatures.Elements.Rectangle.reverse:
/-- The rectangle ABCD, read the other way round from A, is the rectangle ADCB. -/
theorem Rectangle.reverse (h : Rectangle A B C D) : Rectangle A D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Rectangle.rotate:
/-- The rectangle ABCD, named from B, is the rectangle BCDA. -/
theorem Rectangle.rotate (h : Rectangle A B C D) : Rectangle B C D A
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.symm:
/-- If P is on the same side of AB as Q, then Q is on the same side as P. -/
theorem SameSideOf.symm (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : SameSideOf Q P A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.trans:
/-- Points on the same side as a third are on the same side as each other. -/
theorem SameSideOf.trans (h₁ : SameSideOf P Q A B) (h₂ : SameSideOf Q R A B) :
    SameSideOf P R A B
helper_signatures.Elements.SameSideOf.triangle:
/-- A point on one side of the straight line AB is not on it, so ABP is a
triangle. -/
theorem SameSideOf.triangle (h : SameSideOf P Q A B) : Triangle A B P
helper_signatures.Elements.Square.reverse:
/-- The square ABCD, read the other way round from A, is the square ADCB. -/
theorem Square.reverse (h : Square A B C D) (hp : Parallelogram A B C D) :
    Square A D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Square.rotate:
/-- The square ABCD, named from B, is the square BCDA. -/
theorem Square.rotate (h : Square A B C D) : Square B C D A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.add_comm:
/-- The order of adding does not matter. (System E §3.5) -/
axiom add_comm (a b : Magnitude k) : a + b = b + a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.adjacent_eq_of_right:
/-- A right angle is equal to the angle adjacent to it. (Diagram-angle 3; the
other half is Definition 10 together with Postulate 4) -/
axiom adjacent_eq_of_right (hA : OnLine A L) (hB : OnLine B L) (h : Between A C B)
    (hD : ¬ OnLine D L) (hright : ∠ A C D = ∟) : ∠ A C D = ∠ D C B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.angle_symm:
/-- The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4) -/
axiom angle_symm (hAB : A ≠ B) (hCB : C ≠ B) : ∠ A B C = ∠ C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.between_symm:
/-- If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1) -/
axiom between_symm (h : Between A B C) : Between C B A
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.len_add_of_between:
/-- If B is between A and C, then AB and BC together make up AC.
(Diagram-segment 1) -/
axiom len_add_of_between (h : Between A B C) : ‖A B‖ + ‖B C‖ = ‖A C‖
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.len_symm:
/-- The straight line AB is the straight line BA. (Metric 3) -/
axiom len_symm (A B : Point) : ‖A B‖ = ‖B A‖
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.line_circle_beyond:
/-- A straight line through a point B inside a circle, produced beyond B
away from C, cuts the circle there. (Intersections 5) -/
axiom line_circle_beyond {B C : Point} {L : Line} {α : Circle}
    (hB : InsideCircle B α) (hBL : OnLine B L) (hCL : OnLine C L) (hCB : C ≠ B) :
    ∃ A : Point, OnCircle A α ∧ OnLine A L ∧ Between A B C
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.line_unique:
/-- Two points determine a straight line. (Generalities 1) -/
axiom line_unique (hAB : A ≠ B) (hAL : OnLine A L) (hBL : OnLine B L) (hAM : OnLine A M)
    (hBM : OnLine B M) : L = M
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.lt_irrefl:
/-- No magnitude is less than itself. (System E §3.5) -/
axiom lt_irrefl (a : Magnitude k) : ¬ a < a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.lt_trans:
/-- What is less than the less is less still. (System E §3.5) -/
axiom lt_trans {a b c : Magnitude k} : a < b → b < c → a < c
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.lt_trichotomy:
/-- Of two magnitudes, one is less, or they are equal, or the other is less.
(System E §3.5) -/
axiom lt_trichotomy (a b : Magnitude k) : a < b ∨ a = b ∨ b < a
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between:
/-- A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ B
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.ne_of_between_ends:
/-- The ends of a finite straight line differ. (Between 1) -/
axiom ne_of_between_ends (h : Between A B C) : A ≠ C
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_circle_of_len_eq:
/-- A point at the distance of the radius from the centre is on the circle.
(Diagram-segment 3, the half that Definition 15 doesn't give) -/
axiom on_circle_of_len_eq (hA : Centre A α) (hB : OnCircle B α) (h : ‖A C‖ = ‖A B‖) :
    OnCircle C α
helper_signatures.Elements.Tacit.on_line_of_between_ends:
/-- A straight line through A and C passes through every point between them.
(Between 3) -/

I.4.enunciation: If two triangles have the two sides equal to two sides respectively, and have the angles contained by the equal straight lines equal, they will also have the base equal to the base, the triangle will be equal to the triangle, and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles respectively, namely those which the equal sides subtend.

I.10.enunciation: To bisect a given finite straight line.

I.28.enunciation: If a straight line falling on two straight lines make the exterior angle equal to the interior and opposite angle on the same side, or the interior angles on the same side equal to two right angles, the straight lines will be parallel to one another.

I.34.enunciation: In parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the diameter bisects the areas.

I.45.enunciation: To construct, in a given rectilineal angle, a parallelogram equal to a given rectilineal figure.

I.46.enunciation: On a given straight line to describe a square.

I.47.enunciation: In right-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the right angle is equal to the squares on the sides containing the right angle.

II.5.enunciation: If a straight line be cut into equal and unequal segments, the rectangle contained by the unequal segments of the whole together with the square on the straight line between the points of section is equal to the square on the half.

definitions.AreParallel:
/-- The straight lines `AB` and `CD` are parallel (Definition 23). -/
def AreParallel (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ C ≠ D ∧
    ∀ L M : Line, OnLine A L → OnLine B L → OnLine C M → OnLine D M → Parallel L M
definitions.Between:
/-- `Between A B C`: the point `B` lies on the straight line through `A` and `C`,
strictly between them. -/
opaque Between : Point → Point → Point → Prop
definitions.Centre:
/-- `Centre A α`: the point `A` is the centre of the circle `α`. (Def. 16) -/
opaque Centre : Point → Circle → Prop
definitions.Contain:
/-- The lengths `a` and `b` contain the area `x`: some rectangle `PQRS` has `PQ` equal
to `a`, `PS` equal to `b`, and is equal to `x`; or one of `a`, `b` is nothing, and so
is `x`. -/
def Contain (a b : Length) (x : Area) : Prop :=
  ((a = 0 ∨ b = 0) ∧ x = 0) ∨
    ∃ P Q R S : Point, Rectangle P Q R S ∧ ‖P Q‖ = a ∧ ‖P S‖ = b ∧ quadArea P Q R S = x
definitions.InsideCircle:
/-- `InsideCircle A α`: the point `A` lies inside the circle `α`. -/
opaque InsideCircle : Point → Circle → Prop
definitions.Kind:
/-- The kinds of magnitude in Book I. -/
inductive Kind where
  | length
  | angle
  | area
  deriving DecidableEq
definitions.Length:
/-- A length (of a finite straight line). -/
abbrev Length := Magnitude .length
definitions.Line:
/-- **Straight line.** (Defs. 2–4) A `Line` is a whole straight line, extending
without end. Euclid's "finite straight line AB" is the pair of points `A`, `B`,
lying on such a line. -/
opaque Line : Type
definitions.Magnitude:
/-- A magnitude of a given kind: a length, an angle, or an area. -/
def Magnitude (k : Kind) : Type := (MagnitudeImpl k).type
definitions.MagnitudeImpl:
/-- A hidden carrier for each kind of magnitude. -/
opaque MagnitudeImpl : Kind → NonemptyType
definitions.OnCircle:
/-- `OnCircle A α`: the point `A` lies on the circumference of the circle `α`. -/
opaque OnCircle : Point → Circle → Prop
definitions.OnLine:
/-- `OnLine A L`: the point `A` lies on the straight line `L`. -/
opaque OnLine : Point → Line → Prop
definitions.OnRay:
/-- `P` lies on the straight line from `A` through `B`, on `B`'s side of `A`
(it may be `B` itself, or nearer, or beyond). -/
def OnRay (P A B : Point) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ P ≠ A ∧ Collinear A B P ∧ ¬ Between P A B
definitions.Parallel:
/-- **Definition 23.** "Parallel straight lines are straight lines which, being in
the same plane and being produced indefinitely in both directions, do not meet
one another in either direction." -/
def Parallel (L M : Line) : Prop :=
  L ≠ M ∧ ¬ ∃ P : Point, OnLine P L ∧ OnLine P M
definitions.Parallelogram:
/-- The parallelogram `ABCD`, its corners taken in order: `AB` is parallel to
`CD`, and `BC` to `DA`. Euclid does not define it; he first speaks of
"parallelogrammic areas" in I.34. -/
def Parallelogram (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  AreParallel A B C D ∧ AreParallel B C D A
definitions.Point:
/-- **Point.** "A point is that which has no part." (Def. 1) -/
opaque Point : Type
definitions.Rectangle:
/-- **Definition II.1.** A rectangular parallelogram: the parallelogram `ABCD`, its
corners taken in order, with all four of its angles right. Euclid says "rectangular",
as Definition 22 says "right-angled" of the square. -/
def Rectangle (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  Parallelogram A B C D ∧ ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.SameSide:
/-- `SameSide A B L`: the points `A` and `B` lie on the same side of the
straight line `L`. (Neither of them is on `L`.) -/
opaque SameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop
definitions.Square:
/-- **Definition 22.** "Of quadrilateral figures, a square is that which is both
equilateral and right-angled." The corners are `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, in order. -/
def Square (A B C D : Point) : Prop :=
  ‖A B‖ = ‖B C‖ ∧ ‖B C‖ = ‖C D‖ ∧ ‖C D‖ = ‖D A‖ ∧
    ∠ D A B = ∟ ∧ ∠ A B C = ∟ ∧ ∠ B C D = ∟ ∧ ∠ C D A = ∟
definitions.Triangle:
/-- **Definition 19.** A trilateral figure: three points not on one straight
line, joined by three straight lines. -/
def Triangle (A B C : Point) : Prop := ¬ Collinear A B C
definitions.ang:
/-- The angle `ABC`, with vertex `B`. Written `∠ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque ang : Point → Point → Point → Angle
definitions.area:
/-- The area of the triangle `ABC`. Written `△ A B C`. -/
noncomputable opaque area : Point → Point → Point → Area
definitions.len:
/-- The length of the finite straight line from `A` to `B`. Written `‖A B‖`. -/
noncomputable opaque len : Point → Point → Length
definitions.quadArea:
/-- The area of the four-sided figure `ABCD` (corners in order), measured as the
two triangles into which its diameter `AC` cuts it. -/
noncomputable def quadArea (A B C D : Point) : Area := △ A B C + △ A C D
definitions.rect:
/-- **The rectangle contained by `AB`, `CD`** (Definition II.1): the area of any
rectangle whose sides about a right angle are equal to `AB` and `CD`. Lean chooses one
such area (`Classical.epsilon`); `Rectangle.contained` shows that every such
rectangle is equal to it. -/
noncomputable def rect (A B C D : Point) : Area :=
  Classical.epsilon (Contain ‖A B‖ ‖C D‖)
definitions.rightAngle:
/-- The size of a right angle. Postulate 4 says all right angles are equal, so
it makes sense to have one name for their common size. Written `∟`. -/
noncomputable opaque rightAngle : Angle
definitions.sq:
/-- **The square on `AB`**: the rectangle contained by `AB`, `AB`, the area of any
square described on a straight line equal to `AB` (`Square.eq_sq`). -/
noncomputable def sq (A B : Point) : Area := rect A B A B

question.instructions:
Does every proposition called by the proof unit in `lean_proof` do work towards its conclusion or a substantive intermediate step of Euclid's argument? Also check for artificial hypothesis uses. Judge this unit's uses of the supplied helper signatures; helper bodies are outside this question. Heath's sentences stand as `--` lines and `cited` gives exact enunciations. In Lean, `have h : T := p` proves T by p and calls the result h; `obtain ⟨…⟩ := p` takes p apart into named pieces; `rw [h34, h37, …]` rewrites the goal by the equalities named. Follow uses through helper calls and tactics as well as explicit names. An anonymous binding or an unused hypothesis alone does not establish a defect. If both defects occur, choose `a dummy citation`.

docs/FORMALIZATION.md, section 5:
A checked intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid is legitimate, even if the

criteria.cannot tell: What is given here is not enough to decide.
criteria.all do work: Every proposition call supports a later step or the conclusion, or establishes a substantive intermediate fact tied to a real sentence of Euclid. No hypothesis is mentioned merely to look used. With no proposition calls the citation part alone is vacuous; hypothesis use must still be inspected.
criteria.a dummy citation: Some proposition call does no substantive work: its result neither supports the argument nor establishes a substantive intermediate fact, and merely supplies a citation while the step is done another way.
criteria.an artificial hypothesis use: No dummy citation is established, but a hypothesis is mentioned only so that it looks used, and does no substantive work.
